Text:
# Best MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

After generating five candidate models, **Model 1** is selected as the best. It is the most complete and internally consistent formulation: it correctly handles the bidirectional conflict resolution on the shared opposite track, linearizes the quadratic energy function via speed-level binaries, and explicitly couples the timetable with physical speed profiles. Below is the complete, self-contained model.

---

## 1. Problem Statement and Assumptions

**Problem:** A partial segment blockage occurs on one track of a bidirectional high-speed railway line. During a known disruption window $[\tau_s, \tau_e]$ on segment $k_d$, the original direction is unusable, but affected trains may **reroute** to the opposite track. We jointly decide train **retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation**, and **speed profiles** to minimize a weighted sum of total delay and traction energy, while guaranteeing conflict-free operation.

**Assumptions (marked):**
- *(A1)* A single partial blockage affects one segment $k_d$; the disruption window is known in advance.
- *(A2)* Rerouting to the opposite track is permitted only during the disruption window and must remain conflict-free with opposing traffic.
- *(A3)* Homogeneous fleet: uniform train length and dynamics parameters across trains.
- *(A4)* Time and speed are discretized ($\Delta_t$, $\Delta_v$); energy is piecewise-linearized over discrete speed levels.
- *(A5)* Dwell times are bounded; headways are enforced at segment endpoints.
- *(A6)* Quadratic energy $E(v)=c_1 v + c_2 v^2$ is pre-evaluated at each speed level.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Stations, indexed $s$ |
| $K$ | Track segments, indexed $k$ |
| $R$ | Routes (original + rerouting), indexed $r$ |
| $P$ | Discretized time intervals, indexed $t$ |
| $V$ | Discretized speed levels, indexed $v$ |
| $R^{\text{opp}} \subseteq R$ | Rerouting routes |

Segment $k$ connects origin $o(k)$ to destination $d(k)$.

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ |
| $v_{\max}, v_{\min}$ | Max/min operating speed |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration |
| $\tau^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}, \tau^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $\text{dwell}_{\min}, \text{dwell}_{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time |
| $h$ | Minimum headway |
| $E_v$ | Energy rate at speed level $v$ (precomputed) |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $\Delta_t, \Delta_v$ | Time / speed discretization steps |
| $\rho \in [0,1]$ | Delay–energy trade-off weight |
| $\tau_s, \tau_e$ | Disruption window bounds |
| $k_d$ | Disrupted segment |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Binary:**
- $x_{i,k,r}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ on segment $k$
- $y_{i,j,k}$ — 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$
- $z_{i,k,t}$ — 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $k$ at time $t$
- $w_{i,k,t}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on $k$ at $t$ (rerouting)
- $c_i$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $\alpha_{i,k,v,t}$ — 1 if train $i$ on $k$ at $t$ runs at speed level $v$

**Continuous ($\ge 0$):**
- $\tau^a_{i,s}, \tau^d_{i,s}$ — actual arrival / departure times
- $v_{i,k,t}$ — speed; $p_{i,k,t}$ — position
- $e_i$ — energy; $\text{delay}_i$ — delay; $\delta_{i,s}$ — delay at station

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \rho \sum_{i \in T} \text{delay}_i \;+\; (1-\rho)\sum_{i \in T} e_i
$$

with

$$
\text{delay}_i = \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{i,s}, \qquad
e_i = \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{t \in P}\sum_{v \in V} E_v \cdot \alpha_{i,k,v,t} \cdot \Delta_t
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Route selection / flow conservation**
$$
\sum_{r \in R} x_{i,k,r} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, k
$$
$$
x_{i,k,r} = x_{i,k',r} \quad \forall i, r, (k,k') \text{ consecutive through a station}
$$

**(C2) Segment capacity (one train per direction)**
$$
\sum_{i \in T} z_{i,k,t} \le 1 \qquad \forall k, t
$$

**(C3) Bidirectional conflict resolution**
$$
w_{i,k,t} + w_{j,k,t} \le 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j, k, t
$$
$$
w_{i,k,t} \le z_{i,k,t} \qquad \forall i, k, t
$$

**(C4) Disruption window (rerouting forced on blocked segment)**
$$
z_{i,k_d,t} - w_{i,k_d,t} \le 0 \qquad \forall i,\; t \in [\tau_s, \tau_e]
$$

**(C5) Train dynamics (position update)**
$$
p_{i,k,t+1} = p_{i,k,t} + v_{i,k,t}\,\Delta_t \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

**(C6) Speed limits**
$$
v_{\min}\, z_{i,k,t} \le v_{i,k,t} \le v_{\max}\, z_{i,k,t} \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

**(C7) Acceleration / deceleration limits**
$$
v_{i,k,t+1} - v_{i,k,t} \le a_{\max}\Delta_t + M(1-z_{i,k,t}) \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
v_{i,k,t} - v_{i,k,t+1} \le b_{\max}\Delta_t + M(1-z_{i,k,t}) \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

**(C8) Dwell time bounds**
$$
\text{dwell}_{\min} \le \tau^d_{i,s} - \tau^a_{i,s} \le \text{dwell}_{\max} \qquad \forall i,s
$$

**(C9) Headway / ordering**
$$
y_{i,j,k} + y_{j,i,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j, k
$$
$$
\tau^a_{j,d(k)} \ge \tau^a_{i,d(k)} + h - M(1-y_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall i \ne j, k
$$

**(C10) Rerouting feasibility (opposite track conflict-free)**
$$
w_{i,k,t} + w_{j,k,t} \le 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j, k, t
$$
$$
w_{i,k,t} \le 1 - z_{j,k,t} \qquad \forall i \ne j, k, t
$$

**(C11) Cancellation linkage**
$$
z_{i,k,t} \le 1 - c_i, \quad \alpha_{i,k,v,t} \le 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i,k,v,t
$$
$$
\tau^a_{i,s}, \tau^d_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i) \qquad \forall i,s
$$

**(C12) Speed profile ↔ travel distance**
$$
\sum_{t \in P} v_{i,k,t}\,\Delta_t = L_k\,(1-c_i) \qquad \forall i,k
$$

**(C13) Speed-level selection (convex combination)**
$$
\sum_{v \in V} \alpha_{i,k,v,t} = z_{i,k,t} \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
v_{i,k,t} = \sum_{v \in V} v\,\alpha_{i,k,v,t} \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

**(C14) Energy consumption (linearized)**
$$
e_i = \sum_{k,t,v} E_v \cdot \alpha_{i,k,v,t} \cdot \Delta_t \qquad \forall i
$$

**(C15) Arrival / departure consistency**
$$
\tau^a_{i,d(k)} = \tau^d_{i,o(k)} + \sum_{t \in P} \Delta_t\, z_{i,k,t} \qquad \forall i,k
$$
$$
\tau^d_{i,s} \ge \tau^a_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,s
$$

**(C16) Segment occupancy linking**
$$
p_{i,k,t} \le L_k + M(1-z_{i,k,t}), \qquad p_{i,k,t} \ge -M(1-z_{i,k,t}) \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

**(C17) Route–rerouting consistency**
$$
w_{i,k,t} \le \sum_{r \in R^{\text{opp}}} x_{i,k,r} \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

**(C18) Delay definition**
$$
\delta_{i,s} \ge \tau^a_{i,s} - \tau^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \ge \tau^d_{i,s} - \tau^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i,s
$$

**(C19) Domains**
$$
x, y, z, w, c, \alpha \in \{0,1\}; \quad \tau^a, \tau^d, v, p, e, \text{delay}, \delta \ge 0
$$

---

## 7. Why This Model Is Best

1. **Complete integration** — routing, ordering, retiming, rerouting, cancellation, and speed profiles are all co-decided in one MILP, matching the paper's core contribution.
2. **Correct bidirectional conflict handling** — constraints (C3), (C4), (C10), (C17) jointly guarantee that rerouting to the opposite track during the blockage never creates a conflicting opposing movement.
3. **Rigorous linearization** — the quadratic energy and the speed–distance relation are made linear via speed-level binaries $\alpha$ and the convex-combination constraints (C13)–(C14), keeping the model a true MILP.
4. **Physical realizability** — dynamics (C5), speed/acceleration bounds (C6)–(C7), and timetable–profile linking (C12), (C15), (C16) ensure the rescheduled timetable is executable at the control level.
5. **Operational realism** — dwell bounds, headways, and cancellation options reflect real dispatch practice.

**Model size (typical):** $|T|\approx20$, $|K|\approx10$, $|P|\approx100$, $|V|\approx10$ → $10^5$–$10^6$ binaries, solvable with Gurobi/CPLEX using warm starts, symmetry breaking on $y_{i,j,k}$, and rolling-horizon decomposition (as proposed in the paper's decomposition framework).

# Final MILP: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | Stations, ordered along the line |
| $E = \{1,\dots,N-1\}$ | Segments; $e$ connects station $s(e)$ and $s(e)+1$ |
| $K$ | Set of trains |
| $P$ | Position intervals within a segment |
| $Q = \{1,\dots,Q\}$ | Discrete speed levels |
| $e^* \in E$ | Disrupted segment (with entry station $s^* = s(e^*)$) |
| $D = \{\text{up},\text{down}\}$ | Directions |

**Assumptions:** A1 single line; A2 fixed station sequence per train; A3 single disruption segment $e^*$; A4 rerouting only on $e^*$; A5 cancellation allowed; A6 discrete-speed linearization of dynamics; A7 headway $h$; A8 dwell bounds.

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}},\ T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window |
| $T_{\text{horizon}}$ | Planning horizon; **$M = T_{\text{horizon}}$ (big-M)** |
| $\hat a_{k,s},\ \hat d_{k,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure |
| $\text{dir}(k),\ \text{dir}(e)$ | Direction of train / segment |
| $L_{e,p}$ | Length of interval $p$ in segment $e$ ($\sum_p L_{e,p}=L_e$) |
| $v_q,\ u_q = 1/v_q$ | Speed level and its inverse |
| $\alpha_p,\ \beta_p$ | Energy coefficients on interval $p$ |
| $t^{\min}_{k,e},\ t^{\max}_{k,e}$ | Min/max running time |
| $h$ | Minimum headway (same track, same direction) |
| $\tau$ | Minimum separation on shared track |
| $\text{dw}^{\min},\ \text{dw}^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell |
| $c^{\text{dev}},c^{\text{energy}},c^{\text{cancel}}_k,c^{\text{reroute}}$ | Cost coefficients |

---

## Decision Variables

**Scheduling / routing**
- $x_k \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $k$ operated
- $a_{k,s},\,d_{k,s} \ge 0$ — arrival / departure times
- $y_{k,k',e} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if $k$ precedes $k'$ on segment $e$ (same direction)
- $r_{k,e^*} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $k$ rerouted on $e^*$
- $z_{k,k'} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if $k$ uses shared track on $e^*$ before $k'$
- $\sigma_{k} \in \{0,1\}$ — selects which side of the window a non-rerouted train avoids (side selector)

**Speed / energy**
- $w_{k,e,p,q} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $k$ uses speed level $q$ on interval $p$ of segment $e$
- $t_{k,e} \ge 0$ — running time
- $E_{k,e} \ge 0$ — energy

**Deviation**
- $\delta^a_{k,s},\ \delta^d_{k,s} \ge 0$ — absolute arrival / departure deviation

---

## Objective

$$
\min\ Z = c^{\text{dev}}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{s\in S}\big(\delta^a_{k,s}+\delta^d_{k,s}\big)
+ c^{\text{energy}}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{e\in E}E_{k,e}
+ \sum_{k\in K} c^{\text{cancel}}_k\,(1-x_k)
+ c^{\text{reroute}}\sum_{k\in K} r_{k,e^*}
$$

---

## Constraints

### 1. Cancellation linking
$$
a_{k,s}\le M x_k,\quad d_{k,s}\le M x_k \qquad \forall k,s
$$
$$
t_{k,e}\le M x_k,\quad E_{k,e}\le M x_k \qquad \forall k,e
$$
$$
r_{k,e^*}\le x_k \qquad \forall k
$$

### 2. Dwell time bounds
$$
d_{k,s}\ge a_{k,s}+\text{dw}^{\min}-M(1-x_k)\qquad \forall k,s
$$
$$
d_{k,s}\le a_{k,s}+\text{dw}^{\max}+M(1-x_k)\qquad \forall k,s
$$

### 3. Segment running-time consistency
For segment $e$ with entry station $s(e)$:
$$
a_{k,s(e)+1}=d_{k,s(e)}+t_{k,e}\quad\text{(operated)}
$$
Enforced linearly:
$$
-M(1-x_k)\le a_{k,s(e)+1}-d_{k,s(e)}-t_{k,e}\le M(1-x_k)\qquad \forall k,e
$$

### 4. Running-time bounds
$$
t^{\min}_{k,e}\,x_k\le t_{k,e}\le t^{\max}_{k,e}\,x_k\qquad \forall k,e
$$

### 5. Speed-profile selection and coupling (linearized)
$$
\sum_{q\in Q} w_{k,e,p,q}=x_k\qquad \forall k,e,p
$$
$$
t_{k,e}=\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{q\in Q} L_{e,p}\,u_q\,w_{k,e,p,q}\qquad \forall k,e
$$
$$
E_{k,e}=\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{q\in Q}\big(\alpha_p v_q+\beta_p\big)w_{k,e,p,q}\qquad \forall k,e
$$

### 6. Deviation definition (linked to cancellation)
$$
\delta^a_{k,s}\ge a_{k,s}-\hat a_{k,s},\qquad \delta^a_{k,s}\ge \hat a_{k,s}-a_{k,s}\qquad \forall k,s
$$
$$
\delta^d_{k,s}\ge d_{k,s}-\hat d_{k,s},\qquad \delta^d_{k,s}\ge \hat d_{k,s}-d_{k,s}\qquad \forall k,s
$$
$$
\delta^a_{k,s}\le M x_k,\qquad \delta^d_{k,s}\le M x_k\qquad \forall k,s
$$

### 7. Ordering and headway (same direction, same segment)
For each $e$ with $\text{dir}(e)=d$, and $k,k'$ with $\text{dir}(k)=\text{dir}(k')=d$:
$$
y_{k,k',e}+y_{k',k,e}\ge x_k+x_{k'}-1
$$
$$
y_{k,k',e}+y_{k',k,e}\le 1
$$
$$
d_{k',s(e)}\ge d_{k,s(e)}+h-M(1-y_{k,k',e})-M(2-x_k-x_{k'})
$$

### 8. Rerouting eligibility (window overlap)
$$
r_{k,e^*}\le x_k\qquad \forall k
$$
$$
d_{k,s^*}\le T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}+M(1-r_{k,e^*})\qquad \forall k
$$
$$
a_{k,s^*+1}\ge T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}}-M(1-r_{k,e^*})\qquad \forall k
$$

### 9. Non-rerouted trains avoid the blocked window on the normal track
With side selector $\sigma_k\in\{0,1\}$:
$$
a_{k,s^*+1}\le T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}}+M(1-r_{k,e^*})+M(1-x_k)+M\sigma_k\qquad \forall k
$$
$$
d_{k,s^*}\ge T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}-M(1-r_{k,e^*})-M(1-x_k)-M(1-\sigma_k)\qquad \forall k
$$

### 10. Conflict resolution on shared track $e^*$
For each ordered pair $k\ne k'$:
$$
z_{k,k'}+z_{k',k}\ge r_{k,e^*}+r_{k',e^*}-1
$$
$$
z_{k,k'}\le r_{k,e^*},\qquad z_{k,k'}\le r_{k',e^*}
$$
$$
a_{k',s^*+1}+\tau\le d_{k,s^*}+M(1-z_{k',k})
$$
$$
a_{k,s^*+1}+\tau\le d_{k',s^*}+M(1-z_{k,k'})
$$

### 11. Domains
$$
x_k,\ y_{k,k',e},\ r_{k,e^*},\ z_{k,k'},\ \sigma_k,\ w_{k,e,p,q}\in\{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{k,s},\ d_{k,s},\ t_{k,e},\ E_{k,e},\ \delta^a_{k,s},\ \delta^d_{k,s}\ge 0
$$

---

## Model Summary

| Component | Role |
|-----------|------|
| $x_k$ | Operate / cancel |
| $a_{k,s},d_{k,s}$ | Rescheduled timetable |
| $y_{k,k',e}$ | Reordering (same direction) |
| $r_{k,e^*}$ | Local rerouting on $e^*$ |
| $z_{k,k'}$ | Conflict resolution on shared track |
| $\sigma_k$ | Side-of-window selector for non-rerouted trains |
| $w_{k,e,p,q}$ | Discrete speed-level selection |
| $t_{k,e},E_{k,e}$ | Running time and energy |
| $\delta^a,\delta^d$ | Timetable deviation |

**Coupling mechanism:** Constraint (3) links the timetable ($a,d$) to running time $t$; Constraint (5) links $t$ to the discrete speed profile and energy $E$. This guarantees the rescheduled timetable is physically executable by the optimized speed profile, and the speed profile respects the timetable — the core TRP–TSMP coupling. Constraints (7)–(10) resolve same-direction headways and bidirectional conflicts on the shared track under rerouting, and (8)–(9) enforce the disruption-window logic.

Text:
# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Among the three generated models, **Model 2** provides the most complete and self-contained formulation. It offers the clearest separation between rescheduling (TRP) and speed management (TSMP) layers, explicitly captures bidirectional conflict resolution on the shared opposite track (the distinctive difficulty of partial blockage disruptions), and cleanly couples the two layers through running-time equations. It is presented below as the selected best model.

---

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly stated)

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Corridor with stations $i=1,\dots,N$; segment $i$ connects station $i$ and $i+1$. Trains run forward ($+1$) or backward ($-1$). |
| A2 | A single partial blockage occurs on one track of segment $i^\star$ during $[B_s,B_e]$. The opposite track may be used bidirectionally in that window. |
| A3 | Discrete speed levels $k\in K$; running time and energy are precomputed constants per (segment, level) and selected by binary variables. |
| A4 | Energy per segment is a precomputed piecewise-linear value $E_{i,k}$ — kept linear via binary selection. |
| A5 | A cancelled train consumes no capacity/energy and incurs a fixed penalty. |
| A6 | Minimum headway $h_{\min}$ applies between consecutive same-direction trains; at most one train occupies a track segment at a time in the disruption area. |
| A7 | All event times lie in horizon $[0,H]$; big-$M$ large enough to deactivate constraints. |
| A8 | No overtaking inside a segment; ordering binaries enforce consistent order per track. |

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

- $T$ — trains, $t\in T$.
- $I=\{1,\dots,N\}$ — stations/control points.
- $S=\{1,\dots,N-1\}$ — segments, $i\in S$ (segment $i$ connects station $i$ and $i+1$).
- $K$ — discrete speed levels, $k\in K$.
- $i^\star$ — disrupted segment; $b$ — blocked track direction; $[B_s,B_e]$ — blockage window.
- $\text{dir}(t)\in\{+1,-1\}$ — nominal direction of train $t$.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Rescheduling (TRP)**
- $a_{t,i}\ge 0$ — arrival time of $t$ at station $i$.
- $d_{t,i}\ge 0$ — departure time of $t$ from station $i$.
- $c_t\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ is cancelled.
- $r_{t,i}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $i$.
- $u_{t,i}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ traverses segment $i$ during the disruption window.
- $\delta_{t,i}\in\{0,1\}$ — path/ordering variable for shared-track conflicts.
- $y_{t,t',i}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ precedes $t'$ on segment $i$ (same track).

**Speed management (TSMP)**
- $x_{t,i,k}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $i$.
- $q_{t,i,k}\ge 0$ — auxiliary for piecewise-linear energy linearization.

With $\tau_{t,i}=\sum_k \tau_{i,k}x_{t,i,k}$ and $e_{t,i}=\sum_k E_{i,k}x_{t,i,k}$.

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z = \underbrace{w_1\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in I}\ell_{t,i}}_{\text{passenger delay}}
+ \underbrace{w_2\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{k\in K}E_{i,k}\,x_{t,i,k}}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{w_3\sum_{t\in T}c_t}_{\text{cancellation}}
+ \underbrace{w_4\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in S}\delta_{t,i}}_{\text{conflict penalty}}
$$

with delay slack linearization: $\ell_{t,i}\ge a_{t,i}-a^{0}_{t,i},\ \ell_{t,i}\ge 0$.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Cancellation logic
$$a_{t,i}\le M(1-c_t),\quad d_{t,i}\le M(1-c_t)\quad\forall i$$
$$x_{t,i,k}\le 1-c_t,\quad r_{t,i}\le 1-c_t,\quad u_{t,i}\le 1-c_t\quad\forall i,k$$
$$\sum_{k\in K}x_{t,i,k}=1-c_t\qquad\forall t,\ i\in S_{\text{visited}}(t)$$

### 5.2 Timetable / running and dwell
$$a_{t,j}=d_{t,i}+\tau_{t,i}\quad(j=\text{next station after }i\text{ for }t)$$
$$a_{t,i}+\underline{dw}_{t,i}\ \le\ d_{t,i}\ \le\ a_{t,i}+\overline{dw}_{t,i}$$
$$\tau_{t,i}\ \ge\ \tau^{\min}_{i}(1-c_t)$$

### 5.3 Speed-profile feasibility (accel/decel)
For consecutive segments $i,i+1$ with compatibility matrix $C_{k,k'}\in\{0,1\}$:
$$x_{t,i,k}+x_{t,i+1,k'}\ \le\ 1+C_{k,k'}\qquad\forall (k,k')\text{ incompatible}$$

### 5.4 Headway / safety (same track, same direction)
Let $s_{t,i}$ = entry time, $f_{t,i}$ = exit time of segment $i$:
$$s_{t',i}\ \ge\ f_{t,i}+h_{\min}-M(1-y_{t,t',i})$$
$$s_{t,i}\ \ge\ f_{t',i}+h_{\min}-M\,y_{t,t',i}$$
$$y_{t,t',i}+y_{t',t,i}=1,\qquad y_{t,t',i}+y_{t',t'',i}\le 1+y_{t,t'',i}$$

### 5.5 Disruption constraints
**(a) Overlap indicator** for window $[B_s,B_e]$ on segment $i^\star$:
$$s_{t,i^\star}\le B_e+M(1-o^1_t),\quad f_{t,i^\star}\ge B_s-M(1-o^2_t)$$
$$o_{t,i^\star}\ge o^1_t+o^2_t-1,\quad o_{t,i^\star}\le o^1_t,\quad o_{t,i^\star}\le o^2_t$$

**(b) Reroute or cancel if overlapping:**
$$o_{t,i^\star}\le r_{t,i^\star}+c_t$$

**(c) Reroute allowed only inside the window:**
$$s_{t,i^\star}\ge B_s-M(1-r_{t,i^\star}),\quad f_{t,i^\star}\le B_e+M(1-r_{t,i^\star})$$

**(d) Bidirectional conflict resolution** (opposing trains sharing opposite track):
$$f_{t,i^\star}\le s_{t',i^\star}-h_{\min}+M(1-\delta_{t,t'})$$
$$f_{t',i^\star}\le s_{t,i^\star}-h_{\min}+M\,\delta_{t,t'},\qquad \delta_{t,t'}+\delta_{t',t}=1$$

**(e) Rerouting capacity** (at most one train per track per segment at a time):
$$f_{t,i^\star}\le s_{t',i^\star}+M(1-\rho_{t,t'}),\qquad f_{t',i^\star}\le s_{t,i^\star}+M\,\rho_{t,t'}$$

### 5.6 Coupling speed ↔ timetable
Forward ($i\to i+1$): $s_{t,i}=d_{t,i}$, $f_{t,i}=a_{t,i+1}$.
Backward ($i+1\to i$): $s_{t,i}=d_{t,i+1}$, $f_{t,i}=a_{t,i}$.
$$f_{t,i}-s_{t,i}=\sum_{k\in K}\tau_{i,k}\,x_{t,i,k}$$

### 5.7 Energy (linear)
$$e_{t,i}=\sum_{k\in K}E_{i,k}\,x_{t,i,k}$$

### 5.8 Variable domains
$$a_{t,i},d_{t,i},s_{t,i},f_{t,i},\ell_{t,i},e_{t,i}\ge 0$$
$$c_t,x_{t,i,k},u_{t,i},r_{t,i},\delta_{t,i},y_{t,t',i},\rho_{t,t'}\in\{0,1\}$$
$$M=H+\max_{i,k}\tau_{i,k}+\max_{t,i}\overline{dw}_{t,i}$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

| Element | Role |
|---|---|
| $a_{t,i},d_{t,i}$ | Central rescheduling decisions (actual timetable). |
| $c_t$ | Allows retiring a train if rescheduling is infeasible; heavily penalized. |
| $r_{t,i},u_{t,i}$ | Rerouting onto opposite track during the disruption window. |
| $y_{t,t',i}$ | Same-direction sequencing; enforces minimum headway via big-$M$. |
| $\delta_{t,i},\rho_{t,t'}$ | **Bidirectional conflict resolution** on the shared opposite track — the distinctive difficulty of partial blockages. |
| $x_{t,i,k}$ | Discrete speed-level selection; feeds both running time $\tau_{t,i}$ and energy $e_{t,i}$. |
| $\ell_{t,i}$ | Linearizes absolute arrival-delay. |
| Speed↔timetable coupling | $f_{t,i}-s_{t,i}=\sum_k\tau_{i,k}x_{t,i,k}$ truly integrates TRP and TSMP. |

**Summary.** The formulation is a **pure MILP** with binary variables for rerouting, cancellation, ordering, and speed-level selection, and continuous time variables for arrivals/departures. Non-linearities (`1/v`, `max{0,·}`, piecewise-linear energy) are all linearized via SOS/binary expansion, slack variables, and big-$M$ disjunctions. It jointly optimizes train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles, producing a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles under partial segment blockage — directly implementable in Gurobi, CPLEX, or CBC.

Text:
Below is the best complete, linear MILP model for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP), synthesizing the strongest elements of the generated candidates (clean trigger-linearization from Model 3, robust rerouting-window handling from Models 1/4, and clear ordering/headway structure from Model 2).

---

# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $t, t' \in T$ | Trains, $\lvert T\rvert = N_T$ |
| $s \in S$ | Ordered stations, $s = 1,\dots,N_S$; section $s$ lies between station $s$ and $s{+}1$ |
| $s \in S^{sec}$ | Sections (arcs); $\lvert S^{sec}\rvert = N_S - 1$ |
| $k \in K$ | Discrete speed-profile (driving) regimes |
| $\delta \in \mathcal{Dir} = \{\text{nor}, \text{opp}\}$ | Track direction: normal track / opposite track (rerouting) |
| $D \subseteq S^{sec}$ | Disrupted sections |
| $\mathcal{N}(t)$ | Sections in train $t$'s route |
| $T^{canc} \subseteq T$ | Trains eligible for cancellation |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\text{orig\_arr}_{t,s}, \text{orig\_dep}_{t,s}$ | Original planned arrival/departure times |
| $\text{run}_{s,k}$ | Running time in section $s$ under regime $k$ |
| $E_{s,k}$ | Traction energy in section $s$ under regime $k$ (kWh) |
| $\text{min\_dwell}_{t,s}, \text{max\_dwell}_{t,s}$ | Dwell bounds |
| $\text{hw}^{min}$ | Minimum headway, same track/direction |
| $\text{hw}^{opp}$ | Minimum safety gap, opposing movements on shared track |
| $\text{tw}^{start}_d, \text{tw}^{end}_d$ | Disruption time window for section $d$ |
| $\text{blk}_d$ | Blocked direction on disrupted section $d$ |
| $c^{arr}_t, c^{dep}_t$ | Delay penalty weights (passenger importance) |
| $c^{en}$ | Energy penalty coefficient (€/kWh) |
| $c^{cancel}_t$ | Cancellation penalty (large) |
| $c^{reroute}$ | Rerouting penalty |
| $H$ | Planning horizon |
| $M$ | Big-M constant (sufficiently large) |

**Assumptions.** A1: double-track line, normally unidirectional; disruption blocks one track in $D$ over the window; rerouting to the opposite track allowed only then. A2: event times continuous, occupancy discretization implicit via ordering. A3: speed profiles discretized into finite regimes with precomputed (running time, energy) pairs. A4: headway, dwell, turn-around respected. A5: delay weighted by train importance, energy penalized linearly, cancellation heavily penalized. A6: bidirectional conflicts resolved by ordering + headway. A7: block exclusivity approximated by ordering binaries.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Time (continuous, $[0,H]$):** $a_{t,s}$ (arrival), $d_{t,s}$ (departure).

**Delay deviations (continuous, $\ge 0$):** $\delta^{arr+}_{t,s}, \delta^{arr-}_{t,s}, \delta^{dep+}_{t,s}, \delta^{dep-}_{t,s}$.

**Binaries:**
- $z_{t,s,k}$: train $t$ uses regime $k$ on section $s$;
- $y_{t,s,\delta}$: train $t$ uses direction $\delta$ on section $s$;
- $x_{t,t',s,\delta}$: $t$ precedes $t'$ on section $s$, direction $\delta$;
- $c_t$: train $t$ cancelled;
- $w_{t,d}$: train $t$ would be in disrupted section $d$ during the window.

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{t}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{N}(t)}\big(c^{arr}_t\,\delta^{arr+}_{t,s}+c^{dep}_t\,\delta^{dep+}_{t,s}\big)}_{\text{(i) weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{c^{en}\sum_{t}\sum_{s}\sum_{k}E_{s,k}\,z_{t,s,k}}_{\text{(ii) traction energy}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T^{canc}}c^{cancel}_t\,c_t}_{\text{(iii) cancellation}}
+ \underbrace{c^{reroute}\sum_{t}\sum_{s\in D}y_{t,s,\text{opp}}}_{\text{(iv) rerouting}}
$$

We minimize only positive deviations (lateness); earliness gives no reward.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Regime Selection
$$
\sum_{k\in K} z_{t,s,k} = 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t,\; s\in\mathcal{N}(t) \tag{C1}
$$

### 5.2 Time Propagation (Regime-Dependent Running Time)
$$
a_{t,s+1} = d_{t,s} + \sum_{k}\text{run}_{s,k}\,z_{t,s,k} + M\,c_t \cdot \theta_{t,s}, \quad \theta_{t,s}\in[-1,1] \tag{C2}
$$
Implemented as two big-M inequalities to keep linearity and allow cancellation slack:
$$
a_{t,s+1} \ge d_{t,s} + \sum_{k}\text{run}_{s,k}\,z_{t,s,k} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\; s\in\mathcal{N}(t) \tag{C2a}
$$
$$
a_{t,s+1} \le d_{t,s} + \sum_{k}\text{run}_{s,k}\,z_{t,s,k} + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\; s\in\mathcal{N}(t) \tag{C2b}
$$

### 5.3 Dwell Time Bounds
$$
d_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} + \text{min\_dwell}_{t,s} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C3a}
$$
$$
d_{t,s} \le a_{t,s} + \text{max\_dwell}_{t,s} + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C3b}
$$
$$
a_{t,s} \le d_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C3c}
$$

### 5.4 Delay Deviation Linking
$$
\delta^{arr+}_{t,s} - \delta^{arr-}_{t,s} = a_{t,s} - \text{orig\_arr}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C4a}
$$
$$
\delta^{dep+}_{t,s} - \delta^{dep-}_{t,s} = d_{t,s} - \text{orig\_dep}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C4b}
$$

### 5.5 Track/Direction Assignment
$$
y_{t,s,\text{nor}} + y_{t,s,\text{opp}} = 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C5a}
$$
$$
y_{t,s,\text{opp}} = 0 \qquad \forall t,\; s\notin D \tag{C5b}
$$

### 5.6 Disruption-Window Detection and Blocked-Track Prohibition
For each disrupted section $d\in D$, introduce $w_{t,d}=1$ if train $t$ would traverse $d$ within the window:
$$
d_{t,d} \ge \text{tw}^{start}_d - M(1 - w_{t,d}) - M\,c_t \tag{C6a}
$$
$$
d_{t,d} \le \text{tw}^{end}_d + M(1 - w_{t,d}) + M\,c_t \tag{C6b}
$$
$$
w_{t,d} \le 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t,\; d\in D \tag{C6c}
$$
If the blocked direction is the train's normal track, force rerouting (or waiting/cancelling):
$$
y_{t,d,\text{nor}} \le 1 - w_{t,d} + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\; d\in D \tag{C6d}
$$
Rerouting only permitted when the passage actually overlaps the window:
$$
y_{t,d,\text{opp}} \le w_{t,d}, \qquad \forall t,\; d\in D \tag{C6e}
$$

### 5.7 Same-Track, Same-Direction Headway via Ordering
Ordering completeness whenever both trains use the same track/direction:
$$
x_{t,t',s,\delta} + x_{t',t,s,\delta} \ge y_{t,s,\delta} + y_{t',s,\delta} - 1 \qquad \forall t\neq t', s, \delta \tag{C7a}
$$
Headway enforcement:
$$
a_{t',s+1} \ge d_{t,s} + \text{hw}^{min} - M(1 - x_{t,t',s,\delta}) - M(2 - y_{t,s,\delta} - y_{t',s,\delta}) \qquad \forall t\neq t', s, \delta \tag{C7b}
$$

### 5.8 Bidirectional Conflict on the Shared (Opposite) Track
When a rerouted train $t$ (using opp) meets a train $t'$ using the same physical track in the reverse sense, enforce strict pass-through order with safety gap. Define the shared-use indication:
$$
v_{t,t',d} \le y_{t,d,\text{opp}}, \quad v_{t,t',d} \le y_{t',d,\text{nor}}, \quad v_{t,t',d} \ge y_{t,d,\text{opp}} + y_{t',d,\text{nor}} - 1 \quad \forall d\in D \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
a_{t',d+1} \ge d_{t,d} + \text{hw}^{opp} - M(1 - x_{t,t',d,\text{opp}}) - M(1 - v_{t,t',d}) \qquad \forall d\in D \tag{C8b}
$$
$$
a_{t,d+1} \ge d_{t',d} + \text{hw}^{opp} - M(1 - x_{t',t,d,\text{opp}}) - M(1 - v_{t,t',d}) \qquad \forall d\in D \tag{C8c}
$$
$$
x_{t,t',d,\text{opp}} + x_{t',t,d,\text{opp}} \ge y_{t,d,\text{opp}} + y_{t',d,\text{nor}} - 1 \qquad \forall d\in D \tag{C8d}
$$
(One of C8b/C8c always binds; the other is relaxed by big-M, so no meeting inside the shared section occurs.)

### 5.9 Track Exclusivity
$$
y_{t,s,\delta} + y_{t',s,\delta} \le 1 + x_{t,t',s,\delta} + x_{t',t,s,\delta} \qquad \forall t\neq t', s, \delta \tag{C9}
$$

### 5.10 Cancellation Linking
$$
a_{t,s} \le M(1 - c_t), \qquad d_{t,s} \le M(1 - c_t) \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C10a}
$$
$$
z_{t,s,k} \le 1 - c_t, \quad y_{t,s,\delta} \le 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t,s,k,\delta \tag{C10b}
$$
$$
\delta^{arr+}_{t,s} \le M(1 - c_t), \quad \delta^{dep+}_{t,s} \le M(1 - c_t) \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C10c}
$$

### 5.11 Bounds
$$
0 \le a_{t,s},\; d_{t,s} \le H \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C11a}
$$
$$
\delta^{arr\pm}_{t,s},\ \delta^{dep\pm}_{t,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C11b}
$$
$$
z_{t,s,k},\ y_{t,s,\delta},\ x_{t,t',s,\delta},\ c_t,\ w_{t,d},\ v_{t,t',d} \in \{0,1\} \tag{C11c}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Component | Variables | Role |
|-----------|-----------|------|
| Retiming | $a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}$ | arrival/departure adjustment |
| Reordering | $x_{t,t',s,\delta}$ | train order on shared track |
| Rerouting | $y_{t,s,\delta}, w_{t,d}, v_{t,t',d}$ | track choice + window/conflict encoding |
| Cancellation | $c_t$ | service withdrawal |
| Speed management | $z_{t,s,k}$ | selection of executable speed profile |
| Delay accounting | $\delta^{\pm}_{t,s}$ | lateness/earliness |

| Constraint | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| C1 | exactly one regime per active train-section |
| C2 | regime-based running time propagation |
| C3 | dwell bounds and precedence |
| C4 | delay deviation linking |
| C5 | track/direction assignment + rerouting restriction |
| C6 | disruption-window detection & blocked-track prohibition |
| C7 | same-direction headway |
| C8 | bidirectional conflict resolution |
| C9 | track exclusivity |
| C10 | cancellation deactivation |
| C11 | variable bounds |

---

## 7. Justification as the Best Model

- **Complete decision coverage:** retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed profiles are jointly optimized — the full TRSMP scope.
- **Rigorous conflict-freeness:** same-direction headway (C7) plus bidirectional ordering/gap (C8) plus track exclusivity (C9) jointly guarantee a conflict-free timetable under shared-track rerouting.
- **Exact disruption encoding:** the $w_{t,d}$ trigger with two-sided big-M (C6a–C6b) is exact and avoids the weaker approximate encoding present in some candidates.
- **Full linearity:** all products are linearized via binaries ($w, v, x, z$); the model is a pure MILP solvable by Gurobi/CPLEX/HiGHS.
- **Tightness:** cancellation slack is bounded two-sided in C2 and dwell bounds in C3, tightening the LP relaxation relative to one-sided formulations.
- **Decomposition-friendly:** the modular structure (train-plan regime blocks + interaction/IP constraints) directly supports the paper's proposed IP reformulation and adaptive plan-generation algorithm.

**Assumptions marked:** A1–A7 above; A3 (discretized regimes with precomputed time/energy) and A7 (ordering-based exclusivity as an interlocking approximation) are the most consequential simplifying assumptions.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model for Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1, 2, \ldots, S\}$ | Set of stations along the urban rail transit line, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{T} = \{1, 2, \ldots, T\}$ | Set of trains in the rolling stock fleet, indexed by $i$ |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1, 2, \ldots, K\}$ | Set of time intervals in the prediction horizon, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{C} = \{1, 2, \ldots, C\}$ | Set of available train compositions (coupling configurations), indexed by $c$ |
| $\mathcal{P} = \{1, 2, \ldots, P\}$ | Set of MPC prediction steps within the horizon, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of track segments (links) between consecutive stations, indexed by $l = (s, s+1)$ |

**Assumption (A1):** The line is a single bidirectional urban rail transit line with stations ordered sequentially. Trains operate in one direction during the analysis period (or each direction is modeled separately).

**Assumption (A2):** The set $\mathcal{C}$ of train compositions is discrete, where each composition $c$ corresponds to a specific number of coupled train units, yielding capacity $Cap_c$ (number of passengers).

---

## 2. Parameters

### 2.1 Infrastructure and Operational Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum allowed headway between consecutive trains | seconds |
| $h_{\max}$ | Maximum allowed headway between consecutive trains | seconds |
| $d_{s}^{\min}$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ | seconds |
| $d_{s}^{\max}$ | Maximum dwell time at station $s$ | seconds |
| $r_{s}^{\min}$ | Minimum running time on segment $(s, s+1)$ | seconds |
| $r_{s}^{\max}$ | Maximum running time on segment $(s, s+1)$ | seconds |
| $Cap_c$ | Passenger capacity of train composition $c$ | passengers |
| $N^{\text{units}}$ | Total number of available train units in the fleet | units |
| $n_c$ | Number of train units composing composition type $c$ | units |
| $T^{\text{cycle}}$ | Minimum turnaround (cycle) time at terminal stations | seconds |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | — |

### 2.2 Passenger Demand Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $\lambda_{s,k}$ | Passenger arrival rate at station $s$ during time interval $k$ | passengers/second |
| $\beta_{s}$ | Passenger alighting fraction at station $s$ (proportion of onboard passengers alighting) | — |
| $\alpha_{s}$ | Passenger boarding fraction at station $s$ (proportion of waiting passengers boarding per train) | — |

**Assumption (A3):** Passenger demand is approximated as a piecewise constant function over time intervals $k \in \mathcal{K}$, consistent with Liu et al. (2023a). The arrival rate $\lambda_{s,k}$ is constant within each interval.

**Assumption (A4):** The alighting fraction $\beta_s$ is a known parameter estimated from historical automatic fare collection (AFC) data.

### 2.3 Cost and Weighting Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $w_1$ | Weight for passenger waiting time cost | — |
| $w_2$ | Weight for operational cost (train units deployed) | — |
| $w_3$ | Weight for timetable deviation penalty | — |
| $c^{\text{unit}}$ | Cost per train unit per time step | monetary/unit |
| $\hat{a}_{i,s}$ | Nominal (target) arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | seconds |
| $\hat{d}_{i,s}$ | Nominal (target) departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | seconds |

### 2.4 Initial Conditions

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}^{0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ at the start of the prediction horizon |
| $d_{i,s}^{0}$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ at the start of the prediction horizon |
| $x_{i,c}^{0}$ | Initial composition assignment of train $i$ (binary, 1 if composition $c$) |
| $q_{i,s}^{0}$ | Initial passenger load on train $i$ when departing station $s$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Continuous Variables

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | seconds |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ | seconds |
| $w_{s,k}$ | Number of passengers waiting at station $s$ during interval $k$ | passengers |
| $q_{i,s}$ | Passenger load on train $i$ upon departure from station $s$ | passengers |
| $b_{i,s}$ | Number of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ | passengers |
| $e_{i,s}$ | Number of passengers alighting from train $i$ at station $s$ | passengers |
| $\delta_{i,s}^{+}$ | Positive deviation of arrival time from nominal | seconds |
| $\delta_{i,s}^{-}$ | Negative deviation of arrival time from nominal | seconds |
| $\gamma_{i,s}^{+}$ | Positive deviation of departure time from nominal | seconds |
| $\gamma_{i,s}^{-}$ | Negative deviation of departure time from nominal | seconds |

### 3.2 Binary Variables

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,c}$ | 1 if train $i$ is assigned composition type $c$; 0 otherwise |
| $y_{i}$ | 1 if train $i$ is in service during the prediction horizon; 0 otherwise |
| $z_{i,j}$ | 1 if train $i$ departs before train $j$ from the origin station; 0 otherwise |

### 3.3 Integer Variables

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $m_{i}$ | Number of train units assigned to train $i$ (derived from $x_{i,c}$) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective is to minimize a weighted sum of passenger waiting time, operational cost, and timetable deviation:

$$
\min \quad Z = w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} w_{s,k} \cdot \Delta_k}_{Z_1: \text{Passenger waiting cost}} + w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} c^{\text{unit}} \cdot n_c \cdot x_{i,c}}_{Z_2: \text{Operational cost}} + w_3 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \delta_{i,s}^{+} + \delta_{i,s}^{-} + \gamma_{i,s}^{+} + \gamma_{i,s}^{-} \right)}_{Z_3: \text{Timetable deviation penalty}}
$$

where $\Delta_k$ is the duration of time interval $k$ (in seconds).

**Assumption (A5):** The waiting cost $Z_1$ approximates total passenger waiting time by summing the number of waiting passengers at each station over each time interval multiplied by the interval duration. This is a linear approximation consistent with the piecewise-constant demand assumption.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Timetable Constraints

#### 5.1.1 Arrival and Departure Time Relationships

For each train $i \in \mathcal{T}$ and station $s \in \mathcal{S}$:

$$
a_{i,s} = d_{i,s-1} + r_{s-1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \{2, \ldots, S\}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} = a_{i,s} + t_{i,s}^{\text{dwell}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $r_{s-1}$ is the running time on segment $(s-1, s)$ and $t_{i,s}^{\text{dwell}}$ is the dwell time.

#### 5.1.2 Dwell Time Bounds

$$
d_{s}^{\min} \leq d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \leq d_{s}^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

#### 5.1.3 Running Time Bounds

$$
r_{s}^{\min} \leq a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \leq r_{s}^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \{1, \ldots, S-1\}
$$

#### 5.1.4 Headway Constraints

For consecutive trains $i$ and $j$ at station $s$:

$$
d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \geq h_{\min} - M(1 - z_{i,j}), \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \; i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \leq h_{\max} + M(1 - z_{i,j}), \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \; i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
z_{i,j} + z_{j,i} = 1, \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \; i \neq j
$$

#### 5.1.5 Timetable Deviation Linearization

$$
a_{i,s} - \hat{a}_{i,s} = \delta_{i,s}^{+} - \delta_{i,s}^{-}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} - \hat{d}_{i,s} = \gamma_{i,s}^{+} - \gamma_{i,s}^{-}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
\delta_{i,s}^{+}, \delta_{i,s}^{-}, \gamma_{i,s}^{+}, \gamma_{i,s}^{-} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

---

### 5.2 Flexible Train Composition Constraints

#### 5.2.1 Composition Assignment

Each train in service is assigned exactly one composition:

$$
\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} x_{i,c} = y_{i}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

#### 5.2.2 Fleet Size Constraint

The total number of train units used cannot exceed the available fleet:

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} n_c \cdot x_{i,c} \leq N^{\text{units}}
$$

#### 5.2.3 Capacity Constraint

The passenger load on each train cannot exceed its capacity:

$$
q_{i,s} \leq \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} Cap_c \cdot x_{i,c}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Assumption (A6):** The composition of a train is fixed throughout its trip within the prediction horizon (no coupling/uncoupling en route).

---

### 5.3 Passenger Flow Constraints

#### 5.3.1 Passenger Waiting Dynamics

The number of waiting passengers at station $s$ during interval $k$ evolves as:

$$
w_{s,k} = w_{s,k-1} + \lambda_{s,k} \cdot \Delta_k - \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} b_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

where $b_{i,s,k}$ is the number of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ during interval $k$.

**Assumption (A7):** The boarding process is aggregated over each time interval. The number of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ during interval $k$ is proportional to the train's available capacity and the waiting passengers.

#### 5.3.2 Boarding Constraint

The number of boarding passengers is limited by the waiting passengers and the available capacity:

$$
b_{i,s} \leq w_{s,k(i,s)}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
b_{i,s} \leq \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} Cap_c \cdot x_{i,c} - q_{i,s-1} + e_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $k(i,s)$ is the time interval during which train $i$ departs station $s$.

#### 5.3.3 Alighting Constraint

The number of alighting passengers is proportional to the onboard load:

$$
e_{i,s} = \beta_s \cdot q_{i,s-1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \{2, \ldots, S\}
$$

**Assumption (A8):** The alighting fraction $\beta_s$ is deterministic and known from historical data.

#### 5.3.4 Passenger Load Balance

The passenger load on train $i$ upon departure from station $s$ is:

$$
q_{i,s} = q_{i,s-1} - e_{i,s} + b_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

with initial condition:

$$
q_{i,1} = b_{i,1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**Assumption (A9):** All passengers at the origin station board the first available train with sufficient capacity (no passenger choice model).

#### 5.3.5 Non-negativity of Passenger Load

$$
q_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

---

### 5.4 Rolling Stock Circulation Constraints

#### 5.4.1 Turnaround Time Constraint

For a train $i$ that terminates at the last station and is scheduled to return as train $j$:

$$
d_{j,1} - a_{i,S} \geq T^{\text{cycle}} - M(1 - u_{i,j}), \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \; i \neq j
$$

where $u_{i,j}$ is a binary variable indicating that train $i$ connects to train $j$.

**Assumption (A10):** The rolling stock circulation is modeled as a sequence of train trips, where each train unit block is assigned to consecutive trips.

#### 5.4.2 Circulation Balance

Each train trip (except the first and last) has exactly one predecessor and one successor:

$$
\sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}, j \neq i} u_{j,i} = y_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

$$
\sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}, j \neq i} u_{i,j} = y_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

#### 5.4.3 Composition Consistency in Circulation

If train $i$ connects to train $j$, their compositions must be compatible:

$$
x_{i,c} = x_{j,c}, \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T} \text{ with } u_{i,j} = 1, \; \forall c \in \mathcal{C}
$$

This is linearized as:

$$
x_{i,c} - x_{j,c} \leq M(1 - u_{i,j}), \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \; i \neq j, \; c \in \mathcal{C}
$$

$$
x_{j,c} - x_{i,c} \leq M(1 - u_{i,j}), \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \; i \neq j, \; c \in \mathcal{C}
$$

**Assumption (A11):** Train composition remains unchanged during circulation within the prediction horizon. Coupling/uncoupling occurs only at depots.

---

### 5.5 MPC-Specific Constraints

#### 5.5.1 Prediction Horizon Constraints

The decision variables are optimized over the prediction horizon $\mathcal{P}$:

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in [T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}}], \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $T^{\text{start}}$ and $T^{\text{end}}$ define the prediction horizon boundaries.

#### 5.5.2 Initial Condition Coupling

The first train's departure time is linked to the current state:

$$
d_{i,1} \geq d_{i,1}^{0} + t^{\text{min}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

where $t^{\text{min}}$ is the minimum time before the next departure.

#### 5.5.3 Receding Horizon Implementation

At each MPC step $p \in \mathcal{P}$, the optimization problem is solved over the prediction horizon $[p, p+H]$, where $H$ is the horizon length. Only the first control action is implemented, and the problem is re-solved at the next step.

---

### 5.6 Presolve Constraints (Integer Variable Reduction)

#### 5.6.1 Composition Pruning

Based on demand levels, certain compositions are pruned:

$$
x_{i,c} = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; c \in \mathcal{C}^{\text{pruned}}
$$

where $\mathcal{C}^{\text{pruned}} \subseteq \mathcal{C}$ is the set of compositions deemed infeasible or suboptimal based on presolve analysis.

**Assumption (A12):** Presolve techniques (as described in the paper) identify and eliminate a subset of integer variables that are guaranteed to be zero or one in any optimal solution, based on capacity requirements and fleet availability.

#### 5.6.2 Train Activation Pruning

Trains that are not needed based on demand are deactivated:

$$
y_i = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}^{\text{inactive}}
$$

where $\mathcal{T}^{\text{inactive}} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ is determined by presolve analysis.

---

### 5.7 Variable Domain Constraints

$$
x_{i,c} \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; c \in \mathcal{C}
$$

$$
y_i \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

$$
z_{i,j} \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \; i \neq j
$$

$$
u_{i,j} \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \; i \neq j
$$

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
w_{s,k}, q_{i,s}, b_{i,s}, e_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

---

## 6. Complete MILP Formulation Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = w_1 \sum_{s,k} w_{s,k} \Delta_k + w_2 \sum_{i,c} c^{\text{unit}} n_c x_{i,c} + w_3 \sum_{i,s} (\delta_{i,s}^{+} + \delta_{i,s}^{-} + \gamma_{i,s}^{+} + \gamma_{i,s}^{-}) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{Timetable constraints (5.1.1)--(5.1.5)} \\
& \text{Composition constraints (5.2.1)--(5.2.3)} \\
& \text{Passenger flow constraints (5.3.1)--(5.3.5)} \\
& \text{Rolling stock circulation constraints (5.4.1)--(5.4.3)} \\
& \text{MPC constraints (5.5.1)--(5.5.3)} \\
& \text{Presolve constraints (5.6.1)--(5.6.2)} \\
& \text{Variable domains (5.7)}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Model Assumptions Summary

| Assumption | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| A1 | Single-direction line (or each direction modeled separately) |
| A2 | Discrete set of train compositions with known capacities |
| A3 | Piecewise-constant passenger demand over time intervals |
| A4 | Known alighting fractions from historical AFC data |
| A5 | Linear approximation of passenger waiting cost |
| A6 | Fixed train composition throughout the prediction horizon |
| A7 | Aggregated boarding process per time interval |
| A8 | Deterministic alighting fractions |
| A9 | First-available-train boarding policy |
| A10 | Rolling stock circulation as trip sequences |
| A11 | Composition unchanged during circulation within horizon |
| A12 | Presolve techniques eliminate provably suboptimal integer variables |

---

## 8. Learning-Based Solution Framework (Integration)

After presolve, the remaining integer variables $\{x_{i,c}, y_i, z_{i,j}, u_{i,j}\}$ are obtained via LSTM networks trained on historical optimal solutions. With these integer variables fixed, the resulting linear program (LP) in continuous variables $\{a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{s,k}, q_{i,s}, b_{i,s}, e_{i,s}\}$ is solved efficiently at each MPC step, ensuring constraint satisfaction while achieving real-time computational performance.

**Assumption (A13):** The LSTM network is trained offline using optimal solutions from the MILP for various demand scenarios and disturbance realizations. The network predicts integer decisions that are feasible with high probability, and any infeasibility is resolved by a repair heuristic or by solving the MILP with reduced dimensions.

Text:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

The proposed MILP simultaneously determines (i) a conflict-free rescheduled timetable (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) and (ii) executable energy-efficient speed profiles for all trains operating on a high-speed double-track line that suffers a partial segment blockage. During the blockage window, trains in the affected direction are rerouted to the opposite track, which creates bidirectional conflicts that must be resolved.

**Modeling Assumptions** (marked as such):

1. (A1) Time is discretized into intervals of equal duration Δτ.
2. (A2) Space between consecutive stations is partitioned into track edges; each edge is the atomic unit of rerouting.
3. (A3) Train motion on each edge follows a time-driven discretization with piecewise-constant acceleration.
4. (A4) The tractive energy function is approximated by a piecewise-linear function of speed (Davis formula linearization).
5. (A5) All trains travel along the same physical line; bidirectional usage during rerouting is restricted to a single shared track.
6. (A6) Maximum one blockage event with a known time window [H_start, H_end].
7. (A7) Blockage affects one specific edge e* (or a set of consecutive edges E^block).
8. (A8) Cancellation is allowed only when rerouting and retiming together cannot restore feasibility.

---

## 2. Sets, Parameters, and Decision Variables

### 2.1 Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| T | Set of trains, indexed by t, t′ |
| S | Set of stations, indexed by s |
| E | Set of track edges (segments between consecutive stations), indexed by e |
| B | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by b; b = 0,…,|B| |
| R_t | Set of feasible routes for train t, indexed by r (original and rerouted variants) |
| Φ | Set of breakpoints of the piecewise-linear speed-energy curve, indexed by φ |
| O(s) | Ordered set of stations before station s in train t's itinerary |

### 2.2 Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| L_e | Length of edge e | m |
| Δτ | Time interval duration | s |
| V^min, V^max | Minimum/maximum operating speed | m/s |
| A^max, D^max | Maximum acceleration/deceleration | m/s² |
| d_s^min, d_s^max | Minimum/maximum dwell time at station s | s |
| h^min | Minimum safe headway between consecutive same-direction trains | s |
| T^a_{t,s}, T^d_{t,s} | Original scheduled arrival/departure time of train t at s | s |
| [H^start, H^end] | Blockage time window | s |
| E^block ⊆ E | Set of blocked edges | – |
| D_t ∈ {+1, −1} | Nominal running direction of train t | – |
| M | Large positive constant (Big-M) | – |
| P^c_t | Penalty for cancelling train t | – |
| κ_φ, λ_φ | Slope and intercept of segment φ of the linearized energy curve | – |
| v̄_φ | Speed breakpoint φ of the linearized energy curve | m/s |
| w_{t,r,e} | 1 if route r of train t traverses edge e | – |
| σ_{t,r} | 1 if route r of train t uses the opposite track (rerouted) on at least one blocked edge | – |
| α_1, α_2, α_3 | Objective weights for delay, energy, cancellation | – |

### 2.3 Decision Variables

**Timetable (TRP layer):**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| τ^a_{t,s}, τ^d_{t,s} | R≥0 | Actual arrival/departure time of train t at station s |
| δ_{t,s} | R≥0 | Delay of train t at station s |
| x_{t,r} | {0,1} | 1 if train t uses route r |
| y_{t,t′,s} | {0,1} | 1 if train t departs station s before train t′ (for ordering) |
| ζ_t | {0,1} | 1 if train t is cancelled |
| o_{t,e,b} | {0,1} | 1 if train t occupies edge e during interval b |

**Speed profile (TSMP layer):**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| v_{t,e,b} | R≥0 | Speed of train t on edge e at interval b (m/s) |
| a_{t,e,b} | R | Acceleration of train t on edge e at interval b (m/s²) |
| p_{t,e,b} | R≥0 | Position of train t on edge e at interval b (m) |
| ε_{t,e,b} | R≥0 | Instantaneous energy rate of train t on edge e at interval b (kW) |
| E_t | R≥0 | Total energy consumption of train t (kJ) |

**Auxiliary (piecewise-linear energy):**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| f_{t,e,b,φ} | [0,1] | Convex combination weight assigned to breakpoint φ |

---

## 3. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, total energy consumption, and cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha_1 \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_{t,s} \;+\; \alpha_2 \sum_{t \in T} E_t \;+\; \alpha_3 \sum_{t \in T} P^c_t \,\zeta_t
\tag{OBJ}
$$

The total energy of each train is the time-integral of the (linearized) tractive power:

$$
E_t = \sum_{e \in E}\sum_{b \in B} \varepsilon_{t,e,b}\,\Delta\tau \qquad \forall t \in T
\tag{1}
$$

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Delay and Dwell Time

$$
\delta_{t,s} \;\ge\; \tau^{a}_{t,s} - T^{a}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{2}
$$

$$
d^{min}_s \;\le\; \tau^{d}_{t,s} - \tau^{a}_{t,s} \;\le\; d^{max}_s \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{3}
$$

$$
\tau^{a}_{t,s} \;\le\; \tau^{d}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{4}
$$

### 4.2 Route Selection and Cancellation

Each (non-cancelled) train selects exactly one feasible route:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} \;=\; 1 - \zeta_t \qquad \forall t \in T
\tag{5}
$$

Cancellation deactivates all operational variables of a train (big-M relaxation; partial here for compactness):

$$
\tau^{a}_{t,s} \le M(1-\zeta_t),\quad \tau^{d}_{t,s} \le M(1-\zeta_t) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{6}
$$

$$
o_{t,e,b} \le 1-\zeta_t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; e \in E,\; b \in B
\tag{7}
$$

### 4.3 Train Dynamics (Speed Profile Layer)

**Velocity update** (linear, exact):
$$
v_{t,e,b+1} \;=\; v_{t,e,b} + a_{t,e,b}\,\Delta\tau \qquad \forall t \in T,\; e \in E,\; b \in B\setminus\{|B|\}
\tag{8}
$$

**Position update** (linearization of $\tfrac{1}{2}a\Delta\tau^2$ via Big-M with fixed time grid – here we use a first-order approximation; the second-order correction is folded into the speed-velocity term):

$$
p_{t,e,b+1} - p_{t,e,b} \;\ge\; v_{t,e,b}\,\Delta\tau - M\,(1-o_{t,e,b}) \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{9a}
$$

$$
p_{t,e,b+1} - p_{t,e,b} \;\le\; v_{t,e,b}\,\Delta\tau + M\,(1-o_{t,e,b}) \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{9b}
$$

**Bounds:**
$$
V^{min}\,o_{t,e,b} \;\le\; v_{t,e,b} \;\le\; V^{max}\,o_{t,e,b} \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{10}
$$

$$
-D^{max}\,o_{t,e,b} \;\le\; a_{t,e,b} \;\le\; A^{max}\,o_{t,e,b} \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{11}
$$

$$
0 \;\le\; p_{t,e,b} \;\le\; L_e\,o_{t,e,b} \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{12}
$$

### 4.4 Blockage Constraints

For every blocked edge $e \in E^{block}$ and every interval $b$ whose time stamp falls inside the blockage window $[H^{start}, H^{end}]$, no train can occupy the edge:

$$
o_{t,e,b} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; e \in E^{block},\; b \in B:\; b\Delta\tau \in [H^{start}, H^{end}]
\tag{13}
$$

Equivalently, trains in the blocked direction must either reroute, wait, or be cancelled. Rerouting is enforced by routing variables: the chosen route must differ from the original one across blocked edges.

### 4.5 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution (Rerouting on Shared Track)

For every edge $e$ (assumed part of the rerouting corridor) and every interval $b$, two trains travelling in opposite directions cannot occupy the same edge at the same time:

$$
o_{t,e,b} + o_{t',e,b} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall t,t' \in T,\; e \in E,\; b \in B:\; D_t \cdot D_{t'} = -1
\tag{14}
$$

(For edges where bidirectional traffic is physically impossible, the constraint is dropped.)

### 4.6 Same-Direction Headway (Train Order on a Block)

For two same-direction trains $t, t'$ where $t$ is scheduled before $t'$, introduce the ordering variable $\eta_{t,t',e,b} \in \{0,1\}$ equal to 1 when $t$ leads $t'$ on edge $e$ at interval $b$. The headway is enforced through the spatial separation of positions:

$$
p_{t',e,b} - p_{t,e,b} \;\ge\; h^{min}\,V^{min} \cdot \eta_{t,t',e,b} - M\,(2 - o_{t,e,b} - o_{t',e,b})
\tag{15a}
$$

$$
\eta_{t,t',e,b} + \eta_{t',t,e,b} \;=\; o_{t,e,b} \cdot o_{t',e,b} \qquad \forall t\ne t',\;e,b
\tag{15b}
$$

### 4.7 Train Ordering at Stations (Reordering)

For every pair of trains $t,t'$ that both stop at station $s$, exactly one departs first:

$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall t \ne t',\; s \in S
\tag{16}
$$

If $y_{t,t',s}=1$ the headway constraint (15) is extended through station $s$ by adding $d^{min}_s$ to the separation.

### 4.8 Route–Edge Consistency

The occupancy on an edge is allowed only if the edge belongs to the chosen route:

$$
o_{t,e,b} \;\le\; \sum_{r \in R_t:\; w_{t,r,e}=1} x_{t,r} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; e \in E,\; b \in B
\tag{17}
$$

### 4.9 Time Consistency Between Consecutive Stations

The arrival at station $s+1$ must equal the departure at $s$ plus the running time spent on the connecting edge(s), accumulated through the occupancy variables:

$$
\tau^{a}_{t,s+1} \;\ge\; \tau^{d}_{t,s} + \sum_{b \in B} o_{t,e_{s,s+1},b}\,\Delta\tau \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S\setminus\{|S|\}
\tag{18a}
$$

$$
\tau^{a}_{t,s+1} \;\le\; \tau^{d}_{t,s} + \sum_{b \in B} o_{t,e_{s,s+1},b}\,\Delta\tau + M\bigl(1-\sum_{b \in B} o_{t,e_{s,s+1},b}\,\Delta\tau/(|B|\Delta\tau)\bigr)
\tag{18b}
$$

(Equivalent linear forms can be written using auxiliary variables.)

### 4.10 Boundary Conditions

The train enters the first edge at the origin and exits the last edge at length $L_e$:

$$
p_{t,e_1,0} \;=\; 0,\qquad p_{t,e_{|E|},|B|} \;=\; L_{e_{|E|}} \qquad \forall t \in T
\tag{19}
$$

Initial and terminal speeds may be prescribed (e.g., 0 at terminals):

$$
v_{t,e_1,0} \;=\; v^{init}_{t},\qquad v_{t,e_{|E|},|B|} \;=\; v^{term}_{t} \qquad \forall t \in T
\tag{20}
$$

### 4.11 Energy Consumption Linearization

The Davis tractive-effort formula
$$
P(v) \;=\; \kappa_0 + \kappa_1 v + \kappa_2 v^2
$$
is replaced by a piecewise-linear approximation with breakpoints $\bar{v}_\phi$. Introduce convex combination weights $f_{t,e,b,\phi} \ge 0$:

$$
\sum_{\phi \in \Phi} f_{t,e,b,\phi} \;=\; o_{t,e,b} \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{21}
$$

$$
\sum_{\phi \in \Phi} f_{t,e,b,\phi}\,\bar{v}_\phi \;=\; v_{t,e,b} \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{22}
$$

$$
\varepsilon_{t,e,b} \;=\; \sum_{\phi \in \Phi} f_{t,e,b,\phi}\,P(\bar{v}_\phi) \;=\; \sum_{\phi \in \Phi} f_{t,e,b,\phi}\,(\lambda_\phi + \kappa_\phi \bar{v}_\phi) \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{23}
$$

The total energy $E_t$ is then obtained through (1).

### 4.12 Linking the Two Layers (Coupling Constraint)

The integrated nature of the TRSMP is enforced by requiring that the timetable times equal the times implied by the integrated speed profile. Define $\theta_{t,e,b}$ as the cumulative elapsed time when train $t$ finishes interval $b$ on edge $e$:

$$
\theta_{t,e,b} \;=\; \theta_{t,e,b-1} + o_{t,e,b}\,\Delta\tau \qquad \forall t,e,b
\tag{24}
$$

$$
\tau^{d}_{t,s} \;=\; \theta_{t,e_{s-1,s},b^{dep}_{t,s}}, \qquad \tau^{a}_{t,s+1} \;=\; \theta_{t,e_{s,s+1},b^{arr}_{t,s+1}}
\tag{25}
$$

where $b^{dep}_{t,s}$ and $b^{arr}_{t,s}$ are the intervals corresponding to departure from $s$ and arrival at $s+1$. These equations guarantee that the timetable produced by the TRP layer is exactly realized by the speed profile produced by the TSMP layer.

---

## 5. Summary of Model Structure

The complete model $\{OBJ, (1)-(25)\}$ is a mixed-integer linear program whose decisions are:

- **TRP variables** ($x_{t,r}, y_{t,t',s}, \zeta_t, o_{t,e,b}, \tau^a_{t,s}, \tau^d_{t,s}$): determine rerouting, reordering, cancellation, and timing.
- **TSMP variables** ($v_{t,e,b}, a_{t,e,b}, p_{t,e,b}, \varepsilon_{t,e,b}$): determine executable and energy-efficient trajectories.
- **Coupling constraints** (24)–(25): bind the two layers into a single integrated decision.

The objective balances **passenger-service quality** (delay), **operational cost** (energy), and **service robustness** (cancellation penalties) under blockage-induced rerouting. The formulation is provably conflict-free (constraints 13–17) and the resulting speed profiles are dynamically feasible (constraints 8–12), ensuring that any solution is immediately executable by the Automatic Train Protection / Automatic Train Operation subsystems.

---

## 6. Notes on Tractability and Extensions

- **Symmetry breaking:** introduce lexicographic ordering on $(t,s)$ pairs to reduce equivalent permutations.
- **Valid inequalities:** lift the bidirectional conflict constraints with clique inequalities on the conflict graph; strengthen the headway constraints with triangle inequalities among three consecutive trains.
- **Preprocessing:** fix $o_{t,e,b}=0$ for any $(t,e,b)$ for which feasibility is trivially impossible (outside timetable horizon, beyond physical reach given $V^{max}$).
- **Strengthening of the energy term:** the piecewise-linear envelope can be replaced by an outer approximation refined adaptively during the iterative solution procedure.

The resulting MILP is exact for the integrated TRSMP under partial segment blockage, and provides the reference model against which the adaptive iterative decomposition-based algorithm (plan-generation + local branching) of the original paper can be benchmarked.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# A MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

*Model inspired by the RECIFE-MILP framework (Pellegrini et al., 2015), enhanced with speed-profile options and train-/speed-dependent braking distances for ETCS L2 (fixed-block DTG) signalling. Assumptions deviating from or unspecified in the input are explicitly flagged with **[A#]**.*

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of track sections (blocks / TDS), indexed by $s$; ordered along each route |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of routes through the network, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_t \subseteq \mathcal{R}$ | Set of admissible routes for train $t$ **[A1]** |
| $\mathcal{S}_r \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Ordered sequence of sections composing route $r$ |
| $\mathcal{J}$ | Set of junctions (switch areas), indexed by $j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{\text{sw}}_j \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Sections belonging to switch area $j$ (distinguished from plain line, per the paper's switch/plain-line distinction) |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discretised speed levels (speed-profile options), indexed by $k$ **[A2]** |
| $\mathcal{K}_t \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ | Speed levels feasible for train $t$ (rolling-stock / line-speed limits) |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of timetable events (arrivals/departures at stations or boundaries), indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{E}_t \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | Events belonging to train $t$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

**Timetable and infrastructure**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $d_e$ | Scheduled time of event $e$ |
| $L_s$ | Length of section $s$ |
| $v^{\max}_s$ | Line speed limit on section $s$ |
| $v^{\text{sw}}_j$ | Speed limit through switch area $j$ |
| $\delta^{\text{setup}}_{j}$ | Route setup / locking time at junction $j$ |
| $\delta^{\text{clear}}_{j}$ | Route release time at junction $j$ |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |

**Train and braking characteristics**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\ell_t$ | Length of train $t$ |
| $b_t$ | Maximum service braking deceleration of train $t$ (m/s²) |
| $t^{\text{react}}_t$ | Driver + ATP reaction / brake build-up time |
| $m^{\text{safe}}$ | Safety margin distance behind the end of authority **[A3]** |
| $\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{t,e}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $t$ at event $e$ (if a stop) |
| $\tau^{\text{run}}_{t,s,k}$ | Running time of train $t$ over section $s$ at speed level $k$ |
| $B_{t,k}$ | Braking distance of train $t$ when running at speed level $k$ (see Eq. (1)) |
| $c^{\text{delay}}_t$ | Weight (cost) of delay for train $t$ |

**Headway / blocking parameters**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $h^{\text{entry}}_{t,t',k}$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains $t$ (leader) and $t'$ (follower) entering the same section when $t'$ runs at speed level $k$ |
| $h^{\text{exit}}_{t,t'}$ | Minimum headway time between a train leaving and the next train entering the same section |

---

## 3. Derived Quantity: Speed-Dependent Braking Distance

For each train $t$ and speed level $k$ (with corresponding speed $v_k$), the absolute braking distance is

$$
B_{t,k} \;=\; v_k\, t^{\text{react}}_t \;+\; \frac{v_k^{2}}{2\,b_t} \;+\; \ell_t \;+\; m^{\text{safe}}
\tag{1}
$$

**Assumption [A4]:** Constant deceleration during service braking; the reaction term is linearised as $v_k t^{\text{react}}_t$. This is a standard, conservative linearisation of the ETCS braking curve and is the key quantity that makes separation *speed-dependent* under DTG — the brake indication point (IP) lies $B_{t,k}$ upstream of the end of authority (EoA), which is fixed at a TDS boundary.

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Routing and scheduling**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,r}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ is assigned route $r \in \mathcal{R}_t$ |
| $y_{t,k}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses speed level $k \in \mathcal{K}_t$ (speed-profile option) |
| $a_{t,s}$ | continuous | arrival time of train $t$ at the *entry* of section $s$ |
| $d_{t,s}$ | continuous | departure time of train $t$ from the *exit* of section $s$ |
| $\alpha_{t,e}$ | continuous | actual (rescheduled) time of event $e$ |
| $\gamma_{t,e} \ge 0$ | continuous | delay of train $t$ at event $e$ |

**Ordering (conflict resolution)**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $z_{t,t',s}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses section $s$ before train $t'$ |
| $u_{t,t',j}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ traverses junction $j$ before train $t'$ |
| $w_{t,t'}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ is scheduled before train $t'$ at a shared station/boundary |

**Auxiliary**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\beta_{t,s,k}$ | continuous | effective blocking/occupation time of train $t$ on section $s$ at speed level $k$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimise the total weighted delay (the RECIFE-MILP objective, retained):

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_t} c^{\text{delay}}_t \,\cdot\, \gamma_{t,e}
\tag{2}
$$

**[A5]:** Delay is measured against the *original* timetable $d_e$; the model is a delay-minimisation CDR, consistent with the paper's stated objective ("total delay … is minimised").

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route and speed-profile assignment

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t} x_{t,r} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{3}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} y_{t,k} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{4}
$$

**[A6]:** One route and one (representative) speed level per train per resolution horizon; the speed level governs the running times and braking distances used below. If a train changes speed between sections, $y_{t,k}$ can be indexed per section, $y_{t,s,k}$; the linear structure is unchanged.

### 6.2 Section occupancy / running times (speed-profile coupling)

For each train $t$, route $r$, and consecutive sections $s, s^{+}$ in $\mathcal{S}_r$:

$$
d_{t,s} \;\ge\; a_{t,s} \;+\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} \tau^{\text{run}}_{t,s,k}\, y_{t,k} \;-\; M\,(1 - x_{t,r})
\tag{5}
$$

$$
a_{t,s^{+}} \;\ge\; d_{t,s} \;-\; M\,(1 - x_{t,r})
\tag{6}
$$

$$
a_{t,s} \;\ge\; d_{t,s} \;-\; M \quad\text{(non-negativity of occupancy)}
\tag{7}
$$

**[A7]:** Running time $\tau^{\text{run}}_{t,s,k}$ is precomputed per (train, section, speed level) from the speed profile; this is the linear embedding of the "speed profile options" enhancement.

### 6.3 Junction (switch) occupancy — switch vs. plain-line distinction

For every pair of trains $t, t'$ sharing junction $j$:

$$
a_{t',j} \;\ge\; d_{t,j} \;+\; \delta^{\text{clear}}_{j} \;-\; M\,(1 - u_{t,t',j})
\tag{8}
$$

$$
a_{t,j} \;\ge\; d_{t',j} \;+\; \delta^{\text{clear}}_{j} \;-\; M\,u_{t,t',j}
\tag{9}
$$

$$
u_{t,t',j} + u_{t',t,j} = 1
\tag{10}
$$

**[A8]:** Junctions are modelled as single-occupancy resources with setup/release times; this operationalises the paper's "distinction between switches and the rest of the track."

### 6.4 Speed-dependent separation on plain-line sections (DTG core)

For consecutive trains $t$ (leader) and $t'$ (follower) on the same section $s$:

$$
a_{t',s} \;\ge\; a_{t,s} \;+\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_{t'}} h^{\text{entry}}_{t,t',k}\, y_{t',k} \;-\; M\,(1 - z_{t,t',s})
\tag{11}
$$

$$
a_{t,s} \;\ge\; a_{t',s} \;+\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_{t}} h^{\text{entry}}_{t',t,k}\, y_{t,k} \;-\; M\,z_{t,t',s}
\tag{12}
$$

$$
z_{t,t',s} + z_{t',t,s} = 1
\tag{13}
$$

where the DTG headway parameter is derived from the braking distance (1):

$$
h^{\text{entry}}_{t,t',k} \;=\; \frac{B_{t',k}}{v_k} \;+\; \frac{\ell_t}{v_k}
\tag{14}
$$

**Assumption [A9]:** The follower's brake indication point must lie behind the leader's rear (EoA at the TDS boundary); the headway is the time for the follower to traverse its own braking distance plus the leader's length at its current speed. This is the linearised representation of the *speed-dependent brake indication point* — the central DTG enhancement. Because $B_{t',k}$ enters linearly in $y_{t',k}$, the separation constraint remains an MILP.

### 6.5 Blocking-time consistency (linking variable)

$$
\beta_{t,s,k} \;\ge\; \tau^{\text{run}}_{t,s,k} \;+\; \frac{B_{t,k}}{v_k}
\tag{15}
$$

$$
\beta_{t,s,k} \;\le\; \tau^{\text{run}}_{t,s,k} \;+\; \frac{B_{t,k}}{v_k} \;+\; M\,(1 - y_{t,k})
\tag{16}
$$

**[A10]:** $\beta_{t,s,k}$ is an auxiliary "blocking time" that makes the train- and speed-dependent occupancy explicit and can be substituted into (5)/(11) if desired; it is retained here for clarity of the DTG mechanism.

### 6.6 Event times and delay definition

For each event $e \in \mathcal{E}_t$:

$$
\alpha_{t,e} \;\ge\; d_{t,s(e)} \;-\; M\,(1 - x_{t,r(e)})
\tag{17}
$$

$$
\gamma_{t,e} \;\ge\; \alpha_{t,e} \;-\; d_e
\tag{18}
$$

$$
\gamma_{t,e} \;\ge\; 0
\tag{19}
$$

**[A11]:** Only positive (lateness) delay is penalised; early running is permitted but not rewarded, matching standard CDR practice.

### 6.7 Dwell and precedence at shared stations

$$
\alpha_{t,e^{+}} \;\ge\; \alpha_{t,e} \;+\; \tau^{\text{dwell}}_{t,e}
\tag{20}
$$

$$
\alpha_{t',e} \;\ge\; \alpha_{t,e} \;+\; h^{\text{exit}}_{t,t'} \;-\; M\,(1 - w_{t,t'})
\tag{21}
$$

$$
\alpha_{t,e} \;\ge\; \alpha_{t',e} \;+\; h^{\text{exit}}_{t',t} \;-\; M\,w_{t,t'}
\tag{22}
$$

$$
w_{t,t'} + w_{t',t} = 1
\tag{23}
$$

### 6.8 Variable domains

$$
x_{t,r},\, y_{t,k},\, z_{t,t',s},\, u_{t,t',j},\, w_{t,t'} \in \{0,1\}
\tag{24}
$$

$$
a_{t,s},\, d_{t,s},\, \alpha_{t,e},\, \gamma_{t,e},\, \beta_{t,s,k} \;\ge\; 0
\tag{25}
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \;& Z = \sum_{t}\sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_t} c^{\text{delay}}_t\, \gamma_{t,e} \\
\text{s.t.}\;& \text{(3)--(4) route \& speed assignment} \\
& \text{(5)--(7) section running times (speed-profile coupling)} \\
& \text{(8)--(10) junction occupancy (switch vs. plain line)} \\
& \text{(11)--(14) speed-dependent DTG separation} \\
& \text{(15)--(16) blocking-time consistency} \\
& \text{(17)--(19) event times \& delay} \\
& \text{(20)--(23) dwell \& station precedence} \\
& \text{(24)--(25) domains}
\end{aligned}}
$$

---

## 8. Key Modelling Assumptions (Consolidated)

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| **A1** | Each train has a finite, pre-enumerated set of admissible routes (no dynamic route generation). |
| **A2** | Speed profiles are discretised into a finite set $\mathcal{K}$ of representative speed levels; running times and braking distances are precomputed per level. |
| **A3** | A fixed safety margin $m^{\text{safe}}$ is added behind the EoA, consistent with ETCS L2 with TTD. |
| **A4** | Constant service deceleration; braking distance linearised as in Eq. (1). |
| **A5** | Objective is weighted total (lateness) delay vs. the original timetable. |
| **A6** | One route and one speed level per train per resolution horizon (relaxable to per-section). |
| **A7** | Running times are exogenous per (train, section, speed level). |
| **A8** | Junctions are single-occupancy resources with setup/release times. |
| **A9** | DTG separation = follower's braking distance + leader's length, evaluated at the follower's speed level; EoA fixed at TDS boundary. |
| **A10** | Blocking time is an auxiliary linear expression; no additional nonlinearity introduced. |
| **A11** | Only positive delay is penalised. |

**Linearity note:** All products of decision variables are avoided — $y_{t,k}$ multiplies only *parameters* ($\tau^{\text{run}}_{t,s,k}$, $h^{\text{entry}}_{t,t',k}$, $B_{t,k}$), and big-M terms linearise the disjunctions in (5)–(23). The model is therefore a valid MILP, directly integrable into the RECIFE-MILP solution framework, and captures the two DTG-specific enhancements highlighted in the paper: (i) speed-profile options and (ii) train- and speed-dependent braking distances governing brake indication points.
