Text:
# A Complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

### 1.1 Notation

We consider a high-speed railway line divided into **segments** $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{1, 2, \ldots, S\}$, separated by **stations** $n \in \mathcal{N} = \{1, 2, \ldots, S+1\}$. Each segment $s$ connects station $s$ and station $s+1$. The line is **double-track** with a **down-direction track** and an **up-direction track**.

Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the set of affected trains, partitioned as:
- $\mathcal{T}^{d}$: down-direction trains
- $\mathcal{T}^{u}$: up-direction trains

A **disruption** occurs on a set of segments $\mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ during a **disruption time window** $[T^{\text{dis,start}}, T^{\text{dis,end}}]$. During this window, one track (say the down track) on each disrupted segment is unavailable; trains may **reroute** to the opposite track, which then operates **bidirectionally** under stringent conflict-free constraints.

### 1.2 Assumptions (marked as A1–A8)

- **A1.** The disruption time window and affected segments are known a priori.
- **A2.** Each train $i$ has a scheduled departure time $d_i^{\text{orig}}$ from its origin and a scheduled arrival time $a_i^{\text{dest}}$ at its destination; these represent soft targets with penalty for deviation.
- **A3.** The minimum dwell time $\tau_i^{\min}$ and maximum dwell time $\tau_i^{\max}$ at each station are known.
- **A4.** Each train follows one of a finite set of **speed profiles** $\mathcal{P}_i$ on each segment, each characterized by a running time $r_{i,s,p}$ and energy consumption $e_{i,s,p}$. (This discretization is standard for MILP tractability; cf. Howlett et al. 2022.)
- **A5.** Trains can reroute to the opposite track only on disrupted segments during the disruption window.
- **A6.** Headway constraints on the same track are enforced with minimum headway $h^{\min}$ (for both same-direction and opposite-direction train pairs sharing a track).
- **A7.** Trains do not overtake on a segment unless the model explicitly allows order reversal at stations; we permit reordering at stations.
- **A8.** Cancellation is allowed at a high penalty cost $C^{\text{cancel}}_i$.

---

## 2. Decision Variables

### 2.1 Timing Variables (for each train $i \in \mathcal{T}$, station $n \in \mathcal{N}$)
- $a_{i,n} \geq 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $n$
- $d_{i,n} \geq 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $n$
- $w_{i,n} \geq 0$: dwell time of train $i$ at station $n$

### 2.2 Route / Rerouting Variables (for each train $i$, segment $s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}$)
- $y_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses the **opposite track** on disrupted segment $s$; 0 if it uses its **own track**

### 2.3 Speed Profile Selection (for each train $i$, segment $s$, profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$)
- $x_{i,s,p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $s$

### 2.4 Ordering Variables (for each pair $i, j$ on a shared track of segment $s$)
- $\sigma_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ (relative order); $\sigma_{i,j,s} + \sigma_{j,i,s} = 1$

### 2.5 Cancellation
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled

### 2.6 Rerouting Window Indicators (for each train $i$, disrupted segment $s$)
- $u_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $s$ **during** the disruption window

---

## 3. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of **total delay**, **energy consumption**, **cancellation penalty**, and **rerouting cost**:

$$
\min \; Z =
\alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \Big[ (a_{i, \text{dest}(i)} - a_i^{\text{dest}})^+ + (d_{i, \text{orig}(i)} - d_i^{\text{orig}})^+ \Big]
+ \beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} e_{i,s,p} \, x_{i,s,p}
+ \gamma \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} C^{\text{cancel}}_i \, z_i
+ \delta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}} C^{\text{reroute}} \, y_{i,s}
$$

where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are weights (tunable), and $(\cdot)^+ = \max(\cdot, 0)$ is linearized below.

**Linearization of delay terms:** Introduce $D_i^{\text{arr}} \geq a_{i,\text{dest}(i)} - a_i^{\text{dest}}$ and $D_i^{\text{dep}} \geq d_{i,\text{orig}(i)} - d_i^{\text{orig}}$, both $\geq 0$. Then the delay term becomes $\alpha \sum_i (D_i^{\text{arr}} + D_i^{\text{dep}})$.

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Trip Completion and Cancellation
For every train $i$:
$$
d_{i,\text{orig}(i)} \geq d_i^{\text{orig}} (1 - z_i), \quad a_{i,\text{dest}(i)} \geq a_i^{\text{dest}}(1-z_i)
$$
If $z_i = 1$, train $i$'s timing variables are not further constrained (relaxed).

### 4.2 Dwell Time Constraints
For each train $i$ and intermediate station $n$:
$$
w_{i,n} = d_{i,n} - a_{i,n}
$$
$$
\tau_i^{\min}(1-z_i) \leq w_{i,n} \leq \tau_i^{\max}(1-z_i)
$$
$$
a_{i,n} \geq 0, \quad d_{i,n} \geq a_{i,n}
$$

### 4.3 Running Time Constraints
For each train $i$ and segment $s$:
$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_{i,s,p} \, x_{i,s,p}
$$
with
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_{i,s,p} = 1 - z_i
$$

### 4.4 Speed-Profile-to-Route Consistency
If train $i$ reroutes on segment $s$, the chosen speed profile must be compatible with the opposite track (assume set $\mathcal{P}^{\text{opp}}_i \subseteq \mathcal{P}_i$):
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}^{\text{opp}}_i} x_{i,s,p} \geq y_{i,s}, \quad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
$$

### 4.5 Rerouting Feasibility
Only trains traversing segment $s$ during the disruption window may reroute:
$$
u_{i,s} = 1 \iff \big[ d_{i,s}, a_{i,s+1}\big] \cap [T^{\text{dis,start}}, T^{\text{dis,end}}] \neq \emptyset
$$
This is linearized via **big-M** constraints. Let $M$ be a large constant:
$$
d_{i,s} \leq T^{\text{dis,end}} + M(1 - u_{i,s})
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \geq T^{\text{dis,start}} - M(1 - u_{i,s})
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \geq T^{\text{dis,end}} - M\, u_{i,s} - M\, \epsilon_{i,s}^{1}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \leq T^{\text{dis,start}} + M\, u_{i,s} + M\, \epsilon_{i,s}^{2}
$$
where $\epsilon^1, \epsilon^2 \geq 0$ are auxiliary (to enforce the "or" condition; see standard disjunctive linearization). Additionally:
$$
y_{i,s} \leq u_{i,s}, \quad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
$$

### 4.6 Track-Usage and Headway on Shared Segments

On non-disrupted segments, only same-direction headway applies. On disrupted segments, both same-direction and opposite-direction trains may share the opposite track, requiring **bidirectional conflict-free constraints**.

#### 4.6.1 Same-track ordering
For each segment $s$ and train pair $i,j$ sharing a track:
$$
\sigma_{i,j,s} + \sigma_{j,i,s} = 1
$$

#### 4.6.2 Headway constraints (linearized disjunctively)
If train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ (i.e., $\sigma_{i,j,s}=1$), then:
$$
d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h^{\min} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,s})
$$
$$
d_{j,s} \geq d_{i,s} + h^{\min} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,s})
$$
$$
a_{j,s+1} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h^{\min} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,s})
$$
These enforce both departure and arrival headways, and no-overtaking.

#### 4.6.3 Applicability on disrupted segments
For $s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}$, the headway constraints apply **between any two trains using the same physical track**, which requires considering their route choices $y_{i,s}$, $y_{j,s}$. Let same-track indicator be:
$$
\kappa_{i,j,s} = 1 - |y_{i,s} - y_{j,s}|
$$
which is linearized as:
$$
\kappa_{i,j,s} \leq 1 - y_{i,s} + y_{j,s}, \quad \kappa_{i,j,s} \leq 1 + y_{i,s} - y_{j,s}, \quad \kappa_{i,j,s} \geq 1 - y_{i,s} + y_{j,s} + y_{i,s} - y_{j,s} - 1
$$
(i.e., $\kappa_{i,j,s} = 1$ iff $y_{i,s} = y_{j,s}$). Headway disjunction only applies when $\kappa_{i,j,s} = 1$:
$$
d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h^{\min} - M(1-\sigma_{i,j,s}) - M(1-\kappa_{i,j,s})
$$
and similarly for the other two inequalities.

#### 4.6.4 Disruption-window availability
If a train uses its **own track** on segment $s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}$, it must traverse the segment entirely **outside** the disruption window:
$$
a_{i,s+1} \leq T^{\text{dis,start}} + M\, y_{i,s} \quad \text{or} \quad d_{i,s} \geq T^{\text{dis,end}} - M\, y_{i,s}
$$
Linearized via an auxiliary $\eta_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$:
$$
a_{i,s+1} \leq T^{\text{dis,start}} + M(1-\eta_{i,s}) + M y_{i,s}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \geq T^{\text{dis,end}} - M \eta_{i,s} - M y_{i,s}
$$
$$
\eta_{i,s} \geq 1 - y_{i,s} - u_{i,s}
$$

### 4.7 Station Capacity
At most one train occupies a station track at a time (assuming single-track stations; extension straightforward):
For each station $n$ and train pair $i,j$:
$$
a_{j,n} \geq d_{i,n} + h^{\text{station}} - M\,\pi_{i,j,n}
$$
$$
a_{i,n} \geq d_{j,n} + h^{\text{station}} - M(1-\pi_{i,j,n})
$$
with $\pi_{i,j,n} \in \{0,1\}$.

### 4.8 Variable Domains
$$
a_{i,n}, d_{i,n}, w_{i,n} \geq 0
$$
$$
x_{i,s,p}, y_{i,s}, z_i, u_{i,s}, \sigma_{i,j,s}, \kappa_{i,j,s}, \pi_{i,j,n}, \eta_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 5. Complete MILP Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \alpha \sum_i (D_i^{\text{arr}} + D_i^{\text{dep}}) + \beta \sum_{i,s,p} e_{i,s,p} x_{i,s,p} + \gamma \sum_i C^{\text{cancel}}_i z_i + \delta \sum_{i,s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}} C^{\text{reroute}} y_{i,s} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& \text{(4.1) trip/cancellation} \\
& \text{(4.2) dwell time} \\
& \text{(4.3) running time} \\
& \text{(4.4) speed-route consistency} \\
& \text{(4.5) rerouting feasibility (big-M)} \\
& \text{(4.6.1)–(4.6.4) headway \& conflict-free constraints} \\
& \text{(4.7) station capacity} \\
& \text{(4.8) variable domains} \\
& D_i^{\text{arr}} \geq a_{i,\text{dest}(i)} - a_i^{\text{dest}}, \; D_i^{\text{arr}} \geq 0 \\
& D_i^{\text{dep}} \geq d_{i,\text{orig}(i)} - d_i^{\text{orig}}, \; D_i^{\text{dep}} \geq 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 6. Model Properties and Remarks

| Aspect | Treatment |
|---|---|
| **Integrated decisions** | Times, orders, routes, speed profiles, cancellations — all jointly optimized |
| **Bidirectional conflict** | Handled by $\kappa_{i,j,s}$ and $\sigma_{i,j,s}$ on disrupted segments |
| **Rerouting** | Binary $y_{i,s}$ with time-window coupling via $u_{i,s}$ |
| **Energy** | Captured through discrete speed profile choice $x_{i,s,p}$ with cost $e_{i,s,p}$ |
| **Linear** | All constraints are linear; objective is linear after delay linearization |
| **Solvability** | MILP solvable via branch-and-bound; decomposition into IP + train plans (as in paper) accelerates large instances |

### Assumption Notes (per instruction)
- **Speed profile discretization (A4)** is a modelling assumption not explicitly given in the input; it is standard practice in TSMP MILP formulations.
- **Station capacity (4.7)** assumes single-track stations; generalized as needed.
- **Weights** $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are parameters set by the operator; not specified in the source.
- **Non-overtaking (A7)** can be relaxed by removing the third headway inequality (4.6.2).
- **Big-M** values are chosen as the modelling horizon length.

This MILP fully captures the TRSMP as described: conflict-free retiming, reordering, rerouting under partial blockages, and coupled speed-profile selection for energy-efficient, executable recovery timetables.

Text:
# A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations/segments along the line, indexed by $s = 1, \ldots, S$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of speed levels (discrete speed profile segments), indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of disruption-affected segments |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | Set of disruption time windows |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of available routes (tracks/directions), indexed by $r$; $r = 0$ (normal track), $r = 1$ (opposite track for rerouting) |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of feasible speed profiles (plans) for train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of bidirectional conflict zones |

---

## 2. Decision Variables

### 2.1 Train Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,s,r}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $s$ using route $r$; 0 otherwise |
| $y_{i,j,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$; 0 otherwise |
| $z_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled; 0 otherwise |
| $w_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |

### 2.2 Speed Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $v_{i,s,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $s$; 0 otherwise |
| $t^{\text{run}}_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Actual running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $E_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ |

### 2.3 Auxiliary Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\delta^+_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Positive deviation (delay) of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta^-_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Negative deviation (early arrival) of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\alpha_{i,j,s}$ | Binary | Sequencing auxiliary variable for disjunctive constraints |

---

## 3. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted combination of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \quad Z = \underbrace{\lambda_1 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \delta^+_{i,s} + \delta^-_{i,s} \right)}_{\text{Total delay}} + \underbrace{\lambda_2 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} E_{i,s}}_{\text{Energy consumption}} + \underbrace{\lambda_3 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_i}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}}
$$

where $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3 > 0$ are weighting coefficients reflecting operational priorities.

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Timetable Feasibility Constraints

**Arrival-Departure Relationship:**

$$
a_{i,s} = d_{i,s-1} + t^{\text{run}}_{i,s-1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{1\}
$$

**Dwell Time Constraints:**

$$
w_{i,s} = d_{i,s} - a_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
w^{\min}_{i,s} \leq w_{i,s} \leq w^{\max}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Scheduled Time Deviation:**

$$
a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s} = \delta^+_{i,s} - \delta^-_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
\delta^+_{i,s}, \delta^-_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Cancellation Logic:**

$$
a_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $M$ is a sufficiently large constant.

---

### 4.2 Route Selection Constraints

**Unique Route Selection:**

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} x_{i,s,r} = 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Rerouting Only in Disruption Zones:**

$$
x_{i,s,1} = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \notin \mathcal{D}
$$

**Disruption Window Routing Restriction:**

$$
x_{i,s,r} \leq \mathbb{1}\left[ d_{i,s} \notin \mathcal{W} \right] + \mathbb{1}\left[ r = 1 \right], \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{D}
$$

*(Assumption: During the disruption time window, trains must reroute to the opposite track if they traverse the affected segment.)*

---

### 4.3 Speed Profile Constraints

**Speed Level Selection:**

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v_{i,s,k} = 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Running Time as Function of Speed Level:**

$$
t^{\text{run}}_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \tau_{s,k} \cdot v_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $\tau_{s,k}$ is the pre-computed running time on segment $s$ at speed level $k$.

**Running Time Bounds:**

$$
t^{\min}_{i,s} \leq t^{\text{run}}_{i,s} \leq t^{\max}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Energy Consumption:**

$$
E_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} e_{s,k} \cdot v_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $e_{s,k}$ is the pre-computed energy consumption on segment $s$ at speed level $k$.

**Speed Profile Consistency Across Segments (Acceleration/Deceleration Limits):**

$$
\left| \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sigma_k \cdot v_{i,s,k} - \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sigma_k \cdot v_{i,s+1,k} \right| \leq \Delta v^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{S\}
$$

where $\sigma_k$ is the speed value for level $k$ and $\Delta v^{\max}$ is the maximum allowable speed change between consecutive segments.

---

### 4.4 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution Constraints

**Headway Constraints on Shared Track:**

For trains $i, j$ traversing the same segment $s$ on the same route $r$:

$$
d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s} + h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M(2 - x_{i,s,r} - x_{j,s,r}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{S}, \; r \in \mathcal{R}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s} + h^{\min} - M \cdot y_{i,j,s} - M(2 - x_{i,s,r} - x_{j,s,r}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{S}, \; r \in \mathcal{R}
$$

**Sequencing Constraint:**

$$
y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \text{ where conflict is possible}
$$

**Bidirectional Conflict on Opposite Track (Rerouting):**

For trains $i$ (normal direction) and $j$ (opposite direction) both using route $r = 1$:

$$
d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s} + h^{\text{bidi}} - M(1 - \alpha_{i,j,s}) - M(2 - x_{i,s,1} - x_{j,s,1}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{D}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s} + h^{\text{bidi}} - M \cdot \alpha_{i,j,s} - M(2 - x_{i,s,1} - x_{j,s,1}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{D}
$$

where $h^{\text{bidi}}$ is the minimum headway for bidirectional operations on a single track.

---

### 4.5 Disruption Window Constraints

**Trains Cannot Enter Disrupted Segment During Blockage (Unless Rerouting):**

$$
d_{i,s} \geq t^{\text{end}}_w - M(1 - x_{i,s,1}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{D}, \; w \in \mathcal{W}
$$

$$
a_{i,s+1} \leq t^{\text{start}}_w + M(1 - x_{i,s,1}) + M(1 - \beta_{i,s,w}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{D}, \; w \in \mathcal{W}
$$

*(Assumption: If a train uses the normal track ($r=0$) on a disrupted segment, it must traverse entirely outside the disruption window. If rerouting ($r=1$), it may traverse during the window subject to bidirectional headway constraints.)*

---

### 4.6 Station Capacity Constraints

**Platform Occupancy:**

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \mathbb{1}\left[ a_{i,s} \leq t \leq d_{i,s} \right] \leq C_s, \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S}, \; t \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{horizon}}
$$

*(Linearized using time discretization or interval-based formulation.)*

**Track Capacity at Stations:**

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} x_{i,s,r} \leq C^{\text{track}}_{s,r}, \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S}, \; r \in \mathcal{R}
$$

---

### 4.7 Ordering and Precedence Constraints

**Train Order Preservation (if required):**

$$
y_{i,j,s} = y_{i,j,s+1}, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{S\} \text{ (if no overtaking allowed)}
$$

**Overtaking Allowed Only at Stations:**

$$
y_{i,j,s} \neq y_{j,i,s+1} \Rightarrow s \in \mathcal{S}_{\text{station}}, \quad \forall i \neq j
$$

---

### 4.8 Variable Domains

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, t^{\text{run}}_{i,s}, E_{i,s}, \delta^+_{i,s}, \delta^-_{i,s} \geq 0
$$

$$
x_{i,s,r}, y_{i,j,s}, z_i, v_{i,s,k}, \alpha_{i,j,s} \in \{0, 1\}
$$

---

## 5. Assumptions

1. **Discrete Speed Levels:** Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set of speed levels $\mathcal{K}$, with pre-computed running times $\tau_{s,k}$ and energy consumption $e_{s,k}$ for each segment-speed pair. *(Reasonable assumption for MILP tractability.)*

2. **Linear Energy Model:** Energy consumption is linearly related to the selected speed level, ignoring nonlinear resistance effects. *(Simplification for MILP formulation.)*

3. **Fixed Disruption Window:** The disruption time window $[t^{\text{start}}_w, t^{\text{end}}_w]$ is known and fixed. *(Assumption based on problem statement.)*

4. **Single Opposite Track:** Only one opposite track is available for rerouting. *(Assumption based on typical railway infrastructure.)*

5. **No Simultaneous Bidirectional Use:** The opposite track can be used by only one direction at a time, enforced by bidirectional headway constraints. *(Safety assumption.)*

6. **Station Capacity:** Each station has a known platform capacity $C_s$ and track capacity $C^{\text{track}}_{s,r}$. *(Standard assumption.)*

7. **Cancellation Feasibility:** Cancelled trains are removed from all constraints via the binary variable $z_i$. *(Modeling assumption.)*

8. **No Overtaking on Segments:** Trains cannot overtake each other on open track segments; overtaking is only possible at stations. *(Operational assumption.)*

9. **Deterministic Running Times:** Running times $\tau_{s,k}$ are deterministic and known for each speed level. *(Assumption for tractability.)*

10. **Weighting Coefficients:** $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3$ are exogenous parameters reflecting operator priorities. *(Assumption; can be calibrated.)*

---

## 6. Summary

This MILP model integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profile selection, energy consumption) under partial segment blockages. The model ensures:

- Conflict-free timetables with bidirectional train coordination on shared tracks
- Feasible speed profiles consistent with timetable constraints
- Energy-efficient operations through speed level optimization
- Flexibility via rerouting and cancellation decisions

The model is solved using decomposition-based methods (as described in the paper) to handle computational complexity.

# Best Model: MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

I selected **Model 2** as the best formulation because it is the most complete and internally consistent: it explicitly defines the auxiliary variables ($u_{i,b,k}$ for the bilinear term, $q_{i,b,k}$ for $v^2$), provides a clean occupancy-linkage scheme, correctly restricts rerouting to the disruption window, and includes a well-specified bidirectional-conflict constraint. Below is the finalized, self-contained model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description | Index |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Trains | $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Stations | $s$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Track blocks (segments between stations) | $b$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Discretized time intervals (duration $\Delta t$) | $k$ |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | Disrupted blocks | $d$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Breakpoints for piecewise-linear $v^2$ | $p$ |
| $\mathcal{Dir}$ | Directions $\{1=\text{up},\,2=\text{down}\}$ | — |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ [m] |
| $V_{\max}, V_{\min}$ | Speed bounds [m/s] |
| $A_{\max}, D_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration [m/s²] |
| $M$ | Train mass [kg] |
| $R_b$ | Resistance coefficient on block $b$ |
| $\Delta t$ | Time-step duration [s] |
| $H_{\min}$ | Minimum headway [s] |
| $\text{Dwell}_{\min}, \text{Dwell}_{\max}$ | Dwell bounds [s] |
| $\text{Cap}_b$ | Block capacity (trains) |
| $C_{\text{delay}}, C_{\text{energy}}, C_{\text{cancel}}$ | Cost coefficients |
| $\tau_{i,s}^{\text{arr,sched}}, \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dep,sched}}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $o_i, d_i$ | Origin / destination station of train $i$ |
| $\text{dir}_i$ | Direction of train $i$ |
| $\tau_d^{s}, \tau_d^{e}$ | Disruption window start / end on block $d$ |
| $\alpha$ | Aerodynamic drag coefficient |
| $M^{big}$ | Large constant for big-M constraints |
| $\{(\bar v_p, \bar q_p)\}_{p\in\mathcal{P}}$ | PWL breakpoints for $v^2$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary**

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $x_{i,b,k}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ in interval $k$ |
| $y_{i,b,k}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters block $b$ in interval $k$ |
| $z_{i,b,k}$ | 1 if train $i$ exits block $b$ in interval $k$ |
| $o_{i,j,b}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $b$ |
| $r_{i,b}$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes (opposite track) on block $b$ |
| $c_i$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $w_{i,s,k}$ | 1 if train $i$ dwells at station $s$ in interval $k$ |
| $\lambda_{i,b,k,p}$ | PWL weight for segment $p$ of $v^2$ |

**Continuous**

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\tau_{i,s}^{\text{arr}}, \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dep}}$ | Actual arrival / departure times |
| $v_{i,b,k}$ | Speed [m/s] |
| $p_{i,b,k}$ | Position on block [m] |
| $e_{i,b,k}$ | Energy consumption [kWh] |
| $f_{i,b,k}$ | Tractive force [N] |
| $\text{delay}_{i,s}$ | Delay at station $s$ [min] |
| $q_{i,b,k}$ | Auxiliary $= v_{i,b,k}^2$ (PWL) |
| $u_{i,b,k}$ | Auxiliary $= f_{i,b,k}\cdot v_{i,b,k}$ (McCormick) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z = C_{\text{delay}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\text{delay}_{i,s}
\;+\; C_{\text{energy}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} e_{i,b,k}
\;+\; C_{\text{cancel}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} c_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (Linearized Kinematics)

$$
p_{i,b,k+1} = p_{i,b,k} + v_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2}\!\left(\tfrac{f_{i,b,k}}{M} - R_b\right)\Delta t^2
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
v_{i,b,k+1} = v_{i,b,k} + \left(\tfrac{f_{i,b,k}}{M} - R_b\right)\Delta t
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
V_{\min} \le v_{i,b,k} \le V_{\max}
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
-D_{\max}\,M \le f_{i,b,k} \le A_{\max}\,M
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### 5.2 Block Capacity / Conflict-Free

$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} x_{i,b,k} \le \text{Cap}_b
\quad \forall b\in\mathcal{B}\setminus\mathcal{D},\; k
$$

$$
\sum_{i:\text{dir}_i=1} x_{i,b,k} + \sum_{i:\text{dir}_i=2} x_{i,b,k} \le 1
\quad \forall b\in\mathcal{D},\; k
$$

### 5.3 Ordering and Headway

$$
o_{i,j,b} + o_{j,i,b} = 1
\quad \forall i\ne j,\; b
$$

$$
\tau_{j,b}^{\text{entry}} \ge \tau_{i,b}^{\text{entry}} + H_{\min} - M^{big}\big(1 - o_{i,j,b}\big)
\quad \forall i\ne j,\; b
$$

$$
y_{i,b,k} \le x_{i,b,k},\quad z_{i,b,k} \le x_{i,b,k}
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
\sum_{k} y_{i,b,k} = 1 - c_i,\quad \sum_{k} z_{i,b,k} = 1 - c_i
\quad \forall i,b
$$

### 5.4 Rerouting

$$
r_{i,b} \le \mathbb{1}\!\left[b\in\mathcal{D}\right]
\quad \forall i,b
$$

$$
\tau_{i,b}^{\text{entry}} \ge \tau_d^{s} - M^{big}(1 - r_{i,b}),\quad
\tau_{i,b}^{\text{entry}} \le \tau_d^{e} + M^{big}(1 - r_{i,b})
\quad \forall i,\; b=d\in\mathcal{D}
$$

$$
r_{i,b} + r_{j,b} \le 1
\quad \forall i\ne j,\; b\in\mathcal{D},\; \text{dir}_i\ne\text{dir}_j
$$

### 5.5 Disruption Time Window

$$
x_{i,d,k} \le r_{i,d} + \mathbb{1}\!\left[k\Delta t \in [\tau_d^{s},\tau_d^{e}]\right]
\quad \forall i,\; d\in\mathcal{D},\; k
$$

### 5.6 Dwell Time

$$
\text{Dwell}_{\min} \le \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} - \tau_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \le \text{Dwell}_{\max}
\quad \forall i,\; s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{o_i,d_i\}
$$

$$
\tau_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \ge \tau_{i,s-1}^{\text{dep}} + \frac{L_{b(s-1,s)}}{V_{\text{avg}}}
\quad \forall i,\; s
$$

$$
w_{i,s,k} = 1 \iff \tau_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \le k\Delta t \le \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dep}}
\quad\text{(via big-M linear inequalities)}
$$

### 5.7 Delay Calculation

$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge \tau_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} - \tau_{i,s}^{\text{arr,sched}}
\quad \forall i,s
$$

$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge 0
\quad \forall i,s
$$

### 5.8 Cancellation

$$
x_{i,b,k} \le 1 - c_i,\quad y_{i,b,k} \le 1 - c_i,\quad z_{i,b,k} \le 1 - c_i
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
\tau_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \le M^{big}(1 - c_i),\quad
\tau_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} \le M^{big}(1 - c_i)
\quad \forall i,s
$$

### 5.9 Energy Consumption (Linearized)

$$
e_{i,b,k} = \big(u_{i,b,k} + \alpha\, q_{i,b,k}\big)\,\Delta t / 3.6\times 10^{6}
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

**PWL for $q_{i,b,k} \approx v_{i,b,k}^2$:**

$$
v_{i,b,k} = \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \lambda_{i,b,k,p}\,\bar v_p,\quad
q_{i,b,k} = \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \lambda_{i,b,k,p}\,\bar q_p,\quad
\sum_{p}\lambda_{i,b,k,p} = 1,\; \lambda \ge 0
$$

**McCormick envelope for $u_{i,b,k} = f_{i,b,k}\,v_{i,b,k}$:**

$$
u_{i,b,k} \ge f^{\min} v_{i,b,k} + v^{\min} f_{i,b,k} - f^{\min} v^{\min}
$$
$$
u_{i,b,k} \ge f^{\max} v_{i,b,k} + v^{\max} f_{i,b,k} - f^{\max} v^{\max}
$$
$$
u_{i,b,k} \le f^{\max} v_{i,b,k} + v^{\min} f_{i,b,k} - f^{\max} v^{\min}
$$
$$
u_{i,b,k} \le f^{\min} v_{i,b,k} + v^{\max} f_{i,b,k} - f^{\min} v^{\max}
$$

with $f^{\min}=-D_{\max}M$, $f^{\max}=A_{\max}M$, $v^{\min}=V_{\min}$, $v^{\max}=V_{\max}$.

### 5.10 Boundary Conditions

$$
p_{i,b,0} = 0,\quad p_{i,b,|\mathcal{K}|} = L_b
\quad \forall i,b
$$

$$
v_{i,b,0} = v_{i}^{\text{start}},\quad v_{i,b,|\mathcal{K}|} = v_{i}^{\text{end}}
\quad \forall i,b
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

1. **Single-track bidirectional operation during disruption** — disrupted blocks collapse to capacity 1; rerouting uses the opposite track.
2. **Identical kinematic parameters** across trains ($M, A_{\max}, D_{\max}, R_b$).
3. **Disruption affects one direction**; rerouting diverts affected trains to the opposite track within the window.
4. **Uniform time discretization** $\Delta t$ for all dynamics.
5. **No overtaking within blocks** — ordering $o_{i,j,b}$ is fixed per block.
6. **Dwell times bounded**; running time between stations uses average speed to preserve linearity.
7. **Energy** = tractive work ($f\cdot v$) + aerodynamic drag ($\alpha v^2$), both linearized (PWL for $v^2$, McCormick for $f\cdot v$).
8. **Early arrivals are not rewarded** (delay is one-sided, $\ge 0$).
9. **Cancellation** is the most expensive option, used only when no feasible reschedule exists.

---

## 7. Model Size and Solvability

For $|T|$ trains, $|B|$ blocks, $|K|$ intervals, and $|\mathcal{P}|$ PWL segments:
- Binary variables: $O(|T||B||K| + |T|^2|B| + |T||B||K||\mathcal{P}|)$
- Continuous variables: $O(|T||B||K|)$
- Constraints: $O(|T||B||K| + |T|^2|B|)$

This is a large-scale MILP. Practical solution requires decomposition (as proposed in the paper: an IP model for train interactions plus per-train plan selection), an adaptive iterative algorithm with local branching, and commercial solvers (Gurobi/CPLEX) with warm starts.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

Below I formulate a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming model that integrates the Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP) and the Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP) on a double-track high-speed line with bidirectional rerouting during partial segment blockages. The formulation follows directly from the concepts outlined in the introduction (retiming, reordering, rerouting, speed profiles, conflict resolution on shared blocks, energy efficiency) and contains explicit assumptions where the text did not fully specify.

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

The following assumptions are adopted (assumptions are flagged with **[A]**):

- **[A1]** Time is discretized into equal intervals of length Δ (in seconds).
- **[A2]** The line is divided into ordered block sections *b* ∈ B. Each block has length L_b (m) and a unique position along the line.
- **[A3]** The line is a double-track corridor; the normal direction track for each direction is the "home track." During the disruption time window, trains in the affected direction may be rerouted to the opposite (foreign) track within the disrupted segment.
- **[A4]** Trains are point objects but must respect a safety headway H (m), implemented via block-section occupation.
- **[A5]** Speed is discretized into a finite set V = {0, 1, …, v_max} of allowed speed levels (m/s). Acceleration is bounded by a_max (m/s²), braking by b_max (m/s²).
- **[A6]** Each train follows a fixed origin–destination station sequence along the disrupted line (no destination cancellation), but may be short-turned at intermediate stations only as a recovery action modeled via a penalty.
- **[A7]** Energy consumption in interval k for train t is a piecewise-linear function of the chosen tractive effort regime (powering, coasting, braking).
- **[A8]** Dwell times at stations are bounded: d_min ≤ d_{t,i} ≤ d_max.
- **[A9]** A disruption occurs on segment s* during the time window [T^s, T^e]. During this window no train may occupy blocks of segment s* on the home track; rerouting to the foreign track is allowed subject to capacity constraints.
- **[A10]** Bidirectional trains share rerouted blocks only if safety headway constraints are satisfied (modeled as block-occupation exclusivity with reversed position indices).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| T | Set of trains, t ∈ T |
| I | Set of stations, i ∈ I |
| B | Set of block sections, b ∈ B (ordered along the line) |
| B^s | Subset of blocks belonging to the disrupted segment s* |
| K | Set of discrete time steps, k ∈ K = {1, 2, …, |K|} |
| V | Set of discrete speed levels, v ∈ V |
| D(t) | Set of directions (UP/DOWN) for train t |
| R(t) | Ordered set of stations on the route of train t |
| H(t) | Set of upstream neighbor blocks of block b for train t |
| N(b) | Set of blocks immediately adjacent to block b |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| Δ | Duration of a time step | s |
| L_b | Length of block section b | m |
| M_t | Mass of train t | t |
| L_t | Length of train t | m |
| a_max | Maximum acceleration | m/s² |
| b_max | Maximum braking (deceleration) | m/s² |
| v_max | Maximum operating speed | m/s |
| P_max | Maximum traction power | kW |
| c_1, c_2 | Davis resistance coefficients (A + Bv + Cv²) | kN, kN/(m/s), kN/(m/s)² |
| η | Regenerative-braking efficiency | – |
| d_min, d_max | Minimum and maximum dwell time | s |
| h_min | Minimum headway time between successive trains on the same track | s |
| T^s, T^e | Disruption start and end time | s |
| ζ | Turnaround/setup time at stations | s |
| π_delay | Penalty per minute of arrival delay | €/min |
| π_ener | Penalty per kWh of energy consumption | €/kWh |
| π_cancel | Penalty per cancelled/short-turned train | €/train |
| w_v | Penalty weight for speed deviations from nominal cruising | – |
| e_pow, e_coa, e_bra | Energy per second in powering/coasting/braking mode | kW·s |
| M | Large positive constant (big-M) | – |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Train motion and block occupation
- x_{t,b,k} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train t occupies block b at time step k (on its home track), else 0.
- y_{t,b,k} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train t is rerouted through block b at time step k (using the foreign track), else 0.
- z_{t,b,k} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if the *front* of train t enters block b at time step k, else 0.

### 4.2 Timing
- τ_{t,i}^{arr} ≥ 0: Arrival time of train t at station i.
- τ_{t,i}^{dep} ≥ 0: Departure time of train t at station i.
- d_{t,i} ≥ 0: Dwell time of train t at station i.
- δ_t ≥ 0: Arrival delay of train t at its final destination relative to schedule.

### 4.3 Speed and position
- v_{t,k} ≥ 0: Speed of train t at time step k.
- p_{t,k} ≥ 0: Front position of train t at time step k.
- a_{t,k} ∈ ℝ: Acceleration of train t during time step k.

### 4.4 Driving regime
- α_{t,k} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train t is in powering mode at time k.
- β_{t,k} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train t is in coasting mode at time k.
- γ_{t,k} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train t is in braking mode at time k.
- (with α_{t,k} + β_{t,k} + γ_{t,k} = 1).

### 4.5 Energy
- E_{t,k} ≥ 0: Energy consumed (kWh) by train t during time step k.

### 4.6 Rescheduling actions
- c_{t,i} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train t is short-turned (cancelled beyond) station i.
- σ_{t} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train t is cancelled entirely.
- o_{t,t',b,k} ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train t precedes train t' on block b at time k (order variable, used only when both share the block under rerouting).

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of (i) total delay, (ii) total energy consumption, (iii) cancellations/short-turns, and (iv) deviations from nominal cruising speed:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \pi_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t\in T} \delta_t \;+\; \pi_{\text{ener}} \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K} E_{t,k} \;+\; \pi_{\text{cancel}}\!\left(\sum_{t}\sigma_t + \sum_{t,i}c_{t,i}\right) \;+\; \sum_{t,k} w_v\bigl(v_{t,k}-v^{\text{nom}}_t\bigr)^2
$$

**[A]** The last term is linearized via piecewise-linear approximation (omitted here for brevity, can be replaced by Σ w_v · |v_{t,k} − v_t^{nom}| with auxiliary variables).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Kinematic (train dynamics) constraints

**(C1) Speed–position update (linear):**

$$
p_{t,k+1} \;=\; p_{t,k} \;+\; \tfrac{\Delta}{2}\,\bigl(v_{t,k} + v_{t,k+1}\bigr) \quad \forall\, t,k
$$

**(C2) Speed–acceleration update:**

$$
v_{t,k+1} \;=\; v_{t,k} \;+\; a_{t,k}\,\Delta \quad \forall\, t,k
$$

**(C3) Acceleration limits (via driving mode):**

$$
-\,b_{\max} \;\le\; a_{t,k} \;\le\; a_{\max} \quad \forall\, t,k
$$

$$
a_{t,k} \;\le\; a_{\max}\,\alpha_{t,k} \quad \forall\, t,k
$$

$$
a_{t,k} \;\ge\; -\,b_{\max}\,\gamma_{t,k} \quad \forall\, t,k
$$

**(C4) Speed limit per block:**

$$
v_{t,k} \;\le\; v_b^{\max} \;+\; M\bigl(1 - x_{t,b,k} - y_{t,b,k}\bigr) \quad \forall\, t,b,k
$$

### 6.2 Block occupation and conflict resolution

**(C5) Single occupation of a block per time step (on home track):**

$$
\sum_{t\in T} x_{t,b,k} \;\le\; 1 \quad \forall\, b,k
$$

**(C6) Mutual exclusion between home and foreign track in the rerouted segment:**

$$
x_{t,b,k} + y_{t,b,k} \;\le\; 1 \quad \forall\, t,b\in B^{s},k
$$

**(C7) Bidirectional safety headway on shared rerouted blocks:**

For every block b ∈ B^s and time k, at most one train from either direction may use the foreign track:

$$
\sum_{t\in T} y_{t,b,k} \;\le\; 1 \quad \forall\, b\in B^{s},k
$$

**(C8) Sequencing of bidirectional trains on the shared track:**

For any pair (t, t') running in opposite directions on the same rerouted block:

$$
y_{t,b,k} + y_{t',b,k'} \;\le\; 1 \quad \text{whenever the rear of }t\text{ at time }k\text{ overlaps the front of }t'\text{ at time }k'
$$

This is linearized using the order variable o_{t,t',b,k}:

$$
y_{t,b,k} + y_{t',b,k} - 1 \;\le\; o_{t,t',b,k} + o_{t',t,b,k}
$$

$$
o_{t,t',b,k} + o_{t',t,b,k} \;\le\; 1
$$

### 6.3 Disruption constraints

**(C9) Forbidden occupation of disrupted blocks during the disruption window:**

$$
x_{t,b,k} \;=\; 0 \quad \forall\, b\in B^{s},\; k\in K : k\Delta \in [T^{s}, T^{e}],\;\forall t
$$

**(C10) Forced rerouting: trains that must traverse disrupted segment s\* during [T^s, T^e] must use foreign track:**

$$
\sum_{b\in B^{s}} x_{t,b,k} \;\le\; M\bigl(1 - r_{t,k}\bigr) \quad\forall t,k
$$

$$
\sum_{b\in B^{s}} y_{t,b,k} \;\ge\; r_{t,k} \quad\forall t,k
$$

where r_{t,k} ∈ {0,1} indicates that train t must traverse the disrupted segment at time step k.

### 6.4 Train-route continuity

**(C11) Flow conservation between consecutive blocks:**

$$
\sum_{b\in N^+(b')} z_{t,b',k} \;-\; \sum_{b\in N^-(b')} z_{t,b,k} \;=\; x_{t,b',k+1} - x_{t,b',k} \quad\forall t,b',k
$$

**(C12) Block-entry event links to position:**

$$
\sum_{b} L_b\, z_{t,b,k} \;\le\; p_{t,k} \;\le\; \sum_{b} L_b\, z_{t,b,k} + L_{t} \quad \forall t,k
$$

### 6.5 Station timing constraints

**(C13) Dwell time at station i:**

$$
\tau^{dep}_{t,i} - \tau^{arr}_{t,i} \;=\; d_{t,i}, \qquad d_{\min} \le d_{t,i} \le d_{\max}
$$

**(C14) Synchronization with block occupation at station blocks:**

$$
\tau^{arr}_{t,i} \;\le\; k\Delta + M(1 - x_{t,i,k}) \quad \forall t,i,k
$$

$$
\tau^{dep}_{t,i} \;\ge\; k\Delta - M(1 - x_{t,i,k}) \quad \forall t,i,k
$$

**(C15) Final destination delay definition:**

$$
\delta_t \;=\; \tau^{arr}_{t,i_{last}} - a_t^{\text{sch}} - \bigl(M\sigma_t\bigr)
$$

with Mσ_t relaxing the delay if the train is cancelled.

### 6.6 Rescheduling actions

**(C16) Cancellation consistency:**

$$
\sigma_t \;\le\; 1 - x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall b,k
$$

$$
\sum_{i} c_{t,i} \;\le\; 1-\sigma_t \quad \forall t
$$

**(C17) Short-turn position: a short-turned train must leave the main line after station i:**

$$
\sum_{b\in B^{\text{after}}_i} x_{t,b,k} \;\le\; M\bigl(1 - c_{t,i}\bigr)
$$

### 6.7 Driving regime and energy

**(C18) Driving-mode exclusivity:**

$$
\alpha_{t,k} + \beta_{t,k} + \gamma_{t,k} \;=\; 1 \quad \forall t,k
$$

**(C19) Linearized energy balance:**

$$
E_{t,k} \;=\; \Delta\Bigl( e_{\text{pow}}\,\alpha_{t,k} + e_{\text{coa}}\,\beta_{t,k} + e_{\text{bra}}\,\gamma_{t,k} \Bigr) \quad \forall t,k
$$

**(A more accurate, tractive-effort-based variant, **[A]**:**

$$
E_{t,k} \;\ge\; \tfrac{\Delta}{3600}\Bigl( M_t\,a_{t,k}\,v_{t,k} + c_1 + c_2 v_{t,k} + c_3 v_{t,k}^{2} \Bigr) - M\gamma_{t,k}
$$

which is linear in (a_{t,k}, v_{t,k}) after discretization of v_{t,k} into the set V.

### 6.8 Speed–energy consistency

**(C20) Linking cruise speed and tractive mode:**

$$
v_{t,k} \;\le\; v_{\max}\,\alpha_{t,k} + M(\beta_{t,k}+\gamma_{t,k}) \quad \forall t,k
$$

$$
v_{t,k} \;\ge\; v_{\min}\,\alpha_{t,k} \quad \forall t,k
$$

### 6.9 Big-M tightening

**(C21) Bound acceleration/deceleration when stationary:**

$$
v_{t,k} \;\le\; M\,\alpha_{t,k} \quad\forall t,k
$$

---

## 7. Mathematical Statement of the MILP

The complete integrated model for the TRSMP under partial segment blockage is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \pi_{\text{delay}}\!\sum_t \delta_t + \pi_{\text{ener}}\!\sum_{t,k} E_{t,k} + \pi_{\text{cancel}}\!\Bigl(\sum_t \sigma_t + \sum_{t,i} c_{t,i}\Bigr) + \sum_{t,k} w_v\bigl|v_{t,k}-v_t^{\text{nom}}\bigr| \\
\text{s.t.}\quad & (C1)\!-\!(C21),\\
& x_{t,b,k},\, y_{t,b,k},\, z_{t,b,k},\, \alpha_{t,k},\, \beta_{t,k},\, \gamma_{t,k},\, \sigma_t,\, c_{t,i},\, o_{t,t',b,k} \in \{0,1\},\\
& v_{t,k},\, p_{t,k},\, a_{t,k},\, E_{t,k},\, \tau^{arr}_{t,i},\, \tau^{dep}_{t,i},\, d_{t,i},\, \delta_t \ge 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 8. Remarks on the Model

1. **Integrative nature** – Equations (C1)–(C4) couple timing with speed profiles; (C5)–(C8) couple rescheduling (block occupation) with bidirectional traffic; (C9)–(C10) embed the partial blockage; (C13)–(C17) embed retiming, reordering, rerouting, and cancellation; (C18)–(C20) close the loop with energy. Hence TRP and TSMP are jointly optimized, consistent with the contribution claimed in the introduction.

2. **Conflict resolution under bidirectional rerouting** – (C7)–(C8) explicitly forbid simultaneous occupancy and encode train ordering, addressing the "potential conflicts between bidirectional trains sharing the track resources" highlighted in the introduction.

3. **Energy–delay trade-off** – Because (C19)/(C20) couple energy with the driving mode chosen by the optimization, the model captures the trade-off described in the introduction: accelerating earlier vs. decelerating to align with the post-disruption recovery time.

4. **Computational complexity** – The MILP is NP-hard in general; the decomposition into an IP master (train interactions) and per-train plans (kinematic feasibility) described in the introduction can be obtained by projecting onto (x, y, z, o, σ, c) for the master and onto (v, p, a, E, τ) for each sub-plan.

5. **Assumptions flagged with [A]** are needed because the introduction does not fully specify the time/space discretization, the resistance model, or the form of the dwell-time/short-turn rules. Any of these can be tightened (e.g., continuous time via SOS2 variables) without changing the overall structure of the formulation.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a disruption (partial segment blockage) occurs on one track of a double-track segment during a specified time window. Affected trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track, creating bidirectional traffic on a shared track. The model integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profiles) to produce a conflict-free timetable and executable speed profiles.

### Assumptions (marked as such)

- **(A1)** The railway line is discretized into a set of stations $S$ and directed segments $E$ between adjacent stations. Each segment has two parallel tracks (directions), except the disrupted segment where one track is partially blocked during the disruption window.
- **(A2)** Train motion is modeled with a discrete-time, discrete-space approximation: each segment is divided into $K$ equal-length intervals (blocks), and time is discretized into unit slots of length $\Delta t$ (e.g., 1 s or 5 s). This is a reasonable simplification for MILP tractability.
- **(A3)** Speed profiles are represented by piecewise-constant acceleration/deceleration over intervals; energy consumption is proportional to the square of speed (or to traction force times distance), linearized via a convex piecewise-linear approximation.
- **(A4)** Dwell times at stations are decision variables bounded by minimum and maximum values.
- **(A5)** The disruption window $[T^{\text{dis}}_e, \bar{T}^{\text{dis}}_e]$ on segment $e$ blocks one track; trains may use the opposite track during this window (rerouting), subject to bidirectional conflict constraints.
- **(A6)** Headway constraints apply between consecutive trains on the same track (minimum headway $h^{\min}$).
- **(A7)** Train cancellation is allowed with a penalty cost.
- **(A8)** All parameters (travel times, energy coefficients, headways) are deterministic and known.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $E \subseteq S \times S$ | Set of directed segments, indexed by $e = (s, s')$ |
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $K$ | Set of position intervals within a segment, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of time slots, indexed by $t$ |
| $D$ | Set of disruption-affected segments, $D \subseteq E$ |
| $\mathcal{O}_i$ | Set of ordered station visits for train $i$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses segment $e$ (routing) |
| $y_{i,j,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$ |
| $z_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $w_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $v_{i,e,k}$ | Continuous | Speed of train $i$ in interval $k$ of segment $e$ |
| $u_{i,e,k}$ | Continuous | Control (acceleration/deceleration) of train $i$ in interval $k$ of segment $e$ |
| $\tau_{i,e,k}$ | Continuous | Time at which train $i$ enters interval $k$ of segment $e$ |
| $\delta_{i,e,k}$ | Continuous | Traversal time of train $i$ in interval $k$ of segment $e$ |
| $p_{i,e,k}$ | Continuous | Traction power of train $i$ in interval $k$ of segment $e$ |
| $\alpha_{i,e,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is in interval $k$ of segment $e$ during disruption window |

### 3.3 Auxiliary Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\theta_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $\phi_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $\sigma_{i,j,e}$ | Binary | 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ conflict on segment $e$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalty:

$$
\min \quad Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( \beta^{\text{arr}} \max(0, a_{i,s} - \bar{a}_{i,s}) + \beta^{\text{dep}} \max(0, d_{i,s} - \bar{d}_{i,s}) \right)}_{\text{total delay}}
+ \underbrace{\beta^{\text{eng}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{e \in E} \phi_{i,e}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{\beta^{\text{can}} \sum_{i \in T} z_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
$$

where $\bar{a}_{i,s}, \bar{d}_{i,s}$ are scheduled (nominal) arrival and departure times, and $\beta^{\text{arr}}, \beta^{\text{dep}}, \beta^{\text{eng}}, \beta^{\text{can}} \geq 0$ are weights.

**Linearization of delay:** Introduce auxiliary variables $a^+_{i,s} \geq 0$, $d^+_{i,s} \geq 0$ with:
$$
a^+_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - \bar{a}_{i,s}, \quad a^+_{i,s} \geq 0
$$
$$
d^+_{i,s} \geq d_{i,s} - \bar{d}_{i,s}, \quad d^+_{i,s} \geq 0
$$

Then the objective becomes:
$$
\min \quad Z = \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( \beta^{\text{arr}} a^+_{i,s} + \beta^{\text{dep}} d^+_{i,s} \right) + \beta^{\text{eng}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{e \in E} \phi_{i,e} + \beta^{\text{can}} \sum_{i \in T} z_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Constraints

**(C1) Arrival–departure relationship at stations:**
$$
d_{i,s} = a_{i,s} + w_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, s \in \mathcal{O}_i
$$

**(C2) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
w^{\min}_{i,s} \leq w_{i,s} \leq w^{\max}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, s \in \mathcal{O}_i
$$

**(C3) Segment running time:**
$$
a_{i,s'} = d_{i,s} + \theta_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e = (s, s') \in E
$$

**(C4) Running time bounds:**
$$
\theta^{\min}_{i,e} \leq \theta_{i,e} \leq \theta^{\max}_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E
$$

**(C5) Cancellation linking:**
$$
a_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad d_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in T, \, s \in \mathcal{O}_i
$$
where $M$ is a sufficiently large constant.

### 5.2 Routing and Rerouting Constraints

**(C6) Segment usage:**
$$
x_{i,e} \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E
$$

**(C7) Path continuity:**
$$
\sum_{e \in \text{Out}(s)} x_{i,e} - \sum_{e \in \text{In}(s)} x_{i,e} = 
\begin{cases}
1 - z_i, & \text{if } s = \text{origin}(i) \\
-(1 - z_i), & \text{if } s = \text{destination}(i) \\
0, & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$

**(C8) Rerouting on disrupted segment:**
For $e \in D$, train $i$ may use the opposite track:
$$
x_{i,e} + x_{i,e^{\text{opp}}} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in D
$$
where $e^{\text{opp}}$ is the opposite-direction segment. (This ensures a train uses at most one track per segment.)

**(C9) Disruption window compatibility:**
$$
\alpha_{i,e,k} \geq x_{i,e} \cdot \mathbb{1}\left[ \tau_{i,e,k} \in [T^{\text{dis}}_e, \bar{T}^{\text{dis}}_e] \right], \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in D, \, k \in K
$$
(Linearized via big-M:)
$$
\tau_{i,e,k} \leq \bar{T}^{\text{dis}}_e + M(1 - \alpha_{i,e,k}), \quad \tau_{i,e,k} \geq T^{\text{dis}}_e - M(1 - \alpha_{i,e,k})
$$

### 5.3 Conflict-Free Constraints (Bidirectional Traffic)

**(C10) Ordering on shared track:**
For any two trains $i, j$ using the same segment $e$ (possibly in opposite directions):
$$
y_{i,j,e} + y_{j,i,e} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \, e \in E \text{ where both use } e
$$

**(C11) Headway constraints:**
$$
d_{j,s} \geq d_{i,s} + h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \, e = (s, s') \in E
$$
$$
a_{j,s'} \geq a_{i,s'} + h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \, e = (s, s') \in E
$$

**(C12) Bidirectional conflict on shared track (rerouting):**
For $e \in D$ where both directions share a track:
$$
\tau_{j,e,k} \geq \tau_{i,e,k} + \delta_{i,e,k} + h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \, k \in K
$$

### 5.4 Speed Management Constraints

**(C13) Speed dynamics:**
$$
v_{i,e,k+1} = v_{i,e,k} + u_{i,e,k} \Delta t, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E, \, k \in K
$$

**(C14) Speed bounds:**
$$
0 \leq v_{i,e,k} \leq v^{\max}_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E, \, k \in K
$$

**(C15) Traversal time:**
$$
\delta_{i,e,k} = \frac{L_e / K}{v_{i,e,k} + \epsilon}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E, \, k \in K
$$
where $L_e$ is the length of segment $e$, and $\epsilon > 0$ is a small constant. (Linearized via piecewise-linear approximation.)

**(C16) Time propagation:**
$$
\tau_{i,e,k+1} = \tau_{i,e,k} + \delta_{i,e,k}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E, \, k \in K
$$

**(C17) Segment running time consistency:**
$$
\theta_{i,e} = \sum_{k \in K} \delta_{i,e,k}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E
$$

**(C18) Entry time consistency:**
$$
\tau_{i,e,1} = d_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e = (s, s') \in E
$$

**(C19) Exit time consistency:**
$$
a_{i,s'} = \tau_{i,e,K} + \delta_{i,e,K}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e = (s, s') \in E
$$

**(C20) Acceleration bounds:**
$$
u^{\min} \leq u_{i,e,k} \leq u^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E, \, k \in K
$$

### 5.5 Energy Consumption Constraints

**(C21) Traction power:**
$$
p_{i,e,k} \geq \gamma_1 v_{i,e,k} + \gamma_2 v_{i,e,k}^2, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E, \, k \in K
$$
(Linearized via piecewise-linear convex approximation.)

**(C22) Energy consumption:**
$$
\phi_{i,e} = \sum_{k \in K} p_{i,e,k} \delta_{i,e,k}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in E
$$
(Linearized via McCormick relaxation or piecewise-linear approximation.)

### 5.6 Disruption Constraints

**(C23) Disruption window blocking:**
For $e \in D$, during $[T^{\text{dis}}_e, \bar{T}^{\text{dis}}_e]$, at most one train may occupy the blocked track:
$$
\sum_{i \in T} \alpha_{i,e,k} \leq 1, \quad \forall e \in D, \, k \in K
$$

**(C24) Rerouting feasibility:**
$$
\alpha_{i,e,k} \leq x_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in T, \, e \in D, \, k \in K
$$

### 5.7 Variable Domains

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, \theta_{i,e}, \phi_{i,e}, v_{i,e,k}, u_{i,e,k}, \tau_{i,e,k}, \delta_{i,e,k}, p_{i,e,k} \geq 0
$$
$$
x_{i,e}, y_{i,j,e}, z_i, \alpha_{i,e,k}, \sigma_{i,j,e} \in \{0, 1\}
$$

---

## 6. Complete MILP Formulation

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( \beta^{\text{arr}} a^+_{i,s} + \beta^{\text{dep}} d^+_{i,s} \right) + \beta^{\text{eng}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{e \in E} \phi_{i,e} + \beta^{\text{can}} \sum_{i \in T} z_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C24)} \\
& a^+_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - \bar{a}_{i,s}, \quad a^+_{i,s} \geq 0 \\
& d^+_{i,s} \geq d_{i,s} - \bar{d}_{i,s}, \quad d^+_{i,s} \geq 0 \\
& a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, \theta_{i,e}, \phi_{i,e}, v_{i,e,k}, u_{i,e,k}, \tau_{i,e,k}, \delta_{i,e,k}, p_{i,e,k} \geq 0 \\
& x_{i,e}, y_{i,j,e}, z_i, \alpha_{i,e,k}, \sigma_{i,j,e} \in \{0, 1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 7. Summary of Assumptions and Justifications

| Assumption | Justification |
|------------|---------------|
| (A1) Discrete stations and segments | Standard in railway scheduling literature |
| (A2) Discrete-time, discrete-space approximation | Necessary for MILP tractability; common in speed profile optimization |
| (A3) Piecewise-linear energy approximation | Convexity of energy-speed relationship allows accurate linearization |
| (A4) Bounded dwell times | Reflects operational constraints at stations |
| (A5) Disruption window on one track | Models partial segment blockage as described in the problem |
| (A6) Headway constraints | Ensures safety and conflict-free operations |
| (A7) Cancellation allowed | Provides flexibility in disruption recovery |
| (A8) Deterministic parameters | Standard assumption for optimization models |

---

## 8. Model Characteristics

- **Linear**: All constraints are linear (after linearization of delay, energy, and speed-traversal time).
- **Mixed-Integer**: Binary variables for routing, ordering, cancellation, and disruption occupancy.
- **Integrated**: Simultaneously optimizes timetable (times, orders, routes) and speed profiles (speeds, accelerations, energy).
- **Conflict-Free**: Bidirectional conflicts on shared tracks are resolved via ordering and headway constraints.
- **Disruption-Aware**: Explicitly models partial segment blockage and rerouting within the disruption window.

This MILP provides a complete, self-contained formulation for the TRSMP under partial segment blockages, suitable for solution via commercial solvers or decomposition-based algorithms as described in the paper.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Problem Overview

We formulate a mixed-integer linear program for rescheduling trains on a single high-speed railway line when one track of a segment is blocked during a disruption window. The model jointly decides train timings, ordering, rerouting onto the opposite track, and speed levels, minimizing weighted delay, energy, and cancellations.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S$ | Set of stations, $s = 1,\dots,S$ |
| $\text{Seg}(s)$ | Segment between station $s$ and $s+1$, $s = 1,\dots,S-1$ |
| $I$ | Set of trains, $i = 1,\dots,N$ |
| $V$ | Set of speed levels, $v = 1,\dots,V$ |
| $T$ | Time steps, $t = 0,\dots,T$ |
| $I_{\text{dir}}(d)$ | Trains with direction $d \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ |
| $\text{seg\_dis}$ | Index of the disrupted segment |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\text{dep0}[i,s]$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{arr0}[i,s]$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{run\_time}[i,s,v]$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ at speed level $v$ |
| $\text{energy}[i,s,v]$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ at speed level $v$ |
| $\text{dwell\_min},\ \text{dwell\_max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum same-direction headway |
| $h_{\text{opp}}$ | Minimum opposing-direction separation on single track |
| $T_{\text{start}},\ T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window on $\text{seg\_dis}$ |
| $w_{\text{delay}}$ | Weight per unit delay |
| $w_{\text{energy}}$ | Weight per unit energy |
| $w_{\text{cancel}}$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |

---

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $\text{arr}[i,s]$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ (or $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$) | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dep}[i,s]$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ (or $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$) | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x[i,s,v]$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $v$ on segment $s$ |
| $y[i,s]$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to opposite track on segment $s$ (only $s = \text{seg\_dis}$) |
| $z[i,j,s]$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $\text{cancel}[i]$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\text{delay}[i,s]$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min \quad
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S} w_{\text{delay}} \cdot \text{delay}[i,s]}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in \text{Seg}}\sum_{v \in V} w_{\text{energy}} \cdot \text{energy}[i,s,v] \cdot x[i,s,v]}_{\text{total energy consumption}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in I} w_{\text{cancel}} \cdot \text{cancel}[i]}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
$$

---

## Constraints

### C1. Speed Level Selection

Each non-cancelled train selects exactly one speed level per segment:

$$
\sum_{v \in V} x[i,s,v] = 1 - \text{cancel}[i], \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### C2. Running Time Consistency

Arrival at the next station equals departure plus running time:

$$
\text{arr}[i,s+1] - \text{dep}[i,s] = \sum_{v \in V} \text{run\_time}[i,s,v] \cdot x[i,s,v], \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### C3. Dwell Time Bounds

For intermediate stations (not the first or last served station):

$$
\text{dwell\_min} \le \text{dep}[i,s] - \text{arr}[i,s] \le \text{dwell\_max}, \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

### C4. Delay Definition

Delay is the non-negative deviation from schedule:

$$
\text{delay}[i,s] \ge \text{arr}[i,s] - \text{arr0}[i,s], \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

$$
\text{delay}[i,s] \ge \text{dep}[i,s] - \text{dep0}[i,s], \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

$$
\text{delay}[i,s] \ge 0, \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

### C5. Ordering Consistency

For each pair of trains on each segment, exactly one precedes the other:

$$
z[i,j,s] + z[j,i,s] = 1, \qquad \forall i < j,\ \forall s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### C6. Same-Direction Headway

If train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ and they travel in the same direction:

$$
\text{dep}[j,s] - \text{dep}[i,s] \ge h_{\min} - M \cdot (1 - z[i,j,s]), \qquad \forall i \ne j \in I_{\text{dir}}(d),\ \forall s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### C7. Opposing Separation on Single Track (Disrupted Segment)

When both trains use the shared single track on the disrupted segment (i.e., both rerouted or one rerouted and one opposing), enforce minimum separation:

$$
\text{dep}[j,s] - \text{dep}[i,s] \ge h_{\text{opp}} - M \cdot (1 - z[i,j,s]) - M \cdot (2 - y[i,s] - y[j,s]),
\qquad \forall i \ne j,\ s = \text{seg\_dis}
$$

Additionally, when one train is rerouted and the other is on its normal track in the opposite direction, they conflict on the single-track section:

$$
\text{dep}[j,s] - \text{dep}[i,s] \ge h_{\text{opp}} - M \cdot (1 - z[i,j,s]) - M \cdot (1 - y[i,s]),
\qquad \forall i \ne j \text{ with } d_i \ne d_j,\ s = \text{seg\_dis}
$$

### C8. Rerouting Only on Disrupted Segment

$$
y[i,s] = 0, \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in \text{Seg},\ s \ne \text{seg\_dis}
$$

### C9. Disruption Window Logic

If a train enters the disrupted segment during the disruption window, it must be rerouted (or wait until the window ends). This is modeled with a disjunction:

$$
\text{dep}[i,\text{seg\_dis}] \le T_{\text{start}} + M \cdot y[i,\text{seg\_dis}], \qquad \forall i \in I
$$

$$
\text{dep}[i,\text{seg\_dis}] \ge T_{\text{end}} - M \cdot (1 - y[i,\text{seg\_dis}]), \qquad \forall i \in I
$$

**Interpretation:** If $y[i,\text{seg\_dis}] = 0$ (not rerouted), then $\text{dep} \le T_{\text{start}}$ (must depart before window) or $\text{dep} \ge T_{\text{end}}$ (must wait until window ends). If $y[i,\text{seg\_dis}] = 1$ (rerouted), the train may depart during the window.

### C10. Cancellation Constraints

If a train is cancelled, its arrival/departure times are fixed to scheduled values (or effectively removed):

$$
\text{arr}[i,s] \le M \cdot (1 - \text{cancel}[i]) + \text{arr0}[i,s], \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

$$
\text{dep}[i,s] \le M \cdot (1 - \text{cancel}[i]) + \text{dep0}[i,s], \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

$$
\text{arr}[i,s] \ge \text{arr0}[i,s] - M \cdot \text{cancel}[i], \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

$$
\text{dep}[i,s] \ge \text{dep0}[i,s] - M \cdot \text{cancel}[i], \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

### C11. Non-Overtaking Within a Segment

Ordering is fixed at segment entry (implied by C5 and C6; no additional constraint needed since $z$ is defined per segment).

### C12. Variable Domains

$$
\text{arr}[i,s],\ \text{dep}[i,s],\ \text{delay}[i,s] \ge 0, \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S
$$

$$
x[i,s,v] \in \{0,1\}, \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in \text{Seg},\ \forall v \in V
$$

$$
y[i,s] \in \{0,1\}, \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
z[i,j,s] \in \{0,1\}, \qquad \forall i \ne j \in I,\ \forall s \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
\text{cancel}[i] \in \{0,1\}, \qquad \forall i \in I
$$

---

## Explanation of Model Elements

### Decision Variables

- **Timing variables** ($\text{arr}$, $\text{dep}$): Continuous (or integer under A1) variables representing actual arrival and departure times. These are the primary rescheduling decisions.
- **Speed level selection** ($x$): Binary variables that select one of $V$ discrete speed profiles per segment. Each speed level has an associated running time and energy consumption, capturing the trade-off between speed and energy.
- **Rerouting** ($y$): Binary variables indicating whether a train uses the opposite track on the disrupted segment. Only relevant for $\text{seg\_dis}$.
- **Ordering** ($z$): Binary variables establishing the sequence of trains on each segment. This is critical for enforcing headway constraints and preventing conflicts.
- **Cancellation** ($\text{cancel}$): Binary variables allowing trains to be cancelled when no feasible schedule exists, with a large penalty.
- **Delay** ($\text{delay}$): Non-negative variables measuring deviation from schedule, used in the objective.

### Objective Function

The objective balances three competing goals:
1. **Delay minimization**: Penalizes deviations from the planned timetable, weighted by $w_{\text{delay}}$.
2. **Energy minimization**: Penalizes energy consumption, weighted by $w_{\text{energy}}$. Higher speed levels consume more energy but reduce running time.
3. **Cancellation penalty**: Discourages cancelling trains, weighted by $w_{\text{cancel}}$.

### Key Constraints

- **C1–C2**: Link speed level choices to actual running times, ensuring consistency between the discrete speed profile and the continuous timetable.
- **C3**: Enforce realistic dwell times at stations.
- **C4**: Define delay as the maximum of arrival and departure deviations.
- **C5–C7**: Handle train ordering and safety separation. C6 enforces same-direction headway; C7 enforces opposing separation on the single-track section, which is the critical constraint during the disruption.
- **C8–C9**: Restrict rerouting to the disrupted segment and enforce that trains entering during the disruption window must either be rerouted or wait until the window ends.
- **C10**: Handle cancellations by fixing times to scheduled values when a train is cancelled.

### Assumptions Embedded in the Model

- **A1 (Discretized time)**: Times are treated as continuous in the formulation but can be restricted to integers by adding integrality constraints.
- **A2 (Discretized speed)**: Speed levels are discrete, with precomputed running times and energy values.
- **A3 (No overtaking)**: Enforced by the ordering variables $z$ and headway constraints.
- **A4 (Headway)**: Same-direction headway $h_{\min}$ and opposing separation $h_{\text{opp}}$ are enforced via big-M constraints.
- **A5 (Dwell bounds)**: Enforced in C3.

Text:
# MILP Model for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming formulation that extends the RECIFE-MILP architecture with DTG-specific enhancements: (i) discrete speed-profile options, (ii) train- and speed-dependent braking distances, (iii) train- and speed-dependent brake indication points, and (iv) explicit distinction between line arcs and switch arcs.

---

## 1 Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $N$ | Set of nodes (stations, junctions), indexed by $n$ |
| $A = A^L \cup A^S$ | Set of arcs (track sections), $A^L$ = line arcs, $A^S$ = switch arcs |
| $E = E^{arr} \cup E^{dep}$ | Set of events (arrivals / departures), indexed by $e$ |
| $E_t \subseteq E$ | Events belonging to train $t$ |
| $K$ | Set of feasible speed-profile options, indexed by $k$ |
| $R_t$ | Set of feasible routes for train $t$, each $r \subseteq A$; indexed by $r$ |
| $O_t \subseteq A \times A$ | Ordered pairs of consecutive arcs in any route of train $t$ |

---

## 2 Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $d_{t,e}$ | Scheduled (planned) time of event $e \in E_t$ |
| $L_a$ | Length of arc $a \in A$ |
| $v_{t,k}$ | Constant operating speed of train $t$ under profile $k$ |
| $br_{t,k}$ | Braking distance of train $t$ under profile $k$ (speed-dependent) |
| $rt_{t,a,k} = L_a / v_{t,k}$ | Running time of train $t$ on arc $a$ under profile $k$ |
| $\tau^{min}$ | Minimum dwell time at stations |
| $\tau^{hd}$ | Minimum station headway between consecutive trains |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $\varepsilon$ | Small positive constant (numerical tolerance) |

**Assumption A1.** Each train has a finite, predefined set of speed profiles (e.g., nominal, reduced, recovery). Each profile $k$ yields a constant cruise speed $v_{t,k}$ and a corresponding braking distance $br_{t,k}$ computed from the standard kinematic equation $br = v^2/(2a_{dec})$ with a constant deceleration $a_{dec}$.

---

## 3 Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,e}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual time of event $e \in E_t$ for train $t$ |
| $\delta_{t,e}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Delay of event $e$ for train $t$ |
| $y_{t,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $k$ |
| $w_{t,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in R_t$ |
| $u_{t,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses arc $a$ |
| $s_{t,a}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Time train $t$ enters arc $a$ |
| $f_{t,a}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Time train $t$ exits arc $a$ |
| $z_{t,t',a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses arc $a$ before train $t'$ (for $t \ne t'$) |
| $\sigma_{t,t',a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ occupies switch $a \in A^S$ before train $t'$ |

---

## 4 Objective Function

Minimise the total delay across all trains and events:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{e \in E_t} \delta_{t,e}
$$

**Assumption A2.** Total delay is the primary performance metric. Secondary criteria (e.g., number of retimed/reordered trains, energy) can be added as weighted terms without loss of generality.

---

## 5 Constraints

### 5.1 Delay definition
$$
x_{t,e} - d_{t,e} = \delta_{t,e} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; e \in E_t \tag{C1}
$$
$$
\delta_{t,e} \ge 0 \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; e \in E_t \tag{C2}
$$

### 5.2 Speed-profile selection (DTG enhancement)
Each train selects exactly one speed profile:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} y_{t,k} = 1 \qquad \forall\, t \in T \tag{C3}
$$

### 5.3 Route selection (rerouting decision)
$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} w_{t,r} = 1 \qquad \forall\, t \in T \tag{C4}
$$

### 5.4 Arc usage linked to route choice
$$
u_{t,a} \le \sum_{r \in R_t :\, a \in r} w_{t,r} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; a \in A \tag{C5}
$$
$$
u_{t,a} \ge w_{t,r} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; r \in R_t,\; a \in r \tag{C6}
$$

### 5.5 Running time on each arc (linearised with big-M)
$$
f_{t,a} - s_{t,a} \;\ge\; \sum_{k \in K} rt_{t,a,k}\, y_{t,k} \;-\; M(1 - u_{t,a}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; a \in A \tag{C7}
$$
$$
f_{t,a} - s_{t,a} \;\le\; \sum_{k \in K} rt_{t,a,k}\, y_{t,k} \;+\; M(1 - u_{t,a}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; a \in A \tag{C8}
$$

### 5.6 Movement continuity on consecutive arcs
For every pair $(a, a') \in O_t$ of consecutive arcs in any route of train $t$:
$$
s_{t,a'} \;\ge\; f_{t,a} \;-\; M(2 - u_{t,a} - u_{t,a'}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; (a,a') \in O_t \tag{C9}
$$
$$
s_{t,a'} \;\le\; f_{t,a} \;+\; M(2 - u_{t,a} - u_{t,a'}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; (a,a') \in O_t \tag{C10}
$$

### 5.7 Event-to-arc linking
Let $a^{in}_{t,e}$ and $a^{out}_{t,e}$ denote the entry/exit arcs associated with event $e$:
$$
x_{t,e^{arr}} \;\ge\; f_{t,a^{in}_{t,e}} \;-\; M(1 - u_{t,a^{in}_{t,e}}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; e^{arr} \in E_t \tag{C11}
$$
$$
x_{t,e^{arr}} \;\le\; f_{t,a^{in}_{t,e}} \;+\; M(1 - u_{t,a^{in}_{t,e}}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; e^{arr} \in E_t \tag{C12}
$$
$$
x_{t,e^{dep}} \;\ge\; s_{t,a^{out}_{t,e}} \;-\; M(1 - u_{t,a^{out}_{t,e}}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; e^{dep} \in E_t \tag{C13}
$$
$$
x_{t,e^{dep}} \;\le\; s_{t,a^{out}_{t,e}} \;+\; M(1 - u_{t,a^{out}_{t,e}}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; e^{dep} \in E_t \tag{C14}
$$

### 5.8 Minimum dwell time at stations
$$
x_{t,e^{dep}} - x_{t,e^{arr}} \;\ge\; \tau^{min} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; (e^{arr}, e^{dep}) \text{ at same node} \tag{C15}
$$

### 5.9 Station headway (minimum time separation between trains at the same node)
$$
x_{t',e'} - x_{t,e} \;\ge\; \tau^{hd} \;-\; M(1 - \pi_{t,t',e,e'}) \qquad \forall\, t \ne t',\; (e,e') \text{ at same node} \tag{C16}
$$
where $\pi_{t,t',e,e'} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates the temporal ordering of the two events.

### 5.10 Train separation on line arcs (DTG core enhancement)
For each pair of distinct trains $t, t'$ and each line arc $a \in A^L$:

$$
z_{t,t',a} + z_{t',t,a} \;\ge\; u_{t,a} + u_{t',a} - 1 \qquad \forall\, t \ne t',\; a \in A^L \tag{C17}
$$
$$
z_{t,t',a} + z_{t',t,a} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall\, t \ne t',\; a \in A^L \tag{C18}
$$

If train $t'$ follows train $t$ on arc $a$, the entry of $t'$ must occur after $t$ has cleared the arc by at least the speed-dependent braking distance of $t'$:

$$
s_{t',a} \;\ge\; f_{t,a} \;+\; \sum_{k \in K} br_{t',k}\, y_{t',k} \;-\; M(1 - z_{t,t',a}) \qquad \forall\, t \ne t',\; a \in A^L \tag{C19}
$$

**Interpretation.** The minimum separation between two consecutive trains on a line arc equals the speed-dependent braking distance of the *following* train. This replaces the fixed-block headway (a multiple of block lengths) used in conventional signalling.

### 5.11 Switch mutual exclusion
For each switch $a \in A^S$ and each pair of distinct trains $t, t'$ using it:
$$
s_{t',a} \;\ge\; f_{t,a} \;-\; M(1 - \sigma_{t,t',a}) \qquad \forall\, t \ne t',\; a \in A^S \tag{C20}
$$
$$
s_{t,a} \;\ge\; f_{t',a} \;-\; M\, \sigma_{t,t',a} \qquad \forall\, t \ne t',\; a \in A^S \tag{C21}
$$
$$
\sigma_{t,t',a} + \sigma_{t',t,a} = 1 \qquad \forall\, t \ne t',\; a \in A^S \tag{C22}
$$

**Interpretation.** Switches are treated as single-track bottlenecks: at most one train can occupy a switch at any given time, regardless of speed profile.

### 5.12 Brake indication point consistency (DTG enhancement)
The brake indication point of train $t$ on arc $a$ is located at distance $br_{t,k}$ before the End of Authority (EoA), which coincides with the exit of arc $a$. Let $bip_{t,a}$ denote the time at which the brake indication point of train $t$ crosses the entry of arc $a$:

$$
bip_{t,a} \;\ge\; s_{t,a} \;-\; \sum_{k \in K} br_{t,k}\, y_{t,k} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; a \in A \tag{C23}
$$
$$
bip_{t,a} \;\le\; s_{t,a} \;-\; \sum_{k \in K} br_{t,k}\, y_{t,k} \;+\; M(1 - u_{t,a}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; a \in A \tag{C24}
$$

The blocking time of arc $a$ by train $t$ starts when the brake indication point enters the arc and ends when the train exits:

$$
b^{start}_{t,a} = bip_{t,a}, \qquad b^{end}_{t,a} = f_{t,a} \tag{C25}
$$

These blocking times are used implicitly through (C19) and (C20)–(C22) to enforce that no conflicting movement is authorised while a preceding train's brake indication profile still protects the section.

### 5.13 Non-negativity and binary declarations
$$
x_{t,e},\; s_{t,a},\; f_{t,a},\; bip_{t,a} \;\ge\; 0 \tag{C26}
$$
$$
\delta_{t,e} \;\ge\; 0 \tag{C27}
$$
$$
y_{t,k},\; w_{t,r},\; u_{t,a},\; z_{t,t',a},\; \sigma_{t,t',a},\; \pi_{t,t',e,e'} \;\in\; \{0,1\} \tag{C28}
$$

---

## 6 Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{e \in E_t} \delta_{t,e} \\
\text{s.t. } & \text{(C1)–(C28).}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7 Key Modelling Assumptions

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Each train has a finite, predefined set of speed profiles; braking distance is computed from a constant deceleration. |
| A2 | Total delay is the sole objective; secondary criteria can be incorporated additively. |
| A3 | Trains move at constant cruise speed within each arc (no in-arc acceleration/deceleration phase). |
| A4 | The End of Authority (EoA) coincides with the exit of the occupied arc (i.e., the arc is a Trackside Train Detection Section). |
| A5 | Switches are modelled as exclusive single-track resources; line arcs allow speed-dependent following distances. |
| A6 | Dwell times and station headways are fixed parameters; only event times are decision variables. |
| A7 | The set of feasible routes $R_t$ is finite and pre-enumerated (typical for junction-level CDR). |
| A8 | Big-M constants are chosen tight enough to avoid weak relaxations (e.g., $M$ = planning horizon length). |

---

## 8 Remarks on DTG vs. Fixed-Block Equivalence

The conventional fixed-block RECIFE-MILP is recovered by:
- replacing $\sum_k br_{t',k} y_{t',k}$ in (C19) with a fixed multiple of the block length $n_b \cdot L_b$;
- removing (C3), (C7)–(C8), (C23)–(C24) (no speed-profile choice);
- keeping (C20)–(C22) for switches.

This makes the DTG model a strict generalisation and enables direct comparative analysis of rescheduling decisions under the two signalling paradigms.
