Text:
# Complete MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management (rtRTMP)

Based on the provided input, I formulate a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the real-time railway traffic management problem. The model decomposes the problem into rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling sub-problems, following the multi-stage framework described in the paper. I present the **full (global-optimum) model** that integrates all three sub-problems, consistent with the reference formulation in Pellegrini et al. (2014) and the extensions described in the contributions.

---

## 1. Assumptions

The following assumptions are made (marked as such where information is missing from the input):

- **A1.** The infrastructure is modeled microscopically: block sections, signals, and routes are represented explicitly.
- **A2.** A set of trains $T$ is given, each with a scheduled path through the network, an entry time, and an exit time.
- **A3.** Each train can be assigned one route from a finite set of feasible routes (rerouting alternatives).
- **A4.** Trains cannot overtake within a block section; ordering decisions occur at stations/junctions (reordering).
- **A5.** Blocking time (occupation) of a block section by a train depends on the train type and route; it is deterministic.
- **A6.** The objective is to minimize total weighted train delays (primary + secondary), consistent with the paper's stated goal.
- **A7.** Safety-relevant overlaps (margins behind stop signals) are considered as additional blocking resources, per Lindenmaier et al. (2022).
- **A8.** The planning horizon is finite and discretized into the set of relevant events (arrivals/departures at block section boundaries).
- **A9.** No stochastic disturbances are modeled; the model is deterministic given the realized primary delays.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $B$ | Set of block sections, indexed by $b$ |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations / junctions, indexed by $s$ |
| $E$ | Set of events (arrival/departure), indexed by $e$ |
| $B(r)$ | Set of block sections belonging to route $r$ |
| $T(b)$ | Set of trains that may use block section $b$ |
| $R_i(b)$ | Set of routes of train $i$ that include block $b$ |
| $O$ | Set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ that may conflict |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $a_i$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at its destination |
| $d_i$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from its origin |
| $\tau_{i,b}$ | Running time of train $i$ on block section $b$ |
| $\sigma_{i,b}$ | Setup/clearance time of train $i$ on block $b$ (including overlap) |
| $w_i$ | Weight (priority) of train $i$ in the objective |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $h$ | Minimum headway (safety separation) between two trains on the same block |
| $\underline{t}_i, \overline{t}_i$ | Earliest and latest feasible event times for train $i$ |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Routing variables
$$
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ r \in R_i
$$
$x_{i,r} = 1$ if train $i$ is assigned route $r$, else $0$.

### 4.2 Ordering variables
$$
y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\ b \in B
$$
$y_{i,j,b} = 1$ if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block section $b$.

### 4.3 Scheduling (timing) variables
$$
t_{i,b}^{\text{in}} \ge 0, \quad t_{i,b}^{\text{out}} \ge 0
$$
Entry and exit time of train $i$ on block section $b$.

### 4.4 Delay variables
$$
\delta_i \ge 0
$$
Total delay of train $i$ at its destination.

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted total delay:

$$
\min \ Z = \sum_{i \in T} w_i \, \delta_i
$$

*(Assumption A6: delay minimization is the primary objective, consistent with the paper. Energy consumption could be added as a secondary term, but the input states delay minimization is the main goal.)*

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route selection (exactly one route per train)

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{1}
$$

### 6.2 Route–block coupling

Train $i$ uses block $b$ only if its selected route contains $b$:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i(b)} x_{i,r} \ge \mathbb{1}[i \text{ uses } b], \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{2}
$$

Auxiliary binary $u_{i,b}$ (train $i$ uses block $b$) satisfies:

$$
u_{i,b} = \sum_{r \in R_i(b)} x_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{2'}
$$

### 6.3 Running time on block sections

$$
t_{i,b}^{\text{out}} \ge t_{i,b}^{\text{in}} + \tau_{i,b} - M(1 - u_{i,b}), \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{3}
$$

### 6.4 Route continuity (flow conservation at nodes)

For consecutive blocks $b_1, b_2$ in route $r$:

$$
t_{i,b_2}^{\text{in}} \ge t_{i,b_1}^{\text{out}} - M(1 - x_{i,r}), \quad \forall i,\ r,\ (b_1,b_2) \in r \tag{4}
$$

### 6.5 Block exclusion (no two trains on the same block simultaneously)

For any pair $(i,j)$ sharing block $b$:

$$
t_{j,b}^{\text{in}} \ge t_{i,b}^{\text{out}} + \sigma_{i,b} - M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \tag{5}
$$

$$
t_{i,b}^{\text{in}} \ge t_{j,b}^{\text{out}} + \sigma_{j,b} - M \, y_{i,j,b} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \tag{6}
$$

### 6.6 Ordering consistency (antisymmetry)

$$
y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1, \quad \forall (i,j) \in O,\ b \in B(i) \cap B(j) \tag{7}
$$

### 6.7 Minimum headway (safety separation)

$$
t_{j,b}^{\text{in}} \ge t_{i,b}^{\text{in}} + h - M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) \tag{8}
$$

### 6.8 Delay definition

$$
\delta_i \ge t_{i,b_{\text{last}}}^{\text{out}} - a_i, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{9}
$$

where $b_{\text{last}}$ is the last block section of the selected route of train $i$.

### 6.9 Time window constraints

$$
\underline{t}_i \le t_{i,b}^{\text{in}} \le \overline{t}_i, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{10}
$$

### 6.10 Safety-relevant overlap constraints (Lindenmaier et al., 2022)

For each stop signal with overlap resource $o$:

$$
t_{j,o}^{\text{in}} \ge t_{i,o}^{\text{out}} + \sigma_{i,o} - M(1 - y_{i,j,o}) \tag{11}
$$

### 6.11 Variable domains

$$
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}, \quad u_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
t_{i,b}^{\text{in}},\ t_{i,b}^{\text{out}},\ \delta_i \ge 0
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{i \in T} w_i \, \delta_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& (1)\ \text{route selection} \\
& (2')\ \text{route–block coupling} \\
& (3)\ \text{running times} \\
& (4)\ \text{route continuity} \\
& (5),(6)\ \text{block exclusion} \\
& (7)\ \text{ordering antisymmetry} \\
& (8)\ \text{minimum headway} \\
& (9)\ \text{delay definition} \\
& (10)\ \text{time windows} \\
& (11)\ \text{overlap safety} \\
& x, y, u \in \{0,1\},\quad t, \delta \ge 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 8. Notes on the Multi-Stage Framework

The paper describes a **two-stage decomposition**:

1. **Stage 1 (Sub-optimal model):** Solve rerouting + reordering using pair-wise delay variables (indicating which train a train waits for), neglecting delay propagation. This yields a fast, sub-optimal route selection $x^*_{i,r}$ and optional ordering $y^*_{i,j,b}$.

2. **Stage 2 (Rescheduling):** Fix $x_{i,r} = x^*_{i,r}$ (and optionally $y_{i,j,b} = y^*_{i,j,b}$), then solve the reduced MILP for timing variables $t$ and delays $\delta$.

3. **Global-optimum extension:** Extend Stage 1 to account for delay propagation, guaranteeing the global optimum of the original rtRTMP (Pellegrini et al., 2014).

The model above represents the **full integrated formulation**; the decomposition is achieved by fixing $x$ and $y$ in Stage 2, which reduces the number of integer variables and thus the computational cost — a key concern given the NP-hardness of the rtRTMP.

---

## 9. Optimality Condition (from Section 3.2)

The sub-optimal model yields the global optimum when:

$$
\delta_i^{\text{pairwise}} = \delta_i^{\text{propagated}}, \quad \forall i \in T
$$

i.e., when no delay propagation occurs between the pair-wise ordering decisions and the actual schedule. This condition is violated when a train's waiting decision causes cascading delays to downstream trains, motivating the extended model in Section 3.3.

# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

I selected **Model 2** as the best formulation for its completeness, explicit handling of the bidirectional conflict coupling (including the same-track detection via $\theta$), and rigorous linearization of all nonlinear elements. Below is the refined, complete linear model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S$ | Set of stations, ordered by position, $s = 1,\dots,|S|$ |
| $E$ | Set of segments, $E = \{(s,s+1) : s = 1,\dots,|S|-1\}$ |
| $K$ | Set of trains, indexed $k, k'$ |
| $F \subseteq E$ | Set of segments blocked in the primary direction during the disruption window |
| $P$ | Set of breakpoints for the energy–time piecewise-linear (PWL) function |
| $\mathcal{K}_e$ | Trains traversing segment $e$ |
| $\mathcal{S}_k$ | Stations on train $k$'s route |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window boundaries |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time (safety separation) |
| $\tau^{\min,e,\text{normal}}_{k},\, \tau^{\max,e,\text{normal}}_{k}$ | Min/max running time, nominal track |
| $\tau^{\min,e,\text{reverse}}_{k},\, \tau^{\max,e,\text{reverse}}_{k}$ | Min/max running time, reverse track |
| $w_{\min}, w_{\max}$ | Dwell time bounds |
| $a^{\text{sch}}_{k,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, reroute, cancellation) |
| $M$ | Large constant ($M \ge T^{\max}$) |
| $(r_p, E_p)$ | Breakpoints: running time and energy (convex, non-increasing in $r$) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
$$a_{k,s},\, d_{k,s},\, w_{k,s} \ge 0 \qquad \text{(arrival, departure, dwell)}$$
$$\Delta^{\text{delay}}_{k,s} \ge 0 \qquad \text{(arrival delay)}$$
$$t^{\text{run}}_{k,s} \ge 0 \qquad \text{(segment running time)}$$
$$\text{En}_{k,s} \ge 0 \qquad \text{(energy proxy)}$$
$$\lambda_{k,s,p} \ge 0 \qquad \text{(SOS2 interpolation weights, } \textstyle\sum_p \lambda_{k,s,p}=1)$$

**Binary:**
$$y_{k,s} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \text{(1 = reroute onto opposite track on segment } (s,s+1))$$
$$o_{k,k',s} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \text{(1 = train } k \text{ precedes } k' \text{ on the shared track)}$$
$$z_{k,s,p} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \text{(PWL segment selection)}$$
$$\theta_{k,k',s} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \text{(1 = trains } k,k' \text{ use the same physical track)}$$
$$c_k \in \{0,1\} \qquad \text{(1 = train } k \text{ cancelled)}$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}_k}\Delta^{\text{delay}}_{k,s}
\;+\;\beta\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{s:(s,s+1)\in E}\text{En}_{k,s}
\;+\;\gamma\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{s:(s,s+1)\in E}y_{k,s}
\;+\;\delta\sum_{k\in K}c_k
$$

**Terms:** (i) passenger delay, (ii) energy consumption, (iii) rerouting effort, (iv) cancellations.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Continuity
$$d_{k,s} \ge a_{k,s} + w_{k,s} \qquad \forall k,\; s\in\mathcal{S}_k \tag{C1}$$

### 5.2 Dwell Bounds
$$w_{\min} \le w_{k,s} \le w_{\max} \qquad \forall k,\; s\in\mathcal{S}_k \tag{C2}$$

### 5.3 Running-Time Consistency and Bounds
$$a_{k,s+1} - d_{k,s} = t^{\text{run}}_{k,s} \qquad \forall k,\;(s,s+1)\in E \tag{C3a}$$

$$t^{\text{run}}_{k,s} \ge \tau^{\min,\text{nor}}_{k}\,(1-y_{k,s}) + \tau^{\min,\text{rev}}_{k}\,y_{k,s} - M c_k \tag{C3b}$$

$$t^{\text{run}}_{k,s} \le \tau^{\max,\text{nor}}_{k}\,(1-y_{k,s}) + \tau^{\max,\text{rev}}_{k}\,y_{k,s} + M c_k \tag{C3c}$$

### 5.4 Disruption Constraints
For each blocked segment $(s,s+1)\in F$:

**(a) Primary track unavailable in window (if not rerouting):**
$$d_{k,s} \le T_{\text{start}} + M\,y_{k,s} + M\,c_k \tag{C4a}$$
$$a_{k,s+1} \ge T_{\text{end}} - M\,y_{k,s} - M\,c_k \tag{C4b}$$

**(b) Rerouting only allowed within the window (linearized):**
$$y_{k,s} \le \frac{d_{k,s} - T_{\text{start}}}{M} + 1 \tag{C4c-1}$$
$$y_{k,s} \le \frac{T_{\text{end}} - a_{k,s+1}}{M} + 1 \tag{C4c-2}$$

For non-blocked segments outside the window: $y_{k,s} = 0$.

### 5.5 Same-Track Detection and Bidirectional Headway
Same physical track indicator $\theta_{k,k',s}$:
$$\theta_{k,k',s} \le 1 - y_{k,s} + y_{k',s} \tag{C5a-1}$$
$$\theta_{k,k',s} \le 1 + y_{k,s} - y_{k',s} \tag{C5a-2}$$
$$\theta_{k,k',s} \ge 1 - y_{k,s} - y_{k',s} \tag{C5a-3}$$
$$\theta_{k,k',s} \ge y_{k,s} + y_{k',s} - 1 \tag{C5a-4}$$

**Disjunctive headway (big-M):**
$$d_{k',s} \ge a_{k,s+1} + h - M(1 - o_{k,k',s}) - M(1 - \theta_{k,k',s}) - M(c_k+c_{k'}) \tag{C5b}$$
$$d_{k,s} \ge a_{k',s+1} + h - M\,o_{k,k',s} - M(1 - \theta_{k,k',s}) - M(c_k+c_{k'}) \tag{C5c}$$

### 5.6 Opposite-Track (Rerouting) Single-Track Capacity
When both trains reroute:
$$d_{k',s} \ge a_{k,s+1} - M(1-o_{k,k',s}) - M(1-y_{k,s}) - M(1-y_{k',s}) \tag{C6a}$$
$$d_{k,s} \ge a_{k',s+1} - M\,o_{k,k',s} - M(1-y_{k,s}) - M(1-y_{k',s}) \tag{C6b}$$

### 5.7 Energy–Time Coupling (Convex PWL via SOS2)
$$t^{\text{run}}_{k,s} = \sum_{p} r_p\,\lambda_{k,s,p} \tag{C7a}$$
$$\text{En}_{k,s} = \sum_{p} E_p\,\lambda_{k,s,p} \tag{C7b}$$
$$\sum_{p}\lambda_{k,s,p} = 1 \tag{C7c}$$
$$\lambda_{k,s,p} \le z_{k,s,p} + z_{k,s,p-1} \quad \forall p \tag{C7d}$$
$$\sum_{p} z_{k,s,p} = 1 \qquad (z_{k,s,0}=0) \tag{C7e}$$
$$z_{k,s,p}\in\{0,1\},\quad \lambda_{k,s,p}\ge 0 \tag{C7f}$$

### 5.8 Delay Definition
$$\Delta^{\text{delay}}_{k,s} \ge a_{k,s} - a^{\text{sch}}_{k,s} - M c_k \tag{C8a}$$
$$\Delta^{\text{delay}}_{k,s} \ge 0 \tag{C8b}$$

### 5.9 Cancellation Consistency
$$a_{k,s} \le M(1-c_k),\quad d_{k,s} \le M(1-c_k) \tag{C9a}$$
$$y_{k,s} \le 1-c_k,\quad t^{\text{run}}_{k,s} \le M(1-c_k),\quad \text{En}_{k,s} \le M(1-c_k) \tag{C9b}$$

### 5.10 Variable Domains
$$a_{k,s},d_{k,s},w_{k,s},\Delta^{\text{delay}}_{k,s},t^{\text{run}}_{k,s},\text{En}_{k,s},\lambda_{k,s,p}\ge 0$$
$$y_{k,s},o_{k,k',s},z_{k,s,p},\theta_{k,k',s},c_k\in\{0,1\}$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions (marked)

- **(A1)** Minimum headway $h$ enforced between consecutive trains sharing a track.
- **(A2)** Running-time bounds depend on whether the nominal or reverse track is used.
- **(A3)** Dwell bounded $[w_{\min},w_{\max}]$; boarding delays modeled as dwell variability.
- **(A4)** Disruption = primary-direction segment blocked during $[T_{\text{start}},T_{\text{end}}]$; rerouting permitted **only** within this window (assumption).
- **(A5)** Energy is a convex, non-increasing function of running time; modeled exactly by SOS2 PWL (assumption based on standard traction energy curves).
- **(A6)** Cancellation allowed with penalty; cancelled trains released via big-M.
- **(A7)** The model is a single-horizon recovery problem (steady-state scheduling and rolling-horizon extensions left for solution-method design).

**Key insight:** the coupling between rescheduling (times, orders, routes) and speed management (running times → energy) is captured jointly through $t^{\text{run}}_{k,s}$, which appears both in the timetable constraints (C3) and in the energy coupling (C7). Bidirectional conflicts from rerouting are rigorously linearized through the same-track binary $\theta_{k,k',s}$, ensuring conflict-free operation.

# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates the **Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP)** and the **Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP)** for high-speed railway lines under a partial segment blockage disruption with rerouting capability.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, i' \in \mathcal{I}$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of track blocks (segments), indexed by $b \in \mathcal{B}=\{1,2,\dots,|\mathcal{B}|\}$ |
| $\mathcal{J} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | Set of station blocks, indexed by $j \in \mathcal{J}$ |
| $\mathcal{B}^D \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | Set of blocks affected by the partial blockage |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time steps, $t \in \mathcal{T}=\{0,1,\dots,T^{\max}\}$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^D \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Disruption time window $\{T^{D,s},\dots,T^{D,e}\}$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{+1,-1\}$ | Set of travel directions (forward, reverse) |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of breakpoints for piecewise-linear energy approximation, $s \in \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of possible dwelling intervals at a station, $k \in \mathcal{K}=\{0,1,\dots,K^{\max}\}$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a discrete time step | s |
| $v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum operating speed | m/s |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / braking rate | m/s² |
| $\tau_j^{\min}, \tau_j^{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at station $j$ | s |
| $h$ | Minimum safe headway time between trains | s |
| $\bar{a}_{i,j}, \bar{d}_{i,j}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $j$ | s |
| $o_i, d_i$ | Origin and destination station of train $i$ | – |
| $w_1, w_2$ | Weights for delay and energy in the objective | – |
| $c^p$ | Penalty for cancelling a train | – |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Davis resistance coefficients ($\alpha+\beta v+\gamma v^2$) | – |
| $m_i$ | Mass of train $i$ | t |
| $v_s, e_s$ | Speed breakpoints and corresponding specific energy for PWL ($s \in \mathcal{S}$) | m/s, kWh/(train·m) |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-$M$) | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Space–time occupation (binary)

* $x_{i,b,t} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ at time step $t$.
* $y_{i,b,t} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ *enters* block $b$ at the beginning of $t$.
* $z_{i,b,t} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ *leaves* block $b$ at the end of $t$.
* $r_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses the **reverse (opposite) track** on block $b$ (rerouting).

### 3.2 Ordering (binary)

* $\omega_{i,i',b} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ traverses block $b$ strictly before train $i'$.

### 3.3 Train timing (continuous)

* $A_{i,j} \ge 0$ — actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$.
* $D_{i,j} \ge 0$ — actual departure time of train $i$ at station $j$.
* $\Delta_{i,j} \ge 0$ — delay of train $i$ at station $j$ with respect to schedule.

### 3.4 Speed profile (continuous)

* $v_{i,b,t} \in [v^{\min}, v^{\max}]$ — speed of train $i$ inside block $b$ at time $t$.
* $a_{i,b,t} \in [-b^{\max}, a^{\max}]$ — acceleration of train $i$ inside block $b$ at time $t$.
* $\lambda_{i,b,t}^s \in [0,1]$, $\sum_s \lambda_{i,b,t}^s = 1$ — convex-combination weights for PWL energy.

### 3.5 Energy (continuous)

* $E_{i,b,t} \ge 0$ — energy consumed by train $i$ in block $b$ during $t$.
* $E^{\text{tot}}_i \ge 0$ — total energy of train $i$.

### 3.6 Cancellation (binary)

* $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; w_1 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}}\sum_{j \in \mathcal{J}} \Delta_{i,j} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}}\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} E_{i,b,t} \;+\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} c^p\, c_i
\tag{Obj}
$$

The objective balances **(i)** total passenger delay, **(ii)** total traction energy, and **(iii)** penalties for service cancellations.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Space–time flow conservation

Each train can only occupy **one** block per time step and must move to an adjacent block at each step:

$$
x_{i,b,t} \le x_{i,b-1,t-1} + x_{i,b+1,t-1} \quad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\, b\in\mathcal{B},\, t\in\mathcal{T}\setminus\{0\}
\tag{C1}
$$

$$
x_{i,b,t} \ge x_{i,b-1,t-1} + x_{i,b+1,t-1} - 1 \quad \forall i,b,t
\tag{C2}
$$

Entering/leaving indicators are consistent with occupation:

$$
y_{i,b,t} \ge x_{i,b,t} - x_{i,b,t-1} \quad ; \quad y_{i,b,t} \le x_{i,b,t} ; \quad y_{i,b,t} \le 2 - x_{i,b,t-1} - (1-x_{i,b,t})
\tag{C3a}
$$

$$
z_{i,b,t} \ge x_{i,b,t-1} - x_{i,b,t} \quad ; \quad z_{i,b,t} \le x_{i,b,t-1} ; \quad z_{i,b,t} \le 2 - x_{i,b,t} - (1-x_{i,b,t-1})
\tag{C3b}
$$

### 5.2 Origin / destination / boundary conditions

$$
\sum_{b} x_{i,b,0} = 1 - c_i \qquad \text{(train starts at origin block } o_i \text{ if not cancelled)}
\tag{C4}
$$

$$
\sum_{b} x_{i,b,T^{\max}} = 1 - c_i \qquad \text{(train ends at destination block } d_i \text{)}
\tag{C5}
$$

$$
x_{i,b,t} = 0 \quad \forall b \notin [o_i, d_i] \text{ if } i \text{ travels forward},\; \forall t
\tag{C6}
$$

(For reverse-direction trains the interval is reversed.)

### 5.3 Block capacity — headway and bidirectional safety

At most one **non-cancelled** train may occupy a block per time step **on each track direction**, and opposite-direction trains must respect a safe separation:

$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} x_{i,b,t} \le 1 \quad \forall b\in\mathcal{B},\, t\in\mathcal{T}
\tag{C7}
$$

For a train using the reverse track, occupation counts only with reverse-track peers:

$$
\sum_{i} (1-r_{i,b})\, x_{i,b,t} \le 1 \quad ; \quad \sum_{i} r_{i,b}\, x_{i,b,t} \le 1 \quad \forall b,t
\tag{C8}
$$

Headway between successive trains traversing the same block (using the ordering variable $\omega$):

$$
\sum_{t' \le t} x_{i,b,t'} + \sum_{t' \ge t-h+1} x_{i',b,t'} \le 1 + M(1-\omega_{i,i',b}) \quad \forall i\neq i', b, t
\tag{C9}
$$

$$
\omega_{i,i',b} + \omega_{i',i,b} = 1 \quad \forall i \neq i', b \text{ with both trains traversing } b
\tag{C10}
$$

### 5.4 Disruption constraints (partial blockage)

During the disruption window, trains travelling on the **original (forward)** track cannot occupy disrupted blocks:

$$
x_{i,b,t} \le r_{i,b} + (1 - \mathbf{1}_{t\in \mathcal{T}^D}) + M\,c_i \quad \forall i, b\in \mathcal{B}^D, t\in \mathcal{T}^D
\tag{C11}
$$

Equivalently: if $b\in\mathcal{B}^D$, $t\in\mathcal{T}^D$, $c_i=0$, then $x_{i,b,t}=1 \Rightarrow r_{i,b}=1$ (rerouting required).

### 5.5 Rerouting consistency

A train may only enter the reverse track when reaching (or being inside) a disrupted block and only during the disruption window:

$$
r_{i,b} \le \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^D} x_{i,b,t} \quad \forall b\in\mathcal{B}^D
\tag{C12}
$$

$$
r_{i,b+1} \le r_{i,b} + (1-\mathbf{1}_{t\in\mathcal{T}^D}) \quad \forall i, b\in\mathcal{B}^D, t
\tag{C13}
$$

(Reverse-track usage cannot propagate outside the disrupted region.)

### 5.6 Train dynamics — kinematics

Average speed in block $b$ at time $t$:

$$
L_b - \epsilon \le v_{i,b,t}\,\tau_{i,b} \le L_b + \epsilon
\tag{C14}
$$

where $\tau_{i,b} = \Delta t \sum_{t'} x_{i,b,t'}$ is the (continuous proxy) time spent in block $b$. To keep it MILP-linear, **replace** the product with a PWL reformulation linking $v_{i,b,t}$ to $x_{i,b,t}$:

$$
v_{i,b,t} = \frac{L_b}{\Delta t}\cdot x_{i,b,t} + \delta_{i,b,t}, \qquad 0\le \delta_{i,b,t} \le \frac{L_b}{\Delta t}(1-x_{i,b,t})
\tag{C14'}
$$

Acceleration bounded by physical limits:

$$
a_{i,b,t} \le a^{\max}\, x_{i,b,t} \quad ; \quad -a_{i,b,t} \le b^{\max}\, x_{i,b,t} \quad \forall i,b,t
\tag{C15}
$$

Speed transition between consecutive time steps:

$$
v_{i,b,t} - v_{i,b,t-1} \le a^{\max}\,\Delta t + M(1 - x_{i,b,t}) + M(1 - x_{i,b,t-1})
\tag{C16a}
$$

$$
v_{i,b,t-1} - v_{i,b,t} \le b^{\max}\,\Delta t + M(1 - x_{i,b,t}) + M(1 - x_{i,b,t-1})
\tag{C16b}
$$

### 5.7 Station dwell and arrival/departure

Linking block-entering/leaving events to timing variables:

$$
A_{i,j} \ge t \cdot y_{i,j,t} \quad ; \quad A_{i,j} \le t\cdot y_{i,j,t} + M(1-y_{i,j,t}) \quad \forall i,j,t
\tag{C17}
$$

$$
D_{i,j} \ge t \cdot z_{i,j,t} \quad ; \quad D_{i,j} \le t\cdot z_{i,j,t} + M(1-z_{i,j,t}) \quad \forall i,j,t
\tag{C18}
$$

Dwell time bounds:

$$
\tau_j^{\min} \le D_{i,j} - A_{i,j} \le \tau_j^{\max} \quad \forall i,j
\tag{C19}
$$

### 5.8 Delay calculation

$$
\Delta_{i,j} \ge A_{i,j} - \bar{a}_{i,j} \quad ; \quad \Delta_{i,j} \ge 0 \quad \forall i,j
\tag{C20}
$$

### 5.9 Energy model (PWL linearization)

Specific mechanical energy per metre at speed $v$ follows the Davis equation $e(v)=\alpha+\beta v+\gamma v^2$. The $v^2$ term is linearized via breakpoints $\{(v_s,e_s)\}_{s\in\mathcal{S}}$:

$$
E_{i,b,t} \ge \sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} \lambda_{i,b,t}^s\, e_s\, L_b\,x_{i,b,t} \;+\; \tfrac{1}{2}m_i\bigl[(v_{i,b,t}^+)^2 - (v_{i,b,t}^-)^2\bigr]_{+}
\tag{C21}
$$

The kinetic-energy increment $[(v^+)^2-(v^-)^2]_+$ is itself PWL-linearized with breakpoints on speed (or equivalently on $\Delta v^2$), giving an additional set of weights $\mu^s_{i,b,t}\in[0,1]$. For brevity we collapse this into:

$$
E_{i,b,t} \ge \sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} \lambda_{i,b,t}^s\, \hat e_s(v^+_{i,b,t},v^-_{i,b,t}) \, x_{i,b,t}
\tag{C21'}
$$

$$
\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\lambda_{i,b,t}^s = x_{i,b,t} \quad ; \quad \lambda^s_{i,b,t} \in [0,1]
\tag{C22}
$$

Aggregate per-train energy:

$$
E^{\text{tot}}_i = \sum_{b,t} E_{i,b,t}
\tag{C23}
$$

### 5.10 Cancellation logic (optional)

If a train is cancelled it neither moves nor consumes energy:

$$
x_{i,b,t} \le 1 - c_i \quad ; \quad A_{i,j} \le M(1-c_i) \quad ; \quad D_{i,j} \le M(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,b,t,j
\tag{C24}
$$

---

## 6. Summary of Model Components

| Component | Constraints | Variables used |
|---|---|---|
| Train trajectory (space–time) | (C1)–(C6), (C24) | $x,y,z,c$ |
| Bidirectional conflict resolution | (C7)–(C10) | $x,r,\omega$ |
| Disruption & rerouting | (C11)–(C13) | $x,r$ |
| Train dynamics & speed profile | (C14)–(C16) | $x,v,a,\delta$ |
| Station dwell & timings | (C17)–(C19) | $y,z,A,D$ |
| Delay | (C20) | $A,\Delta$ |
| Energy (PWL) | (C21)–(C23) | $v,E,\lambda$ |

---

## 7. Modeling Assumptions (explicit)

1. **Discretization**: Space is partitioned into homogeneous blocks; time is discretized into equal $\Delta t$ steps. Speeds are averaged over the block-time cell.
2. **Linearization of energy**: The nonlinear $v^2$ term in the Davis equation is linearized with a **piecewise-linear** approximation via $\lambda_{i,b,t}^s$ (SOS2 in practice); kinetic-energy increments are linearized similarly. This keeps the model strictly MILP.
3. **Bidirectional conflict resolution**: Trains in opposite directions sharing a track are separated by the block-capacity constraints (C7)–(C8); a headway $h$ between consecutive trains on the same block is enforced via ordering variables (C9)–(C10).
4. **Rerouting strategy**: During the disruption window the forward track on $b \in \mathcal{B}^D$ is unavailable; trains may divert to the reverse track **only** inside the disrupted region (C11)–(C13), reflecting local rerouting.
5. **Cancellation**: Trains may be cancelled with a penalty $c^p$ in the objective (C24).
6. **Single-track line with passing**: Stations provide the only places where opposite-direction trains can pass each other; this is enforced implicitly by the block-occupation constraints.
7. **Constant rolling-stock parameters**: Mass $m_i$ and resistance coefficients are assumed train-specific constants over the planning horizon.
8. **No partial cancellations or short-turning**: This can be added by introducing station-turn variables if required.

---

## 8. Linear Relaxation Strength (comments)

* The model is tight because (i) block occupation is a pure network-flow structure (C1)–(C6), (ii) ordering variables $\omega_{i,i',b}$ are aggregated only over pairs that actually traverse the block (detectable in preprocessing), and (iii) the PWL energy approximation introduces only SOS2-type convexity, which modern MILP solvers handle efficiently.
* For large-scale instances the model can be solved by the **decomposition** described in the paper: an Integer Programming (IP) master that selects among pre-generated per-train plans, plus a feasibility check that produces additional plans in the neighborhood of the current solution.

---

This MILP jointly produces **(a)** a conflict-free rescheduled timetable, **(b)** executable speed profiles, **(c)** a rerouting decision under partial blockage, and **(d)** a co-optimized delay–energy trade-off, fulfilling the scientific objectives stated in the introduction.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S=\{0,\dots,|S|-1\}$ | Stations / block-section boundaries, ordered along the line |
| $A=\{(s,s+1):s\in S\setminus\{|S|-1\}\}$ | Physical segments/blocks |
| $D=\{+1,-1\}$ | Directions ($+1$ forward, $-1$ backward) |
| $T=\{i,j,\dots\}$ | Trains |
| $K$ | Candidate paths; $K_i\subseteq K$ allowed paths for train $i$ |
| $M_a$ | Discrete running-time/speed options on segment $a$ |
| $\bar A\subseteq A$ | Affected segments (one track blocked) |
| $W=[t_w^{start},t_w^{end}]$ | Disruption time window |

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\text{dir}_i\in D$ | Nominal direction of train $i$ |
| $rt_{i,a,m}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $a$ with option $m$ |
| $e_{i,a,m}$ | Energy of train $i$ on segment $a$ with option $m$ |
| $arr^{nom}_{i,s},dep^{nom}_{i,s}$ | Nominal arrival/departure times |
| $dw^{\min}_{i,s},dw^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Dwell bounds |
| $h_{\min},h_{\text{bi}}$ | Minimum same-direction / bidirectional headway |
| $c^{delay}_i,c^{cancel}_i,c^{energy},c^{reroute}$ | Cost coefficients |
| $T^{\min},T^{\max},B$ | Horizon bounds, big-M |
| $a^{ind}_{i,k,a},\;\nu^{sta}_{i,k,s}$ | Binary path-segment / path-station incidence (paths) |
| $\rho_{i,k,a}$ | Binary: path $k$ uses the opposite (rerouted) track on $a$ |
| $\eta_{i,j,a}$ | Binary: $i,j$ may share the same effective physical track on $a$ |
| $\text{sdir}_{i,j}$ | Binary: $i,j$ have the same nominal direction |

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses path $k$ |
| $y_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ cancelled |
| $r_{i,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes on affected segment $a$ |
| $u_{i,a,m}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed option $m$ on $a$ |
| $z_{i,j,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on $a$ (same effective direction) |
| $w_{i,j,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on $a$ (opposite-direction disjunction) |
| $\alpha_{i,a},\beta_{i,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Overlap-window indicator pieces |
| $ovl_{i,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $i$'s occupancy of $a$ overlaps $W$ |
| $arr_{i,s},dep_{i,s},dw_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ | Arrival / departure / dwell |
| $enter_{i,a},exit_{i,a},t^{run}_{i,a}$ | $\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ | Segment entry/exit/running time |
| $E_i$ | $\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ | Energy of train $i$ |
| $\delta^+_{i,s},Del_i$ | $\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ | Delay linearization |
| $\text{used}_{i,a}$ | $[0,1]$ | Traversal indicator $=\sum_m u_{i,a,m}$ |

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min\;Z=\sum_{i\in T}c^{delay}_i Del_i+\sum_{i\in T}c^{cancel}_i y_i+c^{energy}\sum_{i\in T}E_i+c^{reroute}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{a\in\bar A}r_{i,a}\tag{1}
$$

---

## Constraints

### 1. Route / Cancellation
$$
\sum_{k\in K_i}x_{i,k}+y_i=1,\qquad\forall i\in T.\tag{2}
$$

### 2. Reroute Consistency with Path Choice
$$
\sum_{k\in K_i}\rho_{i,k,a}\,x_{i,k}=r_{i,a},\qquad\forall i\in T,\;a\in\bar A,\tag{3a}
$$
$$
r_{i,a}=0,\qquad\forall i\in T,\;a\in A\setminus\bar A.\tag{3b}
$$

### 3. Speed-Option / Traversal Consistency
$$
\text{used}_{i,a}=\sum_{m\in M_a}u_{i,a,m}=\sum_{k\in K_i}a^{ind}_{i,k,a}\,x_{i,k},\qquad\forall i\in T,\;a\in A.\tag{4}
$$

### 4. Timing, Dwell, Running-Time
$$
dw^{\min}_{i,s}\!\sum_{k}\nu^{sta}_{i,k,s}x_{i,k}\le dw_{i,s}\le dw^{\max}_{i,s}\!\sum_{k}\nu^{sta}_{i,k,s}x_{i,k},\;\forall i,s,\tag{5a}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s}=arr_{i,s}+dw_{i,s},\qquad\forall i,s,\tag{5b}
$$
$$
t^{run}_{i,a}=exit_{i,a}-enter_{i,a},\qquad\forall i,a,\tag{5c}
$$
$$
t^{run}_{i,a}=\sum_{m\in M_a}rt_{i,a,m}\,u_{i,a,m},\qquad\forall i,a.\tag{5d}
$$

### 5. Segment–Station Timing Coupling
With $\text{prev}(a,i),\text{next}(a,i)$ mapping to the boundary traversed before/after segment $a$ according to $\text{dir}_i$:
$$
-B(1-\text{used}_{i,a})\le enter_{i,a}-dep_{i,\text{prev}(a,i)}\le B(1-\text{used}_{i,a}),\tag{6a}
$$
$$
-B(1-\text{used}_{i,a})\le exit_{i,a}-arr_{i,\text{next}(a,i)}\le B(1-\text{used}_{i,a}).\tag{6b}
$$

### 6. Horizon Bounds
$$
T^{\min}\le arr_{i,s},dep_{i,s}\le T^{\max},\qquad\forall i,s.\tag{7}
$$

### 7. Disruption-Window Overlap and Forced Reroute
$$
enter_{i,a}\le t^{end}_w+B(1-\alpha_{i,a}),\qquad enter_{i,a}\ge t^{end}_w-B\alpha_{i,a}+\varepsilon,\tag{8a}
$$
$$
exit_{i,a}\ge t^{start}_w-B(1-\beta_{i,a}),\qquad exit_{i,a}\le t^{start}_w+B\beta_{i,a}-\varepsilon,\tag{8b}
$$
$$
ovl_{i,a}\ge\alpha_{i,a}+\beta_{i,a}-1,\qquad ovl_{i,a}\le \alpha_{i,a},\qquad ovl_{i,a}\le\beta_{i,a},\tag{8c}
$$
$$
r_{i,a}\ge ovl_{i,a}-(1-\text{used}_{i,a}),\qquad\forall i\in T,\;a\in\bar A.\tag{8d}
$$

### 8. Same-Direction Headway Disjunction
For pairs with $\text{sdir}_{i,j}=1$ and sharing segment $a$:
$$
exit_{i,a}+h_{\min}\le enter_{j,a}+B(1-z_{i,j,a})+B(2-\text{used}_{i,a}-\text{used}_{j,a}),\tag{9a}
$$
$$
exit_{j,a}+h_{\min}\le enter_{i,a}+Bz_{i,j,a}+B(2-\text{used}_{i,a}-\text{used}_{j,a}),\tag{9b}
$$
$$
z_{i,j,a}+z_{j,i,a}\ge(\text{used}_{i,a}+\text{used}_{j,a}-1)\,\text{sdir}_{i,j}.\tag{9c}
$$

### 9. Opposite-Direction Conflict (Shared Physical Track)
$$
enter_{j,a}\ge exit_{i,a}+h_{\text{bi}}-B(1-w_{i,j,a})-B(2-\text{used}_{i,a}-\text{used}_{j,a}),\tag{10a}
$$
$$
enter_{i,a}\ge exit_{j,a}+h_{\text{bi}}-Bw_{i,j,a}-B(2-\text{used}_{i,a}-\text{used}_{j,a}),\tag{10b}
$$
$$
w_{i,j,a}+w_{j,i,a}\ge\eta_{i,j,a}\,(\text{used}_{i,a}+\text{used}_{j,a}-1).\tag{10c}
$$

### 10. Delay Linearization
$$
\delta^+_{i,s}\ge arr_{i,s}-arr^{nom}_{i,s},\qquad\delta^+_{i,s}\ge0,\tag{11a}
$$
$$
Del_i\ge\delta^+_{i,s},\qquad\forall i,s,\tag{11b}
$$
$$
Del_i\le B(1-y_i).\tag{11c}
$$

### 11. Energy
$$
E_i=\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{m\in M_a}e_{i,a,m}\,u_{i,a,m},\qquad\forall i\in T,\tag{12a}
$$
$$
E_i\le B(1-y_i).\tag{12b}
$$

### 12. Variable Domains
$$
x_{i,k},y_i,r_{i,a},u_{i,a,m},z_{i,j,a},w_{i,j,a},\alpha_{i,a},\beta_{i,a},ovl_{i,a}\in\{0,1\},\tag{13a}
$$
$$
arr_{i,s},dep_{i,s},dw_{i,s},enter_{i,a},exit_{i,a},t^{run}_{i,a},E_i,\delta^+_{i,s},Del_i\ge0,\quad \text{used}_{i,a}\in[0,1].\tag{13b}
$$

---

## Assumptions

- **(A1)** Double-track line; a partial blockage disables one direction's track on $\bar A$ during $W$; rerouting uses the opposite track (single-track bidirectional operation locally).
- **(A2)** Each train traverses a segment at most once; spatial capacity enforced by headway disjunctions.
- **(A3)** Continuous speed profiles are approximated by discrete run-time/energy options (MILP linearity).
- **(A4)** Acceleration/deceleration effects folded into running-time options and transition headways.
- **(A5)** Cancellation removes the train entirely (no partial operation).
- **(A6)** Delay measured relative to nominal arrival times at visited stations.
- **(A7)** $B,\varepsilon$ chosen sufficiently large/small.
- **(A8)** Energy linear in selected discrete speed option.
- **(A9)** Disruption window fixed and known; recovery at $t_w^{end}$.
- **(A10)** Station sequence fixed; rerouting only changes track, not stations.

This formulation is fully linear in all decisions, with disjunctive headway, opposite-direction, reroute, and speed-option constraints implemented via precomputable incidence coefficients and big-M disjunctions.

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code, expressed as mathematical equations.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ | Trains |
| $s \in \mathcal{S}$ | Stations (ordered $1,\dots,|\mathcal{S}|$) |
| $k \in \mathcal{K}$ | Segments between consecutive stations |
| $d \in \mathcal{D}$ | Discretized distance steps within a segment |
| $v \in \mathcal{V}$ | Discretized speed levels |
| $t \in \mathcal{P}$ | Discretized time periods |
| $r \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ | Directions |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ |
| $\Delta_d, \Delta_t$ | Distance and time step sizes |
| $v_{\max}, v_{\min}$ | Speed bounds |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Acceleration / deceleration limits |
| $E_v$ | Energy consumption per unit distance at speed $v$ |
| $\tau_s, \tau_s^{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $t^{\text{dep,sched}}_{i,s}, t^{\text{arr,sched}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure / arrival times |
| $H$ | Minimum headway |
| $\text{blocked}_{k,t}$ | 1 if segment $k$ is blocked at time $t$ |
| $M$ | Large constant |
| $\text{cap}^{\text{opp}}_k$ | Rerouting capacity on segment $k$ |
| $\text{cap}^{\text{stn}}_s$ | Station capacity |
| $\rho$ | Reroute penalty |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Objective weights |
| $s^{\text{term}}$ | Terminal station |
| $\text{seg}(s,s{+}1)=k$ | Segment–station mapping |

---

## Decision Variables

**Binary:**
$$x_{i,k,d,t} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{i,k,v} \in \{0,1\}, \quad z_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}, \quad w_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \alpha_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \text{cancel}_i \in \{0,1\}$$

**Continuous (non-negative):**
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s},\ \text{run}_{i,k},\ e_{i,k} \ge 0$$

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min\ Z = w_1 \sum_{i}\sum_{s}\bigl(t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr,sched}}_{i,s}\bigr)
+ w_2 \sum_{i}\sum_{k} e_{i,k}
+ w_3\,\rho \sum_{i}\sum_{k} w_{i,k}
+ w_4 \sum_{i}\bigl(1 - z_{i,s^{\text{term}}}\bigr)
$$

Minimizes weighted sum of **total arrival delay**, **energy consumption**, **rerouting usage**, and **missed terminal stops**.

---

## Constraints

### 1. Train Movement / Position–Time Consistency

**(1a) Each train occupies each segment exactly once:**
$$\sum_{d\in\mathcal{D}}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{P}} x_{i,k,d,t} = 1 \qquad \forall i,k$$

**(1b) At most one position per time step:**
$$\sum_{d\in\mathcal{D}} x_{i,k,d,t} \le 1 \qquad \forall i,k,t$$

**(1c) Position–time transition:**
$$x_{i,k,d,t} \le x_{i,k,d+1,t+1} \qquad \forall i,k,\ d<|\mathcal{D}|,\ t<|\mathcal{P}|$$

### 2. Speed Profile Selection

**(2a) Exactly one speed per segment:**
$$\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}} y_{i,k,v} = 1 \qquad \forall i,k$$

**(2b) Running time:**
$$\text{run}_{i,k} = \sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}} y_{i,k,v}\,\frac{L_k}{v} \qquad \forall i,k$$

**(2c) Energy consumption:**
$$e_{i,k} = \sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}} y_{i,k,v}\,E_v\,L_k \qquad \forall i,k$$

### 3. Speed and Acceleration Limits

**(3a) Acceleration between consecutive segments:**
$$\frac{\sum_v v\,y_{i,k+1,v} - \sum_v v\,y_{i,k,v}}{\Delta_t} \le a_{\max} \qquad \forall i,\ k<|\mathcal{K}|$$

**(3b) Deceleration between consecutive segments:**
$$\frac{\sum_v v\,y_{i,k,v} - \sum_v v\,y_{i,k+1,v}}{\Delta_t} \le b_{\max} \qquad \forall i,\ k<|\mathcal{K}|$$

### 4. Timetable Consistency

**(4a) Arrival–departure linkage:**
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s+1} = t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} + \text{run}_{i,k}, \quad k=\text{seg}(s,s{+}1) \qquad \forall i,k$$

**(4b) Minimum dwell:**
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} + \tau_s\,z_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,s$$

**(4c) Maximum dwell:**
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \le t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} + \tau_s^{\max}\,z_{i,s} + M\,(1 - z_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i,s$$

**(4d) No early arrival:**
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \ge t^{\text{arr,sched}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,s$$

### 5. Disruption / Blockage Constraints

**(5a) Blocked segment cannot be traversed unless rerouted:**
$$x_{i,k,d,t} \le 1 - w_{i,k} + \bigl(1 - \text{blocked}_{k,t}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,k,d,t$$

### 6. Rerouting Capacity

**(6a) Limited number of trains may reroute per segment:**
$$\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} w_{i,k} \le \text{cap}^{\text{opp}}_k \qquad \forall k$$

### 7. Conflict-Free / Headway Constraints (Same Direction)

**(7a) Ordering complementarity:**
$$\alpha_{i,j,k} + \alpha_{j,i,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i\ne j,\ k$$

**(7b) Headway (i before j):**
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{j,s} - t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge H - M\,(1 - \alpha_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall i\ne j,\ k,\ s=\text{entry}(k)$$

**(7c) Headway (j before i):**
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{dep}}_{j,s} \ge H - M\,\alpha_{i,j,k} \qquad \forall i\ne j,\ k,\ s=\text{entry}(k)$$

### 8. Rerouting Conflict Constraints (Bidirectional)

**(8a) Headway when train $i$ reroutes:**
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{j,s} - t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge H - M\,(1 - w_{i,k}) - M\,(1 - \alpha_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall i\ne j,\ k$$

**(8b) Reverse ordering:**
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{dep}}_{j,s} \ge H - M\,(1 - w_{i,k}) - M\,\alpha_{i,j,k} \qquad \forall i\ne j,\ k$$

### 9. Station Capacity

**(9a) Simultaneous stops limited:**
$$\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} z_{i,s} \le \text{cap}^{\text{stn}}_s \qquad \forall s$$

### 10. Train Cancellation

**(10a) Cancelled trains have zero arrival times:**
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \le M\,(1 - \text{cancel}_i) \qquad \forall i,s$$

### 11. Domain Constraints

$$x_{i,k,d,t},\ y_{i,k,v},\ z_{i,s},\ w_{i,k},\ \alpha_{i,j,k},\ \text{cancel}_i \in \{0,1\}$$
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s},\ \text{run}_{i,k},\ e_{i,k} \ge 0$$

---

## Assumptions (Marked)

1. **Discretized representation** — Time, distance, and speed are discretized to enable MILP linearization of the continuous dynamics.
2. **Convex piecewise-linear energy** — $E_v$ is approximated as a convex piecewise-linear function of speed.
3. **Single disruption window per segment** — Each segment has at most one blockage interval.
4. **Rerouting to opposite track only** — Trains may divert to the opposite track, subject to a capacity limit.
5. **Bounded dwell times** — Dwell times lie in $[\tau_s, \tau_s^{\max}]$.
6. **No early arrival** — Trains cannot arrive before their scheduled time (delay-only recovery).
7. **Uniform headway** — A single headway value $H$ applies to all train pairs.
8. **Simplified station capacity** — Modeled as the number of simultaneous stops, not platform-level detail.
9. **Position–time transition** — Uses a single-step transition $x_{i,k,d,t} \le x_{i,k,d+1,t+1}$ as a linear approximation of the continuous motion.
10. **Speed–acceleration coupling** — Acceleration/deceleration is enforced between consecutive segments using the selected speed levels.

---

**Solver note:** The model contains $|\mathcal{T}|^2 \cdot |\mathcal{K}|$ binary ordering variables $\alpha_{i,j,k}$, which grows quadratically. For large instances, decomposition (as described in the paper's solution framework) or a rolling-horizon approach is recommended.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

Below is a complete linear (MILP) model that captures the essential elements of the passenger-oriented real-time train rescheduling problem described in the introduction: time-varying (piecewise-constant) sectional passenger demand, flexible train composition, rolling-stock circulation, train stopping plans, and timetable adjustments within an MPC prediction horizon.

---

## 1. Modeling Overview and Assumptions

**Assumptions (clearly marked):**

- **A1.** The rail network is a single line (or corridor) with stations ordered $s = 1, 2, \dots, |S|$. Extension to a small network is possible by replicating the model per line and coupling via transfer constraints (not detailed here).
- **A2.** Passenger arrivals are aggregated per origin–destination (OD) pair and approximated as piecewise constant over time intervals of equal length $\Delta t$ (as in Liu et al., 2023a).
- **A3.** Each train is assigned exactly one composition $i \in I$ (number of coupled units), and the capacity of composition $i$ is $C_i$ passengers.
- **A4.** Trains run in a fixed order (no overtaking) along the line.
- **A5.** Dwell time and running time have lower and upper bounds.
- **A6.** Rolling stock units are interchangeable; a unit released by one train can be coupled to the next compatible train after a minimum turnaround time.
- **A7.** The prediction horizon is divided into $T$ equal intervals; the timetable within the horizon is the decision variable.
- **A8.** Passenger waiting time is computed as the difference between the desired departure time interval and the actual boarding train's departure time.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $K$ | Set of trains, indexed by $k$ (operational order $k = 1, \dots, |K|$) |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s = 1, \dots, |S|$ |
| $I$ | Set of train compositions, indexed by $i$ (number of units) |
| $R$ | Set of rolling-stock units, indexed by $r$ |
| $T$ | Set of time intervals in the prediction horizon, indexed by $t$ |
| $P$ | Set of OD passenger pairs, indexed by $p = (o, d)$ |
| $E$ | Set of sections, indexed by $e = (s, s+1)$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $N_H$ | Length of prediction horizon | min |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of each time interval, $\Delta t = N_H / |T|$ | min |
| $d_{p,t}$ | Arrival rate of OD passengers $p$ during interval $t$ | pax/min |
| $C_i$ | Passenger capacity of composition $i$ | pax |
| $L_e$ | Length of section $e$ | km |
| $v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ | Min/max cruising speed | km/h |
| $t^{\min}_e, t^{\max}_e$ | Min/max running time on section $e$ | min |
| $\tau^{\min}, \tau^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at any station | min |
| $h^{\min}, h^{\max}$ | Min/max headway between consecutive trains | min |
| $t^{\text{turn}}$ | Minimum turnaround time at terminals | min |
| $c^{\text{op}}_i$ | Operating cost per train-hour for composition $i$ | €/h |
| $c^{\text{wait}}$ | Passenger waiting-time cost | €/pax·min |
| $c^{\text{trv}}$ | Passenger in-vehicle travel-time cost | €/pax·min |
| $c^{\text{dev}}$ | Penalty for deviation from nominal timetable | €/min |
| $c^{\text{rs}}_i$ | Cost of using composition $i$ (rolling-stock + energy) | €/train-km |
| $\bar{a}_{k,s}$ | Nominal arrival time of train $k$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\bar{d}_{k,s}$ | Nominal departure time of train $k$ at station $s$ | min |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) | — |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Integer / binary variables:**

- $x_{k,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ stops at station $s$.
- $y_{k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ uses composition $i$.
- $\pi_{r,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if rolling-stock unit $r$ is assigned to train $k$.
- $\sigma_{r,k,k'} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ is transferred from train $k$ to train $k'$.
- $z_{k,k',s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ departs station $s$ no later than train $k'$ (ordering).

**Continuous variables:**

- $a_{k,s} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $k$ at station $s$.
- $d_{k,s} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $k$ at station $s$.
- $\tau_{k,s} \geq 0$: dwell time of train $k$ at station $s$.
- $\delta_{k,s} \geq 0$: absolute deviation of $d_{k,s}$ from nominal departure $\bar{d}_{k,s}$.
- $h_{k,s} \geq 0$: headway between train $k$ and $k+1$ at station $s$.
- $\lambda_{p,k,s} \geq 0$: number of OD-$p$ passengers boarding train $k$ at station $s$.
- $w_{p,s} \geq 0$: average waiting time of OD-$p$ passengers at station $s$.
- $\text{load}_{k,s} \geq 0$: number of passengers on board train $k$ when it departs station $s$.

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total system cost:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \underbrace{\sum_{k \in K} \sum_{i \in I} c^{\text{op}}_i \, y_{k,i} \, N_H}_{\text{operating cost}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{k \in K} \sum_{s \in S} c^{\text{rs}}_i \, L_{(s,s+1)} \, y_{k,i}}_{\text{rolling-stock / energy cost}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{p \in P} \sum_{s \in S} c^{\text{wait}} \, w_{p,s}}_{\text{passenger waiting time}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{k \in K} \sum_{s \in S} c^{\text{trv}} \, (a_{k,d_p} - d_{k,o_p})}_{\text{passenger in-vehicle time}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{k \in K} \sum_{s \in S} c^{\text{dev}} \, \delta_{k,s}}_{\text{timetable deviation}}
$$

where $o_p$ and $d_p$ denote the origin and destination of OD pair $p$.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Train Composition and Capacity

**(C1) Single composition per train:**
$$
\sum_{i \in I} y_{k,i} = 1, \quad \forall k \in K.
$$

**(C2) Composition capacity (linearization of $C_i \cdot y_{k,i}$):**
$$
\text{cap}_k = \sum_{i \in I} C_i \, y_{k,i}, \quad \forall k \in K.
$$

**(C3) On-board load limit:**
$$
\text{load}_{k,s} \leq \text{cap}_k, \quad \forall k \in K,\; s \in S.
$$

### 6.2 Stopping Plan

**(C4) Terminals must be served:**
$$
x_{k,1} = x_{k,|S|} = 1, \quad \forall k \in K.
$$

**(C5) Pass-through at intermediate stations:**
$$
d_{k,s} = a_{k,s} + \tau_{k,s}, \quad \text{if } x_{k,s} = 1,
$$
$$
d_{k,s} = a_{k,s}, \quad \text{if } x_{k,s} = 0.
$$

Linearized using Big-M:
$$
d_{k,s} - a_{k,s} - \tau_{k,s} \leq M (1 - x_{k,s}), \quad \forall k,s,
$$
$$
d_{k,s} - a_{k,s} - \tau_{k,s} \geq -M (1 - x_{k,s}), \quad \forall k,s,
$$
$$
\tau^{\min} x_{k,s} \leq \tau_{k,s} \leq \tau^{\max} x_{k,s}, \quad \forall k,s.
$$

### 6.3 Running-Time and Travel-Time Constraints

**(C6) Section running time:**
$$
a_{k,s+1} \geq d_{k,s} + t^{\min}_{(s,s+1)}, \quad \forall k \in K,\; s = 1,\dots,|S|-1,
$$
$$
a_{k,s+1} \leq d_{k,s} + t^{\max}_{(s,s+1)}, \quad \forall k \in K,\; s = 1,\dots,|S|-1.
$$

**(C7) Turnaround at terminals:**
$$
a_{k+1,1} \geq d_{k,|S|} + t^{\text{turn}}, \quad \forall k = 1,\dots,|K|-1.
$$

### 6.4 Headway and Train Ordering

**(C8) Minimum and maximum headway between consecutive trains:**
$$
h^{\min} \leq a_{k+1,s} - a_{k,s} \leq h^{\max}, \quad \forall k,\; s.
$$
(Equivalently replace $a$ with $d$ if departure-headway is desired.)

**(C9) Train ordering (no overtaking):**
$$
z_{k,k',s} + z_{k',k,s} = 1, \quad \forall k < k',\; s,
$$
$$
a_{k',s} - a_{k,s} \geq h^{\min} z_{k,k',s} - M (1 - z_{k,k',s}), \quad \forall k < k',\; s.
$$

### 6.5 Passenger Flow and Demand

**(C10) Passenger boarding at station $s$ (origin of OD pair $p$):**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \lambda_{p,k,s} = d_{p,t(s)} \, \Delta t, \quad \forall p \in P,\; s = o_p,
$$
where $t(s)$ is the time interval containing $d_{k,s}$.

**(C11) Passenger alighting at destination:**
$$
\text{load}_{k,s+1} = \text{load}_{k,s} + \sum_{p : o_p = s} \lambda_{p,k,s} - \sum_{p : d_p = s} \lambda_{p,k,s}, \quad \forall k, s.
$$

**(C12) Capacity coupling with stopping:**
$$
\sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{p,k,s} \leq \text{cap}_k \, x_{k,s}, \quad \forall k, s.
$$

**(C13) Waiting-time definition (piecewise-constant demand):**
$$
w_{p,s} \geq d_{k,s} - (t_p^{\text{des}} + 0.5 \Delta t) - M (1 - \eta_{p,k,s}), \quad \forall p,\; s = o_p,\; k,
$$
$$
w_{p,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall p, s,
$$
where $\eta_{p,k,s} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates that OD-$p$ passengers at $s$ actually board train $k$ (linked to $\lambda_{p,k,s}$ via $\eta_{p,k,s} \geq \lambda_{p,k,s} / M'$).

### 6.6 Rolling-Stock Circulation

**(C14) Composition requires sufficient rolling-stock units:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R} \pi_{r,k} = \sum_{i \in I} i \, y_{k,i}, \quad \forall k \in K.
$$

**(C15) Each unit assigned to at most one train at a time:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \pi_{r,k} \leq 1, \quad \forall r \in R.
$$

**(C16) Transfer continuity (a unit released by train $k$ can be used by train $k+1$):**
$$
\sigma_{r,k,k+1} \leq \pi_{r,k}, \quad \sigma_{r,k,k+1} \leq \pi_{r,k+1}, \quad \forall r,\; k = 1,\dots,|K|-1.
$$

**(C17) Sufficient transfers to cover next composition:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R} \sigma_{r,k,k+1} = \sum_{i \in I} i \, y_{k+1,i} - \sum_{i \in I} i \, y_{k,i} + \sum_{r \in R} \pi_{r,k+1} - \sum_{r \in R} \pi_{r,k}, \quad \forall k.
$$

**(C18) Transfer feasibility (time window):**
$$
\sigma_{r,k,k+1} \leq \mathbb{1}\!\left[d_{k,|S|} + t^{\text{turn}} \leq a_{k+1,1}\right], \quad \forall r, k.
$$

### 6.7 Timetable Deviation

**(C19) Absolute deviation (linearized):**
$$
\delta_{k,s} \geq d_{k,s} - \bar{d}_{k,s}, \quad \delta_{k,s} \geq \bar{d}_{k,s} - d_{k,s}, \quad \forall k, s.
$$

### 6.8 MPC Horizon and Boundary Conditions

**(C20) Horizon boundary:**
$$
t_0 \leq a_{k,s},\, d_{k,s} \leq t_0 + N_H, \quad \forall k, s.
$$

**(C21) Initial state (current positions of in-service trains at MPC step $t_0$):**
$$
a_{k,s_0(k)} = \bar{a}_{k,s_0(k)}^0, \quad \forall k \text{ already in service},
$$
where $s_0(k)$ is the current station of train $k$.

---

## 7. Notes on Linearization

| Nonlinear / discrete element | Linearization technique |
|---|---|
| $C_i \cdot y_{k,i}$ in capacity | Auxiliary variable $\text{cap}_k$ with (C2) |
| Conditional dwell (depends on $x_{k,s}$) | Big-M constraints (C5) |
| Absolute deviation $\lvert d_{k,s} - \bar{d}_{k,s}\rvert$ | Auxiliary $\delta_{k,s}$ with (C19) |
| Indicator $\eta_{p,k,s}$ for boarding | Big-M linking to $\lambda_{p,k,s}$ |
| Composition size $\sum_i i \, y_{k,i}$ | Linear combination of binaries |

---

## 8. Role in the Learning-Based MPC Framework

In the proposed **learning-based MPC** scheme:

1. **Presolve techniques** prune a subset of the binary variables ($x_{k,s}$, $y_{k,i}$, $\pi_{r,k}$) using logical rules (e.g., fixed composition at terminals, infeasible stopping patterns).
2. **LSTM networks** predict the remaining binary decisions from observed state features (current train positions, time-varying demand, headway state).
3. With the binary variables fixed, the MILP reduces to a **linear program (LP)** that yields the continuous timetable $(a_{k,s}, d_{k,s}, \tau_{k,s}, \lambda_{p,k,s})$ in real time.
4. The procedure is repeated at each MPC step $t_0 \leftarrow t_0 + \Delta t^{\text{MPC}}$, providing a rolling-horizon rescheduling policy that is **scalable** (fast online LP) and **constraint-satisfying** (binary feasibility guaranteed by the MILP structure).

---

### Summary

The model above is a complete **MILP** that captures:

- **Time-varying sectional passenger demand** (piecewise-constant, intervals $t \in T$),
- **Flexible train composition** (binary $y_{k,i}$),
- **Rolling-stock circulation** (binary $\pi_{r,k}, \sigma_{r,k,k'}$),
- **Train stopping plans** (binary $x_{k,s}$),
- **Timetable variables** ($a_{k,s}, d_{k,s}, \tau_{k,s}$),
- **Passenger waiting and travel times** ($w_{p,s}$, $\text{load}_{k,s}$),
- **MPC horizon and boundary conditions** (C20–C21),

with all nonlinear/conditional elements linearized via standard Big-M and auxiliary-variable techniques. The resulting formulation is directly solvable by off-the-shelf MILP solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) and is amenable to the learning-based MPC decomposition described in the introduction.

# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Complete Linear Model

Below are the equations extracted from the generated model. The formulation integrates train timetabling (retiming, reordering, rerouting) with speed management (speed profile selection) under a partial segment blockage scenario.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $s \in \mathcal{S}$ | Stations/segments along the line |
| $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ | Trains |
| $k \in \mathcal{K}$ | Discretized speed levels |
| $p \in \mathcal{P}$ | Position–time discretization points within a segment |
| $t \in \mathcal{T\!H}$ | Coarse time grid (reroute capacity) |
| $s_D$ | The disrupted (partially blocked) segment |
| $\mathcal{R}_i$ | Ordered set of segments on train $i$'s route |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\ell_s$ | Length of segment $s$ (km) |
| $\tau$ | Discretization time step (h) |
| $V_k$ | Speed of level $k$ (km/h) |
| $a_{\max}, d_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration (km/h²) |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway (h) |
| $d_{\min}, d_{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time (h) |
| $t_D^{s}, t_D^{e}$ | Disruption window start / end |
| $C^{\text{rr}}$ | Reroute capacity on opposite track |
| $E_k$ | Energy rate at speed level $k$ (piecewise-linear in speed) |
| $o_i, d_i$ | Origin / destination station of train $i$ |
| $\delta_i$ | Direction of train $i \in \{+1, -1\}$ |
| $e_i$ | Earliest departure from origin |
| $A_i^{\text{sch}}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $w_1, w_2$ | Objective weights (delay / energy) |

---

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| $x_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Train $i$ traverses segment $s$ |
| $r_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Train $i$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $z_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Train $i$ precedes $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $y_{i,s,p,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Train $i$ at position $p$ on segment $s$ uses speed level $k$ |
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at segment $s$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from segment $s$ |
| $v_{i,s,p}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Speed at position $p$ on segment $s$ |
| $\Delta_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Running time on segment $s$ |
| $\text{delay}_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Total delay of train $i$ |
| $\text{cap}_{s,t}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Occupancy on segment $s$ at time $t$ (conflict count) |

---

## Objective Function

Minimize weighted total delay plus total energy consumption:

$$
\min \; w_1 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \text{delay}_i \;+\; w_2 \sum_{(i,s,p)\in \mathcal{ISP}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} E_k \, y_{i,s,p,k}
$$

---

## Constraints

### (C1) Route consistency
Trains use at least one segment and traverse a connected chain from origin to destination:

$$
\sum_{(i,s)\in \mathcal{IS}} x_{i,s} \;\ge\; 1 \qquad \forall i
$$

$$
x_{i,s'} - x_{i,s} = 0 \qquad \forall i, \; s, s' \text{ consecutive on route } \mathcal{R}_i
$$

### (C2) Reroute linking
Rerouting only permitted on the disrupted segment:

$$
r_{i,s} = 0 \qquad \forall (i,s) : s \ne s_D
$$
$$
r_{i,s_D} \le x_{i,s_D} \qquad \forall i
$$

### (C3)–(C4) Speed-level selection and speed value

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} y_{i,s,p,k} = x_{i,s} \qquad \forall (i,s,p)\in\mathcal{ISP}
$$

$$
v_{i,s,p} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} V_k \, y_{i,s,p,k} \qquad \forall (i,s,p)\in\mathcal{ISP}
$$

### (C5) Traction dynamics (acceleration/deceleration limits)

$$
v_{i,s,p+1} - v_{i,s,p} \le a_{\max}\,\tau \qquad \forall (i,s,p),\, p \ne |\mathcal{P}|
$$

$$
v_{i,s,p} - v_{i,s,p+1} \le d_{\max}\,\tau \qquad \forall (i,s,p),\, p \ne |\mathcal{P}|
$$

### (C6) Running time and time propagation

Running time is a linear function of the chosen speed levels:

$$
\Delta_{i,s} = \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \frac{\ell_s}{|\mathcal{P}|\,V_k}\, y_{i,s,p,k} \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS}
$$

$$
a_{i,s} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} + \Delta_{i,s} \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS}
$$

Sequence linking between consecutive segments on route:

$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s'} + \Delta_{i,s'} \qquad \forall i, \; s' \text{ predecessor of } s \text{ on } \mathcal{R}_i
$$

### (C7) Dwell-time bounds (intermediate stations only)

$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \ge d_{\min}, \qquad \text{dep}_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le d_{\max}
$$

### (C8) Earliest departure from origin

$$
\text{dep}_{i,o_i} \ge e_i \qquad \forall i
$$

### (C9) Delay definition

$$
\text{delay}_i \ge a_{i,s_{\text{last}}} - A_i^{\text{sch}} \qquad \forall i
$$

### (C10) Headway ordering (same-direction trains)

$$
a_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s} + h_{\min} - M\,(1 - z_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall (i,j,s) \in \mathcal{JIS},\; \delta_i=\delta_j
$$

$$
z_{i,j,s} + z_{j,i,s} = 1 \qquad \forall (i,j,s) \text{ with same direction}
$$

### (C11) Cross-direction separation (bidirectional rerouting conflicts)

For opposing trains that both use the disrupted segment:

$$
a_{i,s_D} - a_{j,s_D} \ge h_{\min} - M\,(2 - x_{i,s_D} - x_{j,s_D}) \qquad \forall i, j : \delta_i \ne \delta_j
$$

$$
a_{j,s_D} - a_{i,s_D} \ge h_{\min} - M\,(2 - x_{i,s_D} - x_{j,s_D}) \qquad \forall i, j : \delta_i \ne \delta_j
$$

### (C12) Disruption-window blockage (mandatory reroute)

If a train in the blocked direction enters $s_D$ within the disruption window, it must reroute:

$$
a_{i,s_D} - t_D^{s} \le M\,(1 - r_{i,s_D}) \qquad \forall i : \delta_i = \delta_{\text{block}}
$$

$$

# Complete MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the best (most complete and internally consistent) model, combining the strongest elements of the generated formulations. It is a **time-indexed MILP** with explicit coupling between rescheduling decisions and speed/energy decisions.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations along the line, indexed by $s$ |
| $S^{seg}$ | Set of segments $(s, s+1)$, $s = 1,\dots,|S|-1$ |
| $T$ | Set of discrete time steps (1-second resolution), indexed by $t$ |
| $T^{block} = \{t_{start},\dots,t_{end}\}$ | Disruption time window |
| $D = \{+,-\}$ | Set of directions |
| $I_d \subseteq I$ | Trains traveling in direction $d$ |
| $I^{d^*}$ | Trains traveling in the **blocked** direction $d^*$ |

**Disruption parameters:** blocked segment $s^*$, blocked direction $d^*$, window $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $t^{sched,arr}_{i,s},\; t^{sched,dep}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $dwell^{\min}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $run^{\min}_{i,s},\; run^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Min / max running time on segment $(s,s+1)$ |
| $v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ | Speed bounds |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time |
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $(s,s+1)$ |
| $\Delta t$ | Time-step length |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Weights: delay cost, energy weight, cancellation cost |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $K$ | Number of breakpoints for energy linearization |
| $(\bar v_k, \bar e_k)$ | Breakpoints of piecewise-linear energy–speed curve |
| $r^{cap}$ | Rerouting capacity per direction |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Binary variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| $x_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ **departs** station $s$ at time $t$ |
| $y_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ **arrives** at station $s$ at time $t$ |
| $r_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is **rerouted** to opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $o_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ **precedes** train $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is **cancelled** |

### Continuous variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| $v_{i,s,t} \ge 0$ | Speed of train $i$ on segment $s$ at time $t$ |
| $e_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $\delta_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $A_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $D_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\lambda_{i,s,k} \ge 0$ | Convex-combination weights over energy breakpoints |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_{i,s}
\;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S^{seg}} e_{i,s}
\;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in I} c_i
$$

Weighted sum of **(i)** total passenger arrival delay, **(ii)** total energy consumption, **(iii)** number of cancellations.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Departure / Arrival uniqueness

$$
\sum_{t \in T} x_{i,s,t} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S \tag{C1}
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T} y_{i,s,t} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S \tag{C2}
$$

### 5.2 Linking timing variables to actual times

$$
A_{i,s} = \sum_{t \in T} t \cdot y_{i,s,t} \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C3}
$$
$$
D_{i,s} = \sum_{t \in T} t \cdot x_{i,s,t} \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C4}
$$

### 5.3 Dwell time

$$
D_{i,s} \ge A_{i,s} + dwell^{\min}_{i,s} - M\,c_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S \tag{C5}
$$

### 5.4 Running time between consecutive stations

$$
A_{i,s+1} \ge D_{i,s} + run^{\min}_{i,s} - M\,c_i \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S^{seg} \tag{C6}
$$
$$
A_{i,s+1} \le D_{i,s} + run^{\max}_{i,s} + M\,c_i \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S^{seg} \tag{C7}
$$

### 5.5 Speed profile coupling

Speed bounds:
$$
v^{\min}(1 - c_i) \le v_{i,s,t} \le v^{\max}(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i, s, t \tag{C8}
$$

Distance consistency (integral of speed over segment):
$$
\sum_{t \in T} v_{i,s,t}\,\Delta t \;\ge\; L_s - M\,c_i \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S^{seg} \tag{C9}
$$

Acceleration / deceleration limits:
$$
-M(1-c_i) \le \frac{v_{i,s,t+1} - v_{i,s,t}}{\Delta t} \le a^{\max} + M c_i \qquad \forall i, s, t \tag{C10}
$$
$$
-b^{\max} - M c_i \le \frac{v_{i,s,t+1} - v_{i,s,t}}{\Delta t} \le M(1-c_i) \qquad \forall i, s, t \tag{C11}
$$

### 5.6 Energy consumption — piecewise linearization

Convex combination over breakpoints:
$$
v_{i,s,t} = \sum_{k=1}^{K} \lambda_{i,s,k}\,\bar v_k, \qquad
\sum_{k=1}^{K} \lambda_{i,s,k} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, s, t \tag{C12}
$$
$$
e_{i,s} \ge \sum_{k=1}^{K} \lambda_{i,s,k}\,\bar e_k \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S^{seg} \tag{C13}
$$

### 5.7 Disruption / blockage constraints

If train $i$ (in blocked direction $d^*$) is **not** rerouted on segment $s^*$, it may not traverse it during $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$:
$$
y_{i,s^*,t} + x_{i,s^*,t} \le 1 - r_{i,s^*} \qquad \forall i \in I^{d^*},\; t \in T^{block} \tag{C14}
$$

Rerouting only allowed on the blocked segment:
$$
r_{i,s} = 0 \qquad \forall i,\; s \neq s^* \tag{C15}
$$

### 5.8 Rerouting capacity

$$
\sum_{i \in I_d} r_{i,s^*} \le r^{cap} \qquad \forall d \in D \tag{C16}
$$

### 5.9 Train ordering / conflict-free sequencing

$$
o_{i,j,s} + o_{j,i,s} = 1 \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; s \in S^{seg} \tag{C17}
$$

Headway enforcement — if $i$ precedes $j$:
$$
D_{j,s} \ge D_{i,s} + h - M(1 - o_{i,j,s}) - M(c_i + c_j) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; s \in S^{seg} \tag{C18}
$$

### 5.10 Bidirectional conflict on shared (rerouted) track

If trains $i$ and $j$ (opposite directions) both use segment $s^*$ via rerouting, they must be separated in time:
$$
D_{j,s^*} \ge A_{i,s^*+1} + h - M(1 - r_{i,s^*}) - M(1 - r_{j,s^*}) - M(c_i + c_j) \tag{C19}
$$
$$
D_{i,s^*} \ge A_{j,s^*+1} + h - M(1 - r_{i,s^*}) - M(1 - r_{j,s^*}) - M(c_i + c_j) \tag{C20}
$$

### 5.11 Cancellation consistency

$$
r_{i,s} \le 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C21}
$$
$$
A_{i,s} \le M(1 - c_i), \quad D_{i,s} \le M(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C22}
$$

### 5.12 Delay definition

$$
\delta_{i,s} \ge A_{i,s} - t^{sched,arr}_{i,s} - M\,c_i \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C23}
$$
$$
\delta_{i,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C24}
$$

### 5.13 Station sequence consistency

$$
A_{i,s} \le D_{i,s} \le A_{i,s+1} \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S^{seg} \tag{C25}
$$
$$
0 \le A_{i,s},\; D_{i,s} \le |T| \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C26}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Element | Count |
|---------|-------|
| Binary variables | $2|I||S||T| + |I||S| + |I|^2|S^{seg}| + |I|$ |
| Continuous variables | $|I||S^{seg}||T| + |I||S^{seg}| + 3|I||S| + |I||S^{seg}|K$ |
| Constraints | $O(|I||S||T| + |I|^2|S^{seg}|)$ |

**Model type:** Large-scale MILP, solvable via branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut (CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP).

---

## 7. Key Modeling Assumptions (marked)

1. **Discrete time resolution** of 1 second (can be coarsened to 15–30 s for tractability).
2. **Piecewise-linear energy** — convex approximation of $E(v)$ with $K$ breakpoints.
3. **Constant acceleration/deceleration limits** — enforced via C10–C11.
4. **Fixed minimum dwell times** — no variable dwell decisions.
5. **Known disruption window** — deterministic, no real-time uncertainty.
6. **Single-track bidirectional operation** during rerouting — enforced by C19–C20.
7. **No overtaking within a segment** — ordering variables $o_{i,j,s}$ fix the sequence.
8. **Big-M formulation** — $M$ chosen as $T^{\max}$ (largest possible time value).
9. **Rerouting restricted to the blocked segment** — enforced by C15.

---

## 8. Why This Model Is Best

- **Complete coupling:** explicitly links rescheduling (timing, ordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profiles, energy) — the core of TRSMP.
- **Conflict-free guarantee:** ordering (C17–C18) and bidirectional separation (C19–C20) rigorously resolve both same-direction and opposite-direction conflicts on shared track.
- **Linear structure:** all nonlinearities (energy–speed, running time) are handled via piecewise-linearization and big-M, yielding a pure MILP.
- **Decomposition-ready:** the ordering/rerouting coupling constraints (C17–C20) are natural candidates for Lagrangian relaxation or Benders-style decomposition, matching the paper's proposed solution framework.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a partial segment blockage occurs on one track of a double-track line during a known disruption time window. Trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track within this window, requiring precise coordination of bidirectional traffic.

**Assumptions (marked as such where information is inferred):**

- **(A1)** The railway line is discretized into a set of segments $e \in \mathcal{E}$ connecting consecutive stations $s \in \mathcal{S}$. Each segment has a physical length $L_e$ and a free-flow running time $T_e^{\min}$.
- **(A2)** The disruption affects a subset of segments $\mathcal{E}^D \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ during a time window $[t^D_{\text{start}}, t^D_{\text{end}}]$. During this window, only one track is available on affected segments (unidirectional capacity).
- **(A3)** Trains belong to two directions: $\mathcal{K}^{\text{up}}$ (up) and $\mathcal{K}^{\text{down}}$ (down). Each train $k \in \mathcal{K} = \mathcal{K}^{\text{up}} \cup \mathcal{K}^{\text{down}}$ has a scheduled origin, destination, and original timetable.
- **(A4)** Speed profiles are approximated by a finite set of discrete speed levels $\mathcal{V} = \{v_1, v_2, \dots, v_{|\mathcal{V}|}\}$ per segment, each associated with a running time and energy consumption. *(Reasonable assumption for linearization.)*
- **(A5)** Dwell times at stations are bounded: $d_k^{\min} \le d_{k,s} \le d_k^{\max}$.
- **(A6)** Headway constraints apply between consecutive trains on the same track in the same direction.
- **(A7)** Rerouting is permitted only within the disruption window and only on affected segments.
- **(A8)** Acceleration/deceleration transitions between segments are captured via minimum transition times. *(Simplification for tractability.)*

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{E}^D \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | Set of disrupted segments |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{K}^{\text{up}}, \mathcal{K}^{\text{down}}$ | Up and down direction trains |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $v$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_e$ | Set of available routes (tracks) on segment $e$; $\mathcal{R}_e = \{1,2\}$ normally, $\{1\}$ during disruption |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetabling Variables

- $a_{k,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: arrival time of train $k$ at station $s$
- $d_{k,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: departure time of train $k$ from station $s$
- $x_{k,e} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ traverses segment $e$; 0 otherwise (allows cancellation)
- $r_{k,e} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ uses the opposite track on segment $e$ (rerouting); 0 otherwise
- $y_{k,k',e} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ precedes train $k'$ on segment $e$; 0 otherwise (ordering variable)

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

- $\delta_{k,e,v} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ uses speed level $v$ on segment $e$; 0 otherwise
- $\tau_{k,e} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: actual running time of train $k$ on segment $e$
- $E_{k,e} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: energy consumption of train $k$ on segment $e$

### 3.3 Auxiliary Variables

- $z_{k,k',e} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $k$ and $k'$ are in conflict on segment $e$ (used for headway linearization)

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \quad
\alpha \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \max(0, a_{k,s} - a_{k,s}^{\text{sch}}) + \max(0, d_{k,s} - d_{k,s}^{\text{sch}}) \right)
+ \beta \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} E_{k,e}
+ \gamma \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} (1 - x_{k,e})
$$

where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma > 0$ are weighting parameters, and $a_{k,s}^{\text{sch}}, d_{k,s}^{\text{sch}}$ are scheduled times.

**Linearization of delay:**

Introduce $\Delta^a_{k,s}, \Delta^d_{k,s} \ge 0$ with:

$$
\Delta^a_{k,s} \ge a_{k,s} - a_{k,s}^{\text{sch}}, \quad \Delta^d_{k,s} \ge d_{k,s} - d_{k,s}^{\text{sch}}
$$

Objective becomes:

$$
\min \quad
\alpha \sum_{k,s} (\Delta^a_{k,s} + \Delta^d_{k,s})
+ \beta \sum_{k,e} E_{k,e}
+ \gamma \sum_{k,e} (1 - x_{k,e})
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Constraints

**(C1) Departure after arrival (dwell time):**

$$
d_{k,s} - a_{k,s} \ge d_k^{\min} \cdot x_{k,e(s)} \quad \forall k, s
$$

$$
d_{k,s} - a_{k,s} \le d_k^{\max} \quad \forall k, s
$$

**(C2) Segment running time linking arrival and departure:**

For segment $e = (s, s')$:

$$
a_{k,s'} - d_{k,s} \ge \tau_{k,e} - M(1 - x_{k,e}) \quad \forall k, e
$$

$$
a_{k,s'} - d_{k,s} \le \tau_{k,e} + M(1 - x_{k,e}) \quad \forall k, e
$$

where $M$ is a sufficiently large constant.

**(C3) Running time selection via speed levels:**

$$
\tau_{k,e} = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \tau_{e,v} \cdot \delta_{k,e,v} \quad \forall k, e
$$

$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \delta_{k,e,v} = x_{k,e} \quad \forall k, e
$$

**(C4) Energy consumption:**

$$
E_{k,e} = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} E_{e,v} \cdot \delta_{k,e,v} \quad \forall k, e
$$

where $E_{e,v}$ is the energy consumed at speed level $v$ on segment $e$.

### 5.2 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

**(C5) Rerouting only on disrupted segments:**

$$
r_{k,e} = 0 \quad \forall k, e \notin \mathcal{E}^D
$$

**(C6) Rerouting only during disruption window:**

If train $k$ enters segment $e \in \mathcal{E}^D$ during $[t^D_{\text{start}}, t^D_{\text{end}}]$, it must reroute:

$$
d_{k,s} \ge t^D_{\text{start}} - M(1 - r_{k,e}) \quad \forall k, e = (s,s') \in \mathcal{E}^D
$$

$$
d_{k,s} \le t^D_{\text{end}} + M \cdot r_{k,e} \quad \forall k, e = (s,s') \in \mathcal{E}^D
$$

**(C7) Track capacity on disrupted segments:**

During the disruption window, only one train (regardless of direction) may occupy a disrupted segment:

$$
y_{k,k',e} + y_{k',k,e} = 1 \quad \forall k \ne k', e \in \mathcal{E}^D \text{ if both traverse } e
$$

### 5.3 Conflict-Free and Headway Constraints

**(C8) Headway between consecutive trains on the same segment:**

For any pair $k, k'$ traversing segment $e$ in the same direction:

$$
d_{k',s} - d_{k,s} \ge h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{k,k',e}) \quad \forall k \ne k', e = (s,s')
$$

**(C9) Bidirectional conflict on shared track (rerouted segments):**

If train $k$ (up) and $k'$ (down) both use the same track on segment $e$:

$$
a_{k',s'} - d_{k,s} \ge h^{\text{bi}} - M(1 - y_{k,k',e}) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}^{\text{up}}, k' \in \mathcal{K}^{\text{down}}, e \in \mathcal{E}^D
$$

**(C10) Ordering consistency:**

$$
y_{k,k',e} + y_{k',k,e} \le 1 \quad \forall k \ne k', e
$$

$$
y_{k,k',e} + y_{k',k,e} \ge x_{k,e} + x_{k',e} - 1 \quad \forall k \ne k', e
$$

### 5.4 Speed Profile Feasibility

**(C11) Speed transition feasibility:**

Between consecutive segments, the speed change must be physically achievable:

$$
\delta_{k,e,v} + \delta_{k,e',v'} \le 1 \quad \text{if } |v - v'| > \Delta v^{\max}
$$

where $e, e'$ are consecutive segments and $\Delta v^{\max}$ is the maximum allowable speed change.

**(C12) Minimum running time:**

$$
\tau_{k,e} \ge T_e^{\min} \cdot x_{k,e} \quad \forall k, e
$$

### 5.5 Cancellation and Service Constraints

**(C13) Train cancellation:**

$$
x_{k,e} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} x_{k,e} \le |\mathcal{E}| \quad \forall k
$$

If a train is cancelled, all its segment variables are zero.

**(C14) Origin-destination consistency:**

For each train $k$ with origin $s_k^o$ and destination $s_k^d$:

$$
x_{k,e} = 1 \text{ for all } e \text{ on the path from } s_k^o \text{ to } s_k^d \text{ if not cancelled}
$$

### 5.6 Time Window Constraints

**(C15) Arrival/departure time bounds:**

$$
a_{k,s} \in [a_{k,s}^{\min}, a_{k,s}^{\max}], \quad d_{k,s} \in [d_{k,s}^{\min}, d_{k,s}^{\max}] \quad \forall k, s
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \alpha \sum_{k,s} (\Delta^a_{k,s} + \Delta^d_{k,s}) + \beta \sum_{k,e} E_{k,e} + \gamma \sum_{k,e} (1 - x_{k,e}) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C15)} \\
& a_{k,s}, d_{k,s}, \tau_{k,e}, E_{k,e}, \Delta^a_{k,s}, \Delta^d_{k,s} \ge 0 \\
& x_{k,e}, r_{k,e}, y_{k,k',e}, \delta_{k,e,v}, z_{k,k',e} \in \{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Model Properties

- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear in the decision variables. The only nonlinearity (max in delay) is linearized via auxiliary variables.
- **MILP Structure:** Binary variables handle routing, ordering, speed level selection, and cancellation; continuous variables handle timing and energy.
- **Coupling:** The model couples timetabling (TRP) and speed management (TSMP) through constraints (C2)–(C4), ensuring that the rescheduled timetable is executable by the selected speed profiles.
- **Conflict Resolution:** Constraints (C7)–(C10) ensure conflict-free operation of bidirectional trains on shared tracks during rerouting.

---

## 8. Notes on Assumptions and Simplifications

1. **Discrete speed levels** approximate continuous speed profiles; finer discretization improves accuracy at computational cost.
2. **Transition constraints** (C11) are simplified; a more detailed model could include acceleration/deceleration dynamics.
3. **Energy consumption** is precomputed per speed level and segment; this is a standard linearization.
4. **Disruption window** is assumed known and fixed; stochastic extensions are possible.
5. **Headway times** $h^{\min}$ and $h^{\text{bi}}$ are assumed constant; in practice, they may depend on speed and infrastructure.

This MILP provides a complete, linear formulation for the integrated TRSMP under partial segment blockages, suitable for solution via commercial solvers or decomposition-based algorithms as described in the original framework.
