After evaluating the three generated models, I select **Model 3** as the best. It provides the most complete and rigorous MILP formulation, with explicit McCormick linearization for the bilinear energy term, clear SOS2 piecewise-linearization of the quadratic Davis resistance, and well-structured disruption/rerouting constraints. Below is the finalized, complete linear model.

---

# Complete MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $i, j \in \mathcal{T} = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | Trains |
| $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,M\}$ | Stations |
| $b \in \mathcal{B} = \{1,\dots,|\mathcal{B}|\}$ | Track blocks (segments between consecutive stations) |
| $k \in \mathcal{K} = \{0,\dots,K_{\max}\}$ | Discretized time steps (interval $\Delta t$) |
| $d \in \mathcal{D} = \{U, D\}$ | Directions (Up / Down) |
| $p \in \mathcal{P} = \{1,\dots,P\}$ | Breakpoints for piecewise-linear approximation of $v^2$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ (km) |
| $V_{\max}, V_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum operating speed (km/h) |
| $A_{\max}, D_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (m/s²) |
| $t^{\text{sched,arr}}_{i,s},\ t^{\text{sched,dep}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $\text{dwell}^{\min}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time |
| $\text{dwell}^{\text{slack}}$ | Maximum dwell slack |
| $\text{dir}_i$ | Direction of train $i$ |
| $\text{disruption}_b$ | 1 if block $b$ is disrupted |
| $t^{\text{dis,start}}_b,\ t^{\text{dis,end}}_b$ | Disruption time window for block $b$ |
| $c_{\text{delay}}, c_{\text{energy}}, c_{\text{cancel}}$ | Objective weights |
| $\alpha_i, \beta_i, \gamma_i$ | Davis equation coefficients |
| $m_i$ | Train mass (kg) |
| $g$ | Gravitational acceleration |
| $\eta_{\text{motor}}$ | Motor efficiency |
| $\Delta t$ | Time step (h) |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time |
| $R_{\max}$ | Maximum rerouted blocks per train |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $V^{\text{init}}_i, V^{\text{final}}_i$ | Initial / final speeds |
| $F^{\max}_{\text{tract}}$ | Maximum tractive force |
| $V_p$ | Breakpoint values for $v^2$ linearization |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \quad \text{(actual arrival/departure times)}$$
$$\text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ \text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \quad \text{(delays)}$$
$$v_{i,b,k} \in [0, V_{\max}] \quad \text{(speed, km/h)}$$
$$p_{i,b,k} \in [0, L_b] \quad \text{(position, km)}$$
$$e_i \ge 0 \quad \text{(energy, kWh)}$$
$$F^{\text{tract}}_{i,b,k},\ F^{\text{brake}}_{i,b,k} \ge 0 \quad \text{(tractive/braking forces)}$$
$$\hat{v}^2_{i,b,k} \ge 0 \quad \text{(auxiliary for } v^2\text{)}$$
$$\lambda_{i,b,k,p} \in [0,1] \quad \text{(SOS2 weights)}$$
$$\phi_{i,b,k} \ge 0 \quad \text{(McCormick auxiliary for } F^{\text{tract}}\cdot v\text{)}$$
$$t^{\text{enter}}_{i,b},\ t^{\text{exit}}_{i,b} \ge 0 \quad \text{(block entry/exit times)}$$

**Binary:**
$$x_{i,b},\ r_{i,b},\ y_{i,j,b,k},\ z_{i,b,k},\ w_{i,j,b,k},\ \text{cancel}_i \in \{0,1\}$$

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\ Z = c_{\text{delay}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\bigl(\text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} + \text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}\bigr)
+ c_{\text{energy}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} e_i
+ c_{\text{cancel}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\text{cancel}_i
$$

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Delay Definitions
$$
\text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \ge t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{sched,arr}}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{sched,dep}}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ \text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge 0
$$

### (C2) Dwell Time
$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \ge \text{dwell}^{\min}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \le \text{dwell}^{\min}_{i,s} + \text{dwell}^{\text{slack}} \quad \forall i,s
$$

### (C3) Position Update (Linearized)
$$
p_{i,b,k+1} = p_{i,b,k} + v_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (C4) Speed Update (Newton's Law, Linearized)
$$
v_{i,b,k+1} = v_{i,b,k} + \frac{\Delta t}{m_i}\Bigl(F^{\text{tract}}_{i,b,k} - F^{\text{brake}}_{i,b,k} - \alpha_i m_i g - \beta_i m_i g\, v_{i,b,k} - \gamma_i m_i g\, \hat{v}^2_{i,b,k}\Bigr) \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (C5) Piecewise-Linear Approximation of $v^2$
$$
\hat{v}^2_{i,b,k} = \sum_{p=1}^{P}\lambda_{i,b,k,p}\,V_p^2,\quad
v_{i,b,k} = \sum_{p=1}^{P}\lambda_{i,b,k,p}\,V_p \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
\sum_{p=1}^{P}\lambda_{i,b,k,p}=1,\quad \lambda_{i,b,k,p}\ge 0 \quad \text{(SOS2 set)}
$$

### (C6) Speed Limits
$$
V_{\min}\,z_{i,b,k} \le v_{i,b,k} \le V_{\max}\,z_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (C7) Acceleration / Deceleration Limits
$$
v_{i,b,k+1} - v_{i,b,k} \le A_{\max}\,\Delta t \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
v_{i,b,k} - v_{i,b,k+1} \le D_{\max}\,\Delta t \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (C8) Block Occupancy
$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} z_{i,b,k} \le 1 + \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} r_{i,b} \quad \forall b,k
$$
$$
z_{i,b,k} \le x_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (C9) Bidirectional Conflict Resolution
For trains $i,j$ with $\text{dir}_i \ne \text{dir}_j$ sharing rerouted block $b$:
$$
y_{i,j,b,k} + y_{j,i,b,k} \ge z_{i,b,k} + z_{j,b,k} - 1 \quad \forall i,j,b,k
$$
$$
t^{\text{enter}}_{j,b} \ge t^{\text{exit}}_{i,b} + h - M\,(1 - y_{i,j,b,k}) \quad \forall i,j,b,k
$$

### (C10) Disruption Constraints
$$
z_{i,b,k} \le r_{i,b} + (1 - \text{disruption}_b) \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
For $k \in [t^{\text{dis,start}}_b, t^{\text{dis,end}}_b]$ with $\text{disruption}_b = 1$:
$$
z_{i,b,k} \le r_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (C11) Rerouting Constraints
$$
r_{i,b} \le \text{disruption}_b \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
r_{i,b} \le x_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}} r_{i,b} \le R_{\max} \quad \forall i
$$

### (C12) Block Traversal Continuity
$$
t^{\text{exit}}_{i,b} - t^{\text{enter}}_{i,b} \ge \frac{L_b}{V_{\max}} - M(1 - x_{i,b}) \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
t^{\text{exit}}_{i,b} - t^{\text{enter}}_{i,b} \le \frac{L_b}{V_{\min}} + M(1 - x_{i,b}) \quad \forall i,b
$$

### (C13) Station–Block Interface
$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} = t^{\text{exit}}_{i,b(s)} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} = t^{\text{enter}}_{i,b(s+1)} \quad \forall i,s
$$

### (C14) Energy Consumption (McCormick Linearization)
$$
e_i = \frac{\Delta t}{\eta_{\text{motor}}}\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \phi_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i
$$
$$
\phi_{i,b,k} \ge 0,\quad \phi_{i,b,k} \ge V_{\max}\,F^{\text{tract}}_{i,b,k} + F^{\max}_{\text{tract}}\,v_{i,b,k} - V_{\max}F^{\max}_{\text{tract}}
$$
$$
\phi_{i,b,k} \le V_{\max}\,F^{\text{tract}}_{i,b,k},\quad \phi_{i,b,k} \le F^{\max}_{\text{tract}}\,v_{i,b,k}
$$

### (C15) Cancellation
$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \le M(1 - \text{cancel}_i) + t^{\text{sched,arr}}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
x_{i,b} \le 1 - \text{cancel}_i \quad \forall i,b
$$

### (C16) Terminal Conditions
$$
v_{i,b,0} = V^{\text{init}}_i,\quad v_{i,b,K_{\max}} = V^{\text{final}}_i \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
p_{i,b,0} = 0,\quad p_{i,b,K_{\max}} = L_b\,x_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b
$$

### (C17) Ordering Constraints
For trains $i,j$ in same direction on same block:
$$
y_{i,j,b,k} + y_{j,i,b,k} \ge z_{i,b,k} + z_{j,b,k} - 1 \quad \forall i,j,b,k
$$
$$
y_{i,j,b,k} + y_{j,i,b,k} \le 1 \quad \forall i,j,b,k
$$

### (C18) Headway Between Consecutive Trains
$$
t^{\text{enter}}_{j,b} \ge t^{\text{enter}}_{i,b} + h - M(1 - y_{i,j,b,k}) \quad \forall i,j,b,k
$$

### (C19) Variable Domains
$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s},\ \text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ \text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge 0
$$
$$
0 \le v_{i,b,k} \le V_{\max},\quad 0 \le p_{i,b,k} \le L_b
$$
$$
e_i \ge 0,\quad F^{\text{tract}}_{i,b,k},\ F^{\text{brake}}_{i,b,k} \ge 0
$$
$$
x_{i,b},\ r_{i,b},\ y_{i,j,b,k},\ z_{i,b,k},\ w_{i,j,b,k},\ \text{cancel}_i \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Model Element Explanations

| Element | Role |
|---------|------|
| **Objective** | Weighted sum of total delay, energy, and cancellations — trades off punctuality against sustainability and service quality |
| **C1–C2** | Define delays as non-negative slacks; enforce realistic dwell times |
| **C3–C5** | Discretized train dynamics; SOS2 piecewise-linear $v^2$ keeps MILP tractable |
| **C6–C7** | Physical speed and acceleration/deceleration limits |
| **C8** | Enforces single-train-per-block unless rerouting is active |
| **C9** | Resolves bidirectional conflicts on shared (rerouted) track via ordering + headway |
| **C10** | Forces rerouting (or absence) during the disruption window |
| **C11** | Restricts rerouting to disrupted blocks and caps frequency |
| **C12–C13** | Couples block traversal times with station arrival/departure |
| **C14** | Linearized energy via McCormick envelopes of $F^{\text{tract}}\cdot v$ |
| **C15** | Allows train cancellation as a last resort |
| **C16** | Boundary conditions for speed and position |
| **C17–C18** | Maintains train ordering and minimum headway |
| **C19** | Declares variable domains |

## 7. Key Modeling Assumptions

1. **Time discretization** into equal intervals $\Delta t$; all events align to the grid.
2. **Piecewise-linear approximation** of $v^2$ (SOS2) and **McCormick envelopes** for $F^{\text{tract}}\cdot v$ preserve MILP structure.
3. **Identical train mechanics** across trains (relaxable by indexing $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,m$ by $i$).
4. **Single-track blockage** per disrupted block; rerouting uses the opposite track.
5. **No overtaking** within a block; ordering fixed by $y_{i,j,b,k}$.
6. **Negligible gradient** (addable as a linear term in C4).
7. **Rerouting only during the disruption window**, enforced by C10–C11.

This formulation is a complete, linear MILP suitable for solution via commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, HiGHS) or decomposition methods (Benders, Lagrangian relaxation) for large-scale instances.

# Final TRSMP-MILP Model

*(This is the final, corrected model after the second revision. It is complete, linear, and free of ill-formed constraints.)*

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| \(T\) | set of trains, indexed by \(t, t'\) |
| \(S\) | set of segments (blocks), indexed by \(s\) |
| \(S^D \subseteq S\) | set of disrupted segments |
| \(S_t \subseteq S\) | ordered set of segments traversed by train \(t\) |
| \(P_s\) | discrete positions on segment \(s\), indexed by \(p = 0,\dots,P_s\) |
| \(K\) | set of discrete speed levels, indexed by \(k\) |
| \(I_t\) | ordered set of stations/stops for train \(t\), indexed by \(i\) |
| \(N(s)\) | ordered train pairs \((t,t')\) that may conflict on segment \(s\) |
| \(s_n, s_{n+1}\) | consecutive segments in \(S_t\) |
| \(b_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) | parameter: 1 if train \(t\) travels in blocked direction on \(s\) |
| \(zd_{t,s}\) | parameter: \(1\) if \(s\in S^D\) and \(b_{t,s}=1\), else \(0\) |
| \(o^{\text{sch}}_{t,t',s}\) | parameter: scheduled ordering (1 if \(t\) precedes \(t'\) on \(s\)) |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| \(v_k\) | speed at level \(k\) (A1) |
| \(\Delta\) | position discretization step (A2) |
| \(L_s\) | length of segment \(s\) |
| \(h_{\min}\) | minimum safety headway |
| \(a_{\max}, d_{\max}\) | max acceleration / deceleration (A3) |
| \(M\) | big-M constant (A5) |
| \(Hor\) | time horizon |
| \(T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}\) | disruption window bounds (for \(s\in S^D\)) |
| \(a_{\text{sch}_{t,i}}, dp_{\text{sch}_{t,i}}\) | scheduled arrival/departure times |
| \(e_{t,s,p,k}\) | piecewise-linear energy rate (A4) |
| \(d^{\min}_{t,i}\) | minimum dwell time at station \(i\) |
| \(c_{\text{delay}}, c_{\text{cancel}}, c_{\text{energy}}, c_{\text{reorder}}\) | cost coefficients |
| \(i_{\text{terminal}}\) | terminal stop index for train \(t\) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Routing / Cancellation (binary)
- \(x_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}\) — train \(t\) traverses segment \(s\) at speed level \(k\)
- \(\text{cancel}_t\in\{0,1\}\) — train \(t\) cancelled
- \(y_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) — train \(t\) rerouted onto opposite track on \(s\)
- \(w_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}\) — train \(t\) traverses \(s\in S^D\) inside the disruption window
- \(z_{t,s,p,k}\in\{0,1\}\) — train \(t\) at position \(p\) of \(s\) uses speed \(k\)
- \(o_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\) — ordering binary for pair \((t,t')\) on \(s\)
- \(\text{same\_track}_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}\) — \(t,t'\) share the same physical track on \(s\)

### 3.2 Timing (continuous)
- \(a_{t,i}\in[0,Hor]\) — arrival time at stop \(i\)
- \(dp_{t,i}\in[0,Hor]\) — departure time from stop \(i\)
- \(\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s}, \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s}\in[0,Hor]\) — segment entry/exit times
- \(u_{t,s,p}\in[0,Hor]\) — time reaching position \(p\) on segment \(s\)
- \(\text{delay}_t\ge 0\) — aggregate delay

### 3.3 Energy & Reorder (continuous)
- \(e_{t,s}\ge 0\) — total energy for train \(t\) on segment \(s\)
- \(\delta_{t,t',s}\ge 0\) — reorder penalty indicator

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; c_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t\in T}\text{delay}_t
\;+\; c_{\text{cancel}}\sum_{t\in T}\text{cancel}_t
\;+\; c_{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S_t} e_{t,s}
\;+\; c_{\text{reorder}}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{(t,t')\in N(s)} \delta_{t,t',s}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Routing and Speed-Level Consistency

**(C1)** Exactly one speed level per traversed segment, or none if cancelled:
$$
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,s,k} = 1 - \text{cancel}_t \qquad \forall t,\; s\in S_t
$$

**(C2)** Sequential segment traversal:
$$
\sum_{k} x_{t,s_{n+1},k} \le \sum_{k} x_{t,s_n,k}
\qquad \forall t,\; (s_n,s_{n+1})\subset S_t \text{ consecutive}
$$

### 5.2 Positional Dynamics (Position–Time Coupling)

**(C3)** Positional time update:
$$
u_{t,s,p+1} - u_{t,s,p} = \sum_{k\in K}\frac{\Delta}{v_k}\,z_{t,s,p,k}
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S_t,\; p=0,\dots,P_s-1
$$

**(C4)** One speed choice per position step (or cancelled):
$$
\sum_{k\in K} z_{t,s,p,k} = 1 - \text{cancel}_t
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S_t,\; p
$$

**(C5)** Consistency between \(z\) and segment-level \(x\):
$$
z_{t,s,p,k} \le x_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall t,\; s\in S_t,\; p,\; k
$$

**(C6)** Bounded use of speed \(k\) over the segment:
$$
\sum_{p=0}^{P_s-1} z_{t,s,p,k} \le P_s \cdot x_{t,s,k}
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S_t,\; k
$$

**(C7)** Global traversal time consistency:
$$
u_{t,s,P_s} - u_{t,s,0} = \sum_{k\in K}\frac{L_s}{v_k}\,x_{t,s,k}
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S_t
$$

### 5.3 Segment Entry/Exit Linkage

**(C8)** Positional boundary linkage:
$$
u_{t,s,0} = \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s}, \qquad u_{t,s,P_s} = \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s}
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S_t
$$

**(C9)** Cancellation gating of times:
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s} \le Hor\,(1-\text{cancel}_t), \qquad
\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s} \le Hor\,(1-\text{cancel}_t)
\qquad \forall t,\; s
$$

### 5.4 Rerouting Logic

**(C10)** No in-window indicator on non-disrupted segments:
$$
w_{t,s} = 0 \qquad \forall s\notin S^D
$$

**(C11)** Big-M coupling of \(w_{t,s}\) to entry time (gated by cancellation):

$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s} \le T_{\text{end}} + M(1-w_{t,s}) + M\,\text{cancel}_t
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S^D
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s} \ge T_{\text{start}} - M(1-w_{t,s}) - M\,\text{cancel}_t
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S^D
$$

**(C12)** Blocked direction inside window ⇒ reroute:
$$
y_{t,s} \ge w_{t,s} - (1-b_{t,s})
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S^D
$$

**(C13)** Reroute only allowed inside the window (blocked segments):
$$
y_{t,s} \le w_{t,s} + (1 - zd_{t,s}) \qquad \forall t,\; s
$$

**(C14)** No reroute on non-disrupted segments:
$$
y_{t,s} = 0 \qquad \forall s\notin S^D
$$

**(C15)** Cancelled train cannot reroute:
$$
y_{t,s} \le 1 - \text{cancel}_t \qquad \forall t,\; s
$$

### 5.5 Same-Track Indicator and Conflict-Free Headways

**(C16)** Same-track linearization (normal–normal, reroute–reroute, and mixed cases):
$$
\text{same\_track}_{t,t',s} \ge y_{t,s} - y_{t',s}
\qquad \forall s,\; (t,t')\in N(s)
$$
$$
\text{same\_track}_{t,t',s} \ge y_{t',s} - y_{t,s}
\qquad \forall s,\; (t,t')\in N(s)
$$
$$
\text{same\_track}_{t,t',s} \ge 1 - y_{t,s} - y_{t',s}
\qquad \forall s,\; (t,t')\in N(s)
$$
$$
\text{same\_track}_{t,t',s} \le 1 \qquad \forall s,\; (t,t')\in N(s)
$$

**(C17)** Ordering antisymmetry:
$$
o_{t,t',s} + o_{t',t,s} = 1
\qquad \forall s,\; t\ne t',\; (t,t')\in N(s)
$$

**(C18)** Conditional headway (forward):
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t',s} \ge \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s} + h_{\min}
- M(1-o_{t,t',s}) - M(1-\text{same\_track}_{t,t',s})
- M\,\text{cancel}_t - M\,\text{cancel}_{t'}
\qquad \forall s,\;(t,t')\in N(s)
$$

**(C19)** Conditional headway (reverse):
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s} \ge \tau^{\text{out}}_{t',s} + h_{\min}
- M\,o_{t,t',s} - M(1-\text{same\_track}_{t,t',s})
- M\,\text{cancel}_t - M\,\text{cancel}_{t'}
\qquad \forall s,\;(t,t')\in N(s)
$$

### 5.6 Acceleration / Deceleration Compatibility

**(C20)** Acceleration bound across consecutive segments:
$$
v_{k_{n+1}} - v_{k_n} \le a_{\max}\,\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s_{n+1}}
+ M(2 - x_{t,s_n,k_n} - x_{t,s_{n+1},k_{n+1}})
$$
$$
\forall t,\; (s_n,s_{n+1})\subset S_t \text{ consecutive},\; k_n,k_{n+1}\in K
$$

**(C21)** Deceleration bound across consecutive segments:
$$
v_{k_n} - v_{k_{n+1}} \le d_{\max}\,\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s_{n+1}}
+ M(2 - x_{t,s_n,k_n} - x_{t,s_{n+1},k_{n+1}})
$$
$$
\forall t,\; (s_n,s_{n+1})\subset S_t \text{ consecutive},\; k_n,k_{n+1}\in K
$$

### 5.7 Segment Duration, Dwell and Schedule Coupling

**(C22)** Minimum segment traversal time:
$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s} \ge \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s} + \frac{L_s}{v_{\max}}
- M\Big(1 - \sum_k x_{t,s,k}\Big) - M\,\text{cancel}_t
\qquad \forall t,\; s
$$

**(C23)** Minimum dwell at intermediate stops:
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s_{n+1}} \ge \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s_n} + d^{\min}_{t,i}
- M\Big(1 - \sum_k x_{t,s_{n+1},k}\Big) - M\,\text{cancel}_t
$$
*(applied at stops \(i\) located between \(s_n\) and \(s_{n+1}\))*

**(C24)** Arrival/departure coupling to segment times:
$$
dp_{t,i} \le \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s} + M\Big(1-\sum_k x_{t,s,k}\Big) + M\,\text{cancel}_t
$$
$$
a_{t,i} \ge \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s} - M\Big(1-\sum_k x_{t,s,k}\Big) - M\,\text{cancel}_t
$$

**(C25)** Time horizon bounds:
$$
0 \le a_{t,i},\; dp_{t,i},\; \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s},\; \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s},\; u_{t,s,p} \le Hor
\qquad \forall t,i,s,p
$$

### 5.8 Delay Definition

**(C26)** Delay lower bounds:
$$
\text{delay}_t \ge a_{t,i} - a_{\text{sch}_{t,i}}
\qquad \forall t,\; i
$$
$$
\text{delay}_t \ge dp_{t,i} - dp_{\text{sch}_{t,i}}
\qquad \forall t,\; i
$$
$$
\text{delay}_t \ge 0 \qquad \forall t
$$

**(C27)** Terminal delay for affected trains:
$$
\text{delay}_t \ge a_{t,i_{\text{terminal}}} - a_{\text{sch}_{t,i_{\text{terminal}}}}
\qquad \forall t
$$

### 5.9 Energy Definition (Piecewise-Linear via \(x\))

**(C28)** Energy accumulation:
$$
e_{t,s} \ge \sum_{p,k} e_{t,s,p,k}\, z_{t,s,p,k}
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in S_t
$$

**(C29)** Zero energy when cancelled:
$$
e_{t,s} \le M \sum_{k} x_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall t,\; s
$$

### 5.10 Reorder Penalty Definition

**(C30)** Linearized absolute order change:
$$
\delta_{t,t',s} \ge o_{t,t',s} - o^{\text{sch}}_{t,t',s}
\qquad \forall s,\; (t,t')\in N(s)
$$
$$
\delta_{t,t',s} \ge o^{\text{sch}}_{t,t',s} - o_{t,t',s}
\qquad \forall s,\; (t,t')\in N(s)
$$
$$
\delta_{t,t',s} \ge 0
\qquad \forall s,\; (t,t')\in N(s)
$$

### 5.11 Cancellation Consistency

**(C31)** Cancelled trains traverse no segment:
$$
\sum_{s\in S_t}\sum_{k} x_{t,s,k} \le |S_t|(1-\text{cancel}_t)
\qquad \forall t
$$

**(C32)** Cancelled trains do not reroute:
$$
y_{t,s} \le 1 - \text{cancel}_t \qquad \forall t,\; s
$$

---

## 6. Variable Domains

$$
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,s,k},\, y_{t,s},\, w_{t,s},\, z_{t,s,p,k},\, o_{t,t',s},\, \text{same\_track}_{t,t',s},\, \text{cancel}_t \in \{0,1\}\\[2pt]
&a_{t,i},\, dp_{t,i},\, \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,s},\, \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,s},\, u_{t,s,p} \in [0,Hor]\\[2pt]
&\text{delay}_t,\, e_{t,s},\, \delta_{t,t',s} \ge 0
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 7. Assumptions (marked)

- **(A1)** Discrete speed levels \(v_k\) → linearizes speed–time–energy relations (C3, C7, C20, C21).
- **(A2)** Uniform position discretization \(\Delta\) → linearizes position–time coupling (C3).
- **(A3)** Constant mass, bounded acceleration \(a_{\max}\) and deceleration \(d_{\max}\) → linearized dynamics (C20, C21).
- **(A4)** Piecewise-linear energy \(e_{t,s,p,k}\) → linear objective term (C28).
- **(A5)** Small reorder penalty and big-M approximation of nonlinear dynamics → (C30) and all big-M constraints.

---

### Summary of what the model captures

| Aspect | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| **Retiming** | arrival/departure times \(a_{t,i}, dp_{t,i}\), segment times \(\tau^{\text{in}}, \tau^{\text{out}}\), delay penalties |
| **Reordering** | ordering binaries \(o_{t,t',s}\) with antisymmetry and reorder penalty \(\delta\) |
| **Rerouting** | \(y_{t,s}\) with window-gated \(w_{t,s}\) (C10–C15) |
| **Cancellation** | binary \(\text{cancel}_t\) with big-M couplings (C9, C15, C31, C32) |
| **Speed profiles** | \(x_{t,s,k}\) + positional \(z_{t,s,p,k}\), plus \(a_{\max}/d_{\max}\) dynamics (C20, C21) |
| **Conflict-free bidirectional operation** | same-track indicator + disjunctive headway constraints (C16–C19) |
| **Energy efficiency** | piecewise-linear energy term (C28) in the objective |

This is the complete, linear, executable model for the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages.

Text:
# Final Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is the consolidated, complete MILP after one revision cycle. It integrates retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed-profile selection into a single optimization framework with a conflict-free timetable as output.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{F}$ | Set of trains, $f \in \mathcal{F}$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{up, down\}$ | Directions |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Ordered block sections (track segments between adjacent stations), $i \in \mathcal{B}$ |
| $\mathcal{G}$ | Speed segments (subdivisions of blocks for the piecewise energy model), $g \in \mathcal{G}$; $\mathcal{G}(i)$ = segments composing block $i$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_g$ | Discrete running-time/energy levels on segment $g$, $k \in \mathcal{K}_g$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Stations (nodes); block $i$ has upstream station $p^{up}(i)$ and downstream station $p^{dn}(i)$ |
| $s^\star \in \mathcal{B}$ | The blocked (disrupted) block |
| $R \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | Rerouting corridor (contiguous blocks around $s^\star$), $R = \{s^\star-1,\,s^\star,\,s^\star+1\}$ |
| $i_{up}$ | Upstream block preceding $s^\star$; $p^{dn}(i_{up}) = p^{up}(s^\star)$ |
| $\mathcal{F}_R \subset \mathcal{F}$ | Trains passing through the corridor $R$ |

**Timing convention (fixed):**
- $y_{f,i}$ = **arrival** of train $f$ at the downstream station of block $i$ (= exit time of block $i$).
- $x_{f,i}$ = **departure** of train $f$ from the downstream station of block $i$ (= after dwell).
- Entry time of block $i$ = $x_{f, i_{prev}}$, where $i_{prev}$ is the upstream neighbor block.
- For $s^\star$: entry $= x_{f,i_{up}}$, exit $= y_{f,s^\star}$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T_W^{start}, T_W^{end}$ | Disruption window boundaries on $s^\star$ |
| $t^{min}_{f,i}, t^{max}_{f,i}$ | Min/max running time of $f$ on block $i$ |
| $d^{min}_{f,p}, d^{max}_{f,p}$ | Min/max dwell of $f$ at station $p$ |
| $\tau_{f,i}$ | Minimum headway on block $i$ |
| $\tau^{cross}$ | Minimum cross-direction separation on shared opposite track |
| $\ell_g$ | Length of speed segment $g$ |
| $\Delta t_{g,k}$ | Running time on segment $g$ at level $k$ |
| $w_{g,k}$ | Energy consumption on segment $g$ at level $k$ |
| $T^{plan}_{f,p}$ | Planned time of train $f$ at station $p$ |
| $T^{term}_f$ | Planned terminal arrival time of $f$ |
| $\mathcal{K}^{feas}_{g,g+1}$ | Feasible consecutive level pairs satisfying acceleration limits |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $\mu, \lambda, \Gamma$ | Objective weights: delay, energy, cancellation |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $y_{f,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Arrival at downstream station of block $i$ |
| $x_{f,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Departure from downstream station of block $i$ |
| $d_{f,p}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Dwell time of $f$ at station $p$ |
| $\Theta_{f,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Running time of $f$ on block $i$ |
| $\sigma_{f,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Schedule delay of $f$ on block $i$ |
| $s_{f,p}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Terminal slack of $f$ at station $p$ |
| $n_{f,g}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Running time of $f$ on speed segment $g$ |
| $E_f$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Total energy of $f$ |
| $u_{f,i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $f$ reroutes on block $i$ (uses opposite track) |
| $z_f$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $f$ is canceled |
| $\theta_{f,s^\star}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $f$ traverses $s^\star$ *before* window (0 = after) |
| $\alpha_{f,g,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $f$ uses running-time level $k$ on segment $g$ |
| $\delta^{same}_{f,f',i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $f$ and $f'$ use the same physical track on block $i$ |
| $\pi_{f,f',i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Precedence: 1 if $f$ precedes $f'$ on block $i$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z \;=\; \sum_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}} \mu\,\sigma_{f,i}
\;+\; \sum_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \lambda\,E_f
\;+\; \sum_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \Gamma\, z_f
$$

with $E_f = \displaystyle\sum_{g\in\mathcal{G}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}_g} w_{g,k}\,\alpha_{f,g,k}$.

Balance: schedule delay + energy + cancellation penalty.

---

## 5. Constraints

### C1 — Block running time and speed-profile linkage
$$
\Theta_{f,i} = y_{f,i} - x_{f,\,i_{prev}} \quad \forall f, i \tag{C1.a}
$$
$$
t^{min}_{f,i}\,(1-z_f) \le \Theta_{f,i} \le t^{max}_{f,i}\,(1-z_f) \quad \forall f, i \tag{C1.b}
$$
$$
n_{f,g} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}_g} \Delta t_{g,k}\,\alpha_{f,g,k}, \qquad \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}_g} \alpha_{f,g,k} = 1-z_f \quad \forall f,g \tag{C1.c}
$$
$$
\sum_{g\in\mathcal{G}(i)} n_{f,g} = \Theta_{f,i} \quad \forall f,i \tag{C1.d}
$$

### C2 — Dwell time
$$
d_{f,p} = x_{f,p} - y_{f,\,i_{dn}(p)} \quad \forall f, p \tag{C2.a}
$$
$$
d^{min}_{f,p}\,(1-z_f) \le d_{f,p} \le d^{max}_{f,p}\,(1-z_f) \quad \forall f,p \tag{C2.b}
$$

### C3 — Schedule delay
$$
\sigma_{f,i} \ge y_{f,i} - T^{plan}_{f,\,p^{dn}(i)} \quad \forall f,i \tag{C3}
$$

### C4 — Terminal boundary conditions
$$
x_{f,p_0} = T^{plan}_{f,p_0} + s_{f,p_0}, \qquad s_{f,p_0} \ge 0 \tag{C4.a}
$$
$$
y_{f,\,i_{dn}(p_L)} = T^{term}_f + s_{f,p_L}, \qquad s_{f,p_L} \ge 0 \tag{C4.b}
$$
$$
T^{plan}_{f,p} \le x_{f,p} \le T^{plan}_{f,p} + \sigma_{f,i_{dn}(p)}, \quad p \in \{p_0, p_L\} \tag{C4.c}
$$

### C5 — Disruption constraint on blocked block $s^\star$ (corrected)
$$
y_{f,s^\star} \le T_W^{start} + M\,(1-\theta_{f,s^\star}) + M\,u_{f,s^\star} + M\,z_f \tag{C5.a}
$$
$$
x_{f,i_{up}} \ge T_W^{end} - M\,\theta_{f,s^\star} - M\,u_{f,s^\star} - M\,z_f \tag{C5.b}
$$

- $\theta_{f,s^\star}=1$, $u=z=0$: exit $s^\star$ before window opens.
- $\theta_{f,s^\star}=0$, $u=z=0$: enter $s^\star$ after window closes.
- $u_{f,s^\star}=1$ or $z_f=1$: both relax.

### C6 — Same-track headway separation
$$
y_{f',i} \ge x_{f,\,i_{prev}} + \tau_{f,i} - M(1-\pi_{f,f',i}) - M(1-\delta^{same}_{f,f',i}) \tag{C6.a}
$$
$$
y_{f,i} \ge x_{f',\,i_{prev}} + \tau_{f',i} - M\,\pi_{f,f',i} - M(1-\delta^{same}_{f,f',i}) \tag{C6.b}
$$

### C7 — Same-track indicator $\delta^{same}_{f,f',i}$ (strengthened)
$$
\delta^{same}_{f,f',i} \ge u_{f,i} - u_{f',i} \tag{C7.a}
$$
$$
\delta^{same}_{f,f',i} \ge u_{f',i} - u_{f,i} \tag{C7.b}
$$
$$
\delta^{same}_{f,f',i} \le u_{f,i} + u_{f',i} \tag{C7.c}
$$
$$
\delta^{same}_{f,f',i} \le 2 - u_{f,i} - u_{f',i} \tag{C7.d}
$$

Encoding: $\delta^{same}=1 \iff u_{f,i}=u_{f',i}$ (same physical track).

### C8 — Bidirectional conflict on shared opposite track in $R$
For opposite-direction pairs $(f,f')$ both rerouted on block $i \in R$, enforce cross-direction separation $\tau^{cross}$ with precedence $\pi_{f,f',i}$ (reusing precedence binaries; ordering across $\pi$):
$$
y_{f',i} \ge x_{f,\,i_{prev}} + \tau^{cross} - M(1-\pi_{f,f',i}) - M(2 - u_{f,i} - u_{f',i}) - M(z_f+z_{f'}) \tag{C8.a}
$$
$$
y_{f,i} \ge x_{f',\,i_{prev}} + \tau^{cross} - M\,\pi_{f,f',i} - M(2 - u_{f,i} - u_{f',i}) - M(z_f+z_{f'}) \tag{C8.b}
$$

Active only when $u_{f,i}=u_{f',i}=1$ and both active.

### C9 — Rerouting contiguity (Assumption A3′)
$$
u_{f,i} = u_{f,i+1} \quad \forall f,\;(i,i+1)\subseteq R \tag{C9}
$$

### C10 — Speed-profile acceleration feasibility (Assumption A9)
Forbid infeasible consecutive running-time levels:
$$
\alpha_{f,g,k} + \alpha_{f,g+1,k'} \le 1 \quad \forall (k,k') \notin \mathcal{K}^{feas}_{g,g+1},\;\forall f \tag{C10}
$$

### C11 — Domains, integrality, and cancellation coupling
$$
y_{f,i},x_{f,i},d_{f,p},\Theta_{f,i},\sigma_{f,i},s_{f,p},n_{f,g},E_f \ge 0
$$
$$
u_{f,i},\,z_f,\,\theta_{f,s^\star},\,\alpha_{f,g,k},\,\delta^{same}_{f,f',i},\,\pi_{f,f',i} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
u_{f,i} = 0 \quad \forall f,\;\forall i \notin R
$$
$$
u_{f,i} \le 1 - z_f, \qquad \theta_{f,s^\star} \le 1 - z_f \quad \forall f
$$

---

## 6. Full Variable Summary

| Variable | Type | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| $y_{f,i}$ | continuous | $\ge 0$ | Arrival at downstream station of block $i$ |
| $x_{f,i}$ | continuous | $\ge 0$ | Departure from downstream station of block $i$ |
| $d_{f,p}$ | continuous | $\ge 0$ | Dwell at station $p$ |
| $\Theta_{f,i}$ | continuous | $\ge 0$ | Running time on block $i$ |
| $\sigma_{f,i}$ | continuous | $\ge 0$ | Schedule delay on block $i$ |
| $s_{f,p}$ | continuous | $\ge 0$ | Terminal slack |
| $n_{f,g}$ | continuous | $\ge 0$ | Running time on speed segment $g$ |
| $E_f$ | continuous | $\ge 0$ | Total energy of train $f$ |
| $u_{f,i}$ | binary | $\{0,1\}$ | Rerouting on block $i$ |
| $z_f$ | binary | $\{0,1\}$ | Cancellation |
| $\theta_{f,s^\star}$ | binary | $\{0,1\}$ | Traverse $s^\star$ before window |
| $\alpha_{f,g,k}$ | binary | $\{0,1\}$ | One-hot level on segment $g$ |
| $\delta^{same}_{f,f',i}$ | binary | $\{0,1\}$ | Same-track indicator |
| $\pi_{f,f',i}$ | binary | $\{0,1\}$ | Precedence ordering |

---

## 7. Assumptions A1–A9

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| **A1** | All blocks are double-directional; "natural" and "opposite" tracks are well-defined and symmetric. |
| **A2** | A single disruption window $[T_W^{start}, T_W^{end}]$ on one block $s^\star$; multiple windows handled by replicating C5. |
| **A3′** | Rerouting is contiguous over the corridor $R$; if a train reroutes any block in $R$, it reroutes all (C9). |
| **A4** | Dwell bounds $[d^{min},d^{max}]$ precomputed from rolling-stock and station characteristics; no extra station capacity constraints. |
| **A5** | Running-time bounds $[t^{min},t^{max}]$ are physical (traction/braking-limited). |
| **A6** | Headway $\tau_{f,i}$ depends only on block $i$ and train class. |
| **A7** | Energy $w_{g,k}$ is convex piecewise-linear in running time; linear interpolation over one-hot $\alpha$ is exact at the chosen level. |
| **A8** | Schedule delay $\sigma_{f,i}$ is measured against planned arrival; non-negative (no early-running credit). |
| **A9** | The piecewise-linear energy curve encodes physically feasible (running-time, energy) pairs; acceleration feasibility enforced linearly by forbidden level-pair constraints (C10). Terminal boundary conditions are consistent ($T^{term}_f = T^{plan}_{f,p_L}$ when no delay). |

---

## 8. Modeling Review & Feedback Applied

**Feedback incorporated from first iteration:**

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model, translated from the generated code into mathematical notation.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Ordered set of stations/nodes, indexed by $s, k$ |
| $G$ | Set of segments (blocks) between consecutive stations, indexed by $g$ |
| $D$ | Set of discretized driving modes (speed profiles), indexed by $d$ |
| $R$ | Set of tracks in a segment, indexed by $r$ (e.g., up / down) |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\text{dep0}_{i,s},\ \text{arr0}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure / arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dwell}^{\min}_{i,s},\ \text{dwell}^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Min / max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau_{i,g,d}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $g$ using mode $d$ |
| $E_{i,g,d}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $g$ using mode $d$ |
| $h$ | Minimum safe headway on the same track |
| $\text{blk}^{\text{start}}_{g},\ \text{blk}^{\text{end}}_{g}$ | Start / end of the blockage window on segment $g$ |
| $\text{blkTrack}_{g}$ | The track of segment $g$ that is blocked |
| $\text{normTrack}_{g}$ | The normal (unblocked) track of segment $g$ |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant |
| $w^{\text{delay}},\ w^{\text{energy}}$ | Cost weights for delay and energy |
| $c^{\text{cancel}}_{i}$ | Cancellation penalty for train $i$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\text{arr}_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\text{start}_{i,g}$ | $\ge 0$ | Entry time of train $i$ into segment $g$ |
| $\text{end}_{i,g}$ | $\ge 0$ | Exit time of train $i$ from segment $g$ |
| $\delta_i$ | $\ge 0$ | Total delay of train $i$ |
| $x_{i,g,d}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses driving mode $d$ on segment $g$ |
| $y_{i,g,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses track $r$ on segment $g$ |
| $z_{i,j,g,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$, track $r$ |
| $u_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $w^{\text{blk}}_{i,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses the blocked track *before* the blockage window |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\ \ 
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} w^{\text{delay}}\,\delta_i}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{g \in G}\sum_{d \in D} w^{\text{energy}}\,E_{i,g,d}\,x_{i,g,d}}_{\text{total energy}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} c^{\text{cancel}}_{i}\,u_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Segment running-time coupling (timing ↔ speed profile):**
$$
\text{end}_{i,g} - \text{start}_{i,g} = \sum_{d \in D} \tau_{i,g,d}\, x_{i,g,d} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

**(2) Exactly one driving mode per segment (if not cancelled):**
$$
\sum_{d \in D} x_{i,g,d} = 1 - u_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

**(3) Exactly one track per segment (if not cancelled):**
$$
\sum_{r \in R} y_{i,g,r} = 1 - u_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

**(4) Blockage disjunction (big-M).** If train $i$ uses the blocked track, its traversal must lie entirely before or entirely after the blockage window, selected by $w^{\text{blk}}_{i,g}$:

$$
\text{end}_{i,g} \le \text{blk}^{\text{start}}_{g} + M\Big[\big(1 - y_{i,g,\text{blkTrack}_g}\big) + \big(1 - w^{\text{blk}}_{i,g}\big)\Big]
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

$$
\text{start}_{i,g} \ge \text{blk}^{\text{end}}_{g} - M\Big[\big(1 - y_{i,g,\text{blkTrack}_g}\big) + w^{\text{blk}}_{i,g}\Big]
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

**(5) Dwell-time bounds:**
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} - \text{arr}_{i,s} \ge \text{dwell}^{\min}_{i,s}\,(1 - u_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} - \text{arr}_{i,s} \le \text{dwell}^{\max}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$

**(6) Arrival at next station = departure from current + running time:**
$$
\text{arr}_{i,\,s+1} - \text{dep}_{i,s} = \sum_{d \in D} \tau_{i,g,d}\, x_{i,g,d} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g = (s, s+1)
$$

**(7) Segment entry/exit timing consistency:**
$$
\text{start}_{i,g} = \text{dep}_{i,s}, \qquad \text{end}_{i,g} = \text{arr}_{i,\,s+1} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g = (s, s+1)
$$

**(8) Delay definition:**
$$
\delta_i \ge \text{arr}_{i,s} - \text{arr0}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$
$$
\delta_i \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} - \text{dep0}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$

**(9) Headway and ordering on the same track (conflict-free).** For all $i \ne j$, $g \in G$, $r \in R$:

$$
\text{start}_{j,g} \ge \text{end}_{i,g} + h - M\big(1 - z_{i,j,g,r}\big)
$$

$$
z_{i,j,g,r} + z_{j,i,g,r} \ge y_{i,g,r} + y_{j,g,r} - 1
$$

$$
z_{i,j,g,r} + z_{j,i,g,r} \le 1
$$

**(10) Rerouting restriction.** On segments not affected by the blockage, trains must use the normal track:
$$
y_{i,g,r} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G,\ r \ne \text{normTrack}_g \quad\text{(for unaffected } g\text{)}
$$

**(11) Cancellation linkage** is implicitly enforced by constraints (2) and (3): if $u_i = 1$, then all $x_{i,g,d} = 0$ and all $y_{i,g,r} = 0$.

---

## 6. Assumptions (marked)

- **A1.** Driving modes are discretized speed profiles with known running time $\tau_{i,g,d}$ and energy $E_{i,g,d}$.
- **A2.** Rerouting to the opposite track is permitted only on the disrupted segment and only within the disruption window.
- **A3.** Cancellation is allowed as a last resort with penalty $c^{\text{cancel}}_i$.
- **A4.** Minimum headway $h$ is constant and identical for all trains and tracks.
- **A5.** Dwell times are bounded between $\text{dwell}^{\min}$ and $\text{dwell}^{\max}$.
- **A6.** Trains stop at all stations (no skip-stop).
- **A7.** The planning horizon is discretized; times are continuous within it.

---

## 7. Solution Approach (from the paper)

The monolithic MILP is decomposed into:
1. A **reformulated IP model** focusing on train interactions (train-plan selection), and
2. A series of **single-train plan subproblems**.

An **adaptive iterative algorithm** refines plan granularity near the previous solution, accelerated by an **adaptive refinement process** and a **local branching strategy**. The IP with sufficiently fine interval plans is proven equivalent to the MILP.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code, expressed as equations. All assumptions are marked with **(A#)**.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, ordered $1,\dots,N$, indexed $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of segments, segment $k$ connects station $k$ and $k+1$, indexed $k$ |
| $P$ | Set of discretized speed profiles, indexed $p$ |
| $R$ | Set of tracks $\{\text{normal}, \text{opposite}\}$, indexed $r$ |
| $B \subseteq K$ | Set of blocked segments (partial segment blockage) |
| $TT$ | Ordered train pairs $\{(i,j) : i < j\}$ |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $rt_{i,k,p}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ using profile $p$ **(A8)** |
| $e_{i,k,p}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $k$ using profile $p$ **(A8)** |
| $sched\_arr_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $sched\_dep_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $min\_dw_{i,s}, max\_dw_{i,s}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ **(A7)** |
| $headway$ | Minimum safety headway between consecutive trains on the same track **(A5)** |
| $tb\_start, tb\_end$ | Disruption time window bounds **(A9)** |
| $w_{delay}, w_{energy}$ | Objective weights |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $first_s(i), last_s(i)$ | First and last station of train $i$ |

---

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,k,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ with speed profile $p$ |
| $y_{i,k,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ on track $r$ |
| $u_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes to the opposite track on segment $k$ |
| $o_{i,j,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ (defined for $i<j$) |
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $dep_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $dw_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $delay_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Total delay of train $i$ at its final station |

---

## Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total train delay and total energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = w_{delay}\sum_{i \in T} delay_i \;+\; w_{energy}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{k \in K}\sum_{p \in P} e_{i,k,p}\, x_{i,k,p}
$$

---

## Constraints

### (1) Speed Profile Selection **(A1)**
Each train uses exactly one speed profile per segment:
$$
\sum_{p \in P} x_{i,k,p} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (2) Track Selection **(A2)**
Each train uses exactly one track per segment:
$$
\sum_{r \in R} y_{i,k,r} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (3) Rerouting Linkage
The rerouting flag equals the selection of the opposite track:
$$
u_{i,k} = y_{i,k,\text{opposite}} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (4) Rerouting Only on Blocked Segments **(A3)**
$$
u_{i,k} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \notin B
$$

### (5) Rerouting Only During the Disruption Window **(A3, A4)**
Trains rerouting must enter the segment after the window opens and clear it before the window closes:
$$
dep_{i,k} \ge tb\_start - M\,(1 - u_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in B
$$
$$
a_{i,k+1} \le tb\_end + M\,(1 - u_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in B
$$

### (6) Running Time Consistency
The travel time across a segment equals the selected profile's running time:
$$
a_{i,k+1} - dep_{i,k} = \sum_{p \in P} rt_{i,k,p}\, x_{i,k,p} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (7) Dwell Time Bounds **(A7)**
$$
min\_dw_{i,s} \le dw_{i,s} \le max\_dw_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (8) Dwell Time Definition
$$
dep_{i,s} - a_{i,s} = dw_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (9) Departure After Arrival Plus Minimum Dwell **(A7)**
$$
dep_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} + min\_dw_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (10) Scheduled Time Anchoring at the First Station
Trains cannot depart their origin earlier than scheduled:
$$
dep_{i,\,first\_s(i)} \ge sched\_dep_{i,\,first\_s(i)} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

### (11) Delay Definition
Delay is measured at the final station and is nonnegative:
$$
delay_i \ge a_{i,\,last\_s(i)} - sched\_arr_{i,\,last\_s(i)} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$
$$
delay_i \ge 0 \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

### (12) Headway / Conflict-Free Operation on Shared Track **(A5)**
For each ordered pair $i<j$, segment $k$, and track $r$, at least one of the two disjunctive orderings must hold when both trains use the same track:

$$
dep_{j,k} \ge a_{i,k+1} + headway - M\,(1 - o_{i,j,k}) - M\,(2 - y_{i,k,r} - y_{j,k,r})
$$

$$
dep_{i,k} \ge a_{j,k+1} + headway - M\,o_{i,j,k} - M\,(2 - y_{i,k,r} - y_{j,k,r})
$$

$$
\forall (i,j) \in TT,\; k \in K,\; r \in R
$$

### (13) Ordering Antisymmetry **(A6)**
Because $o_{i,j,k}$ is defined only for $i<j$, antisymmetry is enforced by construction. An explicit statement:
$$
o_{i,j,k} + o_{j,i,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i<j,\; k \in K
$$

### (14) No Overtaking Within a Segment **(A6)**
If train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$, it must also arrive first at the downstream station:
$$
a_{i,k+1} \le a_{j,k+1} + M\,(1 - o_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TT,\; k \in K
$$

### (15) Track Capacity
Enforced implicitly by the headway constraints (12): at most one train occupies a given track of a segment at any time.

### (16) Variable Domains
$$
x_{i,k,p},\; y_{i,k,r},\; u_{i,k},\; o_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{i,s},\; dep_{i,s},\; dw_{i,s},\; delay_i \ge 0
$$

---

## Summary of Assumptions

- **(A1)** Each train traverses each segment exactly once with exactly one speed profile.
- **(A2)** Each train uses exactly one track per segment.
- **(A3)** Rerouting to the opposite track is permitted only on blocked segments and only during the disruption window.
- **(A4)** The disruption blocks one track direction on blocked segments during $[tb\_start, tb\_end]$; trains otherwise follow their direction's normal track.
- **(A5)** Safety headway applies between any two trains using the same track of the same segment, regardless of direction (bidirectional conflict).
- **(A6)** No overtaking within a segment; ordering is fixed per segment by $o_{i,j,k}$.
- **(A7)** Dwell times are bounded between min and max; trains cannot depart before arrival plus minimum dwell.
- **(A8)** Speed profiles are discretized; running time and energy are precomputed constants.
- **(A9)** The disruption window is known and fixed.

---

This MILP couples train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles in a single model, yielding a **conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles** for the partial-segment-blockage disruption scenario.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

## 1. Modeling Overview

A high-speed rail corridor with ordered stations/segments, bidirectional traffic, and a partial blockage of one segment during a known time window. The model jointly decides **retiming**, **reordering**, **rerouting**, **speed profile selection**, and **cancellation**, minimizing a weighted trade-off of tardiness, energy, and cancellations.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| $T$ | Trains (both directions), indexed by $t, t_1, t_2$ |
| $S$ | Stations/segments along the corridor, ordered by position; segment $s$ connects station $s$ to $s+1$ |
| $K$ | Discretized speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $Z \subseteq S$ | Conflicting blocks / shared bidirectional track resources |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| $\text{sched\_dep}_t,\ \text{sched\_arr}_t$ | Scheduled departure / arrival time of train $t$ |
| $T_{\text{block}}^{\text{start}},\ T_{\text{block}}^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window on blocked segment |
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$ | Min / max allowable speeds |
| $a_{\max}, d_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration |
| $E(v_k)$ | Energy per unit distance at speed $v_k$ |
| $\delta_{\min}, \delta_{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway on a shared resource |
| $\text{direction}_t$ | $+1$ reference direction, $-1$ otherwise |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}$ | Planning horizon bounds |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Objective weights (tardiness, energy, cancellation) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Continuous**

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{t,s}$ | $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{t,s}$ | $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$ | Departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $\delta_{t,s}$ | $[\delta_{\min}, \delta_{\max}]$ | Dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $z_{t,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Running time of train $t$ on segment $s$ |
| $\text{en}_t$ | $\geq 0$ | Total energy consumption of train $t$ |
| $\text{delay}_t$ | $\geq 0$ | Tardiness of train $t$ at final station |

**Binary**

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $r_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ if train $t$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $o_{t_1,t_2,s}\in\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ if train $t_1$ precedes $t_2$ on segment $s$ |
| $v_{\text{seg},t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ if train $t$ on segment $s$ uses speed level $k$ |
| $\text{cancel}_t\in\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ if train $t$ is cancelled |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{\ \min\;\; w_1 \sum_{t\in T}\text{delay}_t \;+\; w_2\sum_{t\in T}\text{en}_t \;+\; w_3\sum_{t\in T}\text{cancel}_t\ }
$$

Trades off passenger punctuality (total tardiness), energy efficiency (traction energy from speed profiles), and service quality (cancellations). Weights reflect operator priorities.

---

## 6. Constraints

### (C1) Departure–Arrival / Running-Time Consistency
$$
y_{t,s} + z_{t,s} = x_{t,s+1} \qquad \forall t\in T,\ s\in S
$$

### (C2) Dwell Time Bounds
$$
\delta_{t,s} = y_{t,s} - x_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
\delta_{\min}\le \delta_{t,s}\le \delta_{\max} \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C3) Speed Profile Selection
$$
\sum_{k\in K} v_{\text{seg},t,s,k} = 1 \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
z_{t,s} = \sum_{k\in K}\frac{L_s}{v_k}\,v_{\text{seg},t,s,k} \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
\text{en}_t = \sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} L_s\,E(v_k)\,v_{\text{seg},t,s,k} \qquad \forall t
$$

### (C4) Speed Feasibility & Acceleration/Deceleration Coupling
$$
v_{\min}\le v_k\le v_{\max}\qquad\forall k
$$

For consecutive segments $s\to s+1$ with choices $k,k'$:
$$
\frac{v_{k'}-v_k}{\Delta t_{t,s,s+1}}\le a_{\max}+M\bigl(2-v_{\text{seg},t,s,k}-v_{\text{seg},t,s+1,k'}\bigr)
$$
$$
\frac{v_k-v_{k'}}{\Delta t_{t,s,s+1}}\le d_{\max}+M\bigl(2-v_{\text{seg},t,s,k}-v_{\text{seg},t,s+1,k'}\bigr)
$$

The big-M terms relax both constraints unless the pair $(k,k')$ is jointly active.

### (C5) Blockage Time-Window Constraints
Let $s_b$ be the blocked segment. For reference-direction trains:
$$
x_{t,s_b} \le T_{\text{block}}^{\text{start}} + M\bigl(r_{t,s_b}+\text{cancel}_t\bigr)
$$
$$
y_{t,s_b} \ge T_{\text{block}}^{\text{end}} - M\bigl(r_{t,s_b}+\text{cancel}_t\bigr)
$$
A rerouted train within the window uses the opposite track (handled through C7/C8).

### (C6) Rerouting Binary Logic
$$
r_{t,s}=0 \qquad \forall t,\ s\ne s_b
$$
Only the blocked segment may be rerouted.

### (C7) Headway / Conflict Constraints on Shared Resources
For each $z\in Z$ and any two trains $t_1,t_2$:
$$
y_{t_1,z} - y_{t_2,z} \ge h_{\min} - M\bigl(1-o_{t_1,t_2,z}\bigr)
$$
$$
y_{t_2,z} - y_{t_1,z} \ge h_{\min} - M\,o_{t_1,t_2,z}
$$

### (C8) Route Capacity on Single-Track Segments
$$
o_{t_1,t_2,s}+o_{t_2,t_1,s}=1 \qquad \forall t_1\ne t_2,\ s\in Z
$$
At most one direction occupies a single-track segment unless a rerouting flag is active:
$$
\sum_{t:\text{direction}_t=+1} \bigl(1-r_{t,z}\bigr)\,\mathbb{1}[t\text{ uses }z] \le 1 + M\sum_{t} r_{t,z}
$$

Rerouted trains are sequenced against opposite-direction trains in C7.

### (C9) Path / Order Consistency
$$
o_{t_1,t_2,s}=o_{t_1,t_2,s+1}\qquad \text{where no overtaking is allowed}
$$
Relaxed at stations with multiple tracks permitting overtaking.

### (C10) Delay Definition
For final station $s_f(t)$:
$$
\text{delay}_t \ge x_{t,s_f(t)} - \text{sched\_arr}_t,\qquad \text{delay}_t\ge 0 \qquad \forall t
$$

### (C11) Cancellation Coupling
$$
x_{t,s} \le \text{sched\_arr}_t + M\,\text{cancel}_t,\qquad x_{t,s}\ge \text{sched\_arr}_t - M\,\text{cancel}_t
$$
$$
y_{t,s} \le \text{sched\_dep}_t + M\,\text{cancel}_t,\qquad y_{t,s}\ge \text{sched\_dep}_t - M\,\text{cancel}_t
$$
$$
z_{t,s}\le M(1-\text{cancel}_t),\quad r_{t,s}\le 1-\text{cancel}_t,\quad v_{\text{seg},t,s,k}\le 1-\text{cancel}_t,\quad \text{en}_t\le M(1-\text{cancel}_t)
$$

### (C12) Time-Horizon Bounds
$$
T_{\text{start}}\le x_{t,s},\,y_{t,s}\le T_{\text{end}} \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C13) Domains
$$
x,y,\delta,z,\text{en},\text{delay}\ge 0;\qquad r,o,v_{\text{seg}},\text{cancel}\in\{0,1\}
$$

---

## 7. Model Interpretation

| Element | Role |
|---------|------|
| $x,y$ | **Retiming** — shift arrivals/departures to absorb the disruption |
| $\delta$ | **Dwell control** — buffers small perturbations without speed changes |
| $z$ | **Running time** — driven by chosen discrete speed profile |
| $v_{\text{seg}},\text{en}$ | **Speed management** — energy-aware profile selection |
| $r$ | **Rerouting** — diversion to opposite track around the blockage |
| $o$ | **Reordering** — which train goes first on a shared resource |
| $\text{cancel}$ | **Fallback** — drops infeasible trains |
| Blockage (C5) | Enforces no reference-direction entry during $[T_0^{blk},T_1^{blk}]$ unless rerouted |
| Headway (C7–C8) | Prevents bidirectional collisions on shared track via big-M disjunction |

All nonlinearities (speed/energy products, min/max logic, headway disjunctions, cancellation implications) are linearized with binaries and big-M, so the model is a **complete MILP** directly solvable by standard solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, HiGHS).

## 8. Assumptions Made (marked)
- **Segment/station indexing:** segment $s$ runs from station $s$ to $s+1$ (assumed).
- **Rerouting possible only on the blocked segment** $\{s_b\}$ (per partial-blockage scenario).
- **Overtaking allowed only at multi-track stations**; otherwise order preserved (C9 relaxed selectively).
- **Constant average transition time** $\Delta t_{t,s,s+1}$ (parametrized or approximated) for accel/decel coupling.
- **Energy given by precomputed discrete profile** $E(v_k)$ for a linearized MILP; real speed management would be continuous.
- **Single planned blockage** with known window; multiple blockages would extend C5/C6 accordingly.

Text:
# Best Model: Integrated MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Among the generated candidates, **Model 1 (set 1)** is selected as the best: it provides the most complete and rigorous formulation — explicitly coupling train dynamics with block occupancy, modeling bidirectional rerouting conflicts, deriving delay/energy/cancellation objectives, and giving a fully linearized treatment of the nonlinear physics (kinematics, quadratic energy). It is the most faithful to the source paper's five scientific contributions (integrated TRP + TSMP, retiming/reordering/rerouting/speed profiles, MILP, conflict-free timetable, coupled speed control). Below is the complete, self-contained model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ | Trains |
| $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | Stations along the line |
| $b \in \mathcal{B} = \{1,\dots,N-1\}$ | Blocks (segments between consecutive stations) |
| $k \in \mathcal{K} = \{U, D\}$ | Track direction (up, down) |
| $r \in \mathcal{R}$ | PWL breakpoints for energy linearization |
| $t \in \mathcal{H} = \{0,\dots,T-1\}$ | Discrete time steps ($\Delta_t$ resolution) |
| $k^\star, b^\star$ | Affected track / block of the partial blockage |
| $[t_s, t_e]$ | Disruption time window |
| $\mathcal{B}^{dis}$ | Blocks eligible for rerouting (disrupted block + crossover-adjacent) |
| $\mathcal{C}$ | Designated crossover points |
| $\mathcal{K}_i$ | Nominal direction of train $i$; $\mathcal{B}_i$ its route |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Block length [m] |
| $V^{\max}, V^{\min}$ | Max / min speed [m/s] |
| $A^{\max}, A^{\min}$ | Max acceleration / braking [m/s²] |
| $J^{\max}$ | Max jerk [m/s³] |
| $\Delta_t$ | Time discretization [s] |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway [s] |
| $dwell^{\min}, dwell^{\max}$ | Min / max station dwell [s] |
| $t_i^{arr, sched}, t_i^{dep, sched}$ | Scheduled terminal arrival / origin departure |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $R_b, G_b$ | Resistance coefficient and grade on block $b$ |
| $m_i$ | Train mass [kg] |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) |
| $\lambda_r, \mu_r$ | PWL slopes / intercepts for the energy curve |
| $f_{k,k'}$ | 1 if directions $k,k'$ conflict on shared track, else 0 |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Binary
| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $x_{i,b,t}^{k}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ in direction $k$ at time $t$ |
| $y_{i,b,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes onto the opposite track on block $b$ at time $t$ |
| $z_{i,j,b,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ is ordered before $j$ on block $b$ at time $t$ |
| $c_i$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\delta_{i,b,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters block $b$ at time $t$ |
| $\eta_{i,j,s}$ | ordering binary at station $s$ |

### Continuous
| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ | Actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $v_{i,b,t}$ | Speed of train $i$ on block $b$ at time $t$ [m/s] |
| $acc_{i,b,t}$ | Acceleration of train $i$ on block $b$ at time $t$ [m/s²] |
| $p_{i,b,t}$ | Position of train $i$ on block $b$ at time $t$ [m] |
| $E_{i,b}$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on block $b$ [J] |
| $delay_i$ | Total delay of train $i$ [s] |
| $u_{i,b,t,r}$ | PWL convex weights |
| $\zeta_{i,b,t,r}$ | McCormick auxiliary for $acc \cdot u$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \;\; w_1 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} delay_i \;+\; w_2 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}_i} E_{i,b} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} c_i
$$

$$
delay_i \;\ge\; a_{i,N} - t_i^{arr, sched}, \qquad delay_i \ge 0
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (linearized kinematic chain)
With piecewise-constant acceleration over $[t,t+1)$:

$$
p_{i,b,t+1} = p_{i,b,t} + v_{i,b,t}\,\Delta_t + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\phi_{i,b,t}, \quad \phi_{i,b,t}\approx acc_{i,b,t}\,\Delta_t^2 \text{ (PWL)} \tag{1'}
$$
$$
v_{i,b,t+1} = v_{i,b,t} + acc_{i,b,t}\,\Delta_t \tag{2}
$$
$$
V^{\min} \le v_{i,b,t} \le V^{\max}, \qquad A^{\min} \le acc_{i,b,t} \le A^{\max} \tag{3,4}
$$
$$
|acc_{i,b,t+1} - acc_{i,b,t}| \le J^{\max}\,\Delta_t \tag{5}
$$

### 5.2 Position–Block Consistency
$$
0 \le p_{i,b,t} \le L_b \!\sum_{k} x_{i,b,t}^{k} \tag{6}
$$
$$
v_{i,b,t} \le V^{\max}\!\sum_{k} x_{i,b,t}^{k} \tag{7}
$$
Cancelled train makes no movements:
$$
c_i = 1 \Rightarrow \sum_{b,t,k} x_{i,b,t}^{k} = 0,\quad a_{i,s}=d_{i,s}=v_{i,b,t}=0 \tag{8}
$$

### 5.3 Block Occupancy (same-direction capacity)
$$
\sum_{i} x_{i,b,t}^{k} \le 1 \quad \forall b,t,k \tag{9}
$$
$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}_i}\sum_{k} x_{i,b,t}^{k} \le 1 \quad \forall i,t \tag{10}
$$

### 5.4 Bi-directional Conflict under Rerouting
$$
x_{i,b,t}^{k} + x_{j,b,t}^{k'} \le 1 \quad \forall i\ne j,\; k\ne k',\; f_{k,k'}=1,\; b\in\mathcal{B}^{dis} \tag{12'}
$$

### 5.5 Disruption Constraints
$$
x_{i,b^\star,t}^{k^\star} = 0 \quad \forall i,\; t \in [t_s, t_e] \tag{13}
$$
$$
\sum_{k \ne k^\star} x_{i,b^\star,t}^{k} + y_{i,b^\star,t} + c_i \ge 1 \quad \forall i,\; t \in [t_s, t_e] \tag{14}
$$

### 5.6 Rerouting Feasibility
$$
y_{i,b,t} \le \sum_{b' \in \mathcal{B}^{dis}} x_{i,b',t}^{k} \tag{15}
$$
$$
y_{i,b,t} = 0 \quad \text{if } b \notin \mathcal{B}^{dis} \tag{16}
$$
$$
y_{i,b,t} - y_{i,b-1,t'} \le M(1 - \delta_{i,b,t}) + \mathbf{1}[b \in \mathcal{C}]\cdot M \tag{17}
$$

### 5.7 Station Dwell Times
$$
dwell^{\min} \le d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le dwell^{\max} \tag{18}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le dwell^{\max}(1 - c_i) \tag{18'}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \le d_{i,s}, \quad d_{i,s} \le a_{i,s+1} \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S}_i \tag{19}
$$

### 5.8 Headway Constraints
$$
\delta_{i,b,t} + \delta_{j,b,t'} \le 1, \quad |t - t'| < h^{\min}/\Delta_t,\; i\ne j \tag{20}
$$
Station ordering (linearized):
$$
a_{i,s} \ge a_{j,s} + h^{\min} - M(1 - \eta_{i,j,s}) \tag{21a}
$$
$$
a_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s} + h^{\min} - M\,\eta_{i,j,s} \tag{21b}
$$

### 5.9 Arrival/Departure Consistency with Position
$$
p_{i,b,t} \ge L_b - M(1 - \delta^{exit}_{i,b,t}),\quad a_{i,s+1} \le t\Delta_t + M(1 - \delta^{exit}_{i,b,t}) \tag{22a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \ge t\Delta_t - M(1 - \delta^{exit}_{i,b,t}) \tag{22b}
$$

### 5.10 Train Ordering on Blocks
$$
z_{i,j,b,t} + z_{j,i,b,t} \ge x_{i,b,t}^{k} + x_{j,b,t}^{k} - 1 \tag{23a}
$$
$$
z_{i,j,b,t} + z_{j,i,b,t} \le 1 \tag{23b}
$$
$$
z_{i,j,b,t} + z_{j,\ell,b,t} - z_{i,\ell,b,t} \le 1 \tag{24}
$$
$$
p_{i,b,t} \ge p_{j,b,t} - M(1 - z_{i,j,b,t}) \tag{25}
$$

### 5.11 Speed Profile Feasibility
$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \ge \frac{L_b}{V^{\max}} \tag{26}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \ge \frac{V^{\max}}{A^{\max}} + \frac{L_b}{V^{\max}} - \frac{V^{\max}}{A^{\max}} \tag{27}
$$

### 5.12 Energy Consumption (PWL + McCormick)
$$
E_{i,b} = \sum_{t} \Big[ m_i\, acc_{i,b,t}\, v_{i,b,t} + \big(R_b v_{i,b,t} + m_i G_b\big) v_{i,b,t} \Big]\Delta_t \tag{28}
$$
PWL convex combination:
$$
v_{i,b,t} = \sum_{r} \lambda_r u_{i,b,t,r},\quad \sum_r u_{i,b,t,r} = 1,\; 0 \le u_{i,b,t,r} \le 1 \tag{29a}
$$
$$
v_{i,b,t}^2 \approx \sum_r \lambda_r^2\, u_{i,b,t,r} \tag{29b}
$$
McCormick envelope for $\zeta_{i,b,t,r} = acc_{i,b,t} u_{i,b,t,r}$:
$$
\zeta_{i,b,t,r} \le A^{\max} u_{i,b,t,r},\qquad \zeta_{i,b,t,r} \ge A^{\min} u_{i,b,t,r}
$$
$$
\zeta_{i,b,t,r} \le acc_{i,b,t} - A^{\min}(1-u_{i,b,t,r}),\qquad \zeta_{i,b,t,r} \ge acc_{i,b,t} - A^{\max}(1-u_{i,b,t,r}) \tag{31}
$$
$$
E_{i,b} \ge \sum_t \Big[ m_i \!\sum_r \lambda_r \zeta_{i,b,t,r} + R_b \!\sum_r \lambda_r^2 u_{i,b,t,r} + m_i G_b \!\sum_r \lambda_r u_{i,b,t,r}\Big]\Delta_t \tag{30}
$$

---

## 6. Variable Domains
$$
x_{i,b,t}^{k},\, y_{i,b,t},\, z_{i,j,b,t},\, c_i,\, \delta_{i,b,t},\, \eta_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\} \tag{32a}
$$
$$
v_{i,b,t} \in [0, V^{\max}],\quad acc_{i,b,t} \in [A^{\min}, A^{\max}],\quad p_{i,b,t} \in [0, L_b] \tag{32b}
$$
$$
u_{i,b,t,r} \in [0,1],\quad \zeta_{i,b,t,r} \in [A^{\min}, A^{\max}] \tag{32c}
$$
$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, E_{i,b}, delay_i \ge 0 \tag{32d}
$$

---

## 7. Model Structure Summary

| Layer | Decision variables |
|---|---|
| **Retiming** | $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, v_{i,b,t}, p_{i,b,t}$ |
| **Reordering** | $z_{i,j,b,t}$ (blocks), $\eta_{i,j,s}$ (stations) |
| **Rerouting** | $y_{i,b,t}$, $x_{i,b,t}^{k}$ (both directions) |
| **Cancellation** | $c_i$ |
| **Energy** | $E_{i,b}$ via PWL($v^2$) + McCormick($acc\cdot v$) |
| **Disruption** | $x_{i,b^\star,t}^{k^\star} = 0$ on $[t_s,t_e]$ |

All nonlinearities are handled by fixed $\Delta_t$ discretization (turns ODEs into linear difference equations), PWL/McCormick envelopes ($v^2$, $acc\cdot v$, energy), and Big-M disjunctions (occupancy, ordering, rerouting, crossover transitions). The result is a **pure MILP** solvable by standard branch-and-bound (Gurobi, CPLEX, HiGHS); large networks may require the paper's decomposition/adaptive refinement or rolling-horizon strategies.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)
## Complete Mixed-Integer Linear Program

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $S$ | Set of segments (blocks), indexed by $s$ |
| $ST$ | Set of stations, indexed by $st$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $S^{out}(st)$ | Segments departing from station $st$ |
| $S^{in}(st)$ | Segments arriving at station $st$ |
| $T^{up}, T^{down} \subseteq T$ | Up- and down-direction trains |

**Special elements:** disrupted segment $s^* \in S$; blocked direction $d^* \in \{up, down\}$; disruption window $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$.

---

## 2. Parameters

### Timetable
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $A^{sch}_{t,st},\ D^{sch}_{t,st}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $t$ at station $st$ |
| $dwell^{min}_{t,st}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $t$ at station $st$ |
| $run^{min}_{t,s},\ run^{max}_{t,s}$ | Min / max running time of train $t$ on segment $s$ |

### Speed profile data
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $run_{t,s,k}$ | Running time of train $t$ on segment $s$ using speed level $k$ |
| $E_{t,s,k}$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $s$ using speed level $k$ |
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ |
| $v^{max}_{t,s}$ | Maximum allowed speed for train $t$ on segment $s$ |

### Safety
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $h^{same}$ | Minimum headway between same-direction trains |
| $h^{opp}$ | Minimum headway between opposite-direction trains (shared track) |

### Disruption
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $t_{start}, t_{end}$ | Disruption window boundaries |
| $s^*, d^*$ | Disrupted segment and blocked direction |

### Objective weights & Big-M
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $w^{arr}, w^{dep}$ | Weights on arrival / departure delay |
| $w^{cancel}$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $w^{energy}$ | Energy cost weight |
| $M_1, M_2$ | Large constants for time-linking and ordering constraints |
| $T_{horizon}$ | End of planning horizon |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timing (continuous):** $a_{t,st} \ge 0$ (arrival), $dep_{t,st} \ge 0$ (departure).

**Delay (continuous, nonnegative):** $\delta^{arr}_{t,st}, \delta^{dep}_{t,st}$.

**Routing (binary):** $x_{t,s} = 1$ if train $t$ uses the opposite track on segment $s$.

**Ordering (binary):** $y_{t,t',s} = 1$ if train $t$ enters segment $s$ before train $t'$.

**Cancellation (binary):** $z_t = 1$ if train $t$ is cancelled.

**Speed profile selection (binary):** $v_{t,s,k} = 1$ if train $t$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $s$.

**Auxiliary (continuous):** $r_{t,s} \ge 0$ (actual running time); $e_{t,s}, f_{t,s} \ge 0$ (segment entry / exit times).

**Auxiliary (binary):** $\phi_{t,t',s}$ (track-sharing indicator for headway linearization).

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{w^{arr}\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{st \in ST} \delta^{arr}_{t,st} + w^{dep}\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{st \in ST} \delta^{dep}_{t,st}}_{\text{total delay}}
+ \underbrace{w^{cancel}\sum_{t \in T} z_t}_{\text{cancellations}}
+ \underbrace{w^{energy}\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K} E_{t,s,k}\, v_{t,s,k}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay definition
$$
\delta^{arr}_{t,st} \geq a_{t,st} - A^{sch}_{t,st}, \qquad \delta^{dep}_{t,st} \geq dep_{t,st} - D^{sch}_{t,st}, \qquad \forall t \in T,\; st \in ST
$$
*(Only positive deviations are penalized; early arrivals are not rewarded.)*

### 5.2 Dwell time feasibility
$$
dep_{t,st} \geq a_{t,st} + dwell^{min}_{t,st}, \qquad \forall t \in T,\; st \in ST
$$

### 5.3 Running time consistency
$$
r_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in K} run_{t,s,k}\, v_{t,s,k}, \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.4 Speed profile selection (exactly one level)
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{t,s,k} = 1, \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.5 Speed profile feasibility (speed limit / traction)
$$
v_{t,s,k} = 0 \quad \text{if } run_{t,s,k} < run^{min}_{t,s} \text{ or } run_{t,s,k} > run^{max}_{t,s}
$$
*(Preprocessing: infeasible speed levels are removed from $K$ for each $(t,s)$.)*

### 5.6 Timetable propagation (arrival = departure + running time)
For each segment $s$ connecting $st_1 \to st_2$:
$$
a_{t,st_2} = dep_{t,st_1} + r_{t,s}, \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.7 Segment entry/exit time linking
$$
e_{t,s} = dep_{t,st_1}, \qquad f_{t,s} = a_{t,st_2}, \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s: st_1 \to st_2
$$

### 5.8 Disruption constraints (blocked segment $s^*$, blocked direction $d^*$)
For trains $t$ with $d(t) = d^*$:
- **Option A — Reroute:** if $x_{t,s^*} = 1$, the train traverses $s^*$ during the window on the opposite track.
- **Option B — Wait:** the train traverses $s^*$ only after $t_{end}$.
- **Option C — Cancel:** if $z_t = 1$, the train is removed.

**Forbidden normal-track usage during window:**
$$
e_{t,s^*} \geq t_{end} - M_1 x_{t,s^*} - M_1 z_t, \qquad \forall t: d(t) = d^*
$$
*(If $x=0$ and $z=0$, entry must be after $t_{end}$.)*

### 5.9 Rerouting restrictions
$$
x_{t,s} = 0, \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{s^*\}
$$
$$
x_{t,s^*} = 0, \qquad \forall t: d(t) \neq d^*
$$
*(Only affected trains on the disrupted segment may reroute.)*

### 5.10 Rerouting window constraint
If train $t$ reroutes on $s^*$ ($x_{t,s^*}=1$), it must traverse within the disruption window:
$$
e_{t,s^*} \geq t_{start} - M_1(1 - x_{t,s^*})
$$
$$
f_{t,s^*} \leq t_{end} + M_1(1 - x_{t,s^*})
$$

### 5.11 Ordering consistency
For any pair $(t, t')$ sharing segment $s$ (both not cancelled):
$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} = 1, \qquad \forall t < t',\; s \in S
$$

### 5.12 Ordering–time linking (big-M)
$$
e_{t',s} \geq f_{t,s} + h_{t,t',s} - M_2(1 - y_{t,t',s}), \qquad \forall t \neq t',\; s \in S
$$

**Effective headway** (same track → $h^{same}$; shared/opposite track → $h^{opp}$):
$$
h_{t,t',s} = h^{same} + (h^{opp} - h^{same})\,\phi_{t,t',s}
$$

**Track-sharing indicator** $\phi_{t,t',s}$ (linearization of $|x_{t,s} - x_{t',s}|$):
$$
\phi_{t,t',s} \geq x_{t,s} - x_{t',s}, \quad \phi_{t,t',s} \geq x_{t',s} - x_{t,s}
$$
$$
\phi_{t,t',s} \leq x_{t,s} + x_{t',s}, \quad \phi_{t,t',s} \leq 2 - x_{t,s} - x_{t',s}
$$

### 5.13 Cancellation constraints
If $z_t = 1$, fix all timing and routing variables:
$$
a_{t,st} \leq M_1(1 - z_t), \qquad dep_{t,st} \leq M_1(1 - z_t), \qquad \forall st \in ST
$$
$$
x_{t,s} \leq 1 - z_t, \qquad v_{t,s,k} \leq 1 - z_t, \qquad \forall s \in S,\; k \in K
$$
*(Cancelled trains contribute zero delay and zero energy.)*

### 5.14 Time horizon bounds
$$
0 \leq a_{t,st} \leq T_{horizon}, \qquad 0 \leq dep_{t,st} \leq T_{horizon}, \qquad \forall t \in T,\; st \in ST
$$

### 5.15 Binary and nonnegativity constraints
$$
x_{t,s},\ y_{t,t',s},\ z_t,\ v_{t,s,k},\ \phi_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{t,st},\ dep_{t,st},\ \delta^{arr}_{t,st},\ \delta^{dep}_{t,st},\ r_{t,s},\ e_{t,s},\ f_{t,s} \geq 0
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Component | Count |
|-----------|-------|
| Continuous variables | $O(|T||ST| + |T||S|)$ |
| Binary variables | $O(|T||S||K| + |T|^2|S| + |T|)$ |
| Constraints | $O(|T||ST| + |T||S||K| + |T|^2|S|)$ |

---

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

### 7.1 Objective Function
The objective is a **weighted sum of three competing goals**:
- **Delay minimization** ($w^{arr}, w^{dep}$): penalizes late arrivals and departures relative to schedule (one-sided deviation).
- **Cancellation penalty** ($w^{cancel}$): a large fixed cost per cancelled train, discouraging unnecessary cancellations.
- **Energy minimization** ($w^{energy}$): encourages selection of energy-efficient speed profiles. The trade-off between speed (shorter running time → less delay) and energy (lower speed → less energy) is captured by the discrete speed level selection.

### 7.2 Speed Profile Selection
Discrete speed levels $k \in K$ approximate continuous speed profiles. Each level $k$ has an associated **running time** $run_{t,s,k}$ and **energy consumption** $E_{t,s,k}$, precomputed from train dynamics (mass, resistance, traction/braking limits). The constraint $\sum_k v_{t,s,k} = 1$ ensures exactly one profile is chosen per train-segment.

### 7.3 Routing and Disruption
The binary variable $x_{t,s}$ captures **rerouting onto the opposite track**. Only affected trains (direction $d^*$) on the disrupted segment $s^*$ may reroute, and only within the disruption window. Trains that do not reroute must either wait until $t_{end}$ or be cancelled.

### 7.4 Ordering and Headway
The binary $y_{t,t',s}$ determines **which train enters a segment first**. The big-M constraint (5.12) enforces that the second train enters only after the first train has exited plus a safety headway. The headway depends on whether trains share the same track (same direction, same track → $h^{same}$) or use opposing/shared tracks (→ $h^{opp}$, typically larger).

### 7.5 Cancellation
The binary $z_t$ removes a train from the timetable. When $z_t = 1$, all timing, routing, and speed variables are forced to zero, effectively eliminating the train from all constraints.

### 7.6 Big-M Linearization
The model uses big-M constraints to linearize:
- **Disjunctive logic** (reroute OR wait OR cancel)
- **Ordering implications** (if $t$ before $t'$, then $e_{t'} \geq f_t + h$)
- **Cancellation** (if cancelled, all variables zero)

The constants $M_1, M_2$ must be chosen large enough to be non-binding when the corresponding binary is inactive, but not so large as to cause numerical issues. A safe choice is $M_1 = M_2 = T_{horizon}$.

### 7.7 Model Linearity
Despite the complex logic, the model is **fully linear** in the decision variables:
- All constraints are linear equalities or inequalities.
- The only nonlinearity (absolute value in headway) is linearized via auxiliary binary $\phi_{t,t',s}$.
- The objective is linear.

This makes the model solvable by standard MILP solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP).

### 7.8 Practical Considerations
- **Symmetry breaking:** For train pairs, $y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} = 1$ avoids symmetric solutions.
- **Valid inequalities:** Preprocessing can fix $v_{t,s,k} = 0$ for infeasible speed levels, and $x_{t,s} = 0$ for unaffected segments.
- **Decomposition:** For large instances, the problem can be decomposed by segment or by train for rolling-horizon solution.

---

## 8. Assumptions (marked)

1. **Discrete speed levels** approximate continuous speed profiles (piecewise-constant approximation).
2. **Constant train mass and resistance coefficients**; energy precomputed per level.
3. **Time-based headways** are constant and known.
4. **Disruption window is known in advance**; single disruption segment $s^*$.
5. **No overtaking within a segment** except via ordering variables.
6. **Rerouting is only permitted on the disrupted segment** (local rerouting strategy).
7. **Cancelled trains** contribute zero delay and zero energy.
8. **Early arrivals are not rewarded** (one-sided delay penalty).
