Text:
# Best Model: MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

I selected **Model 1** as the best candidate, as it provides the most complete and rigorous formulation, with explicit linearization of all nonlinear terms, clear handling of bidirectional conflicts on the rerouted track, and well-defined boundary conditions. Below is the finalized, complete model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T} = \{1,\dots,|T|\}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Set of stations ordered along the line, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{B} = \{1,\dots,|B|\}$ | Set of blocks (segments between consecutive stations), indexed by $b$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{U, D\}$ | Directions (Up, Down), indexed by $d$ |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1,\dots,|K|\}$ | Discretized speed intervals, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{I} = \{1,\dots,|I|\}$ | Discretized time periods, indexed by $t$ |

**Auxiliary mappings:** $b(s,s+1)$ = block between stations $s$ and $s+1$; $s^-(b)$, $s^+(b)$ = upstream/downstream stations of block $b$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $a_i^s$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_i^s$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ (m) |
| $v_{\max}, v_{\min}$ | Maximum/minimum allowed speed (m/s) |
| $a_{\text{acc}}, a_{\text{dec}}$ | Maximum acceleration/deceleration (m/s²) |
| $\tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}, \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}$ | Minimum/maximum dwell time |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time |
| $e_0, e_1, e_2$ | Energy consumption coefficients |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $\Delta_t$ | Time discretization step |
| $b^*$ | Disrupted block index |
| $T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}$ | Objective weights |
| $\text{cap}_{\text{block}}, \text{cap}_{\text{station}}$ | Block/station capacities |
| $d_i$ | Direction of train $i$ |
| $v_k$ | Representative speed of interval $k$ |
| $T_{\text{horizon}}$ | Planning horizon end time |
| $v_{\text{start}}$ | Initial speed at first station |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Binary Variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $b$ |
| $r_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes to opposite track on block $b$ |
| $y_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ operates in speed interval $k$ on block $b$ |
| $z_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is at station $s$ at time $t$ |
| $\sigma_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters block $b$ before train $j$ (bidirectional separation) |

### Continuous Variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $A_{i,s} \geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $D_{i,s} \geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $v_{i,b} \geq 0$ | Average speed of train $i$ on block $b$ |
| $\tau_{i,b} \geq 0$ | Running time of train $i$ on block $b$ |
| $e_i \geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ |
| $\text{delay}_i \geq 0$ | Total delay of train $i$ |
| $\text{delay}^A_{i,s}, \text{delay}^D_{i,s} \geq 0$ | Arrival/departure delay components |
| $\text{entry}_{i,b}, \text{exit}_{i,b} \geq 0$ | Entry/exit times of train $i$ on block $b$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \text{delay}_i \;+\; w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} e_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Arrival–Departure Relationship at Stations
$$
D_{i,s} \geq A_{i,s} + \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\, s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C1}
$$
$$
D_{i,s} \leq A_{i,s} + \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\, s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C2}
$$

### 5.2 Running Time on Blocks (Piecewise Linear Speed Approximation)
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} y_{i,b,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i, b \tag{C3}
$$
$$
v_{i,b} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v_k \, y_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall i, b \tag{C4}
$$
$$
\tau_{i,b} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \frac{L_b}{v_k} \, y_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall i, b \tag{C5}
$$

### 5.3 Travel Time Consistency
$$
A_{i,s+1} = D_{i,s} + \tau_{i,b(s,s+1)} \qquad \forall i,\, s \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\{|S|\} \tag{C6}
$$

### 5.4 Speed Bounds
$$
v_{\min} \leq v_{i,b} \leq v_{\max} \qquad \forall i, b \tag{C7}
$$

### 5.5 Acceleration / Deceleration Constraints
$$
v_{i,b+1} - v_{i,b} \leq a_{\text{acc}} \cdot \tau_{i,b} \qquad \forall i,\, \text{consecutive } b \tag{C8}
$$
$$
v_{i,b} - v_{i,b+1} \leq a_{\text{dec}} \cdot \tau_{i,b+1} \qquad \forall i,\, \text{consecutive } b \tag{C9}
$$

### 5.6 Block Entry / Exit Time Definition
$$
\text{entry}_{i,b} = D_{i,s^-(b)} \qquad \forall i, b \tag{C10}
$$
$$
\text{exit}_{i,b} = A_{i,s^+(b)} \qquad \forall i, b \tag{C11}
$$
$$
\text{exit}_{i,b} = \text{entry}_{i,b} + \tau_{i,b} \qquad \forall i, b \tag{C12}
$$

### 5.7 Ordering Constraints (Same Direction)
$$
x_{i,j,b} + x_{j,i,b} = 1 \qquad \forall i \neq j,\, b \tag{C13}
$$
$$
\text{entry}_{j,b} \geq \text{exit}_{i,b} + h - M(1 - x_{i,j,b}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\, b \tag{C14}
$$

### 5.8 Block Capacity Constraints
$$
t \Delta_t \geq \text{entry}_{i,b} - M(1 - z_{i,b,t}) \qquad \forall i, b, t \tag{C15a}
$$
$$
t \Delta_t \leq \text{exit}_{i,b} + M(1 - z_{i,b,t}) \qquad \forall i, b, t \tag{C15b}
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_{i,b,t} \leq \text{cap}_{\text{block}} \qquad \forall b, t \tag{C15c}
$$

### 5.9 Rerouting Constraints
$$
\text{entry}_{i,b^*} \leq T_{\text{end}} + M(1 - r_{i,b^*}) \qquad \forall i \tag{C16a}
$$
$$
\text{exit}_{i,b^*} \geq T_{\text{start}} - M(1 - r_{i,b^*}) \qquad \forall i \tag{C16b}
$$
$$
r_{i,b} = 0 \qquad \forall i,\, b \neq b^* \tag{C16c}
$$

### 5.10 Bidirectional Conflict on Rerouted Track
$$
\sigma_{i,j,b} + \sigma_{j,i,b} \geq r_{i,b} + r_{j,b} - 1 \qquad \forall i \neq j,\, d_i \neq d_j,\, b \tag{C17}
$$
$$
\text{entry}_{j,b} \geq \text{exit}_{i,b} + h - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,b}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\, b \tag{C18}
$$
$$
\text{entry}_{i,b} \geq \text{exit}_{j,b} + h - M(1 - \sigma_{j,i,b}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\, b \tag{C19}
$$

### 5.11 Station Capacity
$$
t \Delta_t \geq A_{i,s} - M(1 - z_{i,s,t}) \qquad \forall i, s, t \tag{C20a}
$$
$$
t \Delta_t \leq D_{i,s} + M(1 - z_{i,s,t}) \qquad \forall i, s, t \tag{C20b}
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_{i,s,t} \leq \text{cap}_{\text{station}} \qquad \forall s, t \tag{C20c}
$$

### 5.12 Energy Consumption (Piecewise Linear)
$$
e_i = \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \left( e_0 \frac{L_b}{v_k} + e_1 L_b + e_2 v_k L_b \right) y_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall i \tag{C21}
$$

### 5.13 Delay Calculation
$$
\text{delay}^A_{i,s} \geq A_{i,s} - a_i^s, \quad \text{delay}^A_{i,s} \geq 0 \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C22}
$$
$$
\text{delay}^D_{i,s} \geq D_{i,s} - d_i^s, \quad \text{delay}^D_{i,s} \geq 0 \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C23}
$$
$$
\text{delay}_i = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \text{delay}^A_{i,s} + \text{delay}^D_{i,s} \right) \qquad \forall i \tag{C24}
$$

### 5.14 Initial and Boundary Conditions
$$
D_{i,1} \geq d_i^1 \qquad \forall i \tag{C25}
$$
$$
A_{i,|S|} \leq T_{\text{horizon}} \qquad \forall i \tag{C26}
$$
$$
v_{i,1} \leq v_{\text{start}} \qquad \forall i \tag{C27}
$$

### 5.15 Variable Domains
$$
x_{i,j,b},\, r_{i,b},\, y_{i,b,k},\, z_{i,s,t},\, \sigma_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\} \tag{C28}
$$
$$
A_{i,s},\, D_{i,s},\, v_{i,b},\, \tau_{i,b},\, e_i,\, \text{delay}_i,\, \text{delay}^A_{i,s},\, \text{delay}^D_{i,s},\, \text{entry}_{i,b},\, \text{exit}_{i,b} \geq 0 \tag{C29}
$$

---

## 6. Model Explanation

- **Objective:** Weighted sum balancing **service quality** (delay) and **operational cost** (energy), tunable via $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}$.
- **Speed discretization (C3–C5):** The nonlinear relation $\tau = L/v$ is linearized via a convex combination of precomputed breakpoints $L_b/v_k$; binary $y_{i,b,k}$ selects exactly one interval per train-block pair.
- **Ordering & headway (C13–C14):** Binary $x_{i,j,b}$ enforces total order between trains on each block; big-M activates headway only when ordering is active.
- **Rerouting logic (C16):** When a train's occupancy of the disrupted block $b^*$ overlaps $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$, $r_{i,b^*}$ is forced to 1; rerouting is forbidden on all other blocks.
- **Bidirectional conflict (C17–C19):** When opposite-direction trains share the rerouted track, $\sigma_{i,j,b}$ selects which goes first, enforcing headway separation — the key disjunctive constraint for single-track scheduling.
- **Energy linearization (C21):** The quadratic energy function is evaluated at each discretized speed $v_k$ and weighted by $y_{i,b,k}$, yielding an exact PWL representation.
- **Delay linearization (C22–C24):** The $\max(0,\cdot)$ operator is linearized via non-negative delay variables, pushed tight by the minimizing objective.
- **Big-M choice:** $M = T_{\text{horizon}} + \max_b(L_b/v_{\min})$.

---

## 7. Assumptions (marked as such)

1. **Single-track line with bidirectional traffic** (two parallel tracks, one per direction).
2. **Disruption affects one direction's track** on a specific block $b^*$ during $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$.
3. **Homogeneous trains** (identical max speed, acceleration, deceleration).
4. **Time and space are discretized** for tractability.
5. **Energy consumption** is a quadratic function of speed and linear in distance.
6. **No cancellations** in the base model — all trains complete their journeys.
7. **Dwell times are flexible** within $[\tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}, \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}]$.
8. **Perfect information** about disruption timing and location.
9. **Rerouting is permitted only on the disrupted block** $b^*$ (local rerouting strategy).

---

## 8. Complexity and Solution Approach

- **Binary variables:** $O(|T|^2|B|)$ ordering, $O(|T||B||K|)$ speed, $O(|T||S||I|)$ station occupancy.
- **Recommended solvers:** Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP for medium instances.
- **Decomposition (per the paper):** Reformulate into an integer programming (IP) model on train interactions plus a series of single-train plans, transforming the problem into a **train plan selection problem**; solve with an **adaptive iterative algorithm** with local branching for large-scale instances.

Text:
# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Among the three generated models, **Model 3** is the strongest formulation. It most completely captures the coupled TRP–TSMP structure described in the input: it explicitly models bidirectional rerouting conflicts on the shared opposite track (via a dedicated opposite-track ordering variable $y^{opp}_{i,j,s}$), it correctly handles the disruption-window disjunction, and it provides the cleanest linearization of the speed-profile/energy coupling (asymmetric acceleration vs. regenerative braking). Below is the complete, self-contained model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $T_A \subset T$ | Trains traveling in direction A |
| $T_B \subset T$ | Trains traveling in direction B |
| $S$ | Ordered set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $D \subset S$ | Disrupted segments $(s,s+1)$ (partial blockage area) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $(s,s+1)$ [km] |
| $t^{start}, t^{end}$ | Disruption window start/end times |
| $\tau^{min}, \tau^{max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time [min] |
| $v_k$ | Speed of level $k$ [km/h] |
| $e_k$ | Traction energy rate at speed $k$ [kWh/km] |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | Acceleration / regenerative-braking energy coefficients |
| $\bar{a}_{i,s}, \bar{d}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $p_i$ | Passenger demand weight for train $i$ |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Objective weights (delay, cancellation, energy) |
| $N^{max}$ | Maximum number of cancellations |
| $\Delta^{max}$ | Maximum allowed schedule deviation |
| $v^{max}_s$ | Speed limit on segment $s$ (curves/tunnels) |
| $a^{max}, d^{max}$ | Max acceleration/deceleration |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta^{a}_{i,s}, \delta^{d}_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Arrival / departure delay |
| $y_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ departs before $j$ at station $s$ (normal track) |
| $y^{opp}_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Ordering on opposite track for segment $(s,s+1)$ |
| $r_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses opposite track on segment $(s,s+1)$ |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $z_{i,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if speed level $k$ selected on segment $(s,s+1)$ |
| $v^{sel}_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Selected speed on segment $(s,s+1)$ |
| $run_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Running time on segment $(s,s+1)$ |
| $\Delta v^+_{i,s}, \Delta v^-_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Positive / negative speed change between segments |
| $acc_{i,s}, dec_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Acceleration / deceleration indicators |
| $E_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption on segment $(s,s+1)$ |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_1 \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} p_i \left(\delta^{a}_{i,s} + \delta^{d}_{i,s}\right) + w_2 \sum_{i \in T} c_i + w_3 \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S \setminus \{|S|\}} E_{i,s}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Feasibility
$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} + \tau^{min}(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{1a}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \leq a_{i,s} + \tau^{max}(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{1b}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \geq d_{i,s} + run_{i,s} - M \cdot c_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{1c}
$$

### 5.2 Schedule Deviation
$$
\delta^{a}_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - \bar{a}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{2a}
$$
$$
\delta^{d}_{i,s} \geq d_{i,s} - \bar{d}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{2b}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \leq \bar{a}_{i,s} + \Delta^{max}(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{2c}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \leq \bar{d}_{i,s} + \Delta^{max}(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{2d}
$$

### 5.3 Headway and Safety (Normal Track)
$$
y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} \leq 1 \quad \forall i,j \in T,\; i \neq j,\; s \in S \tag{3a}
$$
$$
d_{j,s} \geq d_{i,s} + h - M(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M(c_i + c_j) \quad \forall i,j \in T,\; i \neq j,\; s \in S \tag{3b}
$$
$$
a_{j,s+1} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h - M(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M(c_i + c_j) \quad \forall i,j \in T,\; i \neq j,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{3c}
$$

### 5.4 Disruption Window
For each blocked segment $s \in D$:
$$
a_{i,s+1} \leq t^{start} + M \cdot r_{i,s} + M \cdot c_i \quad \forall i \in T \tag{4a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \geq t^{end} - M \cdot r_{i,s} - M \cdot c_i \quad \forall i \in T \tag{4b}
$$

### 5.5 Rerouting Capacity
$$
\sum_{i \in T_A} r_{i,s} \leq 1 \quad \forall s \in D \tag{5a}
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in T_B} r_{i,s} \leq 1 \quad \forall s \in D \tag{5b}
$$
$$
y^{opp}_{i,j,s} + y^{opp}_{j,i,s} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in T_A,\; j \in T_B,\; s \in D \tag{5c}
$$
$$
a_{j,s+1} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h - M(1 - y^{opp}_{i,j,s}) - M(2 - r_{i,s} - r_{j,s}) \quad \forall i \in T_A,\; j \in T_B,\; s \in D \tag{5d}
$$

### 5.6 Speed Profile
$$
\sum_{k \in K} z_{i,s,k} = 1 - c_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{6a}
$$
$$
v^{sel}_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} v_k \cdot z_{i,s,k} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{6b}
$$
$$
run_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} \frac{L_s}{v_k} \cdot z_{i,s,k} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{6c}
$$
$$
v^{sel}_{i,s} \leq v^{max}_s (1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{6d}
$$

### 5.7 Acceleration / Deceleration Dynamics
$$
\Delta v^+_{i,s} - \Delta v^-_{i,s} = v^{sel}_{i,s} - v^{sel}_{i,s-1} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{1, |S|\} \tag{7a}
$$
$$
\Delta v^+_{i,s} \leq a^{max} \cdot L_s (1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{7b}
$$
$$
\Delta v^-_{i,s} \leq d^{max} \cdot L_s (1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{7c}
$$
$$
acc_{i,s} \geq \frac{\Delta v^+_{i,s}}{M}, \quad dec_{i,s} \geq \frac{\Delta v^-_{i,s}}{M} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{7d}
$$
$$
acc_{i,s} + dec_{i,s} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{7e}
$$

### 5.8 Cancellation
$$
\sum_{i \in T} c_i \leq N^{max} \tag{8a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \leq M(1 - c_i), \quad d_{i,s} \leq M(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{8b}
$$

### 5.9 Energy Consumption
$$
E_{i,s} = L_s \sum_{k \in K} e_k \cdot z_{i,s,k} + \alpha \cdot \Delta v^+_{i,s} - \beta \cdot \Delta v^-_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{|S|\} \tag{9}
$$

### 5.10 Variable Domains
$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \delta^{a}_{i,s}, \delta^{d}_{i,s}, v^{sel}_{i,s}, run_{i,s}, \Delta v^+_{i,s}, \Delta v^-_{i,s}, E_{i,s} \geq 0
$$
$$
y_{i,j,s}, y^{opp}_{i,j,s}, r_{i,s}, c_i, z_{i,s,k}, acc_{i,s}, dec_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

### 6.1 Modeling Philosophy
The model jointly optimizes **timetable rescheduling** (arrival/departure times), **routing** (normal vs. opposite track), **speed profile selection**, and **cancellation decisions** under a fixed disruption window. All nonlinear elements — running time as a function of speed, and energy as a function of speed and acceleration — are **linearized** through binary speed-level selection variables $z_{i,s,k}$.

### 6.2 Key Modeling Choices

- **Piecewise-linear speed representation.** Discretizing speed into $K$ levels converts the nonlinear $L_s/v$ running-time term into a linear selection. Constraint (6a)–(6b) ensures exactly one speed level is active per segment, while (6c) keeps running time linear.
- **Big-M disjunction for the disruption.** Constraints (4a)–(4b) implement the logical OR: a train either finishes the blocked segment before $t^{start}$, starts after $t^{end}$, or reroutes ($r_{i,s}=1$). Big-M terms deactivate the constraint when rerouting or cancellation is chosen.
- **Bidirectional rerouting logic.** Constraints (5a)–(5b) cap the number of rerouted trains per direction on each disrupted segment (single-track opposite-track capacity). Constraint (5d) enforces headway between opposite-direction rerouted trains using a dedicated ordering variable $y^{opp}_{i,j,s}$, activated only when both trains reroute via $M(2 - r_{i,s} - r_{j,s})$.
- **Acceleration energy linearization.** The kinetic-energy change $\tfrac{1}{2}m(v_2^2 - v_1^2)$ is approximated linearly as $\alpha \cdot \Delta v^+ - \beta \cdot \Delta v^-$, with $\Delta v^+$ and $\Delta v^-$ split via (7a). This avoids quadratic terms while capturing the asymmetric cost of acceleration vs. regenerative braking.
- **Cancellation handling.** Binary $c_i$ deactivates all train-specific constraints via big-M terms (1c, 3b, 4a–4b, 8b), and (8a) limits total cancellations.

### 6.3 Objective Components
- **Passenger delay** ($w_1$): weighted by $p_i$ to reflect demand importance; sums arrival and departure deviations.
- **Cancellation penalty** ($w_2$): discourages cancellations, typically the most disruptive intervention.
- **Energy consumption** ($w_3$): captures operational cost and environmental impact via traction energy plus acceleration penalties.

### 6.4 Assumptions Reflected in the Model
1. **Single disruption area / fixed window** — $D$ and $[t^{start}, t^{end}]$ are parameters, not variables.
2. **No overtaking within a segment** — enforced implicitly by segment-level headway (3c) and single rerouting capacity (5a–5b).
3. **Fixed order outside disruption** — $y_{i,j,s}$ allows reordering only at stations, consistent with block-section signaling.
4. **Linearized energy–speed relation** — justified by the discrete speed-level approximation.
5. **Passenger demand weights given** — $p_i$ is exogenous.

### 6.5 Practical Notes
- Solvable by standard MILP solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, HiGHS).
- Tight big-M values (set to the planning horizon) improve solver performance.
- For large instances, valid inequalities (on $y$ symmetry, $z$ linking) and warm-starts from a heuristic substantially reduce solution time.

### 6.6 Model Size
- Continuous variables: $O(|T| \cdot |S|)$
- Binary variables: $O(|T|^2 \cdot |S| + |T| \cdot |S| \cdot |K|)$
- Constraints: dominated by headway ($O(|T|^2 \cdot |S|)$) and speed profile ($O(|T| \cdot |S| \cdot |K|)$)

Text:
# A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Availability Constraints

## 1. Motivation and Scope

We consider the problem faced by a passenger railway operator (e.g., NS in the Netherlands) that must reschedule its rolling stock after a disruption (e.g., a full blockage of a line section). The operator must decide, for each trip in the (possibly adjusted) timetable, which rolling stock units (train units) operate it, how these units are coupled into compositions, and which shunting movements are performed at stations. Crucially, each proposed shunting movement must be feasible with respect to the available railway infrastructure at the station where it takes place. We model this by coupling a **composition model** (rolling stock circulation) with an **infrastructure model** (track occupation and shunting feasibility).

The complete model below is a single MILP that integrates both aspects. It is inspired by the composition model of Fioole et al. (2006) and the infrastructure model of Van Aken et al. (2017), adapted to the rescheduling setting described in the introduction.

---

## 2. Assumptions

1. **Disruption scenario is given.** A set of trips is canceled or has a modified timetable; the set of remaining trips and their (adjusted) departure/arrival times are known.
2. **Rolling stock types.** There is a set of train unit types (e.g., ICM, DDZ, SGM), each with a known capacity (seats) and length.
3. **Composition model.** Each trip is operated by a composition of one or more train units of possibly different types. Coupling/uncoupling is only allowed at stations where shunting is permitted.
4. **Shunting movements.** A shunting movement is a movement of a (part of a) composition between a platform track and a shunting yard track (or between two tracks) at a station. Each shunting movement occupies a specific track for a specific time interval.
5. **Infrastructure.** At each station, a set of tracks is available. Each track can host at most one shunting movement at a time (no overtaking on a single track). Tracks have a minimum headway time between consecutive movements.
6. **Delays.** Other passenger trains may be delayed by at most a small amount (e.g., 3 minutes) to create windows for shunting movements. These delays are assumed to be absorbed by timetable buffers.
7. **Objective.** Minimize a weighted sum of: (a) operational costs (number of units used, shunting movements), (b) passenger service level (seat shortages), (c) deviation from the original plan (stick-to-the-plan), and (d) delays imposed on other trains.
8. **Time discretization.** The planning horizon is discretized into time steps (e.g., minutes). All times are expressed in these discrete units.
9. **Linearization.** All constraints are linear; binary variables are used for logical conditions (e.g., whether a shunting movement occurs, whether a track is occupied).

---

## 3. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \(T\) | Set of trips in the timetable, indexed by \(t\). |
| \(S\) | Set of stations, indexed by \(s\). |
| \(K\) | Set of train unit types, indexed by \(k\). |
| \(U\) | Set of individual rolling stock units, indexed by \(u\). Each unit \(u\) has a type \(k(u) \in K\). |
| \(M\) | Set of shunting movements, indexed by \(m\). |
| \(R_s\) | Set of tracks at station \(s\), indexed by \(r\). |
| \(H\) | Set of time steps in the planning horizon, indexed by \(h\). |
| \(P\) | Set of passenger trains (other than the rescheduled trips) that may be delayed, indexed by \(p\). |
| \(\mathcal{O}\) | Set of ordered pairs of trips \((t, t')\) that can be consecutively operated by the same unit (i.e., \(t'\) departs after \(t\) arrives at the same station, with sufficient turn-around time). |
| \(\mathcal{S}\) | Set of ordered pairs of shunting movements \((m, m')\) that cannot be performed simultaneously on the same track (conflict pairs). |
| \(\mathcal{C}\) | Set of cuts (combinations of shunting movements that are infeasible together), generated by the infrastructure model. |

---

## 4. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \(d_t\) | Departure time of trip \(t\) (in time steps). |
| \(a_t\) | Arrival time of trip \(t\). |
| \(o_t\) | Origin station of trip \(t\). |
| \(e_t\) | Destination station of trip \(t\). |
| \(p_t\) | Number of passengers expected on trip \(t\). |
| \(c_k\) | Capacity (seats) of a unit of type \(k\). |
| \(l_k\) | Length of a unit of type \(k\). |
| \(L_r\) | Maximum length of trains that can be accommodated on track \(r\). |
| \(w_k\) | Operational cost per unit of type \(k\) per time step. |
| \(w^{\text{shunt}}\) | Cost per shunting movement. |
| \(w^{\text{seat}}\) | Penalty per unit of seat shortage. |
| \(w^{\text{dev}}\) | Penalty for deviating from the original plan (per unit reassignment). |
| \(w^{\text{delay}}\) | Penalty per time step of delay imposed on other trains. |
| \(h_{\min}\) | Minimum headway time between consecutive shunting movements on the same track. |
| \(\Delta^{\max}\) | Maximum allowed delay for other trains. |
| \(x_{u,t}^{\text{orig}}\) | 1 if unit \(u\) was originally assigned to trip \(t\), 0 otherwise. |
| \(y_{m}^{\text{orig}}\) | 1 if shunting movement \(m\) was in the original plan, 0 otherwise. |
| \(A_{m,r}\) | 1 if shunting movement \(m\) uses track \(r\), 0 otherwise. |
| \(B_{p,r,h}\) | 1 if passenger train \(p\) occupies track \(r\) at time \(h\), 0 otherwise. |

---

## 5. Decision Variables

### 5.1 Composition and Assignment Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| \(x_{u,t}\) | Binary | 1 if unit \(u\) is assigned to trip \(t\). |
| \(z_{t,k}\) | Integer \(\ge 0\) | Number of units of type \(k\) assigned to trip \(t\). |
| \(v_{t}\) | Integer \(\ge 0\) | Total number of units assigned to trip \(t\). |
| \(q_{t}\) | Continuous \(\ge 0\) | Seat shortage on trip \(t\) (passengers minus capacity). |
| \(\delta_{u,t}\) | Binary | 1 if unit \(u\) is assigned to trip \(t\) but was not originally assigned to it (deviation). |

### 5.2 Shunting Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| \(y_{m}\) | Binary | 1 if shunting movement \(m\) is performed. |
| \(s_{m,h}\) | Binary | 1 if shunting movement \(m\) starts at time \(h\). |
| \(f_{m,h}\) | Binary | 1 if shunting movement \(m\) occupies its track at time \(h\). |

### 5.3 Infrastructure and Delay Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| \(\tau_{p}\) | Integer \(\ge 0\) | Delay imposed on passenger train \(p\) (in time steps). |
| \(\theta_{m}\) | Integer \(\ge 0\) | Start time of shunting movement \(m\). |

### 5.4 Coupling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| \(\lambda_{m,t}\) | Binary | 1 if shunting movement \(m\) is associated with trip \(t\) (e.g., coupling/uncoupling before/after trip \(t\)). |
| \(\mu_{m,m'}\) | Binary | 1 if shunting movements \(m\) and \(m'\) are performed in sequence on the same track. |

---

## 6. Objective Function

Minimize:

\[
\begin{aligned}
Z = & \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{t \in T} w_k \, z_{t,k} 
+ w^{\text{shunt}} \sum_{m \in M} y_m 
+ w^{\text{seat}} \sum_{t \in T} q_t \\
& + w^{\text{dev}} \sum_{u \in U} \sum_{t \in T} \delta_{u,t} 
+ w^{\text{delay}} \sum_{p \in P} \tau_p
\end{aligned}
\]

**Explanation:**
- First term: operational cost of using train units (proportional to type and number).
- Second term: cost of performing shunting movements.
- Third term: penalty for seat shortages (passenger service level).
- Fourth term: penalty for deviating from the original rolling stock plan (stick-to-the-plan).
- Fifth term: penalty for delaying other passenger trains.

---

## 7. Constraints

### 7.1 Composition Model Constraints

**(1) Unit assignment to trips:**

\[
x_{u,t} \le 1 \quad \forall u \in U, \, t \in T
\]

**(2) Consistency between unit assignment and type count:**

\[
z_{t,k} = \sum_{u \in U : k(u) = k} x_{u,t} \quad \forall t \in T, \, k \in K
\]

**(3) Total units per trip:**

\[
v_t = \sum_{k \in K} z_{t,k} \quad \forall t \in T
\]

**(4) Capacity and seat shortage:**

\[
\sum_{k \in K} c_k \, z_{t,k} + q_t \ge p_t \quad \forall t \in T
\]

**(5) Train length limit at stations:**

\[
\sum_{k \in K} l_k \, z_{t,k} \le L_{e_t} \quad \forall t \in T
\]

**(6) Unit flow conservation (each unit is assigned to at most one trip at a time):**

\[
\sum_{t \in T : d_t \le h < a_t} x_{u,t} \le 1 \quad \forall u \in U, \, h \in H
\]

**(7) Consecutive trip compatibility:**

\[
x_{u,t} + x_{u,t'} \le 1 \quad \forall u \in U, \, (t,t') \notin \mathcal{O}
\]

**(8) Deviation from original plan:**

\[
\delta_{u,t} \ge x_{u,t} - x_{u,t}^{\text{orig}} \quad \forall u \in U, \, t \in T
\]

\[
\delta_{u,t} \ge x_{u,t}^{\text{orig}} - x_{u,t} \quad \forall u \in U, \, t \in T
\]

**(9) Coupling/uncoupling requires shunting:**

If a unit is assigned to trip \(t\) and then to trip \(t'\), and the composition changes (i.e., units are coupled/uncoupled), then a shunting movement must occur:

\[
x_{u,t} + x_{u,t'} - 1 \le \sum_{m \in M_{t,t'}} y_m \quad \forall u \in U, \, (t,t') \in \mathcal{O}
\]

where \(M_{t,t'} \subseteq M\) is the set of shunting movements that can serve the connection between \(t\) and \(t'\).

---

### 7.2 Shunting Movement Constraints

**(10) Shunting movement timing:**

Each shunting movement \(m\) has a planned start time window \([h_m^{\min}, h_m^{\max}]\):

\[
\sum_{h = h_m^{\min}}^{h_m^{\max}} s_{m,h} = y_m \quad \forall m \in M
\]

**(11) Track occupation:**

\[
f_{m,h} = \sum_{h' = h - d_m + 1}^{h} s_{m,h'} \quad \forall m \in M, \, h \in H
\]

where \(d_m\) is the duration of shunting movement \(m\).

**(12) Track capacity (at most one shunting movement per track at a time):**

\[
\sum_{m \in M : A_{m,r} = 1} f_{m,h} \le 1 \quad \forall r \in R_s, \, s \in S, \, h \in H
\]

**(13) Minimum headway between consecutive shunting movements on the same track:**

\[
s_{m,h} + s_{m',h'} \le 1 \quad \forall (m,m') \in \mathcal{S}, \, |h - h'| < h_{\min}
\]

**(14) Conflict with passenger trains:**

If a passenger train \(p\) occupies track \(r\) at time \(h\), no shunting movement on that track can occur unless the train is delayed:

\[
f_{m,h} + B_{p,r,h} \le 1 + \sum_{h' = h}^{h + \tau_p} B_{p,r,h'} \quad \forall m \in M, \, r \in R_s, \, p \in P, \, h \in H
\]

**(15) Maximum delay:**

\[
\tau_p \le \Delta^{\max} \quad \forall p \in P
\]

**(16) Shunting movement sequencing (if two movements use the same track in sequence):**

\[
\mu_{m,m'} \ge f_{m,h} + f_{m',h'} - 1 \quad \forall (m,m') \in \mathcal{S}, \, h' > h
\]

\[
\theta_{m'} \ge \theta_m + d_m + h_{\min} - M(1 - \mu_{m,m'}) \quad \forall (m,m') \in \mathcal{S}
\]

---

### 7.3 Infrastructure Feasibility Cuts

**(17) Combinatorial Benders' cuts:**

For each infeasible combination of shunting movements \(C \subseteq M\) identified by the infrastructure model:

\[
\sum_{m \in C} y_m \le |C| - 1
\]

These cuts prohibit the simultaneous performance of shunting movements that cannot be feasibly scheduled on the available infrastructure.

---

### 7.4 Coupling Between Composition and Shunting

**(18) Shunting movement associated with trip:**

\[
\lambda_{m,t} \le y_m \quad \forall m \in M, \, t \in T
\]

\[
\sum_{m \in M} \lambda_{m,t} \ge v_t - 1 \quad \forall t \in T
\]

**(19) Shunting movement only if composition changes:**

\[
y_m \le \sum_{t \in T} \lambda_{m,t} \quad \forall m \in M
\]

**(20) Original shunting movements:**

\[
y_m \ge y_m^{\text{orig}} - \sum_{C \ni m} \left(1 - \sum_{m' \in C} y_{m'}\right) \quad \forall m \in M
\]

---

### 7.5 Variable Domains

\[
x_{u,t}, \, \delta_{u,t}, \, y_m, \, s_{m,h}, \, f_{m,h}, \, \lambda_{m,t}, \, \mu_{m,m'} \in \{0,1\}
\]

\[
z_{t,k}, \, v_t, \, \tau_p, \, \theta_m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}
\]

\[
q_t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}
\]

---

## 8. Model Summary

The complete MILP integrates:

1. **Composition model:** Assigns rolling stock units to trips, ensures capacity and length constraints, and models coupling/uncoupling.
2. **Shunting model:** Determines which shunting movements occur, when they occur, and on which tracks, ensuring no conflicts with other shunting movements or passenger trains.
3. **Infrastructure model:** Enforces track capacity, headway, and delay constraints; generates cuts for infeasible shunting combinations.
4. **Objective:** Balances operational costs, passenger service, stick-to-the-plan, and delays.

The model can be solved using a **Combinatorial Benders' decomposition** (exact approach) or an **iterative heuristic** that feeds shunting movements one by one to the infrastructure model, as described in the introduction.

---

## 9. Notes on Implementation

- **Exact approach:** Solve the MILP with all cuts (17) added iteratively. The master problem is the composition model; the subproblem is the infrastructure model that checks feasibility of shunting movements and generates cuts.
- **Iterative heuristic:** Process shunting movements one by one, checking feasibility with the infrastructure model. If infeasible, cancel or adjust the movement and re-solve the composition model. This mimics the interaction between rolling stock dispatchers and infrastructure dispatchers.
- **Linearization:** All logical constraints are linearized using binary variables and big-M formulations where necessary.
- **Time discretization:** The horizon \(H\) should be fine enough (e.g., 1-minute steps) to capture shunting movements accurately.

---

This model provides a complete, linear formulation for rolling stock rescheduling with infrastructure availability constraints, suitable for both exact and heuristic solution approaches.

Text:
# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Among the three generated formulations, **Model 2** is the strongest: it is the most complete, rigorously linearized, and internally consistent. It uniquely includes the **spatial consistency constraint** (distance covered = segment length), a **monotonic cancellation** structure, **per-direction capacity** constraints that correctly model bidirectional shared-track operation, and **Big-M terms tightened by cancellation variables**. I present it below as the final model, with minor clarifications.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Stations, indexed $s = 1,\dots,S$ (ordered along line) |
| $K$ | Segments, indexed $k = 1,\dots,S-1$ (segment $k$ connects stations $s$ and $s+1$) |
| $T$ | Discretized time steps, $t = 1,\dots,|T|$ |
| $K^* \subseteq K$ | Disrupted segments ($|K^*|=1$, index $k^*$) |
| $T_d = \{t : T_{\text{start}} \le t \le T_{\text{end}}\}$ | Disruption time window |
| $D = \{0,1\}$ | Direction set (0 = nominal, 1 = opposite) |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | s |
| $dep^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | s |
| $\tau^{\min}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time | s |
| $r^{\min}_{i,k}$ | Minimum running time on segment $k$ | s |
| $v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ | Speed bounds | m/s |
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ | m |
| $\Delta t$ | Time-step duration (5 s) | s |
| $h$ | Minimum headway | s |
| $C_k$ | Capacity per direction on segment $k$ (=1) | trains |
| $M$ | Big-M constant | — |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) | — |
| $c_1, c_2$ | Energy coefficients (resistive, inertial) | — |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Delay penalty weight | — |
| $P^{\text{cancel}}$ | Cancellation penalty | — |
| $T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window bounds | s |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual arrival time |
| $dep_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual departure time |
| $x_{i,k,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $k$ at time $t$ |
| $y_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ rerouted to opposite track on segment $k$ |
| $z_{i,j,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ |
| $v_{i,k,t}$ | $[v^{\min}, v^{\max}]$ | Speed of train $i$ on segment $k$ at time $t$ |
| $e_{i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Energy consumed on segment $k$ |
| $u_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ cancelled at/before station $s$ |
| $w_{i,k,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ in disruption area of segment $k$ at time $t$ |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Positive delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $a^{+}_{i,k,t}, a^{-}_{i,k,t}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Positive parts of acceleration / deceleration |
| $\eta_{i,k,t}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Piecewise-linear proxy for $v^2$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S} d_{i,s}\,\delta_{i,s} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{k \in K} e_{i,k} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S} P^{\text{cancel}}\, u_{i,s}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Consistency
$$
dep_{i,s} \;\ge\; a_{i,s} + \tau^{\min}_{i,s} \quad \forall i, s \tag{C1}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \;\ge\; dep_{i,s} + r^{\min}_{i,k} \quad \forall i, k=(s,s+1) \tag{C2}
$$
$$
u_{i,s+1} \;\ge\; u_{i,s} \quad \forall i, s \in S\setminus\{S\} \tag{C3}
$$

### 5.2 Speed–Position Coupling
$$
\sum_{t \in T} x_{i,k,t}\,\Delta t \;=\; a_{i,s+1} - dep_{i,s} \quad \forall i, k=(s,s+1) \tag{C4}
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T} v_{i,k,t}\,\Delta t \;=\; L_k \quad \forall i, k \tag{C5}
$$
$$
v^{\min}\, x_{i,k,t} \;\le\; v_{i,k,t} \;\le\; v^{\max}\, x_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C6}
$$

### 5.3 Acceleration Linearization
$$
v_{i,k,t} - v_{i,k,t-1} \;=\; a^{+}_{i,k,t} - a^{-}_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i,k,t \in T\setminus\{1\} \tag{C7}
$$
$$
a^{+}_{i,k,t} \ge 0,\quad a^{-}_{i,k,t} \ge 0
$$

### 5.4 Energy (Piecewise-Linearized)
With breakpoints $\{(v^p, \eta^p)\}$ and slopes $\lambda^p$:
$$
\eta_{i,k,t} \;\ge\; \lambda^p\, v_{i,k,t} + \mu^p \quad \forall p, i, k, t \tag{C8}
$$
$$
e_{i,k} \;\ge\; c_1 \sum_{t \in T} \eta_{i,k,t}\,\Delta t \;+\; c_2 \sum_{t \in T} \bigl(a^{+}_{i,k,t} + a^{-}_{i,k,t}\bigr)\,\Delta t \quad \forall i,k \tag{C9}
$$

### 5.5 Disruption and Rerouting
$$
x_{i,k^*,t} \;\le\; y_{i,k^*} \quad \forall i, k^* \in K^*,\; t \in T_d \tag{C10}
$$
$$
y_{i,k} \;\le\; \sum_{t \in T_d} w_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i, k \tag{C11}
$$
$$
y_{i,k} \;=\; 0 \quad \forall i, k \in K \setminus K^* \tag{C12}
$$
$$
w_{i,k,t} \;\le\; x_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i, k \in K^*,\; t \in T_d \tag{C13}
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T_d} w_{i,k,t} \;\ge\; y_{i,k} \quad \forall i, k \in K^* \tag{C14}
$$

### 5.6 Track Capacity (Bidirectional Sharing)
$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{i,k,t}\,\mathbb{1}[d_i = 0] \;\le\; C_k \quad \forall k, t \tag{C15}
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{i,k,t}\,\mathbb{1}[d_i = 1] \;\le\; C_k \quad \forall k, t \tag{C16}
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{i,k,t} \;\le\; C_k + \sum_{i \in I} y_{i,k} \quad \forall k \in K^*,\; t \in T_d \tag{C17}
$$

### 5.7 Conflict-Free Ordering and Headway
$$
z_{i,j,k} + z_{j,i,k} \;=\; 1 \quad \forall i < j,\; k \tag{C18}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \;\le\; dep_{j,s} + M\,(1 - z_{i,j,k}) + M\,u_{i,s} + M\,u_{j,s} \quad \forall i \ne j,\; k=(s,s+1) \tag{C19}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} - dep_{j,s} \;\ge\; h - M\,(1 - z_{i,j,k}) - M\,(u_{i,s} + u_{j,s}) \quad \forall i \ne j,\; s \tag{C20}
$$

### 5.8 Delay Linearization
$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\ge\; a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \;\ge\; 0 \quad \forall i, s \tag{C21}
$$

### 5.9 Cancellation Linking
$$
a_{i,s} \;\le\; M\,(1 - u_{i,s}) \quad \forall i, s \tag{C22}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} \;\le\; M\,(1 - u_{i,s}) \quad \forall i, s \tag{C23}
$$
$$
x_{i,k,t} \;\le\; 1 - u_{i,s} \quad \forall i, k=(s,s+1),\; t \tag{C24}
$$

### 5.10 Domains
$$
a_{i,s},\, dep_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}; \quad x_{i,k,t},\, y_{i,k},\, z_{i,j,k},\, u_{i,s},\, w_{i,k,t} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
v_{i,k,t} \in [v^{\min}, v^{\max}]; \quad e_{i,k},\, \delta_{i,s},\, a^{+}_{i,k,t},\, a^{-}_{i,k,t},\, \eta_{i,k,t} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}
$$

---

## 6. Key Modeling Rationale

| Element | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Speed–position coupling (C4–C6)** | Occupancy $x$ linked to continuous speed $v$ and to running time | Makes the model *integrated*: timetable and trajectory cannot be solved separately |
| **Spatial consistency (C5)** | $\sum_t v_{i,k,t}\Delta t = L_k$ | Ensures the speed profile actually covers the segment — a physical feasibility check missing in Models 1 and 3 |
| **Piecewise-linear energy (C8–C9)** | Underestimating cuts on $v^2$ | Converts quadratic drag into MILP while preserving optimality |
| **Disruption (C10–C14)** | Rerouting variable $y$ gates occupancy during $T_d$ | Encodes "blocked unless rerouted" as a logical implication |
| **Bidirectional capacity (C15–C17)** | Per-direction sums + shared-track relaxation | Correctly models single-track bidirectional traffic during disruption |
| **Big-M ordering (C18–C20)** | $z_{i,j,k}$ precedence, tightened by $u$ | Standard conflict-free timetabling; cancellation-aware |
| **Monotonic cancellation (C3)** | $u_{i,s+1} \ge u_{i,s}$ | Prevents illogical "re-appearing" trains |

---

## 7. Assumptions (marked)

- **A1.** Time is discretized at $\Delta t = 5$ s.
- **A2.** Energy quadratic term $c_1 v^2$ is linearized via piecewise-linear underestimators.
- **A3.** A single disrupted segment $k^*$ (partial blockage of one track direction).
- **A4.** Shared-track capacity = 1 train per direction (total 2 during disruption).
- **A5.** Dwell, running, headway times are given parameters.
- **A6.** Cancellation is monotone (once cancelled, a train stays cancelled downstream).

---

## 8. Tractability Notes

- **Symmetry breaking:** fix $z_{i,j,k}=1$ for $i<j$ on a reference segment.
- **Big-M tightening:** use $M = T_{\max} - T_{\min}$ (planning horizon).
- **Dominant size:** $O(|I||K||T|)$ binaries from $x_{i,k,t}$ — recommend rolling-horizon or column-generation decomposition for full-day instances.
- **Solver:** Gurobi / CPLEX / SCIP with branch-and-cut; SOS2 sets on $\eta_{i,k,t}$ accelerate the piecewise-linear cuts.

This formulation is **complete, linear, and directly solvable**, providing a unified framework for simultaneous rescheduling, rerouting, and speed management under partial segment blockages.

Text:
# A MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

Below I present a complete mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates the train rescheduling problem (TRP) and the train speed management problem (TSMP) for a high-speed railway line subject to a partial segment blockage. The model simultaneously decides (i) train arrival/departure times, (ii) train order at each block section, (iii) rerouting decisions (using the opposite track during the disruption window), and (iv) speed profiles, while co-optimizing total delay and energy consumption.

---

## 1. Model Assumptions

1. **Single double-track line** with two unidirectional tracks (one per direction). Under normal operation, each track carries trains in a single direction.
2. **Partial segment blockage**: one track of a contiguous segment `k ∈ K^D` is blocked during the time window `[τ_k^s, τ_k^e]`. Trains may be rerouted to the opposite (still-open) track within this window.
3. **Discrete time** is used: time horizon `H = {1, 2, …, |H|}` with step Δ (seconds).
4. **Discrete space**: the line is partitioned into block sections `k ∈ K`. Each section has length `L_k` (m).
5. **Train dynamics linearization**: tractable energy/speed relations are obtained by piecewise-linear approximation of the nonlinear traction/braking force curves (Howlett, Pudney & Albrecht 2022).
6. **Conflict-free operation**: at any time–space resource, at most one train may occupy it (single-track conflict rule when rerouted trains share the opposite track).
7. **Minimum dwell time** at each station and **minimum headway** between consecutive trains on the same track are enforced.
8. **No train cancellation** is allowed (assumption A1); however, the model can be extended trivially with cancellation binaries.
9. **Train homogeneity within a service class** (assumption A2): all trains in class `c ∈ C` share the same maximum speed `v_c^{max}`, acceleration `a_c^{max}`, deceleration `b_c^{max}`, and resistance coefficients.
10. **Energy model**: tractable mechanical energy `E_mech = F_t·v·Δ` is linearized using a piecewise-linear function of speed (assumption A3).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `T` | Set of trains, indexed by `i, j` |
| `C` | Set of train classes, indexed by `c` |
| `S` | Set of stations, indexed by `s` |
| `K` | Set of block sections, indexed by `k` |
| `K^D ⊆ K` | Set of blocked sections (partial blockage) |
| `R_i` | Set of feasible routes for train `i` (original + rerouting variants), indexed by `r` |
| `H` | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by `t` |
| `V` | Set of speed breakpoints for piecewise-linear energy curve, indexed by `v` |
| `A(s)` | Arcs (block sections) leaving station `s` |
| `B(s)` | Arcs entering station `s` |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| `L_k` | Length of block section `k` | m |
| `v_c^{max}` | Maximum speed of class `c` | m/s |
| `a_c^{max}` | Maximum acceleration of class `c` | m/s² |
| `b_c^{max}` | Maximum deceleration of class `c` | m/s² |
| `d_s^{min}` | Minimum dwell time at station `s` | s |
| `h^{min}` | Minimum headway time on the same track | s |
| `τ_k^s, τ_k^e` | Start/end of blockage on section `k` | s |
| `M` | Big-M constant | s |
| `p_v` | Slope of piecewise-linear energy segment `v` (kW·s / (m/s)) | – |
| `q_v` | Intercept of piecewise-linear energy segment `v` | kW |
| `α` | Weight of delay in objective (vs. energy) | – |
| `β` | Weight of energy in objective | – |
| `γ` | Penalty for rerouting (operational cost) | – |
| `c_{i,s}^{arr,0}, c_{i,s}^{dep,0}` | Scheduled arrival/departure time of train `i` at station `s` | s |
| `T_i^{run,k}` | Nominal running time of train `i` on section `k` | s |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Rescheduling (TRP) variables

- `a_{i,s} ∈ ℝ⁺` — actual arrival time of train `i` at station `s`.
- `d_{i,s} ∈ ℝ⁺` — actual departure time of train `i` at station `s`.
- `y_{i,j,k} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train `i` departs section `k` before train `j` (`i ≠ j`), 0 otherwise.
- `z_{i,r} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train `i` uses route `r`, 0 otherwise.
- `w_{i,k} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train `i` is rerouted to the opposite track on section `k`.

### 4.2 Speed management (TSMP) variables

- `v_{i,k,t} ∈ ℝ⁺` — speed of train `i` on section `k` at time `t` (m/s).
- `s_{i,k,t} ∈ ℝ⁺` — position of train `i` on section `k` at time `t` (m, cumulative from section entry).
- `f_{i,k,t} ∈ ℝ` — tractive effort of train `i` on section `k` at time `t` (kN).
- `e_{i,k,t} ∈ ℝ⁺` — instantaneous power consumption (kW).
- `λ_{i,k,t,v} ∈ [0,1]` — convex combination weight for speed breakpoint `v` at `(i,k,t)`.

### 4.3 Auxiliary variables

- `Δa_{i,s} = a_{i,s} − c_{i,s}^{arr,0}` — arrival delay of train `i` at `s`.
- `Δd_{i,s} = d_{i,s} − c_{i,s}^{dep,0}` — departure delay of train `i` at `s`.
- `E_i` — total energy consumed by train `i` (kWh).

---

## 5. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of total arrival delay, total departure delay, total energy consumption, and rerouting penalties:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\Delta a_{i,s} \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\Delta d_{i,s} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in T} E_i \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{k \in K^D} w_{i,k}
$$

with

$$
E_i \;=\; \Delta \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{t \in H} e_{i,k,t}
$$

and the linearized power function (piecewise-linear in speed):

$$
e_{i,k,t} \;=\; \sum_{v \in V} \lambda_{i,k,t,v}\, q_v \;+\; \sum_{v \in V} \lambda_{i,k,t,v}\, p_v\, v_{i,k,t}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route selection (each train picks exactly one route)

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} z_{i,r} \;=\; 1, \quad \forall i \in T
$$

### 6.2 Rerouting indicator coupling

$$
w_{i,k} \;\geq\; z_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K^D,\; r \in R_i : k \in r^{\text{reroute}}
$$

$$
w_{i,k} \;\leq\; \sum_{r \in R_i : k \in r^{\text{reroute}}} z_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K^D
$$

### 6.3 Blockage feasibility

A train may not travel on the blocked track during the disruption window:

$$
\sum_{t \in [\tau_k^s, \tau_k^e]} v_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; M\,(1 - w_{i,k}), \quad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K^D
$$

Equivalently, if `w_{i,k} = 0` (train stays on its original track), it must satisfy:

$$
s_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; L_k, \quad \forall t \in [\tau_k^s, \tau_k^e]
$$

and the rerouted train (`w_{i,k} = 1`) uses the opposite track, whose capacity is shared with oncoming trains.

### 6.4 Train dynamics (linearized motion)

Position update:

$$
s_{i,k,t+1} \;=\; s_{i,k,t} \;+\; v_{i,k,t}\,\Delta \;-\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,a_{i,k,t}\,\Delta^2, \quad \forall i,k,t
$$

Speed update:

$$
v_{i,k,t+1} \;=\; v_{i,k,t} \;+\; a_{i,k,t}\,\Delta, \quad \forall i,k,t
$$

Acceleration bounds:

$$
-b_c^{max} \;\leq\; a_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; a_c^{max}, \quad \forall i \in T_c,\; k,\; t
$$

Speed bounds:

$$
0 \;\leq\; v_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; v_c^{max}, \quad \forall i \in T_c,\; k,\; t
$$

### 6.5 Section traversal (entry/exit coupling with timetable)

Entry to section `k` from station `s`:

$$
s_{i,k, d_{i,s}} \;=\; 0, \quad \forall i,\; k \in A(s),\; s
$$

Exit from section `k` to station `s'`:

$$
s_{i,k, a_{i,s'}} \;=\; L_k, \quad \forall i,\; k \in B(s')
$$

### 6.6 Running-time consistency

$$
a_{i,s'} - d_{i,s} \;\geq\; T_i^{run,k} - M\,(1 - z_{i,r}), \quad \forall i,\; s,\; s' = s+1,\; k \in (s,s'),\; r
$$

$$
a_{i,s'} - d_{i,s} \;\leq\; T_i^{run,k} + M\,(1 - z_{i,r})
$$

### 6.7 Dwell time

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\geq\; d_s^{min}, \quad \forall i,\; s
$$

### 6.8 Ordering and headway on the same track

For every pair of trains `i, j` sharing the same track on section `k`:

$$
d_{i,s} + h^{min} \;\leq\; d_{j,s} + M\,(1 - y_{i,j,k}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k,\; s \in \text{entry}(k)
$$

$$
d_{j,s} + h^{min} \;\leq\; d_{i,s} + M\,y_{i,j,k}
$$

### 6.9 Bidirectional conflict on the opposite (shared) track

When two trains from opposite directions are rerouted onto the same track on section `k ∈ K^D`, they must not occupy the section simultaneously. This is enforced by a discrete time-indexed occupancy check:

$$
\sum_{t \in H} \mathbb{1}\{s_{i,k,t} \in [0, L_k]\} + \sum_{t \in H} \mathbb{1}\{s_{j,k,t} \in [0, L_k]\} \;\leq\; |H_k|, \quad \forall i \in T^{\uparrow},\; j \in T^{\downarrow},\; k \in K^D
$$

Linearized using auxiliary binaries `θ_{i,k,t} ∈ {0,1}` indicating occupancy:

$$
\theta_{i,k,t} \;\geq\; \frac{s_{i,k,t}}{L_k} - \epsilon, \quad \theta_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; \frac{s_{i,k,t}}{L_k}
$$

$$
\theta_{i,k,t} + \theta_{j,k,t} \;\leq\; 1, \quad \forall i \in T^{\uparrow},\; j \in T^{\downarrow},\; k \in K^D,\; t
$$

### 6.10 Section capacity (single-track rule on the opposite track)

$$
\sum_{i \in T} \theta_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; 1, \quad \forall k \in K^D,\; t
$$

### 6.11 Energy linearization (SOS2 / convex combination)

$$
\sum_{v \in V} \lambda_{i,k,t,v} \;=\; 1, \quad \lambda_{i,k,t,v} \;\geq\; 0
$$

$$
v_{i,k,t} \;=\; \sum_{v \in V} \lambda_{i,k,t,v}\, \bar{v}_v
$$

$$
e_{i,k,t} \;=\; \sum_{v \in V} \lambda_{i,k,t,v}\, \bar{e}_v
$$

(where `(\bar{v}_v, \bar{e}_v)` are breakpoints of the piecewise-linear power curve; SOS2 constraints enforce adjacency for tractability.)

### 6.12 Tractive-effort / power coupling

$$
f_{i,k,t}\, v_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; e_{i,k,t}, \quad \forall i,k,t
$$

with `f_{i,k,t}` bounded by the maximum traction force of class `c`.

### 6.13 Initial / boundary conditions

$$
s_{i,k_0, c_{i,s_0}^{dep,0}} \;=\; 0, \quad v_{i,k_0, c_{i,s_0}^{dep,0}} \;=\; 0, \quad \forall i
$$

$$
s_{i,k_{|S|}, c_{i,s_{|S|}}^{arr,0}} \;=\; L_{k_{|S|}}, \quad v_{i,k_{|S|}, c_{i,s_{|S|}}^{arr,0}} \;=\; 0, \quad \forall i
$$

### 6.14 Delay non-negativity

$$
\Delta a_{i,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} - c_{i,s}^{arr,0}, \quad \Delta a_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0
$$

$$
\Delta d_{i,s} \;\geq\; d_{i,s} - c_{i,s}^{dep,0}, \quad \Delta d_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0
$$

### 6.15 Symmetry breaking (optional)

$$
y_{i,j,k} + y_{j,i,k} \;=\; 1, \quad \forall i < j,\; k
$$

---

## 7. Summary of Variable Types

| Type | Variables | Count (approx.) |
|------|-----------|-----------------|
| Binary | `y_{i,j,k}, z_{i,r}, w_{i,k}, θ_{i,k,t}` | `O(|T|²|K| + |T||R| + |T||K^D||H|)` |
| Continuous (timing) | `a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, Δa_{i,s}, Δd_{i,s}` | `O(|T||S|)` |
| Continuous (dynamics) | `v_{i,k,t}, s_{i,k,t}, a_{i,k,t}, f_{i,k,t}, e_{i,k,t}` | `O(|T||K||H|)` |
| Continuous (SOS2) | `λ_{i,k,t,v}` | `O(|T||K||H||V|)` |

---

## 8. Notes on Tractability

- The full MILP above is exact but computationally heavy for large `|H|` and `|T|`. As indicated in the introduction, the model is intended to be solved via a **decomposition-based scheme**: an IP master problem handles the train-interaction binaries (`y, z, w, θ`), while each train's speed profile is optimized by an independent subproblem parameterized by the master's timing decisions.
- The piecewise-linear energy curve (constraint 6.11) and the SOS2 formulation are the standard linearization that makes the otherwise nonlinear train-dynamics tractable inside an MILP.
- Bidirectional conflict constraints (6.9–6.10) are the key novelty introduced by partial-blockage rerouting and are the dominant source of combinatorial complexity.

This MILP yields, in a single optimization, a **conflict-free rescheduling timetable** (with retiming, reordering, and rerouting decisions) and the corresponding **executable energy-efficient speed profiles**, jointly minimizing delay and energy consumption under partial segment blockages.

Text:
# Final MILP: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## Model Class
Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP). All absolute-value terms appear only in precomputed coefficients (e.g., $\delta_{pos}(l,l')$), never in constraints.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $K$ | Set of all trains, indexed by $k, k'$ |
| $K^{up}, K^{down}$ | Up- / down-direction trains |
| $S$ | Set of track segments |
| $S^{dis} \subseteq S$ | Segments in the disruption area |
| $R_k$ | Ordered segments on train $k$'s route |
| $L$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $l, l'$ |
| $\mathcal{C}^{dis}$ | Consecutive segment pairs $(s,s')$ within $S^{dis}$ |

$s_k^{first}$, $s_k^{last}$ denote the first/last segments of route $R_k$.

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T_{max}$ | Time horizon; all times in $\{0,\dots,T_{max}\}$ |
| $T^{dis}_{start}, T^{dis}_{end}$ | Disruption window bounds |
| $disarea_s$ | 1 if segment $s$ is disrupted |
| $allow_{k,s}$ | 1 if train $k$ may reroute on segment $s$ |
| $h$ | Minimum headway |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $\tau_{k,s,l}$ | Running time of train $k$ on segment $s$ at level $l$ |
| $e^{trac}_{k,s,l}$ | Traction energy at level $l$ |
| $e^{acc}_{k,l,l'}$ | Acceleration energy for transition $l \to l'$ |
| $\delta_{pos}(l,l')$ | Precomputed $= \max(0, e^{acc}_{k,l,l'})$ |
| $t^{entry}_k$ | Fixed entry time at first segment |
| $t^{sched}_{k,s_k^{last}}$ | Scheduled arrival at last segment |
| $pen_k$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) |

---

## Decision Variables

**Timing (integer, $\{0,\dots,T_{max}\}$):** $t^{in}_{k,s},\; t^{out}_{k,s}$

**Binary:** $y_{k,s,l}$ (speed level), $x_{k,s}$ (traversal), $r_{k,s}$ (reroute), $z_{k,s}$ (window overlap), $A_{k,s}, B_{k,s}$ (window auxiliaries), $same\_track_{k,k',s}$, $o_{k,k',s}$ (ordering), $cancel_k$, $u_{k,s,l,l'}$ (transition)

**Continuous $\ge 0$:** $E^{trac}_{k,s},\; E^{acc}_{k,s},\; delay_k$

---

## Objective (J)

$$\min \; Z = w_1 \sum_{k \in K} delay_k \;+\; w_2 \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{s \in R_k}\bigl(E^{trac}_{k,s} + E^{acc}_{k,s}\bigr) \;+\; w_3 \sum_{k \in K} pen_k \cdot cancel_k$$

---

## Constraints

### Exact Running Time (3a–3b)
$$t^{out}_{k,s} \ge t^{in}_{k,s} + \sum_{l} \tau_{k,s,l}\, y_{k,s,l} - M(1 - x_{k,s})$$
$$t^{out}_{k,s} \le t^{in}_{k,s} + \sum_{l} \tau_{k,s,l}\, y_{k,s,l} + M(1 - x_{k,s})$$

### Exact Traction Energy (4a–4d)
$$E^{trac}_{k,s} \ge \sum_{l} e^{trac}_{k,s,l}\, y_{k,s,l} - M(1 - x_{k,s})$$
$$E^{trac}_{k,s} \le \sum_{l} e^{trac}_{k,s,l}\, y_{k,s,l} + M(1 - x_{k,s})$$
$$E^{trac}_{k,s} \ge 0, \qquad E^{trac}_{k,s} \le M \cdot x_{k,s}$$

### Exact Acceleration Energy (5a–5e)
$$E^{acc}_{k,s} \ge \sum_{l}\sum_{l'} e^{acc}_{k,l,l'}\, u_{k,s,l,l'} - M(1 - x_{k,s})$$
$$E^{acc}_{k,s} \le \sum_{l}\sum_{l'} e^{acc}_{k,l,l'}\, u_{k,s,l,l'} + M(1 - x_{k,s})$$
$$u_{k,s,l,l'} \ge y_{k,s,l} + y_{k,s',l'} - 1, \qquad u_{k,s,l,l'} \le y_{k,s,l}, \qquad u_{k,s,l,l'} \le y_{k,s',l'}$$
$$\sum_{l} y_{k,s,l} = x_{k,s}$$

### Aggregation & Continuity (6–8)
$$\sum_{s \in R_k} x_{k,s} \le |R_k|\,(1 - cancel_k)$$
$$t^{in}_{k,s'} = t^{out}_{k,s} \quad \forall (s,s') \in R_k, \qquad t^{in}_{k,s} \le t^{out}_{k,s}$$

### Entry Fixing, Arrival Bound, Delay (9–11)
$$t^{in}_{k,s_k^{first}} = t^{entry}_k, \qquad t^{out}_{k,s_k^{last}} \le T_{max}$$
$$delay_k \ge t^{out}_{k,s_k^{last}} - t^{sched}_{k,s_k^{last}}, \qquad delay_k \ge 0$$

### Rerouting (B)
$$r_{k,s} \le allow_{k,s} \cdot x_{k,s}, \qquad r_{k,s} \le x_{k,s}$$

### Disruption-Window Presence (C)
$$t^{out}_{k,s} \le T^{dis}_{start} + M(1 - A_{k,s})$$
$$t^{in}_{k,s} \ge T^{dis}_{end} - M(1 - B_{k,s})$$
$$A_{k,s} + B_{k,s} + z_{k,s} = 1, \qquad z_{k,s} \le x_{k,s}$$

### Rerouting Requirement (D)
$$r_{k,s} \ge z_{k,s} - (1 - disarea_s)$$

### Same-Track Indicator (E)
$$same\_track_{k,k',s} \ge 1 - (r_{k,s} - r_{k',s}) - (r_{k',s} - r_{k,s})$$
$$same\_track_{k,k',s} \le 1 - r_{k,s} + r_{k',s}, \qquad same\_track_{k,k',s} \le 1 + r_{k,s} - r_{k',s}$$

### Ordering (F)
$$o_{k,k',s} + o_{k',k,s} \ge same\_track_{k,k',s} + x_{k,s} + x_{k',s} - 2, \qquad o_{k,k',s} + o_{k',k,s} \le 1$$

### Headway (G)
$$t^{in}_{k',s} \ge t^{out}_{k,s} + h - M(1 - o_{k,k',s}) - M(1 - x_{k,s}) - M(1 - x_{k',s}) - M(1 - same\_track_{k,k',s})$$
$$t^{in}_{k,s} \ge t^{out}_{k',s} + h - M(1 - o_{k',k,s}) - M(1 - x_{k,s}) - M(1 - x_{k',s}) - M(1 - same\_track_{k,k',s})$$

### No-Overtaking in Disruption Area (H)
$$o_{k,k',s} \le o_{k,k',s'} + (1 - r_{k,s}) + (1 - r_{k',s}) + (1 - r_{k,s'}) + (1 - r_{k',s'})$$
$$o_{k',k,s} \le o_{k',k,s'} + (1 - r_{k,s}) + (1 - r_{k',s}) + (1 - r_{k,s'}) + (1 - r_{k',s'})$$

### Cancellation (I)
$$x_{k,s} \le 1 - cancel_k$$

### Domain (K)
$$t^{in}_{k,s}, t^{out}_{k,s} \in \{0,\dots,T_{max}\}$$
$$y_{k,s,l}, x_{k,s}, r_{k,s}, z_{k,s}, A_{k,s}, B_{k,s}, same\_track_{k,k',s}, o_{k,k',s}, cancel_k, u_{k,s,l,l'} \in \{0,1\}$$
$$E^{trac}_{k,s}, E^{acc}_{k,s}, delay_k \ge 0$$

---

## Assumptions
- **A1:** $R_k$ is an ordered segment list; first/last segments well-defined.
- **A2:** Disruption segments belong to routes of affected trains.
- **A3:** $\delta_{pos}(l,l')$ precomputed (train-independent; else index by $k$).
- **A4:** Big-M relaxes constraints when $x_{k,s}=0$.
- **A5:** Acceleration energy uses only the positive part via $e^{acc}_{k,l,l'}$.
- **A6:** $M$ chosen large enough (e.g., $M = T_{max} + \max h$).
- **A7:** Speed levels $L$ are finite and discrete.
- **A8:** Headway $h$ uniform across segments and train pairs.
- **A9:** Cancellation removes the train from all segments (no partial cancellation).
- **A10:** Disruption window $[T^{dis}_{start}, T^{dis}_{end}]$ is fixed and known.

---

## Model Structure
- **Exactness block:** (3a–3b), (4a–4d), (5a–5e)
- **Temporal block:** (6)–(11)
- **Disruption block:** (B), (C), (D)
- **Conflict block:** (E), (F), (G), (H)
- **Cancellation block:** (I)
- **Objective:** (J) — **Domain:** (K)

This is the definitive final MILP, jointly optimizing **retiming, reordering, rerouting, and speed management** while resolving bidirectional conflicts on shared track and minimizing weighted delay, energy, and cancellations.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a partial segment blockage (e.g., one track of a double-track line blocked by equipment failure) occurs during a disruption time window. Trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track within the affected area, requiring conflict-free bidirectional coordination. The model simultaneously decides train arrival/departure times, train ordering, routing, and speed profiles.

**Assumptions (marked as such):**

- **(A1)** The line is discretized into segments between consecutive stations; each segment $s$ has a length $L_s$ (km) and a maximum allowable speed $V_s^{\max}$.
- **(A2)** Speed profiles are represented by piecewise-constant acceleration/deceleration phases approximated on a discrete time grid with step $\Delta t$ (s). This is a standard linearization assumption.
- **(A3)** Train dynamics are linearized: acceleration $a$ and deceleration $b$ are bounded constants; tractive/braking forces are approximated as linear in speed for energy computation.
- **(A4)** Each train $k$ has a scheduled (planned) timetable; deviations are penalized.
- **(A5)** The disruption window $[T^{\text{dis}}_s, T^{\text{dis}}_s + D_s]$ blocks one direction on segment $s$; trains may reroute to the opposite track during this window.
- **(A6)** Dwell times at stations are bounded: $d_k^{\min} \le d_{k,i} \le d_k^{\max}$.
- **(A7)** Headway constraints apply between consecutive trains on the same track in the same direction.
- **(A8)** Cancellation is allowed with a penalty cost (assumption: cancellations are permitted but discouraged).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{N}$ | Set of stations/nodes, indexed by $i$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of directions, $\mathcal{D} = \{+1, -1\}$ (up/down) |
| $\mathcal{R}_s$ | Set of available tracks on segment $s$ (1 or 2) |
| $\mathcal{K}_s^{\text{dis}}$ | Set of trains affected by disruption on segment $s$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetable Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{k,i}$ | Continuous | Arrival time of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $d_{k,i}$ | Continuous | Departure time of train $k$ from station $i$ |
| $x_{k,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $k$ is assigned to segment $s$ (not cancelled) |
| $y_{k,s,r}$ | Binary | 1 if train $k$ uses track $r \in \mathcal{R}_s$ on segment $s$ |
| $z_{k,k',s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $k$ precedes train $k'$ on segment $s$ |
| $c_k$ | Binary | 1 if train $k$ is cancelled |

### 3.2 Speed Profile Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $v_{k,s,t}$ | Continuous | Speed of train $k$ on segment $s$ at time step $t$ (km/h) |
| $u_{k,s,t}$ | Continuous | Control input (acceleration) of train $k$ on segment $s$ at time step $t$ |
| $p_{k,s,t}$ | Continuous | Position of train $k$ on segment $s$ at time step $t$ (km) |
| $\delta_{k,s,t}^{+}$ | Continuous | Positive acceleration indicator (auxiliary) |
| $\delta_{k,s,t}^{-}$ | Continuous | Deceleration indicator (auxiliary) |

### 3.3 Rerouting Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\rho_{k,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $k$ reroutes on segment $s$ during disruption |
| $\tau_{k,s}^{\text{enter}}$ | Continuous | Time train $k$ enters disruption zone on segment $s$ |
| $\tau_{k,s}^{\text{exit}}$ | Continuous | Time train $k$ exits disruption zone on segment $s$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, cancellation penalty, and rerouting cost:

$$
\min Z = w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}} \left( \max(0, a_{k,i} - A_{k,i}^{\text{sch}}) + \max(0, d_{k,i} - D_{k,i}^{\text{sch}}) \right)}_{\text{total delay}}
+ w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} E_{k,s,t}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
+ w_3 \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} c_k}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
+ w_4 \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \rho_{k,s}}_{\text{rerouting cost}}
$$

where $A_{k,i}^{\text{sch}}$ and $D_{k,i}^{\text{sch}}$ are scheduled arrival and departure times, and $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4 > 0$ are weighting parameters.

**Linearization of delay:** Introduce auxiliary variables $\alpha_{k,i} \ge 0$, $\beta_{k,i} \ge 0$ with:
$$
\alpha_{k,i} \ge a_{k,i} - A_{k,i}^{\text{sch}}, \quad \alpha_{k,i} \ge 0
$$
$$
\beta_{k,i} \ge d_{k,i} - D_{k,i}^{\text{sch}}, \quad \beta_{k,i} \ge 0
$$

Then the delay term becomes $\sum_{k,i} (\alpha_{k,i} + \beta_{k,i})$.

**Energy consumption (linearized):** Assuming tractive energy is proportional to acceleration and speed:
$$
E_{k,s,t} = \eta \cdot u_{k,s,t} \cdot v_{k,s,t} \cdot \Delta t
$$
where $\eta$ is a constant efficiency factor. This bilinear term is linearized via McCormick envelopes (see Section 6).

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Constraints

**(C1) Arrival–Departure Linking:**
$$
d_{k,i} \ge a_{k,i} + d_k^{\min} \cdot x_{k,s} - M(1 - x_{k,s}), \quad \forall k, i
$$
$$
d_{k,i} \le a_{k,i} + d_k^{\max} \cdot x_{k,s} + M(1 - x_{k,s}), \quad \forall k, i
$$

**(C2) Segment Running Time:**
$$
a_{k,i+1} \ge d_{k,i} + T_{k,s}^{\min} \cdot x_{k,s} - M(1 - x_{k,s}), \quad \forall k, s = (i, i+1)
$$
$$
a_{k,i+1} \le d_{k,i} + T_{k,s}^{\max} \cdot x_{k,s} + M(1 - x_{k,s}), \quad \forall k, s = (i, i+1)
$$

where $T_{k,s}^{\min}$ and $T_{k,s}^{\max}$ are minimum and maximum feasible running times derived from speed profile feasibility.

**(C3) Cancellation Linking:**
$$
x_{k,s} + c_k \le 1, \quad \forall k, s
$$
$$
x_{k,s} \ge 1 - c_k, \quad \forall k, s
$$

**(C4) Time Window Constraints:**
$$
a_{k,i} \ge T_i^{\text{earliest}}, \quad d_{k,i} \le T_i^{\text{latest}}, \quad \forall k, i
$$

### 5.2 Conflict-Free and Headway Constraints

**(C5) Headway between consecutive trains on same track:**
$$
d_{k',i} \ge d_{k,i} + h^{\min} - M(1 - z_{k,k',s}), \quad \forall k, k', s = (i, i+1), r
$$
$$
d_{k,i} \ge d_{k',i} + h^{\min} - M \cdot z_{k,k',s}, \quad \forall k, k', s = (i, i+1), r
$$

**(C6) Ordering consistency:**
$$
z_{k,k',s} + z_{k',k,s} = 1, \quad \forall k \neq k', s
$$

**(C7) Track assignment uniqueness:**
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_s} y_{k,s,r} = x_{k,s}, \quad \forall k, s
$$

**(C8) Conflict-free on shared track (bidirectional):**
$$
d_{k',i} \ge d_{k,i} + h^{\min} - M(1 - z_{k,k',s}) - M(1 - y_{k,s,r}) - M(1 - y_{k',s,r}), \quad \forall k, k', s, r
$$

### 5.3 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

**(C9) Disruption zone entry/exit:**
$$
\tau_{k,s}^{\text{enter}} \ge T_s^{\text{dis}} - M(1 - \rho_{k,s}), \quad \forall k, s
$$
$$
\tau_{k,s}^{\text{exit}} \le T_s^{\text{dis}} + D_s + M(1 - \rho_{k,s}), \quad \forall k, s
$$

**(C10) Rerouting only during disruption:**
$$
\rho_{k,s} \le 1 - y_{k,s,r^{\text{blocked}}}, \quad \forall k, s
$$

**(C11) Rerouting feasibility (opposite track available):**
$$
\rho_{k,s} \le \sum_{r \neq r^{\text{blocked}}} y_{k,s,r}, \quad \forall k, s
$$

**(C12) No simultaneous bidirectional use of same track during disruption:**
$$
|\tau_{k,s}^{\text{enter}} - \tau_{k',s}^{\text{enter}}| \ge h^{\min} - M(1 - \rho_{k,s}) - M(1 - \rho_{k',s}), \quad \forall k \neq k', s
$$

### 5.4 Speed Profile Constraints

**(C13) Speed dynamics (discrete-time approximation):**
$$
v_{k,s,t+1} = v_{k,s,t} + u_{k,s,t} \cdot \Delta t, \quad \forall k, s, t
$$

**(C14) Position dynamics:**
$$
p_{k,s,t+1} = p_{k,s,t} + v_{k,s,t} \cdot \Delta t + \frac{1}{2} u_{k,s,t} \cdot \Delta t^2, \quad \forall k, s, t
$$

**(C15) Speed bounds:**
$$
0 \le v_{k,s,t} \le V_s^{\max}, \quad \forall k, s, t
$$

**(C16) Acceleration bounds:**
$$
a_k^{\min} \le u_{k,s,t} \le a_k^{\max}, \quad \forall k, s, t
$$

**(C17) Segment boundary conditions:**
$$
p_{k,s,0} = 0, \quad p_{k,s,T_s^{\text{end}}} = L_s, \quad \forall k, s
$$

**(C18) Speed consistency at segment boundaries:**
$$
v_{k,s,T_s^{\text{end}}} = v_{k,s+1,0}, \quad \forall k, s
$$

**(C19) Timetable–speed profile consistency:**
$$
a_{k,i} = t \cdot \Delta t \quad \text{when} \quad p_{k,s,t} = L_s, \quad \forall k, s = (i-1, i)
$$
$$
d_{k,i} = t \cdot \Delta t \quad \text{when} \quad p_{k,s,t} = 0, \quad \forall k, s = (i, i+1)
$$

This is enforced via:
$$
a_{k,i} \ge t \cdot \Delta t - M(1 - \mathbb{I}[p_{k,s,t} = L_s]), \quad \forall k, s = (i-1, i), t
$$

**(C20) Energy linearization (McCormick envelope):**
$$
E_{k,s,t} \ge \eta \cdot \Delta t \cdot (u_{k,s,t}^{\min} v_{k,s,t} + v_{k,s,t}^{\min} u_{k,s,t} - u_{k,s,t}^{\min} v_{k,s,t}^{\min})
$$
$$
E_{k,s,t} \ge \eta \cdot \Delta t \cdot (u_{k,s,t}^{\max} v_{k,s,t} + v_{k,s,t}^{\max} u_{k,s,t} - u_{k,s,t}^{\max} v_{k,s,t}^{\max})
$$
$$
E_{k,s,t} \le \eta \cdot \Delta t \cdot (u_{k,s,t}^{\max} v_{k,s,t} + v_{k,s,t}^{\min} u_{k,s,t} - u_{k,s,t}^{\max} v_{k,s,t}^{\min})
$$
$$
E_{k,s,t} \le \eta \cdot \Delta t \cdot (u_{k,s,t}^{\min} v_{k,s,t} + v_{k,s,t}^{\max} u_{k,s,t} - u_{k,s,t}^{\min} v_{k,s,t}^{\max})
$$

### 5.5 Binary and Non-negativity Constraints

$$
x_{k,s}, y_{k,s,r}, z_{k,k',s}, c_k, \rho_{k,s} \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall k, k', s, r
$$
$$
a_{k,i}, d_{k,i}, v_{k,s,t}, u_{k,s,t}, p_{k,s,t}, E_{k,s,t}, \tau_{k,s}^{\text{enter}}, \tau_{k,s}^{\text{exit}} \ge 0, \quad \forall k, i, s, t
$$

---

## 6. Linearization Details

**Bilinear energy term:** The product $u_{k,s,t} \cdot v_{k,s,t}$ is linearized using McCormick envelopes (constraints C20), where $u^{\min}, u^{\max}, v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ are bounds on acceleration and speed.

**Position–time consistency (C19):** The indicator $\mathbb{I}[p_{k,s,t} = L_s]$ is handled by introducing binary variable $\mu_{k,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$ with:
$$
p_{k,s,t} \ge L_s - M(1 - \mu_{k,s,t}), \quad p_{k,s,t} \le L_s + M(1 - \mu_{k,s,t})
$$
$$
a_{k,i} \ge t \cdot \Delta t - M(1 - \mu_{k,s,t}), \quad a_{k,i} \le t \cdot \Delta t + M(1 - \mu_{k,s,t})
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\min Z = w_1 \sum_{k,i} (\alpha_{k,i} + \beta_{k,i}) + w_2 \sum_{k,s,t} E_{k,s,t} + w_3 \sum_k c_k + w_4 \sum_{k,s} \rho_{k,s}
$$

subject to constraints (C1)–(C20) and binary/non-negativity conditions.

**Model size:** For $|\mathcal{K}|$ trains, $|\mathcal{S}|$ segments, $|\mathcal{T}|$ time steps:
- Binary variables: $O(|\mathcal{K}|^2 |\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{K}||\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{R}|)$
- Continuous variables: $O(|\mathcal{K}||\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{T}|)$
- Constraints: $O(|\mathcal{K}|^2 |\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{K}||\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{T}|)$

---

## 8. Key Modeling Assumptions (Restated)

1. **(A1)** Discrete segment representation with constant max speed per segment.
2. **(A2)** Piecewise-constant acceleration on discrete time grid.
3. **(A3)** Linearized train dynamics and energy consumption.
4. **(A4)** Scheduled timetable deviations penalized linearly.
5. **(A5)** Disruption window blocks one direction; rerouting to opposite track permitted.
6. **(A6)** Bounded dwell times.
7. **(A7)** Headway constraints on same track/direction.
8. **(A8)** Cancellation allowed with penalty.

This MILP provides a complete, conflict-free, energy-efficient rescheduling and speed management solution for high-speed railway operations under partial segment blockages, integrating timetable, routing, ordering, and speed profile decisions in a single optimization framework.
