Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Best MILP Model

Below is the complete, linear MILP formulation for the TRSMP under partial segment blockage disruptions, integrating train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management.

---

## 1. Assumptions

| # | Assumption |
|---|------------|
| A1 | The line is a double-track railway; segments $e=(s,s+1)$ connect consecutive stations. Under normal operation each direction uses its own track; under disruption, trains may reroute onto the opposite track (bidirectional single-track operation). |
| A2 | Crossovers exist only at stations $S^{\text{cross}} \subseteq S$; rerouting is allowed only if both segment endpoints are crossover stations. |
| A3 | A single segment $e^\ast$ is partially blocked during window $[t^{\text{start}}, t^{\text{end}}]$; the affected track has reduced capacity while the opposite track is used bidirectionally. |
| A4 | Speed profiles are discretized into finite levels $V_e$; running time and energy are piecewise-linear in the selected level (convex-combination / SOS2 linearization). |
| A5 | All event times lie in $[0,T^{\max}]$; cancelled trains are removed from timing/headway constraints via big-M. |
| A6 | Regenerative braking credit linearly reduces net traction energy. |
| A7 | Headway is enforced at segment entry/exit (entry-based separation is sufficient for single-track segments). |
| A8 | Cancellation penalty dominates delay cost, so cancellation is a last resort. |

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S=\{1,\dots,N\}$ | Ordered stations |
| $E\subseteq S\times S$ | Segments, $e=(s,s+1)$ |
| $T$ | Trains |
| $D=\{u,d\}$ | Directions (up/down) |
| $V_e$ | Discrete speed levels on segment $e$ |
| $S^{\text{cross}}\subseteq S$ | Crossover stations |
| $T^{\text{aff}}\subseteq T$ | Trains affected by the disruption |
| $T^{\text{cancel-cand}}\subseteq T$ | Trains eligible for cancellation |
| $e^\ast$ | Disrupted segment |

For each train $i$: $S_i\subseteq S$ ordered stations, $E_i\subseteq E$ traversed segments, $d_i\in D$ direction.

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $a_i^{0}(s),\,d_i^{0}(s)$ | Scheduled arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_i^{\min}(e),\,r_i^{\max}(e)$ | Min/max running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $\tau_i^{\min}(s),\,\tau_i^{\max}(s)$ | Min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{\text{same}},\,h^{\text{opp}}$ | Minimum headway, same/opposite direction |
| $t^{\text{start}},\,t^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window |
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ |
| $v_e^{\max}$ | Normal speed limit on segment $e$ |
| $v_e^{\text{dis}}$ | Temporary speed limit on disrupted segment |
| $a^{\max},\,b^{\max}$ | Max acceleration/deceleration |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $w^{\text{delay}},\,w^{\text{cancel}},\,w^{\text{energy}}$ | Objective weights |
| $c_k(e),\,c_k^{\text{reg}}(e)$ | Traction / regenerative energy rate at speed level $v_k$ on $e$ |
| $\eta$ | Regenerative recovery factor |
| $T^{\max}$ | Time horizon |

Speed–running-time linearization: nominal running time $r_k(e)=L_e/v_k$; energy per traversal $c_k(e)\cdot L_e/v_k$.

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Timing / scheduling
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_i(s)$ | $\ge 0$ cont. | Adjusted arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_i(s)$ | $\ge 0$ cont. | Adjusted departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_i$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\delta_i$ | $\ge 0$ cont. | Delay of train $i$ |

### 4.2 Reordering
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $y_{ij}(e)$ | binary | 1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on segment $e$ (same direction) |
| $z_{ij}(e)$ | binary | 1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on segment $e$ (opposite directions, shared track) |

### 4.3 Rerouting
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\rho_i(e)$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ reroutes onto opposite track on segment $e$ |
| $\sigma_i$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ reroutes at all |

### 4.4 Speed profile
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\lambda_{i,k}(e)$ | $\in[0,1]$ cont. | Convex-combination weight for speed level $k$ |
| $u_{i,k}(e)$ | binary | 1 if speed level $k$ selected |
| $r_i(e)$ | cont. | Actual running time on segment $e$ |
| $E_i^{\text{trac}}(e),\,E_i^{\text{reg}}(e)$ | cont. | Traction / regenerative energy |

### 4.5 Segment occupancy
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $o_i(e)$ | cont. | Entry time into segment $e$ |
| $f_i(e)$ | cont. | Exit time from segment $e$ |
| $\theta_i(e)$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses $e$ during disruption window |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in T} \delta_i \;+\; w^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in T} x_i \;+\; w^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{e \in E_i} \bigl( E_i^{\text{trac}}(e) - \eta \, E_i^{\text{reg}}(e) \bigr)
$$

**Delay definition (linearized max):**
$$
\delta_i \;\ge\; a_i(s) - a_i^{0}(s), \quad \delta_i \;\ge\; d_i(s) - d_i^{0}(s), \quad \delta_i \;\ge\; 0 \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S_i
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Cancellation coupling
$$
a_i(s) \le M(1 - x_i), \qquad d_i(s) \le M(1 - x_i), \qquad \forall s \in S_i
$$
$$
x_i = 0, \qquad \forall i \notin T^{\text{cancel-cand}}
$$

### 6.2 Connectivity, running time, dwell
$$
d_i(s) \ge a_i(s) + \tau_i^{\min}(s) - M x_i, \qquad d_i(s) \le a_i(s) + \tau_i^{\max}(s) + M x_i
$$
$$
a_i(s+1) \ge d_i(s) + r_i(e) - M x_i, \qquad a_i(s+1) \le d_i(s) + r_i(e) + M x_i
$$
$$
r_i^{\min}(e) \le r_i(e) \le r_i^{\max}(e), \qquad 0 \le a_i(s),\, d_i(s) \le T^{\max}
$$

### 6.3 Speed profile linearization
$$
\sum_{k \in V_e} \lambda_{i,k}(e) = 1 - x_i, \qquad \sum_{k \in V_e} u_{i,k}(e) = 1 - x_i, \qquad \lambda_{i,k}(e) \le u_{i,k}(e)
$$
$$
r_i(e) = \sum_{k \in V_e} \lambda_{i,k}(e) \cdot \frac{L_e}{v_k}
$$
$$
E_i^{\text{trac}}(e) = \sum_{k \in V_e} \lambda_{i,k}(e) \cdot c_k(e) \cdot \frac{L_e}{v_k}, \qquad
E_i^{\text{reg}}(e) = \sum_{k \in V_e} \lambda_{i,k}(e) \cdot c_k^{\text{reg}}(e) \cdot \frac{L_e}{v_k}
$$
$$
v_k \le v_e^{\max}, \qquad v_k \cdot u_{i,k}(e^\ast) \le v_{e^\ast}^{\text{dis}} + M\bigl(1 - \theta_i(e^\ast) + \rho_i(e^\ast)\bigr)
$$

### 6.4 Disruption window occupancy
$$
o_i(e) = d_i(s), \qquad f_i(e) = a_i(s+1), \qquad \forall e=(s,s+1)
$$
$$
\theta_i(e^\ast) \ge \frac{o_i(e^\ast) - t^{\text{end}}}{M}, \qquad \theta_i(e^\ast) \ge \frac{t^{\text{start}} - f_i(e^\ast)}{M}
$$
$$
\theta_i(e^\ast) \le 1 + \frac{o_i(e^\ast) - t^{\text{start}}}{M}, \qquad \theta_i(e^\ast) \le 1 + \frac{t^{\text{end}} - f_i(e^\ast)}{M}
$$
$$
o_i(e^\ast) \ge t^{\text{end}} - M\bigl(1 - \theta_i(e^\ast) + \rho_i(e^\ast)\bigr)
$$
$$
f_i(e^\ast) \le t^{\text{start}} + M\bigl(1 - \theta_i(e^\ast) + \rho_i(e^\ast)\bigr)
$$

### 6.5 Rerouting feasibility
$$
\rho_i(e) = 0, \qquad \forall e=(s,s+1) \text{ with } s \notin S^{\text{cross}} \text{ or } s+1 \notin S^{\text{cross}}
$$
$$
\rho_i(e) = 0, \qquad \forall e \neq e^\ast
$$
$$
\sigma_i \ge \rho_i(e^\ast), \qquad \sigma_i \le \sum_{e} \rho_i(e)
$$

### 6.6 Headway and safety separation
**Same direction** ($d_i=d_j$):
$$
o_j(e) \ge f_i(e) + h^{\text{same}} - M\bigl(1 - y_{ij}(e)\bigr) - M(x_i + x_j)
$$
$$
o_i(e) \ge f_j(e) + h^{\text{same}} - M\, y_{ij}(e) - M(x_i + x_j)
$$
$$
y_{ij}(e) + y_{ji}(e) \ge 1 - x_i - x_j, \qquad y_{ij}(e) + y_{ji}(e) \le 1
$$

**Opposite direction** (shared track when rerouted):
$$
o_j(e) \ge f_i(e) + h^{\text{opp}} - M\bigl(1 - z_{ij}(e)\bigr) - M(x_i + x_j)
$$
$$
o_i(e) \ge f_j(e) + h^{\text{opp}} - M\, z_{ij}(e) - M(x_i + x_j)
$$
$$
z_{ij}(e) + z_{ji}(e) \ge \rho_i(e) + \rho_j(e) - 1, \qquad z_{ij}(e) + z_{ji}(e) \le 1
$$

**Segment occupancy (single-track / disrupted):**
$$
o_j(e) \ge f_i(e) - M\bigl(1 - y_{ij}(e)\bigr) - M\bigl(1 - z_{ij}(e)\bigr) - M(x_i + x_j)
$$

### 6.7 Precedence consistency
$$
y_{ij}(e) - y_{ij}(e') \le M \cdot \mathbb{1}[\text{stop at intermediate station}]
$$

### 6.8 Variable domains
$$
a_i(s),\,d_i(s),\,\delta_i,\,r_i(e),\,E_i^{\text{trac}}(e),\,E_i^{\text{reg}}(e),\,o_i(e),\,f_i(e) \ge 0
$$
$$
x_i,\,\rho_i(e),\,\sigma_i,\,y_{ij}(e),\,z_{ij}(e),\,u_{i,k}(e),\,\theta_i(e) \in \{0,1\}, \qquad \lambda_{i,k}(e) \in [0,1]
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & w^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i} \delta_i + w^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i} x_i + w^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,e} \bigl(E_i^{\text{trac}}(e) - \eta E_i^{\text{reg}}(e)\bigr) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(6.1) Cancellation coupling} \\
& \text{(6.2) Connectivity, running time, dwell} \\
& \text{(6.3) Speed profile linearization, speed limits} \\
& \text{(6.4) Disruption window occupancy} \\
& \text{(6.5) Rerouting feasibility} \\
& \text{(6.6) Headway and safety separation} \\
& \text{(6.7) Precedence consistency} \\
& \text{(6.8) Variable domains}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

**Key modeling elements:** retiming ($a_i,d_i$), reordering ($y_{ij},z_{ij}$), rerouting ($\rho_i,\sigma_i$), cancellation ($x_i$), speed profile convex combination ($\lambda,u$), disruption-window indicator ($\theta_i$), and headway on shared track ($h^{\text{same}},h^{\text{opp}}$). All nonlinearities (speed–time, energy, disjunctions, window overlap) are linearized via SOS2/convex combination and big-M, yielding a complete MILP solvable by CPLEX/Gurobi/SCIP.

Text:
# A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

*Model built on the RECIFE-MILP framework (Pellegrini et al., 2015), enhanced with speed profile options and train-/speed-dependent braking distances as described in the introduction. Assumptions made where the input is incomplete are explicitly marked **[A#]**.*

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of track sections (blocks / TDSs), indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of routes (paths) through the network, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_t \subseteq \mathcal{R}$ | Set of feasible routes for train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{S}_r \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Ordered sequence of sections belonging to route $r$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of capacity-constrained resources (track segments, station platforms, switch zones), indexed by $b$ |
| $\mathcal{B}_r \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | Ordered resources traversed by route $r$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discrete speed profile options, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_t \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ | Speed profile options available to train $t$ **[A1]** |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of scheduled events (arrivals/departures), indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{E}_t$ | Events of train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_b$ | Set of ordered pairs $(t, t')$ of trains that can use resource $b$ in conflicting order, $t \neq t'$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $a_e$ | Scheduled time of event $e$ |
| $\underline{a}_e$ | Earliest feasible time of event $e$ (release / minimum running time) |
| $\overline{a}_e$ | Latest feasible time of event $e$ (planning horizon) |
| $d_e$ | Minimum dwell time associated with event $e$ (0 if not a stop) |
| $\tau_{t,r,s}^{\text{run},k}$ | Pure running time of train $t$ on section $s \in \mathcal{S}_r$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $\tau_{t,b}^{\text{occ},k}$ | Minimum occupation time of resource $b$ by train $t$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $\delta_{t,b}^{\text{setup}}$ | Setup/release time on resource $b$ for train $t$ (e.g., switch resetting) |
| $L_t$ | Length of train $t$ |
| $v_{t,s}^{k}$ | Average speed of train $t$ on section $s$ under profile $k$ |
| $b_{t,s}^{k}$ | Braking distance of train $t$ on section $s$ under profile $k$ (from braking-curve supervision) |
| $m^{\text{safe}}$ | Safety margin behind the rear of the preceding train |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $c_e^{\text{delay}}$ | Cost coefficient (weight) of delay at event $e$ **[A2]** |
| $c_{t,r}^{\text{route}}$ | Cost of selecting route $r$ for train $t$ (0 if all routes equivalent) **[A3]** |

**Assumption [A1]:** Speed profile options are discretised (e.g., *fast*, *medium*, *slow*), consistent with the paper's "speed profile options" enhancement.
**Assumption [A2]:** Delay costs are linear per unit of delay; alternative objectives (e.g., max delay) can be substituted.
**Assumption [A3]:** Route selection costs are zero unless local rerouting is penalised.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timing variables
- $a_e \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ — actual (rescheduled) time of event $e$.

### 3.2 Delay variables
- $\Delta_e \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ — delay of event $e$ relative to schedule.

### 3.3 Ordering variables (conflict resolution)
For each resource $b$ and each conflicting pair $(t,t') \in \mathcal{P}_b$:
- $y_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ uses resource $b$ **before** train $t'$.

### 3.4 Route selection variables
- $x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in \mathcal{R}_t$.

### 3.5 Speed profile variables
- $z_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $k \in \mathcal{K}_t$.

### 3.6 Headway / separation variables (DTG-specific)
For each resource $b$ and pair $(t,t') \in \mathcal{P}_b$:
- $h_{t,t',b} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ — minimum time headway between train $t$ and train $t'$ at resource $b$, **speed-dependent**.

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total weighted delay (with optional route cost):

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} c_e^{\text{delay}} \,\Delta_e \;+\; \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t} c_{t,r}^{\text{route}} \, x_{t,r}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay definition
$$
\Delta_e \;\ge\; a_e - a_e^{\text{sched}}, \qquad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}
\tag{1}
$$
$$
\Delta_e \;\ge\; 0, \qquad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}
\tag{2}
$$

### 5.2 Time window / release constraints
$$
\underline{a}_e \;\le\; a_e \;\le\; \overline{a}_e, \qquad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}
\tag{3}
$$

### 5.3 Running time constraints (speed-profile dependent)
For each train $t$, route $r \in \mathcal{R}_t$, and consecutive events $e, e' \in \mathcal{E}_t$ linked by section $s \in \mathcal{S}_r$:
$$
a_{e'} - a_e \;\ge\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} \tau_{t,r,s}^{\text{run},k} \, z_{t,k} \;-\; M\,(1 - x_{t,r}), \qquad \forall (e,e') \in \mathcal{E}_t^{\text{run}}
\tag{4}
$$

### 5.4 Dwell time constraints
For each event $e \in \mathcal{E}_t$ corresponding to a stop:
$$
a_{e'} - a_e \;\ge\; d_e, \qquad \forall (e,e') \in \mathcal{E}_t^{\text{dwell}}
\tag{5}
$$

### 5.5 Route selection
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t} x_{t,r} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{6}
$$

### 5.6 Speed profile selection
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} z_{t,k} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{7}
$$

### 5.7 Resource occupation time (speed-dependent)
For each train $t$, resource $b \in \mathcal{B}_r$, and profile $k$:
$$
\tau_{t,b}^{\text{occ},k} \;=\; \frac{L_t + b_{t,b}^{k} + m^{\text{safe}}}{v_{t,b}^{k}} \;+\; \delta_{t,b}^{\text{setup}}
\tag{8}
$$
*(This is the DTG-specific expression: the occupation time depends on the braking distance $b_{t,b}^{k}$, which is itself speed-dependent.)*

### 5.8 Separation / headway constraints (DTG core)
For each resource $b$ and each ordered pair $(t,t') \in \mathcal{P}_b$:

**If $t$ precedes $t'$ ($y_{t,t',b}=1$):**
$$
a_{t',b}^{\text{in}} \;\ge\; a_{t,b}^{\text{out}} \;+\; h_{t,t',b} \;-\; M\,(1 - y_{t,t',b})
\tag{9}
$$

**If $t'$ precedes $t$ ($y_{t,t',b}=0$):**
$$
a_{t,b}^{\text{in}} \;\ge\; a_{t',b}^{\text{out}} \;+\; h_{t',t,b} \;-\; M\,y_{t,t',b}
\tag{10}
$$

where the **speed-dependent headway** is:
$$
h_{t,t',b} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} \sum_{k' \in \mathcal{K}_{t'}} \left( \frac{L_{t'} + b_{t',b}^{k'} + m^{\text{safe}}}{v_{t,b}^{k}} \right) z_{t,k} \, z_{t',k'}
\tag{11}
$$

**Linearisation of (11)** (product of binaries $z_{t,k} z_{t',k'}$ replaced by $w_{t,t',k,k'} \in \{0,1\}$):
$$
w_{t,t',k,k'} \;\le\; z_{t,k}, \quad w_{t,t',k,k'} \;\le\; z_{t',k'}, \quad w_{t,t',k,k'} \;\ge\; z_{t,k} + z_{t',k'} - 1
\tag{12}
$$
$$
h_{t,t',b} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} \sum_{k' \in \mathcal{K}_{t'}} \frac{L_{t'} + b_{t',b}^{k'} + m^{\text{safe}}}{v_{t,b}^{k}} \, w_{t,t',k,k'}
\tag{13}
$$

### 5.9 Mutual exclusion of ordering
$$
y_{t,t',b} + y_{t',t,b} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall b \in \mathcal{B}, \; (t,t') \in \mathcal{P}_b
\tag{14}
$$

### 5.10 Braking-distance / braking-curve constraint (DTG enhancement)
The braking distance of train $t'$ at resource $b$ under profile $k'$ must be respected relative to the end of authority:
$$
b_{t',b}^{k'} \;\ge\; \frac{(v_{t',b}^{k'})^2}{2 \, a_{t'}^{\text{brake}}}
\tag{15}
$$
where $a_{t'}^{\text{brake}}$ is the guaranteed deceleration of train $t'$ **[A4]**.

**Assumption [A4]:** Braking distance is approximated by the kinematic formula $v^2/(2a)$; a piecewise-linear or tabulated braking curve can replace (15) if data is available.

### 5.11 Switch vs. non-switch distinction
For resources $b \in \mathcal{B}^{\text{switch}} \subset \mathcal{B}$ (switches), an additional setup/reset time applies:
$$
\tau_{t,b}^{\text{occ},k} \;\ge\; \tau_{t,b}^{\text{occ},k,\text{base}} + \delta_{t,b}^{\text{switch}}, \qquad \forall b \in \mathcal{B}^{\text{switch}}
\tag{16}
$$
For $b \in \mathcal{B}^{\text{track}} = \mathcal{B} \setminus \mathcal{B}^{\text{switch}}$, $\delta_{t,b}^{\text{switch}} = 0$.

### 5.12 Variable domains
$$
a_e \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}, \quad \Delta_e \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}, \quad h_{t,t',b} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}
\tag{17}
$$
$$
x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad z_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}, \quad w_{t,t',k,k'} \in \{0,1\}
\tag{18}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Component | Description |
|---|---|
| **Objective** | Minimise weighted total train delay (+ optional route cost) |
| **Key DTG feature** | Speed-dependent headway $h_{t,t',b}$ via braking distance $b_{t,b}^{k}$ (Eq. 8, 11, 13, 15) |
| **Key enhancement 1** | Discrete speed profile options $z_{t,k}$ (Eq. 7, 4) |
| **Key enhancement 2** | Train- and speed-dependent braking distances (Eq. 15) |
| **Key enhancement 3** | Switch vs. non-switch distinction (Eq. 16) |
| **Conflict resolution** | Ordering variables $y_{t,t',b}$ + big-M disjunctions (Eq. 9–10, 14) |
| **Route choice** | Binary $x_{t,r}$ (Eq. 6) |
| **Linearisation** | McCormick-style $w_{t,t',k,k'}$ for products of binaries (Eq. 12) |

---

## 7. Assumptions Made (Summary)

- **[A1]** Speed profiles are discretised into a finite set $\mathcal{K}_t$.
- **[A2]** Delay costs are linear and additive; weights $c_e^{\text{delay}}$ are given.
- **[A3]** Route selection costs are zero unless rerouting is penalised.
- **[A4]** Braking distance follows the kinematic approximation $v^2/(2a)$; tabulated curves can substitute.
- **[A5]** The end of authority (EoA) is located at the end of a block/TDS (fixed-block ETCS L2 with TTD), not moving block.
- **[A6]** All trains are equipped with ETCS L2 and radio communication (GSM-R) is available.
- **[A7]** Setup times $\delta_{t,b}^{\text{setup}}$ for switches are deterministic and known.
- **[A8]** The planning horizon is finite and all events must occur within $[\underline{a}_e, \overline{a}_e]$.

---

This formulation captures the two central DTG enhancements described in the introduction — **speed profile options** and **train-/speed-dependent braking distances** — while preserving the MILP structure of RECIFE-MILP, and adds the switch/non-switch distinction as a third modelling refinement.

Text:
# A MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

## 1. Scope, Notation and Modelling Assumptions

### 1.1 Scope

We formulate a complete, linear (mixed-integer) model for the real-time railway traffic management problem under **fixed-block ETCS Level 2 with trackside train detection (TTD)** — i.e., DTG signalling in which the **end of authority (EoA) is fixed at a block/TDS boundary**, but the **brake indication point (IP) is speed-dependent and may lie anywhere along the track**. The model is a DTG-enhanced variant of the state-of-the-art RECIFE-MILP model (Pellegrini et al., 2015), following the enhancement approach of Versluis et al. (2024).

### 1.2 Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $B$ | set of block sections (TDSs) of the network, indexed by $b, h$ |
| $S \subseteq B$ | set of block sections containing a switch (or located inside a station area) — *assumption: switches are modelled separately because the EoA is always placed at a TDS boundary there, and route locking applies* |
| $R$ | set of routes (paths) through the network, indexed by $r$ |
| $R_i \subseteq R$ | set of feasible routes for train $i$ |
| $B_r \subseteq B$ | ordered set of block sections traversed by route $r$ |
| $V_i$ | set of speed profile options for train $i$ (discrete speed levels / running-time options) |
| $E$ | set of pairs of trains $(i,j)$ that can potentially conflict (share at least one block) |
| $D$ | set of discretised departure/arrival time instants (for linearisation of speed-dependent quantities) |

### 1.3 Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $t_i^{dep,0}$ | scheduled departure time of train $i$ from its origin | s |
| $t_i^{arr,0}$ | scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at its destination | s |
| $\tau_{i,b}^{run}(v)$ | running time of train $i$ on block $b$ under speed profile option $v$ | s |
| $d_{i,b}^{dwell}$ | dwell time of train $i$ at the station located at the end of block $b$ (0 if none) | s |
| $L_b$ | length of block section $b$ | m |
| $M$ | large constant (big-M) | s |
| $\Delta^{setup}$ | interlocking setup/release time for a route through a switch section | s |
| $\Delta^{clear}$ | time for a train to fully clear a block section | s |
| $\sigma$ | safety margin behind the rear of a preceding train | m |
| $v_{i,b}(v)$ | speed of train $i$ on block $b$ under profile option $v$ | m/s |
| $a_i^{brake}$ | guaranteed (worst-case) deceleration of train $i$ | m/s² |
| $t^{react}$ | driver/onboard reaction time before braking curve supervision | s |
| $x_b^{start}$ | position of the start of block $b$ along the line | m |
| $x_b^{end}$ | position of the end of block $b$ along the line | m |

**Speed-dependent braking distance (DTG core).** For train $i$ entering block $b$ at speed $v_{i,b}(v)$, the *absolute braking distance* to a standstill is

$$
d_{i,b}^{brake}(v) \;=\; \frac{v_{i,b}(v)^2}{2\,a_i^{brake}} \;+\; v_{i,b}(v)\cdot t^{react}.
\tag{1}
$$

Because $v_{i,b}(v)$ is chosen from a finite set $V_i$, the quantity $d_{i,b}^{brake}(v)$ is a **parameter** for each $(i,b,v)$ — this is the key linearisation that keeps the model linear. The brake indication point (IP) of train $i$ relative to the EoA at the end of block $b$ is therefore located at position

$$
x^{IP}_{i,b}(v) \;=\; x_b^{end} \;-\; d_{i,b}^{brake}(v) \;-\; \sigma .
\tag{2}
$$

Since $d^{brake}$ depends on $v$, the IP is **train- and speed-dependent**, whereas the EoA remains at the fixed block boundary $x_b^{end}$ (fixed-block ETCS L2 with TTD).

### 1.4 Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $t_{i,b}^{arr}$ | continuous ≥ 0 | arrival time of train $i$ at the end of block $b$ |
| $t_{i,b}^{dep}$ | continuous ≥ 0 | departure time of train $i$ from the end of block $b$ |
| $y_{i,r}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses route $r \in R_i$, 0 otherwise |
| $z_{i,v}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile option $v \in V_i$, 0 otherwise |
| $\delta_{i,b}$ | continuous ≥ 0 | delay of train $i$ on block $b$ (relative to schedule) |
| $\alpha_{i,j,b}$ | binary | ordering variable: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $b$, 0 otherwise |
| $\beta_{i,j,b}$ | binary | 1 if the IP of train $j$ on block $b$ is reached before train $i$ has cleared block $b$ (braking-curve conflict indicator) |
| $\gamma_{i,b}$ | binary | 1 if block $b$ is a switch section and train $i$ requires route locking on $b$ |

### 1.5 Assumptions (marked)

1. **(A1)** The network is discretised into block sections/TDSs; the EoA of every train is always at a block boundary (fixed-block ETCS L2 with TTD). *Reasonable given the paper's focus.*
2. **(A2)** Speed profiles are discretised into a finite set $V_i$ of feasible (speed, running-time) options per train, as in Versluis et al. (2024). This preserves linearity.
3. **(A3)** Braking is modelled with a constant worst-case deceleration $a_i^{brake}$ and a fixed reaction time $t^{react}$; the resulting braking distance (1) is precomputed per $(i,b,v)$.
4. **(A4)** Switch sections $S$ are modelled separately: they require exclusive route locking and a setup/release time $\Delta^{setup}$; on non-switch blocks only the standard headway constraint applies.
5. **(A5)** Trains cannot overtake within a block section (no meeting/passing inside a TDS); reordering is only possible at block boundaries (stations/switches). *Standard RECIFE-MILP assumption.*
6. **(A6)** Dwell times are fixed per train and station; only running times vary with the speed profile option.
7. **(A7)** The objective is total (weighted) delay minimisation, consistent with RECIFE-MILP.

---

## 2. Objective Function

Minimise the total weighted delay of all trains at their final destination:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{i \in T} w_i \cdot \delta_{i,b^{last}(i)}
\tag{3}
$$

where $w_i$ is a priority weight for train $i$ (e.g., 1 for freight, higher for high-speed passenger trains — *assumption A7*), and $b^{last}(i)$ is the last block of the route chosen by train $i$. Equivalently, delay can be accumulated block-by-block:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{b \in B} w_i \cdot \delta_{i,b} .
\tag{3'}
$$

---

## 3. Constraints

### 3.1 Route and Speed Profile Selection

Each train selects exactly one route and one speed profile:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} y_{i,r} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,
\tag{4}
$$

$$
\sum_{v \in V_i} z_{i,v} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T.
\tag{5}
$$

Route–block consistency (train $i$ can only use blocks belonging to its chosen route):

$$
y_{i,r} \le \sum_{v \in V_i} z_{i,v} \quad \text{and} \quad
\sum_{r \in R_i : b \in B_r} y_{i,r} \;\ge\; \text{(block usage indicator)} \qquad \forall i, b.
\tag{6}
$$

### 3.2 Running Time and Speed-Dependent Braking Distance

The running time of train $i$ on block $b$ is the weighted sum over the selected speed profile:

$$
\tau_{i,b}^{run} \;=\; \sum_{v \in V_i} \tau_{i,b}^{run}(v)\, z_{i,v} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B.
\tag{7}
$$

Likewise, the speed-dependent braking distance and IP position are

$$
d_{i,b}^{brake} \;=\; \sum_{v \in V_i} d_{i,b}^{brake}(v)\, z_{i,v},
\qquad
x^{IP}_{i,b} \;=\; x_b^{end} - d_{i,b}^{brake} - \sigma
\qquad \forall i, b.
\tag{8}
$$

These are **linear** in $z_{i,v}$ because $d_{i,b}^{brake}(v)$ is a precomputed parameter (Eq. 1).

### 3.3 Timetable Propagation (Block Sequencing per Train)

For consecutive blocks $b, b'$ on the chosen route of train $i$ (with $b'$ the successor of $b$):

$$
t_{i,b'}^{arr} \;\ge\; t_{i,b}^{dep} + \tau_{i,b'}^{run} \qquad \forall i,\; (b,b') \in \text{succ},
\tag{9}
$$

$$
t_{i,b}^{dep} \;\ge\; t_{i,b}^{arr} + d_{i,b}^{dwell} \qquad \forall i,\; b.
\tag{10}
$$

### 3.4 Delay Definition

$$
\delta_{i,b} \;\ge\; t_{i,b}^{arr} - t_{i,b}^{arr,0} \qquad \forall i,\; b,
\tag{11}
$$

$$
\delta_{i,b} \;\ge\; 0 \qquad \forall i,\; b.
\tag{12}
$$

### 3.5 Headway / Separation Constraints (DTG-Enhanced)

This is the **core DTG enhancement**. Two trains $i, j$ using the same block $b$ must be separated such that the follower $j$ reaches its **brake indication point** $x^{IP}_{j,b}$ only after the leader $i$ has cleared the block (plus safety margin). Because the IP is speed-dependent, the separation constraint becomes:

$$
t_{j,b}^{arr} \;\ge\; t_{i,b}^{dep} + \Delta^{clear} \;-\; M\,(1 - \alpha_{i,j,b})
\qquad \forall (i,j) \in E,\; b \in B,
\tag{13}
$$

$$
t_{i,b}^{arr} \;\ge\; t_{j,b}^{dep} + \Delta^{clear} \;-\; M\,\alpha_{i,j,b}
\qquad \forall (i,j) \in E,\; b \in B.
\tag{14}
$$

Here $\Delta^{clear}$ is the time for the leader to fully clear the block, and the ordering variable $\alpha_{i,j,b}$ enforces that at most one of (13)–(14) is binding. The **speed dependence** enters through the fact that the arrival time $t_{j,b}^{arr}$ is linked to the chosen speed profile via (7), so a faster profile yields an earlier arrival but a *longer* braking distance (1), tightening (13)–(14) implicitly through the IP position.

To make the braking-curve interaction explicit, we add the **IP-conflict constraint**:

$$
t_{j,b}^{arr} \;\ge\; t_{i,b}^{dep} + \frac{x^{IP}_{j,b} - x_b^{start}}{v_{j,b}} \;-\; M\,(1 - \beta_{i,j,b})
\qquad \forall (i,j) \in E,\; b \in B,
\tag{15}
$$

$$
\beta_{i,j,b} + \beta_{j,i,b} \;\ge\; \alpha_{i,j,b} + \alpha_{j,i,b} - 1
\qquad \forall (i,j) \in E,\; b \in B.
\tag{16}
$$

Constraint (15) states that the follower $j$ may not reach its IP (which lies *inside* block $b$ when $d^{brake}_{j,b} < L_b$) before the leader has departed the block. This is precisely the DTG braking-curve supervision condition.

### 3.6 Switch / Route Locking Constraints (for $b \in S$)

For switch sections, exclusive route locking is required:

$$
\sum_{i \in T} \gamma_{i,b} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall b \in S,
\tag{17}
$$

$$
t_{i,b}^{arr} \;\ge\; t_{j,b}^{dep} + \Delta^{setup} \;-\; M\,(1 - \gamma_{i,b})
\qquad \forall i \neq j,\; b \in S,
\tag{18}
$$

$$
\gamma_{i,b} \;\le\; \sum_{r \in R_i : b \in B_r} y_{i,r} \qquad \forall i,\; b \in S.
\tag{19}
$$

This distinguishes switches from plain line, as required by the paper's third enhancement.

### 3.7 No-Overtaking Within a Block (Assumption A5)

$$
\alpha_{i,j,b} + \alpha_{j,i,b} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall (i,j) \in E,\; b \in B \text{ shared by } i,j.
\tag{20}
$$

### 3.8 Variable Domains

$$
t_{i,b}^{arr},\; t_{i,b}^{dep},\; \delta_{i,b} \;\ge\; 0,
\tag{21}
$$

$$
y_{i,r},\; z_{i,v},\; \alpha_{i,j,b},\; \beta_{i,j,b},\; \gamma_{i,b} \;\in\; \{0,1\}.
\tag{22}
$$

---

## 4. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{b \in B} w_i \, \delta_{i,b} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& \sum_{r \in R_i} y_{i,r} = 1 && \forall i \\
& \sum_{v \in V_i} z_{i,v} = 1 && \forall i \\
& \tau_{i,b}^{run} = \sum_{v} \tau_{i,b}^{run}(v)\, z_{i,v} && \forall i,b \\
& d_{i,b}^{brake} = \sum_{v} d_{i,b}^{brake}(v)\, z_{i,v},\quad x^{IP}_{i,b} = x_b^{end} - d_{i,b}^{brake} - \sigma && \forall i,b \\
& t_{i,b'}^{arr} \ge t_{i,b}^{dep} + \tau_{i,b'}^{run} && \forall i,(b,b') \\
& t_{i,b}^{dep} \ge t_{i,b}^{arr} + d_{i,b}^{dwell} && \forall i,b \\
& \delta_{i,b} \ge t_{i,b}^{arr} - t_{i,b}^{arr,0},\quad \delta_{i,b} \ge 0 && \forall i,b \\
& t_{j,b}^{arr} \ge t_{i,b}^{dep} + \Delta^{clear} - M(1-\alpha_{i,j,b}) && \forall (i,j),b \\
& t_{i,b}^{arr} \ge t_{j,b}^{dep} + \Delta^{clear} - M\,\alpha_{i,j,b} && \forall (i,j),b \\
& t_{j,b}^{arr} \ge t_{i,b}^{dep} + \tfrac{x^{IP}_{j,b}-x_b^{start}}{v_{j,b}} - M(1-\beta_{i,j,b}) && \forall (i,j),b \\
& \beta_{i,j,b} + \beta_{j,i,b} \ge \alpha_{i,j,b} + \alpha_{j,i,b} - 1 && \forall (i,j),b \\
& \sum_{i} \gamma_{i,b} \le 1 && \forall b \in S \\
& t_{i,b}^{arr} \ge t_{j,b}^{dep} + \Delta^{setup} - M(1-\gamma_{i,b}) && \forall i\neq j,\; b \in S \\
& \gamma_{i,b} \le \sum_{r: b \in B_r} y_{i,r} && \forall i,\; b \in S \\
& \alpha_{i,j,b} + \alpha_{j,i,b} = 1 && \forall (i,j),b \\
& t \ge 0,\; y,z,\alpha,\beta,\gamma \in \{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}}
$$

---

## 5. Discussion of the DTG Enhancements

1. **Speed profile options (Eqs. 5, 7–8).** By discretising $V_i$, the nonlinear relation $d^{brake} = v^2/(2a) + v\,t^{react}$ becomes a linear selection over precomputed parameters. This is the modelling device that makes the MILP tractable while retaining speed-dependent braking.

2. **Train- and speed-dependent brake indication points (Eq. 8, 15).** The IP $x^{IP}_{i,b}$ moves with the chosen speed profile: a faster train has a *longer* braking distance, hence an IP located *earlier* (further upstream) in the block. Constraint (15) enforces that the follower respects this moving IP, which is exactly the DTG braking-curve supervision that fixed-block models cannot capture.

3. **Switch vs. plain-line distinction (Eqs. 17–19).** Switch sections require exclusive route locking and setup/release time, whereas plain-line blocks only require headway separation. This reflects the operational reality that EoAs and route locking are handled differently around switches.

4. **Consistency with RECIFE-MILP.** Constraints (4), (9)–(14), (20) are the standard RECIFE-MILP structure; the DTG enhancements are (5), (7)–(8), (15)–(16), and (17)–(19). Setting $d^{brake}_{i,b}(v) = L_b$ for all $v$ (i.e., IP at block entry) recovers the conventional fixed-block model, which is the baseline for the comparative analysis in the paper.

5. **Operational relevance.** Because the IP is speed-dependent, the model can trade off *faster running* (shorter travel time) against *longer braking distance* (tighter headway with the preceding train). This trade-off is invisible to fixed-block CDR models and is precisely what the paper's comparative analysis aims to quantify in terms of total delay and rescheduling decisions.

Text:
# Integrated Rolling Stock Rescheduling MILP with Infrastructure Availability Constraints

Below is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming formulation that integrates the **composition model** (rolling stock assignment) and the **infrastructure model** (track-availability feasibility of shunting movements) described in the paper. The model decides which compositions cover the (possibly disrupted) timetable, which shunting movements to execute, and when each shunting movement starts — subject to track-occupation, sequencing, passenger-capacity, driver-availability and disruption constraints.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Train trips in the (possibly disrupted) timetable, indexed by $t, t', t''$ |
| $L$ | Train lines, indexed by $\ell$ |
| $T_\ell \subseteq T$ | Trips belonging to line $\ell$ |
| $R$ | Rolling stock units, indexed by $r$ |
| $C$ | Feasible compositions (multi-unit combinations), indexed by $c$ |
| $U_c \subseteq R$ | Rolling stock units forming composition $c$ |
| $M$ | Candidate shunting movements, indexed by $m$ |
| $M^{tt'} \subseteq M$ | Shunting movements linking trip $t$ to trip $t'$ |
| $S$ | Stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $TR_s$ | Tracks at station $s$; $TR = \bigcup_s TR_s$ |
| $D$ | Shunting drivers, indexed by $d$ |
| $D_s \subseteq D$ | Drivers based at station $s$ |
| $K = \{0,1,\dots,|K|\}$ | Discrete time periods (minutes) |
| $E = T \cup M$ | All events (trips and shunting movements) |

---

## 2. Parameters

**Trip data**
- $a_t, b_t$: scheduled departure and arrival time of trip $t$
- $p_t$: passenger demand for trip $t$
- $s_t^{dep}, s_t^{arr} \in S$: departure/arrival station of trip $t$
- $\mathit{cancel}_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is cancelled by the disruption

**Composition data**
- $\mathit{cap}_c$: seat capacity of composition $c$
- $\mathit{oc}_c$: operational cost of running composition $c$
- $\mathit{orig}_{t,c} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if composition $c$ was originally assigned to trip $t$

**Shunting data**
- $\mathit{dur}_m$: duration of shunting movement $m$
- $s_m \in S$: station where shunting $m$ takes place
- $\mathit{tr}_m \in TR$: track required by shunting $m$
- $t_m, t'_m \in T$: trip pair linked by shunting $m$
- $\Delta_m^{\max}$: maximum allowed delay of shunting movement $m$

**Infrastructure / disruption**
- $\delta$: maximum delay allowed for passenger trains (minutes)
- $\mathit{block}_{\mathit{tr},\tau} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if track $tr$ is blocked at time $\tau$
- $\Delta$: a sufficiently large positive constant (big-$M$)

**Objective weights** $\alpha, \beta, \gamma > 0$ for passenger service, plan-deviation and delay, respectively.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,c}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if composition $c$ is assigned to trip $t$ |
| $y_m$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is executed |
| $f_{t,t',c}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if composition $c$ is transferred from trip $t$ to trip $t'$ via shunting |
| $s_e$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | actual start time of event $e \in E$ |
| $d_e$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | delay of event $e$ ($d_e \ge s_e - a_e$) |
| $\mathit{stand}_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | number of standing passengers on trip $t$ |
| $\mathit{dev}_{t,c}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | absolute deviation from original assignment |
| $\mathit{occ}_{e,\tau}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if event $e$ occupies its track at time $\tau$ |
| $\sigma_{m,d}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if driver $d$ performs shunting movement $m$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha\!\sum_{t\in T}\!\mathit{stand}_t \;+\; \beta\!\sum_{t\in T, c\in C}\!\mathit{dev}_{t,c} \;+\; \gamma\!\sum_{e\in E}\!d_e \;+\; \sum_{t\in T, c\in C}\!\mathit{oc}_c\,x_{t,c}
$$

The four terms capture, respectively: (i) passenger discomfort (standing), (ii) deviation from the original rolling-stock plan, (iii) total delay imposed on passenger trains and shunting, and (iv) operational cost of the compositions used.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Composition-model constraints

**(C1) Trip–composition assignment** (cancelled trips need no composition):
$$
\sum_{c\in C} x_{t,c} \;=\; 1 - \mathit{cancel}_t \qquad \forall\, t\in T
$$

**(C2) Composition flow conservation** — every composition that enters a trip must either continue to a successor trip (through shunting) or end its service:
$$
\sum_{t'\in T:\,m\in M^{tt'}} f_{t,t',c} \;-\; \sum_{t''\in T:\,m\in M^{t''t}} f_{t'',t,c} \;=\; x_{t,c} - x^{end}_{t,c} \qquad \forall\, t\in T,\; c\in C
$$
where $x^{end}_{t,c}\in\{0,1\}$ indicates whether composition $c$ ends service after trip $t$ (preprocessed from the depot plan).

**(C3) Shunting activation** — a shunting movement $m$ is executed iff some composition flows along its trip pair:
$$
y_m \;\le\; \sum_{c\in C} f_{t_m,t'_m,c} \qquad \forall\, m\in M
$$
$$
y_m \;\ge\; f_{t_m,t'_m,c} \qquad \forall\, m\in M,\; c\in C
$$

**(C4) Passenger capacity** — shortfalls are absorbed by standing passengers:
$$
\sum_{c\in C} \mathit{cap}_c\,x_{t,c} \;+\; \mathit{stand}_t \;\ge\; p_t \qquad \forall\, t\in T, \qquad \mathit{stand}_t \ge 0
$$

**(C5) Linearised deviation from the original plan:**
$$
\mathit{dev}_{t,c} \;\ge\; x_{t,c} - \mathit{orig}_{t,c} \qquad \forall\, t\in T,\; c\in C
$$
$$
\mathit{dev}_{t,c} \;\ge\; \mathit{orig}_{t,c} - x_{t,c} \qquad \forall\, t\in T,\; c\in C
$$

### 5.2 Time-window and sequencing constraints

**(C6) Start-time bounds** (passenger trains may be delayed by at most $\delta$; shunting by $\Delta^{\max}_m$):
$$
s_e \;\ge\; a_e \qquad \forall\, e\in E
$$
$$
s_t \;\le\; b_t + \delta \qquad \forall\, t\in T, \qquad s_m \;\le\; b_m + \Delta^{\max}_m \qquad \forall\, m\in M
$$

**(C7) Delay definition:**
$$
d_e \;\ge\; s_e - a_e, \qquad d_e \ge 0 \qquad \forall\, e\in E
$$

**(C8) Sequencing of shunting with linked trips** — shunting starts after the previous trip arrives and finishes before the next trip departs:
$$
s_{t_m} + (b_{t_m} - a_{t_m}) \;\le\; s_m \qquad \forall\, m\in M
$$
$$
s_m + \mathit{dur}_m \;\le\; s_{t'_m} \qquad \forall\, m\in M
$$

### 5.3 Infrastructure-model constraints

**(C9) Track capacity** — at most one event may occupy a given track at any minute:
$$
\sum_{e\in E:\,\mathit{tr}_e = \mathit{tr}} \mathit{occ}_{e,\tau} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall\, \mathit{tr}\in TR,\; \tau\in K
$$

**(C10) Blocked tracks** (modelling the disruption):
$$
\mathit{occ}_{e,\tau} \;\le\; 1 - \mathit{block}_{\mathit{tr}_e,\tau} \qquad \forall\, e\in E,\; \tau\in K
$$

**(C11) Linearised definition of $\mathit{occ}_{m,\tau}$ for shunting movements** — equals 1 iff $y_m=1$ and $\tau\in[s_m, s_m+\mathit{dur}_m)$:
$$
\mathit{occ}_{m,\tau} \;\le\; y_m \qquad \forall\, m\in M,\; \tau\in K
$$
$$
\mathit{occ}_{m,\tau} \;\le\; \frac{s_m - \tau + \Delta}{\Delta} \qquad \forall\, m\in M,\; \tau\in K
$$
$$
\mathit{occ}_{m,\tau} \;\le\; \frac{\tau - s_m - \mathit{dur}_m + 1 + \Delta}{\Delta} \qquad \forall\, m\in M,\; \tau\in K
$$
$$
\mathit{occ}_{m,\tau} \;\ge\; y_m + \frac{s_m - \tau}{\Delta} + \frac{\tau - s_m - \mathit{dur}_m + 1}{\Delta} - 1 \qquad \forall\, m\in M,\; \tau\in K
$$

For non-shunting events $t\in T$, $\mathit{occ}_{t,\tau}$ is fixed to 1 on the time slots corresponding to the (possibly delayed) trip and 0 elsewhere, ensuring that passenger-train movements are always represented on the infrastructure.

**(C12) Shunting-driver assignment and conflict-free scheduling:**
$$
\sum_{d\in \mathit{driver}_m} \sigma_{m,d} \;=\; y_m \qquad \forall\, m\in M
$$
$$
\sum_{m\in M:\,\tau\in[s_m,\,s_m+\mathit{dur}_m)} \sigma_{m,d} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall\, d\in D,\; \tau\in K
$$

### 5.4 Rolling-stock-unit consistency (optional strengthening)

**(C13) Each physical unit appears in at most one composition per trip:**
$$
\sum_{c\in C:\,r\in U_c} x_{t,c} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall\, t\in T,\; r\in R
$$

**(C14) Unit non-overlap across overlapping trips** (enforced via time-indexed copies of $x$ or via the flow conservation (C2) when compositions are decomposed into units):
$$
\sum_{c\in C:\,r\in U_c}\;\sum_{t'\in T:\,[\,a_{t'},b_{t'}\,]\cap[\,a_t,b_t\,]\neq\emptyset} x_{t',c} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall\, t\in T,\; r\in R
$$

---

## 6. Modelling Assumptions (explicit)

1. **Time discretisation.** Time is discretised in minutes; all start times and durations are integer (or treated as continuous with a sufficiently fine grid).
2. **Composition set $C$.** Compositions are pre-generated (e.g., by the method of Fioole et al., 2006); coupling/decoupling of units is captured by selecting different compositions for consecutive trips.
3. **Shunting set $M$.** Candidate shunting movements are pre-enumerated for every feasible trip pair at every station; the model only decides *whether* and *when* to execute them.
4. **Track granularity.** Each shunting movement requires exactly one track; multi-track movements are decomposed.
5. **Bounded delays.** Passenger trains may be delayed by at most $\delta$ minutes (resolved by timetable buffers); shunting movements have their own maximum delay $\Delta^{\max}_m$.
6. **Passengers.** Demand $p_t$ is deterministic and inelastic; only standing is penalised (no denied boarding).
7. **Drivers.** Each shunting movement requires one driver from a station-specific pool; a driver can perform at most one movement at a time.
8. **Disruption.** Track blockages are exogenous and modelled through $\mathit{block}_{\mathit{tr},\tau}$; cancelled trips have $\mathit{cancel}_t = 1$ and need no composition.
9. **Stick-to-the-plan.** Captured by the $\beta$-weighted deviation term $\sum \mathit{dev}_{t,c}$, which counts every trip whose assigned composition differs from the original plan.
10. **Decomposition view.** In the paper's algorithmic framework, the composition block (C1)–(C5) and the infrastructure block (C9)–(C12) are separated by a Combinatorial Benders' decomposition (exact algorithm) or processed sequentially (iterative heuristic); the formulation above is the monolithic master problem that those algorithms implicitly solve.

---

## 7. Compact Reformulation

For implementation, the model can be written compactly as

$$

$$

\underbrace{A_{\text{comp}}\,x + A_{\text{flow}}\,f = b_{\text{comp}}}_{\text{(C1)–(C3)}}\,,\;
\underbrace{A_{\text{cap}}\,x + \mathit{stand} \ge p}_{\text{(C4)}}\,,\;
\underbrace{|\,\cdot\,|\text{ linearised by (C5)}}_{\text{deviation}}\,,
$$
$$
\underbrace{T_s\,s + T_d\,d \le b}_{\text{(C6)–(C8)}}\,,\;
\underbrace{O\,\mathit{occ} \le \mathbf{1}}_{\text{(C9)–(C11)}}\,,\;

This MILP — or its Benders/iterative decomposition — is the formal counterpart of the two-step framework described in the paper: it jointly decides the rolling-stock circulation **and** the timing of every shunting movement such that all movements are feasible with respect to the available tracks at the considered stations.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Based on the inspiration provided, I formulate a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for the rtRTMP. The model follows the two-stage decomposition idea (rerouting/reordering → rescheduling) but is presented as a single, self-contained MILP that captures the essential structure of the reference models (Pellegrini et al., 2014; Samà et al., 2016; Keita et al., 2020).

All assumptions that are not explicitly stated in the input are **marked as assumptions**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in T$ |
| $B$ | Set of block sections (track segments between two consecutive signals), indexed by $b \in B$ |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$ (pre-computed, assumption: finite and small) |
| $R_i^b \subseteq R_i$ | Subset of routes of train $i$ that use block section $b$ |
| $O_b$ | Set of train pairs $(i,j)$ that can potentially conflict on block $b$ (i.e., both have at least one route using $b$) |
| $S$ | Set of stations / stations' platforms, indexed by $s$ (assumption: needed for dwell and overtaking) |
| $B_s$ | Set of block sections adjacent to station $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of ordered pairs $(i,j)$ such that train $i$ precedes train $j$ in the original timetable |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $r_i^{\text{orig}} \in R_i$ | Original (planned) route of train $i$ |
| $t_i^{\text{arr},0}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at its destination |
| $t_i^{\text{dep},0}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from its origin |
| $\tau_{i,b}^{\text{run}}$ | Minimum running time of train $i$ on block $b$ |
| $\tau_{i,s}^{\text{dwell,min}}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau_{i,s}^{\text{dwell,max}}$ | Maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h_b$ | Minimum headway (safety separation time) on block section $b$ |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $w_i$ | Weight (priority) of train $i$ in the objective function |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | Weighting coefficients for delay and route-deviation penalties |

**Assumption:** All times are expressed in a common discrete time unit (e.g., seconds or minutes). All parameters are deterministic (no stochastic disturbances modeled inside the MILP; uncertainty is handled by re-solving).

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Routing Variables

$$
x_{i,r} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if train } i \text{ is assigned route } r \in R_i \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$

### 3.2 Scheduling (Timing) Variables

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| $a_{i,b} \ge 0$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at the beginning of block $b$ |
| $d_{i,b} \ge 0$ | Departure time of train $i$ from block $b$ (i.e., entry time into next block) |
| $a_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\delta_i \ge 0$ | Total delay of train $i$ at its destination |

### 3.3 Ordering Variables

$$
y_{i,j,b} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if train } i \text{ uses block } b \text{ before train } j \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\quad \forall (i,j) \in O_b, \; b \in B
$$

**Assumption:** $y_{i,j,b}$ and $y_{j,i,b}$ are complementary only when both trains actually use $b$; otherwise both may be zero. This is enforced via constraints below.

### 3.4 Route-Usage Indicator

$$
u_{i,b} = \sum_{r \in R_i^b} x_{i,r} \quad \in \{0,1\}
$$

(linear expression, not an independent variable)

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total train delays and route-deviation penalties:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T} w_i \, \delta_i \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{r \in R_i \setminus \{r_i^{\text{orig}}\}} x_{i,r}
$$

**Assumption:** The route-deviation term $\alpha \sum \sum x_{i,r}$ penalizes rerouting away from the original route. If route deviations should not be penalized, set $\alpha = 0$. A secondary term $\beta$ could penalize order changes, but this is omitted here for tractability (assumption).

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Route Assignment

Each train is assigned exactly one route:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T \tag{1}
$$

### 5.2 Route–Block Coupling

A train can only use a block if its chosen route contains that block:

$$
u_{i,b} = \sum_{r \in R_i^b} x_{i,r} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B \tag{2}
$$

$$
u_{i,b} \le \sum_{r \in R_i^b} x_{i,r} \quad \text{(implied by (2), redundant)} \tag{2'}
$$

### 5.3 Running Time on Blocks

For each train $i$ and block $b$ that it uses, the departure from $b$ must be at least the arrival plus the running time:

$$
d_{i,b} \ge a_{i,b} + \tau_{i,b}^{\text{run}} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B \tag{3}
$$

**Assumption:** If train $i$ does not use block $b$, constraint (3) is relaxed by the big-M term.

### 5.4 Block Occupancy and Headway (Ordering Constraints)

For every pair $(i,j) \in O_b$ that can conflict on block $b$:

$$
a_{j,b} \ge d_{i,b} + h_b - M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \tag{4}
$$

$$
a_{i,b} \ge d_{j,b} + h_b - M \, y_{i,j,b} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \tag{5}
$$

$$
y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} \ge u_{i,b} + u_{j,b} - 1 \quad \forall (i,j) \in O_b, \; b \in B \tag{6}
$$

Constraint (6) ensures that if both trains use block $b$, exactly one ordering is selected (i.e., $y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1$). If only one or neither uses $b$, the sum may be 0.

**Assumption:** The headway $h_b$ is constant per block and independent of train type. If train-type-dependent headways are required, $h_b$ can be replaced by $h_{i,j,b}$.

### 5.5 Station Dwell Time

For each train $i$ and station $s$ on its route:

$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dwell,min}} - M(1 - u_{i,s}) \tag{7}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \le a_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dwell,max}} + M(1 - u_{i,s}) \tag{8}
$$

where $u_{i,s} = \sum_{r \in R_i^s} x_{i,r}$ indicates whether station $s$ is on the chosen route (assumption: $R_i^s$ is the set of routes of $i$ passing through $s$).

### 5.6 Block–Station Time Consistency

For a block $b$ entering station $s$ (i.e., $b \in B_s^{\text{in}}$):

$$
a_{i,s} \ge d_{i,b} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) \tag{9}
$$

For a block $b$ leaving station $s$ (i.e., $b \in B_s^{\text{out}}$):

$$
a_{i,b} \ge d_{i,s} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) \tag{10}
$$

**Assumption:** These constraints link block-level and station-level timing variables. They are needed to make the model self-contained.

### 5.7 Delay Definition

The delay of train $i$ is the positive difference between its actual arrival at the destination and the scheduled arrival:

$$
\delta_i \ge a_{i,\text{dest}(i)} - t_i^{\text{arr},0} \quad \forall i \in T \tag{11}
$$

$$
\delta_i \ge 0 \quad \forall i \in T \tag{12}
$$

**Assumption:** $\text{dest}(i)$ is the destination station of train $i$. If the train is early, $\delta_i = 0$ (no negative delay).

### 5.8 Origin Departure Constraint

A train cannot depart before its scheduled departure time (or before the earliest feasible departure):

$$
d_{i,\text{orig}(i)} \ge t_i^{\text{dep},0} \quad \forall i \in T \tag{13}
$$

**Assumption:** Trains may depart later than scheduled (delay), but not earlier.

### 5.9 Precedence Constraints (Optional, FIFO-like)

If the dispatcher wants to enforce the original order on a block $b$ for a pair $(i,j)$:

$$
y_{i,j,b} = 1 \quad \text{for } (i,j) \in \mathcal{E} \cap O_b \tag{14}
$$

**Assumption:** These constraints are optional and can be relaxed to allow reordering. They are included to model the FIFO policy as a special case.

### 5.10 Route–Ordering Coupling (Sub-optimal Model Extension)

In the sub-optimal (first-stage) model, delay propagation is disregarded. This can be modeled by replacing constraints (4)–(5) with a simpler pair-wise delay interpretation:

$$
a_{j,b} \ge a_{i,b} - M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \tag{4'}
$$

**Assumption:** This relaxed version is used in the first stage to obtain a fast, sub-optimal solution. The full model uses (4)–(5).

### 5.11 Variable Domains

$$
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in T, \; r \in R_i \tag{15}
$$

$$
y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (i,j) \in O_b, \; b \in B \tag{16}
$$

$$
a_{i,b}, \; d_{i,b}, \; a_{i,s}, \; d_{i,s}, \; \delta_i \ge 0 \quad \forall i, b, s \tag{17}
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{i \in T} w_i \, \delta_i + \alpha \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{r \in R_i \setminus \{r_i^{\text{orig}}\}} x_{i,r} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1 && \forall i \in T \\
& u_{i,b} = \sum_{r \in R_i^b} x_{i,r} && \forall i \in T, b \in B \\
& d_{i,b} \ge a_{i,b} + \tau_{i,b}^{\text{run}} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) && \forall i, b \\
& a_{j,b} \ge d_{i,b} + h_b - M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) && \forall (i,j) \in O_b, b \\
& a_{i,b} \ge d_{j,b} + h_b - M y_{i,j,b} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) && \forall (i,j) \in O_b, b \\
& y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} \ge u_{i,b} + u_{j,b} - 1 && \forall (i,j) \in O_b, b \\
& d_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dwell,min}} - M(1 - u_{i,s}) && \forall i, s \\
& d_{i,s} \le a_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dwell,max}} + M(1 - u_{i,s}) && \forall i, s \\
& a_{i,s} \ge d_{i,b} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) && \forall i, b \in B_s^{\text{in}} \\
& a_{i,b} \ge d_{i,s} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) && \forall i, b \in B_s^{\text{out}} \\
& \delta_i \ge a_{i,\text{dest}(i)} - t_i^{\text{arr},0} && \forall i \in T \\
& \delta_i \ge 0 && \forall i \in T \\
& d_{i,\text{orig}(i)} \ge t_i^{\text{dep},0} && \forall i \in T \\
& x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \; y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}, \; a, d, \delta \ge 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Assumptions and Remarks

1. **Finite route set:** $R_i$ is pre-computed and finite. This is standard in rtRTMP literature (Samà et al., 2016; Bettinelli et al., 2017).
2. **Deterministic parameters:** All running times, dwell times, and headways are known and deterministic. Uncertainty is handled by re-solving the MILP when disturbances occur.
3. **Big-M validity:** $M$ must be larger than the maximum possible time horizon (e.g., the scheduling horizon length). A common choice is $M = \max_{i} t_i^{\text{arr},0} + \text{horizon}$.
4. **Station capacity:** The model does not explicitly limit the number of trains at a station platform. If platform capacity is limited, additional constraints (e.g., $\sum_i u_{i,s} \le \text{cap}_s$) can be added.
5. **Delay propagation:** The full model (constraints 4–5) captures delay propagation through the headway constraints. The sub-optimal model (constraint 4') does not, which is the key difference analyzed in the paper.
6. **Safety-relevant overlaps:** The model can be extended to include overlap clearance times (Lindenmaier et al., 2022) by adding a minimum clearance time after a train passes a stop signal before the next train can use the overlapping block.
7. **Objective weights:** $w_i$ can be set to 1 for all trains (minimize total delay) or higher for priority trains (e.g., high-speed trains). $\alpha$ controls the trade-off between delay minimization and route adherence.
8. **Computational tractability:** The model is NP-hard. For large instances, decomposition (e.g., Benders or the two-stage approach described in the paper) is recommended.

---

## 8. References (as cited in the input)

- Pellegrini, P., et al. (2014). "Optimal train routing and scheduling for managing traffic perturbations in complex junctions." *Transportation Research Part B*.
- Samà, M., et al. (2016). "Ant colony optimization for the real-time train routing selection problem." *Transportation Research Part B*.
- Keita, K., et al. (2020). "A three-step Benders decomposition for the real-time railway traffic management problem." *Journal of Rail Transport Planning & Management*.
- Lindenmaier, L., et al. (2022). "Optimal railway traffic management with safety-relevant overlaps." *RailNorrköping*.
- Corman, F., et al. (2010). "A tabu search algorithm for rerouting trains during rail operations." *Transportation Research Part B*.
- Törnquist Krasemann, J. (2012). "Design of an effective algorithm for fast response to the re-scheduling of railway traffic during disturbances." *Transportation Research Part C*.

---

This model provides a complete, linear, and self-contained MILP formulation for the rtRTMP, closely following the structure and assumptions of the reference works while marking all additional assumptions explicitly.

messages.content: You convert the text of an optimization model into a structured record. Report only what the text states as mathematics, that is, objective functions, equations and inequalities written with symbols. Do not complete, repair, improve or invent anything.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code. It addresses a disruption caused by a **partial segment blockage**, allowing local rerouting onto the opposite track, and jointly optimizes train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Definition |
|---|---|
| $S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\text{SEG}$ | Set of segment, indexed by $(s,s')$ where $s' = s+1$ |
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i$ (and $i'$) |
| $P = \{0,1,\dots,N_P\}$ | Discretized positions (control points) along a segment, indexed by $p$ |
| $V$ | Set of discretized feasible speed levels (m/s), indexed by $v$ |
| $d_i \in \{1,2\}$ | Direction of train $i$ (1 = up, 2 = down) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $L_{s}$ | Length of segment $(s,s')$ |
| $T^{\min}_{s},\ T^{\max}_{s}$ | Minimum / maximum allowed running time on segment $(s,s')$ |
| $\bar D_{i,s},\ \bar A_{i,s}$ | Planned (scheduled) departure / arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\underline{Dw}_i,\ \overline{Dw}_i$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time of train $i$ |
| $H_{\min}$ | Minimum same-direction headway |
| $H_{\mathrm{opp}}$ | Minimum opposite-direction headway (for shared/opposite track) |
| $[ts_{\text{seg}},\, te_{\text{seg}}]$ | Disruption time window on the affected segment |
| $\text{AFF}$ | Set of affected segments (only one in the example) |
| $dx$ | Position step length |
| $v_{\max},\,v_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum speed |
| $a_{\max},\,b_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / braking rates |
| $K_1,\,K_2$ | Energy coefficient constants |
| $\alpha_i,\ \beta_i,\ \gamma_i$ | Objective weights — delay, energy, cancellation |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $T_{\text{start}},\,T_{\text{end}}$ | Scheduling horizon bounds |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $dep_{i,s} \ge 0$ — actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $arr_{i,s} \ge 0$ — actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $run_{i,\text{seg}} \ge 0$ — actual running time on segment
- $dwell_{i,s} \ge 0$ — actual dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $tpos_{i,\text{seg},p} \ge 0$ — time at which train $i$ reaches position $p$
- $u_{i,\text{seg},p} \ge 0$ — actual speed at position $p$
- $e_{i,\text{seg}} \ge 0$ — energy consumption of train $i$ on segment
- $del_{i,s} \ge 0$ — linearized delay of train $i$ at station $s$

**Binary:**
- $y^{opp}_{i,\text{seg}} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment
- $z_{i,i',\text{seg}} \in \{0,1\}$ — ordering variable: 1 if train $i$ precedes $i'$ on segment
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $v^{sel}_{i,\text{seg},p,v} \in \{0,1\}$ — speed-level selection
- $a^{no}_{i,\text{seg}},\ b^{no}_{i,\text{seg}} \in \{0,1\}$ — no-overlap indicators on the affected segment

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \quad
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \alpha_i \cdot del_{i,s}}_{\text{delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{\text{seg}\in \text{SEG}} \beta_i \cdot e_{i,\text{seg}}}_{\text{energy}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in T} \gamma_i \cdot c_i}_{\text{cancellation}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Arrival–Departure–Running–Dwell Linkage
For each train $i$ with station sequence $r=(r_0,\dots,r_{|r|-1})$:
$$
arr_{i,s_{\text{curr}}} = dep_{i,s_{\text{prev}}} + run_{i,\text{seg}(s_{\text{prev}},s_{\text{curr}})}, \quad \forall (s_{\text{prev}},s_{\text{curr}})\in r
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} = arr_{i,s} + dwell_{i,s}, \quad \forall \text{ intermediate } s
$$
$$
dwell_{i,r_0} = 0, \qquad dwell_{i,r_{\text{end}}} = 0
$$

### (C2) Dwell Bounds
$$
\underline{Dw}_i (1 - c_i) \;\le\; dwell_{i,s} \;\le\; \overline{Dw}_i (1-c_i) + M c_i, \quad \forall i, \text{ intermediate } s
$$

### (C3) Running-Time Bounds
$$
T^{\min}_{s}(1 - c_i) \;\le\; run_{i,\text{seg}} \;\le\; T^{\max}_{s}(1-c_i) + M c_i
$$

### (C4) Same-Direction Headway (Ordering)
For $i \ne i'$ with $d_i = d_{i'}$ and $i < i'$:
$$
dep_{i',s} - dep_{i,s} \;\ge\; H_{\min} - M(1-z_{i,i',\text{seg}}) - M(c_i + c_{i'})
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} - dep_{i',s} \;\ge\; H_{\min} - M\,z_{i,i',\text{seg}} - M(c_i + c_{i'})
$$
$$
z_{i,i',\text{seg}} + z_{i',i,\text{seg}} \;\le\; 1 + c_i + c_{i'}
$$

### (C5) Partial Blockage / Forced Rerouting
For an affected segment $(s,s')$ with entry $= dep_{i,s}$ and exit $= arr_{i,s'}$:
$$
arr_{i,s'} \;\le\; ts_{\text{seg}} + M(1-a^{no}_{i,\text{seg}})
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} \;\ge\; te_{\text{seg}} - M(1-b^{no}_{i,\text{seg}})
$$
$$
a^{no}_{i,\text{seg}} + b^{no}_{i,\text{seg}} + y^{opp}_{i,\text{seg}} \;\ge\; 1 - c_i
$$
$$
y^{opp}_{i,\text{seg}} \;\le\; 1 - a^{no}_{i,\text{seg}} + c_i, \qquad
y^{opp}_{i,\text{seg}} \;\le\; 1 - b^{no}_{i,\text{seg}} + c_i
$$
For non-affected segments: $y^{opp}_{i,\text{seg}} = 0$.

### (C6) Bidirectional Conflict on Shared Opposite Track
For $i \ne i'$ with $d_i \ne d_{i'}$:
$$
dep_{i',s} - dep_{i,s} \;\ge\; H_{\mathrm{opp}} - M(2-y^{opp}_{i,\text{seg}} - y^{opp}_{i',\text{seg}}) - M(c_i + c_{i'})
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} - dep_{i',s} \;\ge\; H_{\mathrm{opp}} - M(2-y^{opp}_{i,\text{seg}} - y^{opp}_{i',\text{seg}}) - M(c_i + c_{i'})
$$

### (C7) Position–Time Monotonicity and Alignment
$$
tpos_{i,\text{seg},p+1} \;\ge\; tpos_{i,\text{seg},p} + \frac{dx}{v_{\max}}, \quad \forall p=0,\dots,N_P-1
$$
$$
tpos_{i,\text{seg},0} = dep_{i,s}, \qquad tpos_{i,\text{seg},N_P} = arr_{i,s'}
$$
(direction of $s,s'$ adapted to $d_i$)

### (C8) Speed Consistency
$$
\sum_{v\in V} v^{sel}_{i,\text{seg},p,v} = 1
$$
$$
u_{i,\text{seg},p} = \sum_{v\in V} v \cdot v^{sel}_{i,\text{seg},p,v}
$$
$$
\frac{dx}{v_{\max}} \;\le\; tpos_{i,\text{seg},p+1} - tpos_{i,\text{seg},p} \;\le\; \frac{dx}{v_{\min}}
$$
$$
tpos_{i,\text{seg},p+1} - tpos_{i,\text{seg},p} \;\ge\; \frac{dx}{v} - M(1-v^{sel}_{i,\text{seg},p,v})
$$
$$
tpos_{i,\text{seg},p+1} - tpos_{i,\text{seg},p} \;\le\; \frac{dx}{v} + M(1-v^{sel}_{i,\text{seg},p,v})
$$

### (C9) Acceleration / Braking Limits
For $p < N_P - 1$:
$$
u_{i,\text{seg},p+1} - u_{i,\text{seg},p} \;\le\; a_{\max}\big(tpos_{i,\text{seg},p+1}-tpos_{i,\text{seg},p}\big)
$$
$$
u_{i,\text{seg},p} - u_{i,\text{seg},p+1} \;\le\; b_{\max}\big(tpos_{i,\text{seg},p+1}-tpos_{i,\text{seg},p}\big)
$$

### (C10) Energy Lower Bounds (Piecewise-Linear Surrogate)
For each $v_k \in V$:
$$
e_{i,\text{seg}} \;\ge\; K_1\, run_{i,\text{seg}} + K_2\big[(2 v_k\, u_{i,\text{seg},N_P} - v_k^2) - (2 v_k\, u_{i,\text{seg},0} - v_k^2)\big]
$$

### (C11) Delay Linearization and Cancellation
$$
del_{i,s} \;\ge\; arr_{i,s} - \bar A_{i,s} - M c_i
$$
$$
del_{i,s} \;\le\; M(1-c_i) + \epsilon
$$

### (C12) Time Horizon
$$
T_{\text{start}}(1-c_i) \;\le\; dep_{i,s},\ arr_{i,s},\ tpos_{i,\text{seg},p} \;\le\; T_{\text{end}}(1-c_i) + M c_i
$$

### (C13) Domains
Continuous variables $\ge 0$; binary variables in $\{0,1\}$.

---

## 6. Assumptions (marked)

1. **Discretized speed profiles** — speed is piecewise-constant with a finite set of levels $V$.
2. **Piecewise-linear traction energy** — energy linearized via tangent-plane lower envelope on $v^2$.
3. **Fixed disruption window** $[ts_{\text{seg}}, te_{\text{seg}}]$ on the affected segment.
4. **Local rerouting only** — trains may use the opposite track exclusively on the affected segment during the blockage window; elsewhere $y^{opp}=0$.
5. **Single-line bidirectional track** — all trains share the same physical infrastructure; dispositive/headway constraints apply uniformly.
6. **Deterministic times** — no stochastic delays or secondary disruptions are modeled.
7. **Cancellation** disables timetable and speed-related constraints via big-M relaxation with zero delay contribution.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a partial segment blockage (e.g., one track of a double-track line is unavailable) occurs during a known disruption time window. Trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track within the disruption area, requiring careful coordination of bidirectional traffic. We integrate train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profile selection) into a single MILP.

**Assumptions (marked as such where information is missing):**

- **(A1)** The line is discretized into a set of *segments* between consecutive stations; each segment has a single running direction per track, but during the disruption window, trains may use the opposite track (local rerouting).
- **(A2)** Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set of *candidate speed profiles* per train per segment, each associated with a running time and energy consumption. This is a standard discretization assumption for MILP tractability (cf. Howlett et al. 2022).
- **(A3)** The disruption is a partial blockage: one track of a segment is unavailable during a known time window $[T^{\text{dis}}_s, \bar{T}^{\text{dis}}_s]$ for each affected segment $s$. The opposite track remains available for bidirectional use with a minimum headway.
- **(A4)** Train order on a segment is determined by the model (reordering allowed), subject to safety headways.
- **(A5)** Dwell times at stations are decision variables bounded by minimum and maximum values.
- **(A6)** Cancellation of trains is allowed at a penalty cost.
- **(A7)** All times are measured in a common discrete time unit (e.g., seconds), and the planning horizon is $[0, T^{\max}]$.
- **(A8)** Acceleration/deceleration is embedded in the speed profile selection; no separate continuous dynamics are modeled (consistent with the discretized profile assumption).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of segments (directed links between consecutive stations), indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Set of segments affected by the partial blockage |
| $\mathcal{K}_t$ | Set of candidate speed profiles for train $t$ on segment $s$, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_t$ | Set of feasible *train plans* (paths through the network with timing and profile choices) for train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of directions, $\mathcal{D} = \{+1, -1\}$ (up/down) |
| $\mathcal{N}$ | Set of nodes (stations), indexed by $n$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling Variables

- $x_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$; 0 otherwise.
- $a_{t,n} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $t$ at station $n$.
- $d_{t,n} \ge 0$: departure time of train $t$ from station $n$.
- $w_{t,n} \ge 0$: dwell time of train $t$ at station $n$.
- $y_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $s$; 0 otherwise.
- $z_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled; 0 otherwise.
- $\delta_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable; 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $s$.
- $u_{t,s} \ge 0$: entry time of train $t$ into segment $s$.
- $v_{t,s} \ge 0$: exit time of train $t$ from segment $s$.

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

- $\tau_{t,s,k} \ge 0$: running time of train $t$ on segment $s$ using profile $k$.
- $e_{t,s,k} \ge 0$: energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $s$ using profile $k$.

These are *parameters* derived from the speed profile library, but we treat the selection via $x_{t,s,k}$.

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, cancellation penalty, and rerouting cost:

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{n \in \mathcal{N}} \left( a_{t,n} - a^{\text{sch}}_{t,n} \right)^+ 
+ \beta \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} e_{t,s,k} \, x_{t,s,k}
+ \gamma \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} z_t
+ \eta \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}} y_{t,s}
$$

where $(\cdot)^+ = \max(0, \cdot)$ is linearized via auxiliary variables $\Delta_{t,n} \ge a_{t,n} - a^{\text{sch}}_{t,n}$, $\Delta_{t,n} \ge 0$. Weights $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \eta \ge 0$ are exogenous.

**Linearized objective:**

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{t,n} \Delta_{t,n} + \beta \sum_{t,s,k} e_{t,s,k} x_{t,s,k} + \gamma \sum_t z_t + \eta \sum_{t,s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}} y_{t,s}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Speed Profile Selection

Each train selects exactly one profile per segment (if not cancelled):

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} x_{t,s,k} = 1 - z_t, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{C1}
$$

### 5.2 Running Time Consistency

The running time on a segment equals the selected profile's running time:

$$
v_{t,s} - u_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t} \tau_{t,s,k} \, x_{t,s,k}, \quad \forall t, s
\tag{C2}
$$

### 5.3 Segment Entry/Exit Linking with Station Times

For each train $t$ and consecutive segments $s^-$ (into station $n$) and $s^+$ (out of station $n$):

$$
a_{t,n} = v_{t,s^-}, \quad d_{t,n} = u_{t,s^+}, \quad \forall t, n
\tag{C3}
$$

### 5.4 Dwell Time Constraints

$$
w_{t,n} = d_{t,n} - a_{t,n}, \quad \forall t, n
\tag{C4}
$$

$$
w^{\min}_{t,n} (1 - z_t) \le w_{t,n} \le w^{\max}_{t,n} (1 - z_t), \quad \forall t, n
\tag{C5}
$$

### 5.5 Disruption Time Window Constraints

If train $t$ traverses segment $s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}$ during the disruption window, it must be rerouted:

$$
u_{t,s} \le \bar{T}^{\text{dis}}_s + M(1 - y_{t,s}), \quad \forall t, s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{C6}
$$

$$
v_{t,s} \ge T^{\text{dis}}_s - M(1 - y_{t,s}), \quad \forall t, s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{C7}
$$

If the train's traversal overlaps the disruption window, $y_{t,s} = 1$ is enforced:

$$
u_{t,s} \le \bar{T}^{\text{dis}}_s + M(1 - y_{t,s}), \quad v_{t,s} \ge T^{\text{dis}}_s - M y_{t,s}
\tag{C8}
$$

### 5.6 Rerouting Capacity (Unidirectional Line Capacity)

At most one train per direction may occupy the rerouted track at a time, and bidirectional trains must be separated by a minimum headway $h^{\text{bi}}$:

$$
|u_{t,s} - u_{t',s}| \ge h^{\text{bi}} - M(2 - y_{t,s} - y_{t',s}), \quad \forall t \ne t', s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{C9}
$$

### 5.7 Headway Constraints (Same Direction)

For trains $t, t'$ on the same segment $s$ in the same direction:

$$
u_{t',s} \ge v_{t,s} + h^{\text{same}} - M(1 - \delta_{t,t',s}), \quad \forall t \ne t', s
\tag{C10}
$$

$$
u_{t,s} \ge v_{t',s} + h^{\text{same}} - M \delta_{t,t',s}, \quad \forall t \ne t', s
\tag{C11}
$$

### 5.8 Ordering Consistency

$$
\delta_{t,t',s} + \delta_{t',t,s} = 1, \quad \forall t \ne t', s
\tag{C12}
$$

### 5.9 Station Capacity / Conflict Constraints

At most one train may occupy a station track at a time (simplified):

$$
a_{t',n} \ge d_{t,n} + h^{\text{station}} - M(1 - \sigma_{t,t',n}), \quad \forall t \ne t', n
\tag{C13}
$$

where $\sigma_{t,t',n}$ is a binary ordering variable at station $n$.

### 5.10 Cancellation Linking

If train $t$ is cancelled, all its segment and station times are zero:

$$
a_{t,n} \le M(1 - z_t), \quad d_{t,n} \le M(1 - z_t), \quad \forall t, n
\tag{C14}
$$

### 5.11 Delay Linearization

$$
\Delta_{t,n} \ge a_{t,n} - a^{\text{sch}}_{t,n}, \quad \Delta_{t,n} \ge 0, \quad \forall t, n
\tag{C15}
$$

### 5.12 Time Horizon

$$
0 \le a_{t,n}, d_{t,n}, u_{t,s}, v_{t,s} \le T^{\max}, \quad \forall t, n, s
\tag{C16}
$$

### 5.13 Binary and Non-negativity

$$
x_{t,s,k}, y_{t,s}, z_t, \delta_{t,t',s}, \sigma_{t,t',n} \in \{0,1\}
\tag{C17}
$$

$$
a_{t,n}, d_{t,n}, w_{t,n}, u_{t,s}, v_{t,s}, \Delta_{t,n} \ge 0
\tag{C18}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \alpha \sum_{t,n} \Delta_{t,n} + \beta \sum_{t,s,k} e_{t,s,k} x_{t,s,k} + \gamma \sum_t z_t + \eta \sum_{t,s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}} y_{t,s} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C18)}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Remarks on Model Properties

- **Conflict-free guarantee:** Constraints (C9)–(C13) ensure that no two trains conflict on segments or at stations, including bidirectional conflicts on rerouted tracks.
- **Coupling of TRP and TSMP:** Constraints (C2) and (C3) link the timetable (arrival/departure times) with the speed profile selection, ensuring that the rescheduled timetable is executable at the control level.
- **Energy efficiency:** The objective includes energy consumption via the selected speed profiles, enabling trade-offs between delay and energy.
- **Rerouting flexibility:** Binary $y_{t,s}$ allows local rerouting only on disrupted segments, preserving unidirectional line capacity.
- **Cancellation:** Binary $z_t$ allows train cancellation with penalty $\gamma$.

---

## 8. Assumptions Marked Explicitly

| Assumption | Justification |
|------------|---------------|
| (A1) Segment discretization | Standard for MILP tractability |
| (A2) Finite speed profiles | Common in TSMP literature (Howlett et al. 2022) |
| (A3) Known disruption window | Given by disruption scenario |
| (A4) Reordering allowed | Required for conflict resolution |
| (A5) Bounded dwell times | Operational realism |
| (A6) Cancellation allowed | Standard in TRP (Cacchiani et al. 2014) |
| (A7) Discrete time horizon | Simplifies MILP formulation |
| (A8) Embedded dynamics | Consistent with profile-based speed management |

This model provides a complete, linear, and solvable MILP formulation for the integrated TRSMP under partial segment blockages, capturing the essential coupling between train rescheduling and speed management while ensuring conflict-free operations.
