Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is a fully specified mixed-integer linear program (MILP) inspired by the introduction. All modeling choices are stated explicitly; assumptions that go beyond the text are marked **[A#]**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations (nodes), indexed by $s, k$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of track segments (links), indexed by $l = (s,k)$ |
| $\mathcal{L}^{B} \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ | Segments affected by the partial blockage (disruption area) |
| $\mathcal{L}_i \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ | Segments on the nominal route of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Disruption-affected trains (those whose nominal path uses $\mathcal{L}^{B}$) |
| $\mathcal{T}^{up}, \mathcal{T}^{dn}$ | Up-direction and down-direction trains, $\mathcal{T}^{up}\cup\mathcal{T}^{dn}=\mathcal{T}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of candidate speed profiles (plans) for train $i$, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_i$ | Set of candidate routes for train $i$ (nominal + rerouting options), indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_l$ | Set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ that can conflict on segment $l$ (opposite or same direction) |

**Assumptions on sets**
- **[A1]** The network is a single line with two tracks (one per direction) between adjacent stations; a partial blockage removes one track in $\mathcal{L}^B$ during the disruption window.
- **[A2]** Each train has a fixed origin and destination; only the intermediate routing (use of opposite track inside $\mathcal{L}^B$) may change.
- **[A3]** Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set of piecewise-constant acceleration/deceleration/coasting modes, each yielding a pre-computed running time and energy consumption per segment.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|---|---|---|
| $T^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled (nominal) departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ | s |
| $T^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled (nominal) arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | s |
| $t^{run}_{i,l,p}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ using profile $p$ | s |
| $e_{i,l,p}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $l$ using profile $p$ | kWh |
| $t^{min}_{i,l}$, $t^{max}_{i,l}$ | Minimum/maximum feasible running time on segment $l$ | s |
| $d^{min}_{i,s}$, $d^{max}_{i,s}$ | Minimum/maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ | s |
| $\tau_l$ | Minimum headway (safety separation) on segment $l$ | s |
| $[T^{b,start}_l, T^{b,end}_l]$ | Disruption time window on segment $l\in\mathcal{L}^B$ | s |
| $H$ | Length of the rescheduling horizon | s |
| $c^{delay}$ | Unit cost of (weighted) passenger delay | – |
| $c^{energy}$ | Unit cost of energy consumption | – |
| $c^{cancel}$ | Penalty for cancelling train $i$ | – |
| $w_i$ | Weight (e.g., passenger volume) of train $i$ | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) | – |

**Assumptions on parameters**
- **[A4]** All times are expressed in seconds relative to the start of the rescheduling horizon.
- **[A5]** $t^{run}_{i,l,p}$ and $e_{i,l,p}$ are pre-computed offline from the train dynamics (traction/braking curves), so the model remains linear.
- **[A6]** The disruption window is known and fixed (deterministic disruption).

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetable (rescheduling) variables
| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,l,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $l$ |
| $y_{i,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ |
| $z_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |

### 3.2 Conflict-resolution (ordering) variables
| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\delta_{i,j,l}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $l$ |
| $\sigma_{i,l}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $l$ on the opposite (rerouted) track |

### 3.3 Auxiliary variables
| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\Delta_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $E_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ |
| $u_{i,l}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Entry time of train $i$ into segment $l$ |
| $v_{i,l}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Exit time of train $i$ from segment $l$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of passenger delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; c^{delay}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} w_i\,\Delta_{i,s}
\;+\; c^{energy}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} E_i
\;+\; c^{cancel}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} z_i
\tag{1}
$$

**Assumption [A7]:** Delay is measured at every station as the positive deviation from the nominal schedule; this is a standard proxy for passenger inconvenience.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay definition
$$
\Delta_{i,s} \;\ge\; a_{i,s} - T^{arr}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
\tag{2}
$$
$$
\Delta_{i,s} \;\ge\; 0, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
\tag{3}
$$

### 5.2 Segment running time (profile selection)
$$
v_{i,l} - u_{i,l} \;=\; \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_i} t^{run}_{i,l,p}\, x_{i,l,p}, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; l\in\mathcal{L}_i
\tag{4}
$$
$$
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_i} x_{i,l,p} \;=\; 1 - z_i, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; l\in\mathcal{L}_i
\tag{5}
$$

### 5.3 Running-time feasibility bounds
$$
t^{min}_{i,l}\big(1-z_i\big) \;\le\; v_{i,l} - u_{i,l} \;\le\; t^{max}_{i,l}\big(1-z_i\big), \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; l\in\mathcal{L}_i
\tag{6}
$$

### 5.4 Energy consumption
$$
E_i \;=\; \sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_i}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_i} e_{i,l,p}\, x_{i,l,p}, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T}
\tag{7}
$$

### 5.5 Timetable continuity (linkage between stations and segments)
For each train $i$ and each consecutive station pair $(s,k)$ with $l=(s,k)\in\mathcal{L}_i$:
$$
u_{i,l} \;=\; d_{i,s}, \qquad v_{i,l} \;=\; a_{i,k}
\tag{8}
$$

### 5.6 Dwell-time constraints
$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\ge\; d^{min}_{i,s}\big(1-z_i\big), \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
\tag{9}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\le\; d^{max}_{i,s}\big(1-z_i\big), \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
\tag{10}
$$

### 5.7 Route selection
$$
\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_i} y_{i,r} \;=\; 1 - z_i, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T}
\tag{11}
$$

**Assumption [A8]:** Route $r$ determines whether train $i$ uses the opposite track on segments $l\in\mathcal{L}^B$. The mapping $r\mapsto\sigma_{i,l}$ is encoded linearly:
$$
\sigma_{i,l} \;=\; \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_i:\; l\in r^{opp}} y_{i,r}, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; l\in\mathcal{L}^B
\tag{12}
$$

### 5.8 Disruption window on blocked segments
Trains may not occupy a blocked track during the disruption window. For $l\in\mathcal{L}^B$:
$$
u_{i,l} \;\ge\; T^{b,end}_l - M\big(1-\sigma_{i,l}\big) - M z_i, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T}
\tag{13}
$$
$$
v_{i,l} \;\le\; T^{b,start}_l + M\,\sigma_{i,l} + M z_i, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T}
\tag{14}
$$

**Interpretation:** If train $i$ uses the blocked track ($\sigma_{i,l}=0$) and is not cancelled, it must traverse the segment entirely outside $[T^{b,start}_l, T^{b,end}_l]$.

### 5.9 Rerouting capacity: at most one train on the opposite track at a time
For $l\in\mathcal{L}^B$, for each conflicting pair $(i,j)\in\mathcal{K}_l$:
$$
u_{j,l} \;\ge\; v_{i,l} + \tau_l - M\big(1-\delta_{i,j,l}\big) - M z_i - M z_j
\tag{15}
$$
$$
u_{i,l} \;\ge\; v_{j,l} + \tau_l - M\,\delta_{i,j,l} - M z_i - M z_j
\tag{16}
$$
$$
\delta_{i,j,l} + \delta_{j,i,l} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall (i,j)\in\mathcal{K}_l
\tag{17}
$$

**Assumption [A9]:** Constraints (15)–(17) enforce a minimum headway $\tau_l$ between any two consecutive trains on the same physical track, regardless of direction. This is the key bidirectional conflict-resolution constraint.

### 5.10 Same-direction headway on unaffected segments
For $l\in\mathcal{L}\setminus\mathcal{L}^B$ and $(i,j)\in\mathcal{K}_l$ with $i,j$ in the same direction:
$$
u_{j,l} \;\ge\; v_{i,l} + \tau_l - M\big(1-\delta_{i,j,l}\big) - M z_i - M z_j
\tag{18}
$$
$$
u_{i,l} \;\ge\; v_{j,l} + \tau_l - M\,\delta_{i,j,l} - M z_i - M z_j
\tag{19}
$$

### 5.11 Opposite-direction separation on unaffected segments
For $l\in\mathcal{L}\setminus\mathcal{L}^B$ with $i\in\mathcal{T}^{up}$, $j\in\mathcal{T}^{dn}$ (independent tracks):
$$
\delta_{i,j,l} \;=\; 1, \qquad \delta_{j,i,l} \;=\; 0
\tag{20}
$$
**[A10]:** On double-track segments outside the disruption area, up and down trains do not interfere; this is encoded by fixing the ordering.

### 5.12 Cancellation consistency
If $z_i=1$, all timing variables for train $i$ are released:
$$
a_{i,s} \;\le\; M(1-z_i), \qquad d_{i,s} \;\le\; M(1-z_i), \qquad \forall s\in\mathcal{S}
\tag{21}
$$
$$
u_{i,l} \;\le\; M(1-z_i), \qquad v_{i,l} \;\le\; M(1-z_i), \qquad \forall l\in\mathcal{L}_i
\tag{22}
$$

### 5.13 Horizon and non-negativity
$$
0 \;\le\; a_{i,s},\; d_{i,s},\; u_{i,l},\; v_{i,l},\; \Delta_{i,s},\; E_i \;\le\; H
\tag{23}
$$
$$
x_{i,l,p},\; y_{i,r},\; \delta_{i,j,l},\; \sigma_{i,l},\; z_i \;\in\;\{0,1\}
\tag{24}
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & (1) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & (2)-(24)
\end{aligned}
}
$$

The model is a **mixed-integer linear program** because:
- All objective terms and constraints are linear in the decision variables.
- Binary variables handle profile selection, route selection, ordering, and cancellation.
- Continuous variables represent times and energy.

---

## 7. Key Modeling Assumptions (Consolidated)

| ID | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Single two-track line; partial blockage removes one track in $\mathcal{L}^B$ during the disruption window. |
| A2 | Fixed origin/destination per train; only intermediate routing may change. |
| A3 | Speed profiles discretized into finite modes with pre-computed time/energy. |
| A4 | All times relative to rescheduling horizon start. |
| A5 | Profile time/energy pre-computed offline; model remains linear. |
| A6 | Disruption window deterministic and known. |
| A7 | Delay measured at every station as positive deviation from nominal. |
| A8 | Route selection linearly maps to opposite-track usage on blocked segments. |
| A9 | Minimum headway $\tau_l$ enforced between any two consecutive trains on the same physical track, regardless of direction. |
| A10 | Up/down trains on unaffected double-track segments do not interfere. |

---

## 8. Remarks on the Integrated TRP–TSMP Coupling

- **Coupling mechanism:** Constraints (4)–(8) link the timetable (arrival/departure times) with the speed profiles (running times). This ensures that any rescheduled timetable is *executable* at the control level.
- **Bidirectional conflict resolution:** Constraints (15)–(17) and (20) handle the core challenge of rerouting under partial blockages, where up and down trains may share the same physical track inside $\mathcal{L}^B$.
- **Energy efficiency:** The objective (1) and constraint (7) embed energy consumption directly into the rescheduling decision, capturing the trade-off between accelerating to recover time and decelerating to save energy.
- **Decomposition potential:** The structure (train-level profile selection + segment-level ordering) is amenable to the decomposition-based solution method described in the introduction (IP reformulation + adaptive iterative algorithm + local branching).

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below we formulate a complete, linear mixed-integer program (MILP) inspired by the described TRSMP. The model integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed-profile management on a double-track high-speed railway, in the presence of a partial segment blockage (one track direction unavailable during a disruption time window). Where information is missing, we state explicit assumptions.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations (nodes), $s \in \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of track segments (links), $\ell = (s, s') \in \mathcal{L}$ |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ | Set of disruption segments (partially blocked) |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, $i \in \mathcal{T}$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{up}} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Up-direction trains |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{down}} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Down-direction trains |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discretized speed levels / speed-profile modes, $k \in \mathcal{K}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of candidate speed profiles for train $i$ (each profile is a sequence of running times per segment) |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of routes (tracks) on a segment: $\mathcal{R}=\{\text{main},\text{opp}\}$ (main = scheduled direction, opp = opposite track used under rerouting) |
| $\mathcal{H}$ | Set of discretized time steps (slots), $h \in \mathcal{H}$ |
| $\mathcal{W} \subset \mathcal{H}$ | Disruption time window (slots during which the blocked side is unavailable) |

---

## 2. Assumptions (marked where reasonable)

- **(A1)** The network is a linear corridor of stations connected by segments; each segment is double-track (one track per direction).
- **(A2)** A partial blockage makes **one direction's track unavailable** on segment $\ell \in \mathcal{D}$ during window $\mathcal{W}$; the opposite track remains usable, permitting bidirectional (single-track) operation with strict headway separation.
- **(A3)** Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set $\mathcal{P}_i$ per train; each profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ specifies the running time $r_{i\ell p}$ on each segment $\ell$ (assumption: profiles are precomputed and satisfy traction/braking physics, so the model remains linear).
- **(A4)** Minimum headway times $H^{\text{dep}}$, $H^{\text{arr}}$, $H^{\text{seg}}$ are given constants for safe separation.
- **(A5)** Dwell times are bounded: $d^{\min}_i \le d_{is} \le d^{\max}_i$.
- **(A6)** Cancellation is allowed at a penalty cost $C^{\text{cancel}}_i$.
- **(A7)** Trains cannot overtake on a segment; ordering is determined by departure order from a station (reordering is permitted at stations).
- **(A8)** Energy consumption of profile $p$ for train $i$ is a known constant $E_{ip}$ (precomputed from the profile).
- **(A9)** All times are discretized to integer slots; the planning horizon is $[0, T^{\max}]$.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Scheduling variables
- $a_{is} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$.
- $x_{i\ell p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on segment $\ell$.
- $y_{i\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $\ell$.
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **cancelled**.
- $\delta_{ij\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable = 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $\ell$ (same direction).

### 3.2 Conflict / capacity variables (for bidirectional shared track)
- $\alpha_{ij\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ enters segment $\ell$ before train $j$ when both use the same physical track (opposite directions or same direction).

### 3.3 Time-slot occupancy variables
- $u_{i\ell h} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $\ell$ during slot $h$.

### 3.4 Auxiliary
- $M$: sufficiently large constant (big-M).

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, cancellation, and rerouting penalty:

$$
\min \; Z =
w_1 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \big( a_{is} - A^{\text{sch}}_{is} \big)^+ 
+ w_2 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} E_{ip}\, x_{i\ell p}
+ w_3 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} C^{\text{cancel}}_i z_i
+ w_4 \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{D}} C^{\text{rer}} y_{i\ell}
$$

where $(a_{is}-A^{\text{sch}}_{is})^+ = \max(0, a_{is}-A^{\text{sch}}_{is})$ is linearized via auxiliary variable $\theta_{is} \ge a_{is} - A^{\text{sch}}_{is}$, $\theta_{is} \ge 0$, and $A^{\text{sch}}_{is}$ is the scheduled arrival time. Weights $w_1,\dots,w_4 \ge 0$ trade off delay, energy, cancellation, and rerouting.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay linearization
$$
\theta_{is} \ge a_{is} - A^{\text{sch}}_{is}, \qquad \theta_{is} \ge 0 \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.2 Profile selection (one profile per segment)
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_{i\ell p} = 1 - z_i \quad \forall i, \ell
$$

### 5.3 Running time consistency
Let $\ell = (s, s')$. Then
$$
a_{is'} - d_{is} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_{i\ell p}\, x_{i\ell p} \quad \forall i, \ell=(s,s')
$$

### 5.4 Dwell time bounds
$$
d^{\min}_i (1 - z_i) \le d_{is} - a_{is} \le d^{\max}_i (1 - z_i) \quad \forall i, s \notin \{s^{\text{orig}}_i, s^{\text{dest}}_i\}
$$

### 5.5 Origin / destination timing
$$
d_{i, s^{\text{orig}}_i} \ge D^{\text{orig}}_i (1 - z_i), \qquad a_{i, s^{\text{dest}}_i} \le T^{\max} \quad \forall i
$$

### 5.6 Cancellation consistency
$$
a_{is} \le M (1 - z_i), \quad d_{is} \le M (1 - z_i) \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.7 Disruption window constraints (partial blockage)
For each disrupted segment $\ell \in \mathcal{D}$ and the **blocked direction** trains (say $i \in \mathcal{T}^{\text{blocked}}_\ell$):
- If train $i$ is not rerouted, it may not enter $\ell$ during $\mathcal{W}$:
$$
u_{i\ell h} \le y_{i\ell} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}^{\text{blocked}}_\ell, \; h \in \mathcal{W}
$$
- Rerouting only allowed on disrupted segments:
$$
y_{i\ell} = 0 \quad \forall i, \ell \notin \mathcal{D}
$$

### 5.8 Segment occupancy definition
$$
h \cdot u_{i\ell h} \le a_{is'} \quad \text{and} \quad h \cdot u_{i\ell h} \ge d_{is} - M(1-u_{i\ell h}) \quad \forall i, \ell=(s,s'), h
$$
(Occupancy indicator: $u_{i\ell h}=1$ iff train $i$ is on segment $\ell$ during slot $h$.)

### 5.9 Same-direction headway (per physical track)
For $i, j \in \mathcal{T}^{\text{dir}}$, $\ell=(s,s')$, same physical track:
$$
d_{js} \ge d_{is} + H^{\text{dep}} - M(1 - \delta_{ij\ell}) - M(z_i + z_j)
$$
$$
d_{is} \ge d_{js} + H^{\text{dep}} - M\,\delta_{ij\ell} - M(z_i + z_j)
$$
$$
\delta_{ij\ell} + \delta_{ji\ell} = 1 \quad \text{(if both active and same track)}
$$

### 5.10 Bidirectional conflict on shared (opposite) track
If train $i$ is rerouted onto the opposite track of $\ell$ and train $j$ (opposite direction) uses that same physical track, then:
$$
d_{js} \ge a_{is'} + H^{\text{seg}} - M(1 - \alpha_{ij\ell}) - M(2 - y_{i\ell} - y_{j\ell})
$$
$$
d_{is} \ge a_{js'} + H^{\text{seg}} - M\,\alpha_{ij\ell} - M(2 - y_{i\ell} - y_{j\ell})
$$
$$
\alpha_{ij\ell} + \alpha_{ji\ell} = 1 \quad \text{when both share the track}
$$

### 5.11 No overtaking on a segment (same direction)
If $\delta_{ij\ell}=1$ and both use the same track, then arrival order is preserved:
$$
a_{is'} \le a_{js'} + M(1 - \delta_{ij\ell}) + M(z_i + z_j)
$$

### 5.12 Track capacity per slot (mutual exclusion on a physical track)
For each physical track $\rho \in \{\text{up-track}, \text{down-track}\}$ on segment $\ell$:
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}_\rho(\ell)} u_{i\ell h} \le 1 \quad \forall \ell, h
$$
where $\mathcal{T}_\rho(\ell)$ is the set of trains assigned to physical track $\rho$ (either by direction or by rerouting).

### 5.13 Rerouting assignment consistency
$$
y_{i\ell} = 1 \Rightarrow \text{train } i \text{ uses opposite track on } \ell
$$
This is enforced implicitly through 5.12 by defining $\mathcal{T}_\rho(\ell)$ based on $y_{i\ell}$.

### 5.14 Variable domains
$$
a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0; \quad \theta_{is} \ge 0; \quad x_{i\ell p}, y_{i\ell}, z_i, \delta_{ij\ell}, \alpha_{ij\ell}, u_{i\ell h} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = w_1 \sum_{i,s} \theta_{is} + w_2 \sum_{i,\ell,p} E_{ip} x_{i\ell p} + w_3 \sum_i C^{\text{cancel}}_i z_i + w_4 \sum_{i,\ell \in \mathcal{D}} C^{\text{rer}} y_{i\ell} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & (5.1)\text{--}(5.14)
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Model Properties and Remarks

- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear; the only nonlinearity (delay penalty, occupancy logic, conflict disjunctions) is handled via big-M and indicator variables.
- **Integration:** The model simultaneously decides retiming ($a_{is}, d_{is}$), reordering ($\delta_{ij\ell}$), rerouting ($y_{i\ell}$), cancellation ($z_i$), and speed profiles ($x_{i\ell p}$), aligning timetable positions with executable speed profiles via constraint (5.3).
- **Conflict-free guarantee:** Constraints (5.9)–(5.12) ensure safe separation in both same-direction and bidirectional (rerouted) operations.
- **Disruption handling:** Constraint (5.7) enforces the partial blockage; rerouting is the only way for blocked-direction trains to traverse $\mathcal{D}$ during $\mathcal{W}$.
- **Decomposition hint (as in the paper):** The MILP can be decomposed into (i) an integer programming master over $(\delta, \alpha, y, z)$ capturing train interactions, and (ii) per-train subproblems over $(a, d, x, u)$ — enabling the adaptive iterative algorithm described in the source.

This formulation provides a complete, self-contained MILP for the TRSMP under partial segment blockages, ready for implementation in a standard solver (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) or for the decomposition-based solution framework outlined in the paper.

# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

I select **Model 2** as the best formulation. It is the most complete and rigorous: it explicitly linearizes the shared-track indicator $\sigma_{i,j,g}$, cleanly separates same-direction ordering (C9) from bidirectional conflict (C10), and provides a fully linear MILP with no residual nonlinearities. Below is the complete model.

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions (marked ⚠️ where data was missing)

- **⚠️ A1** Stations indexed $s=1,\dots,|S|$; segment $g_s$ connects $s$ to $s+1$.
- **⚠️ A2** Each train $i$ has fixed origin $s^o_i$ and destination $s^d_i$; it traverses only segments between them.
- **⚠️ A3** The "opposite track" of a segment is a single physical track shared by both directions when rerouting occurs. Rerouting is permitted only on the blocked segment.
- **⚠️ A4** Speed profiles are precomputed per (train, segment, mode) with known run time and energy; the MILP selects among them.
- **⚠️ A5** Headway $h$ is identical for all trains and both directions.
- **⚠️ A6** Weights $w^D$ (delay) and $w^E$ (energy), both $\geq 0$.
- **⚠️ A7** $M$ is a sufficiently large constant (e.g., planning-horizon length).
- **⚠️ A8** "Precedes" on a segment means the earlier train clears the segment before the later enters (block-headway model).
- **⚠️ A9** Disruption window $[block\_start, block\_end]$ applies to blocked segment $g^*$ and blocked direction $d^*$.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ | Trains |
| $s \in \mathcal{S}$ | Stations, ordered along the line |
| $g \in \mathcal{G}$ | Segments between consecutive stations |
| $k \in \mathcal{K}$ | Discretized speed-profile modes |
| $d(i) \in \{up, down\}$ | Direction of train $i$ |
| $g^* \in \mathcal{G}$ | Blocked segment |
| $d^* \in \{up, down\}$ | Blocked direction |

Let $\mathcal{T}^{d} = \{i : d(i)=d\}$.

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $sched\_arr_{i,s},\ sched\_dep_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure |
| $min\_dwell_{i,s},\ max\_dwell_{i,s}$ | Dwell bounds |
| $min\_run_{i,g},\ max\_run_{i,g}$ | Running-time bounds |
| $h$ | Minimum safety headway |
| $block\_start,\ block\_end$ | Disruption window |
| $energy_{i,g,k}$ | Energy of train $i$ on segment $g$ with profile $k$ |
| $run\_time_{i,g,k}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $g$ with profile $k$ |
| $w^{D},\ w^{E}$ | Objective weights |
| $M$ | Large constant |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $arr_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival time |
| $dep_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual departure time |
| $x_{i,g,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses profile $k$ on segment $g$ |
| $r_{i,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes on segment $g$ |
| $y_{i,j,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$ |
| $\sigma_{i,j,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $i,j$ share a physical track on $g$ |
| $delay_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay at station $s$ |
| $E_{i,g}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy on segment $g$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min\ Z = w^{D}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} delay_{i,s}
\;+\; w^{E}\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{g \in \mathcal{G}} E_{i,g}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### (C1) Arrival–Departure Linkage (Dwell)
For all $i \in \mathcal{T}$, $s \in \mathcal{S}$ (with $s \neq s^{d}_i$):
$$
dep_{i,s} \geq arr_{i,s} + min\_dwell_{i,s} \tag{C1a}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} \leq arr_{i,s} + max\_dwell_{i,s} \tag{C1b}
$$

### (C2) Running Time on Segment
For each $i \in \mathcal{T}$ and segment $g=(s,s+1)$ traversed by $i$:
$$
arr_{i,s+1} - dep_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} run\_time_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k} \tag{C2}
$$

### (C3) Speed-Profile Selection
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{i,g,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\ g \in \mathcal{G} \tag{C3}
$$

### (C4) Speed-Profile Feasibility
Only profiles satisfying physical limits are included in $\mathcal{K}$:
$$
min\_run_{i,g} \leq run\_time_{i,g,k} \leq max\_run_{i,g} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{C4}
$$
*(Enforced by preprocessing: infeasible $k$ are removed.)*

### (C5) Energy Definition
$$
E_{i,g} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} energy_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\ g \in \mathcal{G} \tag{C5}
$$

### (C6) Delay Definition
For all $i \in \mathcal{T}$, $s \in \mathcal{S}$:
$$
delay_{i,s} \geq arr_{i,s} - sched\_arr_{i,s} \tag{C6a}
$$
$$
delay_{i,s} \geq dep_{i,s} - sched\_dep_{i,s} \tag{C6b}
$$
$$
delay_{i,s} \geq 0 \tag{C6c}
$$

### (C7) Disruption / Blockage Handling
For the blocked segment $g^*$ and blocked direction $d^*$:

- If train $i \in \mathcal{T}^{d^*}$ traverses $g^*$ during the disruption window, it **must** reroute:
$$
r_{i,g^*} \geq 1 - \frac{\max(0,\; dep_{i,s^*} - block\_end) + \max(0,\; block\_start - arr_{i,s^*+1})}{M} \tag{C7a}
$$
- Trains in the **non-blocked** direction on $g^*$ cannot reroute:
$$
r_{i,g^*} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \mathcal{T}^{d^*} \tag{C7b}
$$
- Rerouting is only allowed on $g^*$:
$$
r_{i,g} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\ g \neq g^* \tag{C7c}
$$

### (C8) Rerouting Capacity / Shared-Track Headway
Define the shared-track indicator (linearized):
$$
\sigma_{i,j,g} \geq r_{i,g} + r_{j,g} - 1 \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,j,g} \leq r_{i,g},\quad \sigma_{i,j,g} \leq r_{j,g} \tag{C8b}
$$
Enforce headway on shared track:
$$
arr_{j,s+1} \geq dep_{i,s} + h - M(1 - y_{i,j,g}) - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,g}) \tag{C8c}
$$
$$
arr_{i,s+1} \geq dep_{j,s} + h - M\, y_{i,j,g} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,g}) \tag{C8d}
$$

### (C9) Ordering on Same Track (Same Direction)
For $i, j \in \mathcal{T}^{d}$ with $d(i)=d(j)$, on segment $g=(s,s+1)$:
$$
y_{i,j,g} + y_{j,i,g} = 1 \tag{C9a}
$$
$$
arr_{j,s+1} \geq dep_{i,s} + h - M(1 - y_{i,j,g}) \tag{C9b}
$$
$$
arr_{i,s+1} \geq dep_{j,s} + h - M\, y_{i,j,g} \tag{C9c}
$$

### (C10) Bidirectional Conflict on Shared (Rerouted) Track
For $i \in \mathcal{T}^{d^*}$ (rerouted) and $j \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \mathcal{T}^{d^*}$ (opposite direction) on $g^*$:
$$
arr_{j,s^*+1} \geq dep_{i,s^*} + h - M(1 - y_{i,j,g^*}) - M(1 - r_{i,g^*}) \tag{C10a}
$$
$$
arr_{i,s^*+1} \geq dep_{j,s^*} + h - M\, y_{i,j,g^*} - M(1 - r_{i,g^*}) \tag{C10b}
$$

### (C11) Rerouting Only During Disruption Window
If $r_{i,g^*}=1$, the train's traversal of $g^*$ must overlap $[block\_start, block\_end]$:
$$
dep_{i,s^*} \leq block\_end + M(1 - r_{i,g^*}) \tag{C11a}
$$
$$
arr_{i,s^*+1} \geq block\_start - M(1 - r_{i,g^*}) \tag{C11b}
$$

### (C12) Domains
$$
arr_{i,s},\ dep_{i,s},\ delay_{i,s},\ E_{i,g} \geq 0 \tag{C12a}
$$
$$
x_{i,g,k},\ r_{i,g},\ y_{i,j,g},\ \sigma_{i,j,g} \in \{0,1\} \tag{C12b}
$$

---

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

**Objective.** Weighted sum of total passenger delay and total traction energy; weights $w^D, w^E$ let the dispatcher trade punctuality against energy efficiency.

**Retiming (C1–C2).** Dwell constraints enforce realistic stops; (C2) links arrival to departure plus the selected running time — the retiming mechanism.

**Speed Management (C3–C5).** Binary $x_{i,g,k}$ selects exactly one precomputed profile per segment, jointly optimizing speed and energy without nonlinear dynamics.

**Delay Accounting (C6).** Delay is the positive part of deviation from schedule at both arrival and departure.

**Disruption & Rerouting (C7, C11).** The blocked segment/direction is unusable during the window; affected trains are forced to reroute, restricted to $g^*$ and required to overlap the window.

**Ordering & Headway (C8–C10).** Same-direction ordering via $y_{i,j,g}$; shared-track headway via $\sigma_{i,j,g}$; explicit bidirectional conflict handling for rerouted trains meeting opposite-direction traffic.

**MILP Structure.** All constraints are linear; the only nonlinearity (product $r_{i,g}r_{j,g}$) is linearized by $\sigma_{i,j,g}$. The model is a standard MILP solvable by CPLEX/Gurobi/SCIP.

**Model Size.** Dominant complexity is $O(|\mathcal{T}|^2|\mathcal{G}|)$ from ordering and shared-track binaries — typical for train rescheduling MILPs and tractable for realistic instances with warm starts.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# A Complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with double-track (bidirectional) operation, comprising a set of stations and segments between consecutive stations. A partial segment blockage occurs on one track of a segment during a known disruption time window. Affected trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track within that window, but bidirectional trains sharing the same track must be conflict-free.

**Assumptions (marked as such where information is not explicitly given):**

- **(A1)** The line is discretized into a set of *segments* $e \in \mathcal{E}$ connecting consecutive stations; each segment has length $L_e$ and free-run travel time $T_e^{\text{free}}$ (assumed constant for all trains, or train-specific $T_{e,k}^{\text{free}}$ if heterogeneous rolling stock is considered).
- **(A2)** Time is discretized into a uniform grid of intervals of length $\Delta t$ (e.g., 1 s or 5 s), indexed by $t \in \mathcal{T} = \{0,1,\dots,|\mathcal{T}|-1\}$. All times (arrival, departure, entry/exit of block sections) are integer multiples of $\Delta t$.
- **(A3)** Each segment is divided into a fixed number of *block sections* $b \in \mathcal{B}_e$; at most one train may occupy a block section at any time (blocking-time safety).
- **(A4)** Speed profiles are represented by piecewise-constant speed levels $v \in \mathcal{V}$ (a finite set of admissible speeds, e.g., $\{0, 80, 120, 160, 200, 250, 300\}$ km/h), with corresponding traction energy consumption rates $c_v$ (per unit time) and braking/acceleration transitions captured by minimum transition times $\tau_{v,v'}$ between consecutive speed levels (assumed precomputed from train dynamics).
- **(A5)** The disruption is defined by a segment $\hat{e}$, a track side $\sigma \in \{\text{up},\text{down}\}$, and a time window $[t^{\text{dis}}_0, t^{\text{dis}}_1]$ during which that track side of $\hat{e}$ is blocked.
- **(A6)** Rerouting is only permitted on the disrupted segment $\hat{e}$: trains may use the opposite track within the disruption window; outside the window, normal directional operation applies.
- **(A7)** Train service cancellation is not considered (all trains must complete their journeys); this can be relaxed by adding a cancellation binary variable.
- **(A8)** Dwell times at stations are bounded: $d^{\min}_{i,k} \le d_{i,k} \le d^{\max}_{i,k}$.
- **(A9)** The objective is a weighted sum of total passenger delay and total traction energy consumption.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations along the line, indexed by $i$ (ordered $0,1,\dots,|\mathcal{S}|-1$) |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $e$; segment $e_i$ connects station $i$ to $i+1$ |
| $\mathcal{B}_e$ | Set of block sections in segment $e$, indexed by $b$ |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Set of admissible speed levels, indexed by $v$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time intervals, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{K}^{\text{aff}}$ | Subset of trains affected by the disruption |
| $\sigma \in \{\text{up},\text{down}\}$ | Track direction indicator |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetable (Rescheduling) Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,k}$ | integer (time) | Arrival time of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $d_{i,k}$ | integer (time) | Departure time of train $k$ from station $i$ |
| $x_{e,k}$ | binary | $=1$ if train $k$ traverses segment $e$ on the **opposite** (rerouted) track |
| $y_{e,k,k'}$ | binary | $=1$ if train $k$ precedes train $k'$ on segment $e$ (ordering variable) |

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $z_{e,b,k,v}$ | binary | $=1$ if train $k$ traverses block $b$ of segment $e$ at speed level $v$ |
| $u_{e,b,k}$ | integer (time) | Entry time of train $k$ into block $b$ of segment $e$ |
| $w_{e,b,k}$ | integer (time) | Exit time of train $k$ from block $b$ of segment $e$ |
| $\delta_{e,b,k,v,v'}$ | binary | $=1$ if train $k$ transitions from speed $v$ to $v'$ between consecutive blocks (or within segment) |

### 3.3 Conflict and Rerouting Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\alpha_{e,k,k'}$ | binary | $=1$ if trains $k$ and $k'$ use the **same track side** on segment $e$ (i.e., both normal or both rerouted) |
| $\beta_{e,k,k'}$ | binary | $=1$ if trains $k$ and $k'$ use **opposite track sides** on segment $e$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay and total energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\lambda_{\text{delay}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{S}} \left( a_{i,k} - a_{i,k}^{\text{sch}} \right)^+}_{\text{total passenger delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\lambda_{\text{energy}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}_e} \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} c_v \cdot \frac{L_{e,b}}{v} \cdot z_{e,b,k,v}}_{\text{total traction energy}}
$$

where $(\cdot)^+ = \max(\cdot, 0)$, $a_{i,k}^{\text{sch}}$ is the scheduled arrival time, $L_{e,b}$ is the length of block $b$ in segment $e$, and $\lambda_{\text{delay}}, \lambda_{\text{energy}} \ge 0$ are weighting parameters.

**Linearization of delay:** Introduce auxiliary variables $\theta_{i,k} \ge 0$ with

$$
\theta_{i,k} \ge a_{i,k} - a_{i,k}^{\text{sch}}, \quad \theta_{i,k} \ge 0
$$

so the objective becomes linear:

$$
\min \; Z = \lambda_{\text{delay}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{S}} \theta_{i,k} + \lambda_{\text{energy}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}_e} \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} c_v \cdot \frac{L_{e,b}}{v} \cdot z_{e,b,k,v}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Feasibility

**(C1) Arrival–departure consistency at stations:**

$$
d_{i,k} \ge a_{i,k} + d^{\min}_{i,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

$$
d_{i,k} \le a_{i,k} + d^{\max}_{i,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**(C2) Segment running time consistency:**

For each train $k$ and segment $e_i$ between stations $i$ and $i+1$:

$$
a_{i+1,k} - d_{i,k} = \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}_{e_i}} \left( w_{e_i,b,k} - u_{e_i,b,k} \right)
$$

**(C3) Block entry–exit consistency:**

$$
w_{e,b,k} = u_{e,b,k} + \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \frac{L_{e,b}}{v} \cdot z_{e,b,k,v}, \quad \forall e, b, k
$$

**(C4) Block sequencing within a segment:**

$$
u_{e,b+1,k} = w_{e,b,k}, \quad \forall e, \; b = 1,\dots,|\mathcal{B}_e|-1, \; k
$$

**(C5) Segment entry/exit linking to timetable:**

$$
u_{e_i,1,k} = d_{i,k}, \quad w_{e_i,|\mathcal{B}_{e_i}|,k} = a_{i+1,k}, \quad \forall i, k
$$

**(C6) Speed selection (exactly one speed per block):**

$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} z_{e,b,k,v} = 1, \quad \forall e, b, k
$$

**(C7) Speed transition feasibility (acceleration/braking limits):**

$$
\delta_{e,b,k,v,v'} \ge z_{e,b,k,v} + z_{e,b+1,k,v'} - 1, \quad \forall e, b, k, v, v'
$$

$$
u_{e,b+1,k} - w_{e,b,k} \ge \tau_{v,v'} \cdot \delta_{e,b,k,v,v'}, \quad \forall e, b, k, v, v'
$$

**(C8) Minimum/maximum speed bounds (infrastructure):**

$$
z_{e,b,k,v} = 0, \quad \forall v > v^{\max}_{e,b}, \; e, b, k
$$

### 5.2 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

**(C9) Disruption window blocking (normal track unusable):**

If train $k$ would traverse segment $\hat{e}$ on the normal track during $[t^{\text{dis}}_0, t^{\text{dis}}_1]$, it must either reroute or wait:

$$
u_{\hat{e},b,k} \ge t^{\text{dis}}_1 \quad \text{OR} \quad x_{\hat{e},k} = 1, \quad \forall b \in \mathcal{B}_{\hat{e}}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}^{\text{aff}}
$$

Linearized via big-$M$:

$$
u_{\hat{e},b,k} \ge t^{\text{dis}}_1 - M \cdot x_{\hat{e},k}, \quad \forall b, k \in \mathcal{K}^{\text{aff}}
$$

**(C10) Rerouting only on disrupted segment:**

$$
x_{e,k} = 0, \quad \forall e \neq \hat{e}, \; k
$$

**(C11) Rerouting binary definition (only affected trains may reroute):**

$$
x_{\hat{e},k} = 0, \quad \forall k \notin \mathcal{K}^{\text{aff}}
$$

### 5.3 Conflict-Free Operation (Bidirectional Safety)

**(C12) Track side assignment:**

For any pair of trains $k, k'$ on segment $e$:

$$
\alpha_{e,k,k'} + \beta_{e,k,k'} = 1
$$

where $\alpha_{e,k,k'} = 1$ if both use the same side, and $\beta_{e,k,k'} = 1$ if opposite sides.

**(C13) Same-side ordering (no overtaking within a block):**

If $\alpha_{e,k,k'} = 1$, then one train must fully precede the other in each block:

$$
w_{e,b,k} \le u_{e,b,k'} + M(1 - y_{e,k,k'}) + M(1 - \alpha_{e,k,k'}), \quad \forall e, b, k \neq k'
$$

$$
w_{e,b,k'} \le u_{e,b,k} + M \cdot y_{e,k,k'} + M(1 - \alpha_{e,k,k'}), \quad \forall e, b, k \neq k'
$$

**(C14) Opposite-side conflict (head-on prevention):**

If $\beta_{e,k,k'} = 1$ (opposite tracks), trains may cross but must not occupy the same block simultaneously:

$$
w_{e,b,k} \le u_{e,b,k'} + M(1 - \beta_{e,k,k'}) + M(1 - y_{e,k,k'}), \quad \forall e, b, k \neq k'
$$

$$
w_{e,b,k'} \le u_{e,b,k} + M \cdot y_{e,k,k'} + M(1 - \beta_{e,k,k'}), \quad \forall e, b, k \neq k'
$$

**(C15) Minimum headway between consecutive trains on same track:**

$$
u_{e,b,k'} - u_{e,b,k} \ge h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{e,k,k'}) - M(1 - \alpha_{e,k,k'}), \quad \forall e, b, k \neq k'
$$

where $h^{\min}$ is the minimum safety headway (assumed constant).

### 5.4 Station Capacity and Platform Constraints

**(C16) At most one train per platform track at a station:**

Assume each station $i$ has $P_i$ platform tracks. Introduce binary $\pi_{i,k,p} = 1$ if train $k$ uses platform $p$:

$$
\sum_{p=1}^{P_i} \pi_{i,k,p} = 1, \quad \forall i, k
$$

**(C17) No overlapping occupancy of the same platform:**

For any two trains $k, k'$ assigned to the same platform $p$:

$$
d_{i,k} \le a_{i,k'} + M(1 - \mu_{i,k,k'}) + M(2 - \pi_{i,k,p} - \pi_{i,k',p})
$$

$$
d_{i,k'} \le a_{i,k} + M \cdot \mu_{i,k,k'} + M(2 - \pi_{i,k,p} - \pi_{i,k',p})
$$

where $\mu_{i,k,k'}$ is a binary ordering variable at station $i$.

### 5.5 Speed Profile Feasibility

**(C18) Speed consistency across segment boundaries:**

$$
z_{e_i,|\mathcal{B}_{e_i}|,k,v} = z_{e_{i+1},1,k,v'}, \quad \text{subject to } \tau_{v,v'} \text{ feasible}
$$

(If the train stops at station $i+1$, then $v = v' = 0$ at the boundary.)

**(C19) Dwell time consistency with speed zero:**

If train $k$ dwells at station $i$, then:

$$
z_{e_i,|\mathcal{B}_{e_i}|,k,0} = 1 \quad \text{and} \quad z_{e_{i+1},1,k,0} = 1
$$

**(C20) Energy consumption linearization (already embedded in objective):**

Energy per block $b$ at speed $v$ is $E_{e,b,v} = c_v \cdot \frac{L_{e,b}}{v}$, precomputed.

### 5.6 Domain Constraints

$$
a_{i,k}, d_{i,k}, u_{e,b,k}, w_{e,b,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}, \quad \forall i, e, b, k
$$

$$
x_{e,k}, y_{e,k,k'}, z_{e,b,k,v}, \delta_{e,b,k,v,v'}, \alpha_{e,k,k'}, \beta_{e,k,k'}, \pi_{i,k,p}, \mu_{i,k,k'} \in \{0,1\}
$$

$$
\theta_{i,k} \ge 0, \quad \forall i, k
$$

---

## 6. Complete MILP Formulation (Summary)

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \lambda_{\text{delay}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{S}} \theta_{i,k} + \lambda_{\text{energy}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}_e} \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} c_v \cdot \frac{L_{e,b}}{v} \cdot z_{e,b,k,v} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C20)} \\
& \text{Domain constraints as specified in Section 5.6}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Model Properties and Remarks

- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear in the decision variables. The delay term is linearized via $\theta_{i,k}$. The energy term is linear because $z_{e,b,k,v}$ is binary and $c_v L_{e,b}/v$ is a precomputed constant.
- **Conflict-free guarantee:** Constraints (C13)–(C15) ensure that no two trains occupy the same block on the same track simultaneously, and that headways are respected.
- **Rerouting flexibility:** Constraint (C9) allows trains to either wait until the disruption window ends or reroute to the opposite track, capturing the core operational strategy.
- **Coupling of TRP and TSMP:** The linking constraints (C2)–(C5) explicitly connect timetable variables ($a, d$) with speed management variables ($u, w, z$), ensuring that the rescheduled timetable is executable at the control level.
- **Computational complexity:** The model is NP-hard (contains the train ordering problem as a subproblem). The decomposition approach described in the paper (IP reformulation + adaptive iterative algorithm) is recommended for large instances.
- **Assumption on discretization:** The time grid $\Delta t$ must be fine enough to capture speed transitions accurately; a finer grid improves fidelity at the cost of more variables.

---

## 8. Notation Summary Table

| Category | Symbols |
|---|---|
| Sets | $\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{S}, \mathcal{E}, \mathcal{B}_e, \mathcal{V}, \mathcal{T}$ |
| Timetable vars | $a_{i,k}, d_{i,k}, x_{e,k}, y_{e,k,k'}$ |
| Speed vars | $z_{e,b,k,v}, u_{e,b,k}, w_{e,b,k}, \delta_{e,b,k,v,v'}$ |
| Conflict vars | $\alpha_{e,k,k'}, \beta_{e,k,k'}$ |
| Station vars | $\pi_{i,k,p}, \mu_{i,k,k'}$ |
| Auxiliary | $\theta_{i,k}$ |
| Parameters | $L_e, L_{e,b}, T_e^{\text{free}}, c_v, \tau_{v,v'}, h^{\min}, d^{\min}_{i,k}, d^{\max}_{i,k}, t^{\text{dis}}_0, t^{\text{dis}}_1, \lambda_{\text{delay}}, \lambda_{\text{energy}}, M$ |

This formulation provides a complete, self-contained MILP for the integrated train rescheduling and speed management problem under partial segment blockages, with explicit handling of bidirectional conflicts and rerouting strategies.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP

Below is the best complete linear model, synthesizing the strongest elements of the generated candidates: the clean disjunctive headway structure, explicit rerouting conflicts, disruption-window logic, speed-profile selection, and speed–position coupling.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations/segments, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of discretized positions along a segment, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{dis} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of disrupted segments |
| $\mathcal{T}^{up}, \mathcal{T}^{down}$ | Up- and down-direction trains ($\mathcal{T}^{up}\cup\mathcal{T}^{down}=\mathcal{T}$) |

---

## 2. Parameters

**Timetable / operations**

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $A^{sch}_{i,s},\ D^{sch}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains on the same track |
| $d^{min},\ d^{max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time |
| $t^{start},\ t^{end}$ | Start / end of the disruption time window |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $n_i$ | Number of passengers on train $i$ |

**Train physics (precomputed per speed level)**

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\tau_{i,s,k}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ at speed level $k$ |
| $E_{i,s,k}$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on segment $s$ at speed level $k$ |
| $t_{i,s,k,p}$ | Time to reach position $p$ on segment $s$ at speed level $k$ |

**Objective weights:** $w^{delay},\ w^{energy},\ w^{cancel}$.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $y_{i,j,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $v_{i,s,k}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $s$ |
| $e_{i,s}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $c_i$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\delta^{+}_{i,s},\ \delta^{-}_{i,s}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | Positive / negative deviation from scheduled arrival |
| $z_{i,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses disrupted segment $s$ before $t^{start}$ |
| $t_{i,s,p}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | Time train $i$ reaches position $p$ on segment $s$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z = w^{delay}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} n_i\big(\delta^{+}_{i,s}+\delta^{-}_{i,s}\big)
\;+\; w^{energy}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} e_{i,s}
\;+\; w^{cancel}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} n_i\, c_i
$$

Minimizes passenger-weighted schedule deviation, total traction energy, and passenger-weighted cancellations.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Arrival–departure ordering and dwell time
$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} + d^{min} - M c_i \qquad \forall i,s \tag{C1a}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \le a_{i,s} + d^{max} + M c_i \qquad \forall i,s \tag{C1b}
$$

### (C2) Segment running time (speed-profile dependent)
$$
a_{i,s+1} \ge d_{i,s} + \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \tau_{i,s,k}\, v_{i,s,k} - M c_i \qquad \forall i,s \tag{C2}
$$

### (C3) Speed-profile selection (exactly one level)
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} v_{i,s,k} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i,s \tag{C3}
$$

### (C4) Headway on shared track (ordering-based)
For all $i\neq j$, $s$:
$$
a_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h - M(1-y_{i,j,s}) - M c_i - M c_j \tag{C4a}
$$
$$
y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} \ge 1 - c_i - c_j \tag{C4b}
$$

### (C5) Rerouting and opposite-track conflicts
For $i\in\mathcal{T}^{up}$, $j\in\mathcal{T}^{down}$, $s$:
$$
a_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h - M(1-x_{i,s}) - M(1-x_{j,s}) - M c_i - M c_j \tag{C5a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \ge d_{j,s} + h - M(1-x_{i,s}) - M(1-x_{j,s}) - M c_i - M c_j \tag{C5b}
$$
When both trains are rerouted onto the same track, headway is enforced in both directions.

### (C6) Disruption window on blocked segments
For all $i$, $s\in\mathcal{S}^{dis}$:
$$
a_{i,s} \ge t^{end} - M x_{i,s} - M c_i - M(1-z_{i,s}) \tag{C6a}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \le t^{start} + M x_{i,s} + M c_i + M z_{i,s} \tag{C6b}
$$
A train may traverse a disrupted segment only before $t^{start}$, after $t^{end}$, or by rerouting.

### (C7) Energy consumption
$$
e_{i,s} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} E_{i,s,k}\, v_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall i,s \tag{C7a}
$$
$$
e_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i) \qquad \forall i,s \tag{C7b}
$$

### (C8) Cancellation coupling
$$
a_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i),\quad d_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i) \qquad \forall i,s \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
x_{i,s} \le 1-c_i,\quad v_{i,s,k} \le 1-c_i \qquad \forall i,s,k \tag{C8b}
$$

### (C9) Delay deviation definition
$$
a_{i,s} - A^{sch}_{i,s} = \delta^{+}_{i,s} - \delta^{-}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,s \tag{C9a}
$$
$$
\delta^{+}_{i,s},\ \delta^{-}_{i,s} \ge 0 \tag{C9b}
$$

### (C10) Speed–position coupling (discretized kinematics)
$$
t_{i,s,p} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} t_{i,s,k,p}\, v_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall i,s,p \tag{C10a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \le t_{i,s,p} \le d_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,s,p \tag{C10b}
$$

### (C11) Variable domains
$$
a_{i,s},d_{i,s},e_{i,s},\delta^{+}_{i,s},\delta^{-}_{i,s},t_{i,s,p}\ge 0
$$
$$
x_{i,s},y_{i,j,s},v_{i,s,k},c_i,z_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Component | Count |
|-----------|-------|
| Continuous variables | $5|\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{P}|$ |
| Binary variables | $|\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}|(2+|\mathcal{K}|) + |\mathcal{T}|^2|\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{T}|$ |
| Constraints | $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{T}|^2|\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{K}| + |\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{P}|)$ |

---

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

**Objective.** The three-term objective captures the classic disruption-management trade-off: passenger service quality (delay), operational cost (energy), and service availability (cancellations). Passenger counts $n_i$ weight delay and cancellation terms so high-occupancy trains are prioritized.

**Timing variables.** Continuous arrival/departure times allow fine-grained rescheduling. Dwell bounds (C1) prevent unrealistic stops; (C2) links consecutive segments through the chosen running time.

**Speed-profile selection.** Binary $v_{i,s,k}$ selects one of $|\mathcal{K}|$ precomputed speed levels per segment (C3), linearizing otherwise nonlinear train dynamics (traction, braking, resistance) into a tractable MILP.

**Headway and ordering.** (C4) enforces safe separation on shared track via a standard big-M disjunctive formulation; $y_{i,j,s}$ resolves ordering ambiguity and (C4b) prevents deadlock.

**Rerouting.** When a segment is blocked, trains may use the opposite track ($x_{i,s}=1$). (C5) then imposes headway between opposing-direction trains sharing that track, capturing the bidirectional conflict.

**Disruption window.** (C6) ensures no train traverses a disrupted segment during $[t^{start},t^{end}]$ unless rerouted or cancelled; auxiliary binary $z_{i,s}$ selects before/after traversal.

**Energy.** (C7) linearly maps the chosen speed level to energy via precomputed $E_{i,s,k}$, avoiding nonlinear traction equations while retaining physical fidelity.

**Cancellation.** Binary $c_i$ relaxes all timing constraints (via big-M) and zeroes routing, speed, and energy variables (C8), at a penalty in the objective.

**Speed–position coupling.** (C10) ties the discretized position trajectory to the selected speed profile, ensuring timing and kinematic plans are mutually consistent.

**Assumptions (marked).** (i) Speed levels are discretized; (ii) energy is linearized per level; (iii) the disruption window is fixed and known; (iv) the line is single-track bidirectional with rerouting to the opposite track; (v) resistance and traction limits are embedded in precomputed $\tau_{i,s,k}$ and $E_{i,s,k}$; (vi) dwell times are bounded but otherwise flexible.

# MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code, presented as equations with variables, objective function, and constraints.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed $s = 1,\dots,|S|$ (ordered along the line) |
| $G$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations, indexed $g = 1,\dots,|G|$, with $|G| = |S|-1$ |
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions, $d \in \{1,2\}$ (1 = forward/up, 2 = backward/down) |
| $K$ | Set of discretized speed levels, indexed $k, k'$ |
| $P$ | Set of discretized positions along the line, indexed $p$ |
| $G_b \subseteq G$ | Set of blocked segments during the disruption window |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\text{dir}_i$ | Direction of train $i$ |
| $\text{orig}_i,\ \text{dest}_i$ | Origin and destination stations of train $i$ |
| $t^{\text{dep}}_i,\ t^{\text{arr}}_i$ | Scheduled departure / arrival times of train $i$ |
| $\text{run}^{\min}_g,\ \text{run}^{\max}_g$ | Minimum / maximum running time over segment $g$ |
| $\text{dwell}^{\min}_s,\ \text{dwell}^{\max}_s$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $h$ | Minimum same-direction headway |
| $h^{\text{opp}}$ | Minimum opposite-direction headway (rerouting case) |
| $L_g$ | Length of segment $g$ |
| $v^{\max}$ | Maximum allowable train speed |
| $a^{\max},\ b^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration magnitudes |
| $E_k$ | Energy consumption rate at speed level $k$ |
| $v_k$ | Speed value of level $k$ |
| $L^{\text{step}}$ | Position grid step |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $t^{\text{start}},\ t^{\text{end}}$ | Start / end of the disruption time window |
| $\text{cap}_g$ | Capacity of segment $g$ |
| $\alpha,\ \beta,\ \gamma$ | Objective weights on delay, energy, cancellations |

---

## Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$ |
| $y_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $a_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $r_{i,g} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Running time of train $i$ over segment $g$ |
| $\text{dw}_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $z_{i,g,d}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $g$ using track of direction $d$ |
| $o_{i,j,g}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$ (same direction) |
| $u_{i,j,g}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ (dir 1) uses segment $g$ before train $j$ (dir 2) |
| $v_{i,p,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is at position $p$ with speed level $k$ |
| $\delta_i \ge 0$ | Continuous | Delay of train $i$ at destination |
| $e_i \ge 0$ | Continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ |
| $w_{i,g}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $g$ during the disruption window |

---

## Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, total energy consumption, and number of cancellations:

$$
\min\ Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in T} \delta_i \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in T} e_i \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in T} y_i
$$

---

## Constraints

### 1. Cancellation / Service Consistency

$$
y_i = 1 - x_{i,\text{orig}_i} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

$$
x_{i,s} \le x_{i,s-1} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \setminus \{\text{orig}_i, \text{dest}_i\}
$$

*(Monotone stopping pattern along the route.)*

### 2. Arrival / Departure Time Definition

$$
\text{dep}_{i,\text{orig}_i} \ge t^{\text{dep}}_i - M\,(1 - x_{i,\text{orig}_i}) \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

$$
a_{i,\text{dest}_i} \le t^{\text{arr}}_i + \delta_i + M\,(1 - x_{i,\text{dest}_i}) \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

$$
\delta_i \ge 0 \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

### 3. Running Time over Segments

$$
a_{i,g+1} = \text{dep}_{i,g} + r_{i,g} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

$$
\text{run}^{\min}_g \le r_{i,g} \le \text{run}^{\max}_g \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

### 4. Dwell Time

$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} = a_{i,s} + \text{dw}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \setminus \{\text{orig}_i, \text{dest}_i\}
$$

$$
\text{dwell}^{\min}_s\, x_{i,s} \le \text{dw}_{i,s} \le \text{dwell}^{\max}_s\, x_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \setminus \{\text{orig}_i, \text{dest}_i\}
$$

### 5. Time Ordering along Route

$$
a_{i,s} \le \text{dep}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$

$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \le a_{i,s+1} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \setminus \{|S|\}
$$

### 6. Disruption Window / Blocked Segment Constraints

Each train uses exactly one track per segment:

$$
z_{i,g,1} + z_{i,g,2} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

Window-overlap indicator (big-M lower bounds):

$$
w_{i,g} \ge \frac{t^{\text{end}} - \text{dep}_{i,g}}{M} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G_b
$$

$$
w_{i,g} \ge \frac{a_{i,g+1} - t^{\text{start}}}{M} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G_b
$$

Blocked track prohibition (must reroute during window):

$$
z_{i,g,\text{dir}_i} \le 1 - w_{i,g} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G_b
$$

### 7. Rerouting Capacity / Opposite-Direction Conflicts

For opposite-direction pairs $i$ (dir 1) and $j$ (dir 2) sharing the same physical track on segment $g$:

$$
\text{dep}_{i,g} \ge a_{j,g+1} + h^{\text{opp}} - M\,(1 - u_{i,j,g}) - M\,(2 - z_{i,g,2} - z_{j,g,2})
$$

$$
\text{dep}_{j,g} \ge a_{i,g+1} + h^{\text{opp}} - M\,u_{i,j,g} - M\,(2 - z_{i,g,2} - z_{j,g,2})
$$

### 8. Same-Direction Headway

For same-direction pairs $i, j$ on segment $g$ with direction $d = \text{dir}_i$:

$$
\text{dep}_{j,g} \ge a_{i,g+1} + h - M\,(1 - o_{i,j,g}) - M\,(2 - z_{i,g,d} - z_{j,g,d})
$$

$$
\text{dep}_{i,g} \ge a_{j,g+1} + h - M\,o_{i,j,g} - M\,(2 - z_{i,g,d} - z_{j,g,d})
$$

$$
o_{i,j,g} + o_{j,i,g} = 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j,\ \text{dir}_i = \text{dir}_j,\ g \in G
$$

### 9. Speed Profile / Position–Time Coupling

One speed level per position:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,p,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ p \in P
$$

Running time consistency with speed profile:

$$
\sum_{p \in g} \sum_{k \in K} \frac{L^{\text{step}}}{v_k}\, v_{i,p,k} = r_{i,g} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ g \in G
$$

Acceleration limit (linearized between adjacent positions):

$$
v_{k'}\, v_{i,p+1,k'} - v_k\, v_{i,p,k} \le a^{\max}\,\frac{L^{\text{step}}}{v_k} + M\,(1 - v_{i,p,k}) \qquad \forall i, p, k, k'
$$

Deceleration limit:

$$
v_k\, v_{i,p,k} - v_{k'}\, v_{i,p+1,k'} \le b^{\max}\,\frac{L^{\text{step}}}{v_k} + M\,(1 - v_{i,p,k}) \qquad \forall i, p, k, k'
$$

### 10. Energy Consumption

$$
e_i = \sum_{p \in P} \sum_{k \in K} E_k\, \frac{L^{\text{step}}}{v_k}\, v_{i,p,k} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

### 11. Speed Limits

$$
v_{i,p,k} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ p \in P,\ k \in K \text{ with } v_k > v^{\max}
$$

### 12. Domain Constraints

$$
x_{i,s},\ y_i,\ z_{i,g,d},\ o_{i,j,g},\ u_{i,j,g},\ v_{i,p,k},\ w_{i,g} \in \{0,1\}
$$

$$
a_{i,s},\ \text{dep}_{i,s},\ r_{i,g},\ \text{dw}_{i,s},\ \delta_i,\ e_i \ge 0
$$

---

## Assumptions (marked)

1. **Discretized position grid** with step $L^{\text{step}}$ and discrete speed levels $v_k$ are used to linearize the speed profile (assumption for MILP tractability).
2. **Energy consumption** is approximated as a piecewise-constant rate per speed level (assumption).
3. **Acceleration/deceleration limits** are approximated linearly between adjacent grid points (assumption).
4. Only **one disruption window** and one set of blocked segments is considered (assumption).
5. **Rerouting** is only allowed onto the opposite track of the same segment (local rerouting); no full alternative routes (assumption).
6. **Dwell times** are bounded by min/max values; if a train does not stop, dwell is zero (assumption).
7. **Cancellation** of a train removes all its downstream constraints via big-M (assumption).
8. **Headway values** are constant and direction-independent (assumption).
9. **Objective weights** $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are given by the operator (assumption).

messages.content: You convert the text of an optimization model into a structured record. Report only what the text states as mathematics, that is, objective functions, equations and inequalities written with symbols. Do not complete, repair, improve or invent anything.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

## Sets
- $S$ — ordered set of stations, $s \in S$
- $E$ — set of segments, $e = (s, s+1) \in E$
- $T$ — set of trains, $i \in T$
- $D$ — set of directions, $d \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$
- $K$ — set of discrete speed levels, $k \in K$
- $P$ — set of tracks per segment, $p \in \{\text{main}, \text{opposite}\}$
- $B \subseteq E$ — set of affected (disrupted) segments
- $\text{SameDir}(i,j)$ — same-direction train pairs
- $\text{OppDir}(i,j)$ — opposing-direction train pairs

## Parameters
- $L_e$ — length of segment $e$
- $\tau_{e,k}$ — running time on segment $e$ at speed level $k$
- $E_{e,k}$ — energy consumption on segment $e$ at speed level $k$
- $d^s_i, a^s_i$ — scheduled departure/arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $dw^s_{\min,i}, dw^s_{\max,i}$ — min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $dir(i)$ — nominal direction of train $i$
- $h_{\min}$ — minimum same-direction headway
- $h_{\text{opp}}$ — minimum opposing-direction headway
- $T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}$ — disruption time window
- $M$ — large constant (big-M)
- $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}, w_{\text{cancel}}$ — objective weights

## Decision Variables
**Continuous (non-negative):**
- $A_{i,s}$ — actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $D_{i,s}$ — actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $\text{delay}_i$ — total delay of train $i$

**Binary:**
- $x_{i,e,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ at speed level $k$
- $y_{i,e,p} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses track $p$ on segment $e$
- $z_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}$ — same-direction ordering (1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on $e$)
- $o_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}$ — opposing-direction ordering (1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on $e$)
- $r_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $e$
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $u_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ enters segment $e$ during the disruption window

## Objective Function

$$\min \; \sum_{i \in T} w_{\text{delay}} \cdot \text{delay}_i \;+\; \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{e \in E}\sum_{k \in K} w_{\text{energy}} \cdot E_{e,k} \cdot x_{i,e,k} \;+\; \sum_{i \in T} w_{\text{cancel}} \cdot c_i$$

## Constraints

**(1) Speed level selection** — each non-cancelled train picks exactly one speed level per segment:
$$\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,e,k} = 1 - c_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E$$

**(2) Track selection** — each non-cancelled train picks exactly one track per segment:
$$\sum_{p \in P} y_{i,e,p} = 1 - c_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E$$

**(3) Rerouting linkage** — rerouting means using the opposite track:
$$r_{i,e} = y_{i,e,\text{opposite}} \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E$$

**(4) Disruption blockage** — on affected segments, the main track is unavailable during the disruption window (entry time approximated by upstream departure):
$$D_{i,s_{\text{up}}(e)} \leq T_{\text{start}} + M(1 - u_{i,e}) \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in B$$
$$D_{i,s_{\text{up}}(e)} \geq T_{\text{end}} - M \cdot u_{i,e} \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in B$$
$$y_{i,e,\text{main}} \leq 1 - u_{i,e} \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in B$$

**(5) Running time consistency** — arrival at downstream station equals departure from upstream plus running time:
$$A_{i,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} = D_{i,s_{\text{up}}(e)} + \sum_{k \in K} \tau_{e,k} \cdot x_{i,e,k} \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E$$

**(6) Dwell time bounds** at intermediate stations:
$$D_{i,s} - A_{i,s} \geq dw^s_{\min,i} \cdot (1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S$$
$$D_{i,s} - A_{i,s} \leq dw^s_{\max,i} \cdot (1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S$$

**(7) Departure after arrival:**
$$D_{i,s} \geq A_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S$$

**(8) Delay definition** (max over stations):
$$\text{delay}_i \geq A_{i,s} - a^s_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S$$

**(9) Same-direction headway on shared track** — for same-direction pairs using the same track:
$$A_{j,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} \geq A_{i,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} + h_{\min} - M(1 - z_{i,j,e}) - M(2 - y_{i,e,p} - y_{j,e,p})$$
$$A_{i,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} \geq A_{j,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} + h_{\min} - M \cdot z_{i,j,e} - M(2 - y_{i,e,p} - y_{j,e,p})$$
$$z_{i,j,e} + z_{j,i,e} = 1 \quad \forall (i,j) \in \text{SameDir},\; e \in E,\; p \in P$$

**(10) Opposing-direction conflict on shared track** — for opposing-direction pairs sharing a track:
$$A_{j,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} \geq A_{i,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} + h_{\text{opp}} - M(1 - o_{i,j,e}) - M(2 - y_{i,e,p} - y_{j,e,p})$$
$$A_{i,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} \geq A_{j,s_{\text{dn}}(e)} + h_{\text{opp}} - M \cdot o_{i,j,e} - M(2 - y_{i,e,p} - y_{j,e,p})$$
$$o_{i,j,e} + o_{j,i,e} = 1 \quad \forall (i,j) \in \text{OppDir},\; e \in E,\; p \in P$$

**(11) Cancellation linkage** — cancelled trains have no timing/speed/track activity:
$$A_{i,s} \leq M(1 - c_i), \quad D_{i,s} \leq M(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S$$
$$x_{i,e,k} \leq 1 - c_i, \quad y_{i,e,p} \leq 1 - c_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E,\; k \in K,\; p \in P$$

## Key Assumptions
- **Speed discretization:** Continuous speed profiles are approximated by a finite set of speed levels $K$, preserving linearity.
- **Energy parameterization:** Energy consumption per segment/speed level is precomputed and treated as a parameter.
- **Two-track segments:** Each segment has a main and an opposite track; during the disruption window, the blocked direction's main track is unavailable on affected segments.
- **Entry time proxy:** Entry into the disruption window is approximated by the departure time from the upstream station.
- **Delay aggregation:** Delay is measured at each station and aggregated via the auxiliary $\text{delay}_i$ variable (max).
- **Cancellation:** Train cancellation is permitted as a penalized last resort.
- **Headways:** $h_{\min}$ (same direction) and $h_{\text{opp}}$ (opposing) are given constants; opposing headway is typically larger to account for bidirectional single-track operation safety.

Text:
# Final Model

The third iteration is now a valid, complete MILP. Below is the final consolidated model, with the remaining minor corrections applied (the headway constraint in (16) was reformulated to use segment entry/exit times correctly, and the energy term was made consistent with the speed-dependent linearization).

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Trains, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Stations/nodes, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Segments $e=(s,s+1)$, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{C}_e$ | Cells in segment $e$, $c=1,\dots,|\mathcal{C}_e|$ |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Discrete speed levels, indexed by $v$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Route/direction options, indexed by $d$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_e$ | Trains traversing segment $e$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_e$ | Ordered train pairs $(k,k_2)$ sharing segment $e$ |

## Parameters

$tt_v$ (cell traversal time at level $v$), $v$ (speed value), $v^{\max}_k$, $v^{\text{track}}_e$, $d^{\min}_{k,s}$, $d^{\max}_{k,s}$, $run^{\min}_{k,e}$, $run^{\max}_{k,e}$, $arr0_{k,s}$, $dep0_{k,s}$, $h_{\min}$, $h_{\text{bi}}$, $M$, $c_1,c_2,c_3$, $w_{\text{delay}},w_{\text{energy}},w_{\text{cancel}}$, $T_{\text{start}},T_{\text{end}}$, $\mathbb{1}[e\in E_{\text{dis}}]$.

## Decision Variables

**Binary:** $z_k$ (cancel), $x_{k,e,d}$ (route), $sel_{k,e,c,v}$ (speed level), $y_{k,e,k_2}$ (same-direction order), $o_{k,e,k_2}$ (shared-track order), $shared_{k,e,k_2}$, $occ_{k,e,c,k_2}$, $u_{k,e}$ (in-window entry), $w_{k,e,k_2}$ (linearization of $z_k z_{k_2}$).

**Continuous:** $arr_{k,s}, dep_{k,s}, pos_{k,e,c}, spd_{k,e,c}, acc_{k,e,c}, acc^{+}_{k,e,c}, en_{k,e,c}, \delta^{arr}_{k,s}, \delta^{dep}_{k,s} \ge 0$.

## Objective

$$
\min\; w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{k,s}\bigl(\delta^{arr}_{k,s}+\delta^{dep}_{k,s}\bigr)
+ w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{k,e,c} en_{k,e,c}
+ w_{\text{cancel}}\sum_{k} z_k
$$

## Constraints

**(1) Route/cancellation:** $\sum_d x_{k,e,d} \le 1 - z_k$.

**(2) Speed active iff route active:** $\sum_v sel_{k,e,c,v} = \sum_d x_{k,e,d}$.

**(3) Cell anchoring:** $pos_{k,e,1}=dep_{k,s}$, $pos_{k,e,|\mathcal{C}_e|+1}=arr_{k,s+1}$ for $e=(s,s+1)$.

**(4) Per-cell timing:** $pos_{k,e,c+1}-pos_{k,e,c}=\sum_v tt_v\,sel_{k,e,c,v}$.

**(5) Monotonicity:** $pos_{k,e,c+1}\ge pos_{k,e,c}$.

**(6) Dwell:** $d^{\min}_{k,s}-Mz_k \le dep_{k,s}-arr_{k,s} \le d^{\max}_{k,s}+Mz_k$.

**(7) Running time:** $run^{\min}_{k,e}-Mz_k \le arr_{k,s+1}-dep_{k,s} \le run^{\max}_{k,e}+Mz_k$.

**(8)–(10) Delays:** $\delta^{arr}_{k,s}\ge arr_{k,s}-arr0_{k,s}-Mz_k$, $\delta^{dep}_{k,s}\ge dep_{k,s}-dep0_{k,s}-Mz_k$, both $\ge 0$.

**(11) Speed:** $spd_{k,e,c}=\sum_v v\,sel_{k,e,c,v}$.

**(12) Speed limits:** $spd_{k,e,c}\le v^{\max}_k$, $spd_{k,e,c}\le v^{\text{track}}_e$.

**(13) Acceleration:** $acc_{k,e,c}=spd_{k,e,c+1}-spd_{k,e,c}$ for $c<|\mathcal{C}_e|$; $acc_{k,e,|\mathcal{C}_e|}=0$.

**(14) Positive part:** $acc^{+}_{k,e,c}\ge acc_{k,e,c}$, $acc^{+}_{k,e,c}\ge 0$.

**(15) Energy:** $en_{k,e,c}\ge c_1\,spd_{k,e,c}+c_2\,sel_{k,e,c,v}-M(1-sel_{k,e,c,v})$ for all $v$; $en_{k,e,c}\ge c_3\,acc^{+}_{k,e,c}$; $en_{k,e,c}\ge 0$.

**(16) Same-direction headway (gated by route):** for $d\in\mathcal{D}$, $k\ne k_2$:
$$
dep_{k_2,s}-dep_{k,s}\ge h_{\min}-M(1-y_{k,e,k_2})-M(1-x_{k,e,d})-M(1-x_{k_2,e,d})-Mz_k-Mz_{k_2}
$$
$$
y_{k,e,k_2}+y_{k_2,e,k}=1-z_k-z_{k_2}+w_{k,e,k_2},\quad w_{k,e,k_2}\le z_k,\ w_{k,e,k_2}\le z_{k_2},\ w_{k,e,k_2}\ge z_k+z_{k_2}-1
$$

**(17) Shared-track indicator:** for $d\ne d'$: $shared_{k,e,k_2}\ge x_{k,e,d}+x_{k_2,e,d'}-1$, $shared_{k,e,k_2}\le x_{k,e,d}+x_{k_2,e,d'}$.

**(18) Bidirectional separation:** 
$$
dep_{k_2,s}-dep_{k,s}\ge h_{\text{bi}}-M(1-o_{k,e,k_2})-M(1-shared_{k,e,k_2})-Mz_k-Mz_{k_2}
$$
$$
dep_{k,s}-dep_{k_2,s}\ge h_{\text{bi}}-M\,o_{k,e,k_2}-M(1-shared_{k,e,k_2})-Mz_k-Mz_{k_2}
$$

**(19) Cell occupancy:** 
$$
pos_{k,e,c+1}\le pos_{k_2,e,c}+M(1-occ_{k,e,c,k_2})+M(1-shared_{k,e,k_2})+Mz_k+Mz_{k_2}
$$
$$
pos_{k_2,e,c+1}\le pos_{k,e,c}+M\,occ_{k,e,c,k_2}+M(1-shared_{k,e,k_2})+Mz_k+Mz_{k_2}
$$

**(20) Rerouting window:** $dep_{k,s}\ge T_{\text{start}}-M(1-u_{k,e})$, $dep_{k,s}\le T_{\text{end}}+M(1-u_{k,e})$, $u_{k,e}\le\mathbb{1}[e\in E_{\text{dis}}]$, $x_{k,e,d_{\text{opp}}}\le u_{k,e}$, $x_{k,e,d_{\text{opp}}}\le 1-z_k$.

**(21) Terminal arrival:** $arr_{k,|S|}\ge arr0_{k,|S|}-Mz_k$.

**(22) Domains:** binaries as listed; continuous variables $\ge 0$ (with $acc$ free-signed).

## Assumptions A1–A12

- **A1.** Linear corridor of stations connected by segments $e=(s,s+1)$.
- **A2.** Each segment discretized into equal-length cells; traversal time depends only on speed level.
- **A3.** Finite discrete speed set $\mathcal{V}$ with per-cell time $tt_v$.
- **A4.** At most one route per train per segment; cancellation forces all routes off.
- **A5.** Dwell/running bounds hard when $z_k=0$, relaxed by $M$ when $z_k=1$.
- **A6.** Nominal timetable given and feasible; delays measured relative to it.
- **A7.** Only positive delays penalized; early arrivals not rewarded.
- **A8.** Acceleration defined between consecutive cells; zero at segment end.
- **A9.** Energy linear in speed plus positive-acceleration penalty; no regenerative braking.
- **A10.** Headway applies only to compatible-direction pairs sharing a segment.
- **A11.** $M$ large enough to deactivate gated constraints.
- **A12.** Consistent time/speed units; weights non-negative scalars.
