Text:
# Complete MILP Model for Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1, 2, \ldots, S\}$ | Set of stations along the urban rail line, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{T} = \{1, 2, \ldots, T\}$ | Set of trains (services) in the prediction horizon, indexed by $i$ |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1, 2, \ldots, K\}$ | Set of time intervals in the prediction horizon, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{C} = \{1, 2, \ldots, C\}$ | Set of available train compositions (coupling units), indexed by $c$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{1, 2, \ldots, D\}$ | Set of depot/terminal locations, indexed by $d$ |

**Assumption (A1):** The line is a single bidirectional urban rail corridor with $S$ stations. Trains operate in one direction during the scheduling horizon (peak-direction scheduling). This is a reasonable simplification for real-time rescheduling of a metro line.

**Assumption (A2):** The set $\mathcal{C}$ of train compositions represents discrete coupling configurations, where composition $c$ has $n_c$ cars. For example, $c=1$ corresponds to a 4-car train, $c=2$ to a 6-car train, $c=3$ to an 8-car train.

---

## 2. Parameters

### 2.1 Infrastructure and Operational Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains | min |
| $h_{\max}$ | Maximum headway between consecutive trains | min |
| $d_{s,s+1}^{\text{run}}$ | Nominal running time from station $s$ to $s+1$ | min |
| $d_s^{\text{dwell,min}}$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $d_s^{\text{dwell,max}}$ | Maximum dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $\tau_s^{\text{acc}}$ | Acceleration penalty time at station $s$ | min |
| $\tau_s^{\text{dec}}$ | Deceleration penalty time at station $s$ | min |
| $L_s$ | Length of the section between station $s$ and $s+1$ | km |
| $v^{\text{avg}}$ | Average operating speed | km/h |
| $n_c$ | Number of cars in composition $c$ | cars |
| $Q_c$ | Passenger capacity of composition $c$ | passengers |
| $\eta$ | Maximum load factor (e.g., 1.2 for standing passengers) | — |

### 2.2 Demand Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $\lambda_{s,k}^{\text{arr}}$ | Passenger arrival rate at station $s$ during interval $k$ | pax/min |
| $\rho_{s,s',k}$ | OD demand rate from station $s$ to station $s'$ during interval $k$ | pax/min |
| $\beta_{s,s'}$ | Fraction of passengers at station $s$ destined to $s'$ | — |
| $P_{s,k}^{\text{init}}$ | Initial number of waiting passengers at station $s$ at start of interval $k$ | pax |

**Assumption (A3):** Passenger arrivals follow a Poisson process approximated as a piecewise constant rate $\lambda_{s,k}^{\text{arr}}$ over interval $k$. This is standard in urban rail scheduling literature (Liu et al., 2023a).

**Assumption (A4):** The OD split fractions $\beta_{s,s'}$ are time-invariant and known from historical data, so that the arrival rate for passengers from $s$ to $s'$ during interval $k$ is $\rho_{s,s',k} = \lambda_{s,k}^{\text{arr}} \cdot \beta_{s,s'}$.

### 2.3 Cost Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $c^{\text{wait}}$ | Penalty cost per passenger-minute of waiting | \$/pax·min |
| $c^{\text{travel}}$ | Penalty cost per passenger-minute of in-vehicle travel | \$/pax·min |
| $c^{\text{op}}$ | Operating cost per car per km | \$/car·km |
| $c^{\text{dev}}$ | Penalty cost per minute deviation from nominal timetable | \$/min |
| $c^{\text{comp}}$ | Fixed cost of coupling/uncoupling operation | \$/operation |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) | — |

### 2.4 Nominal Timetable Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $\hat{a}_{i,s}$ | Nominal arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\hat{d}_{i,s}$ | Nominal departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ | min |
| $\hat{h}_i$ | Nominal headway before train $i$ | min |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Continuous Variables

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ | min |
| $w_{i,s}$ | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $r_{i,s}$ | Running time of train $i$ from station $s$ to $s+1$ | min |
| $h_i$ | Headway between train $i-1$ and train $i$ | min |
| $W_{s,k}$ | Number of waiting passengers at station $s$ during interval $k$ | pax |
| $B_{i,s}$ | Number of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ | pax |
| $A_{i,s}$ | Number of passengers alighting train $i$ at station $s$ | pax |
| $L_{i,s}$ | Passenger load on train $i$ when departing station $s$ | pax |
| $\delta_i^+$ | Positive deviation of train $i$ from nominal timetable | min |
| $\delta_i^-$ | Negative deviation of train $i$ from nominal timetable | min |
| $E_i$ | Total passenger travel time on train $i$ | pax·min |
| $G_i$ | Total passenger waiting time for train $i$ | pax·min |

### 3.2 Binary Variables

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,c}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses composition $c$; 0 otherwise |
| $y_{i,s}$ | 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$; 0 otherwise |
| $z_{i}$ | 1 if train $i$ is operated; 0 otherwise |
| $u_{i,c,c'}$ | 1 if train $i$ changes from composition $c$ to $c'$ at the terminal; 0 otherwise |

### 3.3 Integer Variables

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $N_k^{\text{train}}$ | Number of trains departing in interval $k$ |
| $m_{i,c}$ | Number of cars of composition $c$ assigned to train $i$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective is to minimize a weighted sum of passenger waiting time, passenger travel time, operational cost, and timetable deviation:

$$
\min \quad Z = c^{\text{wait}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} G_i + c^{\text{travel}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} E_i + c^{\text{op}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} n_c \cdot x_{i,c} \cdot \sum_{s=1}^{S-1} L_s + c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} (\delta_i^+ + \delta_i^-) + c^{\text{comp}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} \sum_{c' \in \mathcal{C}} u_{i,c,c'}
$$

**Explanation of terms:**
- **First term:** Total passenger waiting time cost
- **Second term:** Total passenger in-vehicle travel time cost
- **Third term:** Train operating cost proportional to car-kilometers
- **Fourth term:** Timetable deviation penalty (schedule adherence)
- **Fifth term:** Cost of coupling/uncoupling operations for flexible composition

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Operation and Stopping Constraints

**(C1) Train operation binary linking:**
$$
\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} x_{i,c} = z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
*Each operated train is assigned exactly one composition.*

**(C2) Stopping indicator:**
$$
y_{i,s} \leq z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
*Only operated trains can stop at stations.*

**(C3) First and last station must be served:**
$$
y_{i,1} = z_i, \quad y_{i,S} = z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
*All operated trains serve the first and last stations.*

**(C4) Minimum stops:**
$$
\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} y_{i,s} \geq \sigma_{\min} \cdot z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
where $\sigma_{\min}$ is the minimum number of stops per train (e.g., $\sigma_{\min} = S$ if all-stop operation, or $\sigma_{\min} < S$ if stop-skipping is allowed).

### 5.2 Timetable Constraints

**(C5) Arrival-departure relationship:**
$$
a_{i,s} + w_{i,s} = d_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
*Departure time equals arrival time plus dwell time.*

**(C6) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
d_s^{\text{dwell,min}} \cdot y_{i,s} \leq w_{i,s} \leq d_s^{\text{dwell,max}} \cdot y_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
*Dwell time is zero if the train does not stop; otherwise bounded.*

**(C7) Running time definition:**
$$
d_{i,s} + r_{i,s} = a_{i,s+1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \{1, \ldots, S-1\}
$$
*Departure from station $s$ plus running time equals arrival at station $s+1$.*

**(C8) Running time bounds:**
$$
r_{i,s} \geq d_{s,s+1}^{\text{run}} - \tau_s^{\text{acc}} - \tau_{s+1}^{\text{dec}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \{1, \ldots, S-1\}
$$
$$
r_{i,s} \leq d_{s,s+1}^{\text{run}} + \tau_s^{\text{acc}} + \tau_{s+1}^{\text{dec}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \{1, \ldots, S-1\}
$$
*Running times can vary within acceleration/deceleration margins.*

**(C9) Headway constraints:**
$$
h_i = d_{i,1} - d_{i-1,1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \{1\}
$$
$$
h_{\min} \leq h_i \leq h_{\max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \{1\}
$$
*Minimum and maximum headway between consecutive train departures.*

**(C10) Overtaking prohibition:**
$$
a_{i,s} \leq d_{i-1,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \{1\}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
*No overtaking: train $i$ arrives at station $s$ after train $i-1$ departs.*

**Assumption (A5):** Overtaking is not allowed, which is standard for urban rail transit with a single track per direction.

### 5.3 Timetable Deviation Constraints

**(C11) Deviation linearization:**
$$
a_{i,S} - \hat{a}_{i,S} = \delta_i^+ - \delta_i^-, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
$$
\delta_i^+ \geq 0, \quad \delta_i^- \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
*Deviations at the terminal station are penalized.*

### 5.4 Passenger Flow Constraints

**(C12) Waiting passenger dynamics:**
$$
W_{s,k} = W_{s,k-1} + \lambda_{s,k}^{\text{arr}} \cdot \Delta_k - \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} B_{i,s} \cdot \mathbb{1}[d_{i,s} \in \text{interval } k], \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$
where $\Delta_k$ is the length of interval $k$ and $\mathbb{1}[\cdot]$ is the indicator function.

**Linearization of indicator:** Introduce binary variable $\theta_{i,s,k} = 1$ if train $i$ departs station $s$ during interval $k$. Then:

$$
d_{i,s} \geq t_k^{\text{start}} - M(1 - \theta_{i,s,k}), \quad \forall i, s, k
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \leq t_k^{\text{end}} + M(1 - \theta_{i,s,k}), \quad \forall i, s, k
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \theta_{i,s,k} = y_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C13) Boarding constraint:**
$$
B_{i,s} \leq W_{s,k} \cdot \theta_{i,s,k} + M(1 - \theta_{i,s,k}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$
*Passengers boarding cannot exceed waiting passengers.*

**(C14) Capacity constraint:**
$$
L_{i,s} \leq \eta \cdot \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} Q_c \cdot x_{i,c}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
*Passenger load cannot exceed effective capacity of assigned composition.*

**(C15) Load dynamics:**
$$
L_{i,s} = L_{i,s-1} + B_{i,s} - A_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \{2, \ldots, S\}
$$
$$
L_{i,1} = B_{i,1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
*Load at station $s$ equals load at $s-1$ plus boardings minus alightings.*

**(C16) Alighting constraint:**
$$
A_{i,s} \leq L_{i,s-1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \{2, \ldots, S\}
$$
*Alighting passengers cannot exceed onboard passengers.*

**(C17) Alighting estimation:**
$$
A_{i,s} = \sum_{s'=1}^{s-1} \beta_{s',s} \cdot B_{i,s'}^{\text{cum}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
where $B_{i,s'}^{\text{cum}}$ is the cumulative boarding at station $s'$ for train $i$.

**Assumption (A6):** Alighting passengers are proportional to boarding passengers at previous stations according to OD fractions $\beta_{s',s}$. This is a standard assumption when individual passenger tracking is not available.

**(C18) Total waiting time:**
$$
G_i = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \left( W_{s,k} \cdot \Delta_k - \frac{1}{2} \lambda_{s,k}^{\text{arr}} \cdot \Delta_k^2 \right) \cdot \theta_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**Assumption (A7):** Waiting time is computed using Little's law approximation: average waiting time for passengers arriving during interval $k$ is $\Delta_k / 2$ (uniform arrival assumption).

**(C19) Total travel time:**
$$
E_i = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{s'=s+1}^{S} \rho_{s,s',k} \cdot \Delta_k \cdot (a_{i,s'} - d_{i,s}) \cdot \theta_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
*Travel time for passengers from $s$ to $s'$ is the time between departure at $s$ and arrival at $s'$.*

### 5.5 Flexible Train Composition Constraints

**(C20) Composition assignment:**
$$
\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} x_{i,c} = z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
*Each train has exactly one composition.*

**(C21) Coupling/uncoupling at terminal:**
$$
u_{i,c,c'} \geq x_{i-1,c} + x_{i,c'} - 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \{1\}, \; c, c' \in \mathcal{C}
$$
*$u_{i,c,c'} = 1$ if consecutive trains have different compositions.*

**(C22) Composition change limit:**
$$
\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} \sum_{c' \in \mathcal{C}} u_{i,c,c'} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
*At most one composition change per train transition.*

**(C23) Fleet size constraint:**
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} n_c \cdot x_{i,c} \leq N^{\text{fleet}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$
where $N^{\text{fleet}}$ is the total number of cars available in the fleet.

### 5.6 Rolling Stock Circulation Constraints

**(C24) Train sequencing at terminal:**
$$
d_{i,S} + t^{\text{turn}} \leq d_{i+1,1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \{T\}
$$
where $t^{\text{turn}}$ is the minimum turnaround time at the terminal.

**(C25) Composition continuity:**
$$
x_{i,c} = x_{i+1,c'}, \quad \text{if } u_{i+1,c,c'} = 1
$$

**Linearized form:**
$$
x_{i,c} - x_{i+1,c'} \leq M(1 - u_{i+1,c,c'}), \quad \forall i, c, c'
$$
$$
x_{i+1,c'} - x_{i,c} \leq M(1 - u_{i+1,c,c'}), \quad \forall i, c, c'
$$

### 5.7 Service Frequency Constraints

**(C26) Number of trains per interval:**
$$
N_k^{\text{train}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \theta_{i,1,k}, \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**(C27) Minimum service frequency:**
$$
N_k^{\text{train}} \geq N_k^{\min}, \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}
$$
where $N_k^{\min}$ is the minimum number of trains required during interval $k$ based on demand.

**(C28) Maximum service frequency:**
$$
N_k^{\text{train}} \leq N_k^{\max}, \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}
$$
where $N_k^{\max}$ is limited by infrastructure capacity (e.g., $N_k^{\max} = \lfloor 60 / h_{\min} \rfloor$).

### 5.8 Variable Domain Constraints

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, r_{i,s}, h_i \geq 0, \quad \forall i, s
$$
$$
W_{s,k}, B_{i,s}, A_{i,s}, L_{i,s}, G_i, E_i \geq 0, \quad \forall i, s, k
$$
$$
\delta_i^+, \delta_i^- \geq 0, \quad \forall i
$$
$$
x_{i,c}, y_{i,s}, z_i, u_{i,c,c'}, \theta_{i,s,k} \in \{0, 1\}, \quad \forall i, s, c, c', k
$$
$$
N_k^{\text{train}} \in \mathbb{Z}^+, \quad \forall k
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

The complete MILP model is:

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = c^{\text{wait}} \sum_{i} G_i + c^{\text{travel}} \sum_{i} E_i + c^{\text{op}} \sum_{i,c} n_c \cdot x_{i,c} \cdot \sum_{s} L_s + c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{i} (\delta_i^+ + \delta_i^-) + c^{\text{comp}} \sum_{i,c,c'} u_{i,c,c'} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C28)} \\
& \text{Variable domains as specified}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Assumptions Summary

| Assumption | Description | Justification |
|------------|-------------|---------------|
| A1 | Single-direction corridor scheduling | Standard for peak-direction metro rescheduling |
| A2 | Discrete train compositions | Reflects real coupling configurations |
| A3 | Piecewise constant passenger arrival rates | Standard approximation in Liu et al. (2023a) |
| A4 | Time-invariant OD split fractions | Historical data availability |
| A5 | No overtaking | Standard for single-track-per-direction urban rail |
| A6 | Proportional alighting | Standard when individual tracking unavailable |
| A7 | Uniform passenger arrivals within intervals | Little's law approximation |
| A8 | Deterministic demand | Real-time rescheduling uses point forecasts |

---

## 8. Model Characteristics

- **Type:** Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP)
- **Objective:** Multi-objective weighted sum (passenger service + operational cost + schedule adherence)
- **Key Decisions:** Timetable, stopping plan, train composition, rolling stock circulation
- **Coupling:** Passenger flows couple with timetable through boarding/alighting constraints
- **Complexity:** NP-hard due to binary variables for composition, stopping, and interval assignment

---

## 9. Solution Approach (Per the Paper's Framework)

1. **Presolve:** Apply four presolve techniques to fix a subset of integer variables (e.g., stopping patterns, composition changes at terminals).
2. **Learning:** Train LSTM networks on historical optimal solutions to predict remaining integer variables (e.g., $x_{i,c}$, $y_{i,s}$).
3. **Optimization:** With integer variables fixed, solve the resulting LP for continuous variables (timetable, passenger flows) in real time.

This decomposition enables real-time computation while guaranteeing constraint satisfaction for the continuous subproblem.

# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T} = \{1,\dots,N_T\}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{I} = \{1,\dots,N_I\}$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line), indexed by $i$ |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{0,\dots,N_K\}$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{L} = \{1,\dots,N_L\}$ | Set of track segments between consecutive stations, indexed by $l$ |
| $\mathcal{R} = \{0,1\}$ | Route options ($0$ = normal track, $1$ = rerouting via opposite track) |
| $\mathcal{P} = \{(t_1,t_2) \in \mathcal{T}\times\mathcal{T} : t_1 < t_2\}$ | Ordered train pairs |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $d_l$ | Length of segment $l$ (km) |
| $p_i$ | Cumulative position of station $i$ along the line (km) |
| $D$ | Total line length (km) |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowable speed (km/h) |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (km/h²) |
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization step (s) |
| $E_c$ | Energy consumption coefficient |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $\varepsilon$ | Small positive constant |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway time (s) |
| $\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\min}, \tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time (s) |
| $C^{\text{track}}$ | Track capacity (max trains per segment) |
| $\tau^{\text{reroute}}$ | Extra travel-time penalty for rerouting (s) |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation, dwell) |
| $C^{\text{cancel}}, C^{\text{dwell}}$ | Cancellation / dwell cost coefficients |
| $T^{\text{orig}}_{i,t}$ | Original scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ (s) |
| $s^{\text{dis}}$ | Index of the disrupted segment |
| $t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}}, t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window (s) |
| $V^{\text{br}}$ | Set of breakpoints for piecewise-linear energy approximation |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Rescheduling variables:**

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ stops at station $i$ |
| $y_{i,t_1,t_2}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ departs station $i$ before $t_2$ |
| $r_{l,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ reroutes on segment $l$ |
| $a_{i,t} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ (s) |
| $d_{i,t} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Departure time of train $t$ from station $i$ (s) |
| $\text{cancel}_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $\text{delay}_{i,t} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Delay of train $t$ at station $i$ (s) |

**Speed-profile variables:**

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $v_{k,t} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Speed of train $t$ at step $k$ (km/h) |
| $\text{pos}_{k,t} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Position of train $t$ at step $k$ (km) |
| $e_{k,t} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Energy consumed by train $t$ at step $k$ |
| $\text{acc}_{k,t} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Acceleration of train $t$ at step $k$ (km/h²) |
| $\text{acc}^{\text{neg}}_{k,t} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Deceleration magnitude of train $t$ at step $k$ |
| $p_{k,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is in powered mode at step $k$ |

**Conflict / occupancy variables:**

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $\text{occ}_{k,l,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $l$ at step $k$ |
| $z_{k,l,t_1,t_2}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ precedes $t_2$ on segment $l$ at step $k$ |
| $u_{k,i,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ has reached station $i$ by step $k$ |

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, cancellations, and dwell time:

$$
\min Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \text{delay}_{i,t}
\;+\; \beta \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} e_{k,t}
\;+\; \gamma \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} C^{\text{cancel}} \cdot \text{cancel}_t
\;+\; \delta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} C^{\text{dwell}} \,(d_{i,t} - a_{i,t})
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Speed Profile Dynamics

Position update (kinematic, $\forall k \in \mathcal{K}\setminus\{N_K\}, t \in \mathcal{T}$):

$$
\text{pos}_{k+1,t} = \text{pos}_{k,t} + v_{k,t}\,\Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2}\big(\text{acc}_{k,t} - \text{acc}^{\text{neg}}_{k,t}\big)\,\Delta t^2
$$

Speed update:

$$
v_{k+1,t} = v_{k,t} + \big(\text{acc}_{k,t} - \text{acc}^{\text{neg}}_{k,t}\big)\,\Delta t
$$

Speed bounds ($\forall k,t$):

$$
v^{\min} \le v_{k,t} \le v^{\max}
$$

Acceleration / deceleration bounds ($\forall k,t$):

$$
0 \le \text{acc}_{k,t} \le a^{\max}, \qquad 0 \le \text{acc}^{\text{neg}}_{k,t} \le b^{\max}
$$

Initial and final conditions ($\forall t$):

$$
\text{pos}_{0,t} = 0, \quad \text{pos}_{N_K,t} = D, \quad v_{0,t} = 0, \quad v_{N_K,t} = 0
$$

### 5.2 Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Outer Approximation)

For each breakpoint $v_b \in V^{\text{br}}$ and each $k,t$:

$$
e_{k,t} \ge \frac{E_c \,\Delta t}{1000}\Big(2 v_b \, v_{k,t} - v_b^2\Big)
$$

This outer-approximates the quadratic energy $e_{k,t} \propto v_{k,t}^2$ from below.

### 5.3 Station Arrival / Departure

Reached-indicator definition ($\forall k,i,t$):

$$
\text{pos}_{k,t} \ge p_i - M\,(1 - u_{k,i,t})
$$

Arrival-time link:

$$
a_{i,t} \ge k\,\Delta t - M\,(1 - u_{k,i,t})
$$

Monotonicity of reached-indicator ($\forall k < N_K, i, t$):

$$
u_{k+1,i,t} \ge u_{k,i,t}
$$

Dwell-time coupling ($\forall i \in \mathcal{I}\setminus\{1,N_I\}, t$):

$$
d_{i,t} = a_{i,t} + \tfrac{1}{2}\big(\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\min} + \tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}\big)
$$

Dwell bounds:

$$
\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\min} \le d_{i,t} - a_{i,t} \le \tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}
$$

Delay definition ($\forall i,t$):

$$
\text{delay}_{i,t} \ge a_{i,t} - T^{\text{orig}}_{i,t}
$$

### 5.4 Segment Occupancy

Occupancy lower/upper linking ($\forall k,l,t$):

$$
\text{pos}_{k,t} \ge p_l - M\,(1 - \text{occ}_{k,l,t})
$$
$$
\text{pos}_{k,t} \le p_{l+1} + M\,(1 - \text{occ}_{k,l,t})
$$

Track capacity ($\forall k,l$):

$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \text{occ}_{k,l,t} \le C^{\text{track}}
$$

### 5.5 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

Ordering on shared track ($\forall k,l,(t_1,t_2)\in\mathcal{P}$):

$$
z_{k,l,t_1,t_2} + z_{k,l,t_2,t_1} = 1
$$

Position-based separation:

$$
\text{pos}_{k,t_1} + \text{pos}_{k,t_2} \le d_l + M\,(1 - z_{k,l,t_1,t_2})
$$

### 5.6 Disruption and Rerouting

Rerouting forced when train operates through disrupted segment during the blockage window ($\forall t$):

$$
r_{s^{\text{dis}},t} \ge 1 - M\,(1 - \text{cancel}_t)
$$

Rerouting travel-time penalty ($\forall l < N_L, t$):

$$
a_{l+1,t} \ge a_{l,t} + \tau^{\text{reroute}} \, r_{l,t}
$$

### 5.7 Train Ordering and Headway

Ordering completeness ($\forall i,(t_1,t_2)\in\mathcal{P}$):

$$
y_{i,t_1,t_2} + y_{i,t_2,t_1} = 1
$$

Headway enforcement:

$$
d_{i,t_1} + h^{\min} \le a_{i,t_2} + M\,(1 - y_{i,t_1,t_2})
$$

### 5.8 Cancellation

If train $t$ is cancelled, its arrival and departure times are nullified ($\forall i,t$):

$$
a_{i,t} \le M\,(1 - \text{cancel}_t)
$$
$$
d_{i,t} \le M\,(1 - \text{cancel}_t)
$$

### 5.9 Powered-Mode Linking

Acceleration only occurs in powered mode ($\forall k,t$):

$$
\text{acc}_{k,t} \le a^{\max} \, p_{k,t}
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Single-track bidirectional operation** during disruption; trains may reroute to the opposite track.
2. **Discrete-time approximation** of speed profiles with step $\Delta t$.
3. **Homogeneous fleet** — train characteristics are identical across $t$ (extendable by indexing parameters over $t$).
4. **Energy is quadratic in speed**, linearized via tangent cuts (outer approximation).
5. **Disruption** affects only segment $s^{\text{dis}}$ during $[t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}}, t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}]$.
6. **All non-cancelled trains complete the journey** from origin to destination.
7. **Dwell times are flexible** within $[\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\min}, \tau^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}]$.
8. **No overtaking** on the same track segment (enforced by occupancy/conflict constraints).
9. **Arrival-time link** uses a Big-M reached-indicator surrogate for the exact crossing time (a common linearization).
10. **Objective weights** ($\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$) are tunable to reflect operator priorities.

---

## 7. Model Summary

The formulation is a **MILP** that jointly optimizes:
- **Timetable** (arrival/departure times, delays, dwell),
- **Orders** (train sequencing and headways),
- **Routes** (normal vs. rerouting through the blockage),
- **Speed profiles** (kinematically consistent, energy-aware),

while rigorously enforcing **bidirectional conflict-freedom** on the shared track and **capacity limits** on each segment. The nonlinear energy term is linearized via tangent cuts, and all logical conditions (reached-indicator, occupancy, conflict ordering, cancellation) are encoded with Big-M binaries, yielding a fully linear model solvable by standard MILP solvers (HiGHS, Gurobi, CPLEX).

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete, linear model derived from the generated code. All variables, the objective, and every constraint are given as equations. Assumptions that had to be filled in are marked **[ASSUMPTION]**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | set of trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | set of segments (blocks), indexed $s$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | set of stations/nodes, indexed $k$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | set of discrete speed levels, indexed $l$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | direction set, $\{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ |
| $\mathcal{IS}$ | valid (train, segment) pairs actually traversed |
| $\mathcal{IK}$ | valid (train, station) pairs actually visited |
| $\mathcal{IK}^{int}$ | (train, intermediate station) pairs (dwell applies) |
| $\mathcal{P}^{same}$ | ordered pairs $(i,j)$, $i\neq j$, same direction |
| $\mathcal{P}^{opp}$ | ordered pairs $(i,j)$, $i\neq j$, opposite direction |
| $\mathcal{SLOT}$ | sequence positions $t = 0,\dots,|\mathcal{T}|-1$ **[ASSUMPTION: slot set size $=|\mathcal{T}|$ suffices on a corridor]** |

> **[ASSUMPTION]** The line is a linear corridor: segment $s$ connects station $s$ and $s+1$. A single disrupted segment $s^*$ exists with a known partial-blockage time window. Trains are identical in mass/braking; energy depends only on speed level.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d_s$ | length of segment $s$ (m) |
| $v_l$ | speed at level $l$ (m/s) |
| $e_l$ | energy rate at speed level $l$ (kWh/m) |
| $t_i^{early}$ | earliest departure time of train $i$ |
| $A_i^{sched}$ | scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at destination |
| $C_i$ | cancellation cost of train $i$ |
| $s^*$ | disrupted segment index |
| $T^{start}, T^{end}$ | disruption window start/end |
| $T^{head}$ | minimum headway (same direction) |
| $T^{safe}$ | minimum safety gap (opposite direction, shared track) |
| $T^{dw,min}, T^{dw,max}$ | minimum / maximum dwell time |
| $M$ | large constant (big-M) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary**

$$x_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{train } i \text{ occupies slot } t \text{ on segment } s$$
$$r_{i,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{train } i \text{ rerouted onto opposite track on segment } s$$
$$c_i \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{train } i \text{ cancelled}$$
$$V_{i,s,l} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{train } i \text{ uses speed level } l \text{ on segment } s$$
$$o_{i,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{train } i \text{ traverses disrupted segment before window}$$
$$z_{i,k,j} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{station ordering: } i \text{ served before } j \text{ at station } k$$
$$y_{i,s,j} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{reroute safety order: } i \text{ precedes } j \text{ on segment } s$$

**Continuous (non-negative)**

$$A_{i,k},\; D_{i,k},\; RT_{i,s},\; E_{i,s} \ge 0$$

where $A_{i,k}$ = arrival, $D_{i,k}$ = departure, $RT_{i,s}$ = running time, $E_{i,s}$ = energy.

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; w_1 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\big(A_{i,\text{dest}(i)} - A_i^{sched}\big)
\;+\; w_2 \sum_{(i,s)\in\mathcal{IS}} E_{i,s}
\;+\; w_3 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} C_i\, c_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (1) Train runs with one speed level or is cancelled
$$
\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}} V_{i,s,l} + c_i \;\ge\; 1, \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS}
$$

### (2) Running time consistent with selected speed level
$$
RT_{i,s} \;\ge\; \frac{d_s}{v_l} - M\,(1 - V_{i,s,l}), \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS},\; l\in\mathcal{L}
$$
$$
RT_{i,s} \;\le\; \frac{d_s}{v_l} + M\,(1 - V_{i,s,l}), \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS},\; l\in\mathcal{L}
$$

### (3) Time–space coupling (arrival = previous departure + running time)
$$
A_{i,k_{to}} \;=\; D_{i,k_{from}} + RT_{i,s}, \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS}
$$
where $s$ joins $k_{from}\to k_{to}$ along train $i$'s path.

### (4) Dwell time bounds at intermediate stations
$$
D_{i,k} - A_{i,k} \;\ge\; T^{dw,min}, \qquad \forall (i,k)\in\mathcal{IK}^{int}
$$
$$
D_{i,k} - A_{i,k} \;\le\; T^{dw,max}, \qquad \forall (i,k)\in\mathcal{IK}^{int}
$$

### (5) Earliest departure at origin
$$
D_{i,\text{orig}(i)} \;\ge\; t_i^{early}, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T}
$$

### (6) Disruption / partial segment blockage
A train may only traverse the disrupted segment in the blocked direction if it passes **before** the window or **after** the window, or if it is **rerouted** (or cancelled):

$$
D_{i,k_{from}} \;\le\; T^{start} + M\,(1 - o_{i,s^*}), \qquad \forall i:\; s^* \in \text{path}(i)
$$
$$
D_{i,k_{from}} \;\ge\; T^{end}
 - M(1-o_{i,s^*}) - M\,r_{i,s^*} - M\,c_i
$$

Meaning: if $o=1$ the train departs before $T^{start}$; otherwise it must depart after $T^{end}$ **unless** it is rerouted or cancelled.

### (7) Headway on segments via slot ordering

**Uniqueness of slot per train–segment:**
$$
\sum_{t\in\mathcal{SLOT}} x_{i,s,t} \;=\; 1 - c_i, \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS}
$$

**At most one train per slot per segment:**
$$
\sum_{i:(i,s)\in\mathcal{IS}} x_{i,s,t} \;\le\; 1, \qquad \forall s\in\mathcal{S},\; t\in\mathcal{SLOT}
$$

**Sequence-consistent headway** — for same-direction trains $i,j$ on segment $s$, if $i$ precedes $j$ (slots $t_i<t_j$):
$$
D_{j,k_{from}(s)} - D_{i,k_{from}(s)} - RT_{i,s} \;\ge\; T^{head} - M\,(2 - x_{i,s,t_i} - x_{j,s,t_j})
$$
applied for all $t_i < t_j$, all same-direction pairs $(i,j)$, all shared segments $s$.

### (8) Safety gap for opposite directions on rerouted (shared) segment
Active when $r_{i,s}+r_{j,s}\ge 1$. Linearized with binary $y_{i,s,j}$:

$$
D_{i,k_{from}} - D_{j,k_{from}} \;\ge\; T^{safe} - M\big(1-(r_{i,s}+r_{j,s}-1)\big) - M\,(1-y_{i,s,j})
$$

$$
D_{j,k_{from}} - D_{i,k_{from}} \;\ge\; T^{safe} - M\big(1-(r_{i,s}+r_{j,s}-1)\big) - M\,y_{i,s,j}
$$

for all opposite-direction pairs $(i,j)\in\mathcal{P}^{opp}$ and shared segments $s$.

### (9) Energy consumption (piecewise-linear over speed levels)
$$
E_{i,s} \;=\; \sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}} e_l \, d_s \, V_{i,s,l}, \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS}
$$

### (10) Conflict-free ordering at stations (same direction)
Binary $z_{i,k,j}$ decides order; only one direction of the disjunction is active:

$$
A_{j,k} - D_{i,k} \;\ge\; T^{head} - M\,(1 - z_{i,k,j}) - M\,(c_i + c_j)
$$

$$
A_{i,k} - D_{j,k} \;\ge\; T^{head} - M\,z_{i,k,j} - M\,(c_i + c_j)
$$

for all same-direction pairs and shared stations $k$.

### (11) Rerouting only permitted on the disrupted segment
$$
r_{i,s} \;=\; 0, \qquad \forall (i,s)\in\mathcal{IS},\; s \neq s^*
$$

### (12) Cancellation zeroes all times
$$
D_{i,k} \;\le\; M\,(1 - c_i), \qquad \forall (i,k)\in\mathcal{IK}
$$
$$
A_{i,k} \;\le\; M\,(1 - c_i), \qquad \forall (i,k)\in\mathcal{IK}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| **Objective** | Weighted sum of total delay, total energy, and cancellation cost |
| **Integration** | Timetable variables ($A, D$, orders $x, z$) coupled to speed variables ($V, RT$) and energy ($E$) through constraints (2)–(3) |
| **Disruption handling** | Constraint (6) forces pass-before/after window, or reroute through (8) |
| **Bidirectional conflicts** | Constraint (8) enforces safety gap when trains share the track via rerouting |
| **Feasibility of speed profiles** | Guaranteed by the runtime–speed-level coupling (2) and time–space coupling (3) |

### Key Assumptions (made explicit)
1. **[ASSUMPTION]** Corridor topology (segment $s$ = link $s\!\to\!s{+}1$) for indexing; adaptable to a general network via a from/to incidence map.
2. **[ASSUMPTION]** Piecewise-constant speed approximation per segment with a finite set of levels; acceleration/deceleration absorbed in runtime.
3. **[ASSUMPTION]** Energy is linear in distance and speed level (piecewise-linear proxy for the quadratic energy profile).
4. **[ASSUMPTION]** A single partial-blockage disruption with a known time window on a known segment.
5. **[ASSUMPTION]** Delay measured as positive deviation $A_{i,\text{dest}}-A_i^{sched}$; if only positive delays are admissible, add slack $u_i \ge A_{i,\text{dest}}-A_i^{sched}$, $u_i\ge 0$, and use $u_i$ in the objective instead.
6. **[ASSUMPTION]** Big-M chosen larger than the scheduling horizon so inactive constraints are non-binding.
7. **[ASSUMPTION]** Slot set of size $|\mathcal{T}|$ suffices because constraint (7) forbids two trains in the same direction from occupying a segment simultaneously.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ (ordered along the line) |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments $e=(s,s+1)$, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{E}_{\text{block}} \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | Segments affected by the partial blockage |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of discretized speed levels, indexed by $d$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discretized position steps along a segment, indexed by $k$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ [m] |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum allowed train speed [m/s] |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration [m/s²] |
| $t_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}, t_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time at a station [s] |
| $t_{\text{headway}}$ | Minimum safety headway (same direction, same track) [s] |
| $t_{\text{clear}}$ | Minimum clearance time (opposing directions sharing a track) [s] |
| $T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window on blocked segments |
| $d_i^s$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $a_i^s$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_i^e$ | Scheduled running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $w_i$ | Delay penalty weight (priority) of train $i$ |
| $c_E$ | Energy cost coefficient |
| $v_d$ | Speed value associated with discretized level $d$ |
| $c_d$ | Energy consumption per meter at speed level $d$ |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (e.g., $M = T_{\text{horizon}}$) |

**Assumptions:**
- Trains are identical in mass and resistance characteristics.
- Energy is approximated as a piecewise-linear function of the chosen speed level.
- The disruption window is known and fixed; no further disruptions occur.
- At most one train occupies a given track segment at a time (block signaling).
- All big-M constraints use a valid upper bound on the time horizon.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $A_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{Dep}_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\text{Run}_{i,e}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $\text{Ene}_{i,e}$ | $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $v_{i,e,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Speed of train $i$ at position step $k$ on segment $e$ |
| $\lambda_{i,e,d}$ | $[0,1]$ | Fraction of segment $e$ traversed by train $i$ at speed level $d$ |
| $\delta_{i,s}^{+}$ | $\geq 0$ | Positive departure delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta_{i}^{\text{arr}}$ | $\geq 0$ | Positive arrival delay of train $i$ at final station |

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses segment $e$ (not cancelled before $e$) |
| $y_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted onto the opposite track on segment $e$ (only for $e \in \mathcal{E}_{\text{block}}$) |
| $z_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$ |
| $u_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ during the disruption window |
| $\text{cancel}_i \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \quad 
\underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} w_i \left( \delta_i^{\text{arr}} + \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \delta_{i,s}^{+} \right)}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{c_E \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} \text{Ene}_{i,e}}_{\text{total energy}}
$$

with delay auxiliary variables:

$$
\delta_{i,s}^{+} \geq \text{Dep}_{i,s} - d_i^s, \qquad \delta_{i,s}^{+} \geq 0 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
\delta_i^{\text{arr}} \geq A_{i,|S|} - a_i^{|S|}, \qquad \delta_i^{\text{arr}} \geq 0 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (1) Time Propagation / Running Time

$$
A_{i,s+1} = \text{Dep}_{i,s} + \text{Run}_{i,e} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{E}
$$

### (2) Dwell Time Bounds

$$
t_{\text{dwell}}^{\min} \leq \text{Dep}_{i,s} - A_{i,s} \leq t_{\text{dwell}}^{\max} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\{1,|S|\}
$$

### (3) Scheduled Running Time Consistency

$$
\text{Run}_{i,e} \geq r_i^e - M(1 - x_{i,e}) \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

$$
\text{Run}_{i,e} \leq r_i^e + M(1 - x_{i,e}) \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

### (4) Speed Profile / Running Time Coupling

$$
\sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}} \lambda_{i,e,d} = x_{i,e} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

$$
0 \leq \lambda_{i,e,d} \leq 1 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E},\; d \in \mathcal{D}
$$

$$
\text{Run}_{i,e} \geq \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}} \frac{L_e}{v_d} \lambda_{i,e,d} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

$$
v_{i,e,k} = \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}} v_d \, \lambda_{i,e,d} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E},\; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

$$
v_{i,e,k} \leq v_{\max} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E},\; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

### (5) Energy as Piecewise-Linear Function of Speed Level

$$
\text{Ene}_{i,e} = \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}} c_d \, L_e \, \lambda_{i,e,d} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

### (6) Rerouting Only on Blocked Segments

$$
y_{i,e} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E} \setminus \mathcal{E}_{\text{block}}
$$

### (7) Blockage Enforcement

A train traversing a blocked segment during the disruption window must be rerouted.

**Detection of traversal during window (big-M linearization):**

$$
\text{Dep}_{i,s} \leq T_{\text{end}} + M(1 - u_{i,e}) \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{E}_{\text{block}}
$$

$$
A_{i,s+1} \geq T_{\text{start}} - M(1 - u_{i,e}) \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{E}_{\text{block}}
$$

**Must reroute if traversing during window:**

$$
u_{i,e} \leq y_{i,e} + (1 - x_{i,e}) \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}_{\text{block}}
$$

### (8) Ordering / Headway on Same Track, Same Direction

$$
\text{Dep}_{j,s} \geq A_{i,s} + t_{\text{headway}} - M(1 - z_{i,j,e}) - M(1 - x_{i,e}) - M(1 - x_{j,e})
$$

$$
\forall i \neq j \in \mathcal{T},\; e=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{E}
$$

$$
z_{i,j,e} + z_{j,i,e} = 1 \qquad \forall i \neq j \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

### (9) Opposing-Direction Conflict on Shared (Rerouted) Track

When train $i$ is rerouted onto the opposite track and train $j$ uses the normal track (or vice versa), clearance must be enforced:

$$
\text{Dep}_{j,s} \geq A_{i,s} + t_{\text{clear}} - M(1 - y_{i,e}) - M(1 - y_{j,e}) - M(1 - x_{i,e}) - M(1 - x_{j,e})
$$

$$
\forall i \neq j \in \mathcal{T},\; e=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{E}_{\text{block}}
$$

Symmetric constraint (swap $i$ and $j$):

$$
\text{Dep}_{i,s} \geq A_{j,s} + t_{\text{clear}} - M(1 - y_{i,e}) - M(1 - y_{j,e}) - M(1 - x_{i,e}) - M(1 - x_{j,e})
$$

$$
\forall i \neq j \in \mathcal{T},\; e=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{E}_{\text{block}}
$$

### (10) Cancellation

$$
x_{i,e} \leq 1 - \text{cancel}_i \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

$$
x_{i,e} \geq x_{i,e+1} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; e, e+1 \in \mathcal{E} \text{ (monotonicity: if cancelled, stays cancelled)}
$$

### (11) Variable Domains

$$
A_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \text{Dep}_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \text{Run}_{i,e} \geq 0, \quad \text{Ene}_{i,e} \geq 0
$$

$$
v_{i,e,k} \geq 0, \quad \lambda_{i,e,d} \in [0,1], \quad \delta_{i,s}^{+} \geq 0, \quad \delta_i^{\text{arr}} \geq 0
$$

$$
x_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}, \quad z_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}, \quad u_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \text{cancel}_i \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Decision | Variable |
|----------|----------|
| Retiming (arrival/departure times) | $A_{i,s}, \text{Dep}_{i,s}$ |
| Reordering (train order on segments) | $z_{i,j,e}$ |
| Route choice (normal vs. opposite track) | $y_{i,e}$ |
| Cancellations | $\text{cancel}_i$ |
| Speed management | $\lambda_{i,e,d}, v_{i,e,k}, \text{Run}_{i,e}$ |

**Objective:** Minimize weighted total delay + energy consumption.

**Key coupling constraints:**
- Time propagation links arrivals, departures, and running times.
- Speed-level selection determines both running time and energy.
- Blockage enforcement forces rerouting during the disruption window.
- Headway and clearance constraints ensure conflict-free operations.
- Cancellation variables propagate through the train's route.

**Model size:** $O(|\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{E}| \cdot (|\mathcal{D}| + |\mathcal{K}| + |\mathcal{T}|))$ variables and constraints, suitable for commercial MILP solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) on realistic instances.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete mathematical formulation of the integrated MILP model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem under partial segment blockages.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of segments (between consecutive stations), indexed by $k$ |
| $I$ | Set of discrete time intervals, indexed by $i = 1, \dots, |I|$ |
| $D = \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ | Set of directions |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ (m) |
| $\tau_k$ | Nominal running time on segment $k$ (s) |
| $v_{\max}, v_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowed speed (m/s) |
| $a_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration (m/s²) |
| $b_{\max}$ | Maximum braking deceleration (m/s²) |
| $\Delta$ | Length of each time interval (s) |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway between trains on the same track (s) |
| $d_{\text{safe}}$ | Minimum safety distance between trains (m) |
| $\tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}, \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations (s) |
| $T_d^{\text{start}}, T_d^{\text{end}}$ | Start/end of disruption time window (s) |
| $k_d$ | Disrupted segment |
| $\text{dir}_k$ | Original direction of disrupted segment |
| $\alpha_{\text{delay}}, \alpha_{\text{energy}}$ | Weights for delay and energy in objective |
| $c_{\text{acc}}, c_{\text{cruise}}, c_{\text{brake}}$ | Energy coefficients (traction, cruise, regenerative braking) |
| $\rho_t$ | Priority weight of train $t$ |
| $o_t, \text{dst}_t$ | Origin / destination station of train $t$ |
| $\text{sched\_arr}_{t,s}, \text{sched\_dep}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary variables:**
$$x_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{= 1 if train } t \text{ traverses segment } k \text{ during interval } i$$
$$r_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{= 1 if train } t \text{ is rerouted (uses opposite track) on segment } k \text{ during interval } i$$
$$y_{t,t',k,i} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{= 1 if train } t \text{ precedes train } t' \text{ on segment } k \text{ in interval } i$$
$$p_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{= 1 if train } t \text{ has completed traversing segment } k \text{ by end of interval } i$$
$$\text{cancel}_t \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{= 1 if train } t \text{ is cancelled}$$

**Continuous variables:**
$$a_{t,k} \geq 0 \quad \text{arrival time of train } t \text{ at end of segment } k$$
$$d_{t,k} \geq 0 \quad \text{departure time of train } t \text{ at start of segment } k$$
$$v_{t,k,i} \geq 0 \quad \text{speed of train } t \text{ on segment } k \text{ during interval } i$$
$$\text{acc}_{t,k,i} \quad \text{acceleration of train } t \text{ on segment } k \text{ during interval } i$$
$$e_{t,k,i} \geq 0 \quad \text{energy consumption of train } t \text{ on segment } k \text{ during interval } i$$
$$w_{t,s} \geq 0 \quad \text{dwell time of train } t \text{ at station } s$$
$$\text{delay}_{t,s} \geq 0 \quad \text{delay of train } t \text{ at station } s$$
$$\text{pos}_{t,k,i} \geq 0 \quad \text{position of train } t \text{ on segment } k \text{ at end of interval } i$$
$$\text{acc\_plus}_{t,k,i}, \text{acc\_minus}_{t,k,i} \geq 0 \quad \text{positive/negative parts of acceleration}$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay plus total energy consumption:

$$\min \quad \alpha_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \rho_t \cdot \text{delay}_{t,s} \;+\; \alpha_{\text{energy}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{i \in I} e_{t,k,i}$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Segment traversal — each train traverses each segment at most once:**
$$\sum_{i \in I} x_{t,k,i} \leq 1, \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K$$

**(C2) Continuity of segment traversal — segments completed in order:**
$$\sum_{i \in I} i \cdot x_{t,k,i} \leq \sum_{i \in I} i \cdot x_{t,k+1,i}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K$$

**(C3) Arrival time at end of segment $k$:**
$$a_{t,k} = \sum_{i \in I} (i \cdot \Delta) \cdot x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K$$

**(C4) Departure time at start of segment $k$:**
$$d_{t,k} = a_{t,k-1} + w_{t,s_k}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K \setminus \{k_{\text{first}}\}$$
$$d_{t,k_{\text{first}}} \geq \text{sched\_dep}_{t,o_t}, \quad \forall t \in T$$

**(C5) Position update (kinematic equation), relaxed by big-M:**
$$\left|\text{pos}_{t,k,i} - \text{pos}_{t,k,i-1} - v_{t,k,i-1}\Delta - \tfrac{1}{2}\text{acc}_{t,k,i-1}\Delta^2\right| \leq M(1 - x_{t,k,i}), \quad \forall t, k, i > 1$$

**(C6) Speed update, relaxed by big-M:**
$$\left|v_{t,k,i} - v_{t,k,i-1} - \text{acc}_{t,k,i-1}\Delta\right| \leq M(1 - x_{t,k,i}), \quad \forall t, k, i > 1$$

**(C7) Speed bounds:**
$$v_{\min} \cdot x_{t,k,i} \leq v_{t,k,i} \leq v_{\max} \cdot x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$

**(C8) Acceleration bounds:**
$$-b_{\max} \leq \text{acc}_{t,k,i} \leq a_{\max}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$

**(C9) Position must reach segment length when traversed:**
$$\text{pos}_{t,k,i} \leq L_k \cdot p_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$
$$\sum_{i \in I} p_{t,k,i} \geq \sum_{i \in I} x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k$$

**(C10) Energy consumption (linearized via positive/negative acceleration parts):**
$$\text{acc}_{t,k,i} = \text{acc\_plus}_{t,k,i} - \text{acc\_minus}_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$
$$e_{t,k,i} = c_{\text{acc}}\,\text{acc\_plus}_{t,k,i}\Delta + c_{\text{cruise}}\,x_{t,k,i}\Delta - c_{\text{brake}}\,\text{acc\_minus}_{t,k,i}\Delta, \quad \forall t, k, i$$

**(C11) Disruption constraint — no train traverses disrupted segment in original direction during disruption window:**
$$x_{t,k_d,i} = 0, \quad \forall t \in T: \text{dir}_t = \text{dir}_k, \; i \in I: i\Delta \in [T_d^{\text{start}}, T_d^{\text{end}}]$$

**(C12) Rerouting — affected trains must use the opposite track during disruption:**
$$x_{t,k_d,i} + r_{t,k_d,i} = 1, \quad \forall t \text{ affected}, \; i \in I: i\Delta \in [T_d^{\text{start}}, T_d^{\text{end}}]$$
$$r_{t,k,i} \leq x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$

**(C13) Bidirectional conflict resolution — at most one train occupies a shared segment per interval:**
$$\sum_{t \in T} x_{t,k,i} + \sum_{t \in T} r_{t,k,i} \leq 1, \quad \forall k \in K, \; i \in I$$

**(C14) Ordering of trains on the same segment:**
$$y_{t,t',k,i} + y_{t',t,k,i} = 1, \quad \forall t < t', \; k, i$$
$$a_{t,k} + h_{\min} \leq a_{t',k} + M(1 - y_{t,t',k,i}), \quad \forall t \neq t', \; k, i$$

**(C15) Safety distance on segment:**
$$\text{pos}_{t,k,i} - \text{pos}_{t',k,i} \geq d_{\text{safe}} - M(1 - y_{t,t',k,i}), \quad \forall t \neq t', \; k, i$$

**(C16) Dwell time bounds:**
$$\tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min} \leq w_{t,s} \leq \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S$$

**(C17) Delay definition:**
$$\text{delay}_{t,s} \geq a_{t,k(s)} - \text{sched\_arr}_{t,s}, \quad \forall t, s$$
$$\text{delay}_{t,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall t, s$$

**(C18) First segment departure time:**
$$d_{t,k_{\text{first}}} \geq \text{sched\_dep}_{t,o_t}, \quad \forall t \in T$$

**(C19) Last segment arrival time (relaxed by cancellation):**
$$a_{t,k_{\text{last}}} \leq \text{sched\_arr}_{t,\text{dst}_t} + M \cdot \text{cancel}_t, \quad \forall t \in T$$

**(C20) Cancellation handling:** $\text{cancel}_t$ is a binary variable that relaxes the final arrival constraint, with a large penalty implicitly included via $\rho_t$ in the objective.

**(C21) Linking $x$ and arrival times:**
$$a_{t,k} \geq \sum_{i \in I} i\Delta \cdot x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k$$
$$a_{t,k} \leq \sum_{i \in I} i\Delta \cdot x_{t,k,i} + M\left(1 - \sum_{i \in I} x_{t,k,i}\right), \quad \forall t, k$$

**(C22) Rerouting consistency:**
$$r_{t,k,i} \leq x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$

**(C23) Energy linearization auxiliary constraints:**
$$\text{acc\_plus}_{t,k,i} \geq 0, \quad \text{acc\_minus}_{t,k,i} \geq 0, \quad \forall t, k, i$$
$$\text{acc}_{t,k,i} = \text{acc\_plus}_{t,k,i} - \text{acc\_minus}_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$

**(C24) Big-M activation of dynamics only when train occupies segment:**
$$\text{acc}_{t,k,i} \leq a_{\max} \cdot x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$
$$\text{acc}_{t,k,i} \geq -b_{\max} \cdot x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$
$$v_{t,k,i} \leq v_{\max} \cdot x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t, k, i$$

---

## 6. Key Assumptions (Marked)

1. **Time discretization**: The continuous time horizon is discretized into equal-length intervals $\Delta$; all events (arrival, departure, position) are aligned to interval boundaries. *(Assumption — a discretized approximation of continuous dynamics.)*
2. **Energy model**: Traction energy is linear in positive acceleration; regenerative braking recovers energy proportional to deceleration; cruising incurs a small constant auxiliary load. *(Assumption — simplified linear energy model.)*
3. **Single disrupted segment** $k_d$ with a known time window. *(Assumption — one partial blockage per scenario.)*
4. **Rerouting** is only permitted on the disrupted segment during the disruption window; trains otherwise follow their scheduled paths. *(Assumption — local rerouting strategy.)*
5. **Conflict resolution** on shared (rerouted) track enforces at most one train per segment-interval, and safety distance is maintained via ordering variables. *(Assumption — discretized conflict-free guarantee.)*
6. **Cancellation** is modeled as a binary variable relaxing the final arrival constraint. *(Assumption — cancellations allowed as last resort.)*
7. **Dwell bounds** are enforced directly via variable bounds. *(Assumption — station capacity not explicitly modeled.)*

---

This formulation captures the integrated TRSMP: it simultaneously optimizes **train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles**, yielding a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles, exactly as described in the paper's contribution.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Based on the provided input, I formulate a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the real-time railway traffic management problem, decomposing it into rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling sub-problems. The model follows the reference formulation of Pellegrini et al. (2014) extended with pair-wise delay variables as described in the paper.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(i, j \in T\) |
| \(B\) | Set of block sections (track segments), indexed by \(b \in B\) |
| \(R_i\) | Set of feasible routes for train \(i\) |
| \(R_i^b \subseteq R_i\) | Set of routes of train \(i\) that include block section \(b\) |
| \(S_b\) | Set of trains that can traverse block \(b\), \(S_b \subseteq T\) |
| \(P\) | Set of ordered train pairs \((i,j)\) that can potentially conflict, \(P \subseteq T \times T\), \(i \neq j\) |
| \(P_b\) | Set of ordered pairs \((i,j) \in P\) that can conflict on block \(b\) |

**Assumption (A1):** The infrastructure is represented at a microscopic level, where each block section can be occupied by at most one train at a time.

**Assumption (A2):** Routes are pre-computed feasible paths through the network; each train must select exactly one route.

**Assumption (A3):** The set \(P\) of conflicting pairs is derived from the topology and the timetable (trains whose paths share at least one block section).

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| \(t_i^{arr}\) | Scheduled arrival time of train \(i\) at its destination | s |
| \(t_i^{dep}\) | Scheduled departure time of train \(i\) from its origin | s |
| \(\tau_{i,b}^{run}\) | Minimum running time of train \(i\) on block \(b\) | s |
| \(\tau_{i,b}^{min}\) | Minimum dwell/clearance time of train \(i\) at block \(b\) | s |
| \(h_b\) | Minimum headway (safety separation) time on block \(b\) | s |
| \(M\) | Large positive constant (big-M) | s |
| \(w_i^{arr}\) | Weight (penalty) for arrival delay of train \(i\) | – |
| \(w_i^{dep}\) | Weight (penalty) for departure delay of train \(i\) | – |
| \(c_{i,r}\) | Cost of assigning route \(r\) to train \(i\) (e.g., energy or length) | – |

**Assumption (A4):** Running times \(\tau_{i,b}^{run}\) are deterministic and known; stochastic disturbances are not modeled (following the deterministic rtRTMP formulation).

**Assumption (A5):** The big-M constant is chosen sufficiently large, e.g., \(M = \max_{i \in T} t_i^{arr} + \sum_{b \in B} \tau_{i,b}^{run}\).

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Routing Variables

\[
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ r \in R_i
\]
\(x_{i,r} = 1\) if train \(i\) is assigned route \(r\); \(0\) otherwise.

### 3.2 Scheduling Variables

\[
a_{i,b} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B
\]
Actual arrival time of train \(i\) at block section \(b\).

\[
d_{i,b} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B
\]
Actual departure time of train \(i\) from block section \(b\).

### 3.3 Delay Variables

\[
\delta_i^{arr} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in T
\]
Arrival delay of train \(i\) at destination.

\[
\delta_i^{dep} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in T
\]
Departure delay of train \(i\) from origin.

### 3.4 Pair-Wise Ordering Variables (Reordering)

\[
y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P_b,\ b \in B
\]
\(y_{i,j,b} = 1\) if train \(i\) precedes train \(j\) on block \(b\); \(0\) otherwise.

**Assumption (A6):** \(y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1\) for all conflicting pairs on block \(b\), ensuring a total order.

### 3.5 Pair-Wise Delay Propagation Variables

\[
z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P
\]
\(z_{i,j} = 1\) if train \(i\) waits for train \(j\) (i.e., \(j\) is the blocking train causing delay to \(i\)).

**Assumption (A7):** At most one blocking train is considered per train \(i\) in the simplified model:
\[
\sum_{j:(i,j) \in P} z_{i,j} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \in T
\]

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes the weighted sum of arrival and departure delays:

\[
\min \quad Z = \sum_{i \in T} \left( w_i^{arr} \cdot \delta_i^{arr} + w_i^{dep} \cdot \delta_i^{dep} \right)
\]

**Assumption (A8):** Weights \(w_i^{arr}, w_i^{dep}\) are given by the dispatcher and reflect priority (e.g., passenger trains weighted higher than freight).

**Alternative (energy-aware extension, marked as Assumption A9):** If energy consumption is considered as a secondary objective:
\[
\min \quad Z' = \sum_{i \in T} \left( w_i^{arr} \cdot \delta_i^{arr} + w_i^{dep} \cdot \delta_i^{dep} \right) + \lambda \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{r \in R_i} c_{i,r} \cdot x_{i,r}
\]
where \(\lambda\) is a trade-off parameter.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Route Selection Constraints

Each train must select exactly one route:

\[
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{C1}
\]

### 5.2 Block Section Usage Linking

Train \(i\) uses block \(b\) if and only if its selected route includes \(b\):

\[
\sum_{r \in R_i^b} x_{i,r} = u_{i,b}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{C2}
\]

where \(u_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}\) is an auxiliary variable indicating whether train \(i\) traverses block \(b\).

**Assumption (A10):** \(u_{i,b}\) is treated as a continuous variable in \([0,1]\); since the constraint matrix is totally unimodular with (C1), integrality is preserved.

### 5.3 Running Time Constraints

For each train \(i\) and block \(b\) it traverses:

\[
d_{i,b} - a_{i,b} \geq \tau_{i,b}^{run} \cdot u_{i,b}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{C3}
\]

### 5.4 Connection Constraints Between Consecutive Blocks

For consecutive blocks \(b\) and \(b'\) on route \(r\) of train \(i\):

\[
a_{i,b'} \geq d_{i,b} + \tau_{i,b}^{min} \cdot u_{i,b}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ (b,b') \in \text{route } r \tag{C4}
\]

**Assumption (A11):** The minimum dwell/clearance time \(\tau_{i,b}^{min}\) accounts for station stops and signal clearance.

### 5.5 Departure Delay Definition

\[
\delta_i^{dep} \geq d_{i,b_0} - t_i^{dep}, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{C5}
\]

where \(b_0\) is the first block of train \(i\)'s route.

### 5.6 Arrival Delay Definition

\[
\delta_i^{arr} \geq a_{i,b_f} - t_i^{arr}, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{C6}
\]

where \(b_f\) is the last block of train \(i\)'s route.

### 5.7 Headway / Conflict Constraints (Reordering)

For each conflicting pair \((i,j) \in P_b\) on block \(b\):

\[
a_{j,b} \geq d_{i,b} + h_b - M \cdot (1 - y_{i,j,b}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in P_b,\ b \in B \tag{C7}
\]

\[
a_{i,b} \geq d_{j,b} + h_b - M \cdot y_{i,j,b}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P_b,\ b \in B \tag{C8}
\]

**Assumption (A12):** Constraints (C7)–(C8) enforce that only one train occupies block \(b\) at a time, with minimum headway \(h_b\).

### 5.8 Pair-Wise Ordering Consistency

For each conflicting pair on block \(b\):

\[
y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P_b,\ b \in B \tag{C9}
\]

### 5.9 Delay Propagation Linking (Pair-Wise Interpretation)

The pair-wise delay variable \(z_{i,j}\) is linked to the ordering variables:

\[
z_{i,j} \geq y_{j,i,b} - (1 - u_{i,b}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in P_b,\ b \in B \tag{C10}
\]

\[
z_{i,j} \leq \sum_{b \in B: (i,j) \in P_b} y_{j,i,b}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P \tag{C11}
\]

**Interpretation:** \(z_{i,j} = 1\) if train \(j\) precedes train \(i\) on at least one shared block, meaning \(i\) may wait for \(j\).

### 5.10 Delay Propagation Constraints (Optimal Model Extension)

For the global optimum model (Section 3.3 of the paper), delay propagation is captured by:

\[
a_{i,b} \geq d_{j,b} + h_b - M \cdot (1 - z_{i,j}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in P_b,\ b \in B \tag{C12}
\]

**Assumption (A13):** In the sub-optimal model (Section 3.1), constraint (C12) is relaxed or omitted, and only (C7)–(C8) are used. In the optimal model, (C12) ensures that delay propagation through multiple blocks is captured exactly.

### 5.11 At-Most-One Blocking Train (Simplified Model)

\[
\sum_{j:(i,j) \in P} z_{i,j} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{C13}
\]

**Assumption (A14):** This constraint is active only in the simplified (sub-optimal) model. In the optimal model, it is removed to allow multiple blocking trains.

### 5.12 Safety-Relevant Overlap Constraints (Extended Model)

For the extended rtRTMP with safety-relevant overlaps (Lindenmaier et al., 2022):

\[
a_{i,b} \geq d_{j,b} + h_b + o_b - M \cdot (1 - y_{j,i,b}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in P_b,\ b \in B \tag{C14}
\]

where \(o_b \geq 0\) is the overlap clearance time on block \(b\).

**Assumption (A15):** \(o_b\) is a parameter derived from infrastructure data; it is zero for blocks without safety-relevant overlaps.

### 5.13 Variable Domains

\[
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ r \in R_i \tag{C15}
\]
\[
y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P_b,\ b \in B \tag{C16}
\]
\[
z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P \tag{C17}
\]
\[
u_{i,b} \in [0,1], \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{C18}
\]
\[
a_{i,b},\ d_{i,b} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{C19}
\]
\[
\delta_i^{arr},\ \delta_i^{dep} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{C20}
\]

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

The complete MILP for the rtRTMP is:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{i \in T} \left( w_i^{arr} \cdot \delta_i^{arr} + w_i^{dep} \cdot \delta_i^{dep} \right) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C20)}
\end{aligned}
}
\]

### Model Variants:

| Model | Active Constraints | Purpose |
|-------|-------------------|---------|
| **Sub-optimal (Section 3.1)** | (C1)–(C11), (C13), (C15)–(C20) | Fast rerouting + reordering, ignores delay propagation |
| **Global optimum (Section 3.3)** | (C1)–(C12), (C15)–(C20) | Exact solution with delay propagation |
| **Extended with overlaps** | (C1)–(C12), (C14)–(C20) | Includes safety-relevant overlaps |

---

## 7. Assumptions Summary

| ID | Assumption |
|----|------------|
| A1 | Microscopic infrastructure representation |
| A2 | Pre-computed feasible routes; one route per train |
| A3 | Conflicting pairs derived from topology and timetable |
| A4 | Deterministic running times |
| A5 | Big-M chosen sufficiently large |
| A6 | Total order on each block for conflicting pairs |
| A7 | At most one blocking train per train (simplified model) |
| A8 | Weights given by dispatcher |
| A9 | Optional energy term with trade-off parameter \(\lambda\) |
| A10 | \(u_{i,b}\) continuous in \([0,1]\); integrality preserved |
| A11 | Minimum dwell/clearance time accounts for stops and signals |
| A12 | Headway constraints enforce single occupancy |
| A13 | Delay propagation active only in optimal model |
| A14 | At-most-one blocking train constraint only in simplified model |
| A15 | Overlap clearance time from infrastructure data |

---

## 8. Complexity and Solution Strategy

**Assumption (A16):** The problem is NP-hard (as stated in the paper). The proposed multi-stage framework solves:

1. **Stage 1:** Sub-optimal MILP (Section 3.1) → provides route selection \(x_{i,r}^*\) and optional ordering \(y_{i,j,b}^*\).
2. **Stage 2:** Fix \(x_{i,r} = x_{i,r}^*\) and optionally \(y_{i,j,b} = y_{i,j,b}^*\), then solve the global optimum model (Section 3.3) for rescheduling.

This decomposition reduces the number of integer variables and equivalent combinations, improving runtime efficiency for real-time applications.

---

## 9. References (from input)

- Pellegrini et al. (2014, 2015, 2019) — reference MILP formulations
- Samà et al. (2016) — train route selection problem (TRSP)
- Keita et al. (2016, 2020) — Benders decomposition for rtRTMP
- Lindenmaier et al. (2022) — extended rtRTMP with safety-relevant overlaps
- Corman et al. (2010) — alternative graph model
- Törnquist Krasemann (2012) — greedy depth-first search approach

# Complete MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code, presented as equations with variables, objective function, and constraints.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations along the line, indexed by $s$ (ordered) |
| $G$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations, indexed by $g$ |
| $D$ | Set of discretized distance steps within a segment, indexed by $d$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $TR$ | Set of tracks per segment, indexed by $r \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ |
| $TP$ | Set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ with $i < j$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_g$ | Length of segment $g$ |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum allowed train speed |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration |
| $\tau$ | Discretization time step |
| $\delta_d$ | Distance step size |
| $H$ | Minimum safety headway |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $t^{dep}_{i,s}, t^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure / arrival times |
| $dwell^{min}_{i,s}, dwell^{max}_{i,s}$ | Min / max dwell time |
| $run^{min}_{i,g}, run^{max}_{i,g}$ | Min / max running time on segment $g$ |
| $E_k$ | Energy consumption per distance unit at speed level $k$ |
| $v_k$ | Speed value of level $k$ |
| $w_i$ | Delay penalty weight of train $i$ |
| $w_E$ | Energy consumption weight |
| $g_0, r_0$ | Blocked segment and blocked track |
| $t_{start}, t_{end}$ | Disruption window start / end |
| $z^0_{i,g,r}$ | Original planned track assignment |
| $seg\_s(g), seg\_s1(g)$ | Start / end station of segment $g$ |
| $D_{start}, D_{end}$ | First / last index of set $D$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $u_{i,g,d}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Speed of train $i$ at step $d$ on segment $g$ |
| $t_{i,g,d}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Time at which train $i$ reaches step $d$ on segment $g$ |
| $e_{i,g,d}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ at step $d$ on segment $g$ |
| $z_{i,g,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses track $r$ on segment $g$ |
| $o_{i,j,g,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$, track $r$ |
| $p_{i,g,d,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ at step $d$ on segment $g$ uses speed level $k$ |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\alpha_{i,g,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to track $r$ on segment $g$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total terminal delay and total energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T} w_i \left( x_{i,|S|} - t^{arr}_{i,|S|} \right) + w_E \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{g \in G} \sum_{d \in D} e_{i,g,d}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (1) Dwell time bounds at each station
$$
y_{i,s} \geq x_{i,s} + dwell^{min}_{i,s}\,(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
y_{i,s} \leq x_{i,s} + dwell^{max}_{i,s}\,(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (2) Running time bounds between consecutive stations
$$
x_{i,seg\_s1(g)} - y_{i,seg\_s(g)} \geq run^{min}_{i,g}\,(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$
$$
x_{i,seg\_s1(g)} - y_{i,seg\_s(g)} \leq run^{max}_{i,g}\,(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$

### (3) Track assignment (exactly one track per segment unless cancelled)
$$
\sum_{r \in TR} z_{i,g,r} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$

### (4) Blocked track restriction
$$
z_{i,g_0,r_0} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

### (5) Rerouting indicator linking
$$
\alpha_{i,g,r} \geq z_{i,g,r} - z^0_{i,g,r} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G,\; r \in TR
$$

### (6) Conflict-free headway on shared track (disjunctive)
$$
y_{j,seg\_s(g)} \geq x_{i,seg\_s(g)} + H - M(1 - o_{i,j,g,r}) - M(2 - z_{i,g,r} - z_{j,g,r})
$$
$$
y_{i,seg\_s(g)} \geq x_{j,seg\_s(g)} + H - M\,o_{i,j,g,r} - M(2 - z_{i,g,r} - z_{j,g,r})
$$
$$
\forall (i,j) \in TP,\; g \in G,\; r \in TR
$$

### (7) Ordering antisymmetry
$$
o_{i,j,g,r} + o_{j,i,g,r} \geq z_{i,g,r} + z_{j,g,r} - 1 \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TP,\; g \in G,\; r \in TR
$$

### (8) Speed profile consistency (position–time–speed linking)
$$
t_{i,g,d+1} - t_{i,g,d} \geq \frac{\delta_d}{v_k}\, p_{i,g,d,k} - M(1 - p_{i,g,d,k}) \qquad \forall i,g,d,k
$$
$$
t_{i,g,d+1} - t_{i,g,d} \leq \sum_{k \in K} \frac{\delta_d}{v_k}\, p_{i,g,d,k} + M\,c_i \qquad \forall i,g,d
$$

### (9) Speed level selection
$$
\sum_{k \in K} p_{i,g,d,k} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G,\; d \in D
$$
$$
u_{i,g,d} = \sum_{k \in K} v_k\, p_{i,g,d,k} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G,\; d \in D
$$

### (10) Acceleration / deceleration limits
$$
u_{i,g,d+1} - u_{i,g,d} \leq a_{\max}\,\tau + M\,c_i \qquad \forall i,g,d
$$
$$
u_{i,g,d} - u_{i,g,d+1} \leq b_{\max}\,\tau + M\,c_i \qquad \forall i,g,d
$$

### (11) Speed limits
$$
u_{i,g,d} \leq v_{\max} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G,\; d \in D
$$

### (12) Energy consumption linearization
$$
e_{i,g,d} \geq E_k\,\delta_d\,p_{i,g,d,k} - M(1 - p_{i,g,d,k}) \qquad \forall i,g,d,k
$$

### (13) Coupling timetable with speed profile
$$
x_{i,seg\_s1(g)} = t_{i,g,D_{end}} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$
$$
y_{i,seg\_s(g)} = t_{i,g,D_{start}} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$

### (14) Disruption window handling
$$
t_{i,g_0,d} \leq t_{start} + M(1 - z_{i,g_0,r_0}) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; d \in D
$$
$$
t_{i,g_0,d} \geq t_{end} - M(1 - z_{i,g_0,r_0}) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; d \in D
$$

### (15) Cancellation constraints
$$
x_{i,s} \leq M(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
y_{i,s} \leq M(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (16) Non-negativity and binary domains
$$
x_{i,s}, y_{i,s}, u_{i,g,d}, t_{i,g,d}, e_{i,g,d} \geq 0
$$
$$
z_{i,g,r}, o_{i,j,g,r}, p_{i,g,d,k}, c_i, \alpha_{i,g,r} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions (marked)

1. **Discretized motion** — Continuous train motion is approximated by discrete distance steps $d \in D$ within each segment.
2. **Discrete speed levels** — Train speed is restricted to a finite set of levels $K$; intermediate speeds are not modeled.
3. **Energy linearity** — Energy consumption is proportional to speed level and distance traveled.
4. **Single blockage** — Only one segment $g_0$ on one track $r_0$ is blocked during the disruption window.
5. **Rerouting scope** — Trains may reroute to the opposite track only within the disruption window.
6. **Bounded dwell** — Dwell times are bounded by given min/max values.
7. **Constant headway** — The safety headway $H$ is uniform across all segments and tracks.
8. **Cancellation allowed** — Any train may be cancelled at a penalty captured in the objective.
9. **Given weights** — Delay weights $w_i$ and energy weight $w_E$ are exogenous parameters.
10. **Big-M validity** — $M$ is chosen large enough to deactivate constraints when binary indicators are zero (recommended: $M = t_{end} + \sum_g run^{max}_{i,g}$).

---

This formulation constitutes a complete MILP that simultaneously optimizes train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles, yielding a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles under partial segment blockage disruptions.
