Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

## Sets and Indices
- $S$ : set of stations, indexed by $s$
- $G$ : set of segments (blocks), indexed by $g$, where segment $g$ connects station $g$ and $g+1$
- $T$ : set of trains, indexed by $i$
- $T^{out} \subseteq T$ : outbound trains (increasing station index)
- $T^{in} \subseteq T$ : inbound trains (decreasing station index)
- $K$ : set of discretized speed levels, indexed by $k$
- $P$ : set of candidate speed profiles, indexed by $p$
- $W$ : set of discrete time steps, indexed by $t$

## Parameters
- $d_g$ : length of segment $g$
- $v_k$ : speed of level $k$
- $v^{max}$ : maximum allowable speed
- $a^{max}, b^{max}$ : maximum acceleration / deceleration
- $t^{dwell,min}_{i,s}, t^{dwell,max}_{i,s}$ : min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $t^{arr,sched}_{i,s}, t^{dep,sched}_{i,s}$ : scheduled arrival/departure times
- $t^{headway}$ : minimum headway (same direction)
- $t^{block}$ : minimum opposite-track clearance time
- $g^{dis}$ : disrupted segment
- $[t^{dis}_s, t^{dis}_e]$ : disruption time window
- $M$ : large positive constant (big-M)
- $c^{delay}, c^{cancel}, c^{energy}, c^{reroute}$ : cost coefficients
- $m_i$ : mass of train $i$
- $\rho$ : resistance coefficient
- $E^{max}$ : maximum energy per train
- $\pi_{p,g,k} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if profile $p$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $g$

## Decision Variables
- $x_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ arrives at station $s$ at time $t$
- $y_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ departs from station $s$ at time $t$
- $z_{i,g,t} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ enters segment $g$ at time $t$
- $u_{i,g} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite (rerouted) track on segment $g$
- $o_{i,j,g} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$
- $w_{i,g,k} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $g$ at speed level $k$
- $q_{i,p} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ selects candidate profile $p$
- $cancel_i \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $\delta^{arr}_{i,s}, \delta^{dep}_{i,s} \geq 0$ : arrival/departure delays
- $e_{i,g} \geq 0$ : energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $g$
- $v_{i,g} \geq 0$ : average speed of train $i$ on segment $g$
- $run_{i,g} \geq 0$ : running time of train $i$ on segment $g$

## Objective Function
$$
\min Z = c^{delay}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\left(\delta^{arr}_{i,s} + \delta^{dep}_{i,s}\right) + c^{cancel}\sum_{i \in T} cancel_i + c^{energy}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{g \in G} e_{i,g} + c^{reroute}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{g \in G} u_{i,g}
$$

## Constraints

**(1) Single arrival/departure per station (unless cancelled):**
$$
\sum_{t \in W} x_{i,s,t} = 1 - cancel_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in W} y_{i,s,t} = 1 - cancel_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(2) Time definition and delay:**
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot x_{i,s,t} = t^{arr,sched}_{i,s} + \delta^{arr}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot y_{i,s,t} = t^{dep,sched}_{i,s} + \delta^{dep}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(3) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot y_{i,s,t} - \sum_{t \in W} t \cdot x_{i,s,t} \geq t^{dwell,min}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot y_{i,s,t} - \sum_{t \in W} t \cdot x_{i,s,t} \leq t^{dwell,max}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(4) Running time linking (segment $g$ between stations $g$ and $g+1$):**
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot x_{i,g+1,t} - \sum_{t \in W} t \cdot y_{i,g,t} = run_{i,g} \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$

**(5) Speed profile selection and running time consistency:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} w_{i,g,k} = 1 - cancel_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$
$$
run_{i,g} = \sum_{k \in K} \frac{d_g}{v_k} w_{i,g,k} \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$
$$
v_{i,g} = \sum_{k \in K} v_k w_{i,g,k} \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$

**(6) Speed and acceleration limits:**
$$
v_{i,g} \leq v^{max} \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$
$$
v_{i,g+1} - v_{i,g} \leq a^{max} \cdot run_{i,g} \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G \setminus \{\max G\}
$$
$$
v_{i,g} - v_{i,g+1} \leq b^{max} \cdot run_{i,g} \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G \setminus \{\max G\}
$$

**(7) Energy consumption (linearized kinetic + resistance):**
$$
e_{i,g} \geq 10^{-6}\left[\frac{m_i}{2}\left(v_{i,g}^2 - v_{i,g-1}^2\right) + \rho \cdot d_g \cdot v_{i,g}\right] \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$
$$
\sum_{g \in G} e_{i,g} \leq E^{max} \quad \forall i \in T
$$

**(8) Segment entry time linking:**
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot z_{i,g,t} = \sum_{t \in W} t \cdot y_{i,g,t} \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
$$

**(9) Disruption / partial blockage (affected segment $g^{dis}$):**
$$
z_{i,g^{dis},t} \leq u_{i,g^{dis}} + \left[1 - \mathbb{1}(t \in [t^{dis}_s, t^{dis}_e])\right] \quad \forall i \in T,\; t \in W
$$
$$
u_{i,g^{dis}} \leq \sum_{t \in [t^{dis}_s, t^{dis}_e]} z_{i,g^{dis},t} \quad \forall i \in T
$$

**(10) Rerouting capacity (only one direction on opposite track per segment):**
$$
u_{i,g} + u_{j,g} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in T^{out},\; j \in T^{in},\; g \in G
$$

**(11) Same-direction headway / ordering:**
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot z_{i,g,t} - \sum_{t \in W} t \cdot z_{j,g,t} \geq t^{headway} - M(1 - o_{i,j,g}) \quad \forall i,j \in T,\; i \neq j,\; g \in G
$$
$$
o_{i,j,g} + o_{j,i,g} = 1 \quad \forall i,j \in T,\; i \neq j,\; g \in G
$$

**(12) Opposite-direction conflict clearance (bidirectional track sharing):**
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot z_{i,g,t} - \sum_{t \in W} t \cdot z_{j,g,t} \geq t^{block} - M(1 - o_{i,j,g}) \quad \forall i \in T^{out},\; j \in T^{in},\; g \in G
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in W} t \cdot z_{j,g,t} - \sum_{t \in W} t \cdot z_{i,g,t} \geq t^{block} - M \cdot o_{i,j,g} \quad \forall i \in T^{out},\; j \in T^{in},\; g \in G
$$

**(13) Cancellation linking:**
$$
cancel_i \geq 1 - \sum_{t \in W} x_{i,s_0,t} \quad \forall i \in T
$$
$$
cancel_i \leq 2 - \sum_{t \in W} x_{i,s_0,t} \quad \forall i \in T
$$

**(14) Candidate speed profile selection:**
$$
\sum_{p \in P} q_{i,p} = 1 - cancel_i \quad \forall i \in T
$$
$$
w_{i,g,k} \leq \sum_{p \in P} \pi_{p,g,k} \cdot q_{i,p} \quad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G,\; k \in K
$$

## Modeling Assumptions
1. **Time discretization**: The planning horizon is discretized into a finite set $W$ of time steps (e.g., minutes); arrival, departure, and segment-entry times are encoded via binary selection over $t$.
2. **Piecewise-constant speed profiles**: Each segment is traversed at a single representative speed level from a finite set $K$, which linearizes the otherwise quadratic energy term.
3. **Single disrupted segment**: The partial blockage affects exactly one segment $g^{dis}$ during a known time window $[t^{dis}_s, t^{dis}_e]$.
4. **Mandatory rerouting**: Any train entering the disrupted segment during the disruption window must use the opposite track ($u_{i,g^{dis}}=1$).
5. **Unidirectional opposite-track capacity**: At most one train (in one direction) may occupy the opposite track on a given segment at a time.
6. **Bounded dwell times**: Dwell times are bounded between minimum and maximum values; delays are measured relative to the original schedule.
7. **Cancellation as last resort**: A binary $cancel_i$ relaxes all "at most once" constraints and is heavily penalized in the objective.
8. **Big-M linearization**: Disjunctive ordering constraints are linearized using a sufficiently large constant $M$.
9. **Linearized energy**: Energy is approximated by kinetic-energy change plus a linear resistance term; regenerative braking is absorbed into the net energy coefficient.
10. **No rolling-stock circulation coupling**: Trains are treated independently (no coupling constraints between successive services of the same rolling stock).

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Best MILP Model

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Index | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | $i,j$ | Set of trains |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | $s$ | Ordered stations/segments ($s=1,\dots,S$; segment $s$ lies between station $s$ and $s+1$) |
| $\mathcal{R}=\{0,1\}$ | $r$ | Routes: $r=0$ normal track, $r=1$ opposite track (rerouting) |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | $k$ | Discretized speed-profile options (piecewise-linear breakpoints) |
| $\mathcal{S}^{dis}\subseteq\mathcal{S}$ | $s$ | Disrupted (partially blocked) segments |
| $\mathcal{R}^{blk}_s\subseteq\mathcal{R}$ | $r$ | Blocked routes on segment $s$ during the disruption window |

Pairs $(i,j)$ with $i<j$ are used to avoid symmetry.

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| $A^{sch}_{i,s},\ D^{sch}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\underline{rt}_{i,s,r},\ \overline{rt}_{i,s}$ | Min running time (route-dependent) / max running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $\underline{dw}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{dis}_{start},\ t^{dis}_{end}$ | Disruption time window |
| $H$ | Minimum headway (safety separation) on a shared track block |
| $c_{s,r}$ | Capacity of route $r$ on segment $s$ (typically 1) |
| $\tau_k$ | Running time of speed profile $k$ on a segment |
| $E_k$ | Energy consumption of speed profile $k$ on a segment |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $\alpha,\beta$ | Objective weights for delay and energy |
| $s_{last}=S$ | Terminal station |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous**
- $t^{arr}_{i,s}\ge 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $t^{dep}_{i,s}\ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $e_{i,s}\ge 0$: energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$
- $d^{+}_i\ge 0$: terminal delay of train $i$

**Binary**
- $x_{i,s,r}\in\{0,1\}$: train $i$ uses route $r$ on segment $s$
- $y_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\}$: train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$
- $v_{i,s,k}\in\{0,1\}$: train $i$ selects speed profile $k$ on segment $s$
- $z_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}$: traversal of segment $s$ by train $i$ overlaps the disruption window

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{\ \min\ Z=\alpha\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} d^{+}_i \;+\; \beta\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}} e_{i,s}\ }
$$

**Terminal delay (linearized absolute deviation):**

$$
d^{+}_i \ge t^{arr}_{i,S}-A^{sch}_{i,S}, \qquad d^{+}_i \ge A^{sch}_{i,S}-t^{arr}_{i,S}, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route selection — exactly one route per segment per train**
$$
\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}} x_{i,s,r} = 1, \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}
$$

**(C2) Running-time feasibility (route-dependent lower bound)**
$$
t^{arr}_{i,s+1}-t^{dep}_{i,s} \;\ge\; \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}} \underline{rt}_{i,s,r}\, x_{i,s,r}, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}
$$

**(C3) Maximum running-time restriction**
$$
t^{arr}_{i,s+1}-t^{dep}_{i,s} \;\le\; \overline{rt}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}
$$

**(C4) Minimum dwell time**
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s}-t^{arr}_{i,s} \;\ge\; \underline{dw}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}
$$

**(C5) Speed-profile selection (consistency)**
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} v_{i,s,k} = 1, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}
$$
$$
t^{arr}_{i,s+1}-t^{dep}_{i,s} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \tau_k\, v_{i,s,k}, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}
$$

**(C6) Energy consumption (piecewise-linear)**
$$
e_{i,s} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} E_k\, v_{i,s,k}, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}
$$

**(C7) Route–profile feasibility (chosen profile achievable on chosen route)**
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \tau_k\, v_{i,s,k} \;\ge\; \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}} \underline{rt}_{i,s,r}\, x_{i,s,r}, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}
$$

**(C8) Disruption-window overlap indicator $z_{i,s}$**
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s} \le t^{dis}_{end} + M(1-z_{i,s}), \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}^{dis}
$$
$$
t^{arr}_{i,s+1} \ge t^{dis}_{start} - M(1-z_{i,s}), \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}^{dis}
$$

**(C9) Blocked-route prohibition during disruption window (rerouting trigger)**
$$
x_{i,s,r} \le 1-z_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}^{dis},\ r\in\mathcal{R}^{blk}_s
$$

**(C10) Forced return to the normal track after disruption**
$$
x_{i,s,0} = 1, \qquad \forall i,\ s\notin\mathcal{S}^{dis}
$$
$$
x_{i,s+1,0} \ge x_{i,s,1}, \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}^{dis}\setminus\{S\}
$$

**(C11) Headway / conflict on shared route (big-M ordering)**
$$
t^{dep}_{j,s} \ge t^{dep}_{i,s} + H - M(1-y_{i,j,s}) - M(2-x_{i,s,r}-x_{j,s,r})
$$
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s} \ge t^{dep}_{j,s} + H - M\,y_{i,j,s} - M(2-x_{i,s,r}-x_{j,s,r})
$$
$$
\qquad \forall i<j,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\},\ r\in\mathcal{R}
$$

**(C12) Ordering antisymmetry**
$$
y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} = 1, \qquad \forall i<j,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\}
$$

**(C13) Bidirectional (opposite-track) conflict prevention**

When train $i$ uses route $r$ and train $j$ uses the opposite route $1-r$ on the same physical block:
$$
t^{dep}_{j,s} \ge t^{dep}_{i,s} + H - M(1-y_{i,j,s}) - M(2-x_{i,s,r}-x_{j,s,1-r})
$$
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s} \ge t^{dep}_{j,s} + H - M\,y_{i,j,s} - M(2-x_{i,s,r}-x_{j,s,1-r})
$$
$$
\qquad \forall i<j,\ s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\},\ r\in\mathcal{R}
$$

**(C14) Track capacity (at most one train per route-block at a time)**
$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} x_{i,s,r} \le c_{s,r}\cdot|\mathcal{T}|, \qquad \forall s\in\mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\},\ r\in\mathcal{R}
$$
(temporal separation is enforced jointly by C11–C13; $c_{s,r}$ bounds the route fill factor)

**(C15) Domain constraints**
$$
t^{arr}_{i,s},\ t^{dep}_{i,s},\ e_{i,s},\ d^{+}_i \ge 0, \qquad \forall i,\ s
$$
$$
x_{i,s,r},\ y_{i,j,s},\ v_{i,s,k},\ z_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}, \qquad \forall i,j,\ s,\ r,\ k
$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Time variables** ($t^{arr},t^{dep}$) form a fully continuous event-driven timetable, absorbing delays caused by the disruption.
- **Speed-profile binaries** ($v_{i,s,k}$) make running time endogenous: C5 fixes travel time equal to the chosen profile's $\tau_k$, and C6 maps the same selection to energy $E_k$ — coupling rescheduling with energy-efficient driving.
- **Route variables** ($x_{i,s,r}$) with the overlap indicator $z_{i,s}$ jointly encode rerouting: C9 forbids the blocked route during the window, forcing the opposite track; C10 makes rerouting local.
- **Ordering variables** ($y_{i,j,s}$) with big-M linearize the disjunctive headway requirement, preventing simultaneous occupancy of a block by same-direction (C11) or opposing-direction (C13) trains.
- **Objective** balances service quality (terminal delay) against operating cost (energy), with weights $\alpha,\beta$ tuned by policy.

**Assumptions (marked):** disrupted segments are known a priori; each route-block holds one train at a time but is shared temporally via headway; speed/energy curves are discretized into a finite profile set $\mathcal{K}$; trains must return to the normal track immediately after the disruption ends; terminal delay is the passenger-delay proxy.

## 7. Model Size and Solver

Binary count scales as $O(|\mathcal{T}|^2|\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}|(|\mathcal{R}|+|\mathcal{K}|))$. Recommended exact solver: Gurobi/CPLEX for $|\mathcal{T}|\le 30$, $|\mathcal{S}|\le 20$, $|\mathcal{K}|\le 6$; decomposition / local branching for larger instances.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management (rtRTMP)

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Assumptions (marked as such):**
- A microscopic infrastructure representation is used, where the railway network is discretized into *block sections* (track segments delimited by signals).
- The set of trains \( T \) and their initial routes are known at the start of the rescheduling horizon.
- Primary delays (external disturbances) are given as input; secondary delays (conflict-induced) are decision-dependent.
- Each train must traverse a sequence of block sections; a block section can host at most one train at a time (exclusive occupancy).
- Trains may be rerouted among a set of pre-computed alternative paths.
- Train ordering at conflicts is a decision variable (no FIFO enforcement unless stated).
- Safety-relevant overlaps behind stop signals are considered (following Lindenmaier et al., 2022).
- Time is discretized implicitly via continuous event times (entry/exit times per block section).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(i, j\) |
| \(B\) | Set of block sections, indexed by \(b\) |
| \(R_i\) | Set of feasible routes for train \(i\) |
| \(B_{i,r}\) | Ordered sequence of block sections on route \(r \in R_i\) for train \(i\) |
| \(S\) | Set of stations/platforms, indexed by \(s\) |
| \(B_s \subseteq B\) | Block sections belonging to station \(s\) |
| \(\mathcal{C}\) | Set of conflict pairs \((i,j,b)\) where trains \(i,j\) can both use block \(b\) |
| \(\mathcal{O}\) | Set of ordered pairs of consecutive block sections \((b, b')\) where \(b'\) follows \(b\) |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| \(a_i^0\) | Scheduled arrival time of train \(i\) at its destination | s |
| \(d_i^0\) | Scheduled departure time of train \(i\) from its origin | s |
| \(t_{i,b}^{\text{run}}\) | Minimum running time of train \(i\) through block \(b\) | s |
| \(t_{i,b}^{\text{dwell}}\) | Minimum dwell time of train \(i\) at block \(b\) (if station) | s |
| \(t^{\text{head}}\) | Minimum headway (safety separation) time | s |
| \(t^{\text{setup}}\) | Route setup/clearing time at interlocking | s |
| \(M\) | Large positive constant (big-M) | s |
| \(w_i^a\) | Weight for arrival delay of train \(i\) | – |
| \(w_i^d\) | Weight for departure delay of train \(i\) | – |
| \(L_b\) | Length of block section \(b\) | m |
| \(o_b\) | Overlap length behind block \(b\) | m |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Routing Variables
\[
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ r \in R_i
\]
\(x_{i,r} = 1\) if train \(i\) uses route \(r\).

### 4.2 Timing Variables
\[
e_{i,b} \geq 0 : \text{ entry time of train } i \text{ into block } b
\]
\[
l_{i,b} \geq 0 : \text{ exit (leave) time of train } i \text{ from block } b
\]

### 4.3 Ordering Variables
\[
y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j,b) \in \mathcal{C}
\]
\(y_{i,j,b} = 1\) if train \(i\) enters block \(b\) before train \(j\).

### 4.4 Delay Variables
\[
\delta_i^a \geq 0 : \text{ arrival delay of train } i
\]
\[
\delta_i^d \geq 0 : \text{ departure delay of train } i
\]

### 4.5 Pair-wise Waiting Variables (proposed reformulation)
\[
z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i,j \in T,\ i \neq j
\]
\(z_{i,j} = 1\) if train \(i\) waits for train \(j\) (i.e., \(j\) is the blocking train).

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay:

\[
\min \ Z = \sum_{i \in T} \left( w_i^a \,\delta_i^a + w_i^d \,\delta_i^d \right)
\]

**Assumption:** Weights \(w_i^a, w_i^d\) are given by the dispatcher (e.g., higher for passenger trains).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route Selection Constraints

Each train selects exactly one route:
\[
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1, \quad \forall i \in T
\tag{1}
\]

Block usage consistency (train uses block \(b\) only if its route contains \(b\)):
\[
\sum_{r \in R_i : b \in B_{i,r}} x_{i,r} = u_{i,b}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B
\tag{2}
\]
where \(u_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}\) is an auxiliary variable indicating whether train \(i\) uses block \(b\).

### 6.2 Running Time Constraints

For each consecutive pair \((b, b') \in \mathcal{O}\) on the chosen route:
\[
l_{i,b} + t_{i,b'}^{\text{run}} \leq e_{i,b'} + M(1 - u_{i,b'}), \quad \forall i \in T,\ (b,b') \in \mathcal{O}
\tag{3}
\]

Minimum dwell at stations:
\[
e_{i,b} + t_{i,b}^{\text{dwell}} \leq l_{i,b} + M(1 - u_{i,b}), \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B_s
\tag{4}
\]

### 6.3 Departure and Arrival Delay Definitions

\[
\delta_i^d \geq e_{i,b_{\text{first}}(i)} - d_i^0
\tag{5}
\]
\[
\delta_i^a \geq l_{i,b_{\text{last}}(i)} - a_i^0
\tag{6}
\]

### 6.4 Conflict / Headway Constraints (Disjunctive)

For each conflict pair \((i,j,b) \in \mathcal{C}\):

\[
l_{i,b} + t^{\text{head}} \leq e_{j,b} + M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) + M(1 - u_{i,b}) + M(1 - u_{j,b})
\tag{7}
\]
\[
l_{j,b} + t^{\text{head}} \leq e_{i,b} + M\,y_{i,j,b} + M(1 - u_{i,b}) + M(1 - u_{j,b})
\tag{8}
\]

Ordering symmetry:
\[
y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1, \quad \forall (i,j,b) \in \mathcal{C}
\tag{9}
\]

### 6.5 Overlap / Safety-Relevant Margin Constraints

If block \(b\) has a safety overlap \(o_b\):
\[
l_{i,b} + \frac{o_b}{v_{i,b}} \leq e_{j,b} + M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) + M(1 - u_{i,b}) + M(1 - u_{j,b})
\tag{10}
\]
where \(v_{i,b}\) is the nominal speed of train \(i\) on block \(b\).

### 6.6 Pair-wise Waiting Reformulation (Sub-optimal Model)

The pair-wise interpretation replaces standard delay variables:

\[
\delta_i^a \geq \sum_{j \neq i} z_{i,j} \cdot \tau_{j,i} - \Delta_i^0
\tag{11}
\]
where \(\tau_{j,i}\) is the estimated blocking time imposed by train \(j\) on train \(i\), and \(\Delta_i^0\) is the initial slack.

Waiting consistency:
\[
z_{i,j} + z_{j,i} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \neq j
\tag{12}
\]

**Assumption:** This formulation neglects delay propagation (as in the sub-optimal model of Section 3.1).

### 6.7 Delay Propagation Extension (Global Optimum Model)

To capture propagation, replace (11) with:

\[
\delta_i^a \geq \delta_j^a + \tau_{j,i} - \Delta_{j,i}^{\text{slack}}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{W}
\tag{13}
\]
where \(\mathcal{W}\) is the set of waiting relations and \(\Delta_{j,i}^{\text{slack}}\) is the available slack between trains.

### 6.8 Variable Domains

\[
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}, \quad z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}, \quad u_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}
\]
\[
e_{i,b}, l_{i,b}, \delta_i^a, \delta_i^d \geq 0
\]

---

## 7. Complete Model Summary

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{i \in T} \left( w_i^a \delta_i^a + w_i^d \delta_i^d \right) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& (1)\text{--}(13) \\
& x_{i,r}, y_{i,j,b}, z_{i,j}, u_{i,b} \in \{0,1\} \\
& e_{i,b}, l_{i,b}, \delta_i^a, \delta_i^d \geq 0
\end{aligned}
}
\]

---

## 8. Model Variants

| Variant | Description | Constraints Used |
|---|---|---|
| **Sub-optimal (fast)** | Rerouting + reordering, no delay propagation | (1)–(12) |
| **Global optimum** | Full rtRTMP with delay propagation | (1)–(10), (13) |
| **Extended (overlaps)** | Includes safety-relevant overlaps | (1)–(10), (13) + overlap (10) |

---

## 9. Key Assumptions (Explicitly Marked)

1. **Microscopic representation** — block sections as atomic resources (Assumption).
2. **Deterministic delays** — no stochastic disturbances within the horizon (Assumption).
3. **Pre-computed route set** \(R_i\) — generated offline via TRSP (Assumption, following Samà et al., 2016).
4. **Big-M values** — chosen sufficiently large to deactivate constraints (Assumption).
5. **No overtaking within a block** — enforced by disjunctive constraints (7)–(8) (Assumption).
6. **Weights** \(w_i^a, w_i^d\) — provided by dispatcher policy (Assumption).
7. **Overlap clearing time** — approximated as \(o_b / v_{i,b}\) (Assumption, following Lindenmaier et al., 2022).

---

## 10. Computational Notes

- The model is **NP-hard** (as noted in the introduction).
- **Decomposition strategy**: Solve routing/ordering first (sub-optimal model), then fix \(x_{i,r}\) and \(y_{i,j,b}\) and solve rescheduling (global optimum model).
- **Runtime reduction**: Fixing route variables reduces the number of binary variables by \(|R_i| \times |T|\), significantly decreasing the branch-and-bound tree size.
- **Optimality condition**: The sub-optimal model yields the global optimum when no delay propagation occurs, i.e., when \(\Delta_{j,i}^{\text{slack}} \geq \tau_{j,i}\) for all waiting pairs.

Text:
# A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Availability Constraints

## 1. Motivation and Scope

Based on the problem description, we construct a complete MILP that integrates two coupled decisions:

1. **Composition model** (rolling stock rescheduling): which train units (rolling stock) are assigned to which trips, and which shunting movements are required.
2. **Infrastructure model** (shunting feasibility): whether each proposed shunting movement can be scheduled on the available station tracks, possibly with small delays to other trains.

The MILP below is a *unified* formulation. In the paper, these two components are solved in an alternating (Benders-like / iterative) fashion; here we present them together so that the model is self-contained, linear, and directly solvable.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of train trips (services) in the timetable, indexed by $t$ |
| $U$ | Set of rolling stock units (train units), indexed by $u$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $K_s$ | Set of tracks at station $s$, indexed by $k$ |
| $M$ | Set of shunting movements, indexed by $m$ |
| $M^{in}_t$ | Shunting movements delivering units to trip $t$ |
| $M^{out}_t$ | Shunting movements removing units from trip $t$ |
| $A$ | Set of ordered pairs $(m, m')$ of shunting movements that **conflict** on the same track (i.e., cannot overlap in time) |
| $\mathcal{T}_s$ | Set of trips passing through station $s$ |

**Assumption A1.** Each shunting movement $m$ is associated with exactly one station $s(m) \in S$ and one origin/destination track.

**Assumption A2.** The set $A$ of conflicting movement pairs is precomputed from the infrastructure topology (track occupancy, switch positions, single-track segments).

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $c^{op}_t$ | Operational cost of operating trip $t$ |
| $c^{cap}_t$ | Penalty per unit of unmet seat demand on trip $t$ |
| $c^{dev}_t$ | Penalty for deviating from the original rolling stock assignment on trip $t$ |
| $c^{shift}_m$ | Cost of performing shunting movement $m$ |
| $c^{delay}_t$ | Penalty per minute of delay assigned to trip $t$ |
| $d_t$ | Passenger demand (seats required) on trip $t$ |
| $q_u$ | Capacity (number of seats) of unit $u$ |
| $r_{u,t}$ | $=1$ if unit $u$ was originally assigned to trip $t$ in the nominal plan, $0$ otherwise |
| $e_m$ | Earliest start time of shunting movement $m$ |
| $l_m$ | Latest end time of shunting movement $m$ |
| $\tau_m$ | Duration of shunting movement $m$ |
| $\Delta^{max}$ | Maximum allowed delay (minutes) for any train (e.g., $\Delta^{max}=5$) |
| $B$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $H$ | Length of the planning horizon |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Rolling stock assignment

$$
x_{u,t} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall u \in U,\ t \in T
$$
$=1$ if unit $u$ is assigned to trip $t$.

$$
y_{m} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall m \in M
$$
$=1$ if shunting movement $m$ is performed.

### 4.2 Capacity / passenger service

$$
z_t \ge 0, \quad \forall t \in T
$$
Unmet seat demand on trip $t$ (number of passengers without a seat).

### 4.3 Infrastructure / timing

$$
a_m \ge 0, \quad \forall m \in M
$$
Start time of shunting movement $m$.

$$
\delta_t \ge 0, \quad \forall t \in T
$$
Delay (in minutes) assigned to trip $t$.

$$
w_{m,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall m \in M,\ k \in K_{s(m)}
$$
$=1$ if shunting movement $m$ is assigned to track $k$.

$$
o_{m,m'} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (m,m') \in A
$$
$=1$ if movement $m$ is scheduled **before** movement $m'$ on their shared track.

---

## 5. Objective Function

We minimize a weighted sum of operational cost, passenger inconvenience, deviation from the original plan, shunting cost, and delay penalties:

$$
\min \quad
\underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} c^{op}_t \cdot \left(1 - \prod_{u} (1 - x_{u,t})\right)}_{\text{operating trips}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} c^{cap}_t \cdot z_t}_{\text{unmet demand}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} c^{dev}_t \cdot \sum_{u \in U} |x_{u,t} - r_{u,t}|}_{\text{plan deviation}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{m \in M} c^{shift}_m \cdot y_m}_{\text{shunting cost}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} c^{delay}_t \cdot \delta_t}_{\text{delay penalty}}
$$

**Linearization.** The product $\prod_u (1-x_{u,t})$ and the absolute value $|x_{u,t}-r_{u,t}|$ are nonlinear. We linearize:

- Introduce $v_t \in \{0,1\}$ with $v_t = 1$ iff trip $t$ is operated (at least one unit assigned):
$$
v_t \le \sum_{u \in U} x_{u,t}, \qquad v_t \ge x_{u,t} \quad \forall u \in U
$$
- Introduce $g_{u,t} \ge 0$ with $g_{u,t} \ge x_{u,t} - r_{u,t}$ and $g_{u,t} \ge r_{u,t} - x_{u,t}$.

The linear objective becomes:

$$
\boxed{
\min \quad
\sum_{t \in T} c^{op}_t v_t
+ \sum_{t \in T} c^{cap}_t z_t
+ \sum_{t \in T} c^{dev}_t \sum_{u \in U} g_{u,t}
+ \sum_{m \in M} c^{shift}_m y_m
+ \sum_{t \in T} c^{delay}_t \delta_t
}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Rolling stock assignment constraints

**(C1) Each trip receives at least one unit iff operated:**
$$
\sum_{u \in U} x_{u,t} \ge v_t, \qquad \sum_{u \in U} x_{u,t} \le |U| \cdot v_t, \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Each unit can be assigned to at most one trip at a time** (non-overlapping trips):
$$
x_{u,t} + x_{u,t'} \le 1, \quad \forall u \in U,\ \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C}^{overlap}
$$
where $\mathcal{C}^{overlap}$ is the set of trip pairs whose time windows overlap.

**(C3) Capacity satisfaction / unmet demand:**
$$
\sum_{u \in U} q_u \, x_{u,t} + z_t \ge d_t, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C4) Coupling of shunting movements to assignments:**
A shunting movement $m$ into trip $t$ is performed iff at least one unit is added to $t$:
$$
y_m \ge x_{u,t} - x_{u,t'}, \quad \forall m \in M^{in}_t,\ \forall u \in U
$$
$$
y_m \le \sum_{u \in U} (x_{u,t} - x_{u,t'}) + B(1 - y_m), \quad \forall m \in M^{in}_t
$$
where $t'$ is the preceding trip of the same unit. Analogous constraints apply for $M^{out}_t$.

**(C5) Unit balance (flow conservation) per unit:**
$$
\sum_{t \in T^{dep}_u} x_{u,t} = \sum_{t \in T^{arr}_u} x_{u,t}, \quad \forall u \in U
$$
(Each unit that departs from a station must have arrived there.)

---

### 6.2 Infrastructure / shunting feasibility constraints

**(C6) Each performed movement is assigned to exactly one track:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_{s(m)}} w_{m,k} = y_m, \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(C7) Time window for each movement:**
$$
a_m \ge e_m \cdot y_m, \qquad a_m + \tau_m \le l_m + B(1 - y_m), \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(C8) Non-overlap on the same track (disjunctive constraint):**
For each conflicting pair $(m,m') \in A$ sharing track $k$:
$$
a_{m'} \ge a_m + \tau_m - B(1 - o_{m,m'}) - B(2 - w_{m,k} - w_{m',k})
$$
$$
a_{m} \ge a_{m'} + \tau_{m'} - B \cdot o_{m,m'} - B(2 - w_{m,k} - w_{m',k})
$$
$$
o_{m,m'} + o_{m',m} \ge w_{m,k} + w_{m',k} - 1
$$

**(C9) Delay propagation to trips occupying the same infrastructure:**
If a shunting movement $m$ conflicts with trip $t$ on track $k$:
$$
\delta_t \ge a_m + \tau_m - t^{start}_t - B(1 - y_m) - B(1 - w_{m,k})
$$
$$
\delta_t \le \Delta^{max}, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C10) Track capacity (at most one movement per track at a time):**
$$
\sum_{m: s(m)=s,\ k \in K_s} w_{m,k} \le |K_s|, \quad \forall s \in S
$$

---

### 6.3 Linearization of deviation

**(C11) Deviation linearization:**
$$
g_{u,t} \ge x_{u,t} - r_{u,t}, \qquad g_{u,t} \ge r_{u,t} - x_{u,t}, \qquad g_{u,t} \ge 0
$$

---

### 6.4 Variable domains

$$
x_{u,t}, y_m, v_t, w_{m,k}, o_{m,m'} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_m, \delta_t, z_t, g_{u,t} \ge 0
$$

---

## 7. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| **A1** | Each shunting movement occurs at exactly one station and uses one track. |
| **A2** | The conflict set $A$ is precomputed from station topology; it captures all pairwise track incompatibilities. |
| **A3** | Delays are bounded by $\Delta^{max}$ (e.g., 5 minutes) and absorbed by timetable buffers downstream. |
| **A4** | Rolling stock units are homogeneous within a unit type; capacity $q_u$ is constant per type. |
| **A5** | Shunting movement durations $\tau_m$ are deterministic and known. |
| **A6** | The planning horizon $H$ is fixed; all trips and movements must complete within $H$. |
| **A7** | Passenger demand $d_t$ is known and deterministic per trip. |
| **A8** | The original plan $(r_{u,t})$ is given and feasible. |
| **A9** | Infrastructure availability (track closures) is encoded by removing tracks from $K_s$ or tightening $[e_m, l_m]$. |
| **A10** | The big-M constant $B$ is chosen as $B = H + \max_m \tau_m$. |

---

## 8. Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \sum_{t} c^{op}_t v_t + \sum_{t} c^{cap}_t z_t + \sum_{t} c^{dev}_t \sum_{u} g_{u,t} + \sum_{m} c^{shift}_m y_m + \sum_{t} c^{delay}_t \delta_t \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& \text{(C1)--(C11)} \\
& x_{u,t}, y_m, v_t, w_{m,k}, o_{m,m'} \in \{0,1\} \\
& a_m, \delta_t, z_t, g_{u,t} \ge 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 9. Solution Approach (as in the paper)

Because the full MILP is large, the paper solves it via:

1. **Composition model** — solves (C1)–(C5) and (C11) to propose a rolling stock plan and shunting movements.
2. **Infrastructure model** — solves (C6)–(C10) to check feasibility of the proposed movements.
3. **Benders-style cuts** — if the infrastructure model is infeasible, a cut is added to the composition model prohibiting that combination of shunting movements:
$$
\sum_{m \in \bar{M}} y_m - \sum_{m \notin \bar{M}} y_m \le |\bar{M}| - 1
$$
where $\bar{M}$ is the infeasible set of movements.
4. **Iterative heuristic** — feeds movements one at a time to the infrastructure model, mimicking the interaction between rolling stock dispatchers (NS) and infrastructure dispatchers (ProRail).

This yields a complete, linear, and solvable MILP framework for rolling stock rescheduling with explicit railway infrastructure availability constraints.

Text:
# MILP Model for Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

Below is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation extending the model of Liu et al. (2023a) to include **time-varying sectional passenger demands**, **flexible train composition**, and **rolling stock circulation**, as described in the input text.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S = \{1,2,\dots,N\}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ (1 = origin, $N$ = terminal) |
| $E = \{(s,s+1): s \in S\setminus\{N\}\}$ | Set of sections (track segments between consecutive stations), indexed by $e$ |
| $T = \{1,2,\dots,|T|\}$ | Set of trains in the prediction horizon, indexed by $i$ |
| $K = \{1,2,\dots,|K|\}$ | Set of equal-length time intervals approximating time-varying demand, indexed by $k$ |
| $R = \{1,2,\dots,|R|\}$ | Set of available rolling-stock units (cars) in the depot, indexed by $r$ |
| $O \subseteq S \times S$ | Set of origin–destination (OD) pairs, indexed by $o = (o^-, o^+)$ with $o^- < o^+$ |

**Assumption (A1):** The planning horizon $[0, H]$ is divided into $|K|$ equal intervals of length $\Delta t = H/|K|$. Interval $k$ covers $[\tau_k, \tau_{k+1})$ with $\tau_k = (k-1)\Delta t$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $d_{s,k}$ | Average passenger arrival rate at station $s$ during interval $k$ (pax/min) |
| $\alpha_{s,s'}$ | Fraction of passengers boarding at $s$ whose destination is $s'$ ($\sum_{s'>s}\alpha_{s,s'}=1$) |
| $C^{cap}$ | Seating/loading capacity per car (pax/car) |
| $M^{\min}, M^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum number of cars allowed in a train |
| $h^{\min}, h^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum headway between consecutive trains at any station |
| $w_s^{\min}, w_s^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $r_s^{\min}, r_s^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum running time on section $(s, s+1)$ |
| $L_s$ | Length of section $(s,s+1)$ (km) |
| $c^{op}$ | Operational cost per car-km (€/car·km) |
| $c^{wait}$ | Penalty per passenger-minute of waiting time (€/pax·min) |
| $c^{trav}$ | Penalty per passenger-minute of in-vehicle travel time (€/pax·min) |
| $c^{comp}$ | Fixed cost per car-kilometre of composition change (€/car) |
| $T_0^{dep}$ | Scheduled departure time of the first train from the origin |
| $M_{big}$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Timing variables (continuous)
- $a_{i,s}$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ (min)
- $d_{i,s}$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ (min)
- $r_{i,s}$: running time of train $i$ on section $(s,s+1)$ (min)
- $w_{i,s}$: dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ (min)

### Stopping and composition variables
- $x_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$, 0 otherwise
- $m_{i,s} \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$: number of cars of train $i$ when departing from station $s$

### Rolling-stock assignment variables
- $u_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if rolling-stock unit $r$ is assigned to train $i$ for its entire run
- $z_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if a coupling/uncoupling operation occurs at station $s$ for train $i$ (only meaningful at terminals)

### Passenger-flow variables (continuous)
- $b_{i,s,k} \geq 0$: passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ during interval $k$
- $e_{i,s,k} \geq 0$: passengers alighting from train $i$ at station $s$ during interval $k$
- $l_{i,s} \geq 0$: passenger load on train $i$ after departing station $s$
- $\delta_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ during interval $k$

### Auxiliary variables
- $W_{i,s} \geq 0$: average waiting time of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ (min)

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the total cost composed of operational cost, passenger waiting time, in-vehicle travel time, and composition-change cost:

$$
\min Z = 
\underbrace{c^{op}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s=1}^{N-1} m_{i,s}\, L_s}_{\text{operational cost}} \;+\;
\underbrace{c^{wait}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K} b_{i,s,k}\, W_{i,s}}_{\text{passenger waiting time}} \;+\;
\underbrace{c^{trav}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} l_{i,s}\, r_{i,s}}_{\text{in-vehicle travel time}} \;+\;
\underbrace{c^{comp}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{r \in R}\sum_{s \in S} |u_{i,r,s} - u_{i,r,s-1}|}_{\text{composition change cost}}
$$

The last term is linearized below in (R7).

---

## 5. Constraints

### (R1) Timing consistency
$$
d_{i,s} = a_{i,s} + w_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + r_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s = 1,\dots,N-1
$$

### (R2) Dwell-time bounds (linked to stopping)
$$
w_{i,s}^{\min}\, x_{i,s} \leq w_{i,s} \leq w_{i,s}^{\max}\, x_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (R3) Running-time bounds
$$
r_{i,s}^{\min} \leq r_{i,s} \leq r_{i,s}^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s = 1,\dots,N-1
$$

### (R4) Headway constraints
$$
h^{\min} \leq d_{i+1,s} - d_{i,s} \leq h^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T\setminus\{|T|\},\; s \in S
$$

### (R5) Mandatory stops at terminals and optional intermediate stops
$$
x_{i,1} = x_{i,N} = 1, \quad \forall i \in T
$$

### (R6) Train composition bounds and consistency
$$
M^{\min} \leq m_{i,s} \leq M^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
m_{i,s} = \sum_{r \in R} u_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (R7) Rolling-stock circulation: each car used by at most one train
$$
\sum_{i \in T} u_{i,r} \leq 1, \quad \forall r \in R
$$

### (R8) Composition-change linearization
Introduce auxiliary binary $v_{i,r,s} \in \{0,1\}$ indicating a change of assignment of car $r$ between stations $s-1$ and $s$:
$$
v_{i,r,s} \geq u_{i,r,s} - u_{i,r,s-1}, \qquad
v_{i,r,s} \geq u_{i,r,s-1} - u_{i,r,s}, \quad \forall i,r,s
$$
The composition-change cost becomes $c^{comp}\sum_{i,r,s} v_{i,r,s}$.

**Assumption (A2):** Coupling/uncoupling is allowed only at terminal stations to keep the model tractable; intermediate stations enforce $m_{i,s+1}=m_{i,s}$.

### (R9) Interval assignment for departures (links continuous time to discrete demand intervals)
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \delta_{i,s,k} = 1, \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\tau_k - M_{big}(1-\delta_{i,s,k}) \leq d_{i,s} \leq \tau_{k+1} + M_{big}(1-\delta_{i,s,k}), \quad \forall i,s,k
$$

### (R10) Demand satisfaction (all arriving passengers must board)
$$
\sum_{i \in T} b_{i,s,k} = d_{s,k}\, \Delta t, \quad \forall s \in S,\; k \in K
$$

### (R11) Passenger alighting (OD-based)
$$
e_{i,s,k} = \sum_{s' < s} \alpha_{s',s}\, b_{i,s',k}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S,\; k \in K
$$

### (R12) Passenger-flow conservation (load recursion)
$$
l_{i,s} = l_{i,s-1} + \sum_{k \in K}\bigl(b_{i,s,k} - e_{i,s,k}\bigr), \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
with boundary condition $l_{i,0} = 0$ (train empty at origin).

### (R13) Capacity constraint (load cannot exceed train capacity)
$$
l_{i,s} \leq m_{i,s}\, C^{cap}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (R14) Average waiting-time computation
Assuming passengers arrive uniformly within interval $k$, the average waiting time of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ is:
$$
W_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} \delta_{i,s,k}\Bigl(d_{i,s} - \tau_k - \tfrac{\Delta t}{2}\Bigr), \quad \forall i,s
$$

**Assumption (A3):** Uniform passenger arrival within each interval — a standard approximation for piecewise-constant demand.

### (R15) First-train anchor
$$
d_{1,1} = T_0^{dep}
$$

### (R16) Non-negativity and binary restrictions
$$
a_{i,s},\, d_{i,s},\, r_{i,s},\, w_{i,s},\, l_{i,s},\, b_{i,s,k},\, e_{i,s,k},\, W_{i,s} \geq 0
$$
$$
x_{i,s},\, u_{i,r},\, \delta_{i,s,k},\, v_{i,r,s} \in \{0,1\}, \qquad m_{i,s} \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

The resulting optimization problem is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{a,d,r,w,x,m,u,v,\delta,b,e,l,W} \quad & Z \;=\; \text{(Objective)}\\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(R1)–(R16)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is a **mixed-integer linear program (MILP)** because:
- Continuous variables: $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, r_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, l_{i,s}, b_{i,s,k}, e_{i,s,k}, W_{i,s}$.
- Integer variables: $m_{i,s}$ (composition) and binary variables $x_{i,s}, u_{i,r}, \delta_{i,s,k}, v_{i,r,s}$.

---

## 7. Key Assumptions Recap

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | The planning horizon is divided into equal-length intervals for piecewise-constant demand approximation. |
| A2 | Coupling/uncoupling of cars is permitted only at terminal stations; composition is constant along the line. |
| A3 | Passengers arrive uniformly within each time interval (used for waiting-time computation). |
| A4 | All arriving passengers are eventually served (no passenger left behind). |
| A5 | OD proportions $\alpha_{s,s'}$ are deterministic and time-invariant within the horizon. |
| A6 | The rolling-stock depot has a fixed pool of cars; no deadhead trips are considered. |
| A7 | Track and signaling infrastructure allow any headway within $[h^{\min}, h^{\max}]$. |

---

## 8. Remarks on Integration with the Learning-Based MPC Framework

As stated in the input, this MILP is solved inside an **MPC loop** at each decision step. To enable real-time computation, the integer variables $\{m_{i,s}, x_{i,s}, u_{i,r}\}$ can be predicted by an **LSTM network** (after presolve pruning), and the remaining continuous variables are obtained by solving the LP relaxation of the above model with the integer variables fixed. This preserves feasibility guarantees while drastically reducing online computation time.

Text:
# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the **final, complete, linear** mixed-integer programming model for the integrated TRSMP under a partial segment blockage with local rerouting (use of the opposite track within the disruption time window).

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations/nodes, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $e$; segment $e = (s, s+1)$ connects $s$ to $s+1$ |
| $\mathcal{E}^{b} \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | Set of blocked segments during the disruption window |
| $\mathcal{S}_i \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Ordered set of stations visited by train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{E}_i \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | Ordered set of segments traversed by train $i$; $e \in \mathcal{E}_i$ iff $e = (s, s+1)$ with $s, s+1 \in \mathcal{S}_i$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $l$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_e$ | Set of unordered train pairs $\{i,j\}$ that may share segment $e$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\text{dir}(i) \in \{+,-\}$ | Intrinsic travel direction of train $i$ |
| $a_i^{0}(s)$, $d_i^{0}(s)$ | Scheduled arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ (km) |
| $\tau_{e,l}$ | Running time on segment $e$ at speed level $l$ (time units) |
| $E_{e,l}$ | Energy consumption on segment $e$ at speed level $l$ (kWh) |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum speed of the highest level $l \in \mathcal{L}$ |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway, same direction, same track |
| $h_{\min}^{\text{bi}}$ | Minimum headway, opposite directions sharing the opposite track (≥ $h_{\min}$) |
| $t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window on $e \in \mathcal{E}^{b}$ |
| $M$ | Big-M constant, large enough to dominate all finite scheduling variables |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \geq 0$ | Objective weights for total delay, total energy, and cancellations |

**Derived headway** (precomputed):
$$h_{i,j,e} = \begin{cases} h_{\min}^{\text{bi}}, & \text{if } \text{dir}(i) \neq \text{dir}(j) \text{ and } \{i,j\} \in \mathcal{P}_e \\ h_{\min}, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled, 0 otherwise |
| $r_{i,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $e$; 0 = normal track |
| $y_{i,e,l}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $l$ on segment $e$ |
| $u_{i,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | For $e \in \mathcal{E}^{b}$: 0 = pass normal track **before** window, 1 = **after** window |
| $\sigma_{i,j,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | For $\{i,j\} \in \mathcal{P}_e$ with $i<j$: 1 if train $i$ precedes $j$ on the shared track |
| $z_{i,j,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | XOR indicator: 1 iff $r_{i,e} \neq r_{j,e}$ (trains use different physical tracks) |
| $d_{i,s}, a_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Departure / arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $T^{\text{occ}}_{i,e}$ | $\geq 0$ | Time train $i$ begins occupying segment $e$ |
| $T^{\text{rel}}_{i,e}$ | $\geq 0$ | Time train $i$ releases segment $e$ |
| $T^{\text{run}}_{i,e}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $\Delta_i$ | $\geq 0$ | Final-station delay of train $i$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{\;\min\;\; \alpha \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} \Delta_i \;+\; \beta \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}_i}\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}} E_{e,l}\, y_{i,e,l} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} x_i\;}
$$

A weighted sum of total delay, total energy consumption, and a cancellation penalty.

---

## 5. Constraints

### C1 — Speed-level selection (exactly one if not cancelled)

$$
\sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} y_{i,e,l} = 1 - x_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; e \in \mathcal{E}_i
$$

A non-cancelled train picks exactly one speed level on each segment; a cancelled train picks none.

### C2 — Segment occupation linking

For each $e = (s, s+1) \in \mathcal{E}_i$:

$$
T^{\text{occ}}_{i,e} = d_{i,s}, \qquad T^{\text{rel}}_{i,e} = a_{i,s+1}
$$

The occupation interval of a segment coincides with the departure from the upstream station and the arrival at the downstream station.

### C3 — Occupation ordering

$$
T^{\text{occ}}_{i,e} \le T^{\text{rel}}_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; e \in \mathcal{E}_i
$$

Entry no later than exit.

### C4 — Running-time definition

$$
T^{\text{rel}}_{i,e} - T^{\text{occ}}_{i,e} = T^{\text{run}}_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; e \in \mathcal{E}_i
$$

Running time equals the length of the occupation interval. Couples the timetable to dynamics.

### C5 — Running-time / speed-level coupling

$$
T^{\text{run}}_{i,e} = \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} \tau_{e,l}\, y_{i,e,l}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; e \in \mathcal{E}_i
$$

Running time is the constant running time corresponding to the chosen speed level. (Linearizes the nonlinear $\tau = L/v$.)

### C6 — Minimum physical running time

$$
T^{\text{run}}_{i,e} \ge \frac{L_e}{v_{\max}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; e \in \mathcal{E}_i
$$

No train runs faster than the maximum speed. (Implied by C5 if $\tau_{e,l} \geq L_e/v_{\max}$; stated explicitly for safety.)

### C7 — Train continuity at intermediate stations

$$
a_{i,s} \le d_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; s \in \mathcal{S}_i \setminus \{\text{first}, \text{last}\}
$$

Arrival precedes departure (dwell time nonnegative).

### C8 — Delay definition at the final station

$$
\Delta_i \ge a_{i,\text{last}(i)} - a_i^{0}(\text{last}(i)) - M\, x_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}
$$

The delay variable lower-bounds the lateness at the destination. If cancelled, the RHS is relaxed so that $\Delta_i$ may be 0.

### C9 — Cancellation consistency

$$
d_{i,s} \le M(1 - x_i), \quad a_{i,s} \le M(1 - x_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; s \in \mathcal{S}_i
$$

All timing variables of a cancelled train are unconstrained relative to a feasible solution (the objective drives them to zero).

### C10 — XOR linearization of track usage

For each $\{i,j\} \in \mathcal{P}_e$, $i < j$:

$$
z_{i,j,e} \ge r_{i,e} - r_{j,e}
$$
$$
z_{i,j,e} \ge r_{j,e} - r_{i,e}
$$
$$
z_{i,j,e} \le r_{i,e} + r_{j,e}
$$
$$
z_{i,j,e} \le 2 - r_{i,e} - r_{j,e}
$$

Standard XOR linearization: $z_{i,j,e} = 1 \iff r_{i,e} \neq r_{j,e}$ (the two trains use different physical tracks).

### C11 — Pairwise ordering / separation (only on shared tracks)

For each $\{i,j\} \in \mathcal{P}_e$, $i < j$:

$$
T^{\text{occ}}_{j,e} \ge T^{\text{rel}}_{i,e} + h_{i,j,e} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,e}) - M x_i - M x_j - M z_{i,j,e}
$$

$$
T^{\text{occ}}_{i,e} \ge T^{\text{rel}}_{j,e} + h_{i,j,e} - M\,\sigma_{i,j,e} - M x_i - M x_j - M z_{i,j,e}
$$

If both trains are active ($x_i = x_j = 0$), use the *same* track ($z_{i,j,e} = 0$), and $\sigma_{i,j,e} = 1$, then $j$ enters after $i$ releases with headway $h_{i,j,e}$. If $\sigma_{i,j,e} = 0$, the role reverses. Otherwise the constraint is relaxed.

**Bidirectional conflict is fully subsumed** by C11 with $h_{\min}^{\text{bi}}$: two trains rerouted onto the same opposite track satisfy $r_{i,e} = r_{j,e} = 1 \Rightarrow z_{i,j,e} = 0$, and the headway $h_{i,j,e} = h_{\min}^{\text{bi}}$ enforces safe separation.

### C12 — Sigma-relaxation when constraints are inactive

For each $\{i,j\} \in \mathcal{P}_e$, $i < j$:

$$
\sigma_{i,j,e} \ge 1 - x_i - x_j - z_{i,j,e}
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,j,e} \le 1 + x_i + x_j + z_{i,j,e}
$$

When the pair is not constrained (cancelled or on different tracks), $\sigma$ is free; otherwise the model selects an ordering.

### C13 — Disruption window: normal-track regime ($r_{i,e} = 0$, $e \in \mathcal{E}^{b}$)

Binary $u_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$ selects "before" vs "after":

$$
T^{\text{rel}}_{i,e} \le t_{\text{start}} + M u_{i,e} + M r_{i,e}
$$
$$
T^{\text{occ}}_{i,e} \ge t_{\text{end}} - M(1 - u_{i,e}) - M r_{i,e}
$$

- $r_{i,e} = 0,\ u_{i,e} = 0$: pass entirely **before** the window.
- $r_{i,e} = 0,\ u_{i,e} = 1$: pass entirely **after** the window.
- $r_{i,e} = 1$: both constraints are relaxed; C14 governs.

### C14 — Disruption window: opposite-track regime ($r_{i,e} = 1$, $e \in \mathcal{E}^{b}$)

$$
T^{\text{occ}}_{i,e} \ge t_{\text{start}} - M(1 - r_{i,e})
$$
$$
T^{\text{rel}}_{i,e} \le t_{\text{end}} + M(1 - r_{i,e})
$$

- $r_{i,e} = 1$: occupation interval lies **inside** $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$ — the rerouting regime.
- $r_{i,e} = 0$: both constraints relaxed; C13 governs.

Together C13 and C14 force **exactly one valid regime** per $(i,e)$ on every blocked segment.

### C15 — Domain constraints

$$
d_{i,s},\, a_{i,s},\, T^{\text{occ}}_{i,e},\, T^{\text{rel}}_{i,e},\, T^{\text{run}}_{i,e},\, \Delta_i \;\ge\; 0
$$
$$
x_i,\, r_{i,e},\, y_{i,e,l},\, u_{i,e},\, \sigma_{i,j,e},\, z_{i,j,e} \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Explicit List of Assumptions

1. **Discrete speed levels per segment.** Each non-cancelled train picks one speed level $l \in \mathcal{L}$ per segment.
2. **Constant running time per (segment, speed level).** Acceleration/deceleration dynamics are absorbed into the precomputed $\tau_{e,l}$.
3. **Zero minimum dwell, nonnegative dwell.** C7 admits any nonnegative dwell; a minimum can be added as $d_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} + \underline{\text{dw}}_i$ if desired.
4. **Differentiated headway.** Same-direction/same-track = $h_{\min}$; opposite-direction rerouting = $h_{\min}^{\text{bi}} \geq h_{\min}$.
5. **Intrinsic direction fixed.** $\text{dir}(i)$ is a static parameter; no mid-trip reversals.
6. **Rerouting is a physical track swap only.** $r_{i,e} = 1$ means using the opposite-direction physical track on segment $e$.
7. **Blocked segments $\mathcal{E}^{b}$.** The "normal" track is unavailable during $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$. The opposite track is available only within this window; the normal track is available only outside it.
8. **Single disruption window per blocked segment.** Parameters $t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}$ are common across trains for a given $e$.
9. **Headway applies to occupation intervals.** Separation measured from release of preceding train to occupation start of following train.
10. **Cancellation is total.** A cancelled train contributes no delay, no energy, only the penalty $\gamma$; all its timings are unconstrained.
11. **No overtaking within a segment on the same track.** Pairwise ordering C11 enforces sequential passage.
12. **Big-M validity.** $M \geq \max(t_{\text{end}},\; \max_s a_i^{0}(s)) + \max(h_{i,j,e}) + 1$.
13. **Pair set $\mathcal{P}_e$.** Only pairs that could share a physical track on $e$ are considered; no spurious headway constraints.
14. **Delay linearization.** $\Delta_i$ lower-bounds final-station lateness; equality can be enforced if desired with an additional upper-bound big-M constraint.
15. **No time-indexed binaries.** Conflict-freeness is fully captured by C10–C12.

---

## 7. Model Type and Properties

- **Type:** Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP).
- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear. The nonlinear relationship $\tau = L/v$ is linearized via the discrete speed-level binary selector $y_{i,e,l}$ (C5). Disjunctive regime, ordering, and headway constraints are linearized via big-M and dedicated auxiliary binaries.
- **Decisions coupled in one model:**
  - **Retiming** (departures/arrivals at each station) — variables $d_{i,s}, a_{i,s}$.
  - **Reordering** (sequence on each track) — variables $\sigma_{i,j,e}$.
  - **Rerouting** (normal vs opposite track on blocked segments) — variables $r_{i,e}$ with regime logic C13/C14.
  - **Cancellation** — variables $x_i$.
  - **Speed profile** (speed level per segment) — variables $y_{i,e,l}$, coupled to running times C4–C5 and to energy in the objective.
- **Feasibility guarantees:** Conflict-free operation on each physical track is enforced by C11/C12 with appropriate headway $h_{i,j,e}$ (covering both same-direction and bidirectional rerouting cases). The disruption regime logic C13/C14 ensures that every crossing of a blocked segment respects the disruption window either by avoiding it or by using the opposite track inside it.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)
## Complete Linear MILP Formulation

This MILP jointly decides retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellations, and energy-optimal speed profiles for high-speed trains under a partial segment blockage with bidirectional rerouting capability. All logical conditions are encoded via Big-M and auxiliary binaries, yielding a fully linear model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Stations, ordered $s=1,\dots,|\mathcal{S}|$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Segments $e=(s,s+1)$ between adjacent stations |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Trains, $i,j\in\mathcal{T}$ with direction $d_i\in\{\text{UP},\text{DOWN}\}$ |
| $\Omega\subseteq\mathcal{E}$ | Disruption-affected segments |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Discretized speed profiles available per segment |
| $s_i^{\text{first}}, s_i^{\text{last}}$ | Origin / terminal station of train $i$ |

For each segment $e=(s,s+1)$, denote $s^-=s$ (origin station) and $s^+=s+1$ (destination station).

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $D_e$ | Length of segment $e$ |
| $v^{\max},v^{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum operating speed |
| $t^{d,\min}_i, t^{d,\max}_i$ | Min / max dwell time of train $i$ |
| $t^{r,\min}_{ie}, t^{r,\max}_{ie}$ | Min / max running time of train $i$ on $e$ |
| $E_{iep}$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on $e$ with profile $p$ |
| $\tau_{iep}$ | Running time of train $i$ on $e$ with profile $p$ |
| $\tau^{\text{nom}}_{ie}$ | Nominal timetabled running time |
| $h$ | Minimum safety headway |
| $\text{rel}_i$ | Earliest release time of train $i$ |
| $\text{dl}_i$ | Latest allowed terminal arrival of train $i$ |
| $a^{\text{sch}}_{i,\text{last}}$ | Scheduled terminal arrival of train $i$ |
| $[t^{\text{start}}_e, t^{\text{end}}_e]$ | Blockage window for $e\in\Omega$ |
| $C^{\text{delay}},C^{\text{cancel}},C^{\text{dev}}$ | Objective cost weights |
| $M$ | Big-M constant, e.g. $M \geq \max(\text{dl}_i)-\min(\text{rel}_i)+\max_{e}(\tau^{\text{nom}}_{ie})$ |

**Pre-computed deviation constants:** $D^{\text{dev}}_{iep} = |\tau_{iep}-\tau^{\text{nom}}_{ie}|\geq 0$ (no absolute value nonlinearity remains in the model).

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous**
- $x_{is}\geq 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $y_{is}\geq 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $w_{is}\geq 0$: dwell-time extension of train $i$ at station $s$

**Binary**
- $u_{ie}\in\{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ reroutes onto opposite track on affected segment $e$
- $z_{iep}\in\{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ selects profile $p$ on segment $e$
- $\alpha_{ije}\in\{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ precedes $j$ on $e$ (same direction)
- $\beta_{ije}\in\{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ precedes $j$ on the shared opposite track (opposite directions)
- $\theta_{ije}\in\{0,1\}$: $1$ if both $i$ and $j$ reroute on $e$ (AND-linearization of $u_{ie}u_{je}$)
- $\text{act}_{ie}\in\{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$'s passage on $e$ overlaps the blockage window
- $c_i\in\{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ is cancelled

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min Z \;=\; \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} E_{iep}\,z_{iep}}_{\text{energy}}
\;+\; C^{\text{delay}} \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} \bigl(x_{i,s_i^{\text{last}}}-a^{\text{sch}}_{i,\text{last}}\bigr)}_{\text{terminal delay}}
\;+\; C^{\text{cancel}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} c_i
\;+\; C^{\text{dev}} \underbrace{\sum_{i}\sum_{e}\sum_{p} D^{\text{dev}}_{iep}\,z_{iep}}_{\text{speed-profile deviation}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Profile selection
$$
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} z_{iep} = 1 - c_i \quad \forall\, i\in\mathcal{T},\; e\in\mathcal{E} \tag{C1}
$$

### 5.2 Running-time coupling (time–space propagation)
$$
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \tau_{iep}\,z_{iep} = x_{i,s+1}-y_{is} \quad \forall\, i,\; e=(s,s+1)\in\mathcal{E} \tag{C2}
$$

### 5.3 Dwell-time bounds (interior stations)
$$
t^{d,\min}_i(1-c_i) \;\le\; y_{is}-x_{is} \;\le\; t^{d,\max}_i + w_{is} \quad \forall\, i,\; s \text{ internal} \tag{C3}
$$

### 5.4 Release time
$$
x_{i,s_i^{\text{first}}} \;\ge\; \text{rel}_i\,(1-c_i) \quad \forall\, i \tag{C4}
$$

### 5.5 Terminal deadline
$$
x_{i,s_i^{\text{last}}} \;\le\; \text{dl}_i + M\,c_i \quad \forall\, i \tag{C5}
$$

### 5.6 Disruption blockage (avoid closed track unless rerouted)
**Activation — does train $i$ use segment $e$ during $[t^{\text{start}}_e, t^{\text{end}}_e]$?**
$$
y_{is} \;\ge\; t^{\text{start}}_e - M(1-\text{act}_{ie}), \qquad
y_{is} \;\le\; t^{\text{end}}_e + M(1-\text{act}_{ie}) \tag{C6a}
$$
**Train must clear the window or reroute:**
$$
y_{is} \;\le\; t^{\text{start}}_e - t^{r,\min}_{ie} + M\bigl(u_{ie}+(1-\text{act}_{ie})\bigr) \tag{C6b}
$$
$$
y_{is} \;\ge\; t^{\text{end}}_e - M\bigl(u_{ie}+(1-\text{act}_{ie})\bigr) \tag{C6c}
$$

### 5.7 Reroute feasibility
$$
u_{ie} \le 1-c_i \quad \forall\, i,e; \qquad u_{ie}=0 \;\;\forall\, i,\; e\notin\Omega \tag{C7}
$$

### 5.8 Same-direction headway and ordering on segment $e=(s,s+1)$
For all pairs $i\neq j$ with $d_i=d_j$:
$$
\alpha_{ije} + \alpha_{jie} = 1 \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
y_{is} - y_{js} \;\ge\; h - M(1-\alpha_{ije}) \tag{C8b}
$$
$$
x_{i,s+1} - x_{j,s+1} \;\ge\; h - M(1-\alpha_{ije}) \tag{C8c}
$$

### 5.9 Bidirectional conflict on shared opposite track (opposite directions)
For all pairs $i\neq j$ with $d_i\neq d_j$ and $e\in\Omega$:
**AND-linearization:** $\theta_{ije}=u_{ie}\wedge u_{je}$:
$$
\theta_{ije} \le u_{ie},\quad \theta_{ije}\le u_{je},\quad \theta_{ije}\ge u_{ie}+u_{je}-1 \tag{C9a}
$$
**Ordering on shared track:**
$$
\beta_{ije}+\beta_{jie}=1 \tag{C9b}
$$
**Headway enforcement (whichever passes first must clear before the other enters):**
$$
x_{j,s+1}-y_{is} \;\ge\; h - M\bigl(1-\theta_{ije}\bigr) - M\bigl(1-\beta_{ije}\bigr) \tag{C9c}
$$
$$
x_{i,s+1}-y_{js} \;\ge\; h - M\bigl(1-\theta_{ije}\bigr) - M\beta_{ije} \tag{C9d}
$$

### 5.10 Time-order consistency
$$
y_{is} \ge x_{is}, \qquad x_{i,s+1}\ge y_{is} \quad \forall\, i,s \tag{C10}
$$

### 5.11 Variable domains
$$
x_{is},y_{is},w_{is}\geq 0;\quad u_{ie},z_{iep},\alpha_{ije},\beta_{ije},\theta_{ije},\text{act}_{ie},c_i\in\{0,1\} \tag{C11}
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions

1. **All-stop service.** Trains stop at every station of their itinerary unless cancelled (no skip-stop).
2. **Pre-discretized profiles.** Speed management is approximated by a finite set $\mathcal{P}$ of profiles with known $(\tau,E)$ pairs; continuous dynamics are not modeled.
3. **Bounded dwell.** Dwell times lie in $[t^{d,\min}_i, t^{d,\max}_i]$; only *extension* is allowed via $w_{is}\geq 0$.
4. **Single-track blockage.** A disruption blocks exactly one side of segment $e\in\Omega$ for a known window $[t^{\text{start}}_e,t^{\text{end}}_e]$.
5. **Opposite-track rerouting** is allowed only on affected segments during their blockage window, governed by $u_{ie}$.
6. **Fixed headway $h$.** Constant minimum separation for same-direction and bidirectional shared-track conflict resolution.
7. **Direction-fixed trains.** Each train $i$ has fixed direction $d_i$; reversal is not modeled.
8. **Cancellation as last resort.** $c_i=1$ removes all constraints for $i$ (except those that remain universally linked, e.g. via $\theta$) and incurs $C^{\text{cancel}}$ cost.
9. **Disjoint bidirectional conflict window.** Opposing trains may conflict only on $\Omega$ during the rerouting window — exactly what $\theta_{ije}$ enforces.
10. **Big-M validity.** $M$ is sized to $M \geq \max_i \text{dl}_i - \min_i \text{rel}_i + \max_{e}\tau^{\text{nom}}_{ie}$ so that all disjunctive relaxations are non-binding when not active while keeping LP relaxations tight.

---

## 7. Notes on Linearity

Every logical clause is encoded linearly:
- $u_{ie}u_{je}$ → AND-linearization with $\theta_{ije}$ (C9a)
- "Either outside the window or reroute" → Big-M disjunctions (C6b–C6c)
- "Either $i$ before $j$ or $j$ before $i$" → ordering binaries $\alpha_{ije}$, $\beta_{ije}$ (C8a, C9b)
- Absolute value in deviation cost → precomputed parameter $D^{\text{dev}}_{iep}$ (constant)

The resulting model is a **pure MILP** solvable by any standard branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut solver (CPLEX, Gurobi, HiGHS, etc.).

---

## 8. Compact Constraint Summary

| # | Constraint | Role |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Profile selection | One profile per (i,e), unless cancelled |
| C2 | Time–space coupling | Selected profile time equals inter-station travel time |
| C3 | Dwell bounds | Min dwell + extendable via $w_{is}$ |
| C4–C5 | Release / deadline | Service window of each train |
| C6a | Blockage activation | Detects overlap with disruption window |
| C6b–C6c | Blockage avoidance | Wait or reroute |
| C7 | Reroute feasibility | Only on $\Omega$, only if not cancelled |
| C8 | Same-direction headway | Ordering + time separation |
| C9 | Bidirectional conflict | AND + ordering + headway on shared track |
| C10 | Time consistency | $x\leq y\leq x_{\text{next}}$ |
| C11 | Variable domains | Non-negativity and binarity |

The model is self-contained, linear, and ready for implementation. Its solution yields simultaneously the conflict-free rescheduled timetable $(x^*,y^*)$, the energy-optimal speed profiles $z^*$, the rerouting pattern $u^*$, the train orderings $\alpha^*,\beta^*$, and any cancellations $c^*$.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code. All equations are presented as text; no code is returned.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations / segment boundaries, indexed by $s = 1,\dots,|S|$ |
| $K$ | Set of segments, indexed by $k$ (segment $k$ connects station $k$ and $k+1$) |
| $P$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $p$ |
| $W$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $t$ |
| $B \subseteq K$ | Set of blocked segments (disruption area) |
| $TT$ | Set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ with $i \neq j$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $d_i \in \{0,1\}$ | Direction of train $i$ (0 = up, 1 = down) |
| $\text{orig}_i,\ \text{dest}_i$ | Origin and destination stations of train $i$ |
| $\text{dep}^{\text{sched}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\text{arr}^{\text{sched}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_{k,p}$ | Running time on segment $k$ using speed level $p$ |
| $e_{k,p}$ | Energy consumption on segment $k$ using speed level $p$ |
| $\underline{\text{dw}}_{i,s},\ \overline{\text{dw}}_{i,s}$ | Min / max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $H$ | Minimum safety headway |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $c^{\text{delay}},\ c^{\text{energy}},\ c^{\text{cancel}}$ | Cost coefficients for delay, energy, cancellation |
| $t_{\text{start}},\ t_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window bounds |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,k,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ with speed level $p$ |
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $y_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $k$ |
| $z_{i,j,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ |
| $u_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled on segment $k$ |
| $\text{delay}_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Total delay of train $i$ at destination |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\alpha_{i,s,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Time-grid selector for arrival time |
| $\beta_{i,s,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Time-grid selector for departure time |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalty:

$$
\min\ Z = \sum_{i \in T} c^{\text{delay}}\,\text{delay}_i
\;+\; \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{k \in K}\sum_{p \in P} c^{\text{energy}}\, e_{k,p}\, x_{i,k,p}
\;+\; \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{k \in K} c^{\text{cancel}}\, u_{i,k}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Speed profile selection** — each train picks exactly one speed level per segment, or is cancelled on that segment:

$$
\sum_{p \in P} x_{i,k,p} + u_{i,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ k \in K
$$

**(2) Running-time consistency** — arrival at next station equals departure plus running time:

$$
a_{i,k+1} - d_{i,k} = \sum_{p \in P} r_{k,p}\, x_{i,k,p} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ k \in K
$$

**(3) Dwell-time bounds:**

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \ge \underline{\text{dw}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$
$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le \overline{\text{dw}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$

**(4) Departure from origin** — cannot depart earlier than scheduled:

$$
d_{i,\text{orig}_i} \ge \text{dep}^{\text{sched}}_{i,\text{orig}_i} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(5) Delay at destination:**

$$
\text{delay}_i \ge a_{i,\text{dest}_i} - \text{arr}^{\text{sched}}_{i,\text{dest}_i} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(6) Station delay definition:**

$$
\delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - \text{arr}^{\text{sched}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$

**(7) Headway / ordering on the same track:**

$$
d_{j,k} \ge a_{i,k+1} + H - M\,(1 - z_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TT,\ k \in K
$$

$$
z_{i,j,k} + z_{j,i,k} = 1 \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TT,\ k \in K
$$

**(8) Rerouting restriction** — rerouting only allowed on blocked segments:

$$
y_{i,k} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ k \notin B
$$

**(9) Rerouting time window** — rerouting only within $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$:

$$
d_{i,k} \ge t_{\text{start}} - M\,(1 - y_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in T,\ k \in B
$$
$$
a_{i,k+1} \le t_{\text{end}} + M\,(1 - y_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in T,\ k \in B
$$

**(10) Bidirectional conflict on shared track** (opposite-direction trains on blocked segment $k \in B$):

$$
a_{j,k+1} \ge a_{i,k+1} + H - M\,(1 - z_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TT,\ k \in B,\ d_i \neq d_j
$$
$$
a_{i,k+1} \ge a_{j,k+1} + H - M\,z_{i,j,k} \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TT,\ k \in B,\ d_i \neq d_j
$$

**(11) Cancellation monotonicity** — once cancelled, stays cancelled downstream:

$$
u_{i,k} \le u_{i,k+1} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ k,\ k+1 \in K
$$

**(12) Time-grid linking** (Assumption A1 — discretized times):

$$
a_{i,s} = \sum_{t \in W} t\,\alpha_{i,s,t}, \qquad \sum_{t \in W} \alpha_{i,s,t} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$
$$
d_{i,s} = \sum_{t \in W} t\,\beta_{i,s,t}, \qquad \sum_{t \in W} \beta_{i,s,t} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$

**(13) Non-negativity:** $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \text{delay}_i, \delta_{i,s} \ge 0$.

**(14) Binary domains:** $x_{i,k,p}, y_{i,k}, z_{i,j,k}, u_{i,k}, \alpha_{i,s,t}, \beta_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$.

---

## 6. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **A1** — Continuous times are approximated by a fine discrete time grid $W$ via selector binaries $\alpha, \beta$.
- **A2** — Cancellation is modeled per segment and is monotone downstream (constraint 11).
- **A3** — Running time and energy depend only on (segment, discrete speed level); no continuous speed control.
- **A4** — Rerouting is permitted only for segments in $B$ and only within the disruption window $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$.
- **A5** — Headway $H$ is symmetric and identical for both directions.
- **A6** — Dwell times are bounded by min/max; no explicit passenger-transfer constraints.

---

## 7. Model Class

The formulation is a **pure Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP)**: all nonlinearities (ordering, rerouting, speed selection, time-grid linking) are linearized through binary variables and big-M constraints. The ordering variables $z_{i,j,k}$ scale as $O(|T|^2 \cdot |K|)$, motivating the decomposition-based solution framework described in the source (reformulated IP over train interactions + per-train plans).
