Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is the complete, linear Mixed-Integer Linear Program for the TRSMP under a disruption caused by a partial segment blockage. The model jointly optimizes retiming, reordering, rerouting, and speed profiles while minimizing a weighted combination of arrival delay, departure delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalty.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Stations, ordered along the line |
| $E = \{(s,s+1): s=1,\dots,|S|-1\}$ | Segments between consecutive stations |
| $C_e = \{1,\dots,|C_e|\}$ | Cells (discretized position intervals) in segment $e$ |
| $D = \{\text{up},\text{down}\}$ | Directions |
| $K = \{1,\dots,|K|\}$ | Trains |
| $K_d \subseteq K$ | Trains running in direction $d$ |
| $V$ | Admissible speed levels |
| $T = \{0,1,\dots,T_{\max}\}$ | Discretized time horizon |
| $E_{\text{dis}} \subseteq E$ | Disrupted (blocked-side) segments |
| $W = [t_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}}, t_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window |

**Parameters:** $a^{\text{sched}}_{k,s}$, $dep^{\text{sched}}_{k,s}$, $dwell^{\min}_{k,s}$, $dwell^{\max}_{k,s}$, $run^{\min}_{k,e}$, $run^{\max}_{k,e}$, $\tau_{e,c,v}$ (traversal time of cell $c$ at speed level $v$), $e_{e,c,v}$ (energy per cell at speed level $v$), $v$ (speed level value), $a_{\max}$, $d_{\max}$, $\Delta t$, $h_{\min}$, $h_{\text{opp}}$, weights $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$.

---

## 2. Decision Variables

### Timing / Rescheduling
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{k,s} &\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} && \text{arrival time of train } k \text{ at station } s\\
dep_{k,s} &\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} && \text{departure time of train } k \text{ from station } s\\
x_{k,e,c,t} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } k \text{ occupies cell } c \text{ of segment } e \text{ at time } t\\
y_{k,e,c,v} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } k \text{ traverses cell } c \text{ of segment } e \text{ at speed level } v\\
run_{k,e} &\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} && \text{running time of train } k \text{ on segment } e\\
dwell_{k,s} &\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} && \text{dwell time of train } k \text{ at station } s\\
z_k &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } k \text{ is cancelled}
\end{aligned}
$$

### Routing
$$
\begin{aligned}
r_{k,e} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } k \text{ uses opposite track on segment } e\\
u_{k,e} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } k \text{ uses normal track on segment } e
\end{aligned}
$$

### Ordering / Conflicts
$$
\begin{aligned}
o_{k,k',e,c} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if } k \text{ precedes } k' \text{ in cell } c \text{ of } e \text{ (same direction)}\\
p_{k,k',e,c} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if } k \text{ precedes } k' \text{ in cell } c \text{ of } e \text{ (opposite directions)}
\end{aligned}
$$

### Speed / Energy
$$
\begin{aligned}
acc_{k,e,c} &\ge 0 && \text{acceleration entering cell } c\\
dec_{k,e,c} &\ge 0 && \text{deceleration entering cell } c\\
E_k &\ge 0 && \text{energy consumption of train } k
\end{aligned}
$$

### Auxiliary (linearization)
$$
\begin{aligned}
d^a_{k,s} &\ge 0 && \text{arrival delay}\\
d^{dep}_{k,s} &\ge 0 && \text{departure delay}\\
t^{\text{in}}_{k,e,c} &\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} && \text{entry time into cell } c\\
t^{\text{out}}_{k,e,c} &\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} && \text{exit time from cell } c\\
v_{k,e,c} &\ge 0 && \text{speed of train } k \text{ in cell } c\\
\theta_{k,e} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } k\text{'s traversal of } e \text{ overlaps } W
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 3. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \alpha \sum_{k\in K}\sum_{s\in S} d^a_{k,s}
\;+\; \beta \sum_{k\in K}\sum_{s\in S} d^{dep}_{k,s}
\;+\; \gamma \sum_{k\in K} E_k
\;+\; \delta \sum_{k\in K} z_k
$$

with linearization constraints:
$$
d^a_{k,s} \ge a_{k,s} - a^{\text{sched}}_{k,s}, \quad d^a_{k,s} \ge 0 \quad \forall k,s
$$
$$
d^{dep}_{k,s} \ge dep_{k,s} - dep^{\text{sched}}_{k,s}, \quad d^{dep}_{k,s} \ge 0 \quad \forall k,s
$$

---

## 4. Constraints

### (1) Arrival/Departure Linkage and Running Time
$$
a_{k,s+1} = dep_{k,s} + run_{k,e}, \quad \forall k \in K,\; e=(s,s+1) \in E
$$
$$
dep_{k,s} = a_{k,s} + dwell_{k,s}, \quad \forall k \in K,\; s \in S
$$
(with $dwell_{k,s}=0$ at origin and terminal stations)

### (2) Dwell Bounds
$$
dwell^{\min}_{k,s} \le dwell_{k,s} \le dwell^{\max}_{k,s}, \quad \forall k \in K,\; s \in S
$$

### (3) Running Time Bounds
$$
run^{\min}_{k,e} \le run_{k,e} \le run^{\max}_{k,e}, \quad \forall k \in K,\; e \in E
$$

### (4) Speed-Profile / Running-Time Consistency
$$
run_{k,e} = \sum_{c\in C_e}\sum_{v\in V} \tau_{e,c,v}\, y_{k,e,c,v}, \quad \forall k \in K,\; e \in E
$$
$$
\sum_{v\in V} y_{k,e,c,v} = 1, \quad \forall k \in K,\; e \in E,\; c \in C_e
$$

### (5) Speed Continuity / Acceleration Bounds
$$
v_{k,e,c} = \sum_{v\in V} v\, y_{k,e,c,v}, \quad \forall k,e,c
$$
$$
v_{k,e,c+1} - v_{k,e,c} \le a_{\max}\,\Delta t, \quad \forall k,e,c
$$
$$
v_{k,e,c} - v_{k,e,c+1} \le d_{\max}\,\Delta t, \quad \forall k,e,c
$$

### (6) Energy Linearization
$$
E_k = \sum_{e\in E}\sum_{c\in C_e}\sum_{v\in V} e_{e,c,v}\, y_{k,e,c,v}, \quad \forall k \in K
$$

### (7) Cell Occupancy and Timing Consistency
$$
\sum_{t\in T} x_{k,e,c,t} = \sum_{v\in V} y_{k,e,c,v}, \quad \forall k,e,c
$$
$$
x_{k,e,c,t} \le \sum_{v\in V} y_{k,e,c,v}, \quad \forall k,e,c,t
$$
$$
t^{\text{out}}_{k,e,c} - t^{\text{in}}_{k,e,c} = \sum_{v\in V} \tau_{e,c,v}\, y_{k,e,c,v}, \quad \forall k,e,c
$$
$$
\sum_{t\in T} t\, x_{k,e,c,t} = t^{\text{in}}_{k,e,c}, \quad \forall k,e,c
$$

### (8) Headway (Same Direction, Same Track)
For $k,k' \in K_d$, $k \ne k'$, sharing the same track on segment $e$:
$$
t^{\text{in}}_{k',e,c} \ge t^{\text{out}}_{k,e,c} + h_{\min} - M\,(1 - o_{k,k',e,c})
$$
$$
t^{\text{in}}_{k,e,c} \ge t^{\text{out}}_{k',e,c} + h_{\min} - M\,o_{k,k',e,c}
$$

### (9) Opposing-Direction Conflict (Shared Track During Rerouting)
For $k \in K_{\text{up}}$, $k' \in K_{\text{down}}$ sharing track on segment $e$:
$$
t^{\text{in}}_{k',e,c} \ge t^{\text{out}}_{k,e,c} + h_{\text{opp}} - M\,(1 - p_{k,k',e,c})
$$
$$
t^{\text{in}}_{k,e,c} \ge t^{\text{out}}_{k',e,c} + h_{\text{opp}} - M\,p_{k,k',e,c}
$$

### (10) Routing Constraints
$$
r_{k,e} + u_{k,e} = 1, \quad \forall k \in K,\; e \in E
$$
$$
r_{k,e} = 0, \quad \forall k \in K,\; e \notin E_{\text{dis}}
$$
Rerouting only within disruption window:
$$
t^{\text{in}}_{k,e,c} \ge t_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}} - M\,(1 - r_{k,e}), \quad \forall k,\; e\in E_{\text{dis}},\; c
$$
$$
t^{\text{out}}_{k,e,c} \le t_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}} + M\,(1 - r_{k,e}), \quad \forall k,\; e\in E_{\text{dis}},\; c
$$

### (11) Blocked-Side Constraint
For $e \in E_{\text{dis}}$, if the traversal overlaps $W$ on the blocked side, then $u_{k,e}=0$:
$$
t^{\text{in}}_{k,e,1} \le t_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}} + M\,(1 - \theta_{k,e})
$$
$$
t^{\text{out}}_{k,e,|C_e|} \ge t_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}} - M\,(1 - \theta_{k,e})
$$
$$
u_{k,e} \le 1 - \theta_{k,e}
$$

### (12) Cancellation
$$
\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{c\in C_e}\sum_{t\in T} x_{k,e,c,t} \le M\,(1 - z_k), \quad \forall k \in K
$$
$$
z_k \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall k \in K
$$

### (13) Ordering Consistency (No Overtaking Within a Cell)
For same-direction pairs sharing a cell:
$$
o_{k,k',e,c} + o_{k',k,e,c} = 1
$$

### (14) Time Horizon and Precedence
$$
0 \le a_{k,s} \le T_{\max}, \quad 0 \le dep_{k,s} \le T_{\max}, \quad \forall k,s
$$
$$
a_{k,s} \le dep_{k,s} \le a_{k,s+1}, \quad \forall k,s
$$

### (15) Big-M
$$
M = T_{\max}
$$

---

## 5. Model Summary

The MILP jointly optimizes:

- **Retiming:** $a_{k,s}$, $dep_{k,s}$, $run_{k,e}$, $dwell_{k,s}$
- **Reordering:** $o_{k,k',e,c}$, $p_{k,k',e,c}$
- **Routing:** $r_{k,e}$, $u_{k,e}$
- **Speed profiles:** $y_{k,e,c,v}$, $v_{k,e,c}$, $acc_{k,e,c}$, $dec_{k,e,c}$
- **Cancellation:** $z_k$

subject to physical feasibility (speed continuity, acceleration bounds), safety (headway, cell exclusivity), disruption-specific routing (opposite-track use only within $W$ on $E_{\text{dis}}$), and service requirements (dwell bounds, running-time bounds, monotone progression).

The objective trades off **arrival delay**, **departure delay**, **energy consumption**, and **cancellation penalty** via weights $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta \ge 0$.

---

## 6. Notes on Linearity and Tractability

- All nonlinearities (positive-part delays, energy as function of speed, cell occupancy timing) are linearized via auxiliary variables and big-M constraints.
- The model is a **large-scale MILP**; practical solution requires decomposition (e.g., Lagrangian relaxation on headway constraints), rolling-horizon re-optimization, or commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) with warm starts.
- The binary variables $x_{k,e,c,t}$ dominate the size: $|K|\cdot|E|\cdot|C_e|\cdot|T|$ binaries. Aggregation by block sections or time-window compression is recommended for real instances.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a partial segment blockage occurs on one track of a double-track line during a known disruption time window. Trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track within this window, requiring bidirectional coordination. We integrate train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profile selection) into one MILP.

**Assumptions (marked where introduced):**

- **(A1)** The line is discretized into segments between consecutive stations; each segment has a fixed length and a maximum line speed.
- **(A2)** Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set of candidate profiles per train per segment, each characterized by a running time and an energy consumption value. *(Reasonable assumption to keep the model linear; justified by standard practice in TSMP literature.)*
- **(A3)** The disruption affects a single track direction on a set of segments during a known time window $[T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}}]$.
- **(A4)** Rerouting is only permitted within the disruption window and only onto the opposite track; outside the window, trains use their nominal track.
- **(A5)** Minimum headway times between consecutive trains on the same track are known and constant.
- **(A6)** Dwell times at stations are bounded below by a minimum and above by a maximum.
- **(A7)** Train cancellations are allowed but penalized heavily.
- **(A8)** All times are measured in a common discrete time unit (e.g., seconds), and the planning horizon is finite.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $e = (s, s+1)$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{aff}} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Subset of disruption-affected trains |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments affected by the disruption |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of candidate speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of tracks (directions), $\mathcal{K} = \{1, 2\}$ |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | Disruption time window, discretized into time steps $t$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,e,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses track $k$ on segment $e$ |
| $y_{i,j,e,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$, track $k$ |
| $z_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $w_{i,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ during the disruption window |

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $p_{i,e,r}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $r \in \mathcal{P}_i$ on segment $e$ |
| $R_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $E_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $e$ |

### 3.3 Auxiliary Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\delta_{i,j,e,k}$ | Binary | 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ conflict on segment $e$, track $k$ |
| $\alpha_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Entry time of train $i$ into segment $e$ |
| $\beta_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Exit time of train $i$ from segment $e$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \lambda^{\text{arr}} \cdot \max(0, a_{i,s} - A_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}) + \lambda^{\text{dep}} \cdot \max(0, d_{i,s} - D_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}) \right)}_{\text{total delay}}
+ \underbrace{\lambda^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} E_{i,e}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{\lambda^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_i}_{\text{cancellations}}
$$

where $A_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}$ and $D_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}$ are nominal arrival and departure times, and $\lambda^{\text{arr}}, \lambda^{\text{dep}}, \lambda^{\text{energy}}, \lambda^{\text{cancel}} \geq 0$ are weights.

**Linearization of delay:** Introduce auxiliary variables $u_{i,s} \geq 0$, $v_{i,s} \geq 0$ with:

$$
u_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - A_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}, \quad u_{i,s} \geq 0
$$
$$
v_{i,s} \geq d_{i,s} - D_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}, \quad v_{i,s} \geq 0
$$

Then the objective becomes:

$$
\min \; Z = \lambda^{\text{arr}} \sum_{i,s} u_{i,s} + \lambda^{\text{dep}} \sum_{i,s} v_{i,s} + \lambda^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,e} E_{i,e} + \lambda^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i} z_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Constraints

**(C1) Arrival–departure linkage at each station:**

$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} + \tau^{\text{dwell,min}}_{i,s} \cdot (1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \leq a_{i,s} + \tau^{\text{dwell,max}}_{i,s} \cdot (1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C2) Running time linkage between consecutive stations:**

$$
a_{i,s+1} \geq d_{i,s} + R_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e = (s, s+1) \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C3) Speed profile selection (exactly one profile per segment if not cancelled):**

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{P}_i} p_{i,e,r} = 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C4) Running time determined by selected profile:**

$$
R_{i,e} = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_{i,e,r} \cdot p_{i,e,r}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C5) Energy consumption determined by selected profile:**

$$
E_{i,e} = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{P}_i} \varepsilon_{i,e,r} \cdot p_{i,e,r}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

where $\tau_{i,e,r}$ and $\varepsilon_{i,e,r}$ are the running time and energy consumption of profile $r$.

### 5.2 Rerouting Constraints

**(C6) Track assignment (exactly one track per segment if not cancelled):**

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{i,e,k} = 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C7) Rerouting only within disruption window:**

$$
x_{i,e,k^{\text{opp}}} \leq w_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{D}
$$

where $k^{\text{opp}}$ is the opposite track to the nominal one.

**(C8) Disruption window indicator:**

$$
w_{i,e} = 1 \implies \left[ \alpha_{i,e}, \beta_{i,e} \right] \cap \left[ T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}} \right] \neq \emptyset
$$

Linearized as:

$$
\alpha_{i,e} \leq T^{\text{end}} + M(1 - w_{i,e}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{D}
$$
$$
\beta_{i,e} \geq T^{\text{start}} - M(1 - w_{i,e}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{D}
$$

**(C9) Segment entry/exit times:**

$$
\alpha_{i,e} = d_{i,s}, \quad \beta_{i,e} = a_{i,s+1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e = (s, s+1)
$$

### 5.3 Conflict-Free Constraints (Bidirectional Coordination)

**(C10) Ordering on shared track (disjunctive constraint):**

For any two trains $i, j$ using the same track $k$ on segment $e$:

$$
\beta_{i,e} + h^{\text{min}} \leq \alpha_{j,e} + M(1 - y_{i,j,e,k})
$$
$$
\beta_{j,e} + h^{\text{min}} \leq \alpha_{i,e} + M \cdot y_{i,j,e,k}
$$

where $h^{\text{min}}$ is the minimum headway time.

**(C11) Ordering variable consistency:**

$$
y_{i,j,e,k} + y_{j,i,e,k} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; e \in \mathcal{E}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**(C12) Track usage consistency with ordering:**

$$
y_{i,j,e,k} \leq x_{i,e,k}, \quad y_{i,j,e,k} \leq x_{j,e,k}, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; e \in \mathcal{E}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**(C13) Conflict detection (for decomposition purposes):**

$$
\delta_{i,j,e,k} \geq x_{i,e,k} + x_{j,e,k} - 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; e \in \mathcal{E}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

### 5.4 Cancellation Constraints

**(C14) Cancelled trains do not occupy resources:**

$$
a_{i,s} = d_{i,s} = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}, \; \text{if } z_i = 1
$$

Linearized via big-M:

$$
a_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad d_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C15) Cancellation penalty (already in objective).**

### 5.5 Time Window and Bounds

**(C16) Time bounds:**

$$
T^{\text{min}} \leq a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \leq T^{\text{max}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C17) Running time bounds:**

$$
R_{i,e}^{\text{min}} \leq R_{i,e} \leq R_{i,e}^{\text{max}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C18) Energy bounds:**

$$
E_{i,e}^{\text{min}} \leq E_{i,e} \leq E_{i,e}^{\text{max}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

### 5.6 Binary and Non-negativity Constraints

$$
x_{i,e,k}, \; y_{i,j,e,k}, \; z_i, \; w_{i,e}, \; p_{i,e,r}, \; \delta_{i,j,e,k} \in \{0, 1\}
$$

$$
a_{i,s}, \; d_{i,s}, \; R_{i,e}, \; E_{i,e}, \; \alpha_{i,e}, \; \beta_{i,e}, \; u_{i,s}, \; v_{i,s} \geq 0
$$

---

## 6. Complete MILP Formulation

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \lambda^{\text{arr}} \sum_{i,s} u_{i,s} + \lambda^{\text{dep}} \sum_{i,s} v_{i,s} + \lambda^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,e} E_{i,e} + \lambda^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i} z_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C18)} \\
& u_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - A_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}, \quad u_{i,s} \geq 0 \\
& v_{i,s} \geq d_{i,s} - D_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}, \quad v_{i,s} \geq 0 \\
& x_{i,e,k}, y_{i,j,e,k}, z_i, w_{i,e}, p_{i,e,r}, \delta_{i,j,e,k} \in \{0,1\} \\
& a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, R_{i,e}, E_{i,e}, \alpha_{i,e}, \beta_{i,e}, u_{i,s}, v_{i,s} \geq 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Model Properties and Remarks

- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear; the only nonlinearity (delay penalty) is linearized via auxiliary variables $u_{i,s}, v_{i,s}$.
- **Bidirectional coordination:** Constraints (C10)–(C12) ensure conflict-free operation on shared tracks, critical for rerouting scenarios.
- **Integration of TRP and TSMP:** Constraints (C3)–(C5) link speed profile selection to running times and energy, coupling the timetable with speed management.
- **Rerouting flexibility:** Constraints (C6)–(C9) allow trains to switch tracks within the disruption window, with $w_{i,e}$ enforcing temporal restrictions.
- **Cancellation handling:** Constraints (C14)–(C15) allow cancellations with heavy penalty, ensuring feasibility when no conflict-free solution exists.
- **Decomposition potential:** The model can be decomposed into a master problem (train interactions, constraints C10–C13) and subproblems (individual train plans, constraints C1–C9, C14–C18), enabling the adaptive iterative algorithm described in the introduction.

---

## 8. Summary

This MILP formulation provides a complete, linear model for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages. It simultaneously optimizes train arrival/departure times, orders, routes, speed profiles, and cancellations, while ensuring conflict-free bidirectional operations and energy efficiency. The model is suitable for decomposition-based solution methods and captures the tight coupling between operational-level rescheduling and control-level speed management.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below, I formulate a complete, linear (mixed-integer linear) model inspired by the introduction. Since the input is only an introduction, several parameters and relationships have to be assumed; these are explicitly marked as **[Assumption]**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations/segment boundaries along the line, indexed by $s \in \mathcal{S}$; ordered $1, 2, \dots, |\mathcal{S}|$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of segments (blocks) between consecutive stations, $k = (s, s+1)$, indexed by $k \in \mathcal{K}$ |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ | Set of disrupted segments (partial blockages) |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of candidate speed profiles (plans) for train $i$ **[Assumption: discretized into a finite set]** |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of routes (tracks): $\mathcal{R} = \{up, down\}$ |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | Set of discretized time steps (e.g., 1 s or 15 s) **[Assumption: time is discretized for the MILP]** |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $t^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $t^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_i$ | Original route (track direction) of train $i$ |
| $v^{max}$ | Maximum allowable train speed |
| $a^{max}$ | Maximum acceleration (absolute value) |
| $b^{max}$ | Maximum deceleration (absolute value) |
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ |
| $h^{min}$ | Minimum safety headway (time separation) between consecutive trains |
| $T^{dis}_{start}, T^{dis}_{end}$ | Start and end of the disruption time window |
| $E_{i,p}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ using speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ **[Assumption: precomputed per profile]** |
| $C^{delay}$ | Unit cost of delay (per train per time unit) |
| $C^{cancel}$ | Cost of cancelling a train |
| $C^{energy}$ | Unit cost of energy |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling variables (TRP level)

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,p}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ |
| $y_{i,k,r}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ on route $r \in \mathcal{R}$ |
| $z_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $a_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ (relative to schedule) |
| $o_{i,j,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ |
| $u_{i,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $k$ (rerouting indicator) |

### 3.2 Speed management variables (TSMP level)

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $v_{i,k}$ | Continuous | Average speed of train $i$ on segment $k$ |
| $\tau_{i,k}$ | Continuous | Running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ |
| $e_{i,k}$ | Continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $k$ |
| $\alpha_{i,k}$ | Continuous | Acceleration-related auxiliary variable |
| $\beta_{i,k}$ | Continuous | Deceleration-related auxiliary variable |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, cancellations, and energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = 
\underbrace{C^{delay} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \delta_{i,s}}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{C^{cancel} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_i}_{\text{cancellation cost}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{C^{energy} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} e_{i,k}}_{\text{energy cost}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train plan selection (speed profile choice)

Each non-cancelled train selects exactly one speed profile:

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_{i,p} + z_i = 1, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{1}
$$

### 5.2 Route assignment

Each non-cancelled train traverses each segment on exactly one route:

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} y_{i,k,r} = 1 - z_i, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
\tag{2}
$$

### 5.3 Rerouting logic under disruption

If segment $k$ is disrupted during the disruption window and train $i$ is affected, rerouting to the opposite track is allowed:

$$
u_{i,k} \geq y_{i,k,r^{opp}} - (1 - \mathbb{1}_{k \in \mathcal{D}}), \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{3}
$$

**[Assumption]** Rerouting is only permitted on disrupted segments during the disruption window:

$$
u_{i,k} = 0, \qquad \forall i, \; k \notin \mathcal{D}
\tag{4}
$$

### 5.4 Running time and speed consistency

The running time on segment $k$ is determined by the chosen profile:

$$
\tau_{i,k} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_{i,k,p} \, x_{i,p}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{5}
$$

**[Assumption]** The average speed is related to segment length and running time:

$$
v_{i,k} = \frac{L_k}{\tau_{i,k}}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{6}
$$

Linearized version (since $1/\tau$ is nonlinear), using a piecewise-linear approximation with segments $\ell \in \mathcal{L}_k$:

$$
v_{i,k} = \sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}_k} \lambda_{i,k,\ell} \, v^{lin}_{\ell}, \qquad
\tau_{i,k} = \sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}_k} \lambda_{i,k,\ell} \, \tau^{lin}_{\ell}, \qquad
\sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}_k} \lambda_{i,k,\ell} = 1
\tag{6'}
$$

### 5.5 Timetable consistency (arrival/departure linkage)

Arrival at station $s+1$ equals departure from station $s$ plus running time:

$$
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + \tau_{i,k}, \qquad \forall i, \; k = (s, s+1)
\tag{7}
$$

Departure from station $s$ equals arrival plus dwell time:

$$
d_{i,s} = a_{i,s} + w_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{8}
$$

**[Assumption]** Dwell time $w_{i,s} \geq w^{min}$ (minimum dwell) and $w_{i,s} \leq w^{max}$:

$$
w^{min} \leq w_{i,s} \leq w^{max}, \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{9}
$$

### 5.6 Delay definition

$$
\delta_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - t^{arr}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{10}
$$

$$
\delta_{i,s} \geq d_{i,s} - t^{dep}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{11}
$$

$$
\delta_{i,s} \geq 0, \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{12}
$$

### 5.7 Disruption window constraints

Trains cannot enter a disrupted segment during the disruption window unless rerouted:

$$
a_{i,s} \geq T^{dis}_{end} - M(1 - u_{i,k}) - M z_i, \qquad \forall i, \; k = (s,s+1) \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{13}
$$

**[Assumption]** If not rerouted, entry into disrupted segment must be before disruption starts or after it ends:

$$
d_{i,s} \leq T^{dis}_{start} + M u_{i,k} + M z_i, \qquad \forall i, \; k \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{14}
$$

### 5.8 Headway / safety constraints (conflict-free operation)

For any two trains $i, j$ on the same segment $k$ and same route $r$:

$$
d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s} + h^{min} - M(1 - o_{i,j,k}) - M(2 - y_{i,k,r} - y_{j,k,r}), \qquad \forall i \neq j, k, r
\tag{15}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s} + h^{min} - M \, o_{i,j,k} - M(2 - y_{i,k,r} - y_{j,k,r}), \qquad \forall i \neq j, k, r
\tag{16}
$$

Ordering variable consistency:

$$
o_{i,j,k} + o_{j,i,k} = 1, \qquad \forall i \neq j, k
\tag{17}
$$

### 5.9 Bidirectional conflict constraints (opposite tracks)

If two trains use opposite routes on the same segment, they must not occupy the segment simultaneously:

$$
d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s} + h^{min} - M(1 - o_{i,j,k}) - M(2 - y_{i,k,r} - y_{j,k,r'}), \quad r \neq r', \; \forall i \neq j, k
\tag{18}
$$

**[Assumption]** Additional constraint: at most one train per direction per segment at any time:

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} y_{i,k,r} \leq 1, \qquad \forall k \in \mathcal{D}, \; r \in \mathcal{R}, \; \text{(during disruption window)}
\tag{19}
$$

### 5.10 Speed and acceleration limits

$$
0 \leq v_{i,k} \leq v^{max}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{20}
$$

**[Assumption]** Acceleration between consecutive segments is bounded:

$$
\frac{v_{i,k+1} - v_{i,k}}{\tau_{i,k}} \leq a^{max}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{21}
$$

$$
\frac{v_{i,k} - v_{i,k+1}}{\tau_{i,k}} \leq b^{max}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{22}
$$

Linearized using auxiliary variables $\alpha_{i,k}, \beta_{i,k}$:

$$
v_{i,k+1} - v_{i,k} \leq a^{max} \tau_{i,k}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{21'}
$$

$$
v_{i,k} - v_{i,k+1} \leq b^{max} \tau_{i,k}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{22'}
$$

### 5.11 Energy consumption

**[Assumption]** Energy is proportional to the square of speed and running time (traction energy model):

$$
e_{i,k} \geq c_1 \, v_{i,k}^2 \, \tau_{i,k} + c_2 \, \tau_{i,k}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{23}
$$

Linearized via piecewise-linear approximation over speed intervals:

$$
e_{i,k} \geq \sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}_k} \eta_{\ell} \, \lambda_{i,k,\ell}, \qquad \forall i, k
\tag{23'}
$$

where $\eta_{\ell}$ are precomputed energy coefficients for each linearization segment.

### 5.12 Cancellation constraints

If train $i$ is cancelled, all timing variables are free (or fixed to schedule):

$$
a_{i,s} = t^{arr}_{i,s}, \quad d_{i,s} = t^{dep}_{i,s}, \quad \text{if } z_i = 1
\tag{24}
$$

Relaxed as:

$$
|a_{i,s} - t^{arr}_{i,s}| \leq M z_i, \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{24'}
$$

### 5.13 Domain constraints

$$
x_{i,p} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{i,k,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad z_i \in \{0,1\}, \quad o_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad u_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}
\tag{25}
$$

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}, \tau_{i,k}, v_{i,k}, e_{i,k} \geq 0
\tag{26}
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions Summary

1. **Time discretization**: The model uses continuous time but speed profiles are discretized into a finite set $\mathcal{P}_i$.
2. **Piecewise-linear approximation**: Speed–time and energy–speed relationships are linearized using a finite set of linearization segments $\mathcal{L}_k$.
3. **Rerouting**: Only allowed on disrupted segments during the disruption window; opposite track is assumed available.
4. **Dwell times**: Bounded between minimum and maximum values.
5. **Energy model**: Traction energy is approximated as a piecewise-linear function of speed and running time.
6. **Headway**: Minimum safety headway $h^{min}$ is constant across all segments and trains.
7. **Cancellation**: Cancelled trains are fixed to their scheduled times (or removed from the system).
8. **Bidirectional conflicts**: Modeled via ordering variables and big-M constraints ensuring no simultaneous occupancy of the same track segment by opposing trains.

---

## 7. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\min \; Z = C^{delay} \sum_{i,s} \delta_{i,s} + C^{cancel} \sum_i z_i + C^{energy} \sum_{i,k} e_{i,k}
$$

subject to constraints (1)–(26).

This model simultaneously determines:
- **Train rescheduling decisions**: arrival/departure times, train order, route selection, cancellations.
- **Speed management decisions**: speed profiles, running times, energy consumption.
- **Conflict-free operation**: headway and bidirectional track occupancy constraints.

The model is a **mixed-integer linear program** that can be solved using standard MILP solvers or decomposed via the IP-based decomposition and adaptive iterative algorithm described in the introduction.

Text:
# A MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

*Model inspired by the RECIFE-MILP framework (Pellegrini et al., 2015), enhanced with speed-profile options and speed-dependent braking distances for ETCS L2 with Trackside Train Detection.*

---

## 1. Assumptions

The following assumptions are made (marked **[A]** where the input does not fully specify them):

- **[A1]** The railway network is discretised into *track sections* (TDSs / blocks). Each section can be occupied by at most one train at a time.
- **[A2]** A finite set of candidate *speed profiles* is available per train and per section (e.g., derived from a discrete set of cruising speeds). Each profile has a known running time and a known braking distance.
- **[A3]** The end of authority (EoA) for a train is always located at a section boundary (consistent with ETCS L2 with TTD).
- **[A4]** The brake indication point (IP) may lie anywhere along the track, at a distance equal to the train- and speed-dependent braking distance upstream of the EoA.
- **[A5]** All events (arrivals, departures, section entries/exits) are modelled on a common time axis; the model is a macroscopic-microscopic hybrid (as in RECIFE-MILP).
- **[A6]** The objective is the minimisation of total weighted train delay.
- **[A7]** Trains are assumed to follow their routes without rerouting (only retiming and reordering are considered), consistent with the base RECIFE-MILP formulation.
- **[A8]** Braking distances are piecewise-linearised in speed to preserve linearity (see Section 4.5).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of track sections, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_t$ | Ordered set of sections on the route of train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_t$ | Set of candidate speed profiles for train $t$, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_t^s$ | Set of candidate speed profiles for train $t$ on section $s$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of speed levels (for piecewise linearisation), indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{C}$ | Set of track conflicts (pairs of trains sharing a section), indexed by $c$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{\text{sw}}$ | Subset of sections containing switches |
| $\mathcal{S}^{\text{open}}$ | Subset of open-line sections ($\mathcal{S}^{\text{open}} = \mathcal{S} \setminus \mathcal{S}^{\text{sw}}$) |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $r_{t,s,p}$ | Running time of train $t$ on section $s$ using profile $p$ | s |
| $d_{t,s,p}$ | Braking distance of train $t$ at the exit speed of section $s$ under profile $p$ | m |
| $L_s$ | Length of section $s$ | m |
| $v_{t,s,p}$ | Average speed of train $t$ on section $s$ under profile $p$ | m/s |
| $a_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at section $s$ | s |
| $a_{t,s}^{\text{dep}}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $t$ from section $s$ | s |
| $w_t$ | Delay weight (priority) of train $t$ | – |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway (safety margin) between two trains | s |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) | s |
| $\tau_{t,s}^{\text{dwell}}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $t$ at section $s$ (0 if no stop) | s |
| $\sigma$ | Safety margin behind the rear of the preceding train | m |
| $\alpha_k, \beta_k$ | Coefficients of the piecewise-linear braking-distance approximation for speed level $k$ | – |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Timing variables

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| $x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at section $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}}$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ from section $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $x_{t,s}^{\text{IP}}$ | Time at which train $t$ passes the brake indication point upstream of section $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |

### 4.2 Speed-profile selection

$$y_{t,s,p} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t,\; p \in \mathcal{P}_t^s$$

$y_{t,s,p} = 1$ iff train $t$ uses speed profile $p$ on section $s$.

### 4.3 Ordering variables

$$\delta_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \cap \mathcal{R}_{t'}$$

$\delta_{t,t',s} = 1$ iff train $t$ enters section $s$ before train $t'$.

### 4.4 Delay variables

$$D_t \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}$$

Total delay of train $t$.

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimise the total weighted delay:

$$\boxed{\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} w_t \, D_t}$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Delay definition

For each train $t$ and its final section $s^{\text{end}}_t \in \mathcal{R}_t$:

$$D_t \geq x_{t,s^{\text{end}}_t}^{\text{arr}} - a_{t,s^{\text{end}}_t}^{\text{arr}}, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T} \tag{1}$$

$$D_t \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T} \tag{2}$$

### 6.2 Speed-profile selection (exactly one profile per section)

$$\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_t^s} y_{t,s,p} = 1, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \tag{3}$$

### 6.3 Running time as a function of the selected profile

$$x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} = x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_t^s} r_{t,s,p} \, y_{t,s,p}, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \tag{4}$$

### 6.4 Dwell time at stations

$$x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} \geq x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} + \tau_{t,s}^{\text{dwell}}, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \tag{5}$$

### 6.5 Route continuity (linking consecutive sections)

For consecutive sections $s, s' \in \mathcal{R}_t$ with $s' = \text{succ}(s)$:

$$x_{t,s'}^{\text{arr}} = x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}}, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T} \tag{6}$$

### 6.6 Brake indication point (DTG-specific)

The brake indication point is located a braking distance $d_{t,s,p}$ upstream of the EoA at the entry of section $s$. The time at which the train passes the IP is:

$$x_{t,s}^{\text{IP}} = x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} - \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_t^s} \frac{d_{t,s,p}}{v_{t,s,p}} \, y_{t,s,p}, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \tag{7}$$

> **Interpretation:** In fixed-block signalling, the IP is fixed at a block boundary. Under DTG, it is speed-dependent and may fall anywhere along the track. Equation (7) captures this by subtracting the braking time from the arrival time at the EoA.

### 6.7 Train separation (headway) constraints — DTG-specific

For each pair of trains $(t, t') \in \mathcal{C}$ sharing section $s$, the separation must respect the speed-dependent braking distance:

**Case A: Train $t$ enters before train $t'$ ($\delta_{t,t',s} = 1$)**

$$x_{t',s}^{\text{IP}} \geq x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} + h_{\min} - M(1 - \delta_{t,t',s}), \quad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \cap \mathcal{R}_{t'} \tag{8}$$

**Case B: Train $t'$ enters before train $t$ ($\delta_{t,t',s} = 0$)**

$$x_{t,s}^{\text{IP}} \geq x_{t',s}^{\text{arr}} + h_{\min} - M \, \delta_{t,t',s}, \quad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \cap \mathcal{R}_{t'} \tag{9}$$

> **Interpretation:** The following train must pass its brake indication point only after the preceding train has fully cleared the section (arrival at the next section boundary). This ensures the braking curve is respected. The speed-dependence enters through $x_{t,s}^{\text{IP}}$ in (7).

### 6.8 Section occupancy (no two trains in the same section simultaneously)

$$x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}} \leq x_{t',s}^{\text{arr}} + M(1 - \delta_{t,t',s}), \quad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \cap \mathcal{R}_{t'} \tag{10}$$

$$x_{t',s}^{\text{dep}} \leq x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} + M \, \delta_{t,t',s}, \quad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \cap \mathcal{R}_{t'} \tag{11}$$

### 6.9 Switch sections — additional safety constraints

For sections $s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{sw}}$, a longer minimum headway $h_{\min}^{\text{sw}} \geq h_{\min}$ is enforced:

$$x_{t',s}^{\text{IP}} \geq x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} + h_{\min}^{\text{sw}} - M(1 - \delta_{t,t',s}), \quad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{sw}} \cap \mathcal{R}_t \cap \mathcal{R}_{t'} \tag{12}$$

### 6.10 Ordering consistency (transitivity)

$$\delta_{t,t',s} + \delta_{t',t,s} = 1, \quad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \cap \mathcal{R}_{t'} \tag{13}$$

### 6.11 Piecewise-linear braking distance (linearisation)

The braking distance $d_{t,s,p}$ is approximated as a piecewise-linear function of speed $v_{t,s,p}$:

$$d_{t,s,p} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} (\alpha_k \, v_{t,s,p} + \beta_k) \, \lambda_{t,s,p,k}, \quad \forall t, s, p \tag{14}$$

$$\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \lambda_{t,s,p,k} = 1, \quad \lambda_{t,s,p,k} \geq 0, \quad \forall t, s, p \tag{15}$$

> **Interpretation:** This preserves linearity while allowing the braking distance to vary with speed. In practice, $\lambda$ variables are only active for the speed level closest to $v_{t,s,p}$.

### 6.12 Time-window constraints (release and deadline)

$$x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} \geq a_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} - \Delta^{\text{early}}, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \tag{16}$$

$$x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} \leq a_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} + \Delta^{\text{late}}, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \tag{17}$$

where $\Delta^{\text{early}}, \Delta^{\text{late}}$ are the maximum allowed early/late deviations.

### 6.13 Variable domains

$$x_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}, x_{t,s}^{\text{dep}}, x_{t,s}^{\text{IP}} \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t \tag{18}$$

$$y_{t,s,p} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \delta_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \lambda_{t,s,p,k} \geq 0 \tag{19}$$

$$D_t \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T} \tag{20}$$

---

## 7. Summary of the Model

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Objective** | Minimise total weighted train delay $\sum_t w_t D_t$ |
| **Key DTG enhancement** | Speed-dependent brake indication point $x_{t,s}^{\text{IP}}$ (Eq. 7) and separation constraints (Eqs. 8–9) |
| **Speed-profile options** | Binary selection $y_{t,s,p}$ with running time (Eq. 4) and braking distance (Eq. 7) depending on profile |
| **Switch distinction** | Additional headway $h_{\min}^{\text{sw}}$ on switch sections (Eq. 12) |
| **Linearisation** | Piecewise-linear braking distance (Eqs. 14–15) |
| **Conflict resolution** | Ordering variables $\delta_{t,t',s}$ with big-M constraints (Eqs. 8–11) |

---

## 8. Model Size

| Variable type | Count |
|---------------|-------|
| Continuous ($x$) | $3 \sum_t |\mathcal{R}_t|$ |
| Binary ($y$) | $\sum_t \sum_{s \in \mathcal{R}_t} |\mathcal{P}_t^s|$ |
| Binary ($\delta$) | $2 \sum_{(t,t') \in \mathcal{C}} |\mathcal{R}_t \cap \mathcal{R}_{t'}|$ |
| Continuous ($\lambda$) | $\sum_t \sum_{s \in \mathcal{R}_t} |\mathcal{P}_t^s| \cdot |\mathcal{K}|$ |
| Delay ($D$) | $|\mathcal{T}|$ |

---

## 9. Remarks on the DTG Enhancement

1. **Speed-dependent separation:** Unlike fixed-block models where the IP is at a fixed block boundary, Eq. (7) allows the IP to move with the selected speed profile. This is the core DTG enhancement.

2. **Braking curve supervision:** The constraint in Eqs. (8)–(9) ensures that the following train's IP is only passed after the preceding train has cleared the section, effectively modelling continuous braking curve supervision.

3. **Trade-off:** Higher speeds reduce running time but increase braking distance, potentially increasing headway requirements. The MILP optimises this trade-off.

4. **Switch sections:** The distinction between switch and open-line sections (Eq. 12) reflects the additional safety requirements and lower speed limits around switches.

5. **Linearity:** All constraints are linear in the decision variables, preserving the MILP structure and allowing solution by standard solvers (e.g., CPLEX, Gurobi).

---

*This model is a complete, self-contained MILP for CDR under DTG signalling, inspired by RECIFE-MILP and enhanced with the two key contributions described in the input: speed-profile options and train-/speed-dependent braking distances.*

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below we formulate a complete, linear mixed-integer programming (MILP) model inspired by the introduction. Where the input leaves gaps, we make reasonable assumptions and mark them explicitly as **[Assumption]**.

---

## 1. Notation and Sets

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations (nodes), indexed by $s, k$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of track segments (links) between adjacent stations, indexed by $l = (s,k)$ |
| $\mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}}$ | Set of disrupted segments, $\mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}} \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of directions, $\mathcal{D} = \{up, down\}$, indexed by $d$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{up}}, \mathcal{T}^{\text{down}}$ | Subsets of trains running in each direction |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of candidate speed-profile plans (segments of piecewise-constant speed) for train $i$ **[Assumption: discretized into a finite set of feasible profiles]** |
| $\mathcal{R}_i$ | Set of candidate routes for train $i$ (normal track or opposite track on disrupted segments) |
| $[t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}}, t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window on disrupted segments |

**Parameters**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $T^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum safety headway between consecutive trains on the same track segment |
| $\tau^{\text{run}}_{i,l}$ | Nominal (free-flow) running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $\tau^{\text{dwell}}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $E_{i,p,l}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $l$ using speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ |
| $R_{i,l,p}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ using profile $p$ |
| $c^{\text{delay}}$ | Unit cost of delay (per train per time unit) |
| $c^{\text{energy}}$ | Unit cost of energy consumption |
| $c^{\text{cancel}}_i$ | Penalty cost of cancelling train $i$ |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $\Delta$ | Discretization interval length for time **[Assumption: time discretized into intervals of length $\Delta$]** |

---

## 2. Decision Variables

**Scheduling variables**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,l,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $l$ |
| $y_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ |
| $z_i \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\delta_{i,j,l} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $l$ |
| $\alpha_{i,l} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses disrupted segment $l$ during disruption window |

**Auxiliary variables**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $w_{i,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $g_{i,l} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Actual running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $e_{i,l} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Energy consumed by train $i$ on segment $l$ |

---

## 3. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted cost of delays, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$
\min \; Z = c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} w_{i,s} \;+\; c^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} e_{i,l} \;+\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} c^{\text{cancel}}_i \, z_i
$$

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Train Routing and Cancellation

Each train selects exactly one route (or is cancelled):

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} y_{i,r} + z_i = 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{1}
$$

**[Assumption: A route defines for each segment whether the normal or opposite track is used; on non-disrupted segments only the normal track is available.]**

### 4.2 Speed Profile Selection

Each active (non-cancelled) train selects exactly one speed profile per segment:

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_{i,l,p} = 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; l \in \mathcal{L}
\tag{2}
$$

### 4.3 Running Time and Energy Coupling

Running time on each segment is determined by the chosen profile:

$$
g_{i,l} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} R_{i,l,p} \, x_{i,l,p}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; l \in \mathcal{L}
\tag{3}
$$

Energy consumption on each segment:

$$
e_{i,l} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} E_{i,l,p} \, x_{i,l,p}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; l \in \mathcal{L}
\tag{4}
$$

### 4.4 Timetable Consistency (Arrival–Departure–Running Time)

For each train $i$ and each segment $l = (s,k)$:

$$
a_{i,k} = d_{i,s} + g_{i,l}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; l=(s,k) \in \mathcal{L}
\tag{5}
$$

Minimum dwell time at each station:

$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} + \tau^{\text{dwell}}_{i,s} - M z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{6}
$$

**[Assumption: Dwell time is a decision variable bounded below by a minimum; no upper bound is imposed except through delay penalties.]**

### 4.5 Delay Definition

Delay at each station:

$$
w_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - T^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} - M z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{7}
$$

$$
w_{i,s} \ge d_{i,s} - T^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - M z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{8}
$$

$$
w_{i,s} \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{9}
$$

### 4.6 Headway (Conflict-Free) Constraints on Shared Segments

For each segment $l$ and each ordered pair of trains $(i,j)$ using the same track in the same direction:

$$
d_{j,s} \ge a_{i,k} + h^{\min} - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,l}) - M(z_i + z_j), \quad \forall l=(s,k), \; i \neq j
\tag{10}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{j,k} + h^{\min} - M \delta_{i,j,l} - M(z_i + z_j), \quad \forall l=(s,k), \; i \neq j
\tag{11}
$$

**[Assumption: Headway constraints are enforced only between trains sharing the same physical track (same route on that segment). This is captured by activating (10)–(11) only when $y_{i,r} = y_{j,r'} = 1$ for routes using the same track; otherwise the big-M term relaxes them.]**

### 4.7 Bidirectional Conflict Constraints (Rerouting on Opposite Track)

When a train is rerouted onto the opposite track during the disruption window, it must not conflict with trains running in the opposite direction on that track:

$$
d_{j,s} \ge a_{i,k} + h^{\min} - M(1 - \alpha_{i,l}) - M(1 - \alpha_{j,l}) - M(z_i + z_j), \quad \forall l \in \mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}}, \; i \neq j
\tag{12}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{j,k} + h^{\min} - M \alpha_{i,l} - M(1 - \alpha_{j,l}) - M(z_i + z_j), \quad \forall l \in \mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}}, \; i \neq j
\tag{13}
$$

**Disruption window activation:**

$$
a_{i,k} \le t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}} + M(1 - \alpha_{i,l}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; l=(s,k) \in \mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{14}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \ge t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}} - M(1 - \alpha_{i,l}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; l=(s,k) \in \mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{15}
$$

**[Assumption: $\alpha_{i,l} = 1$ iff train $i$'s traversal of disrupted segment $l$ overlaps the disruption window; this is linearized via (14)–(15) and the binary nature of $\alpha_{i,l}$.]**

### 4.8 Route–Segment Compatibility

A train may only use the opposite track on a disrupted segment if its chosen route permits it:

$$
\alpha_{i,l} \le \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i : r \text{ uses opposite track on } l} y_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; l \in \mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{16}
$$

On non-disrupted segments, only the normal track is available:

$$
y_{i,r} = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; r \text{ using opposite track on } l \notin \mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{17}
$$

### 4.9 Segment Capacity during Disruption

At most one train may occupy a disrupted segment during the disruption window (unidirectional capacity):

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \alpha_{i,l} \le 1, \quad \forall l \in \mathcal{L}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{18}
$$

**[Assumption: This enforces that only one train at a time may traverse the disrupted segment during the disruption window, reflecting the partial blockage.]**

### 4.10 Variable Domains

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, g_{i,l}, e_{i,l} \ge 0
\tag{19}
$$

$$
x_{i,l,p}, y_{i,r}, z_i, \delta_{i,j,l}, \alpha_{i,l} \in \{0,1\}
\tag{20}
$$

---

## 5. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i,s} w_{i,s} + c^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,l} e_{i,l} + \sum_{i} c^{\text{cancel}}_i z_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & (1)\text{--}(20)
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 6. Key Assumptions (Explicitly Marked)

1. **Discretized speed profiles**: The continuous speed management problem is approximated by a finite set of candidate speed profiles per segment per train. Each profile has a known running time and energy consumption. *(This is the standard approach for embedding TSMP into a MILP.)*
2. **Time discretization**: Time variables are continuous, but the disruption window and headway constraints are enforced at event times (arrival/departure), not on a fine time grid. This avoids the need for $\Delta$ in the core model.
3. **Route representation**: A route specifies, for each segment, whether the normal or opposite track is used. On non-disrupted segments, only the normal track is available.
4. **Bidirectional conflict**: When a train is rerouted onto the opposite track during the disruption window, it may conflict with trains running in the opposite direction. Constraints (12)–(13) resolve these conflicts via precedence variables.
5. **Disruption window**: The disruption affects a set of segments during a known time window $[t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}}, t^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}]$. Trains whose traversal overlaps this window are flagged by $\alpha_{i,l}$.
6. **Cancellation**: A cancelled train incurs a penalty and is removed from all operational constraints via the $z_i$ indicator.
7. **No upper bound on dwell time**: Trains may dwell longer than the minimum to resolve conflicts or align with recovery times; this is penalized indirectly through delay costs.
8. **Energy–speed coupling**: Energy consumption is a function of the chosen speed profile, precomputed for each candidate profile.

---

## 7. Remarks on Linearity and Solvability

- All constraints are linear in the decision variables.
- The model is a MILP with binary variables for routing, speed profile selection, precedence, and disruption-window activation.
- The big-M formulation is used to activate/deactivate headway and conflict constraints conditionally.
- The model can be solved directly by commercial MILP solvers for small to medium instances; for large instances, the decomposition-based solution framework described in the introduction (IP reformulation + adaptive iterative algorithm + local branching) is recommended.

---

This formulation captures the integrated TRSMP under partial segment blockages, jointly optimizing train retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed profiles while ensuring conflict-free bidirectional operations and energy efficiency.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for the integrated TRSMP. The formulation couples a time–space–speed network representation (for the TSMP) with conflict-resolution and rerouting decisions (for the TRP).

> **Note on assumptions.** The introduction does not specify all operational details (e.g., exact tractive parameters, headway values, station dwell bounds, energy coefficients). The following standard, widely used assumptions are adopted and clearly flagged:
> 1. A single double-track corridor with two unidirectional tracks (up/down).
> 2. The track is discretized into *block sections* of equal length; time is discretized into uniform intervals.
> 3. All trains have identical consists (mass *M*, length *L*, max tractive/braking effort *F_max*).
> 4. Energy consumption is approximated by a piecewise-linear function of speed (Davis equation: *e = α + βv + γv²*).
> 5. Rerouting is allowed only on the opposite track within the disruption time window and only on the affected segment.
> 6. No train cancellation is allowed (can be relaxed by adding a binary cancellation variable).
> 7. Minimum headway between consecutive trains on the same track and minimum safety distance between opposing trains on the shared (rerouted) track.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| 𝒯 = {1,…,T} | Set of trains |
| 𝒮 = {1,…,S} | Set of stations (ordered along the corridor) |
| ℬ = {1,…,B} | Set of block sections partitioning the corridor |
| 𝒦 = {1,…,K} | Set of discrete time steps (Δt spacing) |
| 𝒟 = {U, D} | Travel directions: Up / Down |
| ℛ = {0, 1} | Rerouting indicator: 0 = original track, 1 = opposite track |
| ℒ = {1,…,Λ} | Set of piecewise-linear segments for the energy function |
| ℋ | Set of consecutive-train pairs on the same track (headway pairs) |
| 𝒫 | Set of opposing-train pairs sharing the rerouted track |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| ℓ_b | Length of block section *b* [m] |
| Δt | Time-step duration [s] |
| v_min, v_max | Minimum / maximum operating speed [m/s] |
| a_max, b_max | Maximum acceleration / deceleration [m/s²] |
| M | Train mass [t] |
| τ_s^min, τ_s^max | Minimum / maximum dwell time at station *s* [s] |
| h | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains on the same track [s] |
| h_opp | Minimum safety time gap between opposing trains on the shared track [s] |
| d̄_{t,s}, ā_{t,s} | Scheduled departure / arrival time of train *t* at station *s* |
| α, β, γ | Davis equation coefficients for energy consumption |
| (b_d, k_d^start, k_d^end) | Disruption: affected block *b_d*, start/end time indices |
| C_delay | Penalty per minute of arrival delay |
| C_early | Penalty per minute of early arrival (if undesired) |
| C_energy | Weight of energy consumption in the objective |
| C_reroute | Penalty per block-section rerouted (operational cost) |
| M_big | A sufficiently large constant (Big-M) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Train rescheduling (TRP) variables
- **a_{t,s} ∈ ℝ₊** — actual arrival time of train *t* at station *s*.
- **d_{t,s} ∈ ℝ₊** — actual departure time of train *t* at station *s*.
- **x_{t,b,k} ∈ {0,1}** — 1 if train *t* occupies block *b* at time *k* on its **original** track.
- **y_{t,b,k} ∈ {0,1}** — 1 if train *t* occupies block *b* at time *k* on the **opposite** (rerouted) track.
- **r_{t,b} ∈ {0,1}** — 1 if train *t* is rerouted on block *b* (only meaningful inside the disruption window).

### 3.2 Train speed management (TSMP) variables
- **v_{t,b,k} ∈ ℝ₊** — speed of train *t* in block *b* at time *k* [m/s].
- **e_{t,b,k} ∈ ℝ₊** — energy consumed by train *t* in block *b* at time *k* [kWh].
- **δ_{t,b,k,ℓ} ∈ {0,1}** — 1 if the speed of train *t* in block *b* at time *k* falls in piecewise-linear segment ℓ (SOS2 structure).

### 3.3 Conflict-resolution variables
- **π_{t,t',b,k} ∈ {0,1}** — 1 if train *t* precedes train *t'* in block *b* at time *k* (ordering on shared/opposite track).
- **σ_{t,t',b,k} ∈ {0,1}** — 1 if trains *t* and *t'* use the rerouted track in block *b* at the same time *k* (forbidden unless resolved by π).

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of (i) total delay, (ii) total energy consumption, and (iii) rerouting cost:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; C_{\text{delay}}\!\!\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\!\!\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\!\!(a_{t,s}-\bar a_{t,s})^{+}
\;+\; C_{\text{early}}\!\!\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\!\!\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\!\!(\bar a_{t,s}-a_{t,s})^{+}
\;+\; C_{\text{energy}}\!\!\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\!\!\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\!\!\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} e_{t,b,k}
\;+\; C_{\text{reroute}}\!\!\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\!\!\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}} r_{t,b}
$$

where $(x)^+ = \max\{x,0\}$. The piecewise-linear terms are linearized via the SOS2 variables δ (see constraints below).

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Block-occupancy and rerouting logic

**(C1) Single-track occupancy at any time step:**
$$
x_{t,b,k} + y_{t,b,k} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall\, t\in\mathcal{T},\; b\in\mathcal{B},\; k\in\mathcal{K}
$$

**(C2) Rerouting only allowed inside the disruption window and on the disrupted block:**
$$
y_{t,b,k} \;\le\; \mathbb{1}\{b = b_d\}\cdot \mathbb{1}\{k_d^{\text{start}} \le k \le k_d^{\text{end}}\} \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$

**(C3) Link between rerouting indicator and rerouted occupancy:**
$$
r_{t,b} \;\ge\; y_{t,b,k} \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$
$$
r_{t,b} \;\le\; \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} y_{t,b,k} \qquad \forall\, t,b
$$

**(C4) Disrupted block forbidden on original track during the disruption:**
$$
x_{t,b_d,k} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall\, t,\; k_d^{\text{start}} \le k \le k_d^{\text{end}}
$$

**(C5) Flow conservation across consecutive blocks (train moves forward):**
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} x_{t,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} x_{t,b+1,k} \qquad \forall\, t,\; b\in\mathcal{B}\setminus\{B\}
$$
(and analogously for *y* on the rerouted track).

---

### 5.2 Train dynamics (kinematic equations for TSMP)

**(C6) Speed bounds:**
$$
v_{\min}\,x_{t,b,k} \;\le\; v_{t,b,k} \;\le\; v_{\max}\,x_{t,b,k} \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$

**(C7) Acceleration / deceleration limits (linearized):**
$$
v_{t,b,k+1} - v_{t,b,k} \;\le\; a_{\max}\Delta t \;+\; M_{\text{big}}(2 - x_{t,b,k} - x_{t,b,k+1}) \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$
$$
v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b,k+1} \;\le\; b_{\max}\Delta t \;+\; M_{\text{big}}(2 - x_{t,b,k} - x_{t,b,k+1}) \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$
(Analogous constraints for the rerouted track using *y*.)

**(C8) Block traversal time (link between speed and occupancy):**
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} x_{t,b,k} \;\ge\; \left\lceil \frac{\ell_b}{v_{\max}\Delta t}\right\rceil
$$
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} x_{t,b,k} \;\le\; \left\lceil \frac{\ell_b}{v_{\min}\Delta t}\right\rceil
$$

**(C9) Position consistency (cumulative distance):**
$$
\sum_{b'\le b}\sum_{k'\le k} v_{t,b',k'}\Delta t \;\le\; \sum_{b'\le b}\ell_b \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$

---

### 5.3 Energy consumption (piecewise-linear Davis equation)

**(C10) SOS2 selection of energy segment:**
$$
\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}} \delta_{t,b,k,\ell} = x_{t,b,k} \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$
$$
\delta \text{ form an SOS2 set for each } (t,b,k)
$$

**(C11) Speed expressed via piecewise-linear segments:**
$$
v_{t,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}} v_\ell^{\text{mid}}\,\delta_{t,b,k,\ell} \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$

**(C12) Energy per block–time equals the piecewise-linear value:**
$$
e_{t,b,k} \;=\; \Delta t \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}} (\alpha + \beta v_\ell^{\text{mid}} + \gamma (v_\ell^{\text{mid}})^2)\,\delta_{t,b,k,\ell} \qquad \forall\, t,b,k
$$

---

### 5.4 Station arrival/departure times and dwell times

**(C13) Arrival time equals the time-step of last occupancy before station *s*:**
$$
a_{t,s} \;=\; \Delta t \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} k\, x_{t,b_s^{\text{in}},k} \qquad \forall\, t,s
$$
(where $b_s^{\text{in}}$ is the block section immediately preceding station *s*.)

**(C14) Departure time equals the time-step of first occupancy after station *s*:**
$$
d_{t,s} \;=\; \Delta t \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} k\, x_{t,b_s^{\text{out}},k} \qquad \forall\, t,s
$$

**(C15) Dwell-time bounds:**
$$
\tau_s^{\min} \;\le\; d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \;\le\; \tau_s^{\max} \qquad \forall\, t,s
$$

**(C16) Schedule adherence (soft constraints via objective penalty already included):**
$$
a_{t,s} \;\ge\; \bar a_{t,s} - M_{\text{big}}(1 - \text{allow early})
$$
(penalized in the objective through the delay/early terms).

---

### 5.5 Conflict resolution — same direction (headway)

**(C17) Headway between consecutive trains on the same track:**
$$
\sum_{k'\le k+h} x_{t,b,k'} + \sum_{k'\le k} x_{t',b,k'} \;\le\; 1 + M_{\text{big}}(1-\pi_{t,t',b,k}) \quad \forall\, (t,t')\in\mathcal{H},\,b,k
$$
$$
\sum_{k'\le k+h} x_{t',b,k'} + \sum_{k'\le k} x_{t,b,k'} \;\le\; 1 + M_{\text{big}}\,\pi_{t,t',b,k} \quad \forall\, (t,t')\in\mathcal{H},\,b,k
$$

---

### 5.6 Conflict resolution — opposite direction on shared (rerouted) track

**(C18) No simultaneous occupancy of the rerouted block by opposing trains:**
$$
y_{t,b,k} + y_{t',b,k} \;\le\; 1 + \sigma_{t,t',b,k} \qquad \forall\, (t,t')\in\mathcal{P},\,b,k
$$

**(C19) Temporal separation of opposing trains on the shared track (safety gap h_opp):**
$$
\sum_{k'\le k+h_{\text{opp}}} y_{t,b,k'} + \sum_{k'\le k} y_{t',b,k'} \;\le\; 1 + M_{\text{big}}(1-\pi_{t,t',b,k}) \quad \forall\, (t,t')\in\mathcal{P},\,b,k
$$
$$
\sum_{k'\le k+h_{\text{opp}}} y_{t',b,k'} + \sum_{k'\le k} y_{t,b,k'} \;\le\; 1 + M_{\text{big}}\,\pi_{t,t',b,k} \quad \forall\, (t,t')\in\mathcal{P},\,b,k
$$

**(C20) Linking σ with ordering variable:**
$$
\sigma_{t,t',b,k} \;\ge\; y_{t,b,k} + y_{t',b,k} - 1 \qquad \forall\, (t,t')\in\mathcal{P},\,b,k
$$

---

### 5.7 Reordering (TRP)

**(C21) Allow overtaking only at stations:**
$$
x_{t,b,k} + x_{t',b,k} \;\le\; 1 \quad \forall\, (t,t')\in\mathcal{H},\; b \notin \mathcal{B}_{\text{station}}
$$
where $\mathcal{B}_{\text{station}}$ are block sections adjacent to stations.

---

### 5.8 Initial and terminal conditions

**(C22) Initial position and time:**
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} x_{t,1,k} \;=\; 1, \qquad \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} k\, x_{t,1,k} \;=\; \bar d_{t,1}/\Delta t \qquad \forall\, t
$$

**(C23) Final block must be occupied exactly once:**
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} x_{t,B,k} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall\, t
$$

---

### 5.9 Variable domains

$$
\begin{aligned}
&x_{t,b,k},\, y_{t,b,k},\, r_{t,b},\, \delta_{t,b,k,\ell},\, \pi_{t,t',b,k},\, \sigma_{t,t',b,k} \in \{0,1\} \\
&v_{t,b,k},\, e_{t,b,k},\, a_{t,s},\, d_{t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_+ \\
&\delta_{t,b,k,\ell} \text{ forms an SOS2 set for each } (t,b,k)
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 6. Summary of the Integrated Model

The model **TRSMP-MILP** is:

$$
\min \; Z \quad \text{subject to } (C1)\text{–}(C23).
$$

It simultaneously decides:

| Decision | Variable |
|---|---|
| Retiming (arrival/departure) | $a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}$ |
| Reordering (overtaking) | $\pi_{t,t',b,k}$ |
| Rerouting (opposite track) | $y_{t,b,k}, r_{t,b}$ |
| Speed profile | $v_{t,b,k}$ |
| Energy consumption | $e_{t,b,k}$ |
| Block occupancy / conflict resolution | $x_{t,b,k}, \sigma_{t,t',b,k}$ |

while guaranteeing:
- **Conflict-free** bidirectional operation (C17–C20),
- **Disruption compliance** (C2, C4),
- **Kinematic feasibility** of every speed profile (C6–C9),
- **Energy-aware** driving (C10–C12),
- **Schedule adherence** via the objective penalties.

This MILP constitutes the integrated foundation referenced in Section 4 of the paper and serves as the master problem that the decomposition-based solution framework (Section 5) addresses through the reformulated IP model and the adaptive iterative algorithm with local branching.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage: A MILP Formulation

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a partial segment blockage disrupts operations during a specified time window. Trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track within the disruption area, requiring precise coordination of bidirectional traffic.

**Assumptions (marked where inferred):**

- **(A1)** The railway line is discretized into a set of segments $e \in \mathcal{E}$ connecting consecutive stations. Each segment has a single-track per direction, but bidirectional use is permitted within the disruption area during the disruption window (local rerouting).
- **(A2)** Each train follows a fixed sequence of stations (no full-line rerouting); only local rerouting within the disruption area is allowed.
- **(A3)** Train speed profiles are approximated by discrete speed levels, enabling piecewise-linear energy consumption modeling. *(Reasonable assumption for MILP tractability.)*
- **(A4)** Acceleration and deceleration are bounded and modeled via speed-level transitions with fixed transition times. *(Assumption: transition times are known constants.)*
- **(A5)** Dwell times at stations are decision variables bounded by minimum and maximum values.
- **(A6)** The disruption is characterized by a blocked segment $e^*$ and a time window $[t^{\text{start}}, t^{\text{end}}]$ during which one track direction is unavailable.
- **(A7)** Train cancellations are permitted but penalized heavily in the objective. *(Assumption: cancellation is a last resort.)*
- **(A8)** Headway constraints apply between consecutive trains on the same track in the same direction.
- **(A9)** Energy consumption is a linear function of speed level and segment length (piecewise-linear approximation). *(Assumption for MILP.)*

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{E}^*$ | Set of segments in the disruption area, $\mathcal{E}^* \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of directions, $\mathcal{D} = \{+1, -1\}$ (up/down) |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $v$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of track resources (blocks/sections), indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of station-sequence positions for train $i$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Train Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses segment $e$; 0 if cancelled or rerouted away |
| $y_{i,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $e \in \mathcal{E}^*$ (uses opposite track) |
| $z_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\delta_{i,j,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$ (same direction) |
| $\gamma_{i,j,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ (direction $+$) and train $j$ (direction $-$) conflict on segment $e \in \mathcal{E}^*$; ordering variable |

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $u_{i,e,v}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ travels on segment $e$ at speed level $v$ |
| $r_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $E_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $e$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$
\min \quad \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{\text{sch}} \right)^+ + \beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} E_{i,e} + \gamma \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_i
$$

where $(\cdot)^+ = \max(0, \cdot)$ is linearized via auxiliary variables $\theta_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{\text{sch}}$, $\theta_{i,s} \geq 0$. Parameters $\alpha, \beta, \gamma > 0$ are weights.

**Linearized objective:**

$$
\min \quad \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \theta_{i,s} + \beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} E_{i,e} + \gamma \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Timing and Sequencing

**(C1) Arrival–departure relationship at each station:**

$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dwell,min}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \leq a_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}^{\text{dwell,max}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C2) Running time on each segment:**

$$
a_{i,s+1} \geq d_{i,s} + r_{i,e(s,s+1)}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, e = (s, s+1) \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C3) Segment running time determined by speed level:**

$$
r_{i,e} = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \frac{L_e}{V_v} \cdot u_{i,e,v}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

where $L_e$ is the length of segment $e$ and $V_v$ is the speed at level $v$.

**(C4) Exactly one speed level per segment (if train uses segment):**

$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} u_{i,e,v} = x_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C5) Cancellation linkage:**

$$
x_{i,e} \leq 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C6) Speed transition feasibility (acceleration/deceleration limits):**

$$
u_{i,e,v} + u_{i,e',v'} \leq 1, \quad \text{if } |V_v - V_{v'}| > \Delta V_{\max}, \quad \forall e, e' \text{ consecutive}
$$

*(Assumption: speed changes between consecutive segments are bounded.)*

### 5.2 Energy Consumption

**(C7) Linear energy model:**

$$
E_{i,e} = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} c_v \cdot L_e \cdot u_{i,e,v}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

where $c_v$ is the energy consumption rate (per unit distance) at speed level $v$. *(Assumption: piecewise-linear approximation.)*

### 5.3 Rerouting and Disruption Constraints

**(C8) Rerouting only within disruption area:**

$$
y_{i,e} = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, e \notin \mathcal{E}^*
$$

**(C9) Rerouting implies segment usage:**

$$
y_{i,e} \leq x_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, e \in \mathcal{E}^*
$$

**(C10) Disruption time window — trains cannot use blocked track during window:**

If train $i$ uses segment $e^* \in \mathcal{E}^*$ without rerouting, it must pass outside the disruption window:

$$
a_{i,s(e^*)} \geq t^{\text{end}} \quad \text{or} \quad d_{i,s(e^*)+1} \leq t^{\text{start}}
$$

Linearized via big-M:

$$
a_{i,s(e^*)} \geq t^{\text{end}} - M(1 - \mu_{i,e^*})
$$

$$
d_{i,s(e^*)+1} \leq t^{\text{start}} + M \cdot \mu_{i,e^*}
$$

where $\mu_{i,e^*} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates whether train $i$ passes before the disruption.

**(C11) Rerouted trains use opposite track:**

$$
y_{i,e} = 1 \implies \text{train } i \text{ uses track of direction } -d_i \text{ on segment } e
$$

### 5.4 Conflict-Free Constraints

**(C12) Same-direction headway on each segment:**

$$
d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s} + h^{\text{headway}} - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \, e = (s, s+1)
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s} + h^{\text{headway}} - M \cdot \delta_{i,j,e}, \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \, e = (s, s+1)
$$

**(C13) Ordering variable consistency:**

$$
\delta_{i,j,e} + \delta_{j,i,e} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \, e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C14) Bidirectional conflict on shared track (rerouting area):**

For trains $i$ (direction $+$) and $j$ (direction $-$) both using segment $e \in \mathcal{E}^*$ (one or both rerouted):

$$
a_{j,s} \geq d_{i,s} + h^{\text{bi}} - M(1 - \gamma_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall e = (s, s+1) \in \mathcal{E}^*
$$

$$
a_{i,s} \geq d_{j,s} + h^{\text{bi}} - M \cdot \gamma_{i,j,e}, \quad \forall e = (s, s+1) \in \mathcal{E}^*
$$

**(C15) No simultaneous occupancy of same track resource:**

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} u_{i,e,v} \cdot \mathbb{1}[\text{train } i \text{ on track } k] \leq 1, \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \, t \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{discretized}}
$$

*(Assumption: time discretization for track occupancy; alternatively, enforced via headway constraints above.)*

### 5.5 Delay and Cancellation Constraints

**(C16) Delay linearization:**

$$
\theta_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{\text{sch}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
\theta_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C17) Cancelled trains have no timing:**

$$
a_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad d_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C18) Minimum turnaround time (if applicable):**

$$
d_{i,s^{\text{terminal}}} \geq a_{i,s^{\text{terminal}}} + \tau^{\text{turn,min}} \cdot (1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

### 5.6 Domain Constraints

$$
a_{i,s}, \, d_{i,s}, \, r_{i,e}, \, E_{i,e}, \, \theta_{i,s} \geq 0
$$

$$
x_{i,e}, \, y_{i,e}, \, z_i, \, \delta_{i,j,e}, \, \gamma_{i,j,e}, \, u_{i,e,v}, \, \mu_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \alpha \sum_{i,s} \theta_{i,s} + \beta \sum_{i,e} E_{i,e} + \gamma \sum_{i} z_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C18)} \\
& \text{Domain constraints}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Key Modeling Features

| Feature | Handling |
|---------|----------|
| **Retiming** | Variables $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ with bounds |
| **Reordering** | Binary $\delta_{i,j,e}$ for same-direction ordering |
| **Rerouting** | Binary $y_{i,e}$ for opposite-track usage in disruption area |
| **Cancellation** | Binary $z_i$ with penalty in objective |
| **Speed profiles** | Discrete speed levels $u_{i,e,v}$ with energy $E_{i,e}$ |
| **Bidirectional conflicts** | Binary $\gamma_{i,j,e}$ with headway constraints |
