Text:
# MILP Formulation for TRSMP under Partial Segment Blockage with Local Rerouting

## 1. Sets and Indices
- $T$ — set of trains, indexed $t \in T$
- $S$ — set of stations (nodes), indexed $i \in S$
- $A$ — set of segments, indexed $a=(i,i{+}1) \in A$
- $D=\{\text{up},\text{down}\}$ — track directions, indexed $d$
- $V$ — set of discrete speed levels, indexed $v$
- $K$ — set of discrete time steps, indexed $k$
- $a^{*}=(i^{*},j^{*})$ — single blocked segment (assumption)
- $d_{b}\in D$ — direction whose track is blocked; $d_{a}\in D\setminus\{d_b\}$ — available opposite track
- $[dis_{start},dis_{end}]$ — disruption window (time-index bounds)

## 2. Parameters
- $sched\_arr_{t,i}$, $sched\_dep_{t,i}$ — scheduled arrival/departure times
- $min\_dw_i$, $max\_dw_i$ — min/max dwell at station $i$
- $run_{a,v}$, $en_{a,v}$ — running time and energy on segment $a$ at speed $v$
- $h_{\min}$ — minimum headway time on shared track
- $M$ — sufficiently large constant
- $w_{delay}, w_{energy}, w_{cancel}$ — objective weights
- $H_{end}$ — planning horizon end

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $arr_{t,i}\ge 0$ — arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $dep_{t,i}\ge 0$ — departure time of train $t$ from station $i$
- $dw_{t,i}\ge 0$ — dwell time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $rt_{t,a,v}\ge 0$ — running time of train $t$ on segment $a$ at speed $v$
- $e_{t,a,v}\ge 0$ — energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $a$ at speed $v$
- $dly_{t,i}\ge 0$ — tardiness of train $t$ at station $i$

**Binary:**
- $y_{t,a,v}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ traverses segment $a$ using speed $v$
- $x_{t,a,d}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ traverses segment $a$ on track $d$
- $z_{t,a}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ is rerouted on segment $a$
- $u_t\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ is canceled
- $o_{t_1,t_2,a}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t_1$ precedes train $t_2$ on segment $a$
- $m_{t,a,k,d}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $a$ on track $d$ at time $k$

## 4. Objective Function
$$
\min Z \;=\; w_{delay}\!\!\sum_{t\in T,\,i\in S} dly_{t,i} \;+\; w_{energy}\!\!\sum_{t\in T,\,a\in A,\,v\in V} e_{t,a,v} \;+\; w_{cancel}\!\!\sum_{t\in T} u_t
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Path timing and start of journey:**
$$dep_{t,i_0}=0 \quad\forall t\in T$$
$$arr_{t,a_{i+1}} \;\ge\; dep_{t,a_i}+\sum_{v\in V} rt_{t,a_i,v} \quad \forall t\in T,\; a_i \in path(t)$$

**(2) Dwell time definition and bounds:**
$$dw_{t,i}=dep_{t,i}-arr_{t,i} \quad \forall t,i\in path(t)\setminus\{i_0,i_{last}\}$$
$$min\_dw_i\cdot(1-u_t)\le dw_{t,i}\le max\_dw_i\cdot(1-u_t)$$

**(3) Speed-level selection (exactly one speed per segment, unless canceled):**
$$\sum_{v\in V} y_{t,a,v}=1-u_t \quad\forall t,a\in path(t)$$
$$rt_{t,a,v}=run_{a,v}\cdot y_{t,a,v}, \quad e_{t,a,v}=en_{a,v}\cdot y_{t,a,v}$$

**(4) Running-time bounds (from speed-level set):**
$$\min_{v} run_{a,v}\cdot(1-u_t)\;\le\;\sum_{v} rt_{t,a,v}\;\le\;\max_{v} run_{a,v}\cdot(1-u_t)$$

**(5) Delay (tardiness) definition:**
$$dly_{t,i}\ge arr_{t,i}-sched\_arr_{t,i}\cdot(1-u_t)-H_{end}\cdot u_t$$
$$dly_{t,i}\le H_{end}\cdot(1-u_t)$$

**(6) Track assignment and rerouting:**
$$\sum_{d\in D} x_{t,a,d}=1-u_t \quad\forall t,a\in path(t)$$
$$z_{t,a}\ge x_{t,a,d_{opp}}, \quad z_{t,a}\le 1-u_t, \quad z_{t,a}\le 1-x_{t,a,d_{norm}}+u_t$$

**(7) Headway / ordering on shared track** (for any pair $t_1<t_2$ sharing segment $a$, direction $d$):
$$arr_{t_2,a_1}\ge dep_{t_1,a_0}+h_{\min}-M(1-o_{t_1,t_2,a})-M(2-x_{t_1,a,d}-x_{t_2,a,d})-M(u_{t_1}+u_{t_2})$$
$$arr_{t_1,a_1}\ge dep_{t_2,a_0}+h_{\min}-M\cdot o_{t_1,t_2,a}-M(2-x_{t_1,a,d}-x_{t_2,a,d})-M(u_{t_1}+u_{t_2})$$
$$o_{t_1,t_2,a}+o_{t_2,t_1,a}\le 1+u_{t_1}+u_{t_2}$$

**(8) Time-indexed occupancy and per-track capacity:**
$$m_{t,a,k,d}\le x_{t,a,d}$$
$$dep_{t,a_0}\le k+M(1-m_{t,a,k,d})+M(1-x_{t,a,d})$$
$$arr_{t,a_1}\ge k-M(1-m_{t,a,k,d})-M(1-x_{t,a,d})$$
$$\sum_{t\in T} m_{t,a,k,d}\le 1 \quad \forall a,k,d$$

**(9) Endogenous disruption-window / blocked track constraint:**
Let $ovlp_t\in\{0,1\}$ with auxiliary binaries $\alpha_t$ ("$dep_{t,i^*}\le dis_{end}$") and $\beta_t$ ("$arr_{t,j^*}\ge dis_{start}$"):
$$dep_{t,i^*}\le dis_{end}+M(1-\alpha_t), \quad dep_{t,i^*}\ge dis_{end}+1-M\cdot\alpha_t$$
$$arr_{t,j^*}\ge dis_{start}-M(1-\beta_t), \quad arr_{t,j^*}\le dis_{start}-1+M\cdot\beta_t$$
$$ovlp_t\le \alpha_t,\quad ovlp_t\le\beta_t,\quad ovlp_t\ge\alpha_t+\beta_t-1$$
$$x_{t,a^{*},d_b}\le 1-ovlp_t+u_t, \quad x_{t,a^{*},d_a}\ge ovlp_t-u_t$$

**(10) Cancellation and path integrity (no resource usage if canceled):**
$$x_{t,a,d}\le 1-u_t, \quad y_{t,a,v}\le 1-u_t$$
$$arr_{t,i}\le H_{end}(1-u_t), \quad dep_{t,i}\le H_{end}(1-u_t)$$

**(11) Domain restrictions:**
$$arr_{t,i},dep_{t,i},dw_{t,i},rt_{t,a,v},e_{t,a,v},dly_{t,i}\ge 0$$
$$y_{t,a,v},x_{t,a,d},z_{t,a},u_t,o_{t_1,t_2,a},m_{t,a,k,d},ovlp_t\in\{0,1\}$$

## 6. Key Coupling (Integration of TRP and TSMP)
- *Speed ↔ timing:* (3) links $y\to rt$, used in (1) to determine $arr$.
- *Routing ↔ conflict:* $x$ variables drive both track choice (6) and headway/occupancy (7)–(8).
- *Disruption ↔ rescheduling:* (9) uses the actual $dep/arr$ to detect window overlap and forces rerouting to $d_a$.

## 7. Assumptions (marked explicitly)
1. **Single affected segment** $a^{*}$ and **single blocked direction** $d_b$.
2. **Discrete speed levels** $V$ with exogenous running time $run_{a,v}$ and energy $en_{a,v}$.
3. **Uniform time discretization** of the planning horizon.
4. **Predefined ordered paths** for each train; rerouting only swaps track direction on a segment.
5. **Minimum headway** on shared track is the only track-side safety constraint (no signaling-block detail).
6. **Single-track-per-direction** capacity; bidirectional trains share the available track in the affected segment.
7. **Cancellation is a binary service decision**; canceled trains incur no resource use.
8. **Dwell-time and running-time bounds** are derived from discrete speed-level sets and operating rules.
9. **Big-M linearization** is used for all disjunctions (occupancy, headway, overlap); $M$ is a sufficiently large constant.
10. **Tardiness-only delay** measure (early arrivals do not incur delay).

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete linear model derived from the code, presented as equations. Reasonable assumptions are marked with **[ASSUMPTION]**.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line), indexed by $s$ |
| $B$ | Set of blocks (track sections between consecutive stations), indexed by $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized speed/control levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $D \subseteq B$ | Set of disruption-affected blocks |

Each block $b$ maps to an ordered pair of stations $(s^{\text{up}}_b, s^{\text{down}}_b)$, i.e., upstream and downstream stations.

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\tau_{i,b,k}$ | Minimum running time of train $i$ on block $b$ at speed level $k$ |
| $E_{i,b,k}$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on block $b$ at speed level $k$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $a_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $T^{\text{start}}_b,\ T^{\text{end}}_b$ | Disruption time window for block $b$ |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum same-direction headway |
| $h_{\text{reroute}}$ | Minimum opposite-direction headway on shared segment |
| $\text{dwell}_{\min}$ | Minimum dwell time at a station |
| $w_{\text{delay}},\ w_{\text{energy}},\ w_{\text{cancel}}$ | Objective weights |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $\text{speed\_adj}(k)$ | Set of admissible next speed levels after level $k$ (acceleration/deceleration limits) |

---

## Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Rescheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Rescheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on block $b$ |
| $z_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled on block $b$ |
| $\delta_{i,j,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $b$ (for $i \neq j$) |
| $u_{i,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on block $b$ |
| $e_{i,b}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on block $b$ |
| $\text{delay}_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min\;
w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \text{delay}_{i,s}
\;+\;
w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{b \in B} e_{i,b}
\;+\;
w_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{b \in B} z_{i,b}
$$

---

## Constraints

### (1) Arrival–Departure Linkage (running time depends on speed level)

$$
y_{i,s^{\text{down}}_b} \;\geq\; x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} \;+\; \sum_{k \in K} u_{i,b,k}\,\tau_{i,b,k}
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B
$$

### (2) Minimum Dwell Time

$$
x_{i,s} \;\geq\; y_{i,s} + \text{dwell}_{\min}
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$

### (3) Delay Definition

$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \;\geq\; x_{i,s} - d_{i,s}
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S
$$

### (4) Speed Level Selection (one level per active block)

$$
\sum_{k \in K} u_{i,b,k} \;=\; 1 - z_{i,b}
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B
$$

### (5) Energy Consumption

$$
e_{i,b} \;=\; \sum_{k \in K} u_{i,b,k}\,E_{i,b,k}
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B
$$

### (6) Disruption / Forced Rerouting

If a train's traversal interval $[x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b},\ y_{i,s^{\text{down}}_b}]$ overlaps the disruption window $[T^{\text{start}}_b, T^{\text{end}}_b]$, then $r_{i,b}=1$ (unless cancelled):

$$
y_{i,s^{\text{down}}_b} \;\geq\; T^{\text{start}}_b - M\,(1 - r_{i,b}) - M\,z_{i,b}
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B
$$

$$
x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} \;\leq\; T^{\text{end}}_b + M\,(1 - r_{i,b}) + M\,z_{i,b}
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B
$$

**[ASSUMPTION]** If the train is cancelled on block $b$ ($z_{i,b}=1$), rerouting is not required. Waiting is allowed only if the train has not yet entered the disruption window.

### (7) Rerouting Capacity (single opposite track)

$$
\sum_{i \in T} r_{i,b} \;\leq\; 1
\qquad \forall b \in B
$$

**[ASSUMPTION]** Capacity of the opposite track is 1 (single-track bidirectional operation).

### (8) Same-Direction Headway

For $i \neq j$:

$$
x_{j,s^{\text{up}}_b} - x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} \;\geq\; h_{\min} - M\,(1 - \delta_{i,j,b}) - M\,(r_{i,b} + r_{j,b})
\qquad \forall i,j \in T,\ b \in B
$$

$$
x_{j,s^{\text{up}}_b} - x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} \;\geq\; h_{\min} - M\,(1 - \delta_{i,j,b}) - M\,(2 - r_{i,b} - r_{j,b})
\qquad \forall i,j \in T,\ b \in B
$$

**[ASSUMPTION]** Same-direction headway applies when both trains use the same track, i.e., $r_{i,b} = r_{j,b}$.

### (9) Opposite-Direction Headway (conflict on shared track)

For $i \neq j$:

$$
x_{j,s^{\text{up}}_b} - x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} \;\geq\; h_{\text{reroute}} - M\,(1 - \delta_{i,j,b}) - M\,(1 - r_{i,b})
\qquad \forall i,j \in T,\ b \in B
$$

$$
x_{j,s^{\text{up}}_b} - x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} \;\geq\; h_{\text{reroute}} - M\,(1 - \delta_{i,j,b}) - M\,(1 - r_{j,b})
\qquad \forall i,j \in T,\ b \in B
$$

### (10) Ordering Transitivity

$$
\delta_{i,j,b} + \delta_{j,i,b} \;=\; 1
\qquad \forall i \neq j \in T,\ b \in B
$$

### (11) Cancellation (freeze times at scheduled values)

For block $b$ with endpoints $(s^{\text{up}}_b, s^{\text{down}}_b)$:

$$
d_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} - M\,(1 - z_{i,b}) \;\leq\; x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} \;\leq\; d_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} + M\,(1 - z_{i,b})
$$

$$
a_{i,s^{\text{down}}_b} - M\,(1 - z_{i,b}) \;\leq\; y_{i,s^{\text{down}}_b} \;\leq\; a_{i,s^{\text{down}}_b} + M\,(1 - z_{i,b})
$$

$$
\forall i \in T,\ b \in B
$$

### (12) Speed Profile Continuity (acceleration/deceleration limits)

For consecutive blocks $b_1 \to b_2$ (i.e., $s^{\text{down}}_{b_1} = s^{\text{up}}_{b_2}$):

$$
u_{i,b_1,k} + u_{i,b_2,k'} \;\leq\; 1
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ k \in K,\ k' \notin \text{speed\_adj}(k)
$$

### (13) Rerouting Time Window

If $r_{i,b}=1$, traversal must lie within the disruption window (for $b \in D$):

$$
x_{i,s^{\text{up}}_b} \;\geq\; T^{\text{start}}_b - M\,(1 - r_{i,b})
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ b \in D
$$

$$
y_{i,s^{\text{down}}_b} \;\leq\; T^{\text{end}}_b + M\,(1 - r_{i,b})
\qquad \forall i \in T,\ b \in D
$$

### (14) Variable Domains

$$
x_{i,s},\ y_{i,s},\ e_{i,b},\ \text{delay}_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0
$$

$$
r_{i,b},\ z_{i,b},\ \delta_{i,j,b},\ u_{i,b,k} \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$

---

## Summary of Modeling Assumptions

1. **Continuous time, discrete speed levels** — times are continuous; speed choices are drawn from a finite set $K$.
2. **Block–station mapping** — each block connects two consecutive stations; arrival at the downstream station equals departure from the upstream station plus running time.
3. **Rerouting semantics** — $r_{i,b}=1$ means the train uses the opposite track on block $b$; only permitted on disrupted blocks.
4. **Forced reroute or wait** — a train whose traversal overlaps the disruption window must reroute or wait until the window clears.
5. **Single opposite track** — capacity of the opposite track is 1.
6. **Cancellation at block level** — partial cancellation is modeled per block; cancelled trains have frozen times.
7. **Headway differentiation** — same-direction headway $h_{\min}$ when both trains share a track; opposite-direction headway $h_{\text{reroute}}$ when at least one is rerouted.
8. **Speed continuity via adjacency** — admissible transitions between consecutive blocks are encoded in $\text{speed\_adj}(k)$, capturing acceleration/deceleration limits.

Text:
# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete, linear MILP formulation for the integrated TRSMP under partial segment blockage disruptions. It is fully linear, solvable by standard MILP solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP), and captures retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed-profile selection in a single framework.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,S\}$ | Stations; segment $s$ connects station $s$ to $s+1$ |
| $i,j \in \mathcal{T} = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | Trains |
| $k \in \mathcal{K}_{i,s}$ | Precomputed speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $d_i \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ | Direction of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Disrupted segment(s) |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{aff}}$ | Trains whose direction is affected by the disruption |
| $\mathcal{C}_s$ | Conflicting train pairs on segment $s$ (share the same physical track) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $A^{\text{sch}}_{i,s},\, D^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{\text{run}}_{i,s,k}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ using profile $k$ |
| $e_{i,s,k}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ using profile $k$ |
| $t^{\min\text{dw}}_s,\, t^{\max\text{dw}}_s$ | Min / max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $H$ | Minimum headway (safety separation) on shared track |
| $H_{\text{st}}$ | Minimum headway at stations |
| $T_{\text{start}},\, T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time-window bounds |
| $\delta_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if segment $s$ is disrupted **and** train $i$'s direction is affected |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $W_{\text{delay}}, W_{\text{energy}}, W_{\text{cancel}}, W_{\text{reroute}}$ | Objective weights |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\text{delay}_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ continuous | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{i,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled on segment $s$ |
| $r_{i,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $y_{i,j,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $z_{i,s,k}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$ |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = 
W_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \text{delay}_{i,s}
\;+\; W_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_{i,s}} e_{i,s,k}\, z_{i,s,k}
\;+\; W_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} x_{i,s}
\;+\; W_{\text{reroute}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} r_{i,s}
$$

with $W_{\text{cancel}} \gg W_{\text{delay}} \gg W_{\text{reroute}} > 0$, and $W_{\text{energy}}$ scaled to comparable magnitude.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Dwell time feasibility**
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} + t^{\min\text{dw}}_s - M\,x_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \le a_{i,s} + t^{\max\text{dw}}_s + M\,x_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C2) Running time (speed profile selection)**
$$
a_{i,s+1} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_{i,s}} t^{\text{run}}_{i,s,k}\, z_{i,s,k} - M\,x_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,\; s=1,\dots,S-1
$$

**(C3) Exactly one speed profile per non-cancelled train-segment**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_{i,s}} z_{i,s,k} = 1 - x_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C4) Delay definition**
$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - A^{\text{sch}}_{i,s} - M\,x_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C5) Rerouting eligibility**
$$
r_{i,s} \le \delta_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
$$
$$
r_{i,s} \le 1 - x_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C6) Disruption window blocking (non-rerouted affected trains must wait past $T_{\text{end}}$)**
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge T_{\text{end}} - M\,(r_{i,s} + x_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}^{\text{aff}},\; s \in \mathcal{D}
$$

**(C7) Rerouted train must operate within the disruption window**
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge T_{\text{start}} - M\,(1 - r_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i, s
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \le T_{\text{end}} + M\,(1 - r_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C8) Conflict-free headway on shared track (same direction or rerouted pairs)**
For each conflicting pair $(i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s$:
$$
a_{j,s+1} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} + H - M\,(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M\,(x_{i,s} + x_{j,s})
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \ge \text{dep}_{j,s} + H - M\,y_{i,j,s} - M\,(x_{i,s} + x_{j,s})
$$

**(C9) Ordering consistency**
$$
y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} = 1 \qquad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s,\; i < j
$$

**(C10) Rerouting conflicts with opposite-direction trains**
If train $i$ reroutes on segment $s$ ($r_{i,s}=1$), it shares the opposite track with opposite-direction trains $j$. For each such pair:
$$
a_{j,s+1} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} + H - M\,(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M\,(1 - r_{i,s}) - M\,x_{j,s}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \ge \text{dep}_{j,s} + H - M\,y_{i,j,s} - M\,(1 - r_{i,s}) - M\,x_{j,s}
$$

**(C11) Cancellation propagation (no reappearance downstream)**
$$
a_{i,s+1} \le M\,(1 - x_{i,s}) + \text{dep}_{i,s} + t^{\max}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
$$
$$
x_{i,s+1} \ge x_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C12) No overtaking inside segments**
For any pair $(i,j)$ with $y_{i,j,s}=1$:
$$
a_{i,s+1} \le a_{j,s+1} + M\,(1 - y_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s
$$

**(C13) Station capacity / no overtaking at stations**
For trains $i,j$ at the same station $s$ with the same direction:
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \le \text{dep}_{j,s} + M\,(1 - y_{i,j,s}) + M\,(x_{i,s} + x_{j,s})
$$

**(C14) Minimum headway at stations**
$$
a_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s} + H_{\text{st}} - M\,(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M\,(x_{i,s} + x_{j,s})
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{j,s} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} + H_{\text{st}} - M\,(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M\,(x_{i,s} + x_{j,s})
$$

**(C15) Speed profile consistency with segment length**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_{i,s}} z_{i,s,k} \cdot v^{\text{avg}}_{i,s,k} \cdot t^{\text{run}}_{i,s,k} = L_s \cdot (1 - x_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C16) Domain constraints**
$$
a_{i,s},\; \text{dep}_{i,s},\; \text{delay}_{i,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s
$$
$$
x_{i,s},\; r_{i,s},\; y_{i,j,s},\; z_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall i,j,s,k
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Timetable variables** ($a_{i,s}, \text{dep}_{i,s}$) capture the retimed schedule; dwell constraints (C1) ensure realistic station stops; running time (C2) links consecutive stations through the selected speed profile.
- **Speed profile selection** ($z_{i,s,k}$): a finite set of precomputed energy-optimal profiles (traction/cruise/coast/braking) per segment per train type. Constraint (C3) forces exactly one profile for non-cancelled trains; the objective's energy term then selects the most energy-efficient feasible profile.
- **Delay** ($\text{delay}_{i,s}$): non-negative deviation from the original schedule (C4), minimized in the objective.
- **Rerouting** ($r_{i,s}$): allowed only for affected-direction trains on disrupted segments (C5). Constraint (C6) forces non-rerouted affected trains to wait until $T_{\text{end}}$; constraint (C7) keeps rerouted trains inside the disruption window — modeling single-track bidirectional operation.
- **Conflict resolution** ($y_{i,j,s}$): ordering binaries enforce minimum headway $H$ between trains sharing the same physical track — same-direction (C8) or rerouted-vs-opposite-direction (C10). Constraint (C9) ensures a consistent total order; (C12) prevents overtaking inside segments.
- **Cancellation** ($x_{i,s}$): large penalty discourages cancellation; big-M terms in (C1)–(C4) relax timing constraints for cancelled trains; (C11) propagates cancellation downstream.
- **Station constraints** (C13)–(C14): prevent overtaking and enforce headway at stations.
- **Big-M**: chosen large enough to deactivate a constraint when its associated binary is 0, e.g. $M = T_{\text{end}} + \max_{i,s,k} t^{\text{run}}_{i,s,k} + \sum_s t^{\max\text{dw}}_s$.
- **Objective weights**: $W_{\text{cancel}}$ very large (e.g. $10^6$) to make cancellation a last resort; $W_{\text{delay}}$ reflects passenger cost; $W_{\text{energy}}$ reflects operational cost; $W_{\text{reroute}}$ is a small penalty to discourage unnecessary track sharing.

**Assumptions (marked):** single bidirectional track per segment; finite precomputed speed profiles per (train, segment); constant minimum headway $H$; disruption window known a priori; no overtaking inside segments (only at stations); energy values precomputed per profile; linear MILP structure preserved throughout.

This formulation is fully linear and captures the integrated rescheduling, rerouting, ordering, and speed-management decisions under partial segment blockage.

# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T = \{i, j\}$ | Set of trains |
| $S = \{s, k\}$ | Set of stations, ordered by index along the line |
| $D = \{d\}$ | Set of directions (up/down); $\text{opp}(d)$ = reverse direction |
| $E = \{e\}$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations; segment $e$ connects $s(e)$ to $s(e)+1$ |
| $B = \{b\}$ | Set of track resources (blocks). $e_0 \in E$ is the disrupted segment; $d_0$ is the blocked direction |
| $P = \{p\}$ | Set of piecewise speed-profile modes (accel, cruise, coast, brake), each with nominal run time and energy |

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T^{\text{dep}}_{i,s},\ T^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure / arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $W^{\min}_i,\ W^{\max}_i$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time of train $i$ |
| $RT_{i,e}$ | Nominal running time of $i$ on segment $e$ (uninterrupted) |
| $h$ | Minimum safety headway between consecutive trains sharing a track resource |
| $\tau$ | Minimum turnaround / setup time to switch direction usage on shared track |
| $RT_{i,e,p}$ | Running time of $i$ on $e$ with speed-profile mode $p$ |
| $E_{i,e,p}$ | Energy consumed by $i$ on $e$ with mode $p$ |
| $E^{\text{cap}}$ | Regenerative-braking energy cap per (train, segment) *[assumption A13]* |
| $\Lambda_{e_0},\ \Lambda^{\text{end}}_{e_0}$ | Disruption start / end time on blocked segment $e_0$ |
| $CP_i$ | Cancellation penalty for train $i$ |
| $\alpha,\ \beta$ | Weights on total delay and total energy, respectively *[assumption A7]* |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |

## Decision Variables

**Continuous (≥ 0):**

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $dep_{i,s}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $rt_{i,e}$ | Actual running time of $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $dwell_{i,s}$ | Actual dwell time of $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}$ | Arrival / departure delay (nonnegative parts) |
| $En_{i,e}$ | Energy consumed by $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $t^{\text{in}}_{i,e},\ t^{\text{out}}_{i,e}$ | Entry / exit time of $i$ into/from resource $e$ |

**Binary:**

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{i,e,p}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ using mode $p$ |
| $y_{i,e}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $e$ (only $e_0$) |
| $z_i$ | 1 if train $i$ is canceled |
| $o_{i,j,e}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on resource $e$ (same-track ordering) |
| $q_{i,j,e}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes $j$ on resource $e$ with direction reversal (reroute) |
| $w_i$ | 1 if affected train $i$ waits for the disruption end (vs. traveling before window) |

---

## Assumptions

*[Marked as reasonable, since not fully specified in the input:]*

- **A1** — The line is linear; stations are ordered and consecutive stations define segments.
- **A2** — Each train has fixed origin/destination and direction, except for local rerouting.
- **A3** — Only one disrupted segment $e_0$ with one blocked direction $d_0$; window $[\Lambda_{e_0}, \Lambda^{\text{end}}_{e_0}]$ is known.
- **A4** — Rerouting is *local* (only on $e_0$), per problem statement.
- **A5** — Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set $P$ with precomputed run times/energies.
- **A6** — Dwell times are bounded by $[W^{\min}_i, W^{\max}_i]$.
- **A7** — Delay is measured against the schedule; early operation is not rewarded (nonnegative delays).
- **A8** — No simultaneous occupancy of a block; headway $h$ enforced between consecutive users.
- **A9** — Energy is additive across segments.
- **A10** — Cancellation relaxes all downstream constraints of a train.
- **A11** — Bidirectional sharing occurs only on the opposite track during the disruption.
- **A12** — All times are continuous and in consistent units.
- **A13** — Regenerative-braking energy per segment is capped; net energy ≥ 0.

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min\ \ \alpha \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\left(\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} + \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}\right)
\;+\; \beta \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{e\in E} En_{i,e}
\;+\; \sum_{i\in T} CP_i\, z_i
$$

---

## Constraints

### 1. Speed-profile selection and coupling of time & energy

$$
\sum_{p \in P} x_{i,e,p} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\ e \in E \tag{1}
$$

$$
rt_{i,e} = \sum_{p \in P} RT_{i,e,p}\, x_{i,e,p} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ e \in E \tag{2}
$$

$$
En_{i,e} = \sum_{p \in P} E_{i,e,p}\, x_{i,e,p} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ e \in E \tag{3}
$$

### 2. Time propagation (arrival / departure / dwell / running)

$$
a_{i,s+1} = dep_{i,s} + rt_{i,(s,s+1)} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ \text{consecutive } s \tag{4}
$$

$$
dep_{i,s} = a_{i,s} + dwell_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \tag{5}
$$

$$
W^{\min}_i (1 - z_i) \le dwell_{i,s} \le W^{\max}_i (1 - z_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \tag{6}
$$

$$
dep_{i,\text{origin}} \ge T^{\text{dep}}_{i,\text{origin}} - M z_i \tag{7}
$$

$$
a_{i,s} \ge T^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} - M z_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \tag{8}
$$

### 3. Nonnegative delay definitions

$$
\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - T^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \tag{9}
$$

$$
\delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge dep_{i,s} - T^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \tag{10}
$$

### 4. Rerouting on the disrupted segment

$$
y_{i,e_0} \le 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{11}
$$

$$
y_{i,e} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\ e \in E \setminus \{e_0\} \tag{12}
$$

A train in the blocked direction must either wait for the disruption to end or reroute:

$$
dep_{i,s(e_0)} \ge \Lambda^{\text{end}}_{e_0} - M\, y_{i,e_0} - M\, z_i \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{13}
$$

### 5. Entry / exit time linking

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,e} = dep_{i,s(e)} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ e \in E \tag{14}
$$

$$
t^{\text{out}}_{i,e} = a_{i,s(e)+1} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ e \in E \tag{15}
$$

### 6. Disruption-window disjunction (wait-before vs. go-after)

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,e_0} \ge \Lambda^{\text{end}}_{e_0} - M(1 - w_i) - M z_i \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{16}
$$

$$
t^{\text{out}}_{i,e_0} \le \Lambda_{e_0} + M w_i + M z_i \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{17}
$$

$$
w_i + y_{i,e_0} \le 1 + z_i \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{18}
$$

### 7. Conflict-free sequencing on shared resources (same direction)

For all pairs $(i,j)$ sharing resource $e$ in the same direction:

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{j,e} \ge t^{\text{out}}_{i,e} + h - M(1 - o_{i,j,e}) - M z_i - M z_j \tag{19}
$$

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,e} \ge t^{\text{out}}_{j,e} + h - M\, o_{i,j,e} - M z_i - M z_j \tag{20}
$$

$$
o_{i,j,e} + o_{j,i,e} = 1 - z_i - z_j \qquad \text{(when both active)} \tag{21}
$$

### 8. Bidirectional conflict on opposite track (rerouted vs. unaffected opposite-direction)

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{j,e_0} \ge t^{\text{out}}_{i,e_0} + h + \tau - M(1 - q_{i,j,e_0}) - M z_i - M z_j \tag{22}
$$

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,e_0} \ge t^{\text{out}}_{j,e_0} + h + \tau - M\, q_{i,j,e_0} - M z_i - M z_j \tag{23}
$$

### 9. Cancellation relaxation of timing bounds

$$
a_{i,s} \le M (1 - z_i) + T^{\max} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \tag{24}
$$

$$
dep_{i,s} \le M (1 - z_i) + T^{\max} \qquad \forall i \in T,\ s \in S \tag{25}
$$

### 10. Energy regeneration cap

$$
En_{i,e} \le E^{\text{cap}} (1 - z_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\ e \in E \tag{26}
$$

### 11. Variable domains

$$
x_{i,e,p},\ y_{i,e},\ z_i,\ o_{i,j,e},\ q_{i,j,e},\ w_i \in \{0,1\} \tag{27}
$$

$$
a_{i,s},\ dep_{i,s},\ rt_{i,e},\ dwell_{i,s},\ \delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\ \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s},\ En_{i,e},\ t^{\text{in}}_{i,e},\ t^{\text{out}}_{i,e} \ge 0 \tag{28}
$$

---

## Remark on Solution Method (not part of the base MILP)

The **decomposition** described in the paper (IP for train interactions + independent train-plan subproblems + adaptive refinement + local branching) is a *solution algorithm* for the above MILP, not a separate model. The base MILP (1)–(28) is exact and equivalent to the reformulated IP model when the discretization of interval plans is sufficiently fine, as proved in the referenced work.

Text:
# A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure-Aware Shunting

## 1. Motivation and Modeling Scope

The problem described combines two coupled decision problems: (i) **rolling stock rescheduling** (assigning train units to trips and composing trains), and (ii) **shunting feasibility** (checking that each required shunting movement can be executed on the available station infrastructure, possibly delaying other trains by a few minutes). We present a complete, linear MILP that captures both aspects in a single model. This corresponds to the "exact" (Combinatorial Benders'-style) integrated view; the iterative heuristic can be obtained by decomposing the same model.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of train trips in the (disrupted) timetable, indexed by $t$ |
| $U$ | Set of rolling stock units, indexed by $u$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of rolling stock compositions (unit-type combinations), indexed by $k$ |
| $M_s$ | Set of shunting movements at station $s$, indexed by $m$ |
| $R_s$ | Set of station tracks (resources) at station $s$, indexed by $r$ |
| $E_s$ | Set of infrastructure events (shunting movements + passing trains) at station $s$, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time slots, indexed by $\tau$ |
| $P$ | Set of consecutive trip pairs (precedence relations), indexed by $(t,t')$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

### Rolling Stock Parameters
| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $c^{\text{unit}}_u$ | Fixed cost of using unit $u$ (capital/operational) |
| $c^{\text{seat}}$ | Penalty per unit of unmet seat demand (passenger service level) |
| $c^{\text{dev}}$ | Penalty per deviation from the original rolling stock plan |
| $c^{\text{shunt}}$ | Cost per shunting movement |
| $c^{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty per minute of delay imposed on a passing train |
| $d_t$ | Passenger seat demand on trip $t$ |
| $\text{cap}_k$ | Seat capacity of composition $k$ |
| $\text{len}_k$ | Number of units in composition $k$ |
| $\text{type}(k)$ | Unit-type vector of composition $k$ |
| $\text{orig}(t)$ | Original composition assigned to trip $t$ (for deviation penalty) |
| $\delta^{\text{min}}$ | Minimum turnaround (shunting) time between two consecutive trips |
| $\Delta^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed delay (minutes) for any passing train (assumption: $\Delta^{\max}=3$) |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-$M$) |

### Infrastructure Parameters
| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $a_e$ | Scheduled start time of event $e$ |
| $b_e$ | Scheduled end time of event $e$ |
| $\ell_e$ | Duration of event $e$ ($= b_e - a_e$) |
| $\text{occ}_{e,r}$ | $=1$ if event $e$ can use track $r$ |
| $\text{headway}$ | Minimum separation time between two events on the same track |
| $\text{shunt}(m)$ | The infrastructure event corresponding to shunting movement $m$ |
| $\text{unit}(m)$ | The rolling stock unit involved in shunting movement $m$ |
| $\text{station}(m)$ | Station at which shunting movement $m$ occurs |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Rolling Stock Variables
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,k}$ | Binary | 1 if composition $k$ is assigned to trip $t$ |
| $y_{u,t}$ | Binary | 1 if unit $u$ is part of the composition on trip $t$ |
| $z_{u,t,t'}$ | Binary | 1 if unit $u$ connects trip $t$ to trip $t'$ (consecutive trips) |
| $w_{u,m}$ | Binary | 1 if unit $u$ performs shunting movement $m$ |
| $q_t$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Unmet seat demand on trip $t$ |
| $v_t$ | Binary | 1 if trip $t$ deviates from original composition |

### Infrastructure Variables
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\alpha_{e,r}$ | Binary | 1 if event $e$ is assigned to track $r$ |
| $\beta_{e,e'}$ | Binary | 1 if event $e$ precedes event $e'$ on the same track |
| $\gamma_e$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Delay (minutes) assigned to event $e$ |
| $\eta_m$ | Binary | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is executed |
| $\theta_{m}$ | Binary | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is canceled |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total cost:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{u \in U} c^{\text{unit}}_u \sum_{t \in T} y_{u,t}}_{\text{unit usage}}
+ \underbrace{c^{\text{seat}} \sum_{t \in T} q_t}_{\text{unmet demand}}
+ \underbrace{c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{t \in T} v_t}_{\text{plan deviation}}
+ \underbrace{c^{\text{shunt}} \sum_{m \in M} \eta_m}_{\text{shunting cost}}
+ \underbrace{c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{e \in E} \gamma_e}_{\text{delay penalty}}
$$

**Assumption:** All cost coefficients are non-negative and expressed in comparable monetary units.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Rolling Stock Composition Constraints

**(C1) Exactly one composition per trip:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{t,k} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Unit–composition consistency:** Unit $u$ is on trip $t$ iff the assigned composition contains $u$:
$$
y_{u,t} = \sum_{k \in K : u \in k} x_{t,k} \qquad \forall u \in U,\; t \in T
$$

**(C3) Seat capacity and unmet demand:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \text{cap}_k \, x_{t,k} + q_t \geq d_t \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C4) Unit conservation across consecutive trips:** For each unit $u$ and each trip $t$ (except terminal trips), the unit either continues to exactly one successor or is shunted:
$$
\sum_{t' : (t,t') \in P} z_{u,t,t'} + \sum_{m \in M : \text{unit}(m)=u,\; \text{from}(m)=t} w_{u,m} = y_{u,t} \qquad \forall u \in U,\; t \in T
$$

**(C5) Unit conservation on arrival:** For each unit $u$ and trip $t'$:
$$
\sum_{t : (t,t') \in P} z_{u,t,t'} + \sum_{m \in M : \text{unit}(m)=u,\; \text{to}(m)=t'} w_{u,m} = y_{u,t'} \qquad \forall u \in U,\; t' \in T
$$

**(C6) Minimum turnaround time:** If unit $u$ connects $t$ to $t'$:
$$
z_{u,t,t'} = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{start}(t') - \text{end}(t) \geq \delta^{\text{min}}
$$
Linearized:
$$
\text{start}(t') - \text{end}(t) \geq \delta^{\text{min}} - M(1 - z_{u,t,t'}) \qquad \forall u, (t,t') \in P
$$

**(C7) Composition length consistency:** The number of units on trip $t$ matches the composition:
$$
\sum_{u \in U} y_{u,t} = \sum_{k \in K} \text{len}_k \, x_{t,k} \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C8) Deviation indicator:**
$$
v_t \geq x_{t,k} - \mathbb{1}[k = \text{orig}(t)] \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$
$$
v_t \geq \mathbb{1}[k = \text{orig}(t)] - x_{t,k} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### 6.2 Shunting Movement Constraints

**(C9) Shunting movement execution linked to unit assignment:**
$$
\eta_m \geq w_{u,m} \qquad \forall m \in M,\; u = \text{unit}(m)
$$
$$
\eta_m \leq \sum_{u \in U} w_{u,m}
$$

**(C10) Shunting cancellation:**
$$
\eta_m + \theta_m = 1 \qquad \forall m \in M
$$

**(C11) Each unit performs at most one shunting movement per time slot:**
$$
\sum_{m \in M : \text{unit}(m)=u,\; \tau \in [a_m, b_m]} \eta_m \leq 1 \qquad \forall u \in U,\; \tau \in \mathcal{T}
$$

### 6.3 Infrastructure Feasibility Constraints

**(C12) Each event assigned to exactly one track:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_s : \text{occ}_{e,r}=1} \alpha_{e,r} = 1 \qquad \forall s \in S,\; e \in E_s
$$

**(C13) Event ordering on the same track:** For any two events $e, e'$ on the same track $r$:
$$
\beta_{e,e'} + \beta_{e',e} \geq \alpha_{e,r} + \alpha_{e',r} - 1 \qquad \forall r,\; e \neq e'
$$

**(C14) No overlap with headway on the same track:**
$$
(a_{e'} + \gamma_{e'}) - (b_e + \gamma_e) \geq \text{headway} - M(1 - \beta_{e,e'}) \qquad \forall e \neq e' \text{ on same } r
$$

**(C15) Shunting movement requires a feasible track:**
$$
\eta_m \leq \sum_{r \in R_s : \text{occ}_{\text{shunt}(m),r}=1} \alpha_{\text{shunt}(m),r} \qquad \forall m \in M
$$

**(C16) Maximum delay bound:**
$$
0 \leq \gamma_e \leq \Delta^{\max} \qquad \forall e \in E
$$

**(C17) Shunting movement time window:** A shunting movement $m$ can only be executed within its allowed window:
$$
a_m + \gamma_{\text{shunt}(m)} \geq \text{ready}(m) - M(1 - \eta_m) \qquad \forall m \in M
$$
$$
b_m + \gamma_{\text{shunt}(m)} \leq \text{deadline}(m) + M(1 - \eta_m) \qquad \forall m \in M
$$

### 6.4 Coupling Constraints

**(C18) Shunting movement requires rolling stock unit availability:**
$$
w_{u,m} \leq \eta_m \qquad \forall u \in U,\; m \in M : \text{unit}(m) = u
$$

**(C19) If shunting is canceled, the affected unit must be re-routed:**
$$
\theta_m = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \sum_{t' : (t,t') \in P} z_{u,t,t'} = y_{u,t} \qquad \forall m \in M,\; u = \text{unit}(m),\; t = \text{from}(m)
$$

**(C20) Infrastructure conflict cut (Benders-style):** For any subset $\mathcal{M}' \subseteq M$ that is infeasible on the infrastructure:
$$
\sum_{m \in \mathcal{M}'} \eta_m \leq |\mathcal{M}'| - 1
$$

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Discrete time slots:** Time is discretized into slots of one minute (assumption for tractability).
2. **Bounded delay:** Passing trains may be delayed by at most $\Delta^{\max} = 3$ minutes; longer delays are assumed absorbed by timetable buffers.
3. **Single-unit shunting:** Each shunting movement involves exactly one rolling stock unit (assumption; multi-unit movements can be modeled by aggregating units into a "consist").
4. **Track compatibility:** $\text{occ}_{e,r}$ is precomputed from track length, electrification, and unit-type compatibility.
5. **No deadlock:** The precedence variables $\beta_{e,e'}$ are assumed to yield an acyclic ordering (enforced implicitly by time ordering in C14).
6. **Deterministic disruption:** The disruption (blockage) is known with certainty; no stochastic recourse is modeled.
7. **Cost linearity:** All operational, passenger, and deviation costs are linear in the decision variables.
8. **Unit homogeneity within type:** Units of the same type are interchangeable for composition purposes.
9. **Shunting driver availability:** Assumed always available; driver scheduling is out of scope.
10. **Station capacity:** The number of tracks $|R_s|$ is fixed and known; no dynamic track closures beyond the disruption are modeled.

---

## 8. Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{u,t} c^{\text{unit}}_u y_{u,t} + c^{\text{seat}} \sum_t q_t + c^{\text{dev}} \sum_t v_t + c^{\text{shunt}} \sum_m \eta_m + c^{\text{delay}} \sum_e \gamma_e \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C20)} \\
& x_{t,k}, y_{u,t}, z_{u,t,t'}, w_{u,m}, v_t, \alpha_{e,r}, \beta_{e,e'}, \eta_m, \theta_m \in \{0,1\} \\
& q_t, \gamma_e \geq 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

This MILP integrates rolling stock rescheduling with infrastructure-aware shunting feasibility. The exact algorithm solves it directly (or via Combinatorial Benders' decomposition using cuts C20), while the iterative heuristic solves the rolling stock subproblem (C1–C11, C18–C19) and the infrastructure subproblem (C12–C17) alternately, feeding shunting movements one by one to the infrastructure model.

---

# Final MILP — Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | trains, indexed $t, t'$ |
| $S$ | stations, indexed $s$ |
| $E$ | track segments, indexed $e$; segment $e$ connects $s_e \to s_{e+1}$ (in the direction of travel of the train) |
| $E_{\text{aff}}\subseteq E$ | segments affected by the disruption |
| $E^{in}(s), E^{out}(s)\subseteq E$ | segments entering/leaving station $s$ |
| $K$ | discrete time steps, indexed $k$ |
| $R_{t,e}$ | admissible speed profiles for train $t$ on segment $e$, indexed $r$ |
| $\mathcal P^O$ | opposite-direction train pairs on $E_{\text{aff}}$: $\{(t,t',e): d(t)\ne d(t'),\, e\in E\}$ |
| $\mathcal P^S$ | same-direction train pairs: $\{(t,t',e): d(t)=d(t'),\, e\in E\}$ |
| $K_W(e,d)$ | disruption-window indices for segment $e$, direction $d$ |

Each train $t$ has direction $d(t)\in\{+1,-1\}$ and a fixed ordered sequence of segments.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\Delta$ | time-step length |
| $h_{sta}, h_{seg}$ | minimum station / segment headway |
| $\tau_s$ | minimum dwell at station $s$ |
| $a^{plan}_{t,s}, d^{plan}_{t,s}$ | planned arrival/departure times |
| $n_r$ | number of time steps of profile $r$ on its segment |
| $E_r$ | energy consumption of profile $r$ |
| $\text{Blocked}(e,d)\in\{0,1\}$ | whether $e$ in direction $d$ is blocked during the window |
| $M$ | large constant (big-M); $M \ge |K|\Delta + h_{seg}$ |
| $\varepsilon$ | small positive constant (strict-boundary convention) |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}, w_{\text{cancel}}, w_{\text{reroute}}$ | objective weights |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous**

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| $a_{t,s}, d_{t,s} \ge 0$ | arrival/departure times of $t$ at $s$ |
| $e_{t,e}, x_{t,e} \ge 0$ | entry/exit times of $t$ on segment $e$ |
| $\delta^+_{t,s} \ge 0$ | non-negative delay of $t$ at $s$ |
| $E^{tot}_{t,e} \ge 0$ | energy of $t$ on $e$ |

**Binary**

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| $\varphi_{t,e,r}$ | 1 if profile $r$ chosen for $t$ on $e$ |
| $c_t$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $r_{t,e}$ | 1 if $t$ reroutes on segment $e\in E_{\text{aff}}$ |
| $\tau_{t,e}$ | track-side assignment (0=normal, 1=opposite) |
| $\text{same}_{t,t',e}$ | 1 iff $\tau_{t,e}=\tau_{t',e}$ for $(t,t',e)\in\mathcal P^O$ |
| $y_{t,e,k}$ | 1 iff $e_{t,e}\le k\Delta$ |
| $z_{t,e,k}$ | 1 iff $k\Delta \le x_{t,e}$ |
| $o_{t,e,k}$ | occupancy of $e$ by $t$ at step $k$ (= $y \wedge z$) |
| $y^O_{t,t',e}$ | opposite-direction sequencing on $e$ |
| $y^S_{t,t',e}$ | same-direction sequencing on $e$ |

---

## 4. Objective

$$
\min\; Z = w_{\text{delay}}\!\sum_{t,s}\delta^+_{t,s}
\;+\; w_{\text{energy}}\!\sum_{t,e} E^{tot}_{t,e}
\;+\; w_{\text{cancel}}\!\sum_{t} c_t
\;+\; w_{\text{reroute}}\!\sum_{t,e\in E_{\text{aff}}} r_{t,e}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### C1. Dwell time
$$\tau_s(1-c_t)\le d_{t,s}-a_{t,s}\le \tau_s^{\max}(1-c_t)+M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s$$

### C2. Delay definition
$$\delta^+_{t,s}\ge a_{t,s}-a^{plan}_{t,s}\qquad\forall t,s$$

### C3. Timetable–segment linkage
$$e_{t,e}=d_{t,s_e},\qquad x_{t,e}=a_{t,s_{e+1}}\qquad\forall t,e$$

### C4. Profile selection (core TRP–TSMP coupling)
$$\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}}\varphi_{t,e,r}=1-c_t\qquad\forall t,e\tag{C4a}$$
$$x_{t,e}-e_{t,e}=\Delta\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}}n_r\,\varphi_{t,e,r}\qquad\forall t,e\tag{C4b}$$
$$E^{tot}_{t,e}=\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}}E_r\,\varphi_{t,e,r}\qquad\forall t,e\tag{C4c}$$

(C4b) is the integration: chosen speed profile $\Rightarrow$ segment duration $\Rightarrow$ timetable.

### C5. Occupancy indicators (exact linearization)
$$k\Delta-e_{t,e}\le M(1-y_{t,e,k})\tag{C5a}$$
$$e_{t,e}-k\Delta-\varepsilon\le M\,y_{t,e,k}\tag{C5b}$$
$$x_{t,e}-k\Delta\le M(1-z_{t,e,k})\tag{C5c}$$
$$k\Delta-x_{t,e}-\varepsilon\le M\,z_{t,e,k}\tag{C5d}$$
$$o_{t,e,k}\le y_{t,e,k},\quad o_{t,e,k}\le z_{t,e,k}\tag{C5e,f}$$
$$o_{t,e,k}\ge y_{t,e,k}+z_{t,e,k}-1\tag{C5g}$$
$$o_{t,e,k}\le 1-c_t\tag{C5h}$$

### C6. Profile–occupancy consistency
$$\sum_{k\in K}o_{t,e,k}=\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}}n_r\,\varphi_{t,e,r}\qquad\forall t,e$$

### C7. Same-direction station & segment headway
For all $(t,t')\in\mathcal P^S$ and the corresponding segment $e$:
$$a_{t',s}\ge d_{t,s}+h_{sta}-M(1-y_{t,t',s})\tag{C7a}$$
$$y_{t,t',s}+y_{t',t,s}=1\tag{C7b}$$
$$y^S_{t,t',e}+y^S_{t',t,e}=1\tag{C7c}$$
$$e_{t',e}\ge x_{t,e}+h_{seg}-M(1-y^S_{t,t',e})-M(c_t+c_{t'})\tag{C7d}$$

### C8. Track-side assignment equality (exact, $\text{same}=\mathbb 1[\tau_{t,e}=\tau_{t',e}]$)
For all $(t,t',e)\in\mathcal P^O$:
$$\text{same}_{t,t',e}\ge \tau_{t,e}+\tau_{t',e}-1\tag{C8a}$$
$$\text{same}_{t,t',e}\ge 1-\tau_{t,e}-\tau_{t',e}\tag{C8b}$$
$$\text{same}_{t,t',e}\le 1-\tau_{t,e}+\tau_{t',e}\tag{C8c}$$
$$\text{same}_{t,t',e}\le 1+\tau_{t,e}-\tau_{t',e}\tag{C8d}$$

### C9. Opposite-direction segment headway on shared track
For all $(t,t',e)\in\mathcal P^O$:
$$y^O_{t,t',e}+y^O_{t',t,e}=1\tag{C9a}$$
$$e_{t',e}\ge x_{t,e}+h_{seg}-M(1-y^O_{t,t',e})-M(1-\text{same}_{t,t',e})-M(c_t+c_{t'})\tag{C9b}$$
$$e_{t,e}\ge x_{t',e}+h_{seg}-M(1-y^O_{t',t,e})-M(1-\text{same}_{t,t',e})-M(c_t+c_{t'})\tag{C9c}$$

When $\text{same}=1$ and both active: exactly one ordering is enforced. When $\text{same}=0$ or either cancelled: constraints inactive.

### C10. Disruption
For $e\in E_{\text{aff}}$, $d=d(t)$, $k\in K_W(e,d)$:
$$o_{t,e,k}\le r_{t,e}+(1-\text{Blocked}(e,d))+c_t\tag{C10a}$$
$$e_{t,e}\ge (k_{\text{end}}+1)\Delta-M\bigl(r_{t,e}+(1-\text{Blocked}(e,d))+c_t\bigr)\tag{C10b}$$

(C10a) forbids occupancy during the window unless rerouted. (C10b) blocks entry until after the window closes when not rerouted.

### C11. Rerouting eligibility
$$r_{t,e}=0\quad\forall e\notin E_{\text{aff}},\forall t\tag{C11a}$$
$$\sum_{e\in E_{\text{aff}}}r_{t,e}\le M(1-c_t)\quad\forall t\tag{C11b}$$

### C12. Cancellation
$$e_{t,e},\,x_{t,e},\,a_{t,s},\,d_{t,s},\,E^{tot}_{t,e}\le M(1-c_t)\quad\forall t,e,s\tag{C12a}$$
$$\delta^+_{t,s}\le M(1-c_t)\quad\forall t,s\tag{C12b}$$

(C5h), (C7d), (C9b,c), (C10a,b), (C11b) all carry $+M\,c_t$ relaxers.

### C13. Variable domains
Continuous variables $\ge 0$; all binaries $\in\{0,1\}$; $n_{t,e}$ integer (or eliminated via C4b's RHS).

---

## 6. Assumptions Marked

1. **Discrete time** with step $\Delta$ converts continuous timetabling to MILP.
2. **Precomputed profile set $R_{t,e}$** encapsulates all acceleration/deceleration physics; the model selects a profile rather than optimizing continuous controls.
3. **Rerouting is segment-local** ($r_{t,e}\in\{0,1\}$ per segment); multi-segment detour paths can be added via a path-selection variable without changing the model structure.
4. **$\text{Blocked}(e,d)$ is exogenous**, derived from the disruption schedule.
5. **Track-side assignment** $\tau$ is binary; bidirectional safety on the shared track is enforced through the $\text{same}$ indicator.
6. **Big-M** chosen as $M\ge |K|\Delta+h_{seg}$ suffices for all disjunctions.
7. **Boundary convention** in C5 uses $\varepsilon>0$ for strict inequality; setting $\varepsilon=0$ yields a closed interval.
8. **Energy** is additive and determined entirely by the chosen profile (linear via C4c).
9. **Bidirectional operation** during disruption is captured by allowing $\tau=1$ on $e\in E_{\text{aff}}$; same-direction trains always use their nominal side ($\tau=0$ by default but allowed to reroute on affected segments only).

---

This MILP is now: (i) **fully linear**, (ii) **non-redundant**, (iii) **consistent** in its representation of occupancy, profile, and timetable, (iv) **faithful to the TRSMP integration** described in the narrative — the speed profile is the decision variable that simultaneously determines the timetable, the energy, and (via rerouting decisions) the route.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
## Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete model, expressed as equations. It is derived from the generated code and describes an integrated rescheduling + speed-management problem on a bidirectional high-speed corridor subject to a partial segment blockage that permits rerouting onto the opposite track.

---

### 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | set of trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | set of stations along the corridor, indexed $s$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | set of physical segments $b=(s,s+1)$, indexed $b$ |
| $\mathcal{O}_i$ | ordered list of stations in train $i$'s travel order (origin first, destination last) |
| $\mathcal{R}_i \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | segments traversed by train $i$; for each $b\in\mathcal{R}_i$ we have an ordered pair $(s^{from}_{i,b},\,s^{to}_{i,b})$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_b$ | unordered train pairs $\{i,j\}$ with $i<j$ that both traverse segment $b$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | set of speed breakpoints $\{v_1,\dots,v_K\}$ |

Unidirectional groups: $\mathcal{D}$ (downward, $s\to s+1$) and $\mathcal{U}$ (upward, $s\to s-1$).

---

### 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | length of segment $b$ |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$ | min / max admissible average speed |
| $d_s$ | minimum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $h$ | minimum safety headway on a shared track |
| $t^0_i$ | scheduled departure time of train $i$ from its origin |
| $\alpha$ | weight on energy (efficiency) |
| $\beta$ | weight on delay (per unit time) |
| $\gamma$ | cancellation penalty |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $W_b=(W_b^{s},\,W_b^{e},\,\rho_b)$ | blockage window on segment $b$ (start, end, blocked travel direction $\rho_b\in\{\mathcal{D},\mathcal{U}\}$) |
| $v_1,\dots,v_K$ | breakpoints for piecewise-linear energy approximation |

---

### 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}\ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\mathrm{dep}_{i,s}\ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,b}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses its **normal** track on segment $b$ |
| $y_{i,b}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ **reroutes** onto the opposite track on segment $b$ |
| $z_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $v_{i,b}\in[v_{\min},v_{\max}]$ | continuous | average running speed of train $i$ on segment $b$ |
| $t_{i,b}\ge 0$ | continuous | running time of train $i$ on segment $b$ |
| $e_{i,b}\ge 0$ | continuous | energy consumed by train $i$ on segment $b$ |
| $\delta_{i,j,b}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | ordering: 1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on segment $b$ |
| $\mathrm{same}_{i,j,b}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if $i,j$ use the **same** physical track on $b$ |
| $\mathrm{blk}_{i,b}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ clears segment $b$ **before** $W_b^s$, 0 if it enters **after** $W_b^e$ |

---

### 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\;
\underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{b\in\mathcal{R}_i} e_{i,b}}_{\text{energy}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\beta \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} \bigl(a_{i,\text{dest}(i)} - t^0_{i}\bigr)}_{\text{terminal delay}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\gamma \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} z_{i}}_{\text{cancellation}}
$$

where $\text{dest}(i)$ is the last station of train $i$. *(Assumption: delay measured at the destination relative to scheduled origin departure, since these coincide for a service run.)*

---

### 5. Constraints

#### 5.1 Route selection
$$
x_{i,b} + y_{i,b} \le 1 \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\, b\in\mathcal{R}_i \tag{R1}
$$
$$
x_{i,b} + y_{i,b} \ge 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\, b\in\mathcal{R}_i \tag{R2}
$$
A running (non-cancelled) train must use exactly one track on every traversed segment; a cancelled train uses none.

#### 5.2 Blockage / rerouting
Only one travel direction is physically unavailable during $W_b$; that direction cannot use its normal track:
$$
y_{i,b} = 0 \qquad \forall i \text{ with } \text{group}(i)=\rho_b,\ b\in\mathcal{R}_i. \tag{B1}
$$
A train using the **normal** track must either clear the segment before the window opens or enter it after the window closes, controlled by $\mathrm{blk}_{i,b}$:
$$
a_{i,s^{to}_{i,b}} \le W_b^{s} + M\,(1-\mathrm{blk}_{i,b}) + M\,(1-x_{i,b}) \tag{B2}
$$
$$
\mathrm{dep}_{i,s^{from}_{i,b}} \ge W_b^{e} - M\,\mathrm{blk}_{i,b} - M\,(1-x_{i,b}) \tag{B3}
$$
If $x_{i,b}=0$ (rerouted or cancelled), both disjunctive constraints relax.

#### 5.3 Departure / arrival ordering
$$
\mathrm{dep}_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{O}_i \tag{C1}
$$
$$
\mathrm{dep}_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \ge d_s \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{O}_i\setminus\{\text{origin},\text{dest}\} \tag{C2}
$$
$$
\mathrm{dep}_{i,\text{origin}(i)} \ge t^0_{i} \qquad \forall i \tag{C3}
$$

#### 5.4 Cancellation
$$
a_{i,s} \le M\,(1-z_i),\qquad \mathrm{dep}_{i,s} \le M\,(1-z_i) \qquad \forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{O}_i \tag{C4}
$$

#### 5.5 Running-time linking and speed
$$
t_{i,b} = a_{i,s^{to}_{i,b}} - \mathrm{dep}_{i,s^{from}_{i,b}} \qquad \forall i,\ b\in\mathcal{R}_i \tag{T1}
$$
Because $t = L_b/v$ is convex in $v$, valid **linear underestimators** via tangent lines at each breakpoint $v_k\in\mathcal{K}$:
$$
t_{i,b} \ge \frac{L_b\,(2 v_k - v_{i,b})}{v_k^{2}} \qquad \forall i,\ b\in\mathcal{R}_i,\ v_k\in\mathcal{K} \tag{T2}
$$
$$
t_{i,b} \ge \frac{L_b}{v_{\max}} \qquad \forall i,\ b\in\mathcal{R}_i \tag{T3}
$$
$$
v_{\min} \le v_{i,b} \le v_{\max} \qquad \forall i,\ b\in\mathcal{R}_i \tag{T4}
$$

#### 5.6 Energy (piecewise-linear, convex underestimation)
Since $e = L_b\,v^2$ is convex in $v$, tangent-line underestimators at each breakpoint:
$$
e_{i,b} \ge L_b\bigl(2 v_k\, v_{i,b} - v_k^{2}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,\ b\in\mathcal{R}_i,\ v_k\in\mathcal{K} \tag{E1}
$$
$$
e_{i,b} \le M\,(1-z_i) \qquad \forall i,\ b\in\mathcal{R}_i \tag{E2}
$$
Because the objective minimizes $e$, the underestimators are tight in the optimum.

#### 5.7 Same-track indicator
$\mathrm{same}_{i,j,b}=1$ only if both trains select the **same** physical track:
$$
\mathrm{same}_{i,j,b} \ge x_{i,b}+x_{j,b}-1 \tag{S1}
$$
$$
\mathrm{same}_{i,j,b} \ge y_{i,b}+y_{j,b}-1 \tag{S2}
$$
$$
\mathrm{same}_{i,j,b} \le \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(x_{i,b}+x_{j,b}+y_{i,b}+y_{j,b}\bigr) \tag{S3}
$$

#### 5.8 Conflict-free sequencing on shared track
For every pair $\{i,j\}\in\mathcal{P}_b$, with $\text{active}=1-z_i-z_j+z_i z_j$ (linearized as $\ge (1-z_i)+(1-z_j)-1$), require headway separation whenever both trains are running and share the track:
$$
\mathrm{dep}_{j,s^{from}_{j,b}} \ge \mathrm{dep}_{i,s^{from}_{i,b}} + h
 - M(1-\delta_{i,j,b}) - M(1-\mathrm{same}_{i,j,b}) - M(1-\text{active}) \tag{H1}
$$
$$
\mathrm{dep}_{i,s^{from}_{i,b}} \ge \mathrm{dep}_{j,s^{from}_{j,b}} + h
 - M\,\delta_{i,j,b} - M(1-\mathrm{same}_{i,j,b}) - M(1-\text{active}) \tag{H2}
$$
Only one of (H1)–(H2) is tight, forcing a unique order $\delta_{i,j,b}$ and a headway of at least $h$ between conflicting trains — this covers both **same-direction** and **opposite-direction** conflicts that arise from rerouting onto a shared track.

#### 5.9 Domains
$$
x_{i,b},\,y_{i,b},\,z_i,\,\delta_{i,j,b},\,\mathrm{same}_{i,j,b},\,\mathrm{blk}_{i,b}\in\{0,1\},\quad
v_{i,b}\ge 0,\ t_{i,b}\ge 0,\ e_{i,b}\ge 0,\ a_{i,s},\mathrm{dep}_{i,s}\ge 0.
$$

---

### 6. Stated Assumptions

1. **Piecewise-linear approximations** of $L_b/v$ (via tangent-line underestimators) and $L_b v^2$ (via tangent-line approximators) are used to retain MILP structure; because $e$ is minimized in the objective, underestimators are tight at optimum.
2. The **disruption window** $W_b$ and blocked direction $\rho_b$ are exogenous inputs.
3. **Minimum dwell** $d_s$ and **headway** $h$ are fixed and identical across stations / directions (a common simplification).
4. Cancelled trains contribute zero running time and zero energy.
5. The rerouting strategy preserves **unidirectional line capacity** by allowing affected trains to temporarily use the opposite track; this creates bidirectional conflicts, modeled via the same-track indicator and sequencing constraints (S1)–(S3) and (H1)–(H2).
6. Delay is measured at the destination relative to the scheduled origin departure (these coincide for a normal run).
7. Only two tracks exist between adjacent stations (one per direction), so $x_{i,b}+y_{i,b}\le 1$ is exact.

Text:
# A MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

*Model inspired by RECIFE-MILP (Pellegrini et al., 2015), enhanced with speed-profile options and train-/speed-dependent braking distances for ETCS L2 (fixed-block DTG). All assumptions are explicitly marked.*

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $B$ | set of block sections (TDSs) of the network, indexed by $b$ |
| $S \subseteq B$ | subset of blocks that are *switches / station areas*; $\bar{S} = B \setminus S$ are open-line blocks |
| $R$ | set of routes (paths) through the network, indexed by $r$ |
| $R_t \subseteq R$ | set of admissible routes for train $t$ |
| $B_r \subseteq B$ | ordered sequence of blocks belonging to route $r$ |
| $K$ | set of available *speed-profile options* (driving regimes), indexed by $k$ |
| $K_t \subseteq K$ | speed-profile options feasible for train $t$ (given rolling-stock and route characteristics) |
| $E$ | set of *events* (arrival/departure at a timing point), indexed by $e$; $e = (t, b, \text{type})$ |
| $E_t \subseteq E$ | events of train $t$ |
| $A$ | set of *track-segment conflicts* (pairs of trains sharing a block), indexed by $(t, t', b)$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | set of *precedence pairs* on a shared block, indexed by $p = (t, t', b)$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $d_e$ | scheduled (timetabled) time of event $e$ | s |
| $\hat{d}_e$ | actual (delayed) reference time of event $e$ (input perturbation) | s |
| $M$ | large positive constant (big-M) | s |
| $L_b$ | length of block $b$ | m |
| $v_{t,k}$ | nominal speed of train $t$ under profile option $k$ | m/s |
| $a_t$ | maximum service deceleration of train $t$ | m/s² |
| $\tau_t$ | reaction / set-up time of train $t$ before braking | s |
| $\sigma$ | safety margin (absolute buffer distance) | m |
| $\ell_t$ | length of train $t$ | m |
| $h_{t,k}$ | *minimum headway time* of train $t$ under speed profile $k$ (derived from braking distance) | s |
| $r_{t,b,k}$ | running time of train $t$ over block $b$ under profile $k$ | s |
| $w_{t,b}$ | minimum dwell / technical time at block $b$ for train $t$ | s |
| $\delta_{t,b}$ | minimum *blocking time* of block $b$ by train $t$ (occupation + release) | s |
| $\gamma$ | weight converting delay into objective cost (default $\gamma = 1$) | – |
| $c^{ord}_{t,t',b}$ | cost of ordering train $t$ before $t'$ on block $b$ (e.g., extra delay penalty) | s |

**Derived parameter — braking distance (Assumption A1).**  
Under continuous braking-curve supervision, the distance needed for train $t$ travelling at speed $v_{t,k}$ to stop is

$$
D^{\text{brake}}_{t,k} = \frac{v_{t,k}^2}{2 a_t} + v_{t,k}\,\tau_t + \sigma .
$$

**Derived parameter — headway time (Assumption A2).**  
The minimum separation time between two consecutive trains $t$ and $t'$ on the same block under profile $k$ is

$$
h_{t,k} = \frac{D^{\text{brake}}_{t,k} + \ell_t}{v_{t,k}} .
$$

This replaces the fixed number-of-blocks separation of conventional fixed-block signalling.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Routing and speed-profile selection

$$
x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall t \in T,\ r \in R_t
$$
$=1$ if train $t$ uses route $r$.

$$
y_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall t \in T,\ k \in K_t
$$
$=1$ if train $t$ adopts speed-profile option $k$.

### 3.2 Timing variables

$$
t_e \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}, \quad \forall e \in E
$$
actual (rescheduled) time of event $e$.

$$
\Delta_e \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}, \quad \forall e \in E
$$
delay of event $e$ relative to schedule.

### 3.3 Ordering / precedence variables

$$
z_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (t,t',b) \in \mathcal{P}
$$
$=1$ if train $t$ is scheduled **before** train $t'$ on block $b$.

### 3.4 Brake-indication point variable (DTG-specific)

$$
\beta_{t,b} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}, \quad \forall t \in T,\ b \in B
$$
position (distance from block entry) of the brake-indication point of train $t$ relative to the end of authority at block $b$. This variable links the chosen speed profile to the separation constraint.

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total weighted delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \gamma \sum_{e \in E} \Delta_e \;+\; \sum_{(t,t',b)\in\mathcal{P}} c^{ord}_{t,t',b}\, z_{t,t',b}
$$

The second term (Assumption A3) penalises "unnatural" orderings that would require extra operational effort; it can be omitted by setting $c^{ord}=0$.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Route and speed-profile assignment

$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1, \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{1}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in K_t} y_{t,k} = 1, \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{2}
$$

$$
x_{t,r} \le \sum_{k \in K_t} y_{t,k}, \qquad \forall t \in T,\ r \in R_t \tag{3}
$$

*(Assumption A4: exactly one route and one speed profile per train; constraint (3) is redundant but tightens the LP relaxation.)*

### 5.2 Delay definition

$$
\Delta_e \ge t_e - d_e, \qquad \forall e \in E \tag{4}
$$

$$
\Delta_e \ge 0, \qquad \forall e \in E \tag{5}
$$

*(Assumption A5: delay is measured against the timetable, not against the perturbed reference time; early running is not rewarded.)*

### 5.3 Running-time constraints (speed-profile dependent)

For each train $t$, route $r$, and consecutive events $e, e'$ on block $b \in B_r$:

$$
t_{e'} - t_e \;\ge\; \sum_{k \in K_t} r_{t,b,k}\, y_{t,k} \;-\; M\,(1 - x_{t,r}), \qquad \forall t,\ r \in R_t,\ b \in B_r \tag{6}
$$

*(Assumption A6: running time is a convex combination of the profile options; the big-M term deactivates the constraint for non-chosen routes.)*

### 5.4 Dwell / minimum technical time

$$
t_{e'} - t_e \;\ge\; w_{t,b}, \qquad \forall t,\ b \in B,\ (e,e') \text{ consecutive at } b \tag{7}
$$

### 5.5 Block-occupation and separation constraints (DTG core)

For each conflict pair $(t,t',b) \in \mathcal{P}$, let $e_t^{\text{in}}, e_t^{\text{out}}$ denote the entry and exit events of train $t$ on block $b$. The DTG separation constraint is:

$$
t_{t'}^{\text{in}} \;\ge\; t_t^{\text{out}} \;+\; \sum_{k \in K_{t'}} h_{t',k}\, y_{t',k} \;-\; M\,(1 - z_{t,t',b}), \qquad \forall (t,t',b) \in \mathcal{P} \tag{8}
$$

$$
t_{t}^{\text{in}} \;\ge\; t_{t'}^{\text{out}} \;+\; \sum_{k \in K_{t}} h_{t,k}\, y_{t,k} \;-\; M\, z_{t,t',b}, \qquad \forall (t,t',b) \in \mathcal{P} \tag{9}
$$

$$
z_{t,t',b} + z_{t',t,b} = 1, \qquad \forall (t,t',b) \in \mathcal{P} \tag{10}
$$

**Interpretation.** Constraint (8) enforces that if $t$ precedes $t'$ ($z=1$), then $t'$ may enter block $b$ only after $t$ has left it **plus** the speed-dependent headway $h_{t',k}$. This headway encodes the brake-indication point $\beta_{t',b}$ implicitly: the faster the chosen profile, the larger $D^{\text{brake}}$ and hence the larger $h$, which pushes the brake-indication point further upstream — exactly the DTG behaviour. Constraint (9) is the symmetric case. Constraint (10) ensures exactly one ordering.

*(Assumption A7: the headway $h_{t,k}$ is computed offline for each candidate profile and treated as a parameter; this keeps the model linear. The brake-indication variable $\beta_{t,b}$ is then recovered as $\beta_{t,b} = v_{t,k}\,\tau_t + v_{t,k}^2/(2a_t)$ for the chosen $k$, and is therefore not needed as an explicit decision variable — it is reported as an output.)*

### 5.6 Switch / station-area distinction

For blocks $b \in S$ (switches, station areas), a stricter separation applies because the end of authority is set at the TDS boundary and additional interlocking constraints hold:

$$
t_{t'}^{\text{in}} \;\ge\; t_t^{\text{out}} \;+\; \sum_{k \in K_{t'}} h_{t',k}\, y_{t',k} \;+\; \delta_{t,b} \;-\; M\,(1 - z_{t,t',b}), \qquad \forall (t,t',b) \in \mathcal{P},\ b \in S \tag{11}
$$

For open-line blocks $b \in \bar{S}$, constraint (8) applies with $\delta_{t,b}=0$.

*(Assumption A8: switch blocks require an extra blocking/release time $\delta_{t,b}$ due to route locking and flank protection; this is the "distinction between switches and the rest of the track" mentioned in the paper.)*

### 5.7 Route–block consistency

$$
x_{t,r} \le \mathbb{1}[b \in B_r], \qquad \forall t,\ r \in R_t,\ b \in B \tag{12}
$$

*(Assumption A9: a train can only occupy blocks on its chosen route; this is enforced implicitly by restricting events to $B_r$.)*

### 5.8 Variable domains

$$
x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad z_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}
$$

$$
t_e \ge 0, \quad \Delta_e \ge 0, \quad \beta_{t,b} \ge 0
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \gamma \sum_{e \in E} \Delta_e + \sum_{(t,t',b)\in\mathcal{P}} c^{ord}_{t,t',b}\, z_{t,t',b} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& \sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1 && \forall t \\
& \sum_{k \in K_t} y_{t,k} = 1 && \forall t \\
& \Delta_e \ge t_e - d_e && \forall e \\
& t_{e'} - t_e \ge \sum_{k} r_{t,b,k}\, y_{t,k} - M(1-x_{t,r}) && \forall t,r,b \\
& t_{e'} - t_e \ge w_{t,b} && \forall t,b \\
& t_{t'}^{\text{in}} \ge t_t^{\text{out}} + \sum_{k} h_{t',k}\, y_{t',k} - M(1-z_{t,t',b}) && \forall (t,t',b) \\
& t_{t}^{\text{in}} \ge t_{t'}^{\text{out}} + \sum_{k} h_{t,k}\, y_{t,k} - M z_{t,t',b} && \forall (t,t',b) \\
& z_{t,t',b} + z_{t',t,b} = 1 && \forall (t,t',b) \\
& \text{(switch blocks: add } \delta_{t,b} \text{ to RHS of separation)} \\
& x, y, z \in \{0,1\}, \quad t, \Delta, \beta \ge 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Key Modelling Assumptions (Explicitly Marked)

| # | Assumption | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Braking distance $D^{\text{brake}}_{t,k} = v^2/(2a) + v\tau + \sigma$ | Standard kinematic braking model under continuous supervision |
| A2 | Headway $h_{t,k} = (D^{\text{brake}}_{t,k} + \ell_t)/v_{t,k}$ | Converts distance-based separation into time-based headway for MILP linearity |
| A3 | Ordering cost $c^{ord}$ optional | Allows penalising reordering without changing model structure |
| A4 | Exactly one route and one speed profile per train | Simplifies binary assignment; multi-profile per train not needed for CDR |
| A5 | Delay measured against timetable | Standard in CDR literature (RECIFE-MILP) |
| A6 | Running time is convex combination of profile options | Keeps model linear; profile options precomputed |
| A7 | Headway precomputed per profile, treated as parameter | Avoids nonlinearity of $v^2$ in constraints; $\beta$ recovered as output |
| A8 | Switch blocks require extra blocking time $\delta_{t,b}$ | Captures interlocking/route-locking at switches |
| A9 | Events restricted to blocks on chosen route | Enforced implicitly by set definition $B_r$ |
| A10 | No early running rewarded ($\Delta_e \ge 0$) | Standard CDR assumption |
| A11 | Single-direction traffic per block | Blocks are unidirectional in the model; bidirectional would require separate block sets |

---

## 8. Model Size

- **Binary variables:** $|T||R| + |T||K| + |\mathcal{P}|$
- **Continuous variables:** $2|E| + |T||B|$
- **Constraints:** $O(|T||R||B| + |\mathcal{P}|)$

The model is a **mixed-integer linear program** solvable by standard branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP). The DTG-specific enhancement is entirely captured by the speed-dependent headway parameter $h_{t,k}$ in constraints (8)–(9), which replaces the fixed number-of-blocks separation of conventional fixed-block CDR models.
