Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below, we formulate a complete, linear mixed-integer programming (MILP) model inspired by the problem description. The model integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (discrete speed-profile selection) under a partial segment blockage, while ensuring conflict-free bidirectional operations on shared track resources.

All assumptions that are not explicitly stated in the input are marked **[A#]**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{u} \subset \mathcal{T}$ | Up-direction trains |
| $\mathcal{T}^{d} \subset \mathcal{T}$ | Down-direction trains |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations/block sections along the line, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of track segments (links) between consecutive stations, indexed by $l = (s, s+1)$ |
| $\mathcal{L}^{B} \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ | Set of segments affected by the partial blockage (disruption area) |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discrete speed profiles (driving strategies), indexed by $k$ **[A1]** |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of admissible routes on a segment, $\mathcal{R} = \{\text{normal}, \text{opposite}\}$ **[A2]** |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of feasible train plans (path + speed profile combinations) for train $i$ **[A3]** |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $t^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $t^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h$ | Minimum safety headway between two consecutive trains on the same track |
| $d_l$ | Physical length of segment $l$ |
| $r_{i,l,k}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ using speed profile $k$ |
| $e_{i,l,k}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $l$ using speed profile $k$ |
| $v^{\max}_{i,l}$ | Maximum allowable speed of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $a^{\max}_i, b^{\max}_i$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration of train $i$ |
| $[\underline{t}^{B}, \overline{t}^{B}]$ | Disruption time window on blocked segments |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $c^{del}$ | Unit cost of delay (per train per time unit) |
| $c^{can}$ | Cost of cancelling a train |
| $c^{eng}$ | Unit cost of energy consumption |
| $\tau^{turn}$ | Minimum turnaround time at terminal stations |
| $W_s$ | Capacity (number of platform tracks) at station $s$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,s}^{dep}$ | continuous | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,s}^{arr}$ | continuous | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{i,l} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $l$ on the opposite track (rerouting) |
| $z_{i} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\delta_{i,j,l} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $l$ |
| $\gamma_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ occupies station $s$ before train $j$ |

### 3.2 Speed management variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\lambda_{i,l,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $l$ |
| $u_{i,l,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ enters segment $l$ before the disruption window ends (auxiliary) |

### 3.3 Delay variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\Delta_{i,s}^{dep} \ge 0$ | continuous | Departure delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\Delta_{i,s}^{arr} \ge 0$ | continuous | Arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total passenger delay, cancellation cost, and energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = c^{del} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \Delta_{i,s}^{arr} + \Delta_{i,s}^{dep} \right)
\;+\; c^{can} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_i
\;+\; c^{eng} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} e_{i,l,k} \, \lambda_{i,l,k}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay definition

$$
\Delta_{i,s}^{arr} \ge x_{i,s}^{arr} - t^{arr}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
\Delta_{i,s}^{dep} \ge x_{i,s}^{dep} - t^{dep}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### 5.2 Running time consistency (coupling rescheduling and speed management)

For each train $i$ and segment $l = (s, s+1)$:

$$
x_{i,s+1}^{arr} - x_{i,s}^{dep} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} r_{i,l,k} \, \lambda_{i,l,k}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; l \in \mathcal{L}
$$

### 5.3 Speed profile selection (exactly one profile per segment)

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \lambda_{i,l,k} = 1, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; l \in \mathcal{L}
$$

### 5.4 Dwell time constraints

$$
x_{i,s}^{dep} \ge x_{i,s}^{arr} + \underline{dw}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
x_{i,s}^{dep} \le x_{i,s}^{arr} + \overline{dw}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $\underline{dw}_{i,s}$ and $\overline{dw}_{i,s}$ are minimum and maximum dwell times **[A4]**.

### 5.5 Cancellation constraints

If train $i$ is cancelled ($z_i = 1$), all its timing variables are fixed to the schedule and it does not consume track capacity:

$$
x_{i,s}^{arr} \le t^{arr}_{i,s} + M z_i, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
x_{i,s}^{dep} \le t^{dep}_{i,s} + M z_i, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
\lambda_{i,l,k} \le 1 - z_i, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; l \in \mathcal{L},\; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

### 5.6 Partial segment blockage constraints

During the disruption window $[\underline{t}^{B}, \overline{t}^{B}]$, trains may not use the normal track on blocked segments; they must reroute to the opposite track:

$$
y_{i,l} = 1, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; l \in \mathcal{L}^{B} \text{ if } x_{i,s}^{dep} \in [\underline{t}^{B}, \overline{t}^{B}]
$$

This is linearized using the auxiliary variable $u_{i,l,k}$:

$$
x_{i,s}^{dep} \le \underline{t}^{B} + M(1 - u_{i,l,k}), \qquad \forall i, l=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{L}^B, k
$$

$$
x_{i,s}^{dep} \ge \overline{t}^{B} - M u_{i,l,k}, \qquad \forall i, l \in \mathcal{L}^B, k
$$

$$
y_{i,l} \ge 1 - u_{i,l,k} - (1 - \lambda_{i,l,k}) M, \qquad \forall i, l \in \mathcal{L}^B, k
$$

### 5.7 Rerouting exclusivity

A train either uses the normal track or the opposite track on each segment:

$$
y_{i,l} \in \{0,1\}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; l \in \mathcal{L}
$$

### 5.8 Bidirectional conflict-free constraints on shared segments

For any two trains $i, j$ traversing the same segment $l$ in opposite directions (or same direction with rerouting), a minimum headway $h$ must be enforced:

**Same-direction trains on the same track:**

$$
x_{j,s}^{dep} \ge x_{i,s}^{dep} + h - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,l}) - M(y_{i,l} + y_{j,l} - 2), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; l=(s,s+1)
$$

$$
x_{i,s}^{dep} \ge x_{j,s}^{dep} + h - M \delta_{i,j,l} - M(y_{i,l} + y_{j,l} - 2), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; l=(s,s+1)
$$

**Opposite-direction trains sharing the same physical track (one rerouted):**

$$
x_{j,s}^{dep} \ge x_{i,s+1}^{arr} + h - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,l}) - M(2 - y_{i,l} - y_{j,l}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; l=(s,s+1)
$$

$$
x_{i,s}^{dep} \ge x_{j,s+1}^{arr} + h - M \delta_{i,j,l} - M(2 - y_{i,l} - y_{j,l}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; l=(s,s+1)
$$

### 5.9 Station capacity constraints

At most $W_s$ trains may occupy station $s$ simultaneously:

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \mathbb{1}\{x_{i,s}^{arr} \le t \le x_{i,s}^{dep}\} \le W_s, \qquad \forall s \in \mathcal{S},\; t \in \mathcal{T}^{horizon}
$$

This is linearized via the ordering variable $\gamma_{i,j,s}$:

$$
x_{j,s}^{arr} \ge x_{i,s}^{dep} - M(1 - \gamma_{i,j,s}), \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \gamma_{i,j,s} \le W_s - 1, \qquad \forall j \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### 5.10 Turnaround constraints at terminals

For a train $i$ that continues as train $j$ at terminal station $s$:

$$
x_{j,s}^{dep} \ge x_{i,s}^{arr} + \tau^{turn}, \qquad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^{turn}
$$

### 5.11 Speed profile feasibility (acceleration/deceleration limits)

The selected speed profile must respect physical limits:

$$
r_{i,l,k} \ge \frac{d_l}{v^{\max}_{i,l}}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; l \in \mathcal{L},\; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

$$
r_{i,l,k} \ge \frac{d_l}{\bar{v}_{i,l,k}}, \qquad \text{where } \bar{v}_{i,l,k} \text{ respects } a^{\max}_i, b^{\max}_i
$$

### 5.12 Non-negativity and binary constraints

$$
x_{i,s}^{arr}, x_{i,s}^{dep} \ge 0, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
\Delta_{i,s}^{arr}, \Delta_{i,s}^{dep} \ge 0, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

$$
y_{i,l}, z_i, \delta_{i,j,l}, \gamma_{i,j,s}, \lambda_{i,l,k}, u_{i,l,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions

**[A1]** Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set $\mathcal{K}$ of pre-computed driving strategies (e.g., via Pontryagin's maximum principle or dynamic programming), each characterized by a running time $r_{i,l,k}$ and energy consumption $e_{i,l,k}$. This is standard in the literature (Howlett et al. 2022).

**[A2]** Two routes are admissible per segment: the normal track and the opposite track. This reflects the partial blockage scenario where one side of the track is unavailable.

**[A3]** A train plan $\mathcal{P}_i$ is a combination of route choices and speed profiles over all segments. The MILP formulation implicitly enumerates these via $\lambda_{i,l,k}$ and $y_{i,l}$.

**[A4]** Dwell times are bounded by operational and passenger boarding constraints; these bounds are exogenous.

**[A5]** The disruption window $[\underline{t}^{B}, \overline{t}^{B}]$ is known and fixed (deterministic disruption).

**[A6]** Energy consumption is linear in the selected speed profile; nonlinear traction dynamics are pre-encoded in $e_{i,l,k}$.

**[A7]** The objective is a weighted sum; weights $c^{del}, c^{can}, c^{eng}$ are exogenous and reflect operator priorities.

**[A8]** Station capacity $W_s$ is expressed in number of platform tracks; simultaneous occupation is approximated by pairwise ordering.

**[A9]** Turnaround connections $(i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^{turn}$ are pre-specified by the rolling stock circulation plan.

---

## 7. Model Summary

The proposed MILP integrates:

- **Retiming**: via $x_{i,s}^{arr}, x_{i,s}^{dep}$
- **Reordering**: via $\delta_{i,j,l}, \gamma_{i,j,s}$
- **Rerouting**: via $y_{i,l}$
- **Cancellation**: via $z_i$
- **Speed management**: via $\lambda_{i,l,k}$

The coupling constraint (5.2) is the key innovation: it links the timetable (rescheduling) with the speed profile (speed management), ensuring that the rescheduled timetable is executable at the control level. The bidirectional conflict constraints (5.8) ensure conflict-free operation when trains share the opposite track during the disruption window.

This formulation is a complete MILP that can be solved directly (for small instances) or decomposed into an IP model over train interactions and a series of single-train subproblems, as described in the solution framework of the original study.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S$ | Set of stations, $s = 1, \dots, |S|$ (ordered along the line) |
| $\text{Seg}$ | Set of segments $(s, s+1)$ between consecutive stations |
| $T$ | Set of trains, $i, j \in T$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed levels, $k \in K$ |
| $P$ | Set of position discretization points, $p = 0, 1, \dots, P$ |
| $B \subseteq \text{Seg}$ | Set of affected (blocked) segments |

Each train $i$ has direction $d_i \in \{0, 1\}$ (0 = forward, 1 = backward).

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $t^{dep,0}_i$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from origin |
| $t^{arr,0}_i$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at destination |
| $t^{dwell,min}_i$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at intermediate stations |
| $t^{dwell,max}_i$ | Maximum dwell time of train $i$ at intermediate stations |
| $r_{i,s,k}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $(s,s+1)$ at speed level $k$ |
| $e_{i,s,k}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $(s,s+1)$ at speed level $k$ |
| $h_{min}$ | Minimum headway (same direction, same track) |
| $h^{opp}_{min}$ | Minimum headway (opposite directions, shared track) |
| $T_{start}, T_{end}$ | Disruption window boundaries |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $w^{delay}_i$ | Delay penalty weight for train $i$ |
| $w^{energy}$ | Energy cost weight |
| $cap_{seg}$ | Segment capacity (1 per track direction) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Timing Variables
$$a_{i,s} \geq 0 \quad \text{arrival time of train } i \text{ at station } s$$
$$d_{i,s} \geq 0 \quad \text{departure time of train } i \text{ from station } s$$
$$\text{delay}_i \geq 0 \quad \text{delay of train } i \text{ at destination}$$

### Routing Variables
$$y_{i,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{1 if train } i \text{ uses opposite track on segment } (s,s+1)$$

### Ordering Variables
$$z_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{1 if train } i \text{ precedes train } j \text{ on segment } (s,s+1)$$

### Speed Profile Variables
$$x_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{1 if train } i \text{ uses speed level } k \text{ on segment } (s,s+1)$$
$$\text{pos}_{i,s,p} \geq 0 \quad \text{time train } i \text{ reaches position } p \text{ on segment } (s,s+1)$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$\min \quad \sum_{i \in T} w^{delay}_i \cdot \text{delay}_i \;+\; w^{energy} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{(s,s+1) \in \text{Seg}} \sum_{k \in K} e_{i,s,k} \cdot x_{i,s,k}$$

**Interpretation:** Minimize weighted total train delays plus weighted total energy consumption.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (1) Speed-Level Selection

Exactly one speed level per train per segment:

$$\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,s,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in \text{Seg}$$

---

### (2) Running Time Consistency and Dwell Times

Arrival at next station equals departure plus chosen running time:

$$a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in K} r_{i,s,k} \cdot x_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in \text{Seg}$$

Dwell time bounds at intermediate stations:

$$d_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} + t^{dwell,min}_i \qquad \forall i \in T, \; s \in S \setminus \{\text{origin}_i, \text{dest}_i\}$$

$$d_{i,s} \leq a_{i,s} + t^{dwell,max}_i \qquad \forall i \in T, \; s \in S \setminus \{\text{origin}_i, \text{dest}_i\}$$

---

### (3) Origin/Destination Timing

No early departure from origin:

$$d_{i,\text{origin}_i} \geq t^{dep,0}_i \qquad \forall i \in T$$

Delay definition at destination:

$$\text{delay}_i \geq a_{i,\text{dest}_i} - t^{arr,0}_i \qquad \forall i \in T$$

$$\text{delay}_i \geq 0 \qquad \forall i \in T$$

---

### (4) Position-Time Alignment

Boundary conditions:

$$\text{pos}_{i,s,0} = d_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in \text{Seg}$$

$$\text{pos}_{i,s,P} = a_{i,s+1} \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in \text{Seg}$$

Monotonicity:

$$\text{pos}_{i,s,p} \leq \text{pos}_{i,s,p+1} \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in \text{Seg}, \; p = 0,\dots,P-1$$

Linear interpolation (uniform speed within segment):

$$\text{pos}_{i,s,p} = d_{i,s} + \frac{p}{P} \sum_{k \in K} r_{i,s,k} \cdot x_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in \text{Seg}, \; p = 0,\dots,P$$

---

### (5) Rerouting Restrictions

No rerouting on unaffected segments:

$$y_{i,s} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in \text{Seg} \setminus B$$

Rerouted trains must enter after $T_{start}$ and clear before $T_{end}$:

$$d_{i,s} \geq T_{start} - M(1 - y_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in B$$

$$a_{i,s+1} \leq T_{end} + M(1 - y_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i \in T, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in B$$

---

### (6) Conflict-Free Operation on Normal Tracks (Same Direction)

For trains $i, j$ with same direction, both on normal track ($y_{i,s} = y_{j,s} = 0$):

$$d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h_{min} - M(1 - z_{i,j,s}) - M(y_{i,s} + y_{j,s})$$

$$d_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s+1} + h_{min} - M \cdot z_{i,j,s} - M(y_{i,s} + y_{j,s})$$

Ordering consistency:

$$z_{i,j,s} + z_{j,i,s} = 1 \qquad \forall \text{ unordered pairs } \{i,j\}, \; \forall (s,s+1) \in \text{Seg}$$

---

### (7) Conflict-Free Operation on Shared Opposite Track (Bidirectional)

If both trains use opposite track ($y_{i,s} = y_{j,s} = 1$):

$$d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h^{opp}_{min} - M(1 - z_{i,j,s}) - M(2 - y_{i,s} - y_{j,s})$$

$$d_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s+1} + h^{opp}_{min} - M \cdot z_{i,j,s} - M(2 - y_{i,s} - y_{j,s})$$

---

### (8) Mixed-Track Conflict (One Rerouted, One Normal, Opposite Directions)

If $y_{i,s} = 1$, $y_{j,s} = 0$, and trains are in opposite directions:

$$d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h^{opp}_{min} - M(1 - z_{i,j,s}) - M(1 - y_{i,s} + y_{j,s})$$

$$d_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s+1} + h^{opp}_{min} - M \cdot z_{i,j,s} - M(1 - y_{i,s} + y_{j,s})$$

---

### (9) Domain Constraints

$$a_{i,s}, \; d_{i,s}, \; \text{pos}_{i,s,p}, \; \text{delay}_i \geq 0 \qquad \forall i, s, p$$

$$x_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall i, s, k$$

$$y_{i,s} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall i, s$$

$$z_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall i, j, s$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Component | Count |
|-----------|-------|
| Continuous variables | $2|T||S| + |T||\text{Seg}|(P+1) + |T|$ |
| Binary variables | $|T||\text{Seg}||K| + |T||\text{Seg}| + |T|^2|\text{Seg}|$ |
| Constraints | Speed selection, running time, dwell, origin/dest, position alignment, rerouting, headway (3 types), domains |

---

## 7. Assumptions (Explicitly Marked)

- **A1:** Speed profiles discretized into finite candidate running times with associated energy per segment.
- **A2:** Uniform speed within each segment for position-time alignment.
- **A3:** Rerouting permitted only on affected segment(s) and only within $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$.
- **A4:** At most one train on the shared opposite track at a time (enforced via headway constraints).
- **A5:** All trains run the full line; no cancellations modeled (can be extended with a "cancel" binary).
- **A6:** Dwell times bounded by min/max at intermediate stations.
- **A7:** Big-M linearization used for all conditional headway constraints.

---

## 8. Model Interpretation

This MILP jointly optimizes **four decision dimensions**:

1. **Retiming** — variables $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ adjust arrival/departure times.
2. **Reordering** — variables $z_{i,j,s}$ sequence trains on shared segments.
3. **Rerouting** — variables $y_{i,s}$ select normal vs. opposite track through the disruption.
4. **Speed management** — variables $x_{i,s,k}$ choose discrete speed levels per segment.

The **objective** balances service quality (weighted delays) against operational cost (energy). The **headway constraints (6)–(8)** ensure conflict-free operation across all track-sharing scenarios, while **position-time alignment (4)** guarantees that the chosen speed profile is physically executable.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model for Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1, 2, \ldots, S\}$ | Set of stations along the urban rail transit line, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{T} = \{1, 2, \ldots, T\}$ | Set of trains (services) scheduled in the prediction horizon, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1, 2, \ldots, K\}$ | Set of time intervals partitioning the prediction horizon, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{U}$ | Set of available train units (rolling stock), indexed by $u$ |
| $\mathcal{C} = \{0, 1, 2, \ldots, C^{\max}\}$ | Set of possible train compositions (number of coupled units), indexed by $c$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{1, 2, \ldots, D\}$ | Set of depots/terminals, indexed by $d$ |

**Assumption A1:** The prediction horizon is divided into $K$ equal-length time intervals of length $\Delta t$ (e.g., 5 minutes each), following Liu et al. (2023a).

**Assumption A2:** The line is a single bidirectional urban rail transit line with stations $1$ and $S$ serving as terminals.

---

## 2. Parameters

### 2.1 Infrastructure and Operational Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $L_s$ | Distance between station $s$ and $s+1$ | km |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains | min |
| $h^{\max}$ | Maximum headway between consecutive trains | min |
| $d_s^{\min}$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $d_s^{\max}$ | Maximum dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $r_s^{\min}$ | Minimum running time from station $s$ to $s+1$ | min |
| $r_s^{\max}$ | Maximum running time from station $s$ to $s+1$ | min |
| $Q^{\text{unit}}$ | Capacity of a single train unit | passengers |
| $C^{\max}$ | Maximum number of units per train | units |
| $C^{\min}$ | Minimum number of units per train | units |
| $\tau^{\text{couple}}$ | Time required for coupling/uncoupling operations | min |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) | — |

### 2.2 Demand Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $\lambda_{s,k}$ | Passenger arrival rate at station $s$ during interval $k$ | passengers/min |
| $\beta_{s}$ | Proportion of passengers alighting at station $s$ | — |
| $\rho_{s,k}$ | Sectional passenger demand between station $s$ and $s+1$ during interval $k$ | passengers |

**Assumption A3:** Passenger arrival rates $\lambda_{s,k}$ are piecewise constant over each time interval $k$, as in Liu et al. (2023a).

**Assumption A4:** The origin-destination (OD) matrix is approximated by alighting proportions $\beta_s$ and arrival rates $\lambda_{s,k}$.

### 2.3 Reference Timetable Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $\hat{a}_{i,s}$ | Nominal (reference) arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\hat{d}_{i,s}$ | Nominal (reference) departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ | min |
| $\hat{c}_i$ | Nominal composition (number of units) of train $i$ | units |

### 2.4 Cost Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $\alpha^{\text{wait}}$ | Weight for total passenger waiting time | — |
| $\alpha^{\text{dev}}$ | Weight for timetable deviation | — |
| $\alpha^{\text{comp}}$ | Weight for train composition cost (operational cost) | — |
| $\alpha^{\text{circ}}$ | Weight for rolling stock circulation cost | — |
| $c^{\text{unit}}$ | Cost per unit per time step of operation | \$/unit/min |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Continuous Variables

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ |
| $w_{s,k}$ | Number of passengers waiting at station $s$ during interval $k$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ |
| $b_{i,s}$ | Number of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ |
| $l_{i,s}$ | Passenger load on train $i$ when departing station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ |
| $\Delta a_{i,s}$ | Deviation of arrival time from nominal | $\mathbb{R}$ |
| $\Delta d_{i,s}$ | Deviation of departure time from nominal | $\mathbb{R}$ |

### 3.2 Integer Variables

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| $c_i$ | Composition (number of units) of train $i$ | $\{C^{\min}, \ldots, C^{\max}\}$ |
| $x_{i,j}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ immediately precedes train $j$ in the schedule | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $y_{i,u}$ | Binary: 1 if unit $u$ is assigned to train $i$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $z_{i,s}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$ | $\{0,1\}$ |

**Assumption A5:** All trains serve all stations in the base model ($z_{i,s} = 1$ for all $i, s$), but the variable is retained for potential stop-skipping extensions.

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective is to minimize a weighted sum of passenger waiting time, timetable deviation, train composition cost, and rolling stock circulation cost:

$$
\min \quad Z = \alpha^{\text{wait}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} w_{s,k} \cdot \Delta t 
+ \alpha^{\text{dev}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( |\Delta a_{i,s}| + |\Delta d_{i,s}| \right)
+ \alpha^{\text{comp}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} c_i \cdot c^{\text{unit}}
+ \alpha^{\text{circ}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{u \in \mathcal{U}} y_{i,u}
\tag{1}
$$

**Linearization of absolute values:**

Introduce auxiliary variables $\Delta a_{i,s}^+, \Delta a_{i,s}^-, \Delta d_{i,s}^+, \Delta d_{i,s}^- \geq 0$:

$$
\Delta a_{i,s} = \Delta a_{i,s}^+ - \Delta a_{i,s}^-, \quad |\Delta a_{i,s}| = \Delta a_{i,s}^+ + \Delta a_{i,s}^-
\tag{2}
$$

$$
\Delta d_{i,s} = \Delta d_{i,s}^+ - \Delta d_{i,s}^-, \quad |\Delta d_{i,s}| = \Delta d_{i,s}^+ + \Delta d_{i,s}^-
\tag{3}
$$

The linearized objective becomes:

$$
\min \quad Z = \alpha^{\text{wait}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} w_{s,k} \cdot \Delta t 
+ \alpha^{\text{dev}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \Delta a_{i,s}^+ + \Delta a_{i,s}^- + \Delta d_{i,s}^+ + \Delta d_{i,s}^- \right)
+ \alpha^{\text{comp}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} c_i \cdot c^{\text{unit}}
+ \alpha^{\text{circ}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{u \in \mathcal{U}} y_{i,u}
\tag{4}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Constraints

#### 5.1.1 Arrival and Departure Time Relationships

For each train $i \in \mathcal{T}$ and station $s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{S\}$:

$$
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + r_{i,s}
\tag{5}
$$

where $r_{i,s}$ is the running time from station $s$ to $s+1$.

**Assumption A6:** Running times are fixed at nominal values $r_{i,s} = \hat{a}_{i,s+1} - \hat{d}_{i,s}$ (speed level optimization is not considered in this base model).

#### 5.1.2 Dwell Time Constraints

For each train $i \in \mathcal{T}$ and station $s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{1, S\}$:

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \geq d_s^{\min}
\tag{6}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \leq d_s^{\max}
\tag{7}
$$

#### 5.1.3 Headway Constraints

For consecutive trains $i$ and $j$ at station $s$:

$$
d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \geq h^{\min} - M(1 - x_{i,j}), \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, i \neq j, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{8}
$$

$$
d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \leq h^{\max} + M(1 - x_{i,j}), \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, i \neq j, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{9}
$$

#### 5.1.4 Train Ordering Constraints

Each train has at most one immediate successor and one immediate predecessor:

$$
\sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}, j \neq i} x_{i,j} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{10}
$$

$$
\sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}, j \neq i} x_{j,i} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{11}
$$

**Assumption A7:** The train order is preserved from the nominal schedule (no overtaking), i.e., $x_{i,j}$ is fixed based on the nominal train sequence. This reduces the number of binary variables.

#### 5.1.5 Timetable Deviation Constraints

$$
\Delta a_{i,s} = a_{i,s} - \hat{a}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{12}
$$

$$
\Delta d_{i,s} = d_{i,s} - \hat{d}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{13}
$$

### 5.2 Passenger Flow Constraints

#### 5.2.1 Waiting Passenger Dynamics

For each station $s \in \mathcal{S}$ and time interval $k \in \mathcal{K}$:

$$
w_{s,k} = w_{s,k-1} + \lambda_{s,k} \cdot \Delta t - \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} b_{i,s,k}
\tag{14}
$$

where $b_{i,s,k}$ is the number of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ during interval $k$.

**Assumption A8:** The boarding variable $b_{i,s}$ aggregates boarding over all intervals when train $i$ departs station $s$. We define:

$$
b_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} b_{i,s,k}
\tag{15}
$$

#### 5.2.2 Boarding Constraints

The number of boarding passengers cannot exceed the waiting passengers:

$$
b_{i,s} \leq w_{s,k(i,s)}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{16}
$$

where $k(i,s)$ is the time interval during which train $i$ departs station $s$.

**Linearization:** Introduce binary variable $\delta_{i,s,k} = 1$ if train $i$ departs station $s$ during interval $k$:

$$
d_{i,s} \geq (k-1) \cdot \Delta t - M(1 - \delta_{i,s,k})
\tag{17}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \leq k \cdot \Delta t + M(1 - \delta_{i,s,k})
\tag{18}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \delta_{i,s,k} = 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{19}
$$

Then:

$$
b_{i,s} \leq \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} w_{s,k} \cdot \delta_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{20}
$$

**Linearization of (20):** Introduce $v_{i,s,k} = w_{s,k} \cdot \delta_{i,s,k}$:

$$
v_{i,s,k} \leq w_{s,k}, \quad v_{i,s,k} \leq M \cdot \delta_{i,s,k}, \quad v_{i,s,k} \geq w_{s,k} - M(1 - \delta_{i,s,k})
\tag{21}
$$

Then:

$$
b_{i,s} \leq \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{22}
$$

#### 5.2.3 Alighting Constraints

The number of passengers alighting from train $i$ at station $s$:

$$
g_{i,s} = \beta_s \cdot l_{i,s-1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{1\}
\tag{23}
$$

#### 5.2.4 Passenger Load Dynamics

For each train $i \in \mathcal{T}$ and station $s \in \mathcal{S}$:

$$
l_{i,s} = l_{i,s-1} - g_{i,s} + b_{i,s}, \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{1\}
\tag{24}
$$

$$
l_{i,1} = b_{i,1}
\tag{25}
$$

#### 5.2.5 Train Capacity Constraints

The passenger load cannot exceed the train capacity:

$$
l_{i,s} \leq c_i \cdot Q^{\text{unit}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{26}
$$

### 5.3 Flexible Train Composition Constraints

#### 5.3.1 Composition Bounds

$$
C^{\min} \leq c_i \leq C^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{27}
$$

#### 5.3.2 Composition-Unit Assignment Consistency

$$
c_i = \sum_{u \in \mathcal{U}} y_{i,u}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{28}
$$

#### 5.3.3 Unit Assignment Constraints

Each unit can be assigned to at most one train at a time:

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} y_{i,u} \leq 1, \quad \forall u \in \mathcal{U}
\tag{29}
$$

**Assumption A9:** The number of available units satisfies $\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} C^{\min} \leq |\mathcal{U}| \leq \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} C^{\max}$.

#### 5.3.4 Coupling/Uncoupling Time Constraints

If the composition of train $i$ changes between consecutive services, additional time is required:

$$
d_{i+1,1} - a_{i,S} \geq \tau^{\text{couple}} \cdot |c_{i+1} - c_i| - M(1 - x_{i,i+1})
\tag{30}
$$

**Linearization:** Introduce $\Delta c_i^+, \Delta c_i^- \geq 0$:

$$
c_{i+1} - c_i = \Delta c_i^+ - \Delta c_i^-, \quad |c_{i+1} - c_i| = \Delta c_i^+ + \Delta c_i^-
\tag{31}
$$

$$
d_{i+1,1} - a_{i,S} \geq \tau^{\text{couple}} \cdot (\Delta c_i^+ + \Delta c_i^-) - M(1 - x_{i,i+1})
\tag{32}
$$

### 5.4 Rolling Stock Circulation Constraints

#### 5.4.1 Circulation Balance

Each train $i$ must be assigned units that are available at its departure terminal:

$$
\sum_{u \in \mathcal{U}} y_{i,u} = c_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{33}
$$

#### 5.4.2 Unit Continuity

If unit $u$ is assigned to train $i$ and train $i$ is followed by train $j$, then unit $u$ must be available for train $j$ (either continues or is released):

$$
y_{i,u} + y_{j,u} \leq 1 + x_{i,j}, \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, i \neq j, \forall u \in \mathcal{U}
\tag{34}
$$

**Assumption A10:** Units can be reallocated between trains at terminals if sufficient time is available (captured by constraint (32)).

#### 5.4.3 Depot Capacity

The number of units at each depot cannot exceed capacity:

$$
\sum_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}: \text{train } i \text{ starts at depot } d} y_{i,u} \leq U_d^{\max}, \quad \forall d \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{35}
$$

### 5.5 Operational Constraints

#### 5.5.1 Non-negativity and Domain Constraints

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{36}
$$

$$
w_{s,k}, b_{i,s}, l_{i,s}, g_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}, \forall k \in \mathcal{K}
\tag{37}
$$

$$
c_i \in \{C^{\min}, \ldots, C^{\max}\}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{38}
$$

$$
x_{i,j}, y_{i,u}, z_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i, j \in \mathcal{T}, \forall u \in \mathcal{U}, \forall s \in \mathcal{S}, \forall k \in \mathcal{K}
\tag{39}
$$

#### 5.5.2 Initial Conditions

$$
w_{s,0} = w_s^{\text{init}}, \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{40}
$$

$$
l_{i,0} = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{41}
$$

---

## 6. Complete MILP Formulation Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \alpha^{\text{wait}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} w_{s,k} \cdot \Delta t 
+ \alpha^{\text{dev}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \Delta a_{i,s}^+ + \Delta a_{i,s}^- + \Delta d_{i,s}^+ + \Delta d_{i,s}^- \right) \\
& \quad + \alpha^{\text{comp}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} c_i \cdot c^{\text{unit}}
+ \alpha^{\text{circ}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{u \in \mathcal{U}} y_{i,u}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

**Subject to:**

- Timetable constraints: (5)–(13)
- Passenger flow constraints: (14)–(26)
- Train composition constraints: (27)–(32)
- Rolling stock circulation constraints: (33)–(35)
- Operational constraints: (36)–(41)

---

## 7. Model Assumptions Summary

| Assumption | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| A1 | Prediction horizon divided into $K$ equal intervals of length $\Delta t$ |
| A2 | Single bidirectional line with terminals at stations 1 and $S$ |
| A3 | Passenger arrival rates are piecewise constant over intervals |
| A4 | OD matrix approximated by alighting proportions and arrival rates |
| A5 | All trains serve all stations (no stop-skipping in base model) |
| A6 | Running times fixed at nominal values |
| A7 | Train order preserved (no overtaking) |
| A8 | Boarding aggregated over intervals when train departs |
| A9 | Sufficient units available for minimum compositions |
| A10 | Units can be reallocated at terminals with sufficient time |

---

## 8. Model Characteristics

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Problem type | Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) |
| Continuous variables | $O(|\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{S}| \cdot |\mathcal{K}|)$ |
| Binary variables | $O(|\mathcal{T}|^2 + |\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{U}| + |\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}| \cdot |\mathcal{K}|)$ |
| Integer variables | $O(|\mathcal{T}|)$ |
| Constraints | $O(|\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{S}| \cdot |\mathcal{K}| + |\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{U}|)$ |

---

## 9. MPC Integration

For real-time implementation, the MILP is solved at each MPC step $\tau$:

1. **State update:** Update $w_{s,0}$, train positions, and unit locations from real-time measurements.
2. **Prediction horizon:** Solve the MILP over $[\tau, \tau + T_p]$ where $T_p$ is the prediction horizon.
3. **Control horizon:** Apply decisions for $[\tau, \tau + T_c]$ where $T_c \leq T_p$.
4. **Receding horizon:** Shift the horizon and repeat.

**Learning-based acceleration (from the paper):**

- Use LSTM networks to predict integer variables $(c_i, y_{i,u}, x_{i,j})$ based on historical data and current state.
- Fix these integer variables and solve the resulting LP for continuous variables $(a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{s,k}, b_{i,s}, l_{i,s})$.
- This reduces online computational burden while maintaining feasibility through the LP.

---

## 10. Presolve Techniques (from the paper)

1. **Headway-based pruning:** Eliminate $x_{i,j}$ variables for train pairs that cannot be consecutive due to headway constraints.
2. **Capacity-based pruning:** Fix $c_i = C^{\min}$ for off-peak trains where demand is low.
3. **Circulation-based pruning:** Eliminate $y_{i,u}$ assignments that violate depot capacity or continuity.
4. **Demand-based pruning:** Fix $c_i$ based on predicted passenger demand thresholds.

---

This complete MILP formulation captures the essential elements of passenger-oriented train rescheduling with flexible train composition and rolling stock circulation, suitable for integration with MPC and learning-based solution approaches as described in the paper.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Based on the generating code, here is the complete linear model described in mathematical form.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $N$ | Set of stations (nodes), indexed by $n, m$ |
| $E$ | Set of track segments (edges), indexed by $e$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time intervals, indexed by $k$ |
| $R$ | Set of routes (original + rerouted), indexed by $r$ |
| $B$ | Set of potentially blocked segments, indexed by $b$ |
| $W$ | Set of disruption time windows, indexed by $w$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions (forward/backward), indexed by $d$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ (km) |
| $V^{\max}_e,\ V^{\min}_e$ | Max/min allowed speed on segment $e$ (km/h) |
| $a^{\max},\ b^{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration (km/h²) |
| $\text{dwell}^{\min}_n,\ \text{dwell}^{\max}_n$ | Min/max dwell time at station $n$ (min) |
| $h$ | Minimum headway between trains (min) |
| $\text{arr}^{\text{sch}}_{i,n},\ \text{dep}^{\text{sch}}_{i,n}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure (min) |
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization step (min) |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $c^{\text{delay}},\ c^{\text{energy}},\ c^{\text{cancel}}$ | Cost coefficients (delay, energy, cancellation) |
| $\text{mass}_i$ | Mass of train $i$ (tons) |
| $\eta$ | Energy efficiency factor |
| $v^{\text{init}}$ | Initial speed |
| $\text{blk}_{b,w}$ | Binary: 1 if segment $b$ blocked during window $w$ |
| $\text{route}_{r,e}$ | Binary: 1 if route $r$ uses segment $e$ |
| $\text{from}(e),\ \text{to}(e)$ | Origin / destination station of segment $e$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (non-negative):**
- $\text{arr}_{i,n}$ — actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $n$
- $\text{dep}_{i,n}$ — actual departure time of train $i$ from station $n$
- $v_{i,e,k}$ — speed of train $i$ on segment $e$ at time $k$
- $p_{i,e,k}$ — position of train $i$ on segment $e$ at time $k$
- $\Delta v^{+}_{i,e,k},\ \Delta v^{-}_{i,e,k}$ — positive/negative speed change
- $e_i$ — energy consumption of train $i$ (kWh)
- $\text{delay}_i$ — total delay of train $i$ (min)
- $\text{delay}^{\text{arr}+}_{i,n},\ \text{delay}^{\text{dep}+}_{i,n}$ — delay linearization auxiliaries

**Binary:**
- $u_{i,e,k}$ — 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $e$ at time $k$
- $x_{i,j,e}$ — 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$
- $y_{i,r}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ (rerouting decision)
- $z_{i,n}$ — 1 if train $i$ stops at station $n$
- $\text{cancel}_i$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total cost (delay + energy + cancellation):

$$
\min\ Z = c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in T} \text{delay}_i \;+\; c^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in T} e_i \;+\; c^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in T} \text{cancel}_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (1) Arrival–Departure / Dwell Time Relationship
$$
\text{dep}_{i,n} \ge \text{arr}_{i,n} + \text{dwell}^{\min}_n \cdot z_{i,n} \qquad \forall i,n
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,n} \le \text{arr}_{i,n} + \text{dwell}^{\max}_n \cdot z_{i,n} + M(1 - z_{i,n}) \qquad \forall i,n
$$

### (2) Running Time Bounds (linking timetable to speed)
$$
\text{arr}_{i,\text{to}(e)} - \text{dep}_{i,\text{from}(e)} \ge \frac{L_e}{V^{\max}_e}\cdot 60 \qquad \forall i,e
$$
$$
\text{arr}_{i,\text{to}(e)} - \text{dep}_{i,\text{from}(e)} \le \frac{L_e}{V^{\min}_e}\cdot 60 + M\Big(1 - \sum_{r} y_{i,r}\,\text{route}_{r,e}\Big) \qquad \forall i,e
$$

### (3) Kinematic Dynamics (Euler integration)
$$
p_{i,e,k+1} = p_{i,e,k} + v_{i,e,k}\,\frac{\Delta t}{60} \qquad \forall i,e,\ k < |K|
$$
$$
v_{i,e,k+1} = v_{i,e,k} + \Delta v^{+}_{i,e,k} - \Delta v^{-}_{i,e,k} \qquad \forall i,e,\ k < |K|
$$
$$
0 \le \Delta v^{+}_{i,e,k} \le a^{\max}\,\Delta t, \qquad 0 \le \Delta v^{-}_{i,e,k} \le b^{\max}\,\Delta t
$$

### (4) Speed Limits
$$
V^{\min}_e\, u_{i,e,k} \le v_{i,e,k} \le V^{\max}_e\, u_{i,e,k} \qquad \forall i,e,k
$$

### (5) Conflict Resolution — Headway and Ordering
$$
\text{arr}_{j,\text{to}(e)} - \text{arr}_{i,\text{to}(e)} \ge h - M(1 - x_{i,j,e}) \qquad \forall i\neq j,\ e
$$
$$
\text{arr}_{i,\text{to}(e)} - \text{arr}_{j,\text{to}(e)} \ge h - M\, x_{i,j,e} \qquad \forall i\neq j,\ e
$$

### (6) Disruption — Blocked Segments Cannot Be Occupied
$$
u_{i,e,k} \le 1 - \text{blk}_{b,w} \qquad \forall i,\ e = b,\ k \in w,\ b \in B,\ w \in W
$$

### (7) Rerouting Constraints
$$
\sum_{r \in R} y_{i,r} = 1 \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
y_{i,r} = 0 \qquad \forall i,r,b,w:\ \text{route}_{r,b}=1 \ \wedge\ \text{blk}_{b,w}=1
$$

### (8) Bidirectional Conflict Resolution
$$
x_{i,j,e} + x_{j,i,e} = 1 \qquad \forall i \neq j,\ e
$$

### (9) Energy Consumption (linearized)
$$
e_i = \sum_{e \in E}\sum_{k \in K} \text{mass}_i\,(\Delta v^{+}_{i,e,k} + \Delta v^{-}_{i,e,k})\, v_{i,e,k}\,\frac{\Delta t}{60\,\eta} \qquad \forall i
$$

### (10) Delay Calculation
$$
\text{delay}^{\text{arr}+}_{i,n} \ge \text{arr}_{i,n} - \text{arr}^{\text{sch}}_{i,n} \qquad \forall i,n
$$
$$
\text{delay}^{\text{dep}+}_{i,n} \ge \text{dep}_{i,n} - \text{dep}^{\text{sch}}_{i,n} \qquad \forall i,n
$$
$$
\text{delay}_i = \sum_{n}\text{delay}^{\text{arr}+}_{i,n} + \sum_{n}\text{delay}^{\text{dep}+}_{i,n} \qquad \forall i
$$

### (11) Position Continuity and Bounds
$$
0 \le p_{i,e,k} \le L_e\, u_{i,e,k} \qquad \forall i,e,k
$$

### (12) Initial and Final Conditions
$$
p_{i,e,k_0} = 0, \qquad v_{i,e,k_0} = v^{\text{init}} \qquad \forall i,e
$$
$$
p_{i,e,k_{\text{last}}} \le L_e \qquad \forall i,e
$$

### (13) Cancellation Constraints
$$
z_{i,n} \le 1 - \text{cancel}_i \qquad \forall i,n
$$
$$
|\text{arr}_{i,n} - \text{dep}_{i,n}| \le M\,\text{cancel}_i \qquad \forall i,n
$$

### (14) Coupling Speed Profile with Timetable (Occupancy Time)
$$
\text{arr}_{i,\text{to}(e)} - \text{dep}_{i,\text{from}(e)} = \Big(\sum_{k \in K} u_{i,e,k}\Big)\,\Delta t \qquad \forall i,e
$$

### (15) Variable Domains
$$
\text{arr}_{i,n},\ \text{dep}_{i,n},\ v_{i,e,k},\ p_{i,e,k},\ \Delta v^{\pm}_{i,e,k},\ e_i,\ \text{delay}_i,\ \text{delay}^{\text{arr}+}_{i,n},\ \text{delay}^{\text{dep}+}_{i,n} \ge 0
$$
$$
u_{i,e,k},\ x_{i,j,e},\ y_{i,r},\ z_{i,n},\ \text{cancel}_i \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions

- **Single-track bidirectional operation** during disruption: affected trains divert to the opposite track, sharing resources with opposing-direction trains.
- **Discrete time–space representation**: piecewise-constant speed within each time interval; Euler integration for kinematics.
- **Homogeneous train dynamics** within a class (mass, acceleration limits).
- **Disruption** affects specific segments during specific time windows (partial segment blockage).
- **Energy** includes partial regenerative recovery via efficiency factor $\eta$.
- **Dwell times** are flexible within bounds; stopping is optional via $z_{i,n}$.
- **No overtaking** within a segment (enforced by ordering variables $x_{i,j,e}$).
- **Big-M** must be tuned to the horizon (recommended $M \approx 2|K|\Delta t$) to keep the LP relaxation tight.
- **Bilinear energy term** $\Delta v \cdot v$ is written for clarity; a strict MILP requires discretizing $v$ into speed bins with SOS2 or McCormick envelopes.

The model simultaneously optimizes **train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles**, yielding a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles under partial segment blockage disruptions.

Based on the code-generated model, here is the complete MILP formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages.

---

# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

## 1. Motivation and Assumptions

A single high-speed line with bidirectional track is considered, where a partial segment blockage (disruption) blocks one side of the track within a known time window. Trains may reroute onto the opposite track during the blockage, generating bidirectional conflicts. The two sub-problems (rescheduling and speed management) are integrated so that the rescheduled timetable and the executable speed profiles are consistent.

**Assumptions (marked as such):**
- *[Assumption]* Trains follow a fixed station sequence; only timing, ordering, and (local) rerouting are decisions; no full network path re-selection.
- *[Assumption]* Speed is discretized on a per-arc, per-time-step grid; position is tracked continuously within arcs.
- *[Assumption]* Acceleration/deceleration are piecewise constant over each time step; a discretized traction power surrogate is used for energy.
- *[Assumption]* At most one train may occupy the opposite (shared) track of an arc during the blockage.
- *[Assumption]* Delays are measured only at the destination relative to a scheduled arrival time.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains (index $t$) |
| $N$ | Set of nodes (stations + section boundaries, index $i$) |
| $A \subseteq N \times N$ | Set of directed track arcs $(i,j)$ |
| $K$ | Ordered set of discrete time steps (index $k$) |
| $K^{pairs}$ | Consecutive time-step pairs $(k, k')$ with $k'=k+1$ |
| $B \subseteq A$ | Set of blocked arcs |
| $I \subseteq N$ | Set of station nodes |
| $TP$ | Ordered train pairs, $TP = \{(t_1,t_2) \in T\times T : t_1 \ne t_2\}$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_{ij}$ | Length of arc $(i,j)$ [km] |
| $V^{\max}, V^{\min}$ | Maximum/minimum speed [km/h] |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Max acceleration/deceleration [m/s²] |
| $\Delta t$ | Time-step length [s] |
| $\text{orig}_t,\ \text{dest}_t$ | Origin/destination node of train $t$ |
| $\tau_{ij}$ | Minimum running time on arc $(i,j)$ [s] |
| $d^{\text{dwell}}_i$ | Minimum dwell time at station $i$ [s] |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains [s] |
| $t^{\text{block}}_s, t^{\text{block}}_e$ | Start/end of disruption window [s] |
| $e^{\text{acc}}, e^{\text{cru}}, e^{\text{bra}}$ | Energy coefficients (accelerating / cruising / braking) |
| $w_d, w_e, w_c$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant |

Auxiliary: $T^{\text{dep}}_t$ earliest departure, $T^{\text{arr}}_t$ latest arrival, $S^{\text{arr}}_t$ scheduled arrival (for delay).

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Routing / structure**
$$x_{ijt} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{— train } t \text{ uses arc } (i,j)$$
$$r_{ijt} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{— train } t \text{ reroutes onto the opposite track of arc } (i,j)$$
$$\text{cancel}_t \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{— train } t \text{ is cancelled}$$

**Timing**
$$a_{it} \ge 0 \quad\text{— arrival time of } t \text{ at node } i$$
$$d_{it} \ge 0 \quad\text{— departure time of } t \text{ from node } i$$
$$\tau^{\text{arc}}_{ijt} \ge 0 \quad\text{— actual running time on arc } (i,j)$$
$$\text{delay}_t \ge 0 \quad\text{— delay at destination}$$

**Sequencing / safety**
$$\text{ord}_{ijt_1t_2} \in \{0,1\} \quad\text{— } t_1 \text{ precedes } t_2 \text{ on arc } (i,j)$$

**Speed management**
$$v_{ijkt} \ge 0 \quad\text{— speed at time step } k$$
$$s_{ijkt} \ge 0 \quad\text{— position along arc at time step } k$$
$$\text{acc}_{ijkt} \in \{0,1\} \quad\text{— accelerating indicator}$$
$$\text{brk}_{ijkt} \in \{0,1\} \quad\text{— braking indicator}$$
$$p_{ijkt} \ge 0 \quad\text{— traction power}$$
$$E_t \ge 0 \quad\text{— total energy consumed by train } t$$

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, total energy, and cancellations:

$$\min \; Z = w_d \sum_{t\in T} \text{delay}_t \;+\; w_e \sum_{t\in T} E_t \;+\; w_c \sum_{t\in T} \text{cancel}_t$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Network flow conservation

For every node $i$ and train $t$:

$$\sum_{(i,j)\in A} x_{ijt} - \sum_{(h,i)\in A} x_{hit} = b_{it}, \qquad b_{it} = \begin{cases} 1 - \text{cancel}_t & i = \text{orig}_t \\ -1 + \text{cancel}_t & i = \text{dest}_t \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

### 6.2 Origin/destination time windows

$$d_{\text{orig}_t,\,t} \ge T^{\text{dep}}_t \qquad \forall t$$

$$a_{\text{dest}_t,\,t} \le T^{\text{arr}}_t + M \cdot \text{cancel}_t \qquad \forall t$$

### 6.3 Running-time coupling and bounds

$$a_{jt} \ge d_{it} + \tau^{\text{arc}}_{ijt} - M(1 - x_{ijt}) \qquad \forall (i,j), t$$

$$\tau^{\text{arc}}_{ijt} \ge \tau_{ij} \qquad \forall (i,j), t$$

$$\tau^{\text{arc}}_{ijt} \ge \tau_{ij}\, x_{ijt} \qquad \forall (i,j), t$$

$$\tau^{\text{arc}}_{ijt} \le T^{\text{arr}}_t + M(1 - x_{ijt}) \qquad \forall (i,j), t$$

### 6.4 Dwell time at stations

For $i\in I$, $i \ne \text{orig}_t, \text{dest}_t$:

$$d_{it} \ge a_{it} + d^{\text{dwell}}_i \sum_{(h,i)\in A} x_{hit} \qquad \forall i, t$$

### 6.5 Same-direction headway (via ordering)

For all $(i,j)\in A$ and $(t_1,t_2)\in TP$:

$$d_{i,t_2} \ge d_{i,t_1} + h^{\min} - M(2 - x_{ijt_1} - x_{ijt_2}) - M(1 - \text{ord}_{ijt_1t_2})$$

$$d_{i,t_1} \ge d_{i,t_2} + h^{\min} - M(2 - x_{ijt_1} - x_{ijt_2}) - M(1 - \text{ord}_{ijt_2t_1})$$

### 6.6 Ordering exclusivity

For $t_1 < t_2$:

$$\text{ord}_{ijt_1t_2} + \text{ord}_{ijt_2t_1} \le 1 + M(2 - x_{ijt_1} - x_{ijt_2}) \qquad \forall (i,j)$$

### 6.7 Bidirectional conflict on shared (rerouted) track

$$d_{i,t_2} \ge d_{i,t_1} + h^{\min} - M(2 - r_{ijt_1} - r_{ijt_2}) \qquad \forall (i,j), (t_1,t_2)$$

### 6.8 Disruption window on blocked arcs

If $(i,j)\in B$ and not rerouted, train must clear before or enter after the window:

$$d_{it} + \tau^{\text{arc}}_{ijt} \le t^{\text{block}}_s + M(1 - x_{ijt} + r_{ijt}) \qquad \forall (i,j)\in B, t$$

$$d_{it} \ge t^{\text{block}}_e - M(1 - x_{ijt} + r_{ijt}) \qquad \forall (i,j)\in B, t$$

### 6.9 Rerouting logic and capacity

$$r_{ijt} \le x_{ijt} \qquad \forall (i,j), t$$

$$\sum_{t\in T} r_{ijt} \le 1 \qquad \forall (i,j)$$

### 6.10 Speed and position dynamics

For each $(k,k')\in K^{pairs}$:

$$v_{ijk't} = v_{ijkt} + \big(a^{\max}\,\text{acc}_{ijkt} - b^{\max}\,\text{brk}_{ijkt}\big)\,\Delta t \cdot 3.6$$

$$s_{ijk't} = s_{ijkt} + v_{ijkt} \cdot \frac{\Delta t}{3600}$$

### 6.11 Acceleration/braking exclusivity

$$\text{acc}_{ijkt} + \text{brk}_{ijkt} \le 1 \qquad \forall (i,j), k, t$$

### 6.12 Speed and position bounds

$$v_{ijkt} \ge V^{\min} - M(1 - x_{ijt}) \qquad \forall (i,j), k, t$$

$$v_{ijkt} \le V^{\max} \qquad \forall (i,j), k, t$$

$$0 \le s_{ijkt} \le L_{ij} + M(1 - x_{ijt}) \qquad \forall (i,j), k, t$$

### 6.13 Coupling of timing with speed profile

$$v_{ij,k_0,t} \le V^{\max}\, x_{ijt} \qquad \forall (i,j), t \quad (k_0 = \text{first step})$$

$$s_{ij,k_f,t} \ge L_{ij} - M(1 - x_{ijt}) \qquad \forall (i,j), t \quad (k_f = \text{last step})$$

$$\tau^{\text{arc}}_{ijt}\, V^{\max} \ge L_{ij} - M(1 - x_{ijt}) \qquad \forall (i,j), t$$

### 6.14 Traction power and energy

$$p_{ijkt} \ge e^{\text{acc}}\, v_{ijkt}\,\text{acc}_{ijkt} + e^{\text{cru}}\, v_{ijkt}\,(1 - \text{acc}_{ijkt} - \text{brk}_{ijkt})$$

$$E_t = \sum_{(i,j)\in A}\sum_{k\in K} p_{ijkt}\,\frac{\Delta t}{3600} \qquad \forall t$$

### 6.15 Delay definition

$$\text{delay}_t \ge a_{\text{dest}_t,\,t} - S^{\text{arr}}_t \qquad \forall t$$

### 6.16 Cancellation consistency

$$\sum_{(i,j)\in A:\, i=\text{orig}_t} x_{ijt} \le 1 - \text{cancel}_t \qquad \forall t$$

---

## 7. Solution-Relevant Remarks

- **Linearization:** The power term in (6.14) contains a product $v\cdot\text{acc}$. Because `acc` is binary and $v$ is bounded, this is standard-linearizable via the McCormick decomposition: $p \ge e^{\text{acc}}v - M(1-\text{acc})$ and $p \ge e^{\text{cru}}v - M\,\text{acc}$ (with $p\ge 0$), matching the code surrogate. *[Assumption]* This is the exact linear form implied by the code and required for MILP validity.
- **Tightness:** Big-M values should be set to $(T^{\text{arr}}_t - T^{\text{dep}}_t)$-scale rather than globally large to improve relaxations.
- **Decomposition structure (Section 5 of the paper):** The MILP decomposes into (i) an interaction IP over $x_{ijt}, r_{ijt}, \text{ord}_{ijt_1t_2}$ and the timing variables, and (ii) per-train plan subproblems over the speed variables $v, s, \text{acc}, \text{brk}, p$ once routing/timing is fixed. Sufficiently fine interval plans ensure the IP is equivalent to the MILP.

This completes the linear model with all variables, the objective, and constraints derived from the generated code.

# Feedback on the Generated MILP and Revised Final Model

## Review of the First Model — Issues Identified

1. **C6.1 is not a valid big-M linearization.** The expression `(T_e - d_{t,s*} - min_run)(1 - x)` multiplies a *variable* (`d`) by a *binary* (`1-x`), which is nonlinear. It must be replaced with a proper disjunctive big-M form.
2. **C4.2 (SOS2 piecewise linear) is over-engineered and inconsistent.** The hyperbolic relation `v·τ = δ` is nonconvex; a convex-combination SOS2 formulation does not correctly represent it and adds unnecessary complexity. A cleaner approach: fix the sub-interval *time* `τ_k` as a parameter and let `v_{t,s,k} = δ_k / τ_k` be determined, or bound speed directly and link running time to speed via a linear lower envelope.
3. **C7.2/C7.3 headway direction is wrong.** The constraint `a_{t,s+1} + h ≤ d_{t',s}` compares an *arrival* at `s+1` with a *departure* at `s` — these are on the same segment but the headway should relate the *entry* times (departures) or *exit* times (arrivals) of the two trains on the segment, not a mix.
4. **C9.2 is too strong.** Setting `y ≤ 1 - z` forces ordering variables to 0 when a train is cancelled, which can make C7.1 (`y + y' = 1`) infeasible. The relaxation should instead appear inside the headway big-M terms only.
5. **Missing link between speed profile and segment running time.** The model never forces `Σ_k τ_{t,s,k}` to equal the actual running time in a way consistent with `v_{t,s,k}`.
6. **Cancellation monotonicity direction.** `z_{t,s} ≤ z_{t,s+1}` is correct, but the model should also force `z_{t,s}=1 ⇒ a,d` frozen (no resource use), which is only partially handled.

## Revised Final MILP

### Sets and Indices
- Stations $S=\{1,\dots,|S|\}$; trains $T$; segments $\mathcal{E}=\{(s,s+1)\}$; sub-intervals $K=\{1,\dots,K\}$.
- Blocked segment $b=(s^*,s^*+1)$; disruption window $[T^{dis}_s, T^{dis}_e]$.
- $\mathcal{C}_s$: same-direction conflicting pairs on segment $s$; $\mathcal{O}_b$: opposite-direction pairs on $b$.

### Parameters
$a^{pl}_{t,s}$, $L_{s,s+1}$, $\delta_k$ (with $\sum_k \delta_k = L_{s,s+1}$), min_dw, max_dw, min_run$_{t,s}$, max_run$_{t,s}$, $h_{\min}$, $v_{\min}$, $v_{\max}$, $c_1,c_2$, weights $w_d,w_c,w_e$, big-M $M$.

### Decision Variables
| Var | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | arrival / departure time |
| $\delta^{del}_{t,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | delay |
| $x_{t,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | reroute on segment $(s,s+1)$ |
| $y_{t,t',s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $t$ precedes $t'$ on segment $s$ |
| $z_{t,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | cancellation at/after $s$ |
| $v_{t,s,k}$ | $\ge 0$ | average speed in sub-interval $k$ |
| $e_{t,s,k}$ | $\ge 0$ | energy in sub-interval $k$ |

### Objective
$$\min\; w_d\sum_{t,s}\delta^{del}_{t,s} + w_c\sum_{t,s} z_{t,s} + w_e\sum_{t,s,k} e_{t,s,k}$$

### Constraints

**(1) Delay linearization**
$$\delta^{del}_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} - a^{pl}_{t,s},\qquad \delta^{del}_{t,s}\ge 0$$

**(2) Dwell**
$$d_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} + \text{min\_dw}\,(1-z_{t,s}),\qquad d_{t,s}\le a_{t,s}+\text{max\_dw}$$

**(3) Running time**
$$a_{t,s+1}\ge d_{t,s}+\text{min\_run}_{t,s}(1-z_{t,s}),\qquad a_{t,s+1}\le d_{t,s}+\text{max\_run}_{t,s}$$

**(4) Speed–time consistency (linear, corrected)**
Fix sub-interval time $\tau_k=\delta_k/v^{ref}$ as a parameter, so the segment running time is
$$a_{t,s+1}-d_{t,s}=\sum_{k}\tau_k \quad\text{(parameterized)}$$
and speed is bounded by the running time via a linear lower envelope:
$$v_{t,s,k}\ \ge\ \frac{\delta_k}{\tau_k}\ -\ \gamma\,(a_{t,s+1}-d_{t,s}-\text{min\_run}_{t,s}),\qquad v_{\min}\le v_{t,s,k}\le v_{\max}$$
*(This replaces the invalid SOS2 hyperbolic formulation with a valid linear relaxation.)*

**(5) Energy**
$$e_{t,s,k}\ \ge\ c_1 v_{t,s,k}+c_2$$

**(6) Disruption / rerouting (corrected big-M)**
For the blocked segment $b=(s^*,s^*+1)$:
$$a_{t,s^*+1}\ \ge\ T^{dis}_e - M(1-x_{t,s^*}) - M z_{t,s^*}$$
$$x_{t,s}\le \mathbb{1}[(s,s+1)=b]$$

**(7) Headway (corrected — compare like with like)**
For $(t,t')\in\mathcal{C}_s$:
$$y_{t,t',s}+y_{t',t,s}=1$$
$$d_{t',s}\ \ge\ d_{t,s}+h_{\min} - M(1-y_{t,t',s}) - M(z_{t,s}+z_{t',s})$$
$$d_{t,s}\ \ge\ d_{t',s}+h_{\min} - M(1-y_{t',t,s}) - M(z_{t,s}+z_{t',s})$$

**(8) Shared single track on $b$ (opposite directions)**
For $(t,t')\in\mathcal{O}_b$:
$$y_{t,t',b}+y_{t',t,b}=1$$
$$d_{t',s^*}\ \ge\ d_{t,s^*}+h_{\min} - M(1-y_{t,t',b}) - M(z_{t,s^*}+z_{t',s^*})$$
$$d_{t,s^*}\ \ge\ d_{t',s^*}+h_{\min} - M(1-y_{t',t,b}) - M(z_{t,s^*}+z_{t',s^*})$$

**(9) Cancellation (corrected)**
$$z_{t,s}\le z_{t,s+1},\qquad z_{t,s}\le \mathbb{1}[\text{$t$ affected}]$$
*(Resource-use relaxation is handled inside the big-M terms of (7)–(8), not by forcing $y=0$.)*

**(10) Domains**
$$a,d,\delta^{del},v,e\ge 0;\qquad x,y,z\in\{0,1\}$$

## Summary of Improvements
- Replaced the **nonlinear C6.1** with a valid disjunctive big-M.
- Replaced the **incorrect SOS2 hyperbolic** speed formulation with a **linear speed–time envelope**.
- Fixed the **headway direction** to compare departure times (entry times) on the same segment.
- Removed the **over-restrictive C9.2** that could cause infeasibility.
- Added the **missing speed–running-time link**.
- Kept the model fully linear and MILP-compliant.

# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

After reviewing the three generated models, **Model 2** is selected as the best because it (i) cleanly separates the disruption logic into a sharp tri-state disjunction ($\phi_{i,g'} + r_{i,g'} + z_i \ge 1$), (ii) keeps the speed/energy coupling fully linear via regime convex combinations with parameterized knot values, and (iii) introduces integer capacity variables $\eta_g^0, \eta_g^1$ that model bidirectional track occupancy rigorously. I refine and complete it below.

---

## 1. Sets, Indices, and Parameters

**Sets / indices**
- $i,j \in \mathcal{T}$: trains ($|\mathcal{T}|=N_T$), each with direction $d_i \in \{0,1\}$ (0 = up, 1 = down)
- $s \in \mathcal{S}$: stations, ordered along the line ($|\mathcal{S}|=N_S$)
- $g \in \mathcal{G}$: segments between consecutive stations ($|\mathcal{G}|=N_S-1$); segment $g$ connects $s^-(g)$ (entry) to $s^+(g)$ (exit in direction of travel)
- $k \in \mathcal{K}(g)$: knot points for speed/energy discretization on segment $g$
- $r \in \mathcal{R}$: piecewise-linear energy regime intervals
- $g'$: the disrupted (partially blocked) segment
- $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$: disruption time window

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}, d_{i,s}^{\text{nom}}$ | nominal arrival / departure times |
| $\underline{w}_{i,s}, \overline{w}_{i,s}$ | min / max dwell time |
| $\underline{tr}_{i,g}, \overline{tr}_{i,g}$ | min / max running time on normal track |
| $\underline{tr}^{b}_{i,g'}, \overline{tr}^{b}_{i,g'}$ | min / max running time on opposite (bidirectional) track at $g'$ |
| $L_g$ | segment length |
| $v_k^{\text{knot}}, \text{tr}_k^{\text{knot}}$ | knot-point speed / running-time values |
| $E^{\text{pl}}_{i,g,r}$ | piecewise-linear energy value at regime $r$ |
| $h^{d}$ | headway for direction $d \in \{0,1\}$ |
| $h^{b}$ | bidirectional-track separation headway |
| $C_{\text{delay}}, C_{\text{energy}}, C_{\text{cancel}}, C_{\text{span}}$ | objective weights |
| $N^{\max}_{\text{cancel}}$ | max allowed cancellations |
| $M$ | large constant, $M = T_{\max}-T_{\min}+\max_g \overline{tr}_{i,g}$ |

---

## 2. Decision Variables

**Continuous** (all $\ge 0$)

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}$ | arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $w_{i,s}$ | dwell time, $w_{i,s}=d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}$ |
| $tr_{i,g}$ | running time on segment $g$ |
| $v_{i,g,k}$ | speed at knot $k$ on segment $g$ |
| $\alpha_{i,g,r}\in[0,1]$ | convex-combination weight for energy regime $r$ |
| $E_{i,g}$ | energy consumed on segment $g$ |
| $\delta^{\text{early}}_{i,s},\ \delta^{\text{late}}_{i,s}$ | early / late deviation |
| $M_{\text{span}}$ | makespan (max deviation) variable |

**Binary**

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| $y_{i,j,g}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$ |
| $r_{i,g}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ uses opposite track on $g$ (fixed $0$ if $g\ne g'$) |
| $z_i$ | $=1$ if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\phi_{i,g'}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ clears $g'$ on the normal track before $t_{\text{start}}$ |

**Integer**

| Variable | Description | Bounds |
|---|---|---|
| $\eta_{g}^{0},\ \eta_{g}^{1}$ | number of direction-0 / direction-1 trains traversing $g$ on the opposite track | $[0,|\mathcal{T}|]$ |

---

## 3. Objective Function

$$
\min\ Z = C_{\text{delay}}\!\!\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\!\big(\delta^{\text{early}}_{i,s}+\delta^{\text{late}}_{i,s}\big)
\;+\; C_{\text{energy}}\!\!\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{g\in\mathcal{G}} E_{i,g}
\;+\; C_{\text{cancel}}\!\!\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} z_i
\;+\; C_{\text{span}}\, M_{\text{span}}
$$

**Deviation definitions** (linear, no absolute values):
$$
a_{i,s}-a_{i,s}^{\text{nom}} = \delta^{\text{late}}_{i,s}-\delta^{\text{early}}_{i,s},\qquad
d_{i,s}-d_{i,s}^{\text{nom}} = \delta^{\text{late}}_{i,s}-\delta^{\text{early}}_{i,s},\qquad \forall i,s
$$

---

## 4. Constraints (all linear)

### (C1) Timetable feasibility
$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} + \underline{w}_{i,s}\,(1-z_i), \quad d_{i,s}-a_{i,s} \le \overline{w}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\underline{tr}_{i,g}\,(1-z_i) \le tr_{i,g} \le \overline{tr}_{i,g}, \quad \forall i,g
$$

### (C2) Segment–station coupling
$$
a_{i,s^+(g)} \ge d_{i,s^-(g)} + tr_{i,g} - M z_i, \quad
a_{i,s^+(g)} \le d_{i,s^-(g)} + tr_{i,g} + M z_i, \quad \forall i,g
$$

### (C3) Speed–running-time coupling (piecewise-linear, convex combination)
$$
tr_{i,g} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}(g)} \lambda_{i,g,k}\,\text{tr}^{\text{knot}}_{k}, \qquad
v_{i,g,k} = \sum_{k'\in\mathcal{K}(g)} \lambda_{i,g,k'}\,v^{\text{knot}}_{k'}, \qquad
\sum_{k}\lambda_{i,g,k}=1,\ \lambda\ge0
$$
Equivalently, using regime variables for energy:
$$
tr_{i,g} = \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}} \alpha_{i,g,r}\,\text{tr}^{\text{pl}}_r, \qquad
E_{i,g} = \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}} \alpha_{i,g,r}\,E^{\text{pl}}_{i,g,r}, \qquad
\sum_{r}\alpha_{i,g,r}=1,\ \alpha_{i,g,r}\in[0,1]
$$
(Coupling is linear because $\text{tr}^{\text{pl}}_r$ and $E^{\text{pl}}_{i,g,r}$ are parameters.)

### (C4) Headway / ordering on shared segments
For all $i\ne j$, $g$:
$$
a_{j,s^+(g)} \ge d_{i,s^-(g)} + tr_{i,g} + h^{d_i} - M(1-y_{i,j,g}) - M(z_i+z_j)
$$
$$
a_{i,s^+(g)} \ge d_{j,s^-(g)} + tr_{j,g} + h^{d_j} - M\,y_{i,j,g} - M(z_i+z_j)
$$
$$
y_{i,j,g}+y_{j,i,g}=1 \quad\text{(both active, same direction)}
$$

### (C5) Bidirectional conflict on $g'$
$$
a_{j,s^+(g')} \ge d_{i,s^-(g')}+h^{b} - M(1-y_{i,j,g'}) - M(2-r_{i,g'}-r_{j,g'})
$$
$$
a_{i,s^+(g')} \ge d_{j,s^-(g')}+h^{b} - M\,y_{i,j,g'} - M(2-r_{i,g'}-r_{j,g'})
$$
When both use the bidirectional track ($r_i=r_j=1$), same-direction trains also respect $h^{d}$:
$$
a_{j,s^+(g')} \ge d_{i,s^-(g')}+h^{d_i}-M(1-y_{i,j,g'})-M(2-r_{i,g'}-r_{j,g'})
$$

### (C6) Disruption constraints on $g'$
No train uses the blocked normal track during the window:
$$
a_{i,s^+(g')} \le t_{\text{start}} + M(1-\phi_{i,g'}) + M\,r_{i,g'}
$$
$$
d_{i,s^-(g')} \ge t_{\text{end}} - M\,\phi_{i,g'} - M\,r_{i,g'}
$$
**Tri-state disjunction** (pre-clear, reroute, or cancel):
$$
\phi_{i,g'} + r_{i,g'} + z_i \ge 1, \quad \forall i
$$
**Capacity on bidirectional track** (per direction):
$$
\sum_{i:\,d_i=0} r_{i,g'} \le \eta_{g'}^{0} \le c_b, \qquad
\sum_{i:\,d_i=1} r_{i,g'} \le \eta_{g'}^{1} \le c_b
$$
where $c_b$ is the per-direction capacity (typically $1$).

### (C7) Rerouting continuity and running-time bounds
$$
r_{i,g}=0 \quad \forall i,\ g\ne g'
$$
$$
tr_{i,g'} \le \overline{tr}_{i,g'} + M\,r_{i,g'}, \qquad
tr_{i,g'} \ge \underline{tr}^{b}_{i,g'} - M(1-r_{i,g'})
$$
$$
tr_{i,g'} \le \overline{tr}^{b}_{i,g'} + M(1-r_{i,g'})
$$

### (C8) Cancel / reroute logic
$$
a_{i,s} \le M(1-z_i),\quad d_{i,s}\le M(1-z_i),\quad tr_{i,g}\le M(1-z_i),\quad E_{i,g}\le M(1-z_i)
$$
$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} z_i \le N^{\max}_{\text{cancel}}, \qquad
r_{i,g'} \le 1-z_i, \qquad \phi_{i,g'} \le 1-z_i
$$

### (C9) Makespan
$$
M_{\text{span}} \ge \delta^{\text{early}}_{i,s}+\delta^{\text{late}}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

### (C10) Variable bounds and integrality
$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, tr_{i,g}, v_{i,g,k}, E_{i,g}, M_{\text{span}} \ge 0
$$
$$
y_{i,j,g},\ r_{i,g},\ z_i,\ \phi_{i,g}\in\{0,1\}, \qquad \eta_g^{0},\eta_g^{1}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}
$$

---

## 5. Assumptions (marked)

1. *(assumption)* A fixed set of trains with known directions and a known nominal timetable is given.
2. *(assumption)* Dwell-time bounds are given per station; energy is a convex piecewise-linear function of speed with discretized knot points.
3. *(assumption)* Bidirectional (opposite-track) operation is permitted **only** on the single disrupted segment $g'$, during the disruption window, with capacity $c_b$ per direction.
4. *(assumption)* Headway times are direction-dependent constants $h^{d}$; the opposite-track separation headway $h^{b}$ is constant.
5. *(assumption)* Segment lengths $L_g$ are known; overtaking within a segment is disallowed (enforced by ordering binaries).
6. *(assumption)* Cancelled trains carry no schedule times and consume no energy.

---

## 6. Structural Summary

| Element | Type | Role |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Timetable recovery |
| $tr_{i,g}, v_{i,g,k}, \alpha_{i,g,r}, E_{i,g}$ | Continuous | Speed profile & energy (PWL, SOS2/convex combination) |
| $y_{i,j,g}$ | Binary | Train ordering / headway on segments |
| $r_{i,g}$ | Binary | Rerouting to opposite track |
| $z_i$ | Binary | Cancellation |
| $\phi_{i,g'}$ | Binary | Pre-disruption traversal of $g'$ |
| $\eta_g^0,\eta_g^1$ | Integer | Bidirectional track capacity |

**Key structural features:** the disruption logic reduces to a compact tri-state disjunction $\phi_{i,g'}+r_{i,g'}+z_i\ge1$; running-time/energy coupling is a pure convex combination over a precomputed knot/regime grid; headway and bidirectional conflicts are handled by ordering binaries with big-$M$ activation tied to routing; capacity on the shared bidirectional track is captured by integer counters. All constraints are linear in the decision variables, yielding a **mixed-integer linear program (MILP)** solvable by standard branch-and-cut solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, HiGHS, CBC).

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code, expressed as equations. All assumptions are marked explicitly.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations along the line, indexed by $s$ (ordered $0,\dots,N$) |
| $\text{SEG} \subseteq S$ | Set of segments (consecutive station pairs), indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $D \subseteq \text{SEG}$ | Set of disruption-affected (blocked) segments |
| $TP = \{(i,j) : i \neq j\}$ | Ordered pairs of distinct trains |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ |
| $v_k$ | Speed value of level $k$ |
| $v^{\max}$ | Maximum allowable speed |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration |
| $\Delta t$ | Time step for acceleration feasibility |
| $d^{\min}$ | Minimum headway (safety separation) |
| $t^{\text{dwell}}_{\min}, t^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time |
| $E_k$ | Energy consumption rate at speed level $k$ |
| $\tau_s$ | Minimum running time on segment $s$ |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window |
| $\text{dep}_i^0$ | Scheduled departure of train $i$ from origin |
| $\text{arr}_i^N$ | Scheduled arrival of train $i$ at destination |
| $\text{arr}^{\text{sched}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $w^{\text{delay}}, w^{\text{energy}}$ | Objective weights for delay and energy |
| $\text{dir}_i$ | Direction of train $i$ ($+1$ or $-1$) |
| $\text{blocked}_s$ | 1 if segment $s$ is blocked during the window, else 0 |

---

## Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $r_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $z_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $v_{i,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ travels segment $s$ at speed level $k$ |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $e_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $u_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled on segment $s$ |
| $\text{before}_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ passes segment $s$ before the disruption window |

---

## Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay and total energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = w^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{i,s} \;+\; w^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in \text{SEG}} e_{i,s}
$$

---

## Constraints

### (1) Dwell time bounds
$$
y_{i,s} - x_{i,s} \ge t^{\text{dwell}}_{\min} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
y_{i,s} - x_{i,s} \le t^{\text{dwell}}_{\max} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (2) Running time consistency with speed profile
$$
x_{i,s+1} - y_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} \frac{L_s}{v_k}\, v_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,s,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$

### (3) Speed limits and acceleration/deceleration feasibility
$$
v_k \le v^{\max} \qquad \forall k \in K
$$
$$
\frac{v_{k+1} - v_k}{\Delta t} \le a^{\max} \qquad \forall k \in K \text{ (consecutive)}
$$
$$
\frac{v_k - v_{k+1}}{\Delta t} \le b^{\max} \qquad \forall k \in K \text{ (consecutive)}
$$

### (4) Energy consumption
$$
e_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} E_k \cdot \frac{L_s}{v_k} \cdot v_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$

### (5) Delay definition
$$
\delta_{i,s} \ge x_{i,s} - \text{arr}^{\text{sched}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta_{i,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (6) Disruption window / segment blockage
If segment $s$ is blocked and the train does not reroute, it must pass either before $T^{\text{start}}$ or after $T^{\text{end}}$:

$$
x_{i,s+1} \le T^{\text{start}} + M(1 - \text{blocked}_s) + M\,r_{i,s} + M(1 - \text{before}_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$
$$
x_{i,s+1} \ge T^{\text{end}} - M(1 - \text{blocked}_s) - M\,r_{i,s} - M\,\text{before}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$

Rerouting is only permitted on disruption-affected segments:
$$
r_{i,s} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SEG} \setminus D
$$

### (7) Headway / conflict-free constraints on shared track
$$
y_{j,s} - y_{i,s} \ge d^{\min} - M(1 - z_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TP,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$
$$
y_{i,s} - y_{j,s} \ge d^{\min} - M\,z_{i,j,s} \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TP,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$

### (8) Bidirectional conflict on rerouted track (ordering complementarity)
$$
z_{i,j,s} + z_{j,i,s} = 1 \qquad \forall (i,j) \in TP,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$

### (9) Cancellation linkage
$$
x_{i,s+1} - x_{i,s} \le M(1 - u_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SEG}
$$
$$
v_{i,s,k} \le 1 - u_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SEG},\; k \in K
$$

### (10) Time horizon bounds
$$
x_{i,s_0} \ge \text{dep}_i^0 \qquad \forall i \in T
$$
$$
x_{i,s_N} \le \text{arr}_i^N + M \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

### (11) Variable domains
$$
r_{i,s},\; z_{i,j,s},\; v_{i,s,k},\; u_{i,s},\; \text{before}_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
x_{i,s},\; y_{i,s},\; \delta_{i,s},\; e_{i,s} \ge 0
$$

---

## Assumptions (marked)

1. **Speed discretization** — Continuous speed profiles are approximated by a finite set of discrete speed levels $K$.
2. **Energy model** — Energy consumption is proportional to the speed level and running time (linear in $v_{i,s,k}$).
3. **Single blockage** — At most one segment per disruption is blocked at a time.
4. **Rerouting scope** — Rerouting to the opposite track is only allowed within disruption-affected segments $D$.
5. **Dwell bounds** — Dwell times are bounded within $[t^{\text{dwell}}_{\min}, t^{\text{dwell}}_{\max}]$.
6. **Big-M linearization** — All disjunctive (either/or) constraints are linearized using big-M with a sufficiently large constant $M$.
7. **Bidirectional conflict handling** — When both trains reroute on the same segment, the ordering binary $z$ enforces separation; when they use different tracks, the ordering constraint is relaxed via big-M.
8. **Cancellation semantics** — A cancelled train does not advance along the segment and selects no speed level.
