Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations/block sections (segments), indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{dis}$ | Set of disrupted segments (partial blockage), $\mathcal{S}^{dis} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of speed levels (discrete speed profile points), indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{TP}$ | Set of time periods (discretized), indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of feasible speed profiles for train $i$, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of routes (track directions), $r \in \{up, down\}$; index $r$ |
| $\mathcal{F}$ | Set of train pairs $(i,j)$ that may conflict |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $T^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\underline{R}_{i,s}$ | Minimum running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $\bar{R}_{i,s}$ | Maximum running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $\underline{D}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\bar{D}_{i,s}$ | Maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h_{min}$ | Minimum safety headway between consecutive trains on same track |
| $\tau^{dis}_{start}, \tau^{dis}_{end}$ | Start and end of disruption time window |
| $C^{pen}$ | Penalty cost per unit delay (per train per time unit) |
| $C^{cancel}$ | Cost of canceling a train service |
| $C^{eng}$ | Energy cost coefficient (per unit of energy) |
| $E_{i,p,s}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ using profile $p$ on segment $s$ |
| $v_{i,p,s,k}$ | Speed of train $i$ on segment $s$ at speed level $k$ under profile $p$ |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $N^{max}$ | Maximum number of trains allowed on a disrupted segment during disruption window |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | Binary parameter: 1 if train $i$'s scheduled route uses segment $s$, 0 otherwise |
| $\alpha_{i}$ | Weight for delay penalty of train $i$ (priority weight) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{i,s}$ | Continuous ($\geq 0$) | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | Continuous ($\geq 0$) | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Continuous ($\geq 0$) | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_{i,s}$ | Continuous ($\geq 0$) | Running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $\Delta^+_{i,s}$ | Continuous ($\geq 0$) | Positive delay of train $i$ at station $s$ (lateness) |
| $z_{i,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is canceled at/before segment $s$, 0 otherwise |
| $\sigma_{i,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $s$ (uses opposite track), 0 otherwise |
| $\theta_{i,j,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ (sequencing), 0 otherwise |
| $u_{i,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $s$ during disruption window, 0 otherwise |

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\lambda_{i,p}$ | Binary | 1 if speed profile $p$ is selected for train $i$, 0 otherwise |
| $\nu_{i,s,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ operates at speed level $k$ on segment $s$, 0 otherwise |
| $e_{i,s}$ | Continuous ($\geq 0$) | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ |

---

## 4. Assumptions

**(A1)** The railway line is discretized into segments (block sections) between consecutive stations. Each segment can accommodate at most one train per direction at any time (fixed block signaling). *(Reasonable modeling assumption)*

**(A2)** During the disruption window $[\tau^{dis}_{start}, \tau^{dis}_{end}]$, the disrupted segment $s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis}$ allows only unidirectional traffic (one track blocked). Trains may be rerouted to the opposite track, but bidirectional traffic on the same track must be mutually exclusive. *(Stated in problem description)*

**(A3)** Speed profiles are precomputed discrete alternatives corresponding to different acceleration/deceleration strategies; the actual speed trajectory is approximated by selecting one profile per train per segment. *(Simplification for MILP tractability)*

**(A4)** Energy consumption is a linear function of the selected speed profile and segment characteristics: $e_{i,s} = \sum_{p} E_{i,p,s} \cdot \lambda_{i,p}$. *(Assumption: precomputed energy values per profile)*

**(A5)** Train cancellation is modeled at the segment level; once canceled, the train does not occupy any subsequent segment. *(Modeling assumption)*

**(A6)** Dwell times can be extended but not reduced below scheduled minimum, to reflect operational constraints. *(Standard assumption in TRP literature)*

**(A7)** All times are expressed in a common discrete time unit (e.g., seconds), and the optimization horizon is finite $[0, T^{max}]$. *(Standard assumption)*

**(A8)** Rerouting is only permitted on disrupted segments during the disruption window; outside this window, trains use their scheduled tracks. *(Reasonable assumption based on problem context)*

---

## 5. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted combination of total passenger delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \quad Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \alpha_i \cdot C^{pen} \cdot \Delta^+_{i,s}}_{\text{Delay cost}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} C^{eng} \cdot e_{i,s}}_{\text{Energy cost}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} C^{cancel} \cdot z_{i,s}}_{\text{Cancellation cost}}
$$

*(Assumption: Linear weighted sum; weights $\alpha_i$ reflect train priority)*

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Timetable Feasibility Constraints

**Departure-arrival linkage:**
$$
y_{i,s+1} = x_{i,s} + r_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\{|\mathcal{S}|\} \tag{1}
$$

**Dwell time definition:**
$$
x_{i,s} = y_{i,s} + d_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{2}
$$

**Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\underline{D}_{i,s} \leq d_{i,s} \leq \bar{D}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{3}
$$

**Running time bounds:**
$$
\underline{R}_{i,s} \leq r_{i,s} \leq \bar{R}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{4}
$$

**Delay definition (lateness):**
$$
\Delta^+_{i,s} \geq y_{i,s} - T^{arr}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{5}
$$
$$
\Delta^+_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{6}
$$

**Cancellation consistency:**
$$
z_{i,s} \leq z_{i,s+1}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\{|\mathcal{S}|\} \tag{7}
$$
*(If canceled at segment $s$, remains canceled downstream)*

---

### 6.2 Speed Profile Selection Constraints

**One profile per train:**
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \lambda_{i,p} = 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{8}
$$

**Speed level linkage with profile:**
$$
\nu_{i,s,k} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i: v_{i,p,s,k} > 0} \lambda_{i,p}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{9}
$$
*(Assumption: each profile determines a unique speed at each segment; this constraint links binary profile selection to speed level indicators)*

**At most one speed level per segment:**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \nu_{i,s,k} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{10}
$$

**Energy consumption linearization:**
$$
e_{i,s} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} E_{i,p,s} \cdot \lambda_{i,p}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{11}
$$

---

### 6.3 Coupling Between Timetable and Speed Profile

**Running time determined by speed profile:**
$$
r_{i,s} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} R_{i,p,s} \cdot \lambda_{i,p}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{12}
$$
*(Assumption: Each profile $p$ implies a specific running time $R_{i,p,s}$ on segment $s$)*

**Consistency of running time bounds with profile selection:**
$$
\underline{R}_{i,s} \cdot \sum_{p} \lambda_{i,p} \leq r_{i,s} \leq \bar{R}_{i,s} \cdot \sum_{p} \lambda_{i,p}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{13}
$$

---

### 6.4 Disruption Window and Rerouting Constraints

**Disruption window occupancy indicator:**
$$
x_{i,s} \geq \tau^{dis}_{start} - M(1 - u_{i,s}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis} \tag{14}
$$
$$
y_{i,s+1} \leq \tau^{dis}_{end} + M(1 - u_{i,s}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis} \tag{15}
$$

**Rerouting only on disrupted segments during window:**
$$
\sigma_{i,s} = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \notin \mathcal{S}^{dis} \tag{16}
$$

**Rerouting allowed only if train traverses during disruption:**
$$
\sigma_{i,s} \leq u_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis} \tag{17}
$$

**Unidirectional capacity on disrupted segment (at most $N^{max}$ trains during window):**
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} u_{i,s} \leq N^{max}, \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis} \tag{18}
$$
*(Assumption: $N^{max}$ reflects residual capacity during partial blockage)*

**Bidirectional exclusivity on rerouted track:**
$$
\sigma_{i,s} + \sigma_{j,s} \leq 1 + (1 - u_{i,s}) + (1 - u_{j,s}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{F}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis}, \; i \neq j \tag{19}
$$
*(If both trains use disrupted segment during window and both reroute, they would conflict on the same opposite track — this is prevented by sequencing constraints below; this constraint is a simplification)*

---

### 6.5 Conflict-Free Sequencing Constraints (Same Direction)

**Headway on same track (no rerouting):**
$$
x_{j,s} \geq x_{i,s} + h_{min} - M(1 - \theta_{i,j,s}) - M \cdot \sigma_{i,s} - M \cdot \sigma_{j,s}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{F}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{20}
$$

$$
x_{i,s} \geq x_{j,s} + h_{min} - M \cdot \theta_{i,j,s} - M \cdot \sigma_{i,s} - M \cdot \sigma_{j,s}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{F}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{21}
$$

**Sequencing variable definition:**
$$
\theta_{i,j,s} + \theta_{j,i,s} = 1, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{F}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{22}
$$

---

### 6.6 Bidirectional Conflict Constraints (Rerouted Trains)

**When both trains reroute on disrupted segment, enforce headway on shared track:**
$$
x_{j,s} \geq x_{i,s} + h_{min} - M(1 - \theta_{i,j,s}) - M(1 - \sigma_{i,s}) - M(1 - \sigma_{j,s}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{F}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis} \tag{23}
$$

$$
x_{i,s} \geq x_{j,s} + h_{min} - M \cdot \theta_{i,j,s} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,s}) - M(1 - \sigma_{j,s}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{F}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis} \tag{24}
$$

**Mutual exclusion of opposing movements on same track during disruption:**
$$
\sigma_{i,s} + \sigma_{j,s} \leq 1 + \theta_{i,j,s} + \theta_{j,i,s}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{F}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis}, \; i \neq j \tag{25}
$$
*(Assumption: If both reroute, they must be sequenced — one passes before the other)*

---

### 6.7 Cancellation Constraints

**If train canceled, no times assigned:**
$$
y_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_{i,s}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{26}
$$
$$
x_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_{i,s}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{27}
$$

**Canceled train has no energy consumption:**
$$
e_{i,s} \leq M(1 - z_{i,s}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{28}
$$

---

### 6.8 Time Horizon and Non-negativity

$$
0 \leq y_{i,s} \leq T^{max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{29}
$$
$$
0 \leq x_{i,s} \leq T^{max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{30}
$$
$$
\Delta^+_{i,s}, \; d_{i,s}, \; r_{i,s}, \; e_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{31}
$$
$$
z_{i,s}, \; \sigma_{i,s}, \; \theta_{i,j,s}, \; u_{i,s}, \; \lambda_{i,p}, \; \nu_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\} \tag{32}
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Objective** | Minimize weighted sum of delay, energy, and cancellation costs |
| **Decision Variables** | Timetable times ($x, y, d, r$), routing ($\sigma$), sequencing ($\theta$), cancellation ($z$), speed profile ($\lambda$), speed level ($\nu$), energy ($e$) |
| **Key Constraints** | Timetable feasibility (1–7), speed profile selection (8–13), disruption/rerouting (14–19), conflict-free sequencing (20–25), cancellation (26–28) |
| **Coupling** | Running time linked to speed profile (12); energy linked to profile (11); rerouting affects sequencing (23–25) |
| **Complexity** | MILP with binary variables for sequencing, routing, profile selection; continuous variables for times and energy |

---

## 8. Assumptions Summary (Explicitly Marked)

| # | Assumption | Justification |
|---|------------|---------------|
| A1 | Fixed block signaling, one train per segment per direction | Standard in railway rescheduling literature |
| A2 | Unidirectional traffic on disrupted segment during window | Stated in problem description |
| A3 | Discrete precomputed speed profiles | Simplification for MILP tractability |
| A4 | Linear energy consumption per profile | Precomputed energy values |
| A5 | Segment-level cancellation | Modeling simplification |
| A6 | Dwell time can only be extended | Operational constraint |
| A7 | Discrete time horizon | Standard in timetabling |
| A8 | Rerouting only on disrupted segments | Based on problem context |
| A9 | Linear weighted objective | Standard multi-objective scalarization |
| A10 | Bidirectional conflicts resolved by sequencing | Necessary for conflict-free operation |

Based on the generated model, here is the complete MILP formulation for the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages.

---

# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line), indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of segments, indexed by $k$ (segment $k$ connects station $k$ to $k+1$) |
| $I$ | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $i$ |
| $R_t$ | Set of feasible routes for train $t$ (original + rerouting alternatives), indexed by $r$ |
| $K_r$ | Set of segments belonging to route $r$ |
| $D \subseteq K \times I$ | Set of blocked (segment, interval) pairs caused by the disruption |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ (m) |
| $\Delta$ | Duration of each time interval (s) |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum operating speed (m/s) |
| $a_{\min}, a_{\max}$ | Minimum (deceleration) / maximum (acceleration) values (m/s²) |
| $e_{coef}(\cdot)$ | Energy consumption rate as a function of speed (kWh/s), piecewise linear |
| $t^{arr}_{t,s}, t^{dep}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $dwell^{\min}_s, dwell^{\max}_s$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $c_{delay}, c_{energy}, c_{cancel}$ | Cost coefficients for delay, energy, and cancellation |
| $dir(t) \in \{+1,-1\}$ | Direction of train $t$ |
| $track(t,r) \in \{1,2\}$ | Physical track used by train $t$ under route $r$ |
| $(v_b, e_b)$ | Breakpoints of the piecewise-linear energy function |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{tki}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses segment $k$ during interval $i$ |
| $y_{tsi}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ dwells at station $s$ during interval $i$ |
| $z_{tr}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r$ |
| $v_{tki}$ | $\ge 0$ | Speed of train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$ |
| $a_{tki}$ | free | Acceleration of train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$ |
| $p_{tki}$ | $\ge 0$ | Position of train $t$ within segment $k$ at end of interval $i$ |
| $arr_{ts}$ | $\ge 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $dep_{ts}$ | $\ge 0$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $dwell_{ts}$ | $\ge 0$ | Actual dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $delay_t$ | $\ge 0$ | Total delay of train $t$ |
| $energy_t$ | $\ge 0$ | Total energy consumption of train $t$ |
| $cancel_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $u_{tki}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is active on segment $k$ in interval $i$ |
| $w_{t_1 t_2 k i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ precedes train $t_2$ on segment $k$ in interval $i$ |
| $\lambda_{tkib}$ | $\ge 0$ | Convex-combination weight for breakpoint $b$ |
| $bp_{tkib}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | SOS2 adjacency indicator for breakpoint $b$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\ Z = c_{delay}\sum_{t \in T} delay_t \;+\; c_{energy}\sum_{t \in T} energy_t \;+\; c_{cancel}\sum_{t \in T} cancel_t
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Route selection**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} z_{tr} = 1 - cancel_t \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(2) Segment–route consistency**
$$
x_{tki} \le \sum_{r \in R_t : k \in K_r} z_{tr} \qquad \forall t \in T,\ k \in K,\ i \in I
$$

**(3) Disruption avoidance**
$$
x_{tki} = 0 \qquad \forall (k,i) \in D,\ \forall t \in T
$$

**(4) Cancellation coupling**
$$
x_{tki} \le 1 - cancel_t,\quad u_{tki} \le 1 - cancel_t,\quad y_{tsi} \le 1 - cancel_t \qquad \forall t, k, s, i
$$

**(5) Flow conservation at stations (interval-based)**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_{in}(s)} x_{tki} = \sum_{k' \in K_{out}(s)} x_{tk'i} + y_{tsi} \qquad \forall t \in T,\ s \in S,\ i \in I
$$

**(6) Position dynamics**
$$
p_{tki} = p_{t,k,i-1} + v_{t,k,i-1}\,\Delta + \tfrac{1}{2}\,a_{t,k,i-1}\,\Delta^{2} \qquad \forall t, k,\ i > i_0
$$

**(7) Speed update**
$$
v_{tki} = v_{t,k,i-1} + a_{t,k,i-1}\,\Delta \qquad \forall t, k,\ i > i_0
$$

**(8) Speed bounds**
$$
v_{\min}\,x_{tki} \le v_{tki} \le v_{\max}\,x_{tki} \qquad \forall t, k, i
$$

**(9) Acceleration bounds**
$$
a_{\min}\,x_{tki} \le a_{tki} \le a_{\max}\,x_{tki} \qquad \forall t, k, i
$$

**(10) Segment length and minimum traversal time**
$$
p_{tki} \le L_k \qquad \forall t, k, i
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{tki}\,\Delta \ge \frac{L_k}{v_{\max}} \qquad \forall t, k
$$

**(11) Dwell time bounds**
$$
dwell^{\min}_s\,(1 - cancel_t) \le dwell_{ts} \le dwell^{\max}_s\,(1 - cancel_t) \qquad \forall t, s
$$

**(12) Arrival / departure linking**
$$
dep_{ts} = arr_{ts} + dwell_{ts} \qquad \forall t, s
$$
$$
i\,\Delta - M(1 - x_{tki}) \le arr_{t,k+1} \le (i+1)\,\Delta + M(1 - x_{tki}) \qquad \forall t, k, i
$$

**(13) Delay**
$$
delay_t \ge arr_{t,s_{dest}} - t^{arr}_{t,s_{dest}}, \qquad delay_t \ge 0 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(14) Bidirectional conflict on shared track**
$$
x_{t_1 k i} + x_{t_2 k i} \le 1 + M\!\left(2 - z_{t_1 0} - z_{t_2 0}\right)
\qquad \forall t_1 < t_2 : dir(t_1) \ne dir(t_2),\ \forall k, i
$$

**(15) Same-direction headway via ordering**
$$
w_{t_1 t_2 k i} + w_{t_2 t_1 k i} \ge x_{t_1 k i} + x_{t_2 k i} - 1
$$
$$
arr_{t_2, k+1} \ge dep_{t_1, k} + h_{\min} - M\!\left(1 - w_{t_1 t_2 k i}\right)
\qquad \forall t_1 \ne t_2 : dir(t_1) = dir(t_2),\ \forall k, i
$$

**(16) Energy — piecewise-linear (SOS2-style convex combination)**
$$
\sum_{b} \lambda_{tkib} = 1, \qquad \sum_{b} bp_{tkib} \le 2, \qquad \lambda_{tkib} \le bp_{tkib} \qquad \forall t, k, i, b
$$
$$
v_{tki} = \sum_{b} \lambda_{tkib}\,v_b \qquad \forall t, k, i
$$
$$
energy_t \ge \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{b} \lambda_{tkib}\,e_b\,\Delta \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(17) Linking $x, u, v, a, p$**
$$
u_{tki} \ge x_{tki}, \quad v_{tki} \le v_{\max}\,u_{tki}, \quad p_{tki} \le L_k\,u_{tki}
$$
$$
a_{\min}\,u_{tki} \le a_{tki} \le a_{\max}\,u_{tki} \qquad \forall t, k, i
$$

---

## 6. Key Modeling Assumptions

1. **Discretized time horizon** — the planning horizon is divided into uniform intervals $\Delta$; segment occupancy, dwell, and speed are tracked per interval (assumption for linearity).
2. **Piecewise-linear energy** — energy is approximated by a convex combination over a fixed set of speed breakpoints $(v_b, e_b)$, keeping the model MILP-representable.
3. **Rerouting** — each train has a small set of routes $R_t$ (original + opposite-track alternative); the binary $z_{tr}$ selects one. Rerouting is only meaningful inside the disruption window.
4. **Bidirectional conflict** — when both trains use the same physical track on the same segment/interval, a big-M term relaxes the exclusion constraint if their routes differ.
5. **Big-M** — chosen large enough to deactivate constraints when the corresponding binary is zero.
6. **Cancellation** — a cancelled train has all activity variables forced to zero and incurs a fixed penalty $c_{cancel}$.
7. **Delay** — measured at the destination station relative to the scheduled arrival time; only positive deviations are penalized.
8. **Headway** — enforced only between same-direction trains via the ordering variable $w$; opposing trains are handled by constraint (14).

This formulation simultaneously optimizes **train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles**, yielding a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles under partial segment blockages.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Model Overview

A mixed-integer linear program that jointly optimizes train timetables and speed profiles on a high-speed rail line under a partial segment blockage. For each train the model decides whether to cancel, reroute, or continue on its nominal path; when it runs, it selects a discrete speed level per segment, sets arrival/departure times, and orders trains to maintain safety headways. The objective trades off passenger delay, traction energy, and cancellation penalties.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of segments, indexed $s = 1,\dots,|S|$; segment $s$ connects station $s$ and $s+1$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed $k$ |
| $B \subseteq S$ | Set of blocked segments (disruption area) |
| $W = [t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window |

Each train $i$ has a direction $d_i \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$.

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ |
| $v_k$ | Speed associated with level $k$ |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum allowable speed |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration |
| $t_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}, t_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time |
| $t_{\text{headway}}$ | Minimum safety headway |
| $t_{\text{setup}}$ | Track switching/setup time for rerouting |
| $E_k$ | Energy per unit distance at speed level $k$ |
| $d_i^s$ | Nominal (scheduled) arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}, w_{\text{cancel}}$ | Objective weights |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $r_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $s$ |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $o_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $v_{i,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $s$ |
| $z_{i,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ transitions from level $k-1$ to level $k$ at segment boundary |
| $\text{delay}_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $e_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Energy of train $i$ on segment $s$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \text{delay}_{i,s}
\;+\; w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} e_{i,s}
\;+\; w_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in T} c_i
$$

The first term penalizes cumulative passenger delay; the second penalizes traction energy; the third penalizes cancellations. Weights let the dispatcher trade off service quality vs. energy vs. service coverage.

---

## 6. Constraints

### (C1) Delay definition
$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge x_{i,s} - d_i^s \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (C2) Dwell time
$$
y_{i,s} - x_{i,s} \ge t_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}\,(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
y_{i,s} - x_{i,s} \le t_{\text{dwell}}^{\max} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (C3) Running time / speed-profile coupling
$$
x_{i,s+1} - y_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} \frac{L_s}{v_k}\, v_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (C4) Speed-level selection
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,s,k} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (C5) Speed feasibility (acceleration/deceleration limits)
Let $\Delta v_k = v_k - v_{k-1}$. Transition variables $z_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$ with $z_{i,s,k} = 1$ iff train $i$ switches from level $k-1$ on segment $s-1$ to level $k$ on segment $s$:
$$
z_{i,s,k} \ge v_{i,s,k} + v_{i,s-1,k-1} - 1
$$
$$
z_{i,s,k} \le v_{i,s,k},\quad z_{i,s,k} \le v_{i,s-1,k-1}
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \Delta v_k\, z_{i,s,k} \le a_{\max}\, \Delta t \quad \text{(acceleration)}
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} (-\Delta v_k)\, z_{i,s,k} \le b_{\max}\, \Delta t \quad \text{(deceleration)}
$$
where $\Delta t$ is the discretization time step.

### (C6) Energy
$$
e_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} E_k\, L_s\, v_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (C7) Rerouting on blocked segments
For $s \in B$ and trains affected during $W$:
$$
r_{i,s} + c_i \ge 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in B
$$
i.e., a train must either reroute or be cancelled on a blocked segment.

### (C8) Rerouting conflict (bidirectional shared track)
For any pair $i \ne j$ on segment $s$ where at least one is rerouted:
$$
x_{j,s} \ge y_{i,s} + t_{\text{headway}} + t_{\text{setup}}(r_{i,s} + r_{j,s}) - M(1 - o_{i,j,s})
$$
$$
x_{i,s} \ge y_{j,s} + t_{\text{headway}} + t_{\text{setup}}(r_{i,s} + r_{j,s}) - M\, o_{i,j,s}
$$

### (C9) Ordering constraints (same direction)
$$
x_{j,s} \ge y_{i,s} + t_{\text{headway}} - M(1 - o_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall i \ne j,\; s
$$

### (C10) Ordering antisymmetry
$$
o_{i,j,s} + o_{j,i,s} = 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j,\; s
$$

### (C11) Cancellation linking
If $c_i = 1$, the train contributes no delay or energy:
$$
x_{i,s} \le M(1 - c_i) + d_i^s, \qquad y_{i,s} \le M(1 - c_i) + d_i^s
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \le M(1 - c_i), \qquad e_{i,s} \le M(1 - c_i)
$$

### (C12) Disruption window
For $s \in B$, trains cannot traverse in the nominal direction during $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$:
$$
y_{i,s} \le t_{\text{start}} + M(1 - r_{i,s}) \quad \text{or} \quad x_{i,s+1} \ge t_{\text{end}} - M(1 - r_{i,s})
$$
(implemented as a disjunction via big-M).

### (C13) Domains
$$
x_{i,s}, y_{i,s}, \text{delay}_{i,s}, e_{i,s} \ge 0
$$
$$
r_{i,s}, c_i, o_{i,j,s}, v_{i,s,k}, z_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Delay variables** capture lateness relative to the nominal timetable; penalized linearly, standard for passenger-delay minimization.
- **Dwell constraints** ensure realistic station stops; cancellation relaxes the minimum dwell.
- **Speed-profile coupling (C3)** is the core link between timetable and speed: travel time on a segment equals $L_s / v_k$ for the chosen level, making the timetable *executable* rather than a pure abstraction.
- **Speed-level selection (C4)** forces exactly one level per segment unless the train is cancelled.
- **Acceleration/deceleration (C5)** prevents physically infeasible jumps between consecutive speed levels.
- **Energy (C6)** is linear in the speed-level choice, giving a tractable surrogate for traction energy.
- **Rerouting (C7–C8)** models use of the opposite track on blocked segments, with setup time and headway penalty for bidirectional operation.
- **Ordering (C9–C10)** enforces safety separation between trains sharing a track via the standard big-M disjunctive formulation.
- **Cancellation (C11)** removes a train from the schedule without breaking linearity.
- **Disruption window (C12)** encodes the temporal restriction on blocked segments.
- **Objective weights** allow scenario-specific trade-offs (e.g., prioritize punctuality during peak hours, energy during off-peak).

---

## 8. Assumptions

1. Discrete speed levels approximate continuous speed profiles.
2. Energy is linear in speed level per unit distance.
3. Headway is constant across segments.
4. Dwell time bounds are uniform across stations.
5. Rerouting is only allowed on blocked segments.
6. Trains are identical in dynamics.

---

## 9. Model Size and Solvability

- **Binary variables:** $O(|T| \cdot |S| \cdot |K|)$ for $v$, plus $O(|T|^2 \cdot |S|)$ for $o$, plus $O(|T| \cdot |S|)$ for $r$ and $O(|T|)$ for $c$.
- **Continuous variables:** $O(|T| \cdot |S|)$.
- **Constraints:** $O(|T|^2 \cdot |S| + |T| \cdot |S| \cdot |K|)$.

For realistic instances (tens of trains, tens of segments, ~5–10 speed levels), the model is solvable by commercial MILP solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) within minutes, and by decomposition or rolling-horizon heuristics for larger networks.

Text:
# A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure-Aware Shunting

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

The following assumptions are made (some are explicit in the problem description, others are reasonable additions marked as *[assumption]*):

1. The timetable is given; each **trip** $t \in T$ has a fixed departure and arrival station and time. Trips may be cancelled at a penalty.
2. Rolling stock is composed of **unit types** $k \in K$; each type has a fixed capacity and length. Compositions are formed by coupling units of the same type (as in Fioole et al., 2006).
3. A **composition** is characterized by the number of units of each type assigned to a trip. Coupling/uncoupling is only allowed at stations where the original plan allows it, and only within a time window. *[assumption]*
4. Shunting movements occur at a set of **stations** $S$ (in the motivating case: Utrecht Centraal and Rotterdam Centraal). Each station has a set of **tracks** $R_s$.
5. Each shunting movement $m \in M$ is an **event** occupying one track $r \in R_s$ during a time interval $[a_m, d_m]$. *[assumption: durations are derived from the composition model's coupling/uncoupling times]*
6. Tracks can host at most one shunting movement at a time (exclusive occupation). *[assumption]*
7. Passenger trains may be **delayed** by at most $\Delta^{\max}$ minutes (a few minutes) to open shunting windows; these delays are absorbed by timetable buffers. *[assumption, explicitly stated in the paper]*
8. The **original plan** is known and used as a reference for the "stick-to-the-plan" objective.
9. Rolling stock units are interchangeable within a type; unit-level identities are not tracked beyond type and count. *[assumption]*
10. The planning horizon is a single disruption day; all movements must be completed before end of horizon. *[assumption]*

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of train trips |
| $K$ | Set of rolling stock unit types |
| $S$ | Set of stations where shunting is considered |
| $R_s$ | Set of tracks at station $s$ |
| $M$ | Set of potential shunting movements |
| $M_s \subseteq M$ | Shunting movements at station $s$ |
| $M_t \subseteq M$ | Shunting movements associated with trip $t$ (before/after) |
| $E$ | Set of ordered pairs $(m, m')$ of shunting movements that could conflict in time |
| $T^{\text{cancel}}$ | Subset of trips that may be cancelled |
| $T^{\text{fix}}$ | Subset of trips that must be operated |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $c^{\text{op}}_k$ | Operating cost per unit of type $k$ per trip |
| $c^{\text{cap}}_k$ | Capacity (seats) of a unit of type $k$ |
| $c^{\text{cancel}}_t$ | Penalty for cancelling trip $t$ |
| $c^{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty per minute of delay |
| $c^{\text{dev}}$ | Penalty per unit of deviation from the original composition |
| $p_t$ | Expected number of passengers on trip $t$ |
| $n^{\text{orig}}_{t,k}$ | Number of type-$k$ units in the original composition of trip $t$ |
| $n^{\max}_{t,k}$ | Maximum number of type-$k$ units allowed on trip $t$ |
| $n^{\min}_{t}$ | Minimum number of units required on trip $t$ (if operated) |
| $u^{\text{init}}_{s,k}$ | Initial number of type-$k$ units available at station $s$ |
| $u^{\text{end}}_{s,k}$ | Target number of type-$k$ units at station $s$ at end of horizon |
| $a_m, d_m$ | Earliest start / latest end time of shunting movement $m$ |
| $\tau_m$ | Duration of shunting movement $m$ |
| $\Delta^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed delay (minutes) |
| $L_r$ | Length of track $r$ |
| $\ell_k$ | Length of a type-$k$ unit |
| $B$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ | Objective weights (operating, passenger, stick-to-plan, delay) |

## 4. Decision Variables

### Composition / rolling stock variables
- $x_{t,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of type-$k$ units assigned to trip $t$.
- $y_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is operated, 0 if cancelled.
- $z_{t,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: deviation $|x_{t,k} - n^{\text{orig}}_{t,k}|$ (linearized).
- $w_{m} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ is performed.
- $f_{m,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of type-$k$ units moved in shunting movement $m$.

### Infrastructure variables
- $\sigma_{m,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ is assigned to track $r$.
- $s_m \ge 0$: start time of shunting movement $m$.
- $e_m \ge 0$: end time of shunting movement $m$ ($e_m = s_m + \tau_m$).
- $\delta_t \ge 0$: delay (minutes) of passenger train trip $t$.
- $\theta_{m,m'} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable for conflicting movements $m, m'$ on the same track.

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of four terms:

$$
\min \; \alpha \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{k \in K} c^{\text{op}}_k\, x_{t,k}}_{\text{operating cost}}
\;+\; \beta \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} c^{\text{cancel}}_t (1 - y_t)}_{\text{cancellations}}
\;+\; \gamma \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{k \in K} c^{\text{dev}}\, z_{t,k}}_{\text{stick-to-plan}}
\;+\; \delta \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} c^{\text{delay}}\, \delta_t}_{\text{delay penalty}}
$$

Additionally, a **passenger service-level** term can be included by penalizing under-capacity:

$$
+ \; \beta' \sum_{t \in T} \max\!\Big(0,\; p_t - \sum_{k \in K} c^{\text{cap}}_k x_{t,k}\Big)
$$

which is linearized with auxiliary variables $q_t \ge p_t - \sum_k c^{\text{cap}}_k x_{t,k}$, $q_t \ge 0$, and penalty $\beta' q_t$ in the objective. *[assumption: linear penalty for unmet demand]*

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Composition constraints

**(C1) Trip operation and minimum composition.**
$$
n^{\min}_t\, y_t \;\le\; \sum_{k \in K} x_{t,k} \;\le\; \Big(\sum_{k \in K} n^{\max}_{t,k}\Big) y_t
\qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Fixed trips must operate.**
$$
y_t = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T^{\text{fix}}
$$

**(C3) Type-specific upper bounds.**
$$
x_{t,k} \le n^{\max}_{t,k}\, y_t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

**(C4) Deviation linearization.**
$$
z_{t,k} \ge x_{t,k} - n^{\text{orig}}_{t,k}, \qquad
z_{t,k} \ge n^{\text{orig}}_{t,k} - x_{t,k}
\qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### 6.2 Rolling stock balance constraints

**(C5) Flow conservation at each station and time.**
For each station $s \in S$, type $k \in K$, and each event index $\nu$ in the ordered sequence of arrivals/departures at $s$:

$$
u^{\text{init}}_{s,k} + \sum_{t \in \text{arr}(s,\nu)} x_{t,k} + \sum_{m \in \text{in}(s,\nu)} f_{m,k}
\;=\;
\sum_{t \in \text{dep}(s,\nu)} x_{t,k} + \sum_{m \in \text{out}(s,\nu)} f_{m,k}
$$

where $\text{arr}(s,\nu)$ / $\text{dep}(s,\nu)$ are trips arriving/departing at station $s$ up to event $\nu$, and $\text{in}/\text{out}(s,\nu)$ are shunting movements entering/leaving the station's shunting area up to event $\nu$. *[assumption: event-based balance, standard in composition models]*

**(C6) End-of-horizon balance.**
$$
u^{\text{init}}_{s,k} + \sum_{t \in \text{arr}(s)} x_{t,k} - \sum_{t \in \text{dep}(s)} x_{t,k} \;\ge\; u^{\text{end}}_{s,k}
\qquad \forall s \in S,\; k \in K
$$

### 6.3 Shunting movement constraints

**(C7) Movement–trip coupling.** A shunting movement $m$ can only be performed if the associated trip(s) are operated:
$$
w_m \le y_t \qquad \forall m \in M_t,\; t \in T
$$

**(C8) Movement flow consistency.** Number of units moved equals the change in composition:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} f_{m,k} = \Big| \sum_{k \in K} x_{t^{+}(m),k} - \sum_{k \in K} x_{t^{-}(m),k} \Big|
\qquad \forall m \in M
$$
and $f_{m,k} \le B\, w_m$ for all $m, k$. *[assumption: movements correspond to composition changes]*

**(C9) Track assignment.** Each performed movement is assigned to exactly one track at its station:
$$
\sum_{r \in R_s} \sigma_{m,r} = w_m \qquad \forall s \in S,\; m \in M_s
$$

**(C10) Track length feasibility.**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \ell_k\, f_{m,k} \;\le\; \sum_{r \in R_s} L_r\, \sigma_{m,r}
\qquad \forall s \in S,\; m \in M_s
$$

### 6.4 Infrastructure / timing constraints

**(C11) Movement start and end times.**
$$
s_m \ge a_m\, w_m, \qquad e_m = s_m + \tau_m\, w_m \qquad \forall m \in M
$$

**(C12) No-overlap on the same track.** For each pair $(m, m') \in E$ with $m \neq m'$ and any common station:
$$
s_{m'} \ge e_m - B\,(1 - \theta_{m,m'}) - B\,(2 - \sigma_{m,r} - \sigma_{m',r})
$$
$$
s_{m} \ge e_{m'} - B\,\theta_{m,m'} - B\,(2 - \sigma_{m,r} - \sigma_{m',r})
$$
for all $r \in R_s$. This enforces that two movements on the same track are ordered in time.

**(C13) Delay bounds.**
$$
0 \le \delta_t \le \Delta^{\max} \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C14) Delay–shunting interaction.** *[assumption: a delayed train frees its track later, so shunting can start after the delayed departure]*
$$
s_m \ge \big(\text{departure time of conflicting train}\big) + \delta_t - B(1 - w_m)
\qquad \forall (m,t) \in \text{Conflict}
$$

### 6.5 Integrality and bounds

$$
x_{t,k}, f_{m,k}, z_{t,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}, \quad
y_t, w_m, \sigma_{m,r}, \theta_{m,m'} \in \{0,1\}, \quad
s_m, e_m, \delta_t \ge 0
$$

## 7. Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \alpha \sum_{t,k} c^{\text{op}}_k x_{t,k} + \beta \sum_t c^{\text{cancel}}_t (1-y_t) + \gamma \sum_{t,k} c^{\text{dev}} z_{t,k} + \delta \sum_t c^{\text{delay}} \delta_t + \beta' \sum_t q_t \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)–(C14)} \\
& x_{t,k}, f_{m,k}, z_{t,k}, q_t \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\; y_t, w_m, \sigma_{m,r}, \theta_{m,m'} \in \{0,1\},\; s_m, e_m, \delta_t \ge 0
\end{aligned}}
$$

## 8. Relation to the Two Solution Approaches

- **Exact (Combinatorial Benders') approach:** Solve the MILP above with all constraints. When the infrastructure subproblem (C9)–(C14) is infeasible for a given set of $w_m$, generate a **Benders cut** prohibiting that combination:
$$
\sum_{m \in \mathcal{M}^+} w_m - \sum_{m \in \mathcal{M}^-} w_m \;\le\; |\mathcal{M}^+| - 1
$$
where $\mathcal{M}^+$ is the set of movements active in the infeasible combination. Add the cut and re-solve.

- **Iterative heuristic:** Solve the composition model (C1)–(C8) first, then feed movements one by one to the infrastructure model (C9)–(C14). If a movement is infeasible, fix $w_m = 0$ and re-solve the composition model. This mimics the rolling-stock-dispatcher / infrastructure-dispatcher interaction.

Both approaches use the **same MILP structure**, differing only in how the infrastructure feasibility check is invoked and how cuts or fixes are generated.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a **partial segment blockage** occurs on one track of a double-track segment during a known disruption time window. Trains may be **rerouted** onto the opposite track within the disruption window, creating bidirectional traffic on a single track. We jointly optimize train **retiming, reordering, rerouting, and speed profiles**.

### Assumptions (marked as such where not directly given)

- **(A1)** The line is discretized into a set of **segments** $e \in \mathcal{E}$ between consecutive stations, and each segment is further discretized into **positions** $p \in \mathcal{P}_e$ (fine spatial grid) to represent speed profiles.
- **(A2)** Each segment has two tracks (directions $d \in \{+,-\}$); during the disruption window, one track is blocked, so trains in the blocked direction may use the opposite track (rerouting).
- **(A3)** Train speed is piecewise-constant over position intervals; acceleration/deceleration limits are respected between consecutive positions.
- **(A4)** Dwell times at stations are bounded within $[\underline{d}_i, \overline{d}_i]$ for train $i$.
- **(A5)** Headway (safety) constraints apply between consecutive trains on the same track in the same direction, and between opposing trains on a shared (rerouted) track.
- **(A6)** Energy consumption is approximated as a linear function of traction force (or speed increments) over the discretized profile.
- **(A7)** All trains must complete their journeys; cancellations are not considered (reasonable simplification; can be relaxed).
- **(A8)** The disruption window $[T^{\text{start}}_e, T^{\text{end}}_e]$ on segment $e$ is known and fixed.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_e$ | Set of discretized positions in segment $e$, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{+,-\}$ | Set of directions |
| $\mathcal{E}^{\text{dis}} \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | Segments affected by the disruption |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $t$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetabling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $e$ (uses opposite track) |
| $y_{i,j,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$ (ordering) |
| $z_{i,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ during the disruption window |

### 3.2 Speed Profile Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $v_{i,e,p}$ | Continuous | Speed of train $i$ at position $p$ on segment $e$ |
| $u_{i,e,p}$ | Continuous | Traction/braking control (acceleration) of train $i$ at position $p$ on segment $e$ |
| $\tau_{i,e,p}$ | Continuous | Time at which train $i$ reaches position $p$ on segment $e$ |

### 3.3 Auxiliary Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\delta_{i,j,e}$ | Binary | 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ use the same track on segment $e$ in conflicting directions |
| $E_i$ | Continuous | Total energy consumption of train $i$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay and total energy consumption:

$$
\min \quad \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s} \right)^+ + \beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} E_i
$$

where $(\cdot)^+ = \max(0, \cdot)$ is linearized via auxiliary variables $\Delta_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}$, $\Delta_{i,s} \geq 0$. Thus:

$$
\min \quad \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \Delta_{i,s} + \beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} E_i
$$

- $\alpha, \beta \geq 0$: weights balancing delay vs. energy (assumption: chosen by operator).
- $a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}$: scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Constraints

**(C1) Arrival–Departure Linking (Dwell Time):**

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \geq \underline{d}_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \leq \overline{d}_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C2) Segment Running Time Linking:**

For each train $i$ and segment $e = (s, s')$:

$$
a_{i,s'} - d_{i,s} = \tau_{i,e,|\mathcal{P}_e|} - \tau_{i,e,1}
$$

**(C3) Minimum Running Time (Physical Feasibility):**

$$
a_{i,s'} - d_{i,s} \geq T^{\min}_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \, e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C4) Delay Definition (Linearization):**

$$
\Delta_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}, \quad \Delta_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

---

### 5.2 Speed Profile Constraints

**(C5) Speed–Position–Time Dynamics (Discretized Kinematics):**

For consecutive positions $p, p+1$ in segment $e$:

$$
\tau_{i,e,p+1} = \tau_{i,e,p} + \frac{\Delta x_e}{\bar{v}_{i,e,p}}, \quad \forall i, e, p
$$

where $\bar{v}_{i,e,p} = \frac{v_{i,e,p} + v_{i,e,p+1}}{2}$ (average speed), and $\Delta x_e$ is the position step length. This is linearized via:

$$
\tau_{i,e,p+1} \geq \tau_{i,e,p} + \frac{2 \Delta x_e}{v_{i,e,p} + v_{i,e,p+1}}
$$

**(Assumption: linearization via tangent/outer approximation or piecewise-linear approximation of $1/v$.)**

**(C6) Speed Limits:**

$$
0 \leq v_{i,e,p} \leq V^{\max}_{e}, \quad \forall i, e, p
$$

**(C7) Acceleration/Braking Limits:**

$$
-a^{\max} \leq \frac{v_{i,e,p+1} - v_{i,e,p}}{\Delta t_{i,e,p}} \leq a^{\max}, \quad \forall i, e, p
$$

where $\Delta t_{i,e,p} = \tau_{i,e,p+1} - \tau_{i,e,p}$.

**(C8) Boundary Speed Conditions:**

$$
v_{i,e,1} = v^{\text{entry}}_{i,e}, \quad v_{i,e,|\mathcal{P}_e|} = v^{\text{exit}}_{i,e}
$$

(Assumption: entry/exit speeds are determined by station stop or pass-through conditions.)

---

### 5.3 Energy Consumption

**(C9) Energy as Function of Traction:**

$$
E_i = \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_e} \left( F^{\text{trac}}_{i,e,p} \cdot \Delta x_e \right), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}
$$

where $F^{\text{trac}}_{i,e,p} \geq 0$ is traction force, related to acceleration via:

$$
F^{\text{trac}}_{i,e,p} - F^{\text{brake}}_{i,e,p} = m_i \cdot u_{i,e,p} + R(v_{i,e,p})
$$

with $R(v)$ a linearized resistance function (assumption: piecewise-linear).

**(C10) Linearized Energy (Simplified):**

$$
E_i \geq \sum_{e,p} \kappa \cdot \left( v_{i,e,p+1} - v_{i,e,p} \right)^+ \cdot \Delta x_e
$$

(Assumption: energy proportional to positive speed increments; $\kappa$ is a constant.)

---

### 5.4 Rerouting and Conflict Constraints

**(C11) Rerouting Indicator:**

$$
x_{i,e} = 1 \implies \text{train } i \text{ uses opposite track on segment } e
$$

$$
x_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \, e \in \mathcal{E}^{\text{dis}}
$$

$$
x_{i,e} = 0, \quad \forall e \notin \mathcal{E}^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C12) Disruption Window Traversal:**

$$
z_{i,e} = 1 \iff \left[ \tau_{i,e,1}, \tau_{i,e,|\mathcal{P}_e|} \right] \cap \left[ T^{\text{start}}_e, T^{\text{end}}_e \right] \neq \emptyset
$$

Linearized as:

$$
\tau_{i,e,|\mathcal{P}_e|} \geq T^{\text{start}}_e - M(1 - z_{i,e})
$$
$$
\tau_{i,e,1} \leq T^{\text{end}}_e + M(1 - z_{i,e})
$$

**(C13) Rerouting Only During Disruption:**

$$
x_{i,e} \leq z_{i,e}, \quad \forall i, e \in \mathcal{E}^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C14) Bidirectional Conflict on Shared Track:**

If trains $i$ and $j$ use the same track in opposite directions on segment $e$:

$$
\delta_{i,j,e} = 1 \implies \text{conflict possible}
$$

$$
\delta_{i,j,e} \geq x_{i,e} + x_{j,e} - 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \, e \in \mathcal{E}^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C15) Headway Constraint (Same Direction):**

For trains $i, j$ in same direction on segment $e$:

$$
\left| \tau_{i,e,1} - \tau_{j,e,1} \right| \geq h^{\min}
$$

Linearized via ordering variable $y_{i,j,e}$:

$$
\tau_{j,e,1} - \tau_{i,e,1} \geq h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,e})
$$
$$
\tau_{i,e,1} - \tau_{j,e,1} \geq h^{\min} - M \cdot y_{i,j,e}
$$

**(C16) Headway Constraint (Opposite Direction, Shared Track):**

If $\delta_{i,j,e} = 1$:

$$
\left| \tau_{i,e,p} - \tau_{j,e,p} \right| \geq h^{\min}_{\text{opp}}, \quad \forall p \in \mathcal{P}_e
$$

Linearized similarly with big-M.

**(C17) No Simultaneous Opposite Direction on Same Track:**

$$
\delta_{i,j,e} \leq 1 - x_{i,e} + x_{j,e} + M(1 - z_{i,e}), \quad \text{(if both rerouted, they must be ordered)}
$$

---

### 5.5 Ordering and Routing Consistency

**(C18) Ordering Transitivity:**

$$
y_{i,j,e} + y_{j,i,e} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \, e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(C19) Rerouting Consistency Across Segments:**

$$
x_{i,e} = x_{i,e'}, \quad \forall e, e' \in \mathcal{E}^{\text{dis}} \text{ consecutive}
$$

(Assumption: rerouting decision is consistent along the disruption zone.)

---

### 5.6 Domain Constraints

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \tau_{i,e,p}, v_{i,e,p}, E_i \geq 0
$$
$$
x_{i,e}, y_{i,j,e}, z_{i,e}, \delta_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Complete MILP Formulation

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \Delta_{i,s} + \beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} E_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C19)} \\
& \text{Domain constraints}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Summary of Assumptions

| Assumption | Justification |
|------------|---------------|
| (A1) Spatial discretization | Standard for speed profile optimization |
| (A2) Double-track with rerouting | Matches partial blockage scenario |
| (A3) Piecewise-constant speed | Enables MILP linearization |
| (A4) Bounded dwell times | Realistic operational constraint |
| (A5) Headway constraints | Safety requirement |
| (A6) Linear energy approximation | Tractable MILP formulation |
| (A7) No cancellations | Simplification; can be relaxed |
| (A8) Known disruption window | Given by disruption scenario |

---

This MILP integrates **train rescheduling** (retiming, reordering, rerouting) and **speed management** (speed profiles, energy) into a single optimization framework, ensuring conflict-free bidirectional operations during partial segment blockages.

# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Among the three generated models, **Model 3** is the best: it is the most complete, correctly handles the disruption-window logic (including the subtle "crawling to hide from the window" loophole), and provides the clearest coupling between speed choice and the disruption window. Below is the finalized, complete linear MILP.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $S = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | Ordered set of stations/segments, indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $R = \{\text{normal}, \text{opposite}\}$ | Route options per segment, indexed by $r$ |
| $B \subseteq S$ | Set of blocked segments |
| $T^{up}, T^{down} \subseteq T$ | Trains by direction |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $d(t) \in \{\text{up},\text{down}\}$ | Direction of train $t$ |
| $a^0(t,s),\; dep^0(t,s)$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $\underline{dw}(t,s),\; \overline{dw}(t,s)$ | Min / max dwell time |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway (same or opposite direction) |
| $L(s)$ | Length of segment $s$ |
| $v(k)$ | Speed of level $k$; $v_{\min} \le v(k) \le v_{\max}$ |
| $rt(s,k) = L(s)/v(k)$ | Running time on segment $s$ at speed level $k$ |
| $e(k)$ | Traction energy coefficient at speed level $k$ |
| $[\tau_{\text{start}}, \tau_{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window |
| $C_{\text{cancel}}(t)$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $C_{\text{delay}}$ | Delay penalty per unit time |
| $w_E$ | Energy cost weight |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (time):**
$$a(t,s) \ge 0, \quad dep(t,s) \ge 0, \quad del(t,s) \ge 0$$

**Binary (routing / speed / cancellation / ordering):**
$$x(t,s,r) \in \{0,1\}, \quad y(t,s,k) \in \{0,1\}, \quad z(t) \in \{0,1\}, \quad o(t,t',s) \in \{0,1\}$$

**Auxiliary binaries (disruption-window indicators):**
$$\alpha(t,s) \in \{0,1\}, \quad \beta(t,s) \in \{0,1\}$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} C_{\text{cancel}}(t)\, z(t)}_{\text{cancellations}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S} C_{\text{delay}}\, del(t,s)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\; \underbrace{w_E \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K} e(k)\, y(t,s,k)\, L(s)}_{\text{traction energy}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Timetable consistency (dwell time)
$$
dep(t,s) \ge a(t,s) + \underline{dw}(t,s)\,(1 - z(t)) \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
dep(t,s) \le a(t,s) + \overline{dw}(t,s) + M\, z(t) \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C2) Running time between consecutive stations
$$
a(t,s+1) \ge dep(t,s) + \sum_{k \in K} rt(s,k)\, y(t,s,k) - M\, z(t) \qquad \forall t,\; s=1,\dots,N-1
$$

### (C3) Speed selection (exactly one level if not cancelled)
$$
\sum_{k \in K} y(t,s,k) = 1 - z(t) \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C4) Route selection (exactly one route if not cancelled)
$$
\sum_{r \in R} x(t,s,r) = 1 - z(t) \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C5) Disruption / rerouting on blocked segments

Define $\alpha(t,s)=1$ if train $t$ enters segment $s$ **before** $\tau_{\text{start}}$, and $\beta(t,s)=1$ if it enters **after** $\tau_{\text{end}}$. Linearize with big-M:

$$
dep(t,s) \le \tau_{\text{start}} + M\,(1-\alpha(t,s)) \qquad \forall t,\; s \in B
$$
$$
dep(t,s) \ge \tau_{\text{end}} - M\,(1-\beta(t,s)) \qquad \forall t,\; s \in B
$$

If the train traverses the blocked segment **inside** the window, it must use the opposite track:

$$
x(t,s,\text{normal}) \le \alpha(t,s) + \beta(t,s) + z(t) \qquad \forall t,\; s \in B
$$

Equivalently, when $\alpha=\beta=0$ and $z=0$, the normal route is forbidden.

### (C6) Headway — same direction (consecutive trains)

For $t,t'$ with $d(t)=d(t')$ and $t \neq t'$ on segment $s$:

$$
a(t',s+1) \ge a(t,s+1) + h_{\min} - M\big(1 - o(t,t',s)\big) - M\big(z(t)+z(t')\big)
$$

### (C7) Headway — opposite direction on shared (opposite) track

If both trains use the opposite track on segment $s$, enforce separation via ordering:

$$
a(t',s+1) \ge a(t,s+1) + h_{\min} - M\big(1 - o(t,t',s)\big) - M\big(2 - x(t,s,\text{opp}) - x(t',s,\text{opp})\big) - M\big(z(t)+z(t')\big)
$$

### (C8) Ordering antisymmetry (for conflicting pairs)

For each conflicting pair $(t,t')$ on segment $s$:

$$
o(t,t',s) + o(t',t,s) = 1
$$

### (C9) Delay definition

$$
del(t,s) \ge a(t,s) - a^0(t,s) \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
del(t,s) \ge 0 \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C10) Cancellation — remove train from timetable

$$
a(t,s) \le M\,(1 - z(t)), \quad dep(t,s) \le M\,(1 - z(t)) \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
del(t,s) \le M\,(1 - z(t)) \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C11) Speed–position–time consistency

Cumulative distance travelled must match the sum of segment lengths traversed at the chosen speed levels. For each train $t$ and station $s$:

$$
\sum_{s'=1}^{s-1} L(s') \cdot \big(1 - z(t)\big) \;=\; \sum_{s'=1}^{s-1}\sum_{k \in K} L(s')\, y(t,s',k)
$$

This is automatically satisfied by (C3); the timing link is enforced through (C2). To explicitly couple speed choice with the disruption window (so that a train cannot "wait out" the window by choosing an arbitrarily slow speed), add:

$$
dep(t,s) + \sum_{k \in K} rt(s,k)\, y(t,s,k) \le \tau_{\text{end}} + M\big(1 - \beta(t,s)\big) + M\, z(t) \qquad \forall t,\; s \in B
$$

### (C12) Domain and binary constraints

$$
a(t,s),\, dep(t,s),\, del(t,s) \ge 0
$$
$$
x(t,s,r),\, y(t,s,k),\, z(t),\, o(t,t',s),\, \alpha(t,s),\, \beta(t,s) \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

### Objective function
The three-term objective captures the three operational goals of the dispatcher:
1. **Cancellation penalty** — discourages removing trains from service.
2. **Delay penalty** — penalizes deviation from the published timetable at every station.
3. **Energy cost** — rewards energy-efficient speed profiles (lower $e(k)$ at moderate speeds), weighted by $w_E$ to trade off against punctuality.

### Timetable constraints (C1–C2)
Enforce realistic dwell times and running times. The running time is a *choice* via $y(t,s,k)$, so the model jointly selects speed and schedule. The $M z(t)$ term deactivates these constraints for cancelled trains.

### Routing and disruption (C4–C5)
On blocked segments, the normal track is unavailable during $[\tau_{\text{start}}, \tau_{\text{end}}]$. The binaries $\alpha, \beta$ detect whether a train passes before or after the window; if it must pass *through* the window, it is forced onto the opposite track. This is the core of the **rerouting** decision.

### Ordering and headway (C6–C8)
Because the opposite track is shared bidirectionally, trains from both directions may conflict. The ordering binary $o(t,t',s)$ decides who goes first, and the headway constraints enforce safe separation. Antisymmetry (C8) prevents cycles in the ordering.

### Delay and cancellation (C9–C10)
Delay is measured against the scheduled arrival. Cancellation is modeled by forcing all times to zero (or below $M$) and removing the train from speed/route selections via (C3)–(C4).

### Speed–position consistency (C11)
Ensures the chosen speed level is physically compatible with the segment length and the disruption window — a train cannot "hide" from the disruption by crawling.

### Big-M role
$M$ is chosen large enough to dominate any feasible time value (e.g., $M = \max_s \tau_{\text{end}} + \sum_s L(s)/v_{\min}$). It linearizes all logical implications (if-then) without introducing nonlinearities.

---

## 7. Model Summary

| Decision | Variable | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| Retiming | $a(t,s), dep(t,s)$ | C1, C2 |
| Reordering | $o(t,t',s)$ | C6–C8 |
| Rerouting | $x(t,s,r)$ | C4, C5 |
| Cancellation | $z(t)$ | C10 |
| Speed profile | $y(t,s,k)$ | C3, C11 |
| Delay | $del(t,s)$ | C9 |

The formulation is a **linear MILP**: all constraints are linear in the decision variables, binaries capture the discrete choices (route, speed, order, cancellation), and the objective is linear. It can be solved with standard branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP) for realistic instance sizes, or decomposed (e.g., Lagrangian relaxation on the headway constraints) for large networks.

---

## 8. Key Assumptions (marked)

1. **Discretized speed levels** — the continuous speed profile is approximated by a finite set $K$ of constant-speed levels per segment, which linearizes the energy–speed relationship $E \propto v^2$.
2. **Single disruption window** — one contiguous blockage $[\tau_{\text{start}}, \tau_{\text{end}}]$ on a fixed set of segments $B$.
3. **Fixed train set** — no new trains are introduced; only existing trains may be cancelled.
4. **Precomputed energy coefficients** $e(k)$ per speed level (traction energy per unit distance).
5. **Ordering binaries only for conflicting pairs** — created only for train pairs sharing a segment with overlapping time windows, keeping the model tractable.
6. **Big-M** chosen as $M = \max_s \tau_{\text{end}} + \sum_s L(s)/v_{\min}$ to dominate all feasible time values.

Text:
# A Complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

**(A1)** A single high-speed railway line is considered, consisting of a sequence of stations $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{1, 2, \dots, |\mathcal{S}|\}$ connected by segments $e \in \mathcal{E} = \{(s, s+1) : s \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\{|\mathcal{S}|\}\}$. Each segment is double-track (one track per direction) and is discretized into positions.

**(A2)** A disruption on segment $e^*\in\mathcal{E}$ blocks one track (one direction) during the disruption time window $[T^{\mathrm{start}}, T^{\mathrm{end}}]$. Trains normally assigned to the blocked direction may reroute onto the opposite track within this window.

**(A3)** When rerouting is invoked on $e^*$, both directions share a single track and are subject to **no-overtaking** and **headway** constraints (unidirectional capacity is preserved).

**(A4)** The set of trains $\mathcal{T}$ comprises trains scheduled in both directions. Trains cannot be overtaken within a segment (no in-segment overtaking in either normal or rerouting mode).

**(A5)** Train motion is modelled in a discrete time-position space with time step $\Delta t$ and position step $\Delta x$; the discrete kinematic relations are linear approximations of the true dynamics (mark as reasonable assumption).

**(A6)** Each train $i$ has a preferred (nominal) speed profile; deviations in running time with respect to the schedule are penalized. Acceleration and deceleration limits are $a^{\max}$, $b^{\max}$.

**(A7)** Trains cannot be cancelled (mark as reasonable assumption for a recovery-focused model); all trains must complete their journeys.

**(A8)** Dwell time at stations is bounded: $d_i^{\min} \le d_{i,s} \le d_i^{\max}$.

**(A9)** Energy consumption is approximated linearly from traction force and distance travelled; a piecewise-linear (PWL) surrogate of the tractive-effort curve is used (mark as reasonable assumption).

**(A10)** The planning horizon is $[0, H]$ discretized into $\mathcal{K} = \{0,1,\dots,K\}$ with $K = H/\Delta t$.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Stations, $s \in \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Segments, $e=(s,s+1)$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Trains, $i \in \mathcal{T}$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{+}_e / \mathcal{T}^{-}_e$ | Trains traversing segment $e$ in the +/− direction |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Time steps, $k \in \mathcal{K}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_e$ | Discretized positions in segment $e$, $p \in \mathcal{P}_e$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of disruption segments (here $|\mathcal{D}|=1$, $e^*$) |
| $\mathcal{M}$ | Speed-profile segments (PWL pieces) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Timetable / routing variables
- $x_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite (rerouted) track on segment $e$ (only meaningful for $e\in\mathcal{D}$).
- $y_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$ (**ordering variable**).
- $A_{i,s} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $D_{i,s} \ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$.
- $d_{i,s} \ge 0$: dwell time at station $s$, $d_{i,s} = D_{i,s} - A_{i,s}$.
- $r_{i,e} \ge 0$: running time of train $i$ in segment $e$, $r_{i,e} = A_{i,s+1} - D_{i,s}$.

### Speed-management variables
- $v_{i,e,p,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is at position $p$ in segment $e$ at time $k$.
- $u_{i,e,p} \ge 0$: speed of train $i$ at position $p$ in segment $e$ (km/h surrogate units).
- $f_{i,e,p} \ge 0$: traction/braking force at position $p$ in segment $e$.

### Auxiliary
- $\delta^{+}_{i}, \delta^{-}_{i} \ge 0$: positive/negative schedule deviation of train $i$ at final station.
- $\Delta_{i,s} \ge 0$: deviation at intermediate stations (used in objective).

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of schedule deviations, energy consumption, and rerouting cost:

$$
\min \; Z =
\underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} w^{\mathrm{del}}\,\Delta_{i,s}}_{\text{delay/deviation}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} w^{+}\delta^{+}_{i} + w^{-}\delta^{-}_{i}}_{\text{terminal deviation}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_e} w^{\mathrm{en}}\, f_{i,e,p}\,\Delta x}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{e\in\mathcal{D}} w^{\mathrm{re}}\, x_{i,e}}_{\text{rerouting cost}}
$$

with $w^{\mathrm{del}}, w^{+}, w^{-}, w^{\mathrm{en}}, w^{\mathrm{re}} \ge 0$ weighting factors.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable and precedence constraints

**Running-time / schedule consistency.**
$$
A_{i,s+1} - D_{i,s} = r_{i,e}, \qquad e=(s,s+1),\; \forall i \in \mathcal{T},
$$
$$
D_{i,s} - A_{i,s} = d_{i,s}.
$$

**Dwell-time bounds (A8).**
$$
d_i^{\min} \le d_{i,s} \le d_i^{\max}.
$$

**Running-time bounds (derived from speed-profile feasibility).**
$$
r_{i,e}^{\min} \le r_{i,e} \le r_{i,e}^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\, e \in \mathcal{E}.
$$

**Departure from first station and arrival at last station fixed (start/end of journey).**
$$
D_{i,s^{\mathrm{first}}_i} \ge D_{i}^{\mathrm{nom,first}}, \quad
A_{i,s^{\mathrm{last}}_i} = A_{i}^{\mathrm{nom,last}} + \delta^{+}_{i} - \delta^{-}_{i}.
$$

### 5.2 Disruption / rerouting constraints

**Direction and window indicator.**
$$
x_{i,e^*} = 0 \;\; \text{if train } i \text{ uses blocked direction and } r_{i,e^*} \notin [T^{\mathrm{start}},T^{\mathrm{end}}]
$$
is enforced via the linear constraint
$$
x_{i,e^*} \le 1 - \mathbb{1}\!\left[ A_{i,s} \ge T^{\mathrm{end}} \;\text{or}\; D_{i,s+1} \le T^{\mathrm{start}}\right].
$$

A tighter MILP form used in the model:
$$
A_{i,s+1} \le T^{\mathrm{start}} + M(1 - \xi^{-}_{i}) + M x_{i,e^*}, 
$$
$$
D_{i,s} \ge T^{\mathrm{end}} - M(1 - \xi^{+}_{i}) - M x_{i,e^*},
$$
where $\xi^{-}_{i}, \xi^{+}_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ indicate the train's normal operations finish before the window ($\xi^{-}$) or start after the window ($\xi^{+}$).

**Track-sharing constraint when rerouting (A3).**
If train $i$ and train $j$ use segment $e^*$ in opposite directions and one of them is rerouted, they cannot overlap in time:
$$
A_{j,s+1} - D_{i,s} \le M (1 - y_{i,j,e^*}) + M(1-x_{i,e^*}-x_{j,e^*}) , 
$$
$$
A_{i,s+1} - D_{j,s} \le M (1 - y_{j,i,e^*}) + M(1-x_{i,e^*}-x_{j,e^*}).
$$
These enforce that when both share the single track, one must fully clear segment $e^*$ before the other enters.

**No-overtaking in segment.** For trains using the same track in the same direction:
$$
y_{i,j,e} + y_{j,i,e} = 1, \qquad \forall e\in\mathcal{E}, \; i,j \in \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{dir}}_e, \; i\neq j.
$$

**Minimum headway (time and space) on the same track.**
$$
D_{j,s} - D_{i,s} \ge h^{\mathrm{dep}} y_{i,j,e} - M(1-x_{i,e}-x_{j,e})(1-\mathbf{1}[e=e^*]) .
$$

### 5.3 Position–time coupling constraints (linking timetable and speed profile)

**Unique position per time (binary activation).**
$$
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_e} v_{i,e,p,k} \le 1, \quad \forall i,e,k.
$$

**Position monotonicity along the train's traversal.**
$$
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_e} v_{i,e,p,k} \le \sum_{p'\in\mathcal{P}_e} v_{i,e,p',k+1} + M(1-z_{i,e,k}) ,
$$
where $z_{i,e,k}=1$ if train $i$ is inside segment $e$ at time $k$; outside $[D_{i,s}, A_{i,s+1}]$ the sum is zero:
$$
z_{i,e,k} = 0 \;\text{if } k\Delta t \le D_{i,s} \text{ or } k\Delta t \ge A_{i,s+1}.
$$

**Position–time consistency with station arrival/departure times.**
$$
\sum_{p \ge p^{\mathrm{end}}} \sum_{k \ge A_{i,s+1}/\Delta t} v_{i,e,p,k} = 1 \quad \text{(exit at arrival time)},
$$
$$
\sum_{p \le p^{\mathrm{start}}} \sum_{k \le D_{i,s}/\Delta t} v_{i,e,p,k} = 1 \quad \text{(entry at departure time)}.
$$

**Linearized kinematic relation (A5).**
$$
\Delta x \sum_{p} v_{i,e,p,k+1} - \Delta x \sum_{p} v_{i,e,p,k} \le u_{i,e}^{\max} \Delta t,
$$
$$
u_{i,e,p} \le u^{\max}\,\sigma_{i,e,p},\quad \sigma_{i,e,p} = \sum_k v_{i,e,p,k}.
$$

### 5.4 Speed-profile and energy constraints

**Speed limits per segment.** $0 \le u_{i,e,p} \le v^{\mathrm{lim}}_{i,e}$.

**Acceleration/braking (A6).**
$$
|u_{i,e,p+1} - u_{i,e,p}| \le a^{\max} \Delta x / u^{\min}_{\mathrm{eff}}.
$$

**Traction force (or energy proxy) bounds with PWL approximation (A9).**
$$
f_{i,e,p} = \sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}} \alpha_m u_{i,e,p} + \beta_m \lambda_{i,e,p,m}, \quad
\sum_m \lambda_{i,e,p,m}=1, \; \lambda_{i,e,p,m} \ge 0
$$
is the standard PWL (SOS2-like) representation of the tractive-effort curve.

**Kinetic/energy coupling with the timetable deviation:**
$$
\frac{1}{\eta}\sum_{p} f_{i,e,p}\Delta x \ge E^{\mathrm{nom}}_{i,e} - \kappa\, (r^{\mathrm{nom}}_{i,e} - r_{i,e}), \quad \forall i, e
$$
captures that slower running on segment $e$ (longer $r_{i,e}$) permits lower energy.

**Conflict-zone (disruption window) traversal constraint.**
If train $i$ traverses the disruption segment $e^*$ within $[T^{\mathrm{start}}, T^{\mathrm{end}}]$, it must satisfy the speed limit of the single-track operation:
$$
u_{i,e^*,p} \le \bar{u}^{\mathrm{dis}} \quad \text{for } k\in[k^{\mathrm{start}},k^{\mathrm{end}}],
$$
activated by a large-$M$ big-M with indicator $\phi_{i,k}$ for $k\Delta t \in [T^{\mathrm{start}}, T^{\mathrm{end}}]$.

### 5.5 Interval-based bidirectional conflict constraints (alternative equivalent tighter form)

Using disjunctive constraints linearized with $y_{i,j,e^*}$ and $x_{i,e^*}$:

$$
A_{i,s+1} \le D_{j,s} + M(1 - y_{i,j,e^*}),
$$
$$
A_{j,s+1} \le D_{i,s} + M\, y_{i,j,e^*}.
$$
These apply whenever $i,j$ share the same track (either both normal on same direction, or one rerouted), which is enforced through the "shared-track indicator":
$$
\sigma^{\mathrm{sh}}_{i,j,e} \ge x_{i,e} + x_{j,e} - 1, \quad \sigma^{\mathrm{sh}}_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}.
$$

### 5.6 Terminal deviation
$$
\delta^{+}_{i} - \delta^{-}_{i} = A_{i,s^{\mathrm{last}}_i} - A_{i}^{\mathrm{nom,last}}.
$$

### 5.7 Domain constraints
$$
A_{i,s}, D_{i,s}, r_{i,e}, d_{i,s}, u_{i,e,p}, f_{i,e,p} \ge 0,
$$
$$
x_{i,e}, y_{i,j,e}, v_{i,e,p,k}, \xi^{-}_{i}, \xi^{+}_{i}, \sigma^{\mathrm{sh}}_{i,j,e}, z_{i,e,k}, \lambda^{\mathrm{int}}_{i,e,p,m} \in \{0,1\}.
$$

---

## 6. Model Properties

- **Type:** Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP).
- **Size (order of magnitude):** $|\mathcal{T}|\cdot|\mathcal{S}|$ time variables; $|\mathcal{T}|\cdot|\mathcal{E}|\cdot|\mathcal{P}|\cdot|\mathcal{K}|$ binaries for the position–time grid; $|\mathcal{T}|^2\cdot|\mathcal{E}|$ ordering binaries.
- **Key coupling:** timetable variables $(A,D,r,d)$ appear both in the ordering/headway constraints and in the position–time linking constraints, which is what renders the model *integrated* rather than two independently solved problems.
- **Disruption handling:** through the rerouting binary $x_{i,e^*}$, the window indicators $(\xi^{-}_{i},\xi^{+}_{i})$, and the shared-track disjunctive constraints $\sigma^{\mathrm{sh}}_{i,j,e}$.

---

## 7. Note on the Decomposition (consistent with the paper's plan)

The MILP above can be decomposed by formally projecting out the per-train speed-profile block $\{(v,u,f)\}$ and replacing it, for each train $i$, by a finite set of candidate interval plans $\mathcal{Q}_i$ (each with an associated running time, energy, and position trajectories). Selecting one plan per train yields the **reformulated integer programming (IP)** model:

$$
\min \sum_{i}\sum_{q\in\mathcal{Q}_i} c_{i,q}\,\theta_{i,q} \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
\sum_{q\in\mathcal{Q}_i}\theta_{i,q} = 1, \quad
\text{and the precedence/window constraints linking } \theta \text{ across trains,}
$$

with $\theta_{i,q}\in\{0,1\}$. With sufficiently fine interval plans the IP is equivalent to the MILP — the equivalence criterion referenced in the introduction — and the adaptive iterative algorithm refines $\mathcal{Q}_i$ only in the neighbourhood of the previous IP solution (local branching + adaptive granularity).

---

### Assumptions marked as such
- **A5**: discrete linearized kinematics (the true dynamics are nonlinear).
- **A7**: no train cancellation.
- **A9**: PWL energy surrogate.
- A single-line, single-disruption setting is preserved for exposition; extension to multiple disruptions simply enlarges $\mathcal{D}$ and the corresponding window indicators.
