Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

The following assumptions are made (some are explicitly stated in the input; others are reasonable additions marked as **[A]**):

- **[A1]** The railway line is discretized into a set of segments (blocks) $\mathcal{S}$, each with a fixed length $L_s$ and a free-flow running time $T_s^{\text{free}}$.
- **[A2]** A disruption affects a subset of segments $\mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ during a time window $[t^{\text{dis,start}}, t^{\text{dis,end}}]$, blocking one track direction (partial blockage).
- **[A3]** During the disruption window, affected trains may reroute onto the opposite track (bidirectional sharing), subject to headway and safety constraints.
- **[A4]** Train speed profiles are approximated by a finite set of discrete speed levels $\mathcal{V} = \{v_1, \dots, v_K\}$ per segment, yielding a finite set of feasible segment running times $\mathcal{T}_s = \{\tau_{s,1}, \dots, \tau_{s,K}\}$.
- **[A5]** Acceleration/deceleration effects are captured via transition penalties between consecutive segments (energy and time).
- **[A6]** Dwell times at stations are decision variables bounded by $[d^{\min}, d^{\max}]$.
- **[A7]** Train cancellations are permitted with a penalty cost.
- **[A8]** The planning horizon is discretized into time steps $\mathcal{T} = \{0, 1, \dots, T^{\max}\}$.
- **[A9]** Energy consumption per segment is a linear function of the chosen speed level (piecewise-linear approximation of traction energy).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}$ | Set of disrupted segments, $\mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $v$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of time steps, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of directions, $\mathcal{D} = \{+1, -1\}$ (up/down) |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of routes (track assignments), indexed by $r$; $r \in \{\text{normal}, \text{reroute}\}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of feasible speed profiles for train $i$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling Variables (TRP)

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,k}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $k$ |
| $d_{i,k}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $k$ |
| $x_{i,s,v}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $s$ at speed level $v$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $s$ |
| $z_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\delta_{i,j,s}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $u_{i,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Entry time of train $i$ into segment $s$ |
| $w_{i,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Exit time of train $i$ from segment $s$ |

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables (TSMP)

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\tau_{i,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Actual running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $E_{i,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $\alpha_{i,s,v}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $v$ on segment $s$ (linked to $x_{i,s,v}$) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, cancellation penalty, and rerouting cost:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \left( \lambda^{\text{arr}} \cdot \max(0, a_{i,k} - A_{i,k}^{\text{sch}}) + \lambda^{\text{dep}} \cdot \max(0, d_{i,k} - D_{i,k}^{\text{sch}}) \right)}_{\text{Total delay}}
$$

$$
+ \underbrace{\lambda^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} E_{i,s}}_{\text{Energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{\lambda^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} z_i}_{\text{Cancellation penalty}}
+ \underbrace{\lambda^{\text{reroute}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}} y_{i,s}}_{\text{Rerouting cost}}
$$

where $A_{i,k}^{\text{sch}}$, $D_{i,k}^{\text{sch}}$ are scheduled arrival/departure times, and $\lambda^{\bullet} \geq 0$ are weighting coefficients.

**Linearization of delay terms** (introducing auxiliary variables $p_{i,k}, q_{i,k} \geq 0$):

$$
p_{i,k} \geq a_{i,k} - A_{i,k}^{\text{sch}}, \quad p_{i,k} \geq 0
$$
$$
q_{i,k} \geq d_{i,k} - D_{i,k}^{\text{sch}}, \quad q_{i,k} \geq 0
$$

Then the objective becomes:

$$
\min \; Z = \lambda^{\text{arr}} \sum_{i,k} p_{i,k} + \lambda^{\text{dep}} \sum_{i,k} q_{i,k} + \lambda^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,s} E_{i,s} + \lambda^{\text{cancel}} \sum_i z_i + \lambda^{\text{reroute}} \sum_{i,s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}} y_{i,s}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Consistency Constraints

**(C1) Arrival–departure linkage at stations:**

$$
d_{i,k} \geq a_{i,k} + d_{i,k}^{\min} \cdot (1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

$$
d_{i,k} \leq a_{i,k} + d_{i,k}^{\max} \cdot (1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**(C2) Segment traversal time consistency:**

$$
w_{i,s} = u_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C3) Station–segment linkage:**

$$
u_{i,s(k)} = d_{i,k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$
$$
a_{i,k+1} = w_{i,s(k)}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

where $s(k)$ denotes the segment departing from station $k$.

**(C4) Cancellation consistency:**

$$
a_{i,k} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad d_{i,k} \leq M(1 - z_i), \quad \forall i, k
$$

---

### 5.2 Speed Profile Selection Constraints

**(C5) Exactly one speed level per segment (if not cancelled):**

$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} x_{i,s,v} = 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C6) Running time determined by speed level:**

$$
\tau_{i,s} = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \tau_{s,v} \cdot x_{i,s,v}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C7) Energy consumption determined by speed level:**

$$
E_{i,s} = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} e_{s,v} \cdot x_{i,s,v}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $e_{s,v}$ is the energy consumed traversing segment $s$ at speed level $v$.

**(C8) Speed transition feasibility (acceleration/deceleration limits):**

$$
x_{i,s,v} + x_{i,s+1,v'} \leq 1, \quad \forall (v, v') \notin \mathcal{V}^{\text{feas}}
$$

where $\mathcal{V}^{\text{feas}}$ is the set of feasible consecutive speed-level pairs.

---

### 5.3 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

**(C9) Disrupted segment usage during disruption window:**

If train $i$ enters disrupted segment $s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}$ during $[t^{\text{dis,start}}, t^{\text{dis,end}}]$, it must reroute:

$$
u_{i,s} \geq t^{\text{dis,start}} - M(1 - y_{i,s}), \quad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
$$
$$
u_{i,s} \leq t^{\text{dis,end}} + M \cdot y_{i,s}, \quad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C10) Rerouting only on disrupted segments:**

$$
y_{i,s} = 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; s \notin \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C11) Rerouted trains use opposite track:**

$$
y_{i,s} \leq 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
$$

---

### 5.4 Conflict-Free Constraints (Bidirectional Sharing)

**(C12) Headway on same track (same direction):**

For trains $i, j$ on segment $s$ with the same route:

$$
u_{j,s} \geq w_{i,s} + h^{\text{same}}, \quad \text{if } \delta_{i,j,s} = 1
$$

Linearized:

$$
u_{j,s} \geq w_{i,s} + h^{\text{same}} - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,s}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s
$$

**(C13) Headway on shared track (opposite directions / rerouted):**

$$
u_{j,s} \geq w_{i,s} + h^{\text{opp}}, \quad \text{if } \delta_{i,j,s} = 1 \text{ and } y_{i,s} \neq y_{j,s}
$$

Linearized:

$$
u_{j,s} \geq w_{i,s} + h^{\text{opp}} - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,s}) - M|y_{i,s} - y_{j,s}|, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C14) Ordering variable consistency:**

$$
\delta_{i,j,s} + \delta_{j,i,s} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s
$$

**(C15) No overtaking within a segment:**

$$
\delta_{i,j,s} = \delta_{i,j,s'}, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; s, s' \text{ consecutive}
$$

---

### 5.5 Station Capacity Constraints

**(C16) Platform occupancy:**

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \mathbb{1}[a_{i,k} \leq t \leq d_{i,k}] \leq C_k^{\text{platform}}, \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \; t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

Linearized via binary occupancy variables $\sigma_{i,k,t}$:

$$
\sigma_{i,k,t} \geq \frac{a_{i,k} - t}{M} + 1, \quad \sigma_{i,k,t} \geq \frac{t - d_{i,k}}{M} + 1
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sigma_{i,k,t} \leq C_k^{\text{platform}}, \quad \forall k, t
$$

---

### 5.6 Time Window Constraints

**(C17) Earliest departure from origin:**

$$
d_{i,k^{\text{orig}}} \geq D_{i,k^{\text{orig}}}^{\text{sch}} - \Delta^{\text{early}}, \quad \forall i
$$

**(C18) Planning horizon:**

$$
0 \leq a_{i,k}, \; d_{i,k} \leq T^{\max}, \quad \forall i, k
$$

**(C19) Minimum running time:**

$$
\tau_{i,s} \geq \tau_s^{\min}, \quad \forall i, s
$$

**(C20) Maximum running time:**

$$
\tau_{i,s} \leq \tau_s^{\max}, \quad \forall i, s
$$

---

### 5.7 Variable Domain Constraints

$$
x_{i,s,v} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}, \quad z_i \in \{0,1\}, \quad \delta_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{i,k}, d_{i,k}, u_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, \tau_{i,s}, E_{i,s}, p_{i,k}, q_{i,k} \geq 0
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \lambda^{\text{arr}} \sum_{i,k} p_{i,k} + \lambda^{\text{dep}} \sum_{i,k} q_{i,k} + \lambda^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,s} E_{i,s} + \lambda^{\text{cancel}} \sum_i z_i + \lambda^{\text{reroute}} \sum_{i,s \in \mathcal{S}^{\text{dis}}} y_{i,s} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C20)} \\
& x_{i,s,v}, y_{i,s}, z_i, \delta_{i,j,s}, \sigma_{i,k,t} \in \{0,1\} \\
& a_{i,k}, d_{i,k}, u_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, \tau_{i,s}, E_{i,s}, p_{i,k}, q_{i,k} \geq 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Model Properties

- **Linearity:** All constraints and the objective are linear (big-$M$ linearizations used for disjunctive constraints).
- **Integrality:** Binary variables govern speed-level selection, rerouting, cancellation, and train ordering.
- **Coupling:** The model couples TRP (timing, ordering, routing) and TSMP (speed, energy) through constraints (C2), (C5)–(C7).
- **Conflict-free guarantee:** Constraints (C12)–(C15) ensure no two trains occupy the same track segment simultaneously without required headway, including bidirectional sharing during rerouting.
- **Solvability:** The MILP can be solved directly by branch-and-bound/cut for small instances; for large instances, the decomposition approach described in the input (IP reformulation + adaptive iterative algorithm + local branching) is recommended.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below we formulate a complete, linear mixed-integer programming (MILP) model inspired by the introduction. The model integrates train rescheduling (TRP) and train speed management (TSMP) under a partial segment blockage, allowing local rerouting (use of the opposite track within the disruption time window), retiming, reordering, and cancellation, while producing executable speed profiles.

All assumptions that are not explicitly stated in the input are marked **[A#]**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{o} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trains originally scheduled in the outbound (down) direction |
| $\mathcal{T}^{r} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trains originally scheduled in the return (up) direction |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations along the line, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of track segments (links) between consecutive stations, indexed by $l = (s, s+1)$ |
| $\mathcal{L}^{D} \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ | Segments affected by the partial blockage (disruption area) |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discretized speed levels (speed profile segments), indexed by $k$ **[A1]** |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of candidate speed profiles (plans) for train $i$ **[A2]** |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | Set of discretized time steps (e.g., 1 s or 15 s), indexed by $t$ **[A3]** |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of directions, $\mathcal{D} = \{+1, -1\}$ (nominal / opposite track) |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $T^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_{i,l}$ | Minimum running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $D_{i,s}$ | Maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h$ | Minimum safety headway (time separation) between two consecutive trains on the same track |
| $[t^{b}_{l}, t^{e}_{l}]$ | Disruption time window on segment $l \in \mathcal{L}^{D}$ |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $E_{i,p}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ under speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ |
| $c^{delay}$ | Unit cost of delay (per time unit) |
| $c^{cancel}$ | Cost of cancelling a train |
| $c^{energy}$ | Unit cost of energy consumption |
| $v^{max}_{i,l}$ | Maximum allowed speed of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $a^{max}_{i}, b^{max}_{i}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration of train $i$ |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a discretized time step |
| $\delta_{i,p,l}$ | Binary parameter: 1 if profile $p$ of train $i$ uses segment $l$ **[A2]** |
| $\tau_{i,p,l}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ under profile $p$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling variables

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,p}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is assigned speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ |
| $y_{i}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $a_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $w_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Actual dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\theta_{i,l}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $l$ (rerouting) |
| $\sigma_{i,j,l}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $l$ (ordering) |
| $\alpha_{i,l}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $l$ during the disruption window |
| $\beta_{i,l}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $l$ outside the disruption window |

### 3.2 Speed management variables

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $v_{i,l,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $l$ |
| $u_{i,l}$ | Continuous | Average speed of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $e_{i,l}$ | Continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $g_{i,l}$ | Continuous | Traction/braking effort indicator (linearized) |

### 3.3 Delay variables

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\delta^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Departure delay of train $i$ from station $s$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, cancellation cost, and energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = c^{delay} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \delta^{arr}_{i,s} + \delta^{dep}_{i,s} \right) + c^{cancel} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} y_i + c^{energy} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} e_{i,l}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train service and profile assignment

Each non-cancelled train must be assigned exactly one speed profile:

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_{i,p} + y_i = 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

### 5.2 Arrival / departure time propagation

For each train $i$ and segment $l = (s, s+1)$:

$$
a_{i,s+1} \geq d_{i,s} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_{i,p,l} \, x_{i,p} - M y_i, \quad \forall i, \; l=(s,s+1)
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} + w_{i,s} - M y_i, \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.3 Dwell time bounds

$$
d_{i,s} \leq w_{i,s} \leq D_{i,s}, \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.4 Delay definition

$$
\delta^{arr}_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - T^{arr}_{i,s} - M y_i, \quad \forall i, s
$$

$$
\delta^{dep}_{i,s} \geq d_{i,s} - T^{dep}_{i,s} - M y_i, \quad \forall i, s
$$

$$
\delta^{arr}_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \delta^{dep}_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.5 Disruption window and rerouting

For each segment $l \in \mathcal{L}^{D}$ and train $i$:

$$
\alpha_{i,l} + \beta_{i,l} = 1 - y_i, \quad \forall i, \; l \in \mathcal{L}^{D}
$$

If train $i$ traverses segment $l$ during the disruption window, it must reroute to the opposite track:

$$
\theta_{i,l} \geq \alpha_{i,l}, \quad \forall i, \; l \in \mathcal{L}^{D}
$$

Trains traversing outside the disruption window use the nominal track:

$$
\theta_{i,l} \leq \alpha_{i,l}, \quad \forall i, \; l \in \mathcal{L}^{D}
$$

For segments not affected by the disruption:

$$
\theta_{i,l} = 0, \quad \forall i, \; l \notin \mathcal{L}^{D}
$$

### 5.6 Disruption window timing

The traversal of segment $l$ by train $i$ is within the disruption window if:

$$
d_{i,s} \geq t^{b}_{l} - M(1 - \alpha_{i,l}), \quad \forall i, \; l=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{L}^{D}
$$

$$
a_{i,s+1} \leq t^{e}_{l} + M(1 - \alpha_{i,l}), \quad \forall i, \; l=(s,s+1) \in \mathcal{L}^{D}
$$

### 5.7 Bidirectional conflict resolution (headway on shared track)

For any two trains $i, j$ using the same track on segment $l$ (i.e., same direction or one rerouted):

$$
d_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s+1} + h - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,l}) - M(1 - \theta^{same}_{i,j,l}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; l=(s,s+1)
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s+1} + h - M \sigma_{i,j,l} - M(1 - \theta^{same}_{i,j,l}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; l=(s,s+1)
$$

where $\theta^{same}_{i,j,l}$ is an auxiliary binary indicating that $i$ and $j$ share the same physical track on segment $l$ **[A4]**:

$$
\theta^{same}_{i,j,l} \geq 1 - |\theta_{i,l} - \theta_{j,l}| - (y_i + y_j), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; l
$$

$$
\sigma_{i,j,l} + \sigma_{j,i,l} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; l
$$

### 5.8 Speed profile consistency

The average speed on segment $l$ is determined by the assigned profile:

$$
u_{i,l} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \bar{v}_{i,p,l} \, x_{i,p}, \quad \forall i, l
$$

where $\bar{v}_{i,p,l}$ is the average speed of profile $p$ on segment $l$.

Speed level selection:

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v_{i,l,k} = 1 - y_i, \quad \forall i, l
$$

$$
u_{i,l} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} V_k \, v_{i,l,k}, \quad \forall i, l
$$

### 5.9 Speed limits and acceleration constraints

$$
u_{i,l} \leq v^{max}_{i,l}, \quad \forall i, l
$$

$$
|u_{i,l+1} - u_{i,l}| \leq a^{max}_{i} \Delta t, \quad \forall i, l
$$

### 5.10 Energy consumption (linearized)

Energy consumption is approximated as a linear function of speed and traction effort:

$$
e_{i,l} \geq \kappa_1 u_{i,l} + \kappa_2 g_{i,l} - M(1 - x_{i,p}), \quad \forall i, l
$$

$$
g_{i,l} \geq u_{i,l} - u_{i,l-1}, \quad \forall i, l
$$

$$
g_{i,l} \geq u_{i,l-1} - u_{i,l}, \quad \forall i, l
$$

$$
e_{i,l} \geq 0, \quad g_{i,l} \geq 0, \quad \forall i, l
$$

where $\kappa_1, \kappa_2$ are linearization coefficients **[A5]**.

### 5.11 Running time consistency

The running time on segment $l$ must be consistent with the assigned speed profile:

$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \geq \frac{L_l}{u_{i,l}} - M(1 - x_{i,p}), \quad \forall i, \; l=(s,s+1)
$$

where $L_l$ is the length of segment $l$ **[A6]**.

### 5.12 Cancellation constraints

If train $i$ is cancelled, all its timing variables are set to zero:

$$
a_{i,s} \leq M(1 - y_i), \quad d_{i,s} \leq M(1 - y_i), \quad \forall i, s
$$

$$
x_{i,p} = 0, \quad \forall i, p, \; \text{if } y_i = 1
$$

### 5.13 Domain constraints

$$
x_{i,p}, y_i, \theta_{i,l}, \sigma_{i,j,l}, \alpha_{i,l}, \beta_{i,l}, v_{i,l,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, \delta^{arr}_{i,s}, \delta^{dep}_{i,s}, u_{i,l}, e_{i,l}, g_{i,l} \geq 0
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions

**[A1]** The speed profile is discretized into a finite set of speed levels $\mathcal{K}$ to enable linearization.

**[A2]** A finite set of candidate speed profiles $\mathcal{P}_i$ is precomputed for each train $i$, each associated with a running time and energy consumption on each segment.

**[A3]** Time is discretized into steps $\Delta t$ for the purpose of conflict detection and speed management.

**[A4]** The auxiliary variable $\theta^{same}_{i,j,l}$ captures whether two trains share the same physical track on a segment, accounting for rerouting and cancellation.

**[A5]** Energy consumption is approximated as a linear function of average speed and traction/braking effort, with coefficients $\kappa_1, \kappa_2$ derived from train dynamics.

**[A6]** The running time on a segment is approximated by the ratio of segment length to average speed; this is linearized via the profile assignment.

**[A7]** The disruption is modeled as a time window $[t^{b}_{l}, t^{e}_{l}]$ on affected segments $\mathcal{L}^{D}$, during which the nominal track is unavailable.

**[A8]** Rerouting is only allowed on affected segments and only during the disruption window.

**[A9]** The minimum headway $h$ is constant and applies to all trains on the same physical track.

**[A10]** All trains are identical in terms of safety and control characteristics unless otherwise specified.

---

## 7. Summary

This MILP model integrates:

- **Train rescheduling**: retiming, reordering, rerouting, and cancellation.
- **Speed management**: speed profile selection, speed limits, acceleration constraints, and energy consumption.
- **Bidirectional conflict resolution**: headway constraints on shared tracks, including rerouted trains.
- **Disruption handling**: time-window-based track unavailability and rerouting.

The model is linear (with big-M linearizations) and can be solved using standard MILP solvers or decomposed via the adaptive iterative algorithm described in the introduction.

Text:
# A MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below we construct a **complete, linear** mixed-integer program that closely follows the description in the introduction. The model simultaneously decides **retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation** (TRP) and **speed profiles** (TSMP) for a set of trains on a high-speed line during a **partial segment blockage** whose disruption time window is known a priori. When information is missing from the input, we state a **reasonable assumption (RA#)** and use it.

---

## 1. Problem Statement and Modeling Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed line with stations $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{1, 2, \ldots, S\}$ (ordered along the line) and **two tracks per segment** (one per direction) between consecutive stations. A disruption on segment $(\hat{s}, \hat{s}+1)$ blocks the nominal direction during a known time window $[T^{\text{d}}_{\text{start}}, T^{\text{d}}_{\text{end}}]$. Affected trains may be **rerouted** onto the opposite track, which must then be used **bidirectionally** in that window, creating additional conflicts.

Key decisions:
- Arrival/departure times at each station (retiming),
- Order of trains on each segment/track (reordering),
- Track usage (rerouting),
- Cancellation of trains,
- Continuous speed profiles satisfying the timetable and dynamics.

**Assumptions (marked where inferred):**
- **RA1:** Trains are a heterogeneous fleet; each train $i$ has a maximum speed $V_i^{\max}$, mass $M_i$, Davis coefficients $(a_i, b_i, c_i)$.
- **RA2:** Speed profiles are discretized on a fine position grid of spacing $\Delta x$ (e.g., 100 m) so that acceleration and energy are linear.
- **RA3 (from text):** For a partial blockage, the affected trains may use the **opposite track** in the disruption window; this is modeled as a rerouting decision.
- **RA4:** Block signalling is approximated by a **minimum headway time** $h_{\min}$ between two trains using the same track in the same direction, and a **safety separation** between opposite-direction trains on a shared track.
- **RA5:** Dwell times are bounded: $d_i^{\min} \le d_i^s \le d_i^{\max}$.
- **RA6:** The scheduling horizon $\mathcal{T} = \{0, \Delta t, 2\Delta t, \ldots, T^{\max}\}$ is discrete; $T^{\max}$ is fixed.
- **RA7:** Energy consumption is linear in tractive effort and velocity (piecewise-linearized if desired); regenerative braking is not credited (conservative).
- **RA8:** Segment travel time must be at least the time to traverse the segment at maximum speed; hence a lower bound $\underline{t}_{i,s}$.

---

## 2. Sets, Indices, and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | set of trains, $i \in \mathcal{I}$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | set of stations, $s \in \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | speed/position grid points, $k = 1,\dots,K$ on each segment |
| $\mathcal{D}_i$ | set of segments $\{1,\dots,S-1\}$ traversed by train $i$ |
| $\Delta x$ | spatial step (km) |
| $\Delta t$ | time step (h) |
| $V_i^{\max}$ | max speed of train $i$ (km/h) |
| $a_i^{\max}, a_i^{\min}$ | max accel / decel magnitudes (km/h²) |
| $d_i^{\min}, d_i^{\max}$ | min / max dwell time at any station (h) |
| $T_i^{s,\text{nom}}$ | nominal scheduled departure/arrival at station $s$ (h) |
| $\alpha_i$ | weight of delay (cost coefficient) |
| $\beta_i$ | weight of energy (cost coefficient) |
| $\gamma$ | penalty per cancellation (large) |
| $h_{\min}$ | minimum same-direction headway (h) |
| $h_{\text{opp}}$ | minimum opposite-direction separation (h) |
| $T^{\text{d}}_{\text{start}}, T^{\text{d}}_{\text{end}}$ | disruption window on segment $(\hat{s},\hat{s}+1)$ |
| $\mathcal{I}^{\text{aff}}$ | trains whose route uses $(\hat{s},\hat{s}+1)$ |
| $E_i(k)$ | energy rate coefficient at grid point $k$ (see §3.6) |
| $M$ | big-M constant |

**Binary parameters:**
- $\delta_i^{\text{dir}} = 1$ if train $i$ travels in the "nominal" direction on its path (most are); opposite-direction trains have $0$.
- Blockage indicator $\chi_{s} = 1$ if segment $s$ is inside the disruption window (for all $i$) — only segment $\hat{s}$.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Scheduling / routing binaries
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ **runs**, 0 if cancelled.
- $r_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ **reroutes** on segment $s$ (uses opposite track), 0 otherwise. By RA3, $r_{i,s} = 0$ for $s \ne \hat{s}$.
- $o_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ (same direction, same track).
- $\sigma_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ and train $j$ run in **opposite** directions on segment $s$ and $i$ enters first (used for shared-track separation).

### 3.2 Timing variables (continuous)
- $A_{i,s} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $D_{i,s} \ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$.
- $d_{i,s} \ge 0$: dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$: $d_{i,s} = D_{i,s} - A_{i,s}$.
- $t_{i,s} \ge 0$: running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ (between stations $s$ and $s+1$).
- $\Delta d_i^+ \ge 0$: positive delay of train $i$.
- $x_{i,k,s} \ge 0$: position of train $i$ at grid point $k$ on segment $s$ — actually we use speed instead.

### 3.3 Speed profile variables (continuous)
For each train $i$, segment $s$, grid point $k$:
- $v_{i,k,s} \ge 0$: speed (km/h) at grid point $k$.
- $u_{i,k,s} \ge 0$: control (tractive/braking) acceleration (km/h²).
- $e_{i,k,s} \ge 0$: energy consumed (kWh) at grid point $k$.

### 3.4 Auxiliary for ordering
- $z_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ and $j$ use the same track on segment $s$ in the same direction.

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of delay, energy, and cancellation:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \alpha_i \Delta d_i^{+}}_{\text{delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \beta_i \sum_{s \in \mathcal{D}_i} \sum_{k=1}^{K} e_{i,k,s}}_{\text{energy}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \gamma (1 - y_i)}_{\text{cancellations}}
\tag{1}
$$

**Rationale (from text):** "different speed profiles give rise to significant differences in energy consumption, thereby naturally establishing energy efficiency as an important co-optimization objective."

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train activation and cancellation

$$
A_{i,s} \le M \, y_i, \quad D_{i,s} \le M \, y_i \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{2}
$$

$$
A_{i,s}, D_{i,s} \ge 0
\tag{3}
$$

### 5.2 Timetable propagation (link arrival–departure–running time)

For each train $i$ and segment $s$ (between stations $s$ and $s+1$):

$$
A_{i,s+1} = D_{i,s} + t_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}, \; s \in \mathcal{D}_i
\tag{4}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} = D_{i,s} - A_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{5}
$$

$$
d_i^{\min} y_i \le d_{i,s} \le d_i^{\max} y_i \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{6}
$$


### 5.3 Segment running time bounds (link timetable to physics)

The running time $t_{i,s}$ must be at least the free-run time at maximum speed, and the speed profile must satisfy:

$$
t_{i,s} = \sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{\Delta x}{\bar{v}_{i,k,s}}\, \Delta t_{\text{unit}} \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad t_{i,s} \cdot \bar{v}_{i,k,s} \ge \Delta x \cdot \Delta t_{\text{unit}}
\tag{7}
$$

To **linearize**, we use a fixed-step formulation where speed at each step is approximated by an average over two consecutive grid points:

$$
t_{i,s} = \frac{K \Delta x}{K \cdot \bar{v}_{i,s}} \quad \text{(discretized)}, \qquad \bar{v}_{i,s} = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} v_{i,k,s}
\tag{8}
$$

**Linear form (using the well-known time–speed relation with small-step linearization):**

$$
t_{i,s} \ge \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} \cdot \frac{1}{v_{i,k,s}} \quad \text{is nonlinear, so we use:}
$$

**Linear alternative (from RA2, small-step):** introduce $T_{i,k,s}$ = time at grid point $k$:

$$
T_{i,k+1,s} = T_{i,k,s} + \frac{\Delta x}{v_{i,k,s}} \quad \text{(nonlinear)} \Rightarrow
$$

**Piecewise-linear (PWL) outer approximation:** let $\mathcal{V} = \{v^1, \ldots, v^L\}$ be breakpoints; define

$$
\lambda_{i,k,s}^l \ge 0, \quad \sum_l \lambda_{i,k,s}^l = 1, \quad
v_{i,k,s} = \sum_l \lambda_{i,k,s}^l v^l, \quad
\frac{1}{v_{i,k,s}} \approx \sum_l \lambda_{i,k,s}^l \frac{1}{v^l}
\tag{9}
$$

so that the segment traversal time constraint is linear:

$$
t_{i,s} = \Delta x \sum_{k=1}^{K} \sum_{l=1}^{L} \lambda_{i,k,s}^l \cdot \frac{1}{v^l}
\tag{10}
$$

Compatibility with the maximum speed:

$$
v_{i,k,s} \le V_i^{\max} y_i \qquad \forall i,s,k
\tag{11}
$$

At segment boundaries, speed must respect station stops (train must decelerate to 0 and accelerate from 0 if stopping). Let $\eta_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$ be a **parameter** indicating whether train $i$ stops at station $s$ (from nominal schedule, RA9):

$$
v_{i,1,s} \le V_i^{\max}(1 - \eta_{i,s}^{\text{start}}) + \epsilon, \qquad
v_{i,K,s} \le V_i^{\max}(1 - \eta_{i,s+1}^{\text{end}}) + \epsilon
\tag{12}
$$

### 5.4 Speed dynamics (linearized)

$$
v_{i,k+1,s} = v_{i,k,s} + u_{i,k,s} \cdot \frac{\Delta x}{\bar{v}_{i,k,s}} \quad \text{(nonlinear)} \Rightarrow
$$

**Small-step linearization:** if $\Delta x$ is small, $\frac{\Delta x}{\bar{v}} \approx \Delta \tau$ (fixed step), giving:

$$
v_{i,k+1,s} = v_{i,k,s} + u_{i,k,s} \, \Delta \tau_{i,k,s}
\tag{13}
$$

where $\Delta \tau_{i,k,s} = t_{i,s}/K$ is the per-step time (also a variable, but we linearize by treating $\Delta \tau$ as $t_{i,s}/K$):

$$
v_{i,k+1,s} = v_{i,k,s} + \frac{u_{i,k,s} \, t_{i,s}}{K}
\tag{14}
$$

This is bilinear; use **McCormick linearization** with $u_{i,k,s} \in [u^{\min}, u^{\max}]$ and $t_{i,s} \in [\underline{t}, \bar{t}]$:

$$
w_{i,k,s} = u_{i,k,s} \cdot t_{i,s}
$$
$$
w_{i,k,s} \ge u^{\min} t_{i,s} + \underline{t} u_{i,k,s} - u^{\min}\underline{t}
\tag{15a}
$$
$$
w_{i,k,s} \ge u^{\max} t_{i,s} + \bar{t} u_{i,k,s} - u^{\max}\bar{t}
\tag{15b}
$$
$$
w_{i,k,s} \le u^{\min} t_{i,s} + \bar{t} u_{i,k,s} - u^{\min}\bar{t}
\tag{15c}
$$
$$
w_{i,k,s} \le u^{\max} t_{i,s} + \underline{t} u_{i,k,s} - u^{\max}\underline{t}
\tag{15d}
$$

$$
v_{i,k+1,s} = v_{i,k,s} + \frac{w_{i,k,s}}{K}
\tag{16}
$$

Acceleration bounds:

$$
a_i^{\min} y_i \le u_{i,k,s} \le a_i^{\max} y_i \qquad \forall i,s,k
\tag{17}
$$

### 5.5 Energy consumption (linear)

Following RA7 (linear energy rate in tractive effort × speed):

$$
e_{i,k,s} \ge \rho_i \, u_{i,k,s} \, v_{i,k,s} \, \Delta \tau_{i,k,s} \quad \text{(nonlinear)} \Rightarrow
$$

**Linearization:** approximate the product $u_{i,k,s} v_{i,k,s}$ via McCormick and multiply by $\Delta x / v$; or use the standard linear form:

$$
e_{i,k,s} \ge \rho_i \left( M_i \, a_i + b_i v_{i,k,s} + c_i v_{i,k,s}^2 \right) \Delta x \cdot \frac{1}{v_{i,k,s}} \quad \text{(nonlinear)}
$$

**Simplified linear form (RA7, Davis linear in $v$):**

$$
e_{i,k,s} \ge \rho_i \, \Delta x \, M_i \, u_{i,k,s} + \rho_i \Delta x \, b_i + \rho_i \Delta x \, c_i \, v_{i,k,s}
\tag{18}
$$

If $u_{i,k,s} < 0$ (braking), we do not credit regenerative energy, so:

$$
e_{i,k,s} \ge 0, \quad e_{i,k,s} \ge \rho_i \Delta x \max(0, \ldots) \to e_{i,k,s} \ge \rho_i \Delta x (M_i u_{i,k,s} + b_i + c_i v_{i,k,s}), \quad e_{i,k,s} \ge 0
\tag{19}
$$

### 5.6 Delay definition and objective linearization

Let $\tilde{D}_i^{s}$ be the nominal scheduled departure time of train $i$ from its final station. The delay is:

$$
\Delta d_i^{+} \ge A_{i, s_i^{\text{end}}} - T_i^{s,\text{nom}} \qquad \forall i
\tag{20}
$$

$$
\Delta d_i^{+} \ge 0
\tag{21}
$$

### 5.7 Disruption: partial blockage and rerouting

Segment $\hat{s}$ is blocked in the nominal direction during $[T^{\text{d}}_{\text{start}}, T^{\text{d}}_{\text{end}}]$. Any train whose **occupation interval** on segment $\hat{s}$ in the nominal direction intersects this window must either be **rerouted** ($r_{i,\hat{s}}=1$) or forced to wait or cancel.

Let $O_{i,\hat{s}}$ be the occupation interval $[D_{i,\hat{s}}, A_{i,\hat{s}+1}]$. Constraint:

$$
\text{If } [D_{i,\hat{s}}, A_{i,\hat{s}+1}] \cap [T^{\text{d}}_{\text{start}}, T^{\text{d}}_{\text{end}}] \ne \emptyset \;\Rightarrow\; r_{i,\hat{s}} = 1 \text{ or } y_i = 0
\tag{22}
$$

**Linear version:** introduce $b_{i}^{\text{block}} \in \{0,1\}$ = 1 if the train's nominal-direction occupation overlaps the window:

$$
D_{i,\hat{s}} \le T^{\text{d}}_{\text{end}} + M(1 - b_{i}^{\text{block}})
\tag{23a}
$$
$$
A_{i,\hat{s}+1} \ge T^{\text{d}}_{\text{start}} - M(1 - b_{i}^{\text{block}})
\tag{23b}
$$
$$
b_{i}^{\text{block}} \le r_{i,\hat{s}} + (1 - y_i)
\tag{23c}
$$

Trains using the opposite track in the disruption window:

$$
r_{i,\hat{s}} = 0 \quad \forall i \notin \mathcal{I}^{\text{aff}}, \; s \ne \hat{s}
\tag{24}
$$

### 5.8 Bidirectional conflicts on the shared (opposite) track

On segment $\hat{s}$, if any train is rerouted, the opposite track is used bidirectionally. Let $\mathcal{I}_{\hat{s}}^{+}$ = nominal direction trains on $\hat{s}$, $\mathcal{I}_{\hat{s}}^{-}$ = opposite direction trains on $\hat{s}$.

For any pair $(i,j)$ with $i \in \mathcal{I}_{\hat{s}}^{+}$, $j \in \mathcal{I}_{\hat{s}}^{-}$ (or vice versa), and both rerouted/using the same physical track:

**Separation in time (opposite direction):**

$$
D_{j,\hat{s}} \ge A_{i,\hat{s}+1} + h_{\text{opp}} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,\hat{s}})
\tag{25a}
$$
$$
D_{i,\hat{s}} \ge A_{j,\hat{s}+1} + h_{\text{opp}} - M \sigma_{i,j,\hat{s}}
\tag{25b}
$$

where $\sigma_{i,j,\hat{s}} = 1$ if $i$ enters the shared track first.

### 5.9 Same-direction ordering (reordering)

For trains $i \ne j$ using the same track in the same direction on segment $s$:

$$
D_{j,s} \ge A_{i,s+1} + h_{\min} - M(1 - o_{i,j,s}) - M(2 - y_i - y_j)
\tag{26a}
$$
$$
D_{i,s} \ge A_{j,s+1} + h_{\min} - M \, o_{i,j,s} - M(2 - y_i - y_j)
\tag{26b}
$$
$$
o_{i,j,s} + o_{j,i,s} = 1 \quad \text{if both run and use same track}
\tag{26c}
$$

**Track consistency:** $o_{i,j,s}$ only active when both use the same track:

$$
o_{i,j,s} \le z_{i,j,s}, \quad z_{i,j,s} = 1 - |r_{i,s} - r_{j,s}| \quad \text{for nominal-direction trains}
\tag{27}
$$

**Linear form for $z$:**

$$
z_{i,j,s} \le 1 - r_{i,s} + r_{j,s}, \quad z_{i,j,s} \le 1 + r_{i,s} - r_{j,s}, \quad z_{i,j,s} \ge r_{i,s} + r_{j,s} - 1, \quad z_{i,j,s} \ge 1 - r_{i,s} - r_{j,s}
\tag{28}
$$

### 5.10 Station capacity / platform constraints

At each station $s$, at most $P_s$ trains can occupy it simultaneously:

$$
\sum_{i} \mathbb{1}[A_{i,s} \le t \le D_{i,s}] \le P_s \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{29}
$$

**Linear version:** for each time step $\tau \in \mathcal{T}$, introduce binary $\mu_{i,s,\tau}$ with:

$$
A_{i,s} \le \tau + M(1 - \mu_{i,s,\tau}), \quad D_{i,s} \ge \tau - M(1 - \mu_{i,s,\tau})
\tag{30}
$$
$$
\sum_i \mu_{i,s,\tau} \le P_s \qquad \forall s, \tau
\tag{31}
$$

### 5.11 Ordered arrival at stations (no overtaking inside stations)

If trains $i$ and $j$ both stop at station $s$, and $i$ precedes $j$ on segment $s-1$, then $A_{i,s} \le A_{j,s}$:

$$
A_{i,s} \le A_{j,s} + M(1 - o_{i,j,s-1})
\tag{32}
$$

### 5.12 Rerouting feasibility

Only trains whose route includes segment $\hat{s}$ can reroute:

$$
r_{i,\hat{s}} \le \mathbb{1}[i \in \mathcal{I}^{\text{aff}}]
\tag{33}
$$

Rerouting is only allowed during the disruption window (outside it, trains return to nominal track):

$$
r_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}, \quad r_{i,s} = 0 \; \forall s \ne \hat{s}
\tag{34}
$$

### 5.13 Time window / horizon

$$
0 \le A_{i,s}, D_{i,s} \le T^{\max}
\tag{35}
$$

### 5.14 Variable domains summary

$$
y_i, r_{i,s}, o_{i,j,s}, \sigma_{i,j,s}, z_{i,j,s}, \mu_{i,s,\tau}, b_i^{\text{block}} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
A_{i,s}, D_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, t_{i,s}, v_{i,k,s}, u_{i,k,s}, e_{i,k,s}, \Delta d_i^+, \lambda_{i,k,s}^l, w_{i,k,s} \ge 0
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{i} \alpha_i \Delta d_i^{+} + \sum_{i} \beta_i \sum_{s,k} e_{i,k,s} + \sum_{i} \gamma (1 - y_i) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& (2)-(6) && \text{timetable and dwell} \\
& (9)-(11) && \text{speed–time link (PWL)} \\
& (12) && \text{boundary speeds at stops} \\
& (15)-(17) && \text{speed dynamics (McCormick)} \\
& (18)-(19) && \text{energy} \\
& (20)-(21) && \text{delay} \\
& (23)-(24) && \text{blockage / rerouting} \\
& (25) && \text{opposite-direction separation} \\
& (26)-(28) && \text{same-direction ordering and track consistency} \\
& (30)-(31) && \text{station capacity} \\
& (32) && \text{station ordering} \\
& (33)-(35) && \text{domain and horizon} \\
& y_i, r_{i,s}, o_{i,j,s}, \sigma_{i,j,s}, z_{i,j,s}, \mu_{i,s,\tau}, b_i^{\text{block}} \in \{0,1\} \\
& \text{all continuous variables} \ge 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Model Properties and Remarks

1. **Linearity.** All non-linear relations (speed–time, acceleration–speed, energy, McCormick products) are linearized via PWL or McCormick envelopes, so the entire model is a **MILP** solvable by branch-and-bound (e.g., Gurobi/CPLEX).
2. **Conflict-free guarantee.** Constraints (25)–(28) enforce both **unidirectional headway** and **bidirectional separation**, ensuring the timetable is conflict-free even on the shared opposite track during the disruption window.
3. **Coupling TRP–TSMP.** Equations (4), (10), (16) explicitly link timetable variables ($A, D, t$) to speed-profile variables ($v, u, e$), realizing the integrated optimization described in the introduction.
4. **Rerouting flexibility.** Binary $r_{i,\hat{s}}$ combined with (23) captures the "local rerouting strategy" that "enhances operational flexibility and maintains unidirectional line capacity."
5. **Energy efficiency.** Objective (1) includes the energy term $\sum e_{i,k,s}$, reflecting the trade-off between early arrival and energy consumption discussed in the text.
6. **Assumption RA9** (stop pattern $\eta_{i,s}$ fixed) could be relaxed by adding binaries, at the cost of model size.
7. **Equivalent IP reformulation.** As stated in the introduction, the MILP can be decomposed into (i) an integer program over train interactions and (ii) per-train plan selection problems; the proposed adaptive iterative algorithm exploits this structure.

Text:
# Passenger-Oriented Train Rescheduling MILP Model

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the real-time passenger-oriented train rescheduling problem with time-varying sectional passenger demands, flexible train composition, and rolling stock circulation. The model is designed to be solved within a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s \in \{1,2,\dots,S\}$ |
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of trains in the prediction horizon, indexed by $i$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of time intervals (piecewise-constant demand), indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of feasible train compositions, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of links (sections between consecutive stations), $\ell \in \{1,\dots,S-1\}$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time steps within the prediction horizon, $t$ |
| $\mathcal{O}$ | Set of origin–destination (OD) pairs, indexed by $(o,d)$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\lambda_{s,k}$ | Passenger arrival rate at station $s$ during interval $k$ (pax/min) |
| $\pi_{o,d,k}$ | OD demand from $o$ to $d$ during interval $k$ |
| $C_r$ | Maximum passenger capacity of composition $r$ |
| $\tau_r^{min}, \tau_r^{max}$ | Min/max number of units in composition $r$ |
| $c_r^{op}$ | Operational cost per departure of composition $r$ |
| $c^{wait}, c^{travel}, c^{delay}$ | Weights for waiting, in-vehicle, and delay costs |
| $t_{run}^{min}, t_{run}^{max}$ | Min/max running time between consecutive stations |
| $t_{dwell}^{min}, t_{dwell}^{max}$ | Min/max dwell time at a station |
| $h^{min}, h^{max}$ | Min/max headway between consecutive trains |
| $\Delta t_k$ | Length of interval $k$ |
| $N_r^{avail}$ | Available rolling-stock units of type $r$ |
| $T_k^{start}, T_k^{end}$ | Start and end time of interval $k$ |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $a_{i,s}^{nom}, d_{i,s}^{nom}$ | Nominal arrival/departure times |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timetable variables (continuous):**
- $a_{i,s} \geq 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{i,s} \geq 0$: departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $r_{i,s} \geq 0$: running time of train $i$ between stations $s$ and $s+1$
- $w_{i,s} \geq 0$: dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$

**Passenger-flow variables (continuous):**
- $b_{i,s,k} \geq 0$: passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ in interval $k$
- $e_{i,s,k} \geq 0$: passengers alighting from train $i$ at station $s$ in interval $k$
- $p_{i,s} \geq 0$: passenger load on train $i$ after departing station $s$
- $W_{i,s,k} \geq 0$: total waiting time of passengers boarding train $i$ at $s$ in $k$
- $T_{i,s,k}^{inv} \geq 0$: in-vehicle time contribution for passengers on train $i$ from $s$ in $k$

**Delay variables (continuous, linearized):**
- $\delta_{i,s}^{+}, \delta_{i,s}^{-} \geq 0$: positive/negative deviation from nominal times

**Binary variables:**
- $x_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$
- $y_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses composition $r$
- $v_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ during interval $k$
- $u_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if rolling stock of train $i$ is reused by train $j$ (circulation)
- $z_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ serves station $s$ in the rescheduled plan

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of passenger waiting time, in-vehicle time, operational cost, and timetable deviation:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \; Z \;=\; & \; c^{wait} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} W_{i,s,k} \\
& + c^{travel} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} T_{i,s,k}^{inv} \\
& + c^{op} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} c_r^{op} \, y_{i,r} \\
& + c^{delay} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \delta_{i,s}^{+} + \delta_{i,s}^{-} \right)
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Consistency

**Arrival–departure relation at each station:**
$$
a_{i,s} + w_{i,s} = d_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Running time between consecutive stations:**
$$
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + r_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\; s \in \{1,\dots,S-1\}
$$

**Bounds on running and dwell times:**
$$
t_{run}^{min} \leq r_{i,s} \leq t_{run}^{max} \quad \forall i, s
$$
$$
x_{i,s} \cdot t_{dwell}^{min} \leq w_{i,s} \leq x_{i,s} \cdot t_{dwell}^{max} \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.2 Headway Constraints

**Minimum headway between consecutive trains at the same station:**
$$
d_{i,s} - d_{i-1,s} \geq h^{min} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I} \setminus \{1\},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Maximum headway (service regularity):**
$$
d_{i,s} - d_{i-1,s} \leq h^{max} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I} \setminus \{1\},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### 5.3 Stopping Plan

Each train must stop at terminal stations and may optionally skip intermediate stations:
$$
x_{i,1} = x_{i,S} = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}
$$
$$
x_{i,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.4 Flexible Train Composition

**Exactly one composition per train:**
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} y_{i,r} = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}
$$

**Capacity of selected composition:**
$$
p_{i,s} \leq \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} C_r \, y_{i,r} \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.5 Rolling Stock Circulation

**Each train (except the first) inherits stock from exactly one predecessor:**
$$
\sum_{j \in \mathcal{I}, j < i} u_{j,i} = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I} \setminus \{1\}
$$

**Sufficient turnaround time at terminals:**
$$
a_{i,1} - d_{j,S} \geq \tau^{turn} \cdot u_{j,i} - M(1 - u_{j,i}) \quad \forall j < i
$$

**Composition consistency along a circulation chain:**
$$
y_{i,r} \geq y_{j,r} + u_{j,i} - 1 \quad \forall j < i,\; r \in \mathcal{R}
$$

**Rolling-stock availability:**
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} y_{i,r} \leq N_r^{avail} \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R}
$$

### 5.6 Passenger Demand (Piecewise-Constant Approximation)

**Assignment of departures to time intervals:**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v_{i,s,k} = x_{i,s} \quad \forall i, s
$$

**Linking departure time to interval:**
$$
T_k^{start} - M(1 - v_{i,s,k}) \leq d_{i,s} \leq T_k^{end} + M(1 - v_{i,s,k}) \quad \forall i, s, k
$$

**Boarding passengers limited by demand in interval:**
$$
b_{i,s,k} \leq \lambda_{s,k} \cdot \Delta t_k \cdot v_{i,s,k} \quad \forall i, s, k
$$

**Total boarding satisfies demand (with leftover passengers carried over):**
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} b_{i,s,k} + \text{leftover}_{s,k} = \lambda_{s,k} \cdot \Delta t_k \quad \forall s, k
$$

### 5.7 Passenger Flow Conservation

**Load update at each station:**
$$
p_{i,s} = p_{i,s-1} + \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} b_{i,s,k} - \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} e_{i,s,k} \quad \forall i, s \in \{2,\dots,S\}
$$

**Initial and final loads:**
$$
p_{i,1} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} b_{i,1,k}, \qquad p_{i,S} = 0 \quad \forall i
$$

**Alighting proportional to OD demand (linearized):**
$$
e_{i,s,k} \leq \sum_{d > s} \pi_{s,d,k} \cdot v_{i,s,k} + M(1 - x_{i,s}) \quad \forall i, s, k
$$

### 5.8 Capacity Constraints

$$
p_{i,s} \leq \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} C_r \, y_{i,r} \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.9 Waiting Time Linearization

Average waiting time for passengers boarding in interval $k$ equals half the interval length minus the time from interval start to departure (linearized):

$$
W_{i,s,k} \geq b_{i,s,k} \cdot \frac{\Delta t_k}{2} - M(1 - v_{i,s,k}) \quad \forall i, s, k
$$
$$
W_{i,s,k} \geq 0, \quad W_{i,s,k} \leq M \cdot v_{i,s,k} \quad \forall i, s, k
$$

### 5.10 In-Vehicle Time

$$
T_{i,s,k}^{inv} \geq b_{i,s,k} \cdot \sum_{s' > s} r_{i,s'} - M(1 - v_{i,s,k}) \quad \forall i, s, k
$$

### 5.11 Timetable Deviation (Linearized)

$$
a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{nom} = \delta_{i,s}^{+} - \delta_{i,s}^{-} \quad \forall i, s
$$
$$
\delta_{i,s}^{+}, \delta_{i,s}^{-} \geq 0 \quad \forall i, s
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Piecewise-constant demand:** Passenger arrival rates $\lambda_{s,k}$ are constant within each interval $k$ of length $\Delta t_k$.
2. **Fixed line topology:** The set of stations, links, and nominal running times are given.
3. **Composition feasibility:** Each composition $r$ is characterized by a fixed capacity $C_r$ and operational cost $c_r^{op}$.
4. **Single rolling-stock type per train:** Each train uses exactly one composition throughout its trip.
5. **Deterministic forecast:** Passenger demand is assumed perfectly known within the prediction horizon (robust extensions can be added).
6. **No-train overtaking:** Trains maintain their nominal order on the line.
7. **Linear dwell-time bounds:** Dwell time scales linearly with passenger exchange (approximation).
8. **Big-M linearization:** All products of binary and continuous variables are linearized using sufficiently large constants $M$.

---

## 7. Remarks on Integration with the Learning-Based MPC

- The **integer variables** $\{x_{i,s}, y_{i,r}, v_{i,s,k}, u_{i,j}\}$ are predicted by an LSTM network after presolve pruning.
- Once fixed, the remaining problem reduces to a **linear program (LP)** in $(a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, p_{i,s}, b_{i,s,k}, e_{i,s,k}, W_{i,s,k}, T_{i,s,k}^{inv}, \delta^{\pm})$, which is solved online at each MPC step.
- The MPC horizon is rolled forward every $\Delta t^{MPC}$ minutes, and only the first control action is applied to the real system.

This completes the MILP formulation of the passenger-oriented train rescheduling model with time-varying demand, flexible composition, and rolling-stock circulation.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below we present a self-contained mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model that integrates the Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP) and the Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP) under a disruption caused by a partial segment blockage. The notation, variables, objective, and constraints are given in full. Assumptions that are not explicitly stated in the inspiration text are marked **[A]**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$. |
| $\mathcal{T}^{o}$ | Subset of trains running in the *original* direction (up-direction), $\mathcal{T}^{o} \subset \mathcal{T}$. |
| $\mathcal{T}^{r}$ | Subset of trains running in the *opposite* direction (down-direction), $\mathcal{T}^{r} \subset \mathcal{T}$. |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations (nodes), indexed by $s$. |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of track segments (links), indexed by $\ell = (s,s')$. |
| $\mathcal{L}^{d}$ | Set of segments that contain a partial blockage (disruption area), indexed by $\ell^{d}$. |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discretized speed levels for the speed profile approximation, indexed by $k$. **[A]** |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | Set of elementary time steps, indexed by $t$. |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of admissible paths between two adjacent stations, indexed by $p$ (used for rerouting). |
| $\mathcal{G}_{i}$ | Set of trains whose paths conflict with train $i$ on any shared segment (conflict set). |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $d_{\ell}$ | Length of segment $\ell$ (km). |
| $v^{\max}_{i,\ell}$ | Maximum allowable speed of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ (km/h). |
| $a^{\max}_{i}, b^{\max}_{i}$ | Maximum acceleration and deceleration of train $i$ (m/s²). |
| $T^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$. |
| $T^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$. |
| $w^{\min}_{i,s}, w^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ (min). |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum safety headway between two consecutive trains on the same track (min). |
| $E^{k}_{i,\ell}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ at speed level $k$. |
| $C^{delay}_{i}$ | Penalty cost per unit delay for train $i$. |
| $C^{cancel}_{i}$ | Penalty cost for cancelling train $i$. |
| $C^{reroute}$ | Additional cost (per segment) for using the opposite track. |
| $M$ | Big-M constant. |
| $[t^{d}_{1}, t^{d}_{2}]$ | Disruption time window on segment $\ell^{d}$. |
| $\delta^{switch}$ | Minimum switching time required to move from one track to the opposite track at a station. |
| $\rho$ | Weighting factor trading off delay cost and energy consumption. |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Scheduling variables (TRP)

- $x_{i,s} \ge 0$: rescheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $y_{i,s} \ge 0$: rescheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$.
- $\alpha_{i,s} \ge 0$: delay of train $i$ at station $s$: $\alpha_{i,s} = \max(0, x_{i,s} - T^{arr}_{i,s})$.
- $u_{i} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ is cancelled, $0$ otherwise.
- $z_{i,\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ uses the *opposite* track on segment $\ell$ (rerouting indicator).
- $\sigma_{i,j,\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $\ell$, $0$ otherwise (ordering).
- $q_{i,\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ passes through the disruption area on segment $\ell^{d}$ *after* the disruption window, $0$ if *before*.

### 3.2 Speed-management variables (TSMP)

- $v_{i,\ell,k} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $\ell$ (speed-profile selection). **[A]**
- $\tau_{i,\ell} \ge 0$: running time of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ (min).
- $e_{i,\ell} \ge 0$: energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $\ell$.

### 3.3 Coupling variables

- $r_{i,\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ traverses segment $\ell$ during the disruption window $[t^{d}_{1}, t^{d}_{2}]$ on the blocked side; forced to $0$ unless rerouted or deferred. **[A]**

---

## 4. Objective Function

We minimize a weighted sum of total delays, cancellations, rerouting cost, and total energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = \rho \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} C^{delay}_{i} \,\alpha_{i,s}}_{\text{delay cost}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} C^{cancel}_{i}\, u_{i}}_{\text{cancellation cost}}
\;+\; \underbrace{C^{reroute} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}} z_{i,\ell}}_{\text{rerouting cost}}
\;+\; (1-\rho) \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}} e_{i,\ell}}_{\text{energy}}.
$$

The weighting parameter $\rho \in [0,1]$ allows the operator to trade off punctuality and energy efficiency.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable and train-order constraints (TRP)

**(C1) Arrival / departure time ordering at stations.**
For every train $i$ and station $s$ where it stops:
$$
y_{i,s} - x_{i,s} \ge w^{\min}_{i,s}\,(1-u_{i}), \qquad
y_{i,s} - x_{i,s} \le w^{\max}_{i,s}\,(1-u_{i}).
$$

**(C2) Running time on segment $\ell = (s,s')$.**
$$
x_{i,s'} - y_{i,s} = \tau_{i,\ell}\,(1-u_{i}), \qquad \tau_{i,\ell} \ge \tau^{\min}_{i,\ell}.
$$

**(C3) Delay definition.**
$$
\alpha_{i,s} \ge x_{i,s} - T^{arr}_{i,s}, \qquad \alpha_{i,s} \ge 0.
$$
*(The penalty term in the objective will drive $\alpha$ to its minimum, so equality is enforced at optimum.)*

**(C4) Headway (safe separation) on each segment.**
For every ordered pair $(i,j)$ with $\sigma_{i,j,\ell}=1$:
$$
y_{j,s} - y_{i,s} \ge h^{\min} - M\,(1-\sigma_{i,j,\ell})\,(1-u_{i}u_{j}).
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,j,\ell} + \sigma_{j,i,\ell} = 1, \qquad \forall i \ne j,\ \forall \ell \in \mathcal{L}.
$$

**(C5) Disruption-window avoidance / deferral.**
For each blocked segment $\ell^{d}$:
$$
x_{i,s'} \le t^{d}_{1} + M\,(1-q_{i,\ell^{d}}) + M u_{i},
$$
$$
y_{i,s} \ge t^{d}_{2} - M\,q_{i,\ell^{d}} - M u_{i}.
$$
Interpretation: if $q_{i,\ell^{d}}=1$, the train traverses the segment *after* the window; if $q=0$, it traverses *before* the window (through the opposite track via rerouting). Traversal strictly *inside* the window on the blocked side is forbidden by **(C6)**.

**(C6) Rerouting permission.**
$$
r_{i,\ell^{d}} \le z_{i,\ell^{d}}, \qquad r_{i,\ell^{d}} \le (1-u_{i}).
$$
Only rerouted trains may traverse a segment during the disruption window.

**(C7) Rerouting feasibility at adjacent stations.**
$$
\sigma_{i,j,\ell} + \sigma_{j,i,\ell} \ge z_{i,\ell} - z_{j,\ell} \quad\text{(consistency)}\,[\text{A}]
$$
and a minimum switch time at the station where the train enters the opposite track:
$$
y_{i,s} \ge x_{i,s} + \delta^{switch}\, z_{i,\ell}, \quad \ell = (s,s').
$$

**(C8) Cancellation.**
$$
x_{i,s} \le T^{arr}_{i,s} + M\,u_{i}, \quad y_{i,s} \le T^{dep}_{i,s} + M\,u_{i}.
$$

---

### 5.2 Speed-profile constraints (TSMP)

**(C9) One speed level per segment.**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v_{i,\ell,k} = 1-u_{i}, \qquad \forall i,\ \forall \ell.
$$

**(C10) Segment running time from the chosen speed profile.**
$$
\tau_{i,\ell} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \frac{d_{\ell}}{v_{k}}\, v_{i,\ell,k}.
$$
(Here $v_{k}$ is the discrete speed of level $k$.)

**(C11) Energy consumption from the chosen speed profile.**
$$
e_{i,\ell} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} E^{k}_{i,\ell}\, v_{i,\ell,k}.
$$

**(C12) Kinematic coupling (monotone speed transitions).** 
Acceleration/deceleration limits link the speed levels on consecutive segments. Let $v^{L}_{i,\ell}, v^{L}_{i,\ell'}$ denote the speeds of the chosen levels on consecutive segments $\ell, \ell'$:
$$
|v_{k}-v_{k'}| \le a^{\max}_{i}\cdot \Delta t \quad\text{(between adjacent segments)},\,[\text{A}]
$$
which is enforced linearly by combining **(C9)** with valid inequalities over adjacent segments.

**(C13) Upper bound on running speed.**
$$
\sum_{k:\, v_{k} > v^{\max}_{i,\ell}} v_{i,\ell,k} = 0.
$$

---

### 5.3 Coupling constraints between TRP and TSMP

**(C14) Consistency of the positioning of the train within the schedule and the phone speed profile**:
$$
v_{i,\ell,k} \le 1 - u_{i}, \qquad \tau_{i,\ell} = x_{i,s'} - y_{i,s}.
$$
This ties the *timing* choice of the timetable (departure-to-arrival difference) to the *kinematic* choice of the speed profile, ensuring feasibility at the control level.

**(C15) Binary / non-negativity domains.**
$$
x_{i,s},\, y_{i,s},\, \alpha_{i,s},\, \tau_{i,\ell},\, e_{i,\ell} \ge 0;\quad
u_{i},\, z_{i,\ell},\, \sigma_{i,j,\ell},\, q_{i,\ell},\, v_{i,\ell,k},\, r_{i,\ell} \in \{0,1\}.
$$

---

## 6. Summary Assumptions

1. **[A]** Discretized speed levels $\mathcal{K}$ are sufficiently fine to approximate continuous speed profiles without losing operational accuracy.
2. **[A]** A minimum switching time $\delta^{switch}$ applies when a train moves from its original track to the opposite track.
3. **[A]** Conflicts are pairwise; higher-order conflicts are accounted for via big-M and ordering binaries.
4. **[A]** Energy consumption $E^{k}_{i,\ell}$ is precomputed for each train–segment–speed combination.
5. **[A]** Kinematic transitions between adjacent speed levels can be enforced through linear valid inequalities with a chosen time discretization $\Delta t$.
6. Delays are only positive (no early departure is allowed beyond a small tolerance; otherwise, adjust $\alpha$ bound).
7. Trains that are cancelled ($u_i=1$) are removed from all timing, sequencing, and energy constraints without infeasibility.

---

This MILP fully integrates the train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) and the train speed management (speed profile selection and energy) under a partial segment blockage. It adheres closely to the problem description and contributes a single monolithic formulation suitable for decomposition into an integer programming master problem (train interactions) and a set of per-train subproblems (train plans), exactly as motivated in the input.

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code, expressed as equations. Assumptions are marked with **[A]**.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S$ | Set of stations, ordered along the line, indexed $s$ |
| $L$ | Set of track segments $l=(s,s+1)$ between consecutive stations |
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized speed levels, indexed $k$ |
| $L_{block}\subseteq L$ | Segments affected by partial blockage |
| $D$ | Directions $\{up, down\}$; each train $i$ has fixed direction $d(i)$ |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $t_{start}, t_{end}$ | Start/end of disruption time window |
| $len_l$ | Length of segment $l$ (km) |
| $v_k$ | Speed at level $k$ (km/h) |
| $E_k$ | Energy rate at level $k$ (per km) |
| $r^{min}_l, r^{max}_l$ | Min/max running time on segment $l$ |
| $w^{min}_s, w^{max}_s$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $h$ | Safety headway (same direction) |
| $\tau$ | Setup time (opposite direction, rerouting) |
| $rel_i$ | Release time of train $i$ |
| $sched_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $c_{delay}, c_{energy}, c_{cancel}, c_{reroute}$ | Cost coefficients |
| $M$ | Large constant |

**[A]** Running time bounds are derived from speed levels: $r^{min}_l = 60\cdot len_l/v_{\max}$, $r^{max}_l = 60\cdot len_l/v_{\min}$.

---

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,s}\ge 0$ | continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}\ge 0$ | continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $r_{i,l}\ge 0$ | continuous | Running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $w_{i,s}\ge 0$ | continuous | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta_{i,s}\ge 0$ | continuous | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $e_{i,l}\ge 0$ | continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $z_{i,l}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ rerouted to opposite track on $l$ |
| $u_i\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\alpha_{i,l,k}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on $l$ |
| $o_{i,j,l}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | Ordering of same-direction trains $i,j$ on $l$ |
| $b_{i,j,l}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | Ordering of opposite-direction trains on $l$ (rerouting) |
| $g_{i,l}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses $l$ during disruption window |
| $a^1_{i,l}, a^2_{i,l}\in\{0,1\}$ | binary | Auxiliaries for AND linearization of $g_{i,l}$ |

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = c_{delay}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\delta_{i,s}
\;+\; c_{energy}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{l\in L} e_{i,l}
\;+\; c_{cancel}\sum_{i\in T} u_i
\;+\; c_{reroute}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{l\in L} z_{i,l}
$$

---

## Constraints

### (1) Arrival–Departure Linkage
$$
y_{i,s} = x_{i,s} + w_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S
$$

### (2) Running Time Propagation
For each train $i$ and consecutive stations $s, s'$ on its path (with $s'=s+1$ for up, $s'=s-1$ for down), and $l=(\min(s,s'),\max(s,s'))$:
$$
x_{i,s'} = y_{i,s} + r_{i,l}
$$

### (3) Running Time Bounds
$$
r^{min}_l\,(1-u_i) \;\le\; r_{i,l} \;\le\; r^{max}_l\,(1-u_i), \qquad \forall i\in T,\; l\in L
$$

### (4) Dwell Time Bounds
$$
w^{min}_s\,(1-u_i) \;\le\; w_{i,s} \;\le\; w^{max}_s\,(1-u_i), \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S
$$

### (5) Speed Level Selection
$$
\sum_{k\in K}\alpha_{i,l,k} = 1 - u_i, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; l\in L
$$

### (6) Running Time from Speed Profile
$$
r_{i,l} = \sum_{k\in K}\alpha_{i,l,k}\cdot\frac{60\cdot len_l}{v_k}, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; l\in L
$$

### (7) Energy Consumption
$$
e_{i,l} = \sum_{k\in K}\alpha_{i,l,k}\cdot E_k\cdot len_l, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; l\in L
$$

### (8) Delay Definition
$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\ge\; x_{i,s} - sched_{i,s} - M\,u_i, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S
$$

### (9) Release Time
$$
y_{i,\,origin(i)} \;\ge\; rel_i\,(1-u_i), \qquad \forall i\in T
$$

### (10) Disruption Window Traversal Indicator
For each $i\in T$, $l\in L$ on the train's path, with departure station $s_d$ and arrival station $s_a$:
$$
y_{i,s_d} \le t_{end} + M(1-a^1_{i,l})
$$
$$
x_{i,s_a} \ge t_{start} - M(1-a^2_{i,l})
$$
$$
g_{i,l} \le a^1_{i,l}, \qquad g_{i,l} \le a^2_{i,l}, \qquad g_{i,l} \ge a^1_{i,l}+a^2_{i,l}-1
$$
For off-path segments: $g_{i,l}=0$.

### (11) Rerouting Restricted to Blocked Segments
$$
z_{i,l} = 0, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; l\notin L_{block}
$$

### (12) Rerouting Capacity (pairwise)
$$
z_{i,l} + z_{j,l} \;\le\; 1 + M\,(1-b_{i,j,l}), \qquad \forall l\in L_{block},\; i<j
$$

### (13) Same-Direction Headway
For $i<j$ with $d(i)=d(j)$, on segment $l$ with departure station $s_d$:
$$
y_{j,s_d} \ge x_{i,s_d} + h - M\,(1-o_{i,j,l})
$$
$$
y_{i,s_d} \ge x_{j,s_d} + h - M\,o_{i,j,l}
$$

### (14) Opposite-Direction Conflict (Rerouting Case)
For $i<j$ with $d(i)\ne d(j)$, on $l\in L_{block}$ with departure stations $s_d^i, s_d^j$:
$$
y_{j,s_d^j} \ge x_{i,s_d^i} + \tau - M(1-b_{i,j,l}) - M(2-z_{i,l}-z_{j,l})
$$
$$
y_{i,s_d^i} \ge x_{j,s_d^j} + \tau - M\,b_{i,j,l} - M(2-z_{i,l}-z_{j,l})
$$

### (15) Ordering Consistency
$o_{i,j,l}$ and $b_{i,j,l}$ are binary; the paired constraints in (13)–(14) enforce a consistent total order.

### (16) Cancellation
$$
x_{i,s} \le M(1-u_i),\quad y_{i,s} \le M(1-u_i),\quad w_{i,s} \le M(1-u_i), \qquad \forall i,s
$$
$$
r_{i,l} \le M(1-u_i),\quad e_{i,l} \le M(1-u_i), \qquad \forall i,l
$$

### (17) Domains
$$
x,y,r,w,\delta,e \ge 0; \qquad z,u,\alpha,o,b,g,a^1,a^2 \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## Assumptions Made

1. **[A]** Each train travels monotonically from origin to destination (no reversals).
2. **[A]** Segments are normalized as $(\min(s,s'),\max(s,s'))$ regardless of direction.
3. **[A]** Disruption indicator $g_{i,l}=1$ iff the traversal interval $[y_{i,s_d}, x_{i,s_a}]$ intersects $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$, linearized via AND of two binaries.
4. **[A]** Rerouting capacity enforced pairwise: at most one rerouted train per blocked segment at a time.
5. **[A]** Schedule arrival times are given per train per station (placeholder values used in code).
6. **[A]** Running time = $60\cdot len_l/v_k$ (minutes); energy = $E_k\cdot len_l$.
7. **[A]** Opposite-direction conflict constraints enforced only on $L_{block}$ (where rerouting occurs).
8. **[A]** Origin/destination dwell modeled but typically set to zero via bounds.

The model is fully linear (MILP) and solvable with CBC, Gurobi, or CPLEX.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Introduction and Modeling Philosophy

The model integrates the **Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP)** and the **Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP)** into a single Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation. The key idea is to use a **time-indexed space–time network** in which binary variables indicate the occupation of each track block during each discrete time interval, while continuous variables describe the speed and acceleration profiles of each train within those intervals. The two sub-problems are coupled through the occupation variables: the time a train spends in each block determines its travel time (TRP), while the speed profile during that occupation determines the energy consumption (TSMP).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$, ordered along the line |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks (segments between consecutive stations), indexed by $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time intervals, indexed by $k = 0, 1, \dots, |K|$ |
| $V$ | Set of discrete speed levels for piecewise-linear energy approximation, indexed by $v$ |
| $A$ | Set of discrete acceleration levels, indexed by $a$ |
| $B^{\text{dis}} \subseteq B$ | Set of disrupted blocks |
| $K^{\text{dis}} \subseteq K$ | Set of time intervals during the disruption window |
| $T^{+}, T^{-}$ | Trains travelling in the forward (+) and backward (−) directions |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | km |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of each time interval | min |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum operating speed | km/h |
| $a_{\max}^{\text{acc}}, a_{\max}^{\text{dec}}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | km/h per $\Delta t$ |
| $\tau_s^{\min}, \tau_s^{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $h_{\text{safe}}$ | Minimum safety headway | min |
| $t^{\text{dis}}_s, t^{\text{dis}}_e$ | Start / end of disruption window | min |
| $\text{arr}^0_t$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at destination | min |
| $\text{dep}^0_t$ | Scheduled departure time of train $t$ from origin | min |
| $o_t, d_t$ | Origin / destination station of train $t$ | – |
| $\text{dir}_t \in \{+1,-1\}$ | Direction of train $t$ | – |
| $m_t$ | Mass of train $t$ | t |
| $C_r, C_d, A_t, \rho, \eta$ | Resistance, drag, area, air density, motor efficiency | – |
| $\bar{v}_v, \bar{a}_a$ | Speed / acceleration value of level $v, a$ | km/h, km/h/$\Delta t$ |
| $\bar{P}_{v,a}$ | Electric power at speed level $v$ and acceleration level $a$ | kW |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) | min |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Objective weights | – |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Train Movement and Timing
- $x_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ during interval $k$
- $y_{t,t',b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ in block $b$ at time $k$ (ordering)
- $\text{arr}_{t,s} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\text{dep}_{t,s} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\text{cancel}_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled

### Rerouting
- $r_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses the opposite track in block $b$

### Speed Profile
- $v_{t,k} \geq 0$: speed of train $t$ at the beginning of interval $k$
- $a_{t,k} \in \mathbb{R}$: acceleration of train $t$ during interval $k$
- $z^v_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ operates at speed level $v$ in block $b$ at time $k$
- $z^a_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ operates at acceleration level $a$ in block $b$ at time $k$

### Energy and Delay
- $e_{t,b,k} \geq 0$: energy consumption of train $t$ in block $b$ during interval $k$ (kWh)
- $E_{\text{total}} \geq 0$: total energy consumption (kWh)
- $\text{delay}_t \geq 0$: arrival delay of train $t$ at destination (min)

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \sum_{t \in T} \text{delay}_t \;+\; w_2 \, E_{\text{total}} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{t \in T} \text{cancel}_t \;+\; w_4 \sum_{t \in T,\, b \in B} r_{t,b}
$$

The objective balances four goals: (i) minimizing passenger delay, (ii) minimizing energy consumption, (iii) minimizing service cancellations, and (iv) minimizing the use of rerouting (which increases complexity and conflict risk).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Block Capacity and Conflict Resolution

**(C1) At most one train per block per time interval** (handles bidirectional conflicts during rerouting):
$$
\sum_{t \in T} x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; 1, \quad \forall\, b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C2) Train ordering for conflict resolution:**
$$
x_{t,b,k} + x_{t',b,k} \;\leq\; 1 + y_{t,t',b,k} + y_{t',t,b,k}, \quad \forall\, t < t',\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$
$$
y_{t,t',b,k} + y_{t',t,b,k} \;=\; 1, \quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### 6.2 Train Flow Conservation and Sequential Movement

**(C3) Each train occupies at most one block at any time:**
$$
\sum_{b \in B} x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; 1, \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

**(C4) Sequential block traversal (forward direction):**
$$
x_{t,b,k} + x_{t,b+1,k'} \;\leq\; 1, \quad \forall\, t \in T^{+},\; b \in B \setminus \{|B|\},\; k \in K,\; k' \leq k
$$

**(C5) Sequential block traversal (backward direction):**
$$
x_{t,b,k} + x_{t,b-1,k'} \;\leq\; 1, \quad \forall\, t \in T^{-},\; b \in B \setminus \{1\},\; k \in K,\; k' \leq k
$$

**(C6) Path continuity from origin to destination:**
$$
\sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} x_{t,b,k} \;\geq\; \sum_{b \in B_{o_t \to d_t}} 1 - M \cdot \text{cancel}_t, \quad \forall\, t \in T
$$
where $B_{o_t \to d_t}$ is the set of blocks on the path from $o_t$ to $d_t$.

### 6.3 Rerouting Constraints

**(C7) Rerouting only allowed in disrupted blocks during the disruption window:**
$$
r_{t,b} \;\leq\; \sum_{k \in K^{\text{dis}}} x_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B^{\text{dis}}
$$
$$
r_{t,b} \;=\; 0, \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B \setminus B^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C8) Trains traversing a disrupted block during the disruption window must use the opposite track:**
$$
x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; r_{t,b} + (1 - \mathbb{1}[k \in K^{\text{dis}}]) + \mathbb{1}[b \notin B^{\text{dis}}], \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### 6.4 Speed Profile and Train Dynamics

**(C9) Speed limits:**
$$
v_{\min} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; v_{t,k} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; v_{\max} \cdot x_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C10) Acceleration limits:**
$$
-a_{\max}^{\text{dec}} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; a_{t,k} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; a_{\max}^{\text{acc}} \cdot x_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C11) Kinematic equation (speed evolution):**
$$
v_{t,k+1} \;=\; v_{t,k} + a_{t,k} \cdot \Delta t, \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K \setminus \{|K|\}
$$

**(C12) Selection of speed and acceleration levels (for energy linearization):**
$$
\sum_{v \in V} z^v_{t,b,k} \;=\; x_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$
