Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete linear model for the integrated TRSMP under partial segment blockages with bidirectional traffic and local rerouting.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S$ | Stations, $s = 1,\dots,|S|$ |
| $\text{Seg}(s)$ | Segment between station $s$ and $s+1$, $s=1,\dots,|S|-1$ |
| $T$ | Trains, $i \in T$ |
| $T_{\text{dir}}(d)$ | Trains with direction $d \in \{1,2\}$ |
| $K$ | Discrete speed levels, $k \in K$ |
| $\text{SegBlock}$ | Blocked segments during disruption window |

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum allowed speed |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration |
| $d_{\min}$ | Minimum headway (safety separation) |
| $\text{dwell}^{\min}_i, \text{dwell}^{\max}_i$ | Min/max dwell time of train $i$ |
| $t^{\text{arr}}_{\text{sched}}[i,s], t^{\text{dep}}_{\text{sched}}[i,s]$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window start/end |
| $E_k$ | Energy rate at speed level $k$ |
| $v_k$ | Speed at level $k$ |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}, w_{\text{cancel}}$ | Objective weights |
| $c^{\text{cancel}}_i$ | Cancellation penalty for train $i$ |

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{i,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled on segment $s$ |
| $\text{arr}_{i,s}$ | cont. | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,s}$ | cont. | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\text{run}_{i,s}$ | cont. | Running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $z_{i,j,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ |
| $v_{i,s,k}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $s$ |
| $e_{i,s}$ | cont. | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}, \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}$ | cont. | Positive delays of train $i$ at station $s$ |

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\left(\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} + \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}\right) + w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in \text{Seg}} e_{i,s} + w_{\text{cancel}}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in \text{Seg}} c^{\text{cancel}}_i \, x_{i,s}
$$

---

## Constraints

### (1) Timing Propagation
$$
\text{arr}_{i,s+1} = \text{dep}_{i,s} + \text{run}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (2) Dwell Time Bounds
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} - \text{arr}_{i,s} \ge \text{dwell}^{\min}_i \left(1 - x_{i,s}\right), \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} - \text{arr}_{i,s} \le \text{dwell}^{\max}_i + M\, x_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (3) Delay Definition
$$
\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \ge \text{arr}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{\text{sched}}[i,s], \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} - t^{\text{dep}}_{\text{sched}}[i,s], \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \ge 0, \quad \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \ge 0
$$

### (4) Speed Profile Selection
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,s,k} = 1 - x_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (5) Running Time from Speed Levels
$$
\text{run}_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} \frac{L_s}{v_k}\, v_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (6) Energy Consumption
$$
e_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K} E_k \, L_s \, v_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (7) Acceleration / Deceleration Limits (Speed-Level Linking)
For consecutive segments $s, s+1$:
$$
\sum_{k' \in K} v_{k'}\, v_{i,s+1,k'} - \sum_{k \in K} v_k\, v_{i,s,k} \le a_{\max} \cdot \text{run}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}\setminus\{|S|-1\}
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_k\, v_{i,s,k} - \sum_{k' \in K} v_{k'}\, v_{i,s+1,k'} \le b_{\max} \cdot \text{run}_{i,s+1}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}\setminus\{|S|-1\}
$$

*(Linearized by enumerating feasible $(k,k')$ pairs or introducing auxiliary binary products.)*

### (8) Headway on Same Track (Ordering)
For trains $i \ne j$ on the same segment $s$ with the same track usage ($y_{i,s} = y_{j,s}$):
$$
\text{dep}_{j,s} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} + d_{\min} - M\left(1 - z_{i,j,s}\right)
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge \text{dep}_{j,s} + d_{\min} - M\, z_{i,j,s}
$$

### (9) Rerouting Eligibility
$$
y_{i,s} = 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \notin \text{SegBlock}
$$
$$
y_{i,s} \le 1 - x_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{SegBlock}
$$

### (10) Disruption Window on Blocked Track
For $s \in \text{SegBlock}$ and $y_{i,s} = 0$:
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge t_{\text{end}} - M\, y_{i,s} - M\, x_{i,s}
$$
$$
\text{arr}_{i,s+1} \le t_{\text{start}} + M\, y_{i,s} + M\, x_{i,s}
$$

### (11) Bidirectional Conflict on Shared Physical Track
For trains $i, j$ using the same physical track on segment $s$ (i.e., $y_{i,s} \ne y_{j,s}$), enforce ordering:
$$
\text{dep}_{j,s} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} + d_{\min} - M\left(1 - z_{i,j,s}\right)
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge \text{dep}_{j,s} + d_{\min} - M\, z_{i,j,s}
$$

### (12) Cancellation Linking
$$
\text{arr}_{i,s} \le M\left(1 - x_{i,s}\right), \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \le M\left(1 - x_{i,s}\right), \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\text{run}_{i,s} \le M\left(1 - x_{i,s}\right), \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}
$$
$$
e_{i,s} \le M\left(1 - x_{i,s}\right), \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (13) Variable Bounds
$$
0 \le \text{arr}_{i,s},\; \text{dep}_{i,s},\; \text{run}_{i,s},\; e_{i,s} \le M
$$
$$
x_{i,s},\; y_{i,s},\; z_{i,j,s},\; v_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$

### (14) Ordering Consistency
$$
z_{i,j,s} + z_{j,i,s} = 1, \quad \forall i \ne j \in T,\; s \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (15) Speed Level Feasibility
$$
v_{i,s,k} = 0 \quad \text{if } v_k > v_{\max}
$$

---

## Summary

The model minimizes a weighted combination of **passenger delay**, **traction energy**, and **cancellation penalties**, subject to:

- Timing propagation and dwell constraints,
- Speed-level selection with acceleration/deceleration limits,
- Headway safety on shared tracks (same-direction and bidirectional),
- Rerouting eligibility restricted to blocked segments,
- Disruption-window restrictions on blocked tracks,
- Cancellation linking constraints.

The formulation is a **mixed-integer linear program** (MILP) solvable by standard solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP) after linearizing the acceleration/deceleration products in constraint (7).

---

## Assumptions (marked as such)

1. **Discretized speed levels** are used to keep the model linear; continuous speed profiles are approximated by a finite set $K$.
2. **Single-track bidirectional operation** on blocked segments: rerouted trains share the opposite track, requiring headway coordination.
3. **Segment-level granularity** for rerouting decisions (a train reroutes for an entire segment, not partially).
4. **Deterministic disruption window** $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$ is known in advance.
5. **Energy is proportional to distance and speed level** (constant $E_k$ per level), ignoring regenerative braking.
6. **Cancellation is modeled per segment**; a train may be cancelled on affected segments only.
7. **Dwell times are bounded** by train-specific min/max values.
8. **Big-M** is chosen large enough to deactivate constraints when binaries are zero.

# Complete MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management (rtRTMP)

Based on the provided text, I will formulate a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the real-time railway traffic management problem. The model follows the approach described in the paper, decomposing the problem into rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling sub-problems.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| \(T\) | Set of trains, indexed by \(i, j\) |
| \(B\) | Set of block sections (track segments), indexed by \(b\) |
| \(R_i\) | Set of feasible routes for train \(i\) |
| \(R_i^b\) | Subset of routes for train \(i\) that include block section \(b\) |
| \(S_b\) | Set of trains that can use block section \(b\) |
| \(P\) | Set of ordered pairs \((i,j)\) of trains that share at least one block section |
| \(N_b\) | Set of nodes (stations/junctions) adjacent to block section \(b\) |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| \(t_i^{dep}\) | Scheduled departure time of train \(i\) from its origin | s |
| \(t_i^{arr}\) | Scheduled arrival time of train \(i\) at its destination | s |
| \(\tau_{i,b}^{run}\) | Running time of train \(i\) on block section \(b\) | s |
| \(\tau_{i,b}^{min}\) | Minimum running time of train \(i\) on block section \(b\) | s |
| \(h_b^{min}\) | Minimum headway (safety separation time) on block section \(b\) | s |
| \(w_i^{max}\) | Maximum allowed delay for train \(i\) | s |
| \(M\) | Large positive constant (big-M) | s |
| \(c_i^{delay}\) | Cost coefficient for delay of train \(i\) | - |
| \(c_{i,j}^{order}\) | Cost coefficient for ordering penalty between trains \(i\) and \(j\) | - |

**Assumption 1:** Running times \(\tau_{i,b}^{run}\) are deterministic and known a priori (no stochastic disturbances considered in the base model).

**Assumption 2:** All trains must complete their journeys; no cancellation is allowed.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Routing Variables

\[
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in T, \forall r \in R_i
\]

\(x_{i,r} = 1\) if train \(i\) is assigned to route \(r\); \(0\) otherwise.

### 3.2 Ordering Variables

\[
y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (i,j) \in P, \forall b \in B: i,j \in S_b
\]

\(y_{i,j,b} = 1\) if train \(i\) precedes train \(j\) on block section \(b\); \(0\) otherwise.

### 3.3 Timing Variables

\[
e_{i,b} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T, \forall b \in B
\]

Entry time of train \(i\) into block section \(b\).

\[
l_{i,b} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T, \forall b \in B
\]

Exit time (leaving time) of train \(i\) from block section \(b\).

### 3.4 Delay Variables

\[
d_i \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T
\]

Total delay of train \(i\) at its destination.

### 3.5 Pair-wise Delay Variables (for sub-optimal model)

\[
\delta_{i,j} \geq 0 \quad \forall (i,j) \in P
\]

Delay incurred by train \(i\) due to waiting for train \(j\).

---

## 4. Objective Function

### 4.1 Sub-Optimal Model (Rerouting and Reordering Only)

Minimize the total weighted delay, neglecting delay propagation:

\[
\min Z_1 = \sum_{i \in T} c_i^{delay} \cdot d_i + \sum_{(i,j) \in P} c_{i,j}^{order} \cdot \delta_{i,j}
\]

### 4.2 Global Optimum Model (Full rtRTMP)

Minimize the total weighted delay considering delay propagation:

\[
\min Z_2 = \sum_{i \in T} c_i^{delay} \cdot d_i
\]

**Assumption 3:** The cost coefficients \(c_i^{delay}\) are set to 1 for all trains in the base case, but can be differentiated based on train priority (e.g., freight vs. passenger).

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Route Selection Constraints

Each train must be assigned exactly one route:

\[
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T \tag{1}
\]

### 5.2 Route-Block Coupling Constraints

Train \(i\) uses block section \(b\) if and only if its selected route includes \(b\):

\[
\sum_{r \in R_i^b} x_{i,r} = z_{i,b} \quad \forall i \in T, \forall b \in B \tag{2}
\]

where \(z_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}\) is an auxiliary binary variable indicating whether train \(i\) uses block \(b\).

**Assumption 4:** \(z_{i,b}\) is introduced for notational convenience and can be substituted directly.

### 5.3 Running Time Constraints

The exit time from a block section must respect the minimum running time:

\[
l_{i,b} \geq e_{i,b} + \tau_{i,b}^{min} \cdot z_{i,b} \quad \forall i \in T, \forall b \in B \tag{3}
\]

**Assumption 5:** Trains may run slower than the minimum running time (e.g., due to energy-saving driving), so \(l_{i,b} - e_{i,b} \geq \tau_{i,b}^{min}\) is a lower bound.

### 5.4 Connection Constraints Between Consecutive Block Sections

For consecutive block sections \(b_1, b_2\) on route \(r\) of train \(i\):

\[
e_{i,b_2} \geq l_{i,b_1} \quad \forall i \in T, \forall (b_1, b_2) \in \text{consecutive}(r), \forall r \in R_i \tag{4}
\]

### 5.5 Headway (Safety Separation) Constraints

For any pair of trains \((i,j) \in P\) sharing block section \(b\):

\[
e_{j,b} \geq l_{i,b} + h_b^{min} - M \cdot (1 - y_{i,j,b}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in P, \forall b \in B \tag{5}
\]

\[
e_{i,b} \geq l_{j,b} + h_b^{min} - M \cdot y_{i,j,b} \quad \forall (i,j) \in P, \forall b \in B \tag{6}
\]

### 5.6 Ordering Consistency Constraints

If train \(i\) precedes train \(j\) on block \(b\), then train \(j\) cannot precede train \(i\):

\[
y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1 \quad \forall (i,j) \in P, \forall b \in B: i,j \in S_b \tag{7}
\]

**Assumption 6:** This constraint ensures a total ordering on each block section where both trains are present.

### 5.7 Delay Computation Constraints

The delay of train \(i\) at its destination is:

\[
d_i \geq l_{i,b_{last}(i)} - t_i^{arr} \quad \forall i \in T \tag{8}
\]

where \(b_{last}(i)\) is the last block section on the route of train \(i\).

**Assumption 7:** Delay is measured as the difference between actual and scheduled arrival times at the destination.

### 5.8 Maximum Delay Constraints

\[
d_i \leq w_i^{max} \quad \forall i \in T \tag{9}
\]

### 5.9 Pair-wise Delay Constraints (Sub-Optimal Model Only)

For the sub-optimal model, the pair-wise delay \(\delta_{i,j}\) captures the waiting time of train \(i\) for train \(j\):

\[
\delta_{i,j} \geq l_{j,b} + h_b^{min} - e_{i,b} - M \cdot (1 - y_{j,i,b}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in P, \forall b \in B \tag{10}
\]

\[
\delta_{i,j} \geq 0 \quad \forall (i,j) \in P \tag{11}
\]

### 5.10 Delay Propagation Constraints (Global Optimum Model Only)

For the global optimum model, delay propagation is captured by linking entry times to delays:

\[
e_{i,b} \geq t_i^{dep} + \sum_{b' \prec b} \tau_{i,b'}^{run} - M \cdot (1 - z_{i,b}) \quad \forall i \in T, \forall b \in B \tag{12}
\]

**Assumption 8:** This constraint ensures that entry times are consistent with the cumulative running times along the route, accounting for delays accumulated upstream.

### 5.11 Variable Domain Constraints

\[
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in T, \forall r \in R_i \tag{13}
\]

\[
y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (i,j) \in P, \forall b \in B \tag{14}
\]

\[
z_{i,b} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in T, \forall b \in B \tag{15}
\]

\[
e_{i,b}, l_{i,b} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T, \forall b \in B \tag{16}
\]

\[
d_i \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T \tag{17}
\]

\[
\delta_{i,j} \geq 0 \quad \forall (i,j) \in P \tag{18}
\]

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

### 6.1 Sub-Optimal Model (Stage 1: Rerouting and Reordering)

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z_1 = \sum_{i \in T} c_i^{delay} \cdot d_i + \sum_{(i,j) \in P} c_{i,j}^{order} \cdot \delta_{i,j} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & (1) - (11), (13) - (18)
\end{aligned}
}
\]

### 6.2 Global Optimum Model (Stage 2: Rescheduling with Fixed Routes)

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z_2 = \sum_{i \in T} c_i^{delay} \cdot d_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & (1) - (9), (12) - (18) \\
& x_{i,r} = x_{i,r}^* \quad \text{(fixed from Stage 1)}
\end{aligned}
}
\]

---

## 7. Assumptions Summary

| # | Assumption |
|---|------------|
| 1 | Running times are deterministic and known a priori |
| 2 | All trains must complete their journeys; no cancellation allowed |
| 3 | Cost coefficients can be differentiated based on train priority |
| 4 | Auxiliary variable \(z_{i,b}\) is used for notational convenience |
| 5 | Trains may run slower than minimum running time |
| 6 | Total ordering is enforced on each block section |
| 7 | Delay is measured at the destination |
| 8 | Delay propagation is captured via cumulative running times |

---

## 8. Model Interpretation

This MILP formulation decomposes the rtRTMP into two stages:

1. **Stage 1 (Sub-Optimal):** Solves rerouting and reordering using pair-wise delay variables, providing a fast but potentially sub-optimal solution.

2. **Stage 2 (Global Optimum):** Fixes the route selection from Stage 1 and solves the full rescheduling problem, considering delay propagation for optimality.

The model minimizes total weighted train delays while respecting safety constraints (headways), infrastructure capacity (block sections), and operational constraints (running times, connections).

# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| \(S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}\) | Stations, indexed \(i, j\) |
| \(E = \{(i,i+1) : i \in S \setminus \{|S|\}\}\) | Segments, indexed \(e = (i,i+1)\) |
| \(T\) | Trains, indexed \(k, l\) |
| \(D = \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}\) | Directions |
| \(P_{k,e}\) | Candidate speed profiles for train \(k\) on segment \(e\), indexed \(p\) |
| \(\mathcal{E}^{dis} \subseteq E\) | Disrupted segment(s) |
| \(\mathcal{T}^{dis} = [t^{start}, t^{end}]\) | Disruption time window |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| \(r_{k,e,p}\) | Running time of train \(k\) on segment \(e\) with profile \(p\) |
| \(en_{k,e,p}\) | Energy consumption of train \(k\) on segment \(e\) with profile \(p\) |
| \(d^{min}_k, d^{max}_k\) | Minimum / maximum dwell time of train \(k\) |
| \(h\) | Minimum headway, same direction, same track |
| \(h^{bi}\) | Minimum headway, opposite directions on shared track |
| \(t^{start}, t^{end}\) | Disruption window bounds |
| \(M\) | Large constant |
| \(c^{delay}\) | Delay penalty per time unit |
| \(c^{cancel}\) | Cancellation penalty |
| \(c^{energy}\) | Energy cost weight |
| \(a^0_k, dep^0_k\) | Nominal scheduled arrival / departure times |
| \(orig_k, dest_k\) | Origin / destination stations of train \(k\) |
| \(dir_k \in D\) | Direction of train \(k\) |
| \(H\) | Time horizon |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| \(x_{k,e,p}\) | binary | 1 if train \(k\) uses profile \(p\) on segment \(e\) |
| \(y_{k,e}\) | binary | 1 if train \(k\) traverses segment \(e\) |
| \(z_k\) | binary | 1 if train \(k\) is cancelled |
| \(a_{k,i}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Arrival time of train \(k\) at station \(i\) |
| \(d_{k,i}\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Departure time of train \(k\) from station \(i\) |
| \(u_{k,e}\) | binary | 1 if train \(k\) uses the opposite (rerouted) track on segment \(e\) |
| \(o_{k,l,e}\) | binary | 1 if train \(k\) precedes train \(l\) on segment \(e\) |
| \(delay_k\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) | Delay of train \(k\) at destination |

## 4. Objective Function

\[
\min \; Z = c^{delay}\sum_{k \in T} delay_k \;+\; c^{cancel}\sum_{k \in T} z_k \;+\; c^{energy}\sum_{k \in T}\sum_{e \in E}\sum_{p \in P_{k,e}} en_{k,e,p}\, x_{k,e,p}
\]

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Profile selection and cancellation

\[
\sum_{p \in P_{k,e}} x_{k,e,p} = y_{k,e} \qquad \forall k \in T,\; e \in E \tag{1}
\]

\[
z_k = 1 - y_{k,e^{first}_k} \qquad \forall k \in T \tag{2}
\]

\[
y_{k,e} \le y_{k,e'} \quad \text{for consecutive segments } e \prec e' \text{ of train } k \tag{3}
\]

### 5.2 Timetable consistency

\[
a_{k,i+1} - d_{k,i} = \sum_{p \in P_{k,e}} r_{k,e,p}\, x_{k,e,p} \qquad \forall k \in T,\; e=(i,i+1) \in E \tag{4}
\]

\[
d^{min}_k\, y_{k,e} \le d_{k,i} - a_{k,i} \le d^{max}_k\, y_{k,e} \qquad \forall k \in T,\; i \in S \tag{5}
\]

\[
d_{k,i} \ge a_{k,i} \qquad \forall k \in T,\; i \in S \tag{6}
\]

\[
a_{k,i} \le H\, y_{k,e} \qquad \forall k \in T,\; e=(i,i+1) \tag{7}
\]

### 5.3 Delay definition

\[
delay_k \ge a_{k,dest_k} - a^0_k \qquad \forall k \in T \tag{8}
\]

### 5.4 Rerouting constraints

\[
u_{k,e} = 0 \qquad \forall k \in T,\; e \notin \mathcal{E}^{dis} \tag{9}
\]

\[
d_{k,i} \ge t^{start} - M(1 - u_{k,e}) \qquad \forall k \in T,\; e=(i,i+1) \in \mathcal{E}^{dis} \tag{10}
\]

\[
a_{k,i+1} \le t^{end} + M(1 - u_{k,e}) \qquad \forall k \in T,\; e=(i,i+1) \in \mathcal{E}^{dis} \tag{11}
\]

### 5.5 Disruption blocking (no use of blocked track during window unless rerouted)

\[
d_{k,i} \ge t^{end} - M(1 - u_{k,e}) - M(1 - y_{k,e}) \qquad \forall k \in T,\; e=(i,i+1) \in \mathcal{E}^{dis} \tag{12}
\]

### 5.6 Ordering consistency

\[
o_{k,l,e} + o_{l,k,e} = 1 \qquad \forall k < l \in T,\; e \in E \tag{13}
\]

### 5.7 Same-direction headway (same track)

For \(k,l\) with \(dir_k = dir_l\) and \(u_{k,e} = u_{l,e}\):

\[
d_{l,i} \ge d_{k,i} + h - M(1 - o_{k,l,e}) - M(1 - y_{k,e}) - M(1 - y_{l,e}) \tag{14}
\]

### 5.8 Bidirectional conflict on shared track

For \(k,l\) with \(dir_k \ne dir_l\) and \(u_{k,e} \ne u_{l,e}\) (opposite tracks used):

\[
a_{l,i+1} \ge a_{k,i+1} + h^{bi} - M(1 - o_{k,l,e}) - M(1 - y_{k,e}) - M(1 - y_{l,e}) \tag{15}
\]

### 5.9 Time ordering

\[
a_{k,i+1} \le a_{l,i+1} + M(1 - o_{k,l,e}) \qquad \forall k \ne l,\; e=(i,i+1) \tag{16}
\]

### 5.10 Domain constraints

\[
x_{k,e,p}, y_{k,e}, z_k, u_{k,e}, o_{k,l,e} \in \{0,1\} \tag{17}
\]

\[
a_{k,i}, d_{k,i}, delay_k \ge 0 \tag{18}
\]

## 6. Assumptions (marked)

- **A1.** Discretized time horizon with unit steps \(t = 0,\dots,H\).
- **A2.** Fixed origin/destination and station sequence (no skipping) unless cancelled.
- **A3.** Finite set of precomputed candidate speed profiles per train per segment, each with known running time and energy consumption (reasonable assumption: energy-speed relation precomputed offline).
- **A4.** Acceleration/deceleration limits encoded in candidate profiles (reasonable assumption).
- **A5.** Minimum headway between consecutive trains on same track, same direction.
- **A6.** Minimum and maximum dwell times at stations.
- **A7.** Rerouting permitted only on the disrupted segment during the disruption window (local rerouting).
- **A8.** Cancellation allowed with penalty cost.
- **A9.** No overtaking within a segment; reordering realized at stations (reasonable assumption for single-track segments).

## 7. Notes on Linearity

All disjunctions (ordering, rerouting, track sharing) are linearized using big-\(M\) constraints (14)–(16). The energy term is linear in \(x_{k,e,p}\). The model is a complete MILP.

Text:
# A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Availability Constraints

## 1. Motivation and Scope

Based on the problem description, we develop a complete MILP that integrates:

1. **A composition model** (based on Fioole et al., 2006) that assigns rolling stock compositions to train trips and prescribes shunting movements.
2. **An infrastructure model** (based on Van Aken et al., 2017) that verifies whether the prescribed shunting movements can be executed on the available station tracks, possibly delaying other trains by a small amount.

The two models are linked through a **Combinatorial Benders'-style** scheme: the composition model proposes shunting movements; the infrastructure model returns cuts that forbid infeasible combinations. Below we present the full MILP formulation of both components, together with the linking cuts.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of train trips in the timetable, indexed by $t$. |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$. |
| $U$ | Set of rolling stock unit types, indexed by $u$. |
| $K$ | Set of compositions (ordered multisets of unit types) that can be assigned to a trip, indexed by $k$. |
| $M$ | Set of shunting movements, indexed by $m$. |
| $R_s$ | Set of tracks at station $s$, indexed by $r$. |
| $E$ | Set of infrastructure events (arrivals, departures, shunting movements) at a station, indexed by $e$. |
| $\mathcal{C}$ | Set of Benders' cuts (infeasible shunting combinations), indexed by $c$. |

**Assumption A1 (marked):** The timetable is given and fixed except for small delays (at most $\delta^{\max}$ minutes) that may be imposed by the infrastructure model.

**Assumption A2 (marked):** Each composition $k \in K$ is a feasible coupling of unit types (length, power, seating capacity constraints already encoded in $K$).

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $c^{\text{op}}_k$ | Operational cost of using composition $k$ (per trip). |
| $c^{\text{seat}}_k$ | Passenger seat capacity of composition $k$. |
| $d_t$ | Expected passenger demand on trip $t$. |
| $c^{\text{dev}}$ | Penalty per unit of deviation from the original rolling stock plan. |
| $a^{\text{orig}}_{t,k}$ | 1 if trip $t$ was originally assigned composition $k$, 0 otherwise. |
| $c^{\text{shunt}}$ | Cost per shunting movement performed. |
| $c^{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty per minute of delay imposed on a passenger train. |
| $\delta^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed delay (minutes) for any train. |
| $[\,t^{\text{start}}_e,\ t^{\text{end}}_e\,]$ | Time window during which event $e$ occupies a track. |
| $\tau_{e,e'}$ | Minimum headway (setup) time between consecutive events $e,e'$ on the same track. |
| $b_{m}$ | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is required by the original plan, 0 otherwise. |
| $L_u$ | Number of carriages of unit type $u$. |
| $N_u$ | Number of available units of type $u$. |
| $M^{\text{big}}$ | A sufficiently large constant. |

---

## 4. Decision Variables — Composition Model

$$
x_{t,k} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall t \in T,\ k \in K
$$
1 if trip $t$ is operated with composition $k$.

$$
y_{m} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall m \in M
$$
1 if shunting movement $m$ is performed.

$$
z_{t} \ge 0 \quad \forall t \in T
$$
Number of passengers that cannot be seated on trip $t$ (standing/denied passengers).

$$
w_{t,k} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall t \in T,\ k \in K
$$
1 if trip $t$ deviates from its original composition (used for the stick-to-the-plan objective).

---

## 5. Decision Variables — Infrastructure Model

$$
\alpha_{e,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall e \in E,\ r \in R_{s(e)}
$$
1 if event $e$ is assigned to track $r$.

$$
\Delta_e \ge 0 \quad \forall e \in E
$$
Delay (in minutes) imposed on event $e$ (0 for shunting movements that must be on time, or small for passenger trains).

$$
\beta_{e,e'} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (e,e') \in \text{conflicting pairs}
$$
1 if event $e$ is scheduled before event $e'$ on the same track.

---

## 6. Objective Function

We minimize a weighted sum of operational cost, passenger inconvenience, deviation from the original plan, shunting cost, and delay penalties:

$$
\min \ Z =
\underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} \sum_{k \in K} c^{\text{op}}_k \, x_{t,k}}_{\text{operational cost}}
+
\underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} c^{\text{pax}} \, z_{t}}_{\text{passenger inconvenience}}
+
\underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} \sum_{k \in K} c^{\text{dev}} \, w_{t,k}}_{\text{stick-to-the-plan}}
+
\underbrace{\sum_{m \in M} c^{\text{shunt}} \, y_{m}}_{\text{shunting cost}}
+
\underbrace{\sum_{e \in E} c^{\text{delay}} \, \Delta_e}_{\text{delay penalty}}
$$

where $c^{\text{pax}}$ is a penalty per unseated passenger.

---

## 7. Constraints — Composition Model

### 7.1 Unique composition per trip

$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{t,k} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{C1}
$$

### 7.2 Seat capacity and passenger overflow

$$
z_{t} \ge d_t - \sum_{k \in K} c^{\text{seat}}_k \, x_{t,k} \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{C2}
$$

### 7.3 Fleet size availability

$$
\sum_{t \in T} \sum_{k \in K} n_{u,k} \, x_{t,k} \le N_u \qquad \forall u \in U \tag{C3}
$$

where $n_{u,k}$ is the number of units of type $u$ in composition $k$.

### 7.4 Coupling / decoupling consistency

For each pair of consecutive trips $(t,t')$ that share rolling stock:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{t,k} \cdot \mathbb{1}[k \text{ can couple to } k'] \ge x_{t',k'} \qquad \forall (t,t'),\ k' \in K \tag{C4}
$$

**Assumption A3 (marked):** Coupling feasibility between compositions is precomputed and encoded in the indicator above.

### 7.5 Shunting movement activation

Shunting movement $m$ is performed only if the associated composition change occurs:

$$
y_{m} \ge x_{t,k} + x_{t',k'} - 1 \qquad \forall m = (t,k,t',k') \in M \tag{C5}
$$

$$
y_{m} \le x_{t,k} \qquad \forall m = (t,k,t',k') \in M \tag{C6}
$$

### 7.6 Deviation indicator

$$
w_{t,k} \ge x_{t,k} - a^{\text{orig}}_{t,k} \qquad \forall t \in T,\ k \in K \tag{C7}
$$

$$
w_{t,k} \ge a^{\text{orig}}_{t,k} - x_{t,k} \qquad \forall t \in T,\ k \in K \tag{C8}
$$

---

## 8. Constraints — Infrastructure Model

### 8.1 Unique track assignment

$$
\sum_{r \in R_{s(e)}} \alpha_{e,r} = 1 \qquad \forall e \in E \tag{I1}
$$

### 8.2 Track compatibility

Event $e$ can only be assigned to a track $r$ that is compatible with its type (length, electrification, direction):

$$
\alpha_{e,r} = 0 \qquad \forall e \in E,\ r \notin R^{\text{compat}}_e \tag{I2}
$$

### 8.3 No-overlap / headway constraints

For each pair of conflicting events $(e,e')$ on the same station:

$$
\alpha_{e,r} + \alpha_{e',r} \le 1 + \beta_{e,e'} + \beta_{e',e} \qquad \forall r \in R_s,\ (e,e') \in \mathcal{P}_s \tag{I3}
$$

$$
t^{\text{start}}_{e'} + \Delta_{e'} \ge t^{\text{end}}_{e} + \Delta_{e} + \tau_{e,e'} - M^{\text{big}}(1 - \beta_{e,e'}) \qquad \forall (e,e') \tag{I4}
$$

$$
t^{\text{start}}_{e} + \Delta_{e} \ge t^{\text{end}}_{e'} + \Delta_{e'} + \tau_{e',e} - M^{\text{big}}(1 - \beta_{e',e}) \qquad \forall (e',e) \tag{I5}
$$

$$
\beta_{e,e'} + \beta_{e',e} \le 1 \qquad \forall (e,e') \tag{I6}
$$

### 8.4 Bounded delays

$$
0 \le \Delta_e \le \delta^{\max} \qquad \forall e \in E \tag{I7}
$$

### 8.5 Shunting movement feasibility

A shunting movement $m$ can only be executed if it is selected by the composition model:

$$
y_m \le \sum_{r \in R_{s(m)}} \alpha_{m,r} \qquad \forall m \in M \tag{I8}
$$

**Assumption A4 (marked):** Shunting movements have fixed time windows; only passenger train events may be delayed.

### 8.6 Linking: only selected shunting movements enter the infrastructure model

$$
\alpha_{m,r} \le y_m \qquad \forall m \in M,\ r \in R_{s(m)} \tag{I9}
$$

---

## 9. Combinatorial Benders' Cuts

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the collection of infeasible subsets of shunting movements identified by the infrastructure model. For each cut $c \in \mathcal{C}$ with associated subset $M_c \subseteq M$:

$$
\sum_{m \in M_c} y_m \le |M_c| - 1 \qquad \forall c \in \mathcal{C} \tag{B1}
$$

These cuts forbid the simultaneous execution of shunting movements in $M_c$, which the infrastructure model has proven infeasible.

---

## 10. Complete Integrated MILP

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z \ \text{(as in Section 6)} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C8)} \quad \text{(composition model)} \\
& \text{(I1)--(I9)} \quad \text{(infrastructure model)} \\
& \text{(B1)} \quad \text{(Benders' cuts)} \\
& x_{t,k}, y_m, w_{t,k}, \alpha_{e,r}, \beta_{e,e'} \in \{0,1\} \\
& z_t, \Delta_e \ge 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 11. Solution Algorithm (Combinatorial Benders' Decomposition)

**Step 1 (Master problem):** Solve the composition model (C1)–(C8) with the current set of cuts $\mathcal{C}$ to obtain $\bar{x}, \bar{y}$.

**Step 2 (Subproblem):** Fix $\bar{y}$ and solve the infrastructure model (I1)–(I9). If feasible, stop — optimal solution found. If infeasible, extract a minimal infeasible subset $M_c \subseteq \{m : \bar{y}_m = 1\}$.

**Step 3 (Cut generation):** Add cut (B1) to the master problem, set $\mathcal{C} \leftarrow \mathcal{C} \cup \{c\}$, and return to Step 1.

**Iterative heuristic variant:** Instead of adding cuts for the entire subset, feed shunting movements to the infrastructure model one at a time. This mimics the interaction between rolling stock dispatchers (NS) and infrastructure dispatchers (ProRail) under European separation-of-roles legislation.

---

## 12. Summary of Assumptions (marked)

- **A1:** Timetable fixed except for small delays ($\le \delta^{\max}$).
- **A2:** Composition set $K$ pre-encoded with feasibility (length, power, capacity).
- **A3:** Coupling feasibility between compositions precomputed.
- **A4:** Only passenger train events may be delayed; shunting movements have fixed windows.
- **A5 (implicit):** Short delays are absorbed by timetable buffers downstream.
- **A6 (implicit):** Shunting drivers are assumed available (crew scheduling treated separately).

---

## 13. Model Properties

- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear; integrality is imposed on assignment, shunting, and sequencing variables.
- **Exactness:** The Benders' cuts guarantee that the final solution satisfies both rolling stock and infrastructure feasibility.
- **Genericity:** The framework allows substitution of either submodel with alternative formulations, as emphasized in the source text.
- **Practical relevance:** The iterative heuristic variant reflects the organizational separation between ProRail and NS, making the model directly applicable in the Dutch railway context.

Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.

# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Among the three generated models, **Model 3** is the best. It provides the most complete and rigorous treatment of the two hardest features of this problem: (i) the **track-sharing logic** that governs bidirectional conflicts when trains reroute onto the opposite track, and (ii) the **disruption-window disjunction** that forces non-rerouted trains to either clear the blocked segment before $T_{start}$ or enter after $T_{end}$. Model 1 leaves the track-sharing indicator $\phi$ under-specified and its disruption constraint (C10) is not a clean disjunction; Model 2's disruption constraint (C9) is too weak (it only forces departure after $T_{end}$ and omits the "pass before" alternative). Model 3 also gives the cleanest energy linearization via a convex piecewise-linear function of the running-time ratio, which keeps the LP relaxation tight. Below is the complete, self-contained formulation.

---

## 0. Assumptions (marked where data is missing)

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Single line, stations ordered $s=1,\dots,S$; segment $s$ connects station $s$ to $s+1$. |
| A2 | Two tracks: a "normal" direction-specific track and an "opposite" track. Up trains normally use track UP; down trains use track DOWN. |
| A3 | Disruption occurs on segment $d$ on the track used by the affected direction (say DOWN). Affected trains may reroute to the opposite (UP) track during $[T_{start},T_{end}]$. |
| A4 | Speed is modeled via segment running time $rt_{i,s}$; average speed $v_{i,s}=L_s/rt_{i,s}$ is handled through the energy linearization. |
| A5 | Energy is a convex piecewise-linear function of running time (shorter running time ⇒ higher energy). |
| A6 | Minimum headway $h$ is identical for all train pairs and both tracks. |
| A7 | Dwell time $dwell_{i,s}\in[d^{min},d^{max}]$; extra dwell allowed via binary $w_{i,s}$. |
| A8 | If $z_i=1$ (cancelled), all timing variables are relaxed via big-$M$. |
| A9 | Big-$M$ dominates all time differences (e.g., $M=T_{horizon}$). |
| A10 | At most one train per track per station at a time; minimum station headway $h^{st}$; no overtaking unless allowed. |
| A11 | Nominal arrival/departure times $\hat a_{i,s},\hat d_{i,s}$ are given. |
| A12 | All trains complete their journey within $[0,T_{horizon}]$. |

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Trains, $i,j\in I$ |
| $S=\{1,\dots,S\}$ | Stations |
| $Seg=\{1,\dots,S-1\}$ | Segments (segment $s$ between stations $s$ and $s+1$) |
| $I^{up},I^{dn}\subset I$ | Up- and down-direction trains |
| $d$ | Disruption segment |
| $[T_{start},T_{end}]$ | Disruption time window |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|---|---|---|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ | km |
| $d^{min},d^{max}$ | Min / max dwell time | min |
| $rt^{min}_s,rt^{max}_s$ | Min / max running time on segment $s$ | min |
| $h$ | Minimum headway (same track) | min |
| $h^{st}$ | Minimum station headway | min |
| $\hat a_{i,s},\hat d_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure | min |
| $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ | Weights: delay, energy, cancellation | — |
| $c^{cancel}_i$ | Cancellation penalty for train $i$ | — |
| $M$ | Big-$M$ constant | min |
| $T_{horizon}$ | Planning horizon | min |
| $K$ | Number of linearization pieces for energy | — |
| $(\rho_k,e_k)$ | Breakpoints: running-time ratio $\rho_k$, energy rate $e_k$ | — |
| $\epsilon$ | Small positive constant | min |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Continuous
| Variable | Description | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | $[0,T_{horizon}]$ |
| $dep_{i,s}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ | $[0,T_{horizon}]$ |
| $rt_{i,s}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ | $[rt^{min}_s,rt^{max}_s]$ |
| $E_{i,s}$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on segment $s$ | $\ge 0$ |
| $\delta^a_{i,s}$ | Arrival delay (positive part) | $\ge 0$ |
| $\delta^d_{i,s}$ | Departure delay (positive part) | $\ge 0$ |
| $\lambda_{i,s,k}$ | PWL weight for energy piece $k$ | $[0,1]$ |

### Binary
| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| $x_{i,j,s}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ (same track) |
| $y_{i,s}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $z_i$ | $=1$ if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $w_{i,s}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ takes extra dwell at station $s$ |
| $\theta_i$ | $=1$ if train $i$ passes the blocked segment after $T_{end}$ |
| $\xi_{i,j,s}$ | $=1$ if trains $i,j$ share a physical track on segment $s$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z=\alpha\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\left(\delta^a_{i,s}+\delta^d_{i,s}\right)}_{\text{total delay}}
+\beta\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in Seg}E_{i,s}}_{\text{total energy}}
+\gamma\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}c^{cancel}_i\,z_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Feasibility

$$
dep_{i,s}\ge a_{i,s}+d^{min}-Mz_i \qquad \forall i,s \tag{1}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s}\le a_{i,s}+d^{max}+Mz_i \qquad \forall i,s \tag{2}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1}\ge dep_{i,s}+rt_{i,s}-Mz_i \qquad \forall i,\;s\in Seg \tag{3}
$$

**Extra dwell indicator:**
$$
dep_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\le d^{min}+(d^{max}-d^{min})w_{i,s}+Mz_i \tag{4}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\ge d^{min}+\epsilon\,w_{i,s}-Mz_i \tag{5}
$$

### 5.2 Delay Definition

$$
\delta^a_{i,s}\ge a_{i,s}-\hat a_{i,s}-Mz_i,\qquad \delta^a_{i,s}\ge 0 \tag{6}
$$
$$
\delta^d_{i,s}\ge dep_{i,s}-\hat d_{i,s}-Mz_i,\qquad \delta^d_{i,s}\ge 0 \tag{7}
$$

### 5.3 Speed Profile Coupling

$$
rt^{min}_s\le rt_{i,s}\le rt^{max}_s \qquad \forall i,s \tag{8}
$$

Acceleration/deceleration proxy (conservative linear bound on running-time change):
$$
-\Delta rt^{max}\le rt_{i,s+1}-rt_{i,s}\le \Delta rt^{max} \tag{9}
$$

### 5.4 Energy Linearization (Convex Piecewise Linear)

Let $\rho_{i,s}=rt_{i,s}/rt^{min}_s\in[1,\rho^{max}]$ with breakpoints $(\rho_k,e_k)$, $k=0,\dots,K$:

$$
rt_{i,s}=rt^{min}_s\sum_{k=0}^{K}\rho_k\lambda_{i,s,k} \tag{10}
$$
$$
\sum_{k=0}^{K}\lambda_{i,s,k}=1,\qquad \lambda_{i,s,k}\ge 0 \tag{11}
$$
$$
E_{i,s}=L_s\sum_{k=0}^{K}e_k\lambda_{i,s,k} \tag{12}
$$

*(Convexity of $e(\cdot)$ makes the LP relaxation tight; SOS2/adjacency constraints may be added if needed.)*

### 5.5 Disruption Constraints

For the disruption segment $d$, affected-direction trains $i\in I^{dn}$:

**Blocked track forbidden during window** — train must clear before $T_{start}$ or enter after $T_{end}$ (unless rerouted):
$$
a_{i,d+1}\le T_{start}+M(1-y_{i,d})+M(1-\theta_i)+Mz_i \tag{13a}
$$
$$
dep_{i,d}\ge T_{end}-My_{i,d}-M\theta_i-Mz_i \tag{13b}
$$
$$
\theta_i\in\{0,1\} \tag{13c}
$$

**Rerouting only on disruption segment:**
$$
y_{i,s}=0 \qquad \forall i,\;s\ne d \tag{14}
$$
$$
y_{i,d}=0 \qquad \forall i\in I^{up} \tag{15}
$$

### 5.6 Headway / Ordering Constraints

**Track-sharing indicator** $\xi_{i,j,s}=1$ if $i,j$ share a physical track on segment $s$:

For same-direction trains on $s\ne d$: $\xi_{i,j,s}=1$ (if both active).
For affected-direction trains on $s=d$:
$$
\xi_{i,j,d}\ge 1-y_{i,d}-y_{j,d} \tag{19a}
$$
$$
\xi_{i,j,d}\ge y_{i,d}+y_{j,d}-1 \tag{19b}
$$
$$
\xi_{i,j,d}\le 1-y_{i,d}+y_{j,d} \tag{19c1}
$$
$$
\xi_{i,j,d}\le 1+y_{i,d}-y_{j,d} \tag{19c2}
$$

**Ordering constraints** (enforced only when sharing a track):
$$
dep_{j,s}\ge a_{i,s+1}+h-M(1-x_{i,j,s})-M(1-\xi_{i,j,s})-Mz_i-Mz_j \tag{16'}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s}\ge a_{j,s+1}+h-Mx_{i,j,s}-M(1-\xi_{i,j,s})-Mz_i-Mz_j \tag{17'}
$$
$$
x_{i,j,s}+x_{j,i,s}=1 \tag{18}
$$

**Opposite-direction conflict on shared track (disruption segment):** for $i\in I^{dn}$ rerouting and $j\in I^{up}$:
$$
\xi_{i,j,d}\ge y_{i,d} \qquad \forall i\in I^{dn},\;j\in I^{up} \tag{20}
$$
then (16′)–(17′) apply.

### 5.7 Station Capacity / No Overtaking

$$
a_{j,s}\ge dep_{i,s}+h^{st}-M(1-x_{i,j,s})-Mz_i-Mz_j \tag{21}
$$
$$
a_{i,s}\ge dep_{j,s}+h^{st}-Mx_{i,j,s}-Mz_i-Mz_j \tag{22}
$$

**Ordering consistency** (same direction, consecutive segments):
$$
x_{i,j,s}=x_{i,j,s+1}\qquad \forall i,j\in I^{up}\text{ or }I^{dn},\;s\in Seg \tag{23}
$$

### 5.8 Cancellation Constraints

$$
a_{i,s}\le M(1-z_i),\qquad dep_{i,s}\le M(1-z_i) \tag{24}
$$
$$
rt_{i,s}\le rt^{max}_s(1-z_i)+rt^{min}_s z_i \tag{25}
$$
$$
E_{i,s}\le E^{max}(1-z_i) \tag{26}
$$
$$
y_{i,s}\le 1-z_i,\qquad w_{i,s}\le 1-z_i \tag{27}
$$

### 5.9 Time Horizon Bounds

$$
0\le a_{i,s},\;dep_{i,s}\le T_{horizon} \tag{28}
$$

### 5.10 Variable Domains

$$
x_{i,j,s},y_{i,s},z_i,w_{i,s},\theta_i,\xi_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\} \tag{29}
$$
$$
a_{i,s},dep_{i,s},rt_{i,s},E_{i,s},\delta^a_{i,s},\delta^d_{i,s},\lambda_{i,s,k}\ge 0 \tag{30}
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min\quad & \alpha\sum_{i,s}(\delta^a_{i,s}+\delta^d_{i,s})+\beta\sum_{i,s}E_{i,s}+\gamma\sum_i c^{cancel}_i z_i \\
\text{s.t.}\quad & (1)\text{–}(30)
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

| Element | Role |
|---|---|
| $a_{i,s},dep_{i,s}$ | Core timetable variables; linked by dwell and running-time constraints. |
| $rt_{i,s}$ | Speed-management proxy; shorter $rt$ ⇒ higher speed ⇒ more energy. |
| $E_{i,s}$ | Energy per segment, linearized via convex PWL of running-time ratio. |
| $x_{i,j,s}$ | Ordering binary; enforces headway on shared track. |
| $y_{i,s}$ | Rerouting binary; only active on disruption segment for affected direction. |
| $z_i$ | Cancellation; relaxes all timing constraints via big-$M$. |
| $w_{i,s}$ | Extra dwell indicator; allows recovery time at stations. |
| $\theta_i$ | Selects whether train passes before $T_{start}$ or after $T_{end}$ on blocked track. |
| $\xi_{i,j,s}$ | Track-sharing indicator; activates headway constraints only when trains share a physical track. |
| $\lambda_{i,s,k}$ | PWL weights for energy linearization. |
| $\delta^a,\delta^d$ | Positive delay deviations from schedule. |

### Key Modeling Choices
1. **Simultaneous timetable + speed**: $rt_{i,s}$ couples both via (3) and (8)–(12).
2. **Local rerouting**: $y_{i,d}$ lets affected trains use the opposite track during the window, with bidirectional headway constraints (16′)–(17′) and (20).
3. **Disruption window**: (13a)–(13c) enforce that non-rerouted trains either clear the segment before $T_{start}$ or enter after $T_{end}$.
4. **Energy**: convex PWL keeps the LP relaxation tight at breakpoints.
5. **Cancellation**: big-$M$ relaxation (24)–(27) removes cancelled trains from the timetable.

### Solvability Notes
- The model is a **MILP** with $O(|I|^2|Seg|)$ binaries from $x$ and $\xi$, plus $O(|I||Seg|)$ from $y,w$ and $O(|I|)$ from $z,\theta$.
- For realistic instances (10–50 trains, 5–20 stations), commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) handle this within minutes.
- For large $|I|$, symmetry-breaking on $x_{i,j,s}$ and decomposition (the paper's IP + train-plan selection scheme) are recommended.

# Best Model: Integrated MILP for Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

After evaluating the three generated models, **Model 1** is selected as the best. It is the most complete and rigorous: it explicitly handles the disruption window on the blocked segment, provides a clean piecewise-linear (PWL) formulation of the $v^2$ energy term with binary selectors, correctly links the speed profile to the timetable via occupancy binaries, and includes rerouting continuity and bidirectional conflict resolution. Below is the finalized, self-contained model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, $s \in \{0,1,\dots,|S|\}$ |
| $K$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations, indexed by $k$ |
| $K(s,s+1)$ | Segment connecting station $s$ to $s+1$ |
| $T$ | Set of discrete time periods, $t \in \{0,1,\dots,|T|\}$ |
| $D = \{\text{up},\text{down}\}$ | Running directions; $D_i$ = direction of train $i$ |
| $O_i, \hat{D}_i$ | Origin and destination stations of train $i$ |
| $T_b = [T_b^{\text{start}}, T_b^{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window on blocked segment $k_b$ |
| $N_v$ | Number of breakpoints for PWL approximation of $v^2$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $a_i^s, d_i^s$ | Scheduled arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | s |
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ | m |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum/minimum operating speed | m/s |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / braking deceleration | m/s² |
| $\tau_{\min}^s, \tau_{\max}^s$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway time | s |
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization step | s |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) | — |
| $C^{\text{delay}}, C^{\text{energy}}, C^{\text{cancel}}$ | Cost coefficients (delay, energy, cancellation) | €/min, €/kWh, € |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Energy coefficients (rolling resistance, drag, inertia) | — |
| $m_i$ | Mass of train $i$ | kg |
| $g$ | Gravitational acceleration (9.81) | m/s² |
| $\sigma_k$ | Gradient of segment $k$ | ‰ |
| $f^{\max}$ | Maximum traction/braking force | N |
| $\eta$ | Traction efficiency ($0<\eta\le1$) | — |
| $\bar{v}_n, \bar{v}_n^2$ | Speed and squared-speed breakpoints, $n=1,\dots,N_v$ | m/s, m²/s² |
| $s_n, b_n$ | Slope and intercept of $n$-th linear piece of $v^2$ | — |
| $\varepsilon$ | Small tolerance for occupancy linking | — |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Continuous
| Variable | Description | Domain |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| $x_i^s$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | $\ge 0$ |
| $y_i^s$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | $\ge 0$ |
| $v_{i,k,t}$ | Speed of train $i$ on segment $k$ at time $t$ | $[v^{\min}, v^{\max}]$ |
| $p_{i,k,t}$ | Position of train $i$ on segment $k$ at time $t$ | $[0, L_k]$ |
| $a_{i,k,t}$ | Acceleration of train $i$ on segment $k$ at time $t$ | $[-b^{\max}, a^{\max}]$ |
| $f_{i,k,t}$ | Traction force of train $i$ on segment $k$ at time $t$ | $[-f^{\max}, f^{\max}]$ |
| $v^2_{i,k,t}$ | Auxiliary variable equal to $v_{i,k,t}^2$ | $\ge 0$ |
| $e_i$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ | kWh |
| $\delta_i^s$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ | $\ge 0$ |
| $\Delta\tau_i^s$ | Additional (unscheduled) dwell time of train $i$ at $s$ | $\ge 0$ |

### Binary
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $w_i$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $r_{i,k}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted (uses opposite track) on segment $k$ |
| $o_{i,j,k}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ |
| $u_{i,k,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $k$ at time $t$ |
| $q_{i,k,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters segment $k$ at time $t$ |
| $\theta_{i,k,t,n}$ | 1 if the $n$-th piece of the $v^2$ PWL is active for $(i,k,t)$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min Z \;=\; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S} C^{\text{delay}}\,\delta_i^s}_{\text{delay cost}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in I} C^{\text{energy}}\, e_i}_{\text{energy cost}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in I} C^{\text{cancel}}\, w_i}_{\text{cancellation cost}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Dwell Time
$$
\tau_{\min}^s\,(1-w_i) \;\le\; y_i^s - x_i^s \;\le\; \tau_{\max}^s\,(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,\; s
$$

### 5.2 Running Time (Segment Traversal)
For each segment $k = K(s,s+1)$:
$$
\frac{L_k}{v^{\max}}(1-w_i) \;\le\; x_i^{s+1} - y_i^s \;\le\; \frac{L_k}{v^{\min}}(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,\; s
$$

### 5.3 Speed Dynamics (Linearized Motion)
$$
v_{i,k,t+1} = v_{i,k,t} + a_{i,k,t}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
p_{i,k,t+1} = p_{i,k,t} + v_{i,k,t}\,\Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2}\,a_{i,k,t}\,\Delta t^2 \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

### 5.4 Speed, Acceleration, Position Bounds
$$
v^{\min}(1-w_i) \le v_{i,k,t} \le v^{\max}(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
-b^{\max}(1-w_i) \le a_{i,k,t} \le a^{\max}(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
0 \le p_{i,k,t} \le L_k(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

### 5.5 Terminal Conditions
$$
p_{i,k,0} = 0, \qquad p_{i,k,|T|} = L_k(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,k
$$
$$
v_{i,k,0} = v_{i,k,|T|} = 0 \qquad \forall i,k
$$

### 5.6 Headway (Same Direction, Same Track)
For $i \neq j$ with $D_i = D_j$ sharing segment $k$:
$$
x_j^s - x_i^s \;\ge\; h_{\min}\bigl(o_{i,j,k} - 1\bigr) + h_{\min} \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; s
$$
$$
y_j^s - y_i^s \;\ge\; h_{\min}\bigl(o_{i,j,k} - 1\bigr) + h_{\min} \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; s
$$

### 5.7 Segment Occupancy (Linking Speed Profile to Timetable)
$$
\sum_{i \in I} u_{i,k,t} \le 1 \qquad \forall k,t
$$
$$
u_{i,k,t} \;\ge\; \frac{p_{i,k,t}}{L_k} - \varepsilon \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
u_{i,k,t} \;\le\; \frac{p_{i,k,t}}{L_k} + \varepsilon \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

### 5.8 Disruption Constraints (Blocked Segment)
For $t \in T_b$:
$$
u_{i,k_b,t} \;\le\; r_{i,k_b} \qquad \forall i,\; t \in T_b
$$
$$
u_{i,k_b,t} = 0 \qquad \forall i,\; t \in T_b \quad \text{if } r_{i,k_b}=0
$$

### 5.9 Rerouting Constraints
$$
\sum_{t \in T_b} u_{i,k_b,t} \;\ge\; 1 - M(1-r_{i,k_b}) \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T_b} u_{i,k_b,t} \;\le\; M\,r_{i,k_b} \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
r_{i,k} = 0 \quad \forall k \neq k_b \qquad \text{(rerouting only on blocked segment)}
$$

### 5.10 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution
For $i \neq j$ with $D_i \neq D_j$ on segment $k$:
$$
o_{i,j,k} + o_{j,i,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; k
$$
$$
x_j^{s+1} - x_i^s \;\ge\; h_{\min}\,o_{i,j,k} - M(1-o_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; k
$$
$$
x_i^{s+1} - x_j^s \;\ge\; h_{\min}\,o_{j,i,k} - M(1-o_{j,i,k}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; k
$$

### 5.11 Cancellation Constraints
$$
x_i^s \le M(1-w_i), \qquad y_i^s \le M(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,s
$$
$$
v_{i,k,t} \le M(1-w_i), \qquad p_{i,k,t} \le M(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
\sum_{t} q_{i,k,t} = 1 - w_i \qquad \forall i,k
$$

### 5.12 Delay Calculation
$$
\delta_i^s \;\ge\; x_i^s - a_i^s \qquad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\delta_i^s \;\ge\; 0 \qquad \forall i,s
$$

### 5.13 Energy Consumption (Linearized)
**Traction force balance:**
$$
f_{i,k,t} = m_i\,a_{i,k,t} + \alpha + \beta\,v_{i,k,t} + m_i\,g\,\sigma_k \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

**Piecewise-linear approximation of $v^2$:**
$$
\sum_{n=1}^{N_v} \theta_{i,k,t,n} = 1 \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
v_{i,k,t} \;\ge\; \bar{v}_{n-1}\,\theta_{i,k,t,n} \qquad \forall i,k,t,\; n
$$
$$
v_{i,k,t} \;\le\; \bar{v}_n\,\theta_{i,k,t,n} + M(1-\theta_{i,k,t,n}) \qquad \forall i,k,t,\; n
$$
$$
v^2_{i,k,t} \;\le\; s_n\,v_{i,k,t} + b_n + M(1-\theta_{i,k,t,n}) \qquad \forall i,k,t,\; n
$$
$$
v^2_{i,k,t} \;\ge\; s_n\,v_{i,k,t} + b_n - M(1-\theta_{i,k,t,n}) \qquad \forall i,k,t,\; n
$$

**Total energy:**
$$
e_i = \frac{1}{\eta}\sum_{k \in K}\sum_{t \in T} f_{i,k,t}\,v_{i,k,t}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall i
$$

### 5.14 Traction Force Limits
$$
-f^{\max}(1-w_i) \le f_{i,k,t} \le f^{\max}(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

### 5.15 Station Dwell Coordination
$$
y_i^s - x_i^s = (d_i^s - a_i^s) + \Delta\tau_i^s \qquad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\Delta\tau_i^s \ge 0 \qquad \forall i,s
$$

### 5.16 Ordering Consistency (Transitivity)
$$
o_{i,j,k} + o_{j,l,k} - o_{i,l,k} \le 1 \qquad \forall i \neq j \neq l,\; k
$$
$$
o_{i,j,k} + o_{j,i,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; k
$$

### 5.17 Initial and Final Conditions
$$
x_i^{O_i} \ge a_i^{O_i} \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
y_i^{\hat{D}_i} \le d_i^{\hat{D}_i} + \Delta^{\max} \qquad \forall i
$$

### 5.18 Segment Traversal Completeness
$$
\sum_{t \in T} q_{i,k,t} = 1 - w_i \qquad \forall i,k
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T} u_{i,k,t} \;\ge\; \frac{L_k}{v^{\max}\,\Delta t}(1-w_i) \qquad \forall i,k
$$
$$
q_{i,k,t} \le u_{i,k,t}, \qquad q_{i,k,t} \ge u_{i,k,t} - u_{i,k,t-1} \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

### 5.19 Rerouting Continuity
$$
r_{i,k_b} \;\le\; \sum_{t \in T_b} u_{i,k_b,t} \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
p_{i,k_b,t} \;\ge\; L_k\,r_{i,k_b} - M(1-u_{i,k_b,t}) \qquad \forall i,\; t \in T_b
$$

### 5.20 Non-Negativity and Binary Domains
$$
x_i^s, y_i^s, v_{i,k,t}, p_{i,k,t}, a_{i,k,t}, f_{i,k,t}, e_i, \delta_i^s, \Delta\tau_i^s, v^2_{i,k,t} \ge 0
$$
$$
w_i, r_{i,k}, o_{i,j,k}, u_{i,k,t}, q_{i,k,t}, \theta_{i,k,t,n} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Linearization Techniques

| Non-linearity | Technique |
|---------------|-----------|
| $v^2$ in energy function | Piecewise-linear approximation with breakpoints $\bar{v}_n$ and binary selectors $\theta_{i,k,t,n}$ |
| $f \cdot v$ (force × speed) | Linear after PWL of $v^2$ (force is linear in $a$ and $v$) |
| Indicator constraints ($w_i=1 \Rightarrow \cdot=0$) | Big-M with $M$ |
| Disjunctive occupancy | Binary $u_{i,k,t}$ linked to $p_{i,k,t}$ via $\varepsilon$-tolerance |
| Train ordering | Binary $o_{i,j,k}$ with big-M headway relaxation |
| Rerouting activation | Big-M linking $r_{i,k_b}$ to occupancy counts |

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. Time and space are uniformly discretized.
2. Homogeneous train fleet (identical mass and traction characteristics).
3. Only one segment is disrupted at a time, with a known time window $T_b$.
4. Rerouting is permitted only on the blocked segment $k_b$.
5. Energy includes traction, aerodynamic resistance, and gradient effects; regenerative braking is allowed.
6. Minimum headway is enforced for safety.
7. Cancellation is allowed as a last resort.
8. Bidirectional trains share track resources during rerouting.

---

## 8. Model Summary

The proposed MILP integrates **train rescheduling** (timetable-level: $x_i^s, y_i^s, w_i, r_{i,k}$) with **speed management** (trajectory-level: $v_{i,k,t}, a_{i,k,t}, f_{i,k,t}$) under a partial segment blockage. Key features:

1. **Unified decision framework** — simultaneously determines cancellations, rerouting, and speed profiles.
2. **Disruption handling** — constraints (5.8)–(5.9) and (5.19) ensure the blocked side is unused during $T_b$ unless rerouted, and rerouting is confined to $k_b$.
3. **Bidirectional safety** — constraints (5.10) and (5.16) prevent collisions when opposite-direction trains share a track.
4. **Energy-aware operations** — PWL $v^2$ approximation (5.13) preserves MILP structure while capturing gradient and resistance effects.
5. **Multi-objective trade-off** — the objective balances passenger delay, energy use, and cancellation via tunable cost coefficients.

The resulting large-scale MILP is suitable for decomposition (Benders, column generation) or direct solution by modern solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, HiGHS) for practical instance sizes after appropriate time/space aggregation.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete, linear MILP for the TRSMP under a partial segment blockage with local rerouting.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Stations, ordered along the corridor |
| $E = \{1,\dots,|S|-1\}$ | Segments, $e=(s,s+1)$ |
| $T$ | Trains, indexed $i,j$ |
| $D = \{0,1\}$ | Directions (0 = up/forward, 1 = down/backward) |
| $K$ | Discrete speed levels |
| $P = \{1,\dots,|P|\}$ | Discretized positions along a segment |
| $W$ | Disruption time window |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ |
| $v_k$ | Speed of level $k$ (increasing in $k$) |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration |
| $t^{\min}_{\text{dwell}}, t^{\max}_{\text{dwell}}$ | Dwell time bounds |
| $t^{\min}_{i,e}, t^{\max}_{i,e}$ | Min/max running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $t_{\text{head}}$ | Minimum same-direction headway |
| $t_{\text{clear}}$ | Minimum opposing-train clearance time |
| $E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e,k}$ | Energy for train $i$ on segment $e$ at speed level $k$ |
| $w_{\text{time}}, w_{\text{energy}}, w_{\text{cancel}}$ | Objective weights |
| $t^{\text{arr,sched}}_{i,s}, t^{\text{dep,sched}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $\text{disr}_e$ | 1 if segment $e$ is disrupted |
| $\text{block\_dir}_e$ | Blocked direction on segment $e$ |
| $t^{\text{start}}_e, t^{\text{end}}_e$ | Disruption window on segment $e$ |
| $\text{orig\_dir}_i$ | Original direction of train $i$ |
| $\text{cancel\_allowed}_i$ | 1 if train $i$ may be cancelled |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (≥ 0):**
- $\text{arr}_{i,s}$ — arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\text{dep}_{i,s}$ — departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $\text{run}_{i,e}$ — running time of train $i$ on segment $e$
- $\text{dwell}_{i,s}$ — dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\text{delay}_{i,s}$ — delay of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\text{pos}_{i,e,p}$ — time train $i$ reaches position $p$ on segment $e$

**Binary:**
- $x_{i,e,k}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $e$
- $y_{i,e}$ — 1 if train $i$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $e$
- $z_{i,e}$ — 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$
- $\text{cancel}_i$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $o_{i,j,e}$ — 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$ (same direction)
- $u_{i,j,e}$ — 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $e$ before train $j$ (opposite direction, single-track)
- $\alpha_{i,e}, \beta_{i,e}$ — 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ before / after the disruption window

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; w_{\text{time}}\sum_{i,s}\text{delay}_{i,s}
\;+\; w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{i,e,k} E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e,k}\, x_{i,e,k}
\;+\; w_{\text{cancel}}\sum_{i}\text{cancel}_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Delay definition
$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge \text{arr}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr,sched}}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s} - t^{\text{dep,sched}}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge 0 \quad \forall i,s
$$

### (C2) Time propagation
$$
\text{arr}_{i,s+1} = \text{dep}_{i,s} + \text{run}_{i,(s,s+1)} \quad \forall i,\; s=1,\dots,|S|-1
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} = \text{arr}_{i,s} + \text{dwell}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,\; s=2,\dots,|S|-1
$$

### (C3) Dwell time bounds
$$
t^{\min}_{\text{dwell}} \le \text{dwell}_{i,s} \le t^{\max}_{\text{dwell}} \quad \forall i,s
$$

### (C4) Running time and speed-level selection
$$
t^{\min}_{i,e}\, z_{i,e} \le \text{run}_{i,e} \le t^{\max}_{i,e}\, z_{i,e} \quad \forall i,e
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,e,k} = z_{i,e} \quad \forall i,e
$$
$$
\text{run}_{i,e} = \sum_{k \in K} \frac{L_e}{v_k}\, x_{i,e,k} \quad \forall i,e
$$

### (C5) Position–time alignment
For $e=(s,s+1)$:
$$
\text{pos}_{i,e,1} = \text{dep}_{i,s}, \qquad \text{pos}_{i,e,|P|} = \text{arr}_{i,s+1}
$$
$$
\text{pos}_{i,e,p+1} \ge \text{pos}_{i,e,p} + \frac{L_e/|P|}{v_{\max}}\, z_{i,e}
$$
$$
\text{pos}_{i,e,p+1} \le \text{pos}_{i,e,p} + \frac{L_e/|P|}{v_{\min}}\, z_{i,e}
$$

### (C6) Rerouting logic
$$
y_{i,e} \le \text{disr}_e, \qquad y_{i,e} \le z_{i,e} \quad \forall i,e
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \ge t^{\text{start}}_e - M(1-y_{i,e}) \quad \forall i,\; e=(s,s+1)
$$
$$
\text{arr}_{i,s+1} \le t^{\text{end}}_e + M(1-y_{i,e}) \quad \forall i,\; e=(s,s+1)
$$

### (C7) Same-direction headway
For $i,j$ with $\text{orig\_dir}_i = \text{orig\_dir}_j$, $e=(s,s+1)$:
$$
\text{dep}_{j,s} \ge \text{arr}_{i,s+1} + t_{\text{head}} - M(1-o_{i,j,e}) - M(1-z_{i,e}) - M(1-z_{j,e})
$$
$$
o_{i,j,e} + o_{j,i,e} = 1
$$

### (C8) Opposing-train conflict on single-track
For $i,j$ with opposite directions, $e=(s,s+1)$:
$$
\text{dep}_{j,s'} \ge \text{arr}_{i,s+1} + t_{\text{clear}} - M(1-u_{i,j,e}) - M(1-y_{i,e}) - M(1-y_{j,e})
$$
$$
u_{i,j,e} + u_{j,i,e} = 1
$$

### (C9) Cancellation coupling
$$
z_{i,e} \le 1 - \text{cancel}_i \quad \forall i,e
$$
$$
\text{cancel}_i \le \text{cancel\_allowed}_i \quad \forall i
$$
$$
\text{arr}_{i,s} \le M(1-\text{cancel}_i), \qquad \text{dep}_{i,s} \le M(1-\text{cancel}_i) \quad \forall i,s
$$

### (C10) Disruption blocking
For affected $e$ with blocked direction $\text{block\_dir}_e$, and train $i$ with $\text{orig\_dir}_i = \text{block\_dir}_e$:
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \le t^{\text{start}}_e + M(1-\alpha_{i,e}), \qquad
\text{arr}_{i,s+1} \ge t^{\text{end}}_e - M(1-\beta_{i,e})
$$
$$
z_{i,e} \le y_{i,e} + (1-\text{disr}_e) + \alpha_{i,e} + \beta_{i,e}
$$

### (C11) Domains
$$
\text{arr},\text{dep},\text{run},\text{dwell},\text{delay},\text{pos} \ge 0
$$
$$
x,y,z,\text{cancel},o,u,\alpha,\beta \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

**Objective.** A weighted sum of three terms: (i) total schedule deviation (delay), (ii) traction energy from the chosen speed levels, and (iii) a fixed penalty per cancelled train. Weights let the dispatcher trade punctuality against energy and service loss.

**Delay definition (C1).** Linearizes $|\text{actual} - \text{scheduled}|$ from above using two inequalities; since the objective minimizes delay, the LP relaxation pushes it to the true positive deviation.

**Time propagation (C2).** Links arrival, departure, dwell, and running times along the route — the backbone of the timetable.

**Dwell bounds (C3).** Enforces realistic station stop durations.

**Running time / speed selection (C4).** The binary $x_{i,e,k}$ picks exactly one speed level per traversed segment. Running time is then the segment length divided by that speed. The $z_{i,e}$ factor switches the bounds off for cancelled or non-traversed segments.

**Position–time alignment (C5).** Couples the discrete speed profile to the continuous timetable by requiring the position–time curve to advance at a rate consistent with the chosen speed. This is a linear approximation of train dynamics (Assumption A4).

**Rerouting logic (C6).** $y_{i,e}$ can only be 1 on disrupted segments and only if the train actually traverses the segment. The two big-M constraints force the train's occupancy of the segment to lie inside the disruption window when rerouting.

**Same-direction headway (C7).** Sequencing variable $o_{i,j,e}$ enforces that consecutive trains in the same direction are separated by at least $t_{\text{head}}$. The complementarity $o_{i,j,e}+o_{j,i,e}=1$ ensures a total order.

**Opposing-train conflict (C8).** When two trains in opposite directions both reroute onto the same single-track segment, $u_{i,j,e}$ enforces that only one direction occupies the segment at a time, separated by $t_{\text{clear}}$. This is the core safety constraint for single-track operation.

**Cancellation coupling (C9).** Cancelled trains are removed from all segment operations ($z_{i,e}=0$) and their times are driven to zero. Cancellation is only allowed if the train is flagged as cancellable.

**Disruption blocking (C10).** A train travelling in the blocked direction on a disrupted segment must either reroute ($y_{i,e}=1$) or traverse the segment entirely outside the disruption window (captured by $\alpha_{i,e}, \beta_{i,e}$).

**Domains (C11).** Standard non-negativity and binary restrictions.

---

## 7. Structural Notes

- **Linear**: All constraints are linear; the only nonlinearity (speed × binary) is handled by the discrete speed-level selection.
- **Decomposable**: The model separates naturally into an integer master (train ordering $o$, $u$, rerouting $y$, cancellation) and per-train continuous subproblems (times, speed profiles), making it suitable for Lagrangian or Benders decomposition.
- **Conflict-free guarantee**: Constraints (C7)–(C8) plus (C10) ensure that the resulting timetable is safe under both normal and single-track operation.
- **Energy efficiency**: The objective explicitly trades off energy against delay, so the optimizer will choose lower speed levels when the schedule permits.

# A Complete MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management with Rerouting, Reordering, and Rescheduling

## 1. Model Overview

Based on the introduction, I formulate a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for the real-time railway traffic management problem (rtRTMP). The model follows the multi-stage decomposition described in the paper: it determines (i) route selection, (ii) train ordering, and (iii) rescheduling (timing) to minimize overall delays, while accounting for delay propagation.

The formulation is inspired by the reference models of Pellegrini et al. (2014, 2015, 2019) and the pair-wise delay interpretation proposed in the paper. Assumptions that are not explicitly stated in the input are marked as **[Assumption]**.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $B$ | Set of block sections (track segments), indexed by $b$ |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$, indexed by $r$ |
| $B_{ir} \subseteq B$ | Set of block sections traversed by train $i$ on route $r$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations / junctions, indexed by $s$ **[Assumption: used for capacity constraints]** |
| $B_s \subseteq B$ | Set of block sections belonging to station/junction $s$ **[Assumption]** |
| $O_b$ | Set of ordered pairs $(i,j)$ of trains that can potentially conflict on block $b$ |
| $P$ | Set of pairs of trains $(i,j)$ that share at least one block section |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $d_i$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from its origin |
| $a_i$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at its destination |
| $t_{irb}^{\text{run}}$ | Running time of train $i$ on block $b$ using route $r$ |
| $h_b$ | Minimum headway (safety separation time) on block $b$ |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $w_i$ | Weight (priority) of train $i$ in the objective **[Assumption: $w_i = 1$ unless priorities are given]** |
| $\tau_{ir}^{\text{min}}$ | Minimum travel time of train $i$ on route $r$ (sum of running times) |
| $\delta_i^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed delay for train $i$ **[Assumption: operational limit]** |
| $c_b$ | Capacity of block $b$ (max simultaneous trains) **[Assumption: typically 1 for single-track blocks]** |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Routing Variables
$$
x_{ir} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ r \in R_i
$$
$=1$ if train $i$ is assigned to route $r$, $0$ otherwise.

### 4.2 Ordering Variables
$$
y_{ijb} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in O_b,\ b \in B
$$
$=1$ if train $i$ uses block $b$ before train $j$, $0$ otherwise.

### 4.3 Timing Variables
$$
e_{ib} \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B_{ir}
$$
Entry time of train $i$ into block $b$.

$$
l_{ib} \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B_{ir}
$$
Exit (leaving) time of train $i$ from block $b$.

### 4.4 Delay Variables
$$
\delta_i \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in T
$$
Total delay of train $i$ at its destination.

$$
\delta_i^{\text{prop}} \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in T
$$
Propagated delay component of train $i$ **[Assumption: used to capture delay propagation as in the paper's extended model]**.

### 4.5 Pair-wise Delay Variables
$$
z_{ij} \ge 0, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P
$$
Delay incurred by train $j$ due to waiting for train $i$ (pair-wise delay interpretation).

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delays, including propagated delays:

$$
\min \quad Z = \sum_{i \in T} w_i \cdot \delta_i + \alpha \sum_{i \in T} \delta_i^{\text{prop}} + \beta \sum_{(i,j) \in P} z_{ij}
$$

where:
- $\alpha \ge 0$ is a weight penalizing delay propagation **[Assumption: $\alpha = 1$ if not specified]**,
- $\beta \ge 0$ is a weight on pair-wise delays **[Assumption: $\beta$ small, e.g., $\beta = 0.1$, to prioritize global delay minimization]**.

**[Assumption]** The primary objective is total delay minimization, consistent with the paper's statement: *"Usually, the optimization goal is to minimize train delays, as in the proposed method."*

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route Selection Constraints

Each train must be assigned exactly one route:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{ir} = 1, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{1}
$$

### 6.2 Block Usage Linking

Train $i$ uses block $b$ if and only if it is assigned to a route containing $b$:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i : b \in B_{ir}} x_{ir} \le u_{ib} \le \sum_{r \in R_i : b \in B_{ir}} x_{ir}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ b \in B \tag{2}
$$

where $u_{ib} \in \{0,1\}$ is an auxiliary variable indicating block usage **[Assumption: introduced to simplify linking constraints]**.

### 6.3 Running Time Constraints

For each train and each block on its chosen route, the traversal time must be at least the minimum running time:

$$
l_{ib} - e_{ib} \ge t_{irb}^{\text{run}} - M(1 - x_{ir}), \quad \forall i \in T,\ r \in R_i,\ b \in B_{ir} \tag{3}
$$

### 6.4 Route Continuity (Precedence Within a Route)

For consecutive blocks $b_1, b_2$ in route $r$ of train $i$:

$$
e_{ib_2} \ge l_{ib_1}, \quad \forall i \in T,\ r \in R_i,\ (b_1, b_2) \in \text{seq}(r) \tag{4}
$$

where $\text{seq}(r)$ denotes the ordered sequence of consecutive block pairs in route $r$.

### 6.5 Departure Time Constraints

Each train cannot depart before its scheduled departure time:

$$
e_{ib_0} \ge d_i, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{5}
$$

where $b_0$ is the first block of the chosen route.

### 6.6 Headway / Safety Constraints (Ordering)

For any pair of trains $(i,j)$ that can conflict on block $b$:

$$
e_{jb} \ge l_{ib} + h_b - M(1 - y_{ijb}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in O_b,\ b \in B \tag{6}
$$

$$
e_{ib} \ge l_{jb} + h_b - M \cdot y_{ijb}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in O_b,\ b \in B \tag{7}
$$

These ensure that only one ordering is active and the minimum headway is respected.

### 6.7 Ordering Consistency

If both trains use block $b$, exactly one ordering must be selected:

$$
y_{ijb} + y_{jib} = 1, \quad \forall (i,j) \in O_b,\ b \in B \tag{8}
$$

**[Assumption]** This applies when both trains use block $b$; otherwise, the ordering variable is inactive via the big-M constraints.

### 6.8 Delay Computation

The delay of train $i$ is the difference between its actual and scheduled arrival:

$$
\delta_i \ge l_{ib_f} - a_i, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{9}
$$

where $b_f$ is the last block of the chosen route.

### 6.9 Delay Propagation Constraints

Propagated delay captures the effect of upstream delays on downstream trains:

$$
\delta_i^{\text{prop}} \ge \delta_i - \delta_i^{\text{primary}}, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{10}
$$

**[Assumption]** $\delta_i^{\text{primary}}$ is a parameter representing the primary delay (known disturbance) of train $i$; if not given, $\delta_i^{\text{primary}} = 0$.

### 6.10 Pair-wise Delay Linking

The pair-wise delay $z_{ij}$ captures the waiting time of train $j$ for train $i$:

$$
z_{ij} \ge e_{jb} - l_{ib} - h_b - M(1 - y_{ijb}), \quad \forall (i,j) \in P,\ b \in B_{ir} \cap B_{jr} \tag{11}
$$

$$
z_{ij} \ge 0, \quad \forall (i,j) \in P \tag{12}
$$

### 6.11 Maximum Delay Constraints

Each train's delay must not exceed the operational limit:

$$
\delta_i \le \delta_i^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{13}
$$

### 6.12 Block Capacity Constraints

For each block $b$, the number of trains simultaneously occupying it must not exceed capacity:

$$
\sum_{i \in T} u_{ib} \le c_b, \quad \forall b \in B \tag{14}
$$

**[Assumption]** For single-track blocks, $c_b = 1$; for multi-track, $c_b \ge 2$.

### 6.13 Station / Junction Capacity Constraints

For each station $s$ and each time window $[t_1, t_2]$ **[Assumption: discretized time windows]**:

$$
\sum_{i \in T} \sum_{b \in B_s} \mathbb{1}_{[t_1, t_2]}(e_{ib}) \le C_s \tag{15}
$$

where $C_s$ is the capacity of station $s$. **[Assumption: this constraint may be linearized using time-indexed variables if needed.]**

### 6.14 FIFO Policy (Optional Soft Constraint)

To optionally enforce or penalize deviation from FIFO:

$$
y_{ijb} \ge 1 - M \cdot \max(0, d_j - d_i), \quad \forall (i,j) \in O_b \tag{16}
$$

**[Assumption]** This is a soft FIFO preference; the model may deviate if it reduces total delay.

### 6.15 Variable Domains

$$
x_{ir} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{ijb} \in \{0,1\}, \quad u_{ib} \in \{0,1\} \tag{17}
$$

$$
e_{ib}, l_{ib}, \delta_i, \delta_i^{\text{prop}}, z_{ij} \ge 0 \tag{18}
$$

---

## 7. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{i \in T} w_i \delta_i + \alpha \sum_{i \in T} \delta_i^{\text{prop}} + \beta \sum_{(i,j) \in P} z_{ij} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & (1) - (18)
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 8. Assumptions and Remarks

1. **Route pre-selection**: The model assumes a finite set of feasible routes $R_i$ per train, consistent with the paper's TRSP approach.
2. **Big-M values**: $M$ should be chosen as a tight upper bound on the maximum possible time difference, e.g., $M = \max_{i} \delta_i^{\max} + \max_{b} h_b$.
3. **Delay propagation**: The term $\delta_i^{\text{prop}}$ is included to capture the extended model described in the paper (Section 3.3), which guarantees global optimality.
4. **Pair-wise delays**: The variables $z_{ij}$ implement the pair-wise delay interpretation mentioned in the paper (Section 3.1), which enables the sub-optimal but fast solution.
5. **Overlaps**: The model can be extended to include safety-relevant overlaps (Lindenmaier et al., 2022) by adding constraints on the clearance of overlap sections behind stop signals **[Assumption: not detailed here for brevity]**.
6. **Computational efficiency**: The decomposition into rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling can be implemented by fixing $x_{ir}$ and $y_{ijb}$ from a first-stage solution and re-solving the timing variables, as described in the paper's multi-stage framework.
7. **Time discretization**: For station capacity constraints, a time-indexed formulation may be required; alternatively, continuous-time constraints with cumulative variables can be used (Meng and Zhou, 2014).

---

## 9. References (as cited in the input)

- Pellegrini et al. (2014, 2015, 2019) — reference MILP models for rtRTMP.
- Samà et al. (2016) — train route selection problem (TRSP).
- Keita et al. (2016, 2020) — Benders decomposition for rtRTMP.
- Lindenmaier et al. (2022) — extended rtRTMP with safety-relevant overlaps.
- Meng and Zhou (2014) — cumulative flow variables for simultaneous rerouting and rescheduling.

---

This model provides a complete, linear, and solvable MILP formulation for the real-time railway traffic management problem, integrating rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling with delay propagation, consistent with the paper's contributions.
