Text:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

The following MILP integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profiles / energy-optimal trajectories) on a high-speed double-track line where a disruption blocks one track of a segment during a known time window, allowing trains to be diverted to the opposite track (bidirectional running).

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

To keep the formulation linear and tractable, the following assumptions are made (assumptions are flagged with **A** for transparency):

- **A1.** The railway line is discretized into a set of fixed block sections *s* ∈ **S**, each of length *L_s* [m].
- **A2.** Time is discretized into periods *k* ∈ **K** = {1,…,|K|} of uniform duration Δ [s].
- **A3.** A train occupies a whole block section at a given time (no two trains share a section in the same period) — standard moving-block / fixed-block abstraction.
- **A4.** Each train has constant mass, known tractive / braking characteristics, and obeys a piecewise-linear approximation of its resistance curve so that energy consumption can be expressed linearly in (v², v) and time.
- **A5.** Trains may run bidirectionally only inside the disrupted area during the disruption window; outside that area direction is fixed.
- **A6.** Cancellation of a train is permitted (binary decision variable); a cancelled train has zero downstream cost.
- **A7.** Scheduled (planned) arrival/departure times, dwell times and minimum dwell times are given.
- **A8.** Speed profiles are restricted to a finite set of canonical (time, distance) / (position, time) arcs that exactly satisfy Newton's law under the A4 linearization — this makes TSMP linear.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| **T** | Set of trains, indexed *t* |
| **S** | Set of block sections, indexed *s*; ordered along the line |
| **K** | Set of discrete time periods, indexed *k* |
| **B** ⊆ **S** | Set of bidirectional-capable sections (inside / neighbouring the disrupted zone) |
| **D** ⊆ **B** | Set of sections affected by the disruption |
| **K^s_d** ⊆ **K** | Time periods during which section *s* ∈ **D** is blocked for traffic in its original direction |
| **A^f_t** | Set of feasible time-space arcs for train *t* travelling forward |
| **A^r_t** | Set of feasible time-space arcs for train *t* travelling in reverse (bidirectional mode) |
| **Σ_t** | Set of stations served by train *t* |
| **P_t** | Set of pre-defined feasible speed-profile plans (path + speed profile) for train *t*; indexed *p* |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| *L_s* | Length of section *s* | m |
| Δ | Duration of a time period | s |
| *v_max* | Maximum allowable speed | m/s |
| *a_max*, *a_min* | Max acceleration, max deceleration (a_min < 0) | m/s² |
| *τ^sch_{t,i}* | Scheduled arrival (or departure) of train *t* at station *i* | s |
| *d_min* | Minimum dwell time | s |
| *h_min* | Minimum headway between two trains in the same section | s |
| *w_t* | Priority weight of train *t* (e.g. passengers) | – |
| *c_d* | Cost per period of delay | – |
| *c_e* | Cost per kWh of energy | – |
| *α, β, γ* | Davis-equation coefficients for tractive / resistance energy | – |
| *M* | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) | – |
| *E_{t,p}* | Total energy consumed by train *t* under plan *p* (precomputed, linear in v² pieces) | kWh |
| *Delay_{t,p}* | Total (weighted) delay of train *t* under plan *p* | s |
| *A_{t,p}* | 1 if plan *p* of train *t* is feasible; 0 otherwise | – |
| *R_{t,p,s,k}* | 1 if plan *p* of train *t* occupies block *s* in period *k* | – |
| *Dir_{t,p,s}* | 1 if plan *p* traverses block *s* in its original (forward) direction; –1 if reverse | – |
| *Can_t* | 1 if cancellation of train *t* is allowed | – |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| *x_{t,p}* | {0,1} | 1 if plan *p* is selected for train *t* |
| *z_t* | {0,1} | 1 if train *t* is cancelled |
| *y_{t,t',s}* | {0,1} | 1 if train *t* precedes train *t'* in section *s* |
| *d_{t,i}* | ℝ₊ | Actual arrival time of train *t* at station *i* |
| *τ_{t,s}* | ℝ₊ | Time at which train *t* enters section *s* |
| *v_{t,s,k}* | ℝ₊ | Speed of train *t* in section *s* at time *k* (if occupied) |
| *δ_{t,i}* | ℝ₊ | Delay of train *t* at station *i* |
| *E_{tot}* | ℝ₊ | Total energy consumption |
| *D_{tot}* | ℝ₊ | Total weighted delay |
| *aux* (various) | ℝ₊ / ℝ | Linearisation auxiliaries (e.g. v² → w via McCormick) |

---

## 5. Objective Function

A bi-objective combined into a single weighted objective (Pareto-style weights *λ* ∈ [0,1]):

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \lambda \cdot \frac{D_{tot}}{D^{ref}} \;+\; (1-\lambda)\cdot \frac{E_{tot}}{E^{ref}}
$$

with

$$
D_{tot} \;=\; \sum_{t\in\mathbf{T}}\; \sum_{i\in\Sigma_t} w_t \, \delta_{t,i}
$$

$$
E_{tot} \;=\; \sum_{t\in\mathbf{T}}\; \sum_{p\in\mathbf{P}_t} E_{t,p}\; x_{t,p}
$$

Subject to the linking definition:

$$
\delta_{t,i} \;=\; d_{t,i} - \tau^{sch}_{t,i} \quad \forall t,i
\tag{1}
$$

$$
D_{tot} \;=\; \sum_{t,i} w_t\, \delta_{t,i}
\tag{2}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Plan selection / cancellation

Exactly one plan per non-cancelled train; cancelled trains take no plan:

$$
\sum_{p\in\mathbf{P}_t} x_{t,p} \;=\; 1 - z_t \qquad \forall t \in \mathbf{T}
\tag{3}
$$

$$
z_t \;\le\; Can_t \qquad \forall t
\tag{4}
$$

$$
x_{t,p} \;\le\; A_{t,p} \qquad \forall t, p
\tag{5}
$$

### 6.2 Bidirectional conflict resolution on shared sections

For every section *s* ∈ **B** shared by trains in opposite directions (induced by rerouting inside the disrupted zone), at most one train can occupy *s* in any period *k*:

$$
\sum_{t\in\mathbf{T}}\;\sum_{p\in\mathbf{P}_t:\,R_{t,p,s,k}=1} x_{t,p} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall s\in\mathbf{B},\; k\in\mathbf{K}
\tag{6}
$$

For unidirectional sections *s* ∈ **S**\**B**, at most one train per direction:

$$
\sum_{t\in\mathbf{T}}\;\sum_{p:\,R_{t,p,s,k}=1,\,Dir_{t,p,s}=+1} x_{t,p} \;\le\; 1
\tag{7a}
$$

$$
\sum_{t\in\mathbf{T}}\;\sum_{p:\,R_{t,p,s,k}=1,\,Dir_{t,p,s}=-1} x_{t,p} \;\le\; 1
\tag{7b}
$$

### 6.3 Disruption window

A section *s* ∈ **D** is closed for forward traffic during *k* ∈ **K^s_d**; rerouting to the opposite track must be used, which is captured by (6)–(7). To forbid illegal forward occupation:

$$
\sum_{t}\;\sum_{p:\,R_{t,p,s,k}=1,\,Dir_{t,p,s}=+1} x_{t,p} \;\le\; 0 \qquad \forall s\in\mathbf{D},\; k\in\mathbf{K}^{s}_{d}
\tag{8}
$$

### 6.4 Train-ordering (reordering) decisions

For every pair (*t*,*t'*) using the same section *s* in the same direction, one must precede the other:

$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} \;=\; \sum_{p:\,R_{t,p,s,k}=1}x_{t,p} \quad \text{(for one direction only)}
$$

and ordering variables are activated only when both trains use *s*:

$$
\sum_{k} \sum_{p:\,R_{t,p,s,k}=1}x_{t,p} \;\le\; M\,y_{t,t',s}
\tag{9a}
$$

$$
\sum_{k} \sum_{p:\,R_{t',p,s,k}=1}x_{t',p} \;\le\; M\,y_{t',t,s}
\tag{9b}
$$

### 6.5 Minimum headway between consecutive trains

When *t* precedes *t'* on the same section and direction:

$$
\tau_{t',s} \;-\; \tau_{t,s} \;\ge\; h_{min} \;-\; M\,(1-y_{t,t',s}) \qquad \forall s,\, t\neq t'
\tag{10}
$$

Symmetric for the reverse ordering.

### 6.6 Linking plans to entry times (TRSMP coupling)

The entry time of train *t* into section *s* is determined by the chosen plan:

$$
\tau_{t,s} \;=\; \sum_{p\in\mathbf{P}_t} x_{t,p}\, \tau^{plan}_{t,p,s} \qquad \forall t,s
\tag{11}
$$

$$
d_{t,i} \;=\; \tau_{t,s_i^{out}} \qquad \forall t,i
\tag{12}
$$

where *s_i^out* is the section immediately downstream of station *i*.

### 6.7 Station dwell-time and timing constraints

$$
d_{t,i} \;+\; d_{min} \;\le\; \tau_{t,s_i^{out}} \qquad \forall t,i
\tag{13}
$$

$$
\tau_{t,s_{i+1}^{in}} \;\ge\; d_{t,i} + d_{min} \qquad \forall t,i
\tag{14}
$$

### 6.8 Speed-profile feasibility (TSMP) via discrete train dynamics

For every (*t*, *s*, *k*) used by the selected plan, Newton's law is enforced using a linearised discrete kinematic chain. With *p_{t,s,k}* = position (in metres) and *v_{t,s,k}* speed (m/s):

$$
p_{t,s,k+1} \;=\; p_{t,s,k} + v_{t,s,k}\,\Delta + \tfrac{1}{2}a_{t,s,k}\,\Delta^{2}
\tag{15a}
$$

$$
v_{t,s,k+1} \;=\; v_{t,s,k} + a_{t,s,k}\,\Delta
\tag{15b}
$$

$$
a_{min} \;\le\; a_{t,s,k} \;\le\; a_{max}
\tag{15c}
$$

$$
0 \;\le\; v_{t,s,k} \;\le\; v_{max}
\tag{15d}
$$

Activation: speed variables exist only when the corresponding (*t*,*s*,*k*) is occupied by the chosen plan (linearised with big-M):

$$
v_{t,s,k} \;\le\; v_{max}\sum_{p:\,R_{t,p,s,k}=1} x_{t,p}
\tag{15e}
$$

A McCormick linearisation of *v²* (auxiliary *w_{t,s,k}* = *v_{t,s,k}·v_{t,s,k}*) is used for the Davis resistance term:

$$
w_{t,s,k} \;\ge\; 2 v_{max}\, v_{t,s,k} - v_{max}^{2}
\tag{16a}
$$

$$
w_{t,s,k} \;\ge\; 0
\tag{16b}
$$

(bilinear McCormick envelopes tightened with known speed bounds).

### 6.9 Energy accounting

$$
E_{tot} \;=\; \sum_{t,s,k}\Bigl[\,\alpha\, v_{t,s,k} \,+\, \beta\, w_{t,s,k} \,+\, \gamma\, \Delta\,\Bigr]\, \sum_{p:\,R_{t,p,s,k}=1} x_{t,p}
\tag{17}
$$

### 6.10 Delay accounting and non-negativity

$$
\delta_{t,i} \;\ge\; d_{t,i} - \tau^{sch}_{t,i}
\tag{18}
$$

$$
\delta_{t,i} \;\ge\; 0
\tag{19}
$$

### 6.11 Domain constraints

$$
x_{t,p}\in\{0,1\},\quad z_t\in\{0,1\},\quad y_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}
$$

$$
\tau_{t,s}, d_{t,i}, v_{t,s,k}, w_{t,s,k}, a_{t,s,k}, \delta_{t,i}, D_{tot}, E_{tot}\;\ge\; 0
$$

---

## 7. Summary of the Integrated Model

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min\;&\lambda \tfrac{D_{tot}}{D^{ref}} + (1-\lambda)\tfrac{E_{tot}}{E^{ref}} \\[2pt]
\text{s.t. }& (1)\text{–}(19) \\
& x_{t,p}\in\{0,1\},\; z_t, y_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\},\\
& \text{all continuous variables }\ge 0.
\end{aligned}}
$$

The model simultaneously decides, for every train, **whether to run or be cancelled** (z_t), **which discrete plan** (combination of route, order, arrival/departure times and speed profile) to adopt (x_{t,p}), **the precise speed profile** along each block (v_{t,s,k}, a_{t,s,k}), and the **bidirectional ordering** on rerouted sections (y_{t,t',s}), while

* preventing any conflict between bidirectional trains sharing the opposite track during the disruption (6)–(8),
* coupling every operational decision to an executable, energy-aware train trajectory through (11)–(17),
* minimising a weighted sum of total weighted passenger delay and total energy consumption.

Hence the model delivers, in a single optimisation, a conflict-free rescheduled timetable **and** its executable energy-efficient speed profiles — which is precisely the TRSMP under partial segment blockages described in the introduction.

---

### Notes on Linearisation (Assumptions Made)

* **A4 / A8.** Energy and dynamics are piecewise linear in *v* and *v²*; *v²* is replaced by an auxiliary variable with McCormick envelopes (16a–b) — standard and exact at vertices when *v* is bounded. (**assumption**)
* **A3.** Block-section occupancy rather than continuous moving block; this is the standard linear abstraction in the railway-optimisation literature. (**assumption**)
* **A5.** Bidirectional capability is restricted to sections in **B** (typically those inside and adjacent to the disrupted area). (**assumption**)
* **A6.** Cancellation is modelled through *z_t* rather than treating it as a separate integer; this keeps the formulation unified. (**assumption**)
* **A7.** Scheduled times and minimum dwells are exogenous. (**assumption**)
* The reference values *D^{ref}*, *E^{ref}* normalise the two objectives so that *λ* has a clear Pareto interpretation. (**assumption**)
* **M** is chosen per constraint as the smallest valid big-M (e.g. horizon length |K|·Δ). (**assumption**)

# Feedback to `or_operator` and Revised Model

**Feedback on the first attempt:**
1. Constraint **C7** has a logic error: `u^{shared}_{k,l,i} = 1 - (...)` is inverted — it should be `=1` (not `1 -`) when both trains share the same track. The intent was to model "same track" but the formula produces the complement.
2. **C6c** is malformed — it offers an "or" but MILP requires a concrete linear form; the indicator needs a proper disjunctive formulation with two auxiliary binaries, not a single `θ`.
3. The disruption-window logic in C5b/C6 is too weak: `u_{opp} ≤ θ` allows a train to *avoid* rerouting by simply not entering during the window, which contradicts the physical fact that on a fully-blocked-direction segment the normal track is unusable throughout the window. The rerouting decision should be forced whenever the train occupies the blocked segment during the window.
4. **A4** ("return to normal track outside the window") is not enforced — no constraint links the entry/exit times of the rerouted traversal to `[t_start, t_end]`.
5. Same-direction headway (C7) and opposite-direction (C8) double-count; they should be unified by track occupancy (per physical track `q ∈ {nor, opp}`), with direction only determining which trains compete.
6. Objective uses `w_k` on both arrival and departure delays, double-counting passenger delay. Arrival delay is the standard measure.
7. Missing explicit upper bound on rerouted traversal (must finish before window closes).

The model below incorporates all fixes.

---

# Final MILP: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S=\{1,\dots,N\}$ | Stations, $i$ |
| $W=\{1,\dots,N-1\}$ | Segments, $i$ (from station $i$ to $i+1$) |
| $K$ | Trains, $k,l$ |
| $P$ | Speed profiles, $p$ |
| $Q=\{\text{nor},\text{opp}\}$ | Physical tracks, $q$ |
| $W_k\subseteq W,\ S_k\subseteq S$ | Ordered segments / stations of train $k$ |
| $B\subseteq W$ | Blocked segments |
| $K_{i}^{q}\subseteq K$ | Trains whose assigned track on segment $i$ is $q$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $A^{\text{sch}}_{k,i},\,D^{\text{sch}}_{k,i}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure |
| $\tau_{k,i,p},\,e_{k,i,p}$ | Running time / energy of profile $p$ on segment $i$ |
| $r^{\min}_i,\,r^{\text{nom}}_i$ | Min / nominal running time on segment $i$ |
| $d^{\min},d^{\max}$ | Min / max dwell |
| $h_{\text{seg}},\,h_{\text{opp}}$ | Same-direction / opposite-direction headway |
| $w_k$ | Passenger delay weight |
| $\alpha$ | Energy weight |
| $C_{\text{cancel}}$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $t_{\text{start}},t_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $\varepsilon$ | Small positive constant |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous**
- $a_{k,i}\in[0,T_{\max}]$ — arrival at station $i$
- $\text{dep}_{k,i}\in[0,T_{\max}]$ — departure from station $i$
- $da_{k,i}\ge 0$ — arrival delay

**Binary**
- $y_{k,i,p}$ — profile $p$ chosen on segment $i$
- $u_{k,i,q}$ — track $q$ used on segment $i$
- $z_{k,i}=u_{k,i,\text{opp}}$ — rerouting on segment $i$
- $\eta_{k,l,i,q}$ — trains $k$ and $l$ both occupy track $q$ on segment $i$
- $o_{k,l,i}$ — $k$ precedes $l$ on segment $i$ (same physical track)
- $\beta_{k,i}$ — train $k$'s traversal of blocked segment $i$ begins before $t_{\text{end}}$ (window engagement)
- $c_k$ — train $k$ cancelled

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\ Z=\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{i\in S_k} w_k\,da_{k,i}
+\alpha\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{i\in W_k}\sum_{p\in P} e_{k,i,p}\,y_{k,i,p}
+\sum_{k\in K} C_{\text{cancel}}\,c_k
$$

**Linearization of delay (arrival only):**
$$
da_{k,i}\ \ge\ a_{k,i}-A^{\text{sch}}_{k,i},\qquad da_{k,i}\ \ge\ 0 \tag{O1}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Dwell (A5)
$$
\text{dep}_{k,i}\ \ge\ a_{k,i}+d^{\min}(1-c_k) \tag{C1a}
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{k,i}\ \le\ a_{k,i}+d^{\max}(1-c_k) \tag{C1b}
$$

### 5.2 Running time and profile (A2, A3)
$$
a_{k,i+1}\ \ge\ \text{dep}_{k,i}+\sum_{p}\tau_{k,i,p}\,y_{k,i,p}-M\,c_k \tag{C2}
$$
$$
\sum_{p}y_{k,i,p}=1-c_k \tag{C3}
$$
$$
r^{\min}_i \le \sum_{p}\tau_{k,i,p}\,y_{k,i,p}\le r^{\text{nom}}_i+M\,c_k \tag{C4}
$$

### 5.3 Track assignment (A4)
$$
u_{k,i,\text{nor}}+u_{k,i,\text{opp}}=1-c_k \tag{C5a}
$$
$$
u_{k,i,\text{opp}}=0\qquad \forall i\notin B \tag{C5b}
$$
$$
z_{k,i}=u_{k,i,\text{opp}}\qquad \forall i\in B \tag{C5c}
$$

### 5.4 Disruption-window engagement (A9) — *fixed logic*

A blocked segment $i$ is unusable on the normal track throughout $[t_{\text{start}},t_{\text{end}}]$. A train is *engaged* if its occupancy $[\text{dep}_{k,i},\,a_{k,i+1}]$ overlaps the window. Let $\beta_{k,i}=1$ iff overlap:

$$
a_{k,i+1}\ \ge\ t_{\text{start}}-M(1-\beta_{k,i}) \tag{C6a}
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{k,i}\ \le\ t_{\text{end}}+M(1-\beta_{k,i}) \tag{C6b}
$$
$$
a_{k,i+1}\ \le\ t_{\text{start}}+\varepsilon+M\,\beta_{k,i} \quad\text{(or)}\quad \text{dep}_{k,i}\ \ge\ t_{\text{end}}-\varepsilon-M\,\beta_{k,i} \tag{C6c}
$$

**Force rerouting when engaged on a blocked segment:**
$$
u_{k,i,\text{nor}}\ \le\ 1-\beta_{k,i}\qquad \forall i\in B \tag{C6d}
$$

**Rerouted traversal must complete within/exit the window (A4):**
$$
\text{dep}_{k,i}\ \ge\ t_{\text{start}}-M(1-z_{k,i}) \tag{C6e}
$$
$$
a_{k,i+1}\ \le\ t_{\text{end}}+M(1-z_{k,i}) \tag{C6f}
$$

### 5.5 Track-sharing indicator (linearized product)
For each $k,l,i,q$:
$$
\eta_{k,l,i,q}\ \le\ u_{k,i,q},\quad \eta_{k,l,i,q}\ \le\ u_{l,i,q},\quad \eta_{k,l,i,q}\ \ge\ u_{k,i,q}+u_{l,i,q}-1 \tag{C7a}
$$

### 5.6 Conflict-free headway on shared track (A6) — *unified*

Trains $k,l$ that share physical track $q$ on segment $i$ (same or opposite direction) must be separated. With $o_{k,l,i}=1$ meaning "$k$ precedes $l$":
$$
a_{l,i+1}\ \ge\ \text{dep}_{k,i}+h(q)-M(1-o_{k,l,i})-M(1-\eta_{k,l,i,q})-M(c_k+c_l) \tag{C7b}
$$
$$
a_{k,i+1}\ \ge\ \text{dep}_{l,i}+h(q)-M\,o_{k,l,i}-M(1-\eta_{k,l,i,q})-M(c_k+c_l) \tag{C7c}
$$
$$
o_{k,l,i}+o_{l,k,i}\ \ge\ \eta_{k,l,i,q}-(c_k+c_l) \tag{C7d}
$$
where $h(q)=h_{\text{seg}}$ for same-direction pairs and $h_{\text{opp}}$ for opposite-direction pairs on the same track.

### 5.7 Cancellation consistency
$$
a_{k,i}\ \ge\ A^{\text{sch}}_{k,i}-M\,c_k,\qquad a_{k,i}\ \le\ A^{\text{sch}}_{k,i}+M\,c_k \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{k,i}\ \ge\ D^{\text{sch}}_{k,i}-M\,c_k,\qquad \text{dep}_{k,i}\ \le\ D^{\text{sch}}_{k,i}+M\,c_k \tag{C8b}
$$
$$
y_{k,i,p},\ u_{k,i,q},\ z_{k,i},\ \beta_{k,i}\ \le\ 1-c_k \tag{C8c}
$$

### 5.8 Continuity and horizon (A1)
$$
a_{k,i}\ \le\ \text{dep}_{k,i},\qquad 0\ \le\ a_{k,i},\ \text{dep}_{k,i}\ \le\ T_{\max} \tag{C9}
$$

## 6. Variable Domains

| Variable | Domain |
|----------|--------|
| $a_{k,i},\text{dep}_{k,i}$ | $[0,T_{\max}]$ |
| $da_{k,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ |
| $y_{k,i,p},u_{k,i,q},z_{k,i},\eta_{k,l,i,q},o_{k,l,i},\beta_{k,i},c_k$ | $\{0,1\}$ |

The model is fully linear, produces a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles, and captures retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and energy-speed tradeoffs.

# Final MILP — Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

The following is the consolidated, corrected, fully linear model. All choices not fixed by the problem description are marked **[ASSUMPTION]**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed $t, t'$ (direction $D(t)\in\{\text{up},\text{down}\}$) |
| $S=\{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Ordered set of stations, indexed $s$ |
| $E=\{(s,s+1): s=1,\dots,|S|-1\}$ | Directed segments, indexed $e=(s,s+1)$ |
| $E_{\text{disr}}\subseteq E$ | Disrupted segment(s) — partial blockage (one track direction unusable) |
| $\Omega$ | Set of disruption windows, indexed $\omega$, with window on segment $e(\omega)$ |
| $K=\{0,1,2,3\}$ | Speed regimes: 0 = traction, 1 = cruise, 2 = coast, 3 = brake **[ASSUMPTION]** |
| $\mathcal{R}=\{\text{normal},\text{opposite}\}$ | Abstract track resources per segment |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $A^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}, D^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ |
| $u_{t,e,k}$ | Speed of train $t$ on $e$ under regime $k$ (precomputed) |
| $\tau_{t,e,k}=L_e/u_{t,e,k}$ | Traversal time under regime $k$ **[ASSUMPTION]** |
| $E_{t,e,k}$ | Energy of train $t$ on $e$ under regime $k$ |
| $\text{Dwell}_{\min}, \text{Dwell}_{\max}$ | Min / max dwell at any station |
| $\text{Traverse}_{\min}, \text{Traverse}_{\max}$ | Min / max traversal time |
| $H_{\min}$ | Minimum safe headway on a shared resource |
| $w^{\text{start}}_\omega, w^{\text{end}}_\omega$ | Disruption window bounds |
| $\text{bigM\_siding}_s\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if station $s$ has a siding permitting overtaking |
| $B$ | Big-M ≥ planning-horizon scale |
| $\varepsilon>0$ | Minimum time resolution |
| $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\pi^{\text{reroute}}$ | Objective weights, ≥ 0 |
| $\text{Pen}^{\text{cancel}}$ | Cancellation penalty |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (≥ 0):** $a_{t,s}$ (arrival), $d_{t,s}$ (departure), $rt_{t,e}$ (running time), $\delta_{t,s}$ (delay), $E_{\text{total}}$.

**Binary:** $z_{t,e,k}$ (regime), $x_{t,e}$ (reroute), $c_t$ (cancel), $w^{\text{in}}_{t,\omega}$, $q_{t,\omega}$, $r_{t,\omega}$ (window overlap), $u_{t,e,\rho}$ (resource usage), $\zeta_{t,e,t',\rho}$ (both-use-resource AND), $y_{t,e,t'}$ (ordering), $o_{t,s,t'}$ (overtake).

Useful identities: $de_{t,e}=d_{t,s}$, $\;ex_{t,e}=a_{t,s+1}$ for $e=(s,s+1)$.

---

## 4. Objective

$$
\min\; F=\alpha\sum_{t,s}\delta_{t,s}+\beta\sum_{t,e,k}E_{t,e,k}\,z_{t,e,k}+\gamma\sum_t \text{Pen}^{\text{cancel}}\,c_t+\pi^{\text{reroute}}\sum_{t,e}x_{t,e}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Time propagation.** For all $t$, $e=(s,s+1)$:
$$a_{t,s+1}=d_{t,s}+rt_{t,e}$$

**(C2) Running time from regime.** $rt_{t,e}=\sum_k \tau_{t,e,k}\,z_{t,e,k}$

**(C3) One regime per train-segment.** $\sum_k z_{t,e,k}=1-c_t$

**(C4) Traverse-time bounds.** $\text{Traverse}_{\min}\le rt_{t,e}\le \text{Traverse}_{\max}$

**(C5) Dwell bounds.** $\text{Dwell}_{\min}\le d_{t,s}-a_{t,s}\le \text{Dwell}_{\max}$

**(C6) Delay.** $\delta_{t,s}\ge a_{t,s}-A^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}$, $\delta_{t,s}\ge 0$ **[ASSUMPTION: lateness-only penalty; add an earliness term if desired]**

**(C7) Initial/terminal.** $a_{t,1}=A^{\text{sched}}_{t,1}$, $d_{t,1}\ge D^{\text{sched}}_{t,1}$

**(C8) Window-overlap detection (corrected).** For each $t,\omega$, $e=e(\omega)=(s,s+1)$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{t,s+1}&\ge w^{\text{start}}_\omega-B(1-w^{\text{in}}_{t,\omega})-B\,q_{t,\omega}\\
d_{t,s}&\le w^{\text{end}}_\omega+B(1-w^{\text{in}}_{t,\omega})+B\,r_{t,\omega}\\
a_{t,s+1}&\le w^{\text{start}}_\omega-\varepsilon+B(1-q_{t,\omega})\\
d_{t,s}&\ge w^{\text{end}}_\omega+\varepsilon-B(1-r_{t,\omega})\\
q_{t,\omega}+r_{t,\omega}+w^{\text{in}}_{t,\omega}&=1\\
x_{t,e}&\ge w^{\text{in}}_{t,\omega}
\end{aligned}
$$

**(C9) Conflict-free headway on both resources (corrected).**
Resource usage: $\;u_{t,e,\text{normal}}=1-x_{t,e},\quad u_{t,e,\text{opposite}}=x_{t,e}$.
AND: $\zeta_{t,e,t',\rho}\le u_{t,e,\rho}$, $\zeta_{t,e,t',\rho}\le u_{t',e,\rho}$, $\zeta_{t,e,t',\rho}\ge u_{t,e,\rho}+u_{t',e,\rho}-1$.
Ordering: $y_{t,e,t'}+y_{t',e,t}=1$ (unordered pairs), $\;y_{t,e,t}=0$.
Headway, for each resource $\rho\in\mathcal R$:
$$ex_{t,e}+H_{\min}\le de_{t',e}+B\,(1-y_{t,e,t'})+B\,(1-\zeta_{t,e,t',\rho})$$

**(C10) Overtaking / sequence preservation (corrected).** Adjacent $e_1=(s-1,s)$, $e_2=(s,s+1)$:
$$y_{t,e_1,t'}-y_{t,e_2,t'}\le o_{t,s,t'},\quad y_{t,e_2,t'}-y_{t,e_1,t'}\le o_{t,s,t'},\quad o_{t,s,t'}\le \text{bigM\_siding}_s$$

**(C11) Cancellation linking (corrected).**
$$
\begin{aligned}
A^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}-Bc_t&\le a_{t,s}\le A^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}+Bc_t\\
D^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}-Bc_t&\le d_{t,s}\le D^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}+Bc_t\\
\sum_k z_{t,e,k}&=1-c_t,\quad x_{t,e}\le 1-c_t\\
y_{t,e,t'}&\le 1-c_t,\quad y_{t,e,t'}\le 1-c_{t'},\quad \delta_{t,s}\le B(1-c_t)
\end{aligned}
$$

**(C12) Energy coupling.** $E_{\text{total}}=\sum_{t,e,k}E_{t,e,k}\,z_{t,e,k}$

**(C13) Domains.** Times, $rt$, $\delta$, $E_{\text{total}}\ge 0$; all indicator variables $\in\{0,1\}$.

---

## 6. Assumptions (summary)

1. Discrete regime set $K=\{0,1,2,3\}$; run time and energy depend only on regime.
2. Scheduled times exist for every train–station and serve as objective targets and cancellation freeze values.
3. $B$ dominates all time differences (schedules, window bounds, run times, headways); per-constraint tighter $B$ allowed.
4. $\varepsilon>0$ is the minimum time grid unit.
5. Each segment carries two abstract resources (`normal`, `opposite`); headway enforced independently on each.
6. Overtaking only at sidings ($\text{bigM\_siding}_s$).
7. Windows are hard; any overlap forces rerouting.
8. Cancellation is all-or-nothing per train (removed from conflicts, frozen to schedule, zero delay).
9. Cancelled trains do not participate in ordering/headway.
10. Delay is lateness-only; all objective weights are nonnegative.

---

## 7. Corrections applied in the final round

| # | Defect in prior model | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | $w^{\text{in}}=\pi^L+\pi^R$ could equal 2; containment unrepresentable | Mutually exclusive $q,r,w^{\text{in}}$ with $q+r+w^{\text{in}}=1$ and exact big-M semantics (C8) |
| 2 | Stray `B*(2−x−x)*0` term and a big-M sign error | Clean resource-AND $\zeta$ gating headway on two resources (C9) |
| 3 | Mis-stated no-overtaking constraint | Siding-gated overtake indicator $o$ bounding adjacent ordering differences (C10) |
| 4 | Incoherent cancellation rules with undefined bounds | Clean freeze + deactivation of regime/reroute/order/delay (C11) |
| 5 | Only rerouted track had headway | Explicit two-resource headway covering normal and opposite tracks (C9) |

This is the final, complete, fully linear MILP for the TRSMP under partial segment blockages.

# A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Feasibility

## 1. Motivation and Scope

The model below formalizes the problem described in the introduction: given a disrupted railway network, find an updated rolling stock circulation (which train units operate which trips, and which shunting movements are performed) such that (i) the composition model constraints of Fioole et al. (2006) are satisfied, and (ii) every shunting movement is feasible with respect to the available railway infrastructure, as in the Train Timetable Adjustment Problem of Van Aken et al. (2017). The model is linear and mixed-integer. It is intended as the **composition model** component of the Combinatorial Benders' framework, extended with infrastructure-availability variables and cuts, so that it can be solved either exactly or within the iterative heuristic.

Assumptions that are not stated explicitly in the input are marked **[A#]**.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of train trips in the (disrupted) timetable, indexed by $t$. |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$. |
| $K$ | Set of rolling stock unit *types*, indexed by $k$. |
| $U$ | Set of individual rolling stock units, indexed by $u$. |
| $U_k \subseteq U$ | Units of type $k$. |
| $M$ | Set of shunting movements (candidate movements between consecutive trips or to/from storage), indexed by $m$. |
| $M^{dep}_t \subseteq M$ | Shunting movements that can precede trip $t$ (arrival at the departure station). |
| $M^{arr}_t \subseteq M$ | Shunting movements that can follow trip $t$ (departure from the arrival station). |
| $R_s$ | Set of tracks (resources) at station $s$, indexed by $r$. |
| $E$ | Set of infrastructure events (occupations of a track by a train or shunting movement), indexed by $e$. |
| $E_m \subseteq E$ | Events associated with shunting movement $m$. |
| $E^{pax}$ | Events corresponding to passenger train movements (fixed, may be delayed). |
| $\mathcal{C}$ | Set of infrastructure-conflict cuts returned by the infrastructure model, indexed by $c$. |

**[A1]** Each trip $t$ has a fixed origin station $o(t) \in S$, destination $d(t) \in S$, scheduled departure time $\tau^{dep}_t$, scheduled arrival time $\tau^{arr}_t$, and a minimum required number of seats $q_t$ (derived from expected passenger demand).

**[A2]** Each shunting movement $m$ is characterized by a station $s(m) \in S$, an earliest start time $a_m$, a latest end time $b_m$, and a duration $\delta_m$.

**[A3]** Time is discretized into minutes; $t$ indexes the resulting time slots where relevant.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rolling stock composition variables

- $x_{u,t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $u$ is assigned to trip $t$, 0 otherwise.
- $y_{u,m} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $u$ performs shunting movement $m$, 0 otherwise.
- $z_{u,t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $u$ is the *first* unit (lead unit) of the composition on trip $t$, 0 otherwise. **[A4]** Used to enforce coupling/decoupling consistency.
- $n_{k,t} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $k$ assigned to trip $t$.

### 3.2 Infrastructure variables

- $w_m \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ is *scheduled* (i.e., performed), 0 otherwise.
- $\phi_{m,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ uses track $r$ at its station, 0 otherwise.
- $d_e \ge 0$: delay (in minutes) imposed on infrastructure event $e \in E^{pax}$ to open a window for shunting.
- $\pi_{e,e'} \in \{0,1\}$: sequencing variable — 1 if event $e$ precedes event $e'$ on the same track.

### 3.3 Deviation / objective variables

- $\Delta^{comp}_t \ge 0$: absolute deviation in composition (number of units) on trip $t$ from the original plan.
- $\Delta^{cancel}_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is canceled.
- $\Delta^{shunt}_m \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ deviates from the original plan (added or removed).
- $\Delta^{delay}_e \ge 0$: delay assigned to passenger event $e$.

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of operational cost, passenger service level, and stick-to-the-plan penalties:

$$
\min \; Z =
\alpha_1 \sum_{t \in T} \Delta^{comp}_t
+ \alpha_2 \sum_{t \in T} \Delta^{cancel}_t
+ \alpha_3 \sum_{m \in M} \Delta^{shunt}_m
+ \alpha_4 \sum_{e \in E^{pax}} \Delta^{delay}_e
+ \alpha_5 \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{t \in T} c_k \, n_{k,t}
$$

where:

- $\alpha_1$ penalizes deviation from the original composition (stick-to-the-plan for passengers/crew).
- $\alpha_2$ penalizes cancellations (passenger service level).
- $\alpha_3$ penalizes deviation from the original shunting plan (fewer night movements).
- $\alpha_4$ penalizes delays to other trains (infrastructure feasibility cost).
- $\alpha_5$ with unit cost $c_k$ penalizes total unit-kilometres / capital usage.

**[A5]** Weights satisfy $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3, \alpha_4, \alpha_5 \ge 0$ and are chosen by the dispatcher to reflect the relative priority of each objective.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Composition model constraints (Fioole et al., 2006)

**(C1) Trip coverage.** Every non-canceled trip must be operated by a feasible composition:

$$
\sum_{u \in U} x_{u,t} + \Delta^{cancel}_t \cdot |U| \;\ge\; 1 \quad \forall t \in T.
$$

**(C2) Capacity requirement.** The composition on trip $t$ must provide at least $q_t$ seats:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} \text{cap}_k \, n_{k,t} \;\ge\; q_t \,(1 - \Delta^{cancel}_t) \quad \forall t \in T,
$$

where $\text{cap}_k$ is the seat capacity of a unit of type $k$.

**(C3) Type-count consistency.** The number of units of each type on trip $t$ equals the sum of assigned units of that type:

$$
n_{k,t} = \sum_{u \in U_k} x_{u,t} \quad \forall k \in K,\; t \in T.
$$

**(C4) Unit uniqueness per trip.** Each unit operates at most one trip at a time:

$$
\sum_{t \in T:\, \tau^{dep}_t \le \tau < \tau^{arr}_t} x_{u,t} \;\le\; 1 \quad \forall u \in U,\; \tau.
$$

**[A6]** Trips whose time windows overlap cannot share a unit.

**(C5) Flow conservation (unit continuity).** For each unit $u$ and each station $s$, the number of arrivals equals the number of departures plus units remaining at $s$:

$$
\sum_{t:\, d(t)=s} x_{u,t} + \sum_{m \in M^{dep}_s} y_{u,m}
= \sum_{t:\, o(t)=s} x_{u,t} + \sum_{m \in M^{arr}_s} y_{u,m} \quad \forall u \in U,\; s \in S.
$$

**[A7]** $M^{dep}_s$ and $M^{arr}_s$ denote shunting movements departing from and arriving at station $s$, respectively.

**(C6) Coupling/decoupling consistency.** A unit can only perform a shunting movement if it is part of the composition before and after:

$$
y_{u,m} \;\le\; \sum_{t \in \text{pre}(m)} x_{u,t} \quad \text{and} \quad y_{u,m} \;\le\; \sum_{t \in \text{suc}(m)} x_{u,t} \quad \forall u \in U,\; m \in M.
$$

**(C7) Lead-unit consistency.**

$$
z_{u,t} \;\le\; x_{u,t} \quad \forall u \in U,\; t \in T, \qquad \sum_{u \in U} z_{u,t} = 1 - \Delta^{cancel}_t \quad \forall t \in T.
$$

**(C8) Composition deviation.** Linearization of the absolute deviation:

$$
\Delta^{comp}_t \;\ge\; \sum_{u \in U} x_{u,t} - N^{orig}_t, \qquad
\Delta^{comp}_t \;\ge\; N^{orig}_t - \sum_{u \in U} x_{u,t} \quad \forall t \in T,
$$

where $N^{orig}_t$ is the original number of units on trip $t$.

**(C9) Shunting deviation.**

$$
\Delta^{shunt}_m \;\ge\; w_m - w^{orig}_m, \qquad
\Delta^{shunt}_m \;\ge\; w^{orig}_m - w_m \quad \forall m \in M,
$$

where $w^{orig}_m \in \{0,1\}$ indicates whether $m$ was in the original plan.

**(C10) Shunting–unit linkage.** A shunting movement is scheduled iff at least one unit performs it:

$$
w_m \;\le\; \sum_{u \in U} y_{u,m} \;\le\; |U| \, w_m \quad \forall m \in M.
$$

### 5.2 Infrastructure model constraints (Van Aken et al., 2017, tailored)

**(C11) Track assignment.** Each scheduled shunting movement occupies exactly one track at its station:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_{s(m)}} \phi_{m,r} = w_m \quad \forall m \in M.
$$

**(C12) Track capacity.** At most one event occupies a given track at any time. Using sequencing variables $\pi_{e,e'}$ for events $e,e'$ on the same track $r$:

$$
\pi_{e,e'} + \pi_{e',e} \;\ge\; \phi_{m(e),r} + \phi_{m(e'),r} - 1 \quad \forall r \in R_s,\; e,e' \in E_r,\; e \neq e'.
$$

**(C13) Time-window consistency.** If $e$ precedes $e'$ on the same track, then the end of $e$ (plus a safety margin $\sigma$) must not exceed the start of $e'$:

$$
\tau^{end}_e + \sigma \;\le\; \tau^{start}_{e'} + M^{big}(1 - \pi_{e,e'}) \quad \forall e,e' \in E_r.
$$

**(C14) Delay propagation.** Delays assigned to passenger events must be consistent with the timetable:

$$
\tau^{start}_e = \tau^{start,orig}_e + d_e \quad \forall e \in E^{pax}, \qquad 0 \le d_e \le d^{max}.
$$

**[A8]** $d^{max}$ is a small bound (a few minutes) reflecting the assumption that short delays are absorbed by timetable buffers.

**(C15) Shunting time-window feasibility.** Each scheduled shunting movement must fit within its allowed window:

$$
a_m \le \tau^{start}_m \quad \text{and} \quad \tau^{end}_m \le b_m \quad \forall m \in M \text{ with } w_m = 1.
$$

Linearized:

$$
\tau^{start}_m \;\ge\; a_m - M^{big}(1 - w_m), \qquad
\tau^{end}_m \;\le\; b_m + M^{big}(1 - w_m) \quad \forall m \in M.
$$

### 5.3 Combinatorial Benders' cuts

Whenever the infrastructure model detects that a subset $\bar{M} \subseteq M$ of shunting movements cannot be scheduled simultaneously, the following **no-good cut** is added to the composition model:

$$
\sum_{m \in \bar{M}} w_m \;\le\; |\bar{M}| - 1 \quad \forall \bar{M} \in \mathcal{C}.
$$

These cuts progressively remove infeasible combinations of shunting movements from the composition model's feasible region, which is the essence of the Combinatorial Benders' decomposition of Codato and Fischetti (2004).

---

## 6. Iterative Heuristic Variant

In the iterative heuristic, the cuts (C16) are not added all at once. Instead:

1. Solve the composition model (C1)–(C10) with the current set of cuts $\mathcal{C}$.
2. Feed the resulting shunting movements $\{m : w_m = 1\}$ **one by one** to the infrastructure model (C11)–(C15).
3. For each infeasible movement, add a cut of the form (C16) with $|\bar{M}| = 1$, i.e., $w_m \le 0$.
4. Repeat until the infrastructure model accepts all scheduled shunting movements.

**[A9]** This mimics the interaction between rolling stock dispatchers (NS) and infrastructure dispatchers (ProRail), consistent with the European separation of railway tasks.

---

## 7. Summary of Assumptions

| ID | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Each trip has fixed origin, destination, times, and seat demand. |
| A2 | Each shunting movement has a station, time window, and duration. |
| A3 | Time is discretized into minutes. |
| A4 | A lead-unit variable is used to enforce coupling consistency. |
| A5 | Objective weights are non-negative and chosen by the dispatcher. |
| A6 | Overlapping trips cannot share a unit. |
| A7 | $M^{dep}_s$, $M^{arr}_s$ partition shunting movements by station. |
| A8 | Delays to passenger trains are bounded by $d^{max}$ (a few minutes). |
| A9 | The iterative heuristic processes shunting movements sequentially, reflecting the NS–ProRail separation. |

---

## 8. Model Class

The formulation is a **Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP)**:

- Binary variables: $x_{u,t}, y_{u,m}, z_{u,t}, w_m, \phi_{m,r}, \pi_{e,e'}, \Delta^{cancel}_t, \Delta^{shunt}_m$.
- Integer variables: $n_{k,t}$.
- Continuous variables: $\Delta^{comp}_t, d_e, \Delta^{delay}_e, \tau^{start}_e, \tau^{end}_e$.
- Objective: linear.
- Constraints: all linear (big-$M$ disjunctions and absolute-value linearizations).

It can be solved directly by an MILP solver (exact approach) or decomposed via Combinatorial Benders' / iterative heuristic, as described in the paper.

# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Final Model

Below is the complete, self-contained linear MILP for the integrated train rescheduling and speed management problem under a partial segment blockage disruption. Assumptions added where the input leaves gaps are explicitly flagged **(A#)**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Stations, $s = 1,\dots,|\mathcal{S}|$, ordered along the corridor |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Track segments $\ell=(s,s{+}1)$ between consecutive stations |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Trains, indices $i,j$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Discrete speed levels (traction / coasting / braking) |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Motion phases $p=1,\dots,P$ per inter-station run |
| $\mathcal{A}_{\text{aff}} \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ | Segments affected by the blockage |
| $W=[t_{\text{start}},t_{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window |
| $d(i)\in\{\text{UP},\text{DOWN}\}$ | Direction of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{R}(s)$ | Trains sharing a conflict resource on segment $s$ |
| blocked_dir | Direction whose nominal track is blocked |

**(A1)** Double-track line; stations are the only rerouting points.
**(A2)** Blockage affects one track of the affected segments over the known window $W$.
**(A3)** Speed profile discretized into $P$ phases, each picking a level $k$ with speed $v_k$.
**(A4)** Trapezoidal / piecewise-linear speed matching via average phase speed.
**(A5)** Minimum headway enforced on shared track-direction resources.
**(A6)** Non-cancelled trains serve all scheduled stops.
**(A7)** Timing in seconds, distances in km.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $D_{s,s+1}$ | Distance between stations $s$, $s{+}1$ |
| $v_k$ | Speed at level $k$ |
| $e_k$ | Energy rate (per unit time) at level $k$ |
| $\Delta t_p$ | Duration of motion phase $p$ |
| $r^{\min}_{i,s}, r^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Min/max running time, train $i$, segment $s$ |
| $\mathrm{dw}^{\min}_{i,s}, \mathrm{dw}^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Min/max dwell time |
| $h_{\min}$ | Same-track, same-direction headway |
| $h_{\text{cross}}$ | Opposing-train safe interval (rerouting) |
| $m$ | Margin around disruption window |
| $C^{\text{cancel}}_i$ | Cancellation cost of train $i$ |
| $a^{\text{ref}}_i$ | Reference arrival time of train $i$ at last station |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3 \ge 0$ | Objective weights |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary**
- $x_i \in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.
- $y_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $s$.
- $z_{i,s,p,k}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if phase $p$ of train $i$ on segment $s$ uses level $k$.
- $u_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$.

**Continuous**
- $a_{i,s}\ge 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $d_{i,s}\ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$.
- $t_{i,s}\ge 0$: running time on segment $s$.
- $w_{i,s}\ge 0$: dwell time at station $s$.
- $v_{i,s,p}\ge 0$: realized phase speed (linking variable).
- $E_i\ge 0$: total energy of train $i$; $\;E_{\text{total}}\ge 0$.

---

## 4. Objective

$$
\min\;
\alpha_1 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} C^{\text{cancel}}_i\,x_i
\;+\;
\alpha_2 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} \bigl(a_{i,|\mathcal{S}|} - a^{\text{ref}}_i\bigr)
\;+\;
\alpha_3 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} E_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Timing propagation — $\forall i,\; s=1,\dots,|\mathcal{S}|-1$
$$
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + t_{i,s}, \qquad d_{i,s} = a_{i,s} + w_{i,s}
$$

### (C2) Running-time bounds
$$
r^{\min}_{i,s}(1-x_i) \le t_{i,s} \le r^{\max}_{i,s}(1-x_i)
$$

### (C3) Dwell bounds
$$
\mathrm{dw}^{\min}_{i,s}(1-x_i) \le w_{i,s} \le \mathrm{dw}^{\max}_{i,s}(1-x_i)
$$

### (C4) Speed-profile ↔ travel-time coupling — $\forall i,s,p$
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} z_{i,s,p,k} = 1, \qquad
v_{i,s,p} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} v_k\,z_{i,s,p,k}
$$
$$
\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \Delta t_p\,v_{i,s,p} = D_{s,s+1}(1-x_i), \qquad
t_{i,s} = \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \Delta t_p\,(1-x_i)
$$

### (C5) Energy accounting
$$
E_i = \sum_{s}\sum_{p}\sum_{k}\Delta t_p\,e_k\,z_{i,s,p,k}, \qquad
E_{\text{total}} = \sum_{i} E_i
$$

### (C6) Cancellation big-M linking — $\forall i,s$
$$
a_{i,s} \le M(1-x_i),\quad d_{i,s} \le M(1-x_i),\quad
t_{i,s} \le M(1-x_i),\quad w_{i,s} \le M(1-x_i)
$$

### (C7) Same-resource headway / no-overtaking — $\forall s,\;(i,j)\in\mathcal{R}(s)\times\mathcal{R}(s),\,i\ne j$
$$
a_{j,s+1} \ge a_{i,s+1} + h_{\min} - M(1-u_{i,j,s})
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \ge a_{j,s+1} + h_{\min} - M\,u_{i,j,s}
$$
$$
u_{i,j,s} + u_{j,i,s} = 1
$$

### (C8) Rerouting / bidirectional conflict
Eligibility:
$$
y_{i,s} \le \mathbb{1}\!\left[d(i)=\text{blocked\_dir}\right]\cdot\mathbb{1}\!\left[s\in\mathcal{A}_{\text{aff}}\right]
$$
Window containment (with margin $m$):
$$
a_{i,s} \ge t_{\text{start}} - m - M(1-y_{i,s}), \qquad
d_{i,s+1} \le t_{\text{end}} + m + M(1-y_{i,s})
$$
Bidirectional separation with an opposing train $j$ (opposite direction, $y_{j,s}=0$):
$$
a_{j,s+1} \ge a_{i,s+1} + h_{\text{cross}} - M(1-u_{i,j,s}) - M(1-y_{i,s})
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \ge a_{j,s+1} + h_{\text{cross}} - M\,u_{i,j,s} - M(1-y_{i,s})
$$

$$
u_{i,j,s} = u_{i,j,s+1}
$$

### (C10) Station (platform) capacity — $\forall s,\;(i,j)$ conflicting at $s$
$$
d_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h_{\min} - M(1-u_{i,j,s-1})
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \ge d_{j,s} + h_{\min} - M\,u_{i,j,s-1}
$$

$$
x_i,\;y_{i,s},\;z_{i,s,p,k},\;u_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{i,s},\,d_{i,s},\,t_{i,s},\,w_{i,s},\,v_{i,s,p},\,E_i,\,E_{\text{total}} \ge 0
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

A joint solution $(x^*,y^*,a^*,d^*,t^*,w^*,z^*,u^*)$ yields a **conflict-free, executable timetable** with explicit route assignments, orderings, cancellation decisions, and energy-optimal speed profiles.

- **Timetable layer** (C1–C3, C6): retiming, dwell control, and cancellation.
- **Speed layer** (C4–C5): executable, energy-priced speed profiles.
- **Conflict layer** (C7–C10): reordering, rerouting on the shared opposite track, and platform exclusivity — keeping all constraints linear (headway, cross-direction separation, order continuity).

The scalarized objective $\alpha_1$ (service quality / cancellations), $\alpha_2$ (punctuality / delay vs. reference), $\alpha_3$ (energy / sustainability) trades off recovery speed against operational cost, suitable for the decomposition into an interaction-focused IP and per-train plan selection described in the paper.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)
## Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Formulation

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of segments (and stations), indexed by $s, s'$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discretized time steps, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $v$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of tracks (up/down), indexed by $r$ |

**Derived sets:**
- $\mathcal{S}^{dis} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$: disrupted segment(s)
- $\mathcal{R}^{blocked} \subseteq \mathcal{R}$: blocked track(s) on disrupted segment
- $\mathcal{K}^{dis} = \{k : t_{start} \le k\Delta t \le t_{end}\}$: disruption time window
- $\mathcal{T}^{up}, \mathcal{T}^{down} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$: trains by direction

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization step (1 s) |
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ (m) |
| $v^{max}_s$ | Maximum line speed on segment $s$ (m/s) |
| $v^{level}_v$ | Speed value of level $v$ (m/s) |
| $a^{sch}_{t,s}, d^{sch}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $w^{delay}$ | Weight on passenger delay |
| $w^{energy}$ | Weight on energy consumption |
| $w^{cancel}$ | Cancellation penalty per train |
| $h$ | Minimum headway (180 s) |
| $\tau^{min}_s, \tau^{max}_s$ | Min/max running time on segment $s$ |
| $dwell^{min}, dwell^{max}$ | Dwell bounds (30 s, 300 s) |
| $a^{max}$ | Acceleration/deceleration bound |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $\eta$ | Energy coefficient (tractive resistance) |
| $P_t$ | Passenger count on train $t$ |
| $r^{orig}_t$ | Nominal track of train $t$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary:**
$$x_{t,s,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{(track assignment / rerouting)}$$
$$y_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{(ordering: } t \text{ precedes } t' \text{ on } s\text{)}$$
$$z_{t,s,k,v} \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{(speed level selection)}$$
$$u_t \in \{0,1\} \quad \text{(cancellation)}$$

**Continuous:**
$$a_{t,s}, \; d_{t,s} \ge 0 \quad \text{(arrival/departure times)}$$
$$v_{t,s,k} \ge 0 \quad \text{(speed)}$$
$$p_{t,s,k} \ge 0 \quad \text{(position along segment)}$$
$$e^a_{t,s}, \; e^d_{t,s} \ge 0 \quad \text{(delay linearization auxiliaries)}$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{w^{delay}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} P_t \left(e^a_{t,s} + e^d_{t,s}\right)}_{\text{passenger delay}}
+ \underbrace{w^{energy}\sum_{t,s,k,v} \eta \, (v^{level}_v)^2 \, z_{t,s,k,v} \, \Delta t}_{\text{energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{w^{cancel}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} P_t \, u_t}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
$$

**Delay linearization:** $e^a_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} - a^{sch}_{t,s}$, $e^a_{t,s} \ge 0$ (similarly $e^d_{t,s}$), replacing the positive-part terms.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Train dynamics — discrete motion
$$
p_{t,s,k+1} = p_{t,s,k} + v_{t,s,k}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall t,s,k
$$

### (C2) Speed profile selection
$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} z_{t,s,k,v} = 1 \qquad \forall t,s,k
$$
$$
v_{t,s,k} = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} v^{level}_v \, z_{t,s,k,v} \qquad \forall t,s,k
$$

### (C3) Speed limits
$$
v_{t,s,k} \le v^{max}_s \qquad \forall t,s,k
$$

### (C4) Acceleration / deceleration bounds
$$
-a^{max}\,\Delta t \le v_{t,s,k+1} - v_{t,s,k} \le a^{max}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall t,s,k
$$

### (C5) Segment traversal (running time bounds)
$$
\tau^{min}_s \le a_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} \le \tau^{max}_s \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
p_{t,s,k} \le L_s \qquad \forall t,s,k
$$

### (C6) Headway on same track
For $t \ne t'$ assigned to the same track $r$ on segment $s$:
$$
a_{t',s} - a_{t,s} \ge h - M(1 - y_{t,t',s}) - M(2 - x_{t,s,r} - x_{t',s,r})
$$
$$
a_{t,s} - a_{t',s} \ge h - M\,y_{t,t',s} - M(2 - x_{t,s,r} - x_{t',s,r})
$$

### (C7) Bidirectional conflict during disruption
For opposite-direction trains $t \in \mathcal{T}^{up}, t' \in \mathcal{T}^{down}$ sharing a track $r$ on disrupted segment $s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis}$:
$$
a_{t',s} - d_{t,s} \ge -M(1 - x_{t,s,r}) - M(1 - x_{t',s,r}) + \epsilon
$$
$$
a_{t,s} - d_{t',s} \ge -M(1 - x_{t,s,r}) - M(1 - x_{t',s,r}) + \epsilon
$$

### (C8) Disruption window — blocked track
$$
x_{t,s,r} = 0 \qquad \forall t, \; s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis}, \; r \in \mathcal{R}^{blocked}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}^{dis}
$$

### (C9) Rerouting return condition
If train $t$ uses the opposite track on the disrupted segment, it must return to its original track on the next segment:
$$
x_{t,s+1,r^{orig}_t} \ge x_{t,s,r^{opp}} \qquad \forall t, s \in \mathcal{S}^{dis}
$$

### (C10) Dwell time bounds
$$
dwell^{min} \le d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \le dwell^{max} \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C11) Arrival/departure ordering
$$
d_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C12) Segment connection
$$
a_{t,s+1} \ge d_{t,s} + \tau^{min}_s \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C13) Cancellation
$$
a_{t,s} \le M(1 - u_t), \quad d_{t,s} \le M(1 - u_t) \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
v_{t,s,k} \le v^{max}_s (1 - u_t), \quad p_{t,s,k} \le L_s (1 - u_t) \qquad \forall t,s,k
$$

### (C14) Track assignment consistency
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} x_{t,s,r} = 1 - u_t \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C15) Big-M linearization of ordering
$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} \le 1 \qquad \forall t \ne t', s
$$
$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} \ge x_{t,s,r} + x_{t',s,r} - 1 \qquad \forall t \ne t', s, r
$$

### (C16) Delay linearization
$$
e^a_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} - a^{sch}_{t,s}, \quad e^a_{t,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall t,s
$$
$$
e^d_{t,s} \ge d_{t,s} - d^{sch}_{t,s}, \quad e^d_{t,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall t,s
$$

### (C17) Variable domains
$$
x, y, z, u \in \{0,1\}; \quad a, d, v, p, e^a, e^d \ge 0
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

**Objective.** The three-term objective captures the operational trade-off in disruption management. Passenger delay is weighted by train occupancy $P_t$ so high-load trains are prioritized. Energy is approximated as proportional to $v^2$ (tractive resistance) and linearized via discrete speed levels $z_{t,s,k,v}$. Cancellation is heavily penalized to discourage dropping services.

**Rerouting ($x_{t,s,r}$).** Allows trains to switch to the opposite track when their own track is blocked. Constraint (C9) forces a return to the original track after the disruption, preventing long-term schedule distortion.

**Ordering ($y_{t,t',s}$).** Encodes the sequence of trains on a segment. Combined with (C6), it enforces the 180 s headway only when two trains actually share a track — the Big-M terms deactivate the constraint otherwise.

**Speed discretization ($z_{t,s,k,v}$).** Converts the nonlinear speed profile into a linear selection problem. With 5–10 levels between 0 and line speed, this gives a good trade-off between fidelity and tractability.

**Position dynamics (C1).** A first-order Euler discretization at 1 s resolution — fine enough for HSR precision (≈80 m at 300 km/h) while keeping the LP relaxation tight.

**Disruption window (C8).** Hard-forbids use of the blocked track during $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$. Combined with (C7), it prevents opposing trains from occupying the same segment simultaneously during recovery.

**Cancellation (C13).** Uses Big-M to "switch off" all timing and motion variables when $u_t = 1$, effectively removing the train from the network.

**Bidirectional conflict (C7).** Ensures that during the disruption, when both directions may share a single remaining track, trains cannot meet head-on — one must fully clear the segment before the other enters.

**Computational note.** The model is a large-scale MILP: $|\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}| \cdot |\mathcal{K}| \cdot |\mathcal{V}|$ binaries for $z$ alone. Practical solution requires rolling-horizon decomposition or Lagrangian relaxation of the headway constraints (C6)–(C7).

---

## 7. Assumptions (marked)

- Time discretization of 1 s; speed levels 5–10 between 0 and line speed.
- Single disruption segment with known time window.
- Fixed origins/destinations; no new trains introduced.
- Energy approximated as piecewise-linear in $v^2$.
- Dwell ∈ [30, 300] s; headway = 180 s.
- Rerouting only within disruption window plus buffer.

---

**Selected model: Model 3** — it is the most complete and internally consistent formulation. It uniquely provides (i) explicit delay linearization via auxiliary variables $e^a, e^d$ (avoiding the nonlinear positive-part in the objective), (ii) a correct rerouting-return constraint (C9) linking opposite-track use to the next segment, (iii) a cancellation-aware track-assignment consistency constraint (C14) that couples $x$ and $u$, and (iv) passenger-weighted delay and cancellation terms that reflect the operational priority of high-occupancy trains. These features make it both physically faithful and directly solvable as a MILP.

Text:
# A MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

*Model inspired by the RECIFE-MILP enhancement described in the input. All modelling choices not explicitly given in the input are marked as **[Assumption]**.*

---

## 1. Scope and Modelling Idea

We consider a single railway line (or corridor) with a set of **block sections** (TDSs) and a set of **switches** at the boundaries of some sections. A timetable with a set of **train requests** (paths through the corridor) is given, together with initial delays. We must find a new timetable (retiming, reordering, local rerouting at switches) such that:

1. No two trains occupy the same **block section** at the same time (fixed-block safety, inherited from ETCS L2 with TTD).
2. Trains keep a **speed-dependent braking distance** to the end of movement authority (EoA) — this is the DTG-specific feature. The EoA is set at the end of the first occupied TDS; the brake indication point (IP) lies *before* it by the train- and speed-dependent braking distance.
3. Switches are modelled separately from plain track, so that rerouting decisions can be taken.

The model is a **time-indexed / big-M MILP** in the spirit of RECIFE-MILP: continuous event times, binary ordering variables, and big-M disjunctive constraints.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $t$ |
| $S$ | set of block sections (TDSs) along the corridor, index $s$ |
| $S^{sw} \subseteq S$ | subset of sections that are switches **[Assumption: switches are modelled as sections with a routing choice]** |
| $R_s$ | set of possible routes through switch section $s \in S^{sw}$ **[Assumption]** |
| $P_t$ | ordered sequence of sections forming the path of train $t$ |
| $V$ | set of discrete speed levels (speed profile options), index $v$ **[Assumption: speed profile options are discretised, as suggested by "introduction of speed profile options"]** |
| $K$ | set of conflict points (section boundaries where two trains can conflict), index $k$ |

Each train $t$ has an ordered path $P_t = (s_{t,1}, s_{t,2}, \dots, s_{t,n_t})$.

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d_t$ | initial delay of train $t$ (min) |
| $a_{t,s}^{nom}$ | nominal arrival time of train $t$ at section $s$ (min) |
| $dep_{t,s}^{nom}$ | nominal departure time of train $t$ from section $s$ (min) |
| $L_s$ | length of section $s$ (m) |
| $v_{t,v}$ | speed of train $t$ under speed profile option $v$ (m/min) |
| $b_{t,v}$ | braking distance of train $t$ at speed $v$ (m) — **train- and speed-dependent** |
| $\tau_{t,s}$ | minimum running time of train $t$ through section $s$ (min) |
| $h_{t}$ | minimum headway / setup time for train $t$ (min) |
| $M$ | large constant (big-M) |
| $w^{delay}$ | weight on total delay in the objective |
| $w^{speed}$ | weight on speed-profile deviation (energy / comfort penalty) **[Assumption]** |

**Braking distance parameter.** For each train $t$ and speed level $v$, $b_{t,v}$ is precomputed from the braking curve (e.g. from ETCS braking models). This is the key DTG input: the IP lies $b_{t,v}$ metres upstream of the EoA.

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Timing variables
- $a_{t,s} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $t$ at section $s$ (min)
- $dep_{t,s} \ge 0$: departure time of train $t$ from section $s$ (min)
- $D_t \ge 0$: final delay of train $t$ at the end of its path (min)

### 4.2 Speed-profile variables
- $x_{t,v} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile option $v$

### 4.3 Ordering variables (conflict resolution)
- $y_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ enters section $s$ before train $t'$ (for $t \ne t'$, $s \in P_t \cap P_{t'}$)

### 4.4 Routing variables (switches)
- $z_{t,s,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses route $r$ through switch section $s \in S^{sw}$ **[Assumption]**

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimise a weighted sum of total delay and speed-profile deviation:

$$
\min \; Z = w^{delay} \sum_{t \in T} D_t \;+\; w^{speed} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{v \in V} c_{t,v} \, x_{t,v}
$$

where $c_{t,v}$ is a penalty for using speed profile $v$ (e.g. deviation from nominal speed, energy cost) **[Assumption]**.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Speed profile selection
Each train chooses exactly one speed profile:

$$
\sum_{v \in V} x_{t,v} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{1}
$$

### 6.2 Running time and speed consistency
The running time through a section depends on the chosen speed profile. With $L_s$ the section length:

$$
dep_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \;\ge\; \sum_{v \in V} \frac{L_s}{v_{t,v}} \, x_{t,v} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in P_t \tag{2}
$$

**[Assumption: linearisation by convex combination of speed options; dwell time can be added as a constant.]**

### 6.3 Path continuity (event propagation)
Arrival at the next section equals departure from the current one:

$$
a_{t,s_{i+1}} \;\ge\; dep_{t,s_i} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; i = 1,\dots,n_t-1 \tag{3}
$$

### 6.4 Nominal timetable and delay definition
Arrival cannot be earlier than nominal (no early running) **[Assumption: standard in CDR models]**:

$$
a_{t,s} \;\ge\; a_{t,s}^{nom} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in P_t \tag{4}
$$

Final delay:

$$
D_t \;\ge\; a_{t,s_{t,n_t}} - a_{t,s_{t,n_t}}^{nom} \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{5}
$$

### 6.5 Fixed-block safety: no two trains in the same section
For each pair of trains sharing a section, enforce a disjunctive ordering:

$$
a_{t',s} \;\ge\; dep_{t,s} + h_{t'} - M\,(1 - y_{t,t',s}) \qquad \forall t \ne t',\; s \in P_t \cap P_{t'} \tag{6}
$$

$$
a_{t,s} \;\ge\; dep_{t',s} + h_{t} - M\, y_{t,t',s} \qquad \forall t \ne t',\; s \in P_t \cap P_{t'} \tag{7}
$$

These ensure one train clears the section before the other enters, with headway $h$.

### 6.6 DTG-specific: speed-dependent braking distance / brake indication point

This is the core enhancement. The **end of authority (EoA)** of train $t$ approaching section $s$ is at the entry of the first occupied section downstream. The **brake indication point (IP)** lies $b_{t,v}$ metres before the EoA.

Let $k$ be a conflict point at the boundary between sections $s$ and $s'$ (i.e. $s$ is upstream, $s'$ downstream). The EoA of train $t$ is at the entry of $s'$ if $s'$ is occupied by another train $t'$. The IP is reached when train $t$ is still $b_{t,v}$ metres before that boundary.

**Linearised formulation.** Let $t_{t,k}$ be the time at which train $t$ passes conflict point $k$, and let $\Delta_{t,k}$ be the time offset corresponding to the braking distance:

$$
\Delta_{t,k} \;=\; \sum_{v \in V} \frac{b_{t,v}}{v_{t,v}} \, x_{t,v} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K \tag{8}
$$

**[Assumption: $\Delta_{t,k}$ is the time to traverse the braking distance at the chosen speed; this is the linearisation of the speed-dependent braking curve.]**

The DTG separation constraint at conflict point $k$ between trains $t$ and $t'$ (with $t$ upstream of $t'$) is:

$$
t_{t',k} \;\ge\; t_{t,k} + \Delta_{t,k} + h_t - M\,(1 - y_{t,t',k}) \qquad \forall t \ne t',\; k \in K \tag{9}
$$

$$
t_{t,k} \;\ge\; t_{t',k} + \Delta_{t',k} + h_{t'} - M\, y_{t,t',k} \qquad \forall t \ne t',\; k \in K \tag{10}
$$

**Interpretation:** train $t$ must have passed the conflict point at least $\Delta_{t,k}$ (its braking time) plus headway before train $t'$ reaches it — i.e. the IP of $t'$ must be respected. This replaces the fixed-block headway with a **speed-dependent** one.

**Linking $t_{t,k}$ to arrival/departure times.** For a conflict point $k$ at the boundary between $s$ and $s'$:

$$
t_{t,k} \;=\; dep_{t,s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad t_{t,k} \;=\; a_{t,s'} \tag{11}
$$

**[Assumption: conflict points coincide with section boundaries; this is consistent with EoA at TDS boundaries in ETCS L2 with TTD.]**

### 6.7 Switch routing constraints

For each switch section $s \in S^{sw}$ and train $t$:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_s} z_{t,s,r} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in P_t \cap S^{sw} \tag{12}
$$

**Route compatibility (no conflicting routes simultaneously):** if two trains use incompatible routes through the same switch, they must be separated in time:

$$
a_{t',s} \;\ge\; dep_{t,s} + h_{t'} - M\,(1 - y_{t,t',s}) - M\,(1 - \xi_{r,r'})
\qquad \forall t \ne t',\; s \in S^{sw},\; r,r' \in R_s \tag{13}
$$

where $\xi_{r,r'} = 1$ if routes $r$ and $r'$ are compatible, 0 otherwise **[Assumption]**.

**Route selection linking:**

$$
z_{t,s,r} \;\le\; 1 - y_{t',t,s} + (1 - \xi_{r,r'}) \qquad \forall t \ne t',\; s \in S^{sw},\; r,r' \in R_s \tag{14}
$$

**[Assumption: this enforces that if two trains take incompatible routes, one must precede the other.]**

### 6.8 Domain and integrality

$$
a_{t,s}, dep_{t,s}, D_t, t_{t,k}, \Delta_{t,k} \ge 0 \tag{15}
$$

$$
x_{t,v} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}, \quad z_{t,s,r} \in \{0,1\} \tag{16}
$$

---

## 7. Summary of the DTG Enhancement

| Feature | Fixed-block (RECIFE-MILP) | This DTG model |
|---|---|---|
| Separation | Fixed number of blocks | Speed-dependent braking distance $\Delta_{t,k}$ |
| Brake indication | At block entry | Anywhere along track, at IP = EoA − $b_{t,v}$ |
| Speed profile | Fixed | Discrete options $v \in V$, binary $x_{t,v}$ |
| Switches | Implicit in blocks | Explicit routing variables $z_{t,s,r}$ |
| EoA | Block boundary | TDS boundary (first occupied section) |

The key DTG constraints are **(8)–(11)**, which make the separation distance train- and speed-dependent, and **(12)–(14)**, which handle switch routing explicitly.

---

## 8. Assumptions Made (Summary)

1. **Discrete speed levels** $V$ are used to linearise the continuous speed profile (as suggested by "speed profile options").
2. **Braking distance** $b_{t,v}$ is precomputed per train and speed level from the ETCS braking curve.
3. **Braking time** $\Delta_{t,k} = b_{t,v}/v_{t,v}$ is a linear function of the chosen speed profile.
4. **Conflict points** coincide with section (TDS) boundaries, consistent with EoA placement in ETCS L2 with TTD.
5. **Switches** are modelled as sections with a finite set of routes $R_s$; route compatibility $\xi_{r,r'}$ is given.
6. **No early running** is allowed (standard in CDR models).
7. **Dwell times** are treated as constants or absorbed into running times.
8. **Objective weights** $w^{delay}, w^{speed}$ and speed penalties $c_{t,v}$ are exogenous.

This model is a complete, linear (MILP) formulation that captures the DTG-specific features described in the input while remaining close to the RECIFE-MILP structure.

# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Among the three generated models, **Model 1** is selected as the best: it is the most complete, internally consistent (its linearization via a finite speed-mode set folds all nonlinearities into precomputed constants, avoiding the problematic $L_s/v$ and $v\cdot\sigma$ bilinear terms that appear in Models 2 and 3), and it provides the cleanest disjunctive handling of bidirectional conflicts and the blockage window.

---

## 0. Assumptions (Explicit)

- **A1.** Fixed set of trains $T$; each runs its full route in one direction $d(t)\in\{\text{fwd},\text{bwd}\}$. Cancellation is a soft option via $\text{cnl}_t$ (default 0).
- **A2.** One segment $B=(\sigma,\sigma+1)$ is blocked in the **forward** direction during $[D_{\text{start}},D_{\text{end}}]$. Backward traffic is unaffected except for shared-track use under rerouting.
- **A3.** Speed profile per segment is **discretized** into a finite mode set $k\in K$ (accel / cruise / decel / coast). Per-mode running time and energy rate are precomputed constants.
- **A4.** Energy is linear in mode duration: $E_t=\sum_{s}\sum_k e_{t,s,k}\tau_{t,s,k}\lambda_{t,s,k}$.
- **A5.** All times lie in $[0,H]$; disruption window and blocked segment are deterministic.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | trains, $t\in T$ |
| $S=\{1,\dots,N\}$ | ordered stations |
| $G=\{(s,s+1)\}$ | segments |
| $D=\{\text{fwd},\text{bwd}\}$ | directions |
| $K$ | speed modes |
| $\mathcal O_t$ | ordered station sequence of train $t$ |
| $B=(\sigma,\sigma+1)$ | blocked segment |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a^{\text{sch}}_{t,s}, d^{\text{sch}}_{t,s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure |
| $h^{\min}$ | minimum headway |
| $\text{dw}^{\min}_t$ | minimum dwell |
| $L_s$ | segment length |
| $\tau^{\min}_{t,s},\tau^{\max}_{t,s}$ | min/max running time |
| $v^{\max}_{t,s}$ | max speed |
| $\rho_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}$ | mode-allowed indicator |
| $e_{t,s,k}$ | energy rate of mode $k$ (kJ/s) |
| $\tau_{t,s,k}$ | nominal mode-$k$ duration |
| $M$ | big-M |
| $w^A,w^E,w^R,w^C$ | weight on delay, energy, reroute, cancellation |
| $[D_{\text{start}},D_{\text{end}}]$ | disruption window |
| $\beta_s$ | 1 if segment has bidirectional capability |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timing**
- $A_{t,s}\ge 0$ : arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $D_{t,s}\ge 0$ : departure time of train $t$ from station $s$

**Sequencing**
- $y_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}$ : 1 if $t$ departs $s$ before $t'$
- $z_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}$ : 1 if $t,t'$ consecutive on segment $s$ (same direction)

**Rerouting**
- $r_t\in\{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $t$ rerouted onto the opposing (bidirectional) track inside the window

**Speed / energy**
- $\lambda_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}$ : 1 if mode $k$ selected
- $\Delta\tau_{t,s}\ge 0$ : actual running time on segment $s$
- $E_t\ge 0$ : total energy for train $t$

**Delay / conflict / cancellation**
- $\delta^A_{t,s}\ge 0$ : arrival delay
- $u_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}$ : opposite-direction shared-track ordering indicator
- $\text{cnl}_t\in\{0,1\}$ : cancellation (soft)

---

## 4. Objective

$$
\min\; Z = w^{A}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in \mathcal O_t}\delta^A_{t,s}
\;+\; w^{E}\sum_{t\in T}E_t
\;+\; w^{R}\sum_{t\in T} r_t
\;+\; w^{C}\sum_{t\in T}\text{cnl}_t .
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (5.1) Delay definition
$$
\delta^A_{t,s}\;\ge\; A_{t,s}-a^{\text{sch}}_{t,s}
\qquad \forall t,\; s\in\mathcal O_t. \tag{C1}
$$

### (5.2) Time propagation
$$
D_{t,s}\;\ge\; A_{t,s}+\text{dw}^{\min}_t, \tag{C2}
$$
$$
A_{t,s+1}\;\ge\; D_{t,s}+\Delta\tau_{t,s}. \tag{C3}
$$

### (5.3) Speed-profile consistency
$$
\sum_{k\in K}\lambda_{t,s,k}=1, \tag{C4}
$$
$$
\Delta\tau_{t,s}=\sum_{k}\tau_{t,s,k}\,\lambda_{t,s,k}, \tag{C5}
$$
$$
E_t=\sum_{s\in\mathcal O_t}\sum_{k} e_{t,s,k}\,\tau_{t,s,k}\,\lambda_{t,s,k}. \tag{C6}
$$
Mode filtering: $\lambda_{t,s,k}\le \rho_{t,s,k}$. Running-time bounds follow from the mode set: $\tau^{\min}_{t,s}\le\Delta\tau_{t,s}\le\tau^{\max}_{t,s}$.

### (5.4) Same-direction headway (big-M)
$$
A_{t',s+1}-D_{t,s}\;\ge\; h^{\min}-M(1-y_{t,t',s}), \tag{C7a}
$$
$$
A_{t,s+1}-D_{t',s}\;\ge\; h^{\min}-M\,y_{t,t',s}, \tag{C7b}
$$
$$
y_{t,t',s}+y_{t',t,s}=1. \tag{C7c}
$$

### (5.5) Consecutiveness (strengthening)
$$
z_{t,t',s}\le y_{t,t',s},\quad z_{t,t',s}\le 1-y_{t',t,s},\quad \sum_{t'}z_{t,t',s}=1. \tag{C8}
$$

### (5.6) Bidirectional safe separation on shared track
For $t$ (forward, rerouted) and $t'$ (backward) sharing segment $s$, with $u_{t,t',s}=1$ if $t$ passes first:
$$
A_{t,s+1}-D_{t',s}\;\ge\; h^{\min}-M(1-u_{t,t',s}), \tag{C9a}
$$
$$
A_{t',s+1}-D_{t,s}\;\ge\; h^{\min}-M\,u_{t,t',s}, \tag{C9b}
$$
with the conditional activation driven by $r_t$ and the direction pair (relaxed when trains use distinct physical tracks).

### (5.7) Disruption blockage
For forward train $t$ entering $B=(\sigma,\sigma+1)$:
$$
D_{t,\sigma}\;\le\; D_{\text{start}}+M\,r_t+M\,\text{cnl}_t, \tag{C10a}
$$
$$
D_{t,\sigma}\;\ge\; D_{\text{end}}-M\,r_t-M(1-\text{cnl}_t). \tag{C10b}
$$
If $r_t=0,\ \text{cnl}_t=0$, train must clear before $D_{\text{start}}$ or after $D_{\text{end}}$; if $r_t=1$, it may use the opposite track inside the window.

### (5.8) Rerouting feasibility
$$
r_t\;\le\;\beta_\sigma,\qquad r_t\in\{0,1\}. \tag{C11}
$$

### (5.9) Station capacity
$$
\sum_{t}\mathbf{1}\{A_{t,s}\le\tau\le D_{t,s}\}\;\le\;C_s
\qquad\forall s,\ \forall\tau\in[0,H]. \tag{C12}
$$
Discretized over time slots or replaced by an interval-packing formulation with binaries $b_{t,s,\tau}$.

### (5.10) Bounds and domains
$$
0\le A_{t,s},D_{t,s}\le H,\quad \Delta\tau_{t,s}\ge0,\quad E_t\ge0, \tag{C13}
$$
$$
y_{t,t',s},z_{t,t',s},u_{t,t',s},r_t,\lambda_{t,s,k},\text{cnl}_t\in\{0,1\}. \tag{C14}
$$

---

## 6. Model Interpretation

| Block | Captures | Key trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| C1–C3 | Train motion and dwell | Downstream delay propagation |
| C4–C6 | Discretized speed profile → running time & energy | Faster mode ⇔ more energy |
| C7 | Same-direction headway ordering | Ordering governs delay propagation |
| C8 | Consecutiveness | Tightens LP relaxation |
| C9 | Opposite-direction shared-track separation | Rerouting creates new conflicts |
| C10 | Blocked segment avoidance | Forces reroute or wait |
| C11 | Rerouting feasibility | Only bidirectional segments |
| C12 | Station capacity | Limits convoys at stations |
| Objective | Delay + energy + reroute + cancel | Dispatcher priority weighting |

**Linearization strategy.** All nonlinear couplings (position–timing, energy, speed) are folded into the finite mode set $K$ via $\lambda_{t,s,k}$, so C5–C6 are linear. The disjunctions inherent to train ordering and blockage are encoded with big-M constraints (C7, C9, C10). The result is a **linear MILP** in binaries $y,z,u,r,\lambda,\text{cnl}$ and continuous times $A,D,\Delta\tau,\delta^A,E$ — solvable by a standard branch-and-bound MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, HiGHS).
