# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Overview

This MILP jointly optimizes **train rescheduling** (arrival/departure times, ordering, routing) and **train speed management** (speed profiles along blocks) for a double-track high-speed railway line subject to a **partial segment blockage** — one track of a specific segment is blocked during a known time window. Trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track during the disruption, and the model explicitly resolves bidirectional conflicts on the shared (rerouted) block.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, i'$ |
| $J$ | Set of stations, indexed by $j$ ($j=1$ origin, $j=|J|$ destination) |
| $B$ | Set of blocks (segments between consecutive stations), indexed by $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized time steps, indexed by $k = 1,\dots,|K|$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions, $dir \in \{1,2\}$ ($1$ = normal, $2$ = opposite/rerouted) |

Helper mappings: $\text{orig}(b)$ = origin station of block $b$; $\text{dest}(b)$ = destination station of block $b$.

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ (km) |
| $TT_b$ | Scheduled travel time on block $b$ (min) |
| $T^{sched}_{i,j}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$ (min) |
| $Dwell_{i,j}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $j$ (min) |
| $H$ | Minimum headway time (min) |
| $V^{max}, V^{min}$ | Max / min allowed speed (km/h) |
| $A^{max}, D^{max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration (km/h per min) |
| $\Delta t$ | Time step duration (min) |
| $E^{coef}$ | Energy coefficient (kWh per km) |
| $T^{blk}_{start}, T^{blk}_{end}$ | Start / end of disruption window (min) |
| $Block\_seg$ | Index of the blocked segment |
| $Block\_dir$ | Direction of the blocked track ($1$ or $2$) |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $W_1, W_2, W_3$ | Weights for delay, energy, cancellation ($W_1+W_2+W_3=1$) |
| $Penalty_{cancel}$ | Penalty per cancelled train |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | Coefficients for energy linearization |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Rescheduling
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,j} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $dep_{i,j} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $j$ |
| $x_{i,b,dir} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses block $b$ in direction $dir$ |
| $y_{i,i',b} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ exits block $b$ before train $i'$ enters |
| $order_{i,i',j} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ departs station $j$ before train $i'$ arrives |
| $cancel_i \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |

### Speed Management
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $v_{i,b,k} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Speed of train $i$ on block $b$ at step $k$ (km/h) |
| $pos_{i,b,k} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Position of train $i$ on block $b$ at step $k$ (km) |
| $e_{i,b,k} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Energy consumed on block $b$ at step $k$ (kWh) |
| $enter_{i,b} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Time train $i$ enters block $b$ (min) |
| $exit_{i,b} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Time train $i$ exits block $b$ (min) |

### Disruption Auxiliary
| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $z^{before}_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses blocked block $b$ before disruption |
| $z^{after}_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses blocked block $b$ after disruption |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z = W_1 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{j \in J} \left(a_{i,j} - T^{sched}_{i,j}\right)}_{\text{total arrival delay}} \;+\; W_2 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{b \in B}\sum_{k \in K} e_{i,b,k}}_{\text{total energy}} \;+\; W_3 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in I} Penalty_{cancel}\cdot cancel_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### (1) Station Flow Conservation

$$
a_{i,j} + Dwell_{i,j} \le dep_{i,j} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J \setminus \{|J|\} \tag{1a}
$$

$$
dep_{i,j-1} + \sum_{b:\,\text{dest}(b)=j} \left(exit_{i,b} - enter_{i,b}\right) \le a_{i,j} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J \setminus \{1\} \tag{1b}
$$

### (2) Block Entry/Exit Timing

$$
enter_{i,b} = dep_{i,\text{orig}(b)} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B \tag{2a}
$$
$$
exit_{i,b} = a_{i,\text{dest}(b)} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B \tag{2b}
$$

### (3) Block Traversal Time Bounds

$$
exit_{i,b} - enter_{i,b} \ge \frac{L_b}{V^{max}}\cdot 60 - M\left(1 - \textstyle\sum_{dir \in D} x_{i,b,dir}\right) \qquad \forall i,b \tag{3a}
$$
$$
exit_{i,b} - enter_{i,b} \le \frac{L_b}{V^{min}}\cdot 60 + M\left(1 - \textstyle\sum_{dir \in D} x_{i,b,dir}\right) \qquad \forall i,b \tag{3b}
$$

### (4) Speed Dynamics (Linearized)

Position update (km/h × min → km):
$$
pos_{i,b,k+1} - pos_{i,b,k} = \frac{v_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t}{60} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k = 1,\dots,|K|-1 \tag{4a}
$$

Acceleration / deceleration limits:
$$
v_{i,b,k+1} - v_{i,b,k} \le A^{max}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall i,b,k \tag{4b}
$$
$$
v_{i,b,k} - v_{i,b,k+1} \le D^{max}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall i,b,k \tag{4c}
$$

Speed bounds:
$$
V^{min} \le v_{i,b,k} \le V^{max} \qquad \forall i,b,k \tag{4d}
$$

Boundary positions:
$$
pos_{i,b,1} = 0 \qquad \forall i,b \tag{4e}
$$
$$
pos_{i,b,|K|} = L_b \sum_{dir \in D} x_{i,b,dir} \qquad \forall i,b \tag{4f}
$$

### (5) Disruption Constraints

For $b = Block\_seg$ and $dir = Block\_dir$, a train traversing the blocked track must complete traversal **before** $T^{blk}_{start}$ or **after** $T^{blk}_{end}$:

$$
enter_{i,b} \le T^{blk}_{start} + M\,(1 - z^{before}_{i,b}) + M\,(1 - x_{i,b,Block\_dir}) \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{5a}
$$
$$
exit_{i,b} \ge T^{blk}_{end} - M\,(1 - z^{after}_{i,b}) - M\,(1 - x_{i,b,Block\_dir}) \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{5b}
$$
$$
z^{before}_{i,b} + z^{after}_{i,b} \ge x_{i,b,Block\_dir} \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{5c}
$$
$$
z^{before}_{i,b} + z^{after}_{i,b} \le 1 \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{5d}
$$

If the train uses the **opposite (unblocked) track**, no time-window restriction applies (handled implicitly by the Big-M terms).

### (6) Rerouting Constraints

Each train must traverse each block exactly once (in some direction), unless cancelled:
$$
\sum_{dir \in D} x_{i,b,dir} = 1 - cancel_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B \tag{6a}
$$

For non-disrupted blocks, rerouting is not permitted:
$$
x_{i,b,2} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B \setminus \{Block\_seg\} \tag{6b}
$$

For the disrupted block, either direction is allowed (subject to disruption constraints):
$$
x_{i,Block\_seg,1} + x_{i,Block\_seg,2} = 1 - cancel_i \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{6c}
$$

### (7) Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

For each block $b$ and each ordered pair $(i,i')$, $i \neq i'$:

$$
y_{i,i',b} + y_{i',i,b} = 1 \qquad \forall i \ne i',\; b \in B \tag{7a}
$$

If both trains use block $b$, enforce non-overlap (no simultaneous occupancy):
$$
enter_{i,b} \ge exit_{i',b} - M\,(1 - y_{i,i',b}) - M\left(2 - \textstyle\sum_{dir} x_{i,b,dir} - \sum_{dir} x_{i',b,dir}\right) \qquad \forall i \ne i', b \tag{7b}
$$
$$
enter_{i',b} \ge exit_{i,b} - M\,(1 - y_{i',i,b}) - M\left(2 - \textstyle\sum_{dir} x_{i,b,dir} - \sum_{dir} x_{i',b,dir}\right) \qquad \forall i \ne i', b \tag{7c}
$$

### (8) Headway Constraints at Stations

For all $i, i' \in I$, $i \neq i'$, $j \in J$:
$$
dep_{i,j} - a_{i',j} \ge H - M\,(1 - order_{i,i',j}) \qquad \forall i \ne i', j \tag{8a}
$$
$$
a_{i,j} - dep_{i',j} \ge H - M\,order_{i,i',j} \qquad \forall i \ne i', j \tag{8b}
$$

### (9) Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

Energy is a convex function of speed; a simplified linear surrogate is:
$$
e_{i,b,k} = E^{coef}\,\frac{\Delta t}{60}\,\frac{pos_{i,b,k+1} - pos_{i,b,k}}{L_b}\,\left(\alpha\, v_{i,b,k} + \beta\right) \qquad \forall i,b,k \tag{9}
$$

For higher accuracy, a piecewise-linear approximation with breakpoints can be used (introducing SOS1 variables $\lambda_{i,b,k,s}$ with $\sum_s \lambda_{i,b,k,s} = 1$ and $v_{i,b,k} = \sum_s \bar{v}_s \lambda_{i,b,k,s}$, $e_{i,b,k} = \sum_s \bar{e}_s \lambda_{i,b,k,s}$).

### (10) Cancellation Coupling

If $cancel_i = 1$, all routing and timing variables are deactivated:
$$
x_{i,b,dir} \le 1 - cancel_i \qquad \forall i,b,dir \tag{10a}
$$
$$
a_{i,j} \le M\,(1 - cancel_i) \qquad \forall i,j \tag{10b}
$$
$$
dep_{i,j} \le M\,(1 - cancel_i) \qquad \forall i,j \tag{10c}
$$

### (11) Origin / Destination Boundary Conditions

Departure from origin not earlier than scheduled:
$$
dep_{i,1} \ge T^{sched}_{i,1} \cdot (1 - cancel_i) \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{11a}
$$

### (12) Variable Domains

$$
a_{i,j}, dep_{i,j}, enter_{i,b}, exit_{i,b}, v_{i,b,k}, pos_{i,b,k}, e_{i,b,k} \ge 0 \tag{12a}
$$
$$
x_{i,b,dir},\, y_{i,i',b},\, order_{i,i',j},\, cancel_i,\, z^{before}_{i,b},\, z^{after}_{i,b} \in \{0,1\} \tag{12b}
$$

---

## 7. Key Modeling Elements

| Element | Role |
|---|---|
| $x_{i,b,dir}$ | **Routing decision** — captures whether a train uses the normal or opposite track on each block |
| $z^{before}_{i,b}, z^{after}_{i,b}$ | **Disruption-window binaries** — encode "before vs. after" the blockage window |
| $y_{i,i',b}$ | **Block ordering** — prevents two trains (possibly opposite directions) from occupying the same block simultaneously |
| $enter_{i,b}, exit_{i,b}$ | **Coupling variables** — link routing decisions with the speed profile; connect rescheduling to speed management |
| $v_{i,b,k}, pos_{i,b,k}$ | **Discretized speed/position profile** — ensures physical feasibility (acceleration, deceleration, speed limits) |
| $e_{i,b,k}$ | **Energy term** in objective — encourages energy-efficient speed profiles |
| $cancel_i$ | Allows service removal at a penalty, ensuring model feasibility under severe disruption |
| Big-M constraints | Linearize logical implications (if-then) between binary routing/ordering and continuous timing |

**Coupling logic:** Routing ($x$) determines which blocks are used and in which direction → timing ($enter, exit$) must respect disruption windows and block conflicts → speed profile ($v, pos$) must fit inside the timing window → energy ($e$) depends on speed → objective trades off delay, energy, and cancellations.

---

## 8. Assumptions

1. **Homogeneous trains** — all trains share the same $V^{max}, A^{max}, D^{max}$.
2. **Single-segment, single-direction blockage** — exactly one segment and one of its two tracks is blocked during a known window.
3. **Rerouting only on the disrupted segment** — trains may only use the opposite track on $Block\_seg$; all other blocks enforce $x_{i,b,2}=0$.
4. **Fixed minimum dwell times** and **fixed minimum headways**.
5. **Piecewise-linear energy approximation** — the quadratic speed–energy relationship is linearized.
6. **Discretized speed profile** — speed is constant within each $\Delta t$ interval; acceleration/deceleration limits are enforced between consecutive steps.
7. **Cancellation is permitted but penalized** — ensures feasibility when disruption is severe.
8. **All trains must complete their journey** unless explicitly cancelled.
9. **Double-track line** with two unidirectional tracks; the blocked track is unidirectional during the disruption window.

---

## 9. Model Summary

| Component | Approximate Count |
|---|---|
| Continuous variables | $O(|I||J| + |I||B||K|)$ |
| Binary variables | $O(|I||B||D| + |I|^2|B| + |I|^2|J|)$ |
| Constraints | $O(|I||B||K| + |I|^2|B| + |I|^2|J|)$ |

**Solver recommendation:** This is a large-scale MILP; use **Gurobi**, **CPLEX**, or **HiGHS** with a time limit and MIP gap tolerance. For realistic instances, decomposition (e.g., Lagrangian relaxation on the bidirectional conflict constraints, or the iterative plan-selection method described in the paper) is advisable.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Availability Constraints

Below I present a complete, linear (mixed-integer linear) model inspired by the description above. It combines a **composition model** (rolling stock circulation) and an **infrastructure model** (shunting movement feasibility), linked through a set of coupling constraints. Where the input is silent on specific details, I make reasonable assumptions and mark them explicitly with **[Assumption]**.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of train trips in the timetable, indexed by $t$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $U$ | Set of rolling stock units (train units), indexed by $u$ |
| $K$ | Set of composition types (train unit types), indexed by $k$ |
| $M$ | Set of shunting movements, indexed by $m$ |
| $M_s \subseteq M$ | Shunting movements at station $s$ |
| $R_s$ | Set of railway tracks (resources) at station $s$, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time steps (minutes), indexed by $\tau$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of ordered event pairs $(m, m')$ that cannot occur simultaneously on the same track **[Assumption: conflict pairs are precomputed from the infrastructure topology]** |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $c^{\text{op}}_k$ | Operational cost per unit of type $k$ per trip |
| $c^{\text{cap}}_k$ | Capacity (seats) of a unit of type $k$ |
| $d_t$ | Expected passenger demand (seats required) on trip $t$ |
| $c^{\text{dev}}$ | Penalty cost for deviating from the original rolling stock assignment |
| $c^{\text{shunt}}$ | Cost of performing one shunting movement |
| $c^{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty per minute of delay imposed on a passenger train |
| $\delta^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed delay (in minutes) per train **[Assumption: a few minutes, e.g., 3]** |
| $\ell_m$ | Duration (in minutes) of shunting movement $m$ |
| $a_m$ | Earliest start time of shunting movement $m$ |
| $b_m$ | Latest end time of shunting movement $m$ |
| $\text{orig}_{u,t}$ | 1 if unit $u$ was originally assigned to trip $t$, 0 otherwise |
| $\text{orig}^{\text{shunt}}_{m}$ | 1 if shunting movement $m$ was in the original plan, 0 otherwise |
| $\text{occ}_{t,r,\tau}$ | 1 if passenger train $t$ occupies track $r$ at time $\tau$ in the original timetable, 0 otherwise |
| $\text{avail}_{r,\tau}$ | 1 if track $r$ is available at time $\tau$, 0 otherwise |
| $n^{\min}_t$ | Minimum number of units required on trip $t$ |
| $n^{\max}_t$ | Maximum number of units allowed on trip $t$ |
| $H$ | Large positive constant (big-$M$) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Composition Model Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{u,t}$ | Binary | 1 if unit $u$ is assigned to trip $t$, 0 otherwise |
| $y_{k,t}$ | Integer $\geq 0$ | Number of units of type $k$ assigned to trip $t$ |
| $z_{m}$ | Binary | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is performed, 0 otherwise |
| $w_{u,m}$ | Binary | 1 if unit $u$ performs shunting movement $m$, 0 otherwise |
| $\sigma_t$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Shortfall in capacity (seats) on trip $t$ (passenger dissatisfaction proxy) |

### 3.2 Infrastructure Model Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\alpha_{m,r}$ | Binary | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is assigned to track $r$, 0 otherwise |
| $\beta_{m,\tau}$ | Binary | 1 if shunting movement $m$ starts at time $\tau$, 0 otherwise |
| $\gamma_{m}$ | Binary | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is canceled (not performed), 0 otherwise |
| $\delta_t$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Delay (in minutes) imposed on passenger train $t$ |

### 3.3 Coupling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_{m}$ | Binary | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is feasible w.r.t. infrastructure, 0 otherwise |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total cost:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{k \in K} \sum_{t \in T} c^{\text{op}}_k \, y_{k,t}}_{\text{operational cost}}
+ \underbrace{c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{u \in U} \sum_{t \in T} \left( x_{u,t} - \text{orig}_{u,t} \right)^2}_{\text{deviation from original plan}}
+ \underbrace{c^{\text{shunt}} \sum_{m \in M} z_m}_{\text{shunting cost}}
+ \underbrace{c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in T} \delta_t}_{\text{passenger delay cost}}
+ \underbrace{P \sum_{t \in T} \sigma_t}_{\text{capacity shortfall penalty}}
$$

where $P$ is a large penalty for unmet demand.

**[Assumption]** The quadratic deviation term is linearized below in Section 5.6.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Composition Model Constraints

**(C1) Unit–trip assignment consistency:**

$$
x_{u,t} \leq \sum_{k \in K} \mathbb{1}[u \text{ is of type } k] \quad \forall u \in U, \; t \in T
$$

**(C2) Composition type count:**

$$
y_{k,t} = \sum_{u \in U_k} x_{u,t} \quad \forall k \in K, \; t \in T
$$

where $U_k \subseteq U$ is the set of units of type $k$.

**(C3) Minimum and maximum composition size:**

$$
n^{\min}_t \leq \sum_{k \in K} y_{k,t} \leq n^{\max}_t \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C4) Capacity requirement (with shortfall):**

$$
\sum_{k \in K} c^{\text{cap}}_k \, y_{k,t} + \sigma_t \geq d_t \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C5) Each unit assigned to at most one trip at a time [Assumption: trips are non-overlapping in the planning horizon]:**

$$
\sum_{t \in T} x_{u,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall u \in U
$$

**(C6) Shunting movement performed only if a unit is assigned:**

$$
z_m \leq \sum_{u \in U} w_{u,m} \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(C7) Unit performs shunting only if assigned to relevant trip:**

$$
w_{u,m} \leq \sum_{t \in T_m} x_{u,t} \quad \forall u \in U, \; m \in M
$$

where $T_m \subseteq T$ is the set of trips adjacent to shunting movement $m$.

**(C8) Shunting movement selection:**

$$
z_m \in \{0,1\}, \quad w_{u,m} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall u \in U, \; m \in M
$$

---

### 5.2 Infrastructure Model Constraints

**(I1) Each performed shunting movement assigned to exactly one track:**

$$
\sum_{r \in R_{s(m)}} \alpha_{m,r} = z_m \quad \forall m \in M
$$

where $s(m)$ is the station of movement $m$.

**(I2) Each performed shunting movement has exactly one start time:**

$$
\sum_{\tau \in \mathcal{T}} \beta_{m,\tau} = z_m \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(I3) Start time within feasible window:**

$$
a_m \leq \sum_{\tau \in \mathcal{T}} \tau \, \beta_{m,\tau} \leq b_m - \ell_m \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(I4) Track availability:**

$$
\alpha_{m,r} \leq \text{avail}_{r,\tau} \quad \forall m \in M, \; r \in R_{s(m)}, \; \tau \in [a_m, b_m]
$$

**(I5) No two conflicting shunting movements on the same track at the same time:**

For each conflict pair $(m, m') \in \mathcal{E}$ and each track $r$:

$$
\alpha_{m,r} + \alpha_{m',r} + \beta_{m,\tau} + \beta_{m',\tau'} \leq 3
\quad \forall \tau, \tau' \text{ with } [\tau, \tau+\ell_m] \cap [\tau', \tau'+\ell_{m'}] \neq \emptyset
$$

**(I6) Shunting movement vs. passenger train conflict:**

For each shunting movement $m$, track $r$, and time $\tau$ where a passenger train $t$ occupies track $r$:

$$
\alpha_{m,r} + \beta_{m,\tau} + \text{occ}_{t,r,\tau} \leq 2 + \frac{\delta_t}{\delta^{\max}}
\quad \forall m, r, \tau, t
$$

**[Assumption]** This constraint allows a shunting movement to proceed if the passenger train is delayed by at most $\delta^{\max}$ minutes.

**(I7) Maximum delay:**

$$
0 \leq \delta_t \leq \delta^{\max} \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(I8) Cancellation indicator:**

$$
\gamma_m = 1 - z_m \quad \forall m \in M
$$

---

### 5.3 Coupling Constraints

**(X1) Shunting movement feasible only if infrastructure allows:**

$$
\theta_m \leq z_m \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(X2) Feasibility implies track and time assignment:**

$$
\theta_m \leq \sum_{r \in R_{s(m)}} \alpha_{m,r} \quad \forall m \in M
$$

$$
\theta_m \leq \sum_{\tau \in \mathcal{T}} \beta_{m,\tau} \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(X3) Infeasible shunting movements must be canceled:**

$$
z_m \leq \theta_m + \gamma_m \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(X4) Benders-style cut generation [Assumption: cuts are added iteratively]:**

For each infeasible combination $\mathcal{M}' \subseteq M$ identified by the infrastructure model:

$$
\sum_{m \in \mathcal{M}'} z_m \leq |\mathcal{M}'| - 1
$$

---

### 5.4 Objective Linearization

**(L1) Deviation linearization:**

Introduce auxiliary variables $\Delta^+_{u,t}, \Delta^-_{u,t} \geq 0$:

$$
x_{u,t} - \text{orig}_{u,t} = \Delta^+_{u,t} - \Delta^-_{u,t} \quad \forall u \in U, \; t \in T
$$

$$
\Delta^+_{u,t} + \Delta^-_{u,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall u \in U, \; t \in T
$$

The deviation cost becomes:

$$
c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{u \in U} \sum_{t \in T} \left( \Delta^+_{u,t} + \Delta^-_{u,t} \right)
$$

---

### 5.5 Variable Domains

$$
x_{u,t}, z_m, w_{u,m}, \alpha_{m,r}, \beta_{m,\tau}, \gamma_m, \theta_m \in \{0,1\}
$$

$$
y_{k,t} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}, \quad \sigma_t, \delta_t, \Delta^+_{u,t}, \Delta^-_{u,t} \geq 0
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \sum_{k,t} c^{\text{op}}_k y_{k,t} + c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{u,t} (\Delta^+_{u,t} + \Delta^-_{u,t}) + c^{\text{shunt}} \sum_m z_m + c^{\text{delay}} \sum_t \delta_t + P \sum_t \sigma_t \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)--(C8), (I1)--(I8), (X1)--(X4), (L1)} \\
& x_{u,t}, z_m, w_{u,m}, \alpha_{m,r}, \beta_{m,\tau}, \gamma_m, \theta_m \in \{0,1\} \\
& y_{k,t} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}, \quad \sigma_t, \delta_t, \Delta^+_{u,t}, \Delta^-_{u,t} \geq 0
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Assumptions Made

1. **Non-overlapping trips:** Each rolling stock unit can be assigned to at most one trip at a time (C5). In practice, this is enforced by the timetable structure.
2. **Precomputed conflict pairs:** The set $\mathcal{E}$ of shunting movements that cannot occur simultaneously is precomputed from the station topology.
3. **Maximum delay:** Passenger trains can be delayed by at most $\delta^{\max}$ minutes (I7), assumed to be absorbed by timetable buffers.
4. **Benders cuts:** The exact algorithm iteratively adds cuts (X4) when the infrastructure model identifies infeasible shunting combinations.
5. **Linearized deviation:** The quadratic deviation from the original plan is linearized using auxiliary variables (L1).
6. **Single planning horizon:** The model considers a single disruption period; extensions to multiple periods would require additional indices.
7. **Deterministic demand:** Passenger demand $d_t$ is assumed known and deterministic.

---

## 8. Solution Approach (Brief)

- **Exact Algorithm (Combinatorial Benders):**
  1. Solve the composition model (C1–C8) to obtain a candidate shunting plan $\{z_m\}$.
  2. Solve the infrastructure model (I1–I8) to check feasibility of $\{z_m\}$.
  3. If infeasible, add Benders cuts (X4) and return to Step 1.
  4. Repeat until convergence.

- **Iterative Heuristic:**
  1. Solve the composition model.
  2. Feed shunting movements one-by-one to the infrastructure model.
  3. If a movement is infeasible, fix $z_m = 0$ and re-solve.
  4. Repeat until all movements are processed.

This model provides a complete, linear formulation that integrates rolling stock rescheduling with infrastructure availability constraints, suitable for implementation in a MILP solver.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Complete MILP Formulation

## 1. Sets & Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of stations, indexed by $s=1,\dots,|S|$ |
| $E \subseteq S\times S$ | track segments between consecutive stations, indexed by $e=(s,s+1)$ |
| $E_d \subseteq E$ | disrupted (partially blocked) segments |
| $K$ | micro-position steps inside a segment, indexed by $k=0,\dots,|K|-1$ |
| $R$ | regimes of the piecewise-linear (SOS2) approximation, indexed by $r$ |
| $T$ | time-discretization steps, indexed by $t$ |
| $D=\{\text{up},\text{down}\}$ | travel directions; $d(i)\in D$ |
| $s(e),\ s'(e)$ | upstream / downstream station of segment $e$ |
| $\text{aff}_i \subseteq E_d$ | blocked segments on $i$'s nominal path |

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $L_e$ | length of segment $e$; $\delta_e=L_e/|K|$ micro-segment length |
| $\hat a_{i,s},\ \hat d_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure |
| $\tau^{\min}_{i,s},\ \tau^{\min}_{i,e}$ | minimum dwell / minimum running time |
| $\tau^{\max}_{i,s}$ | maximum dwell |
| $v^{\min}_i,\ v^{\max}_e,\ v^{\max,\text{rer}}_e$ | minimum speed, nominal max, rerouted max |
| $a^{\max}_i,\ b^{\max}_i$ | max acceleration / braking (m/s²) |
| $\Delta t$ | discrete time step |
| $h$ | minimum safety headway |
| $[t_s,t_e]$ | disruption time window |
| $W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\ge 0$ | objective weights |
| $M_1,\dots,M_5$ | sufficiently large big-M constants |
| $\{v_r\},\{E_r\},\{T_r\}$ | speed / energy / traverse-time breakpoints with $T_r=\delta_e/v_r$ |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timetable (TRP):**
- $a_{i,s}\ge 0$ — arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{i,s}\ge 0$ — departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $x_{i,e}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ reroutes onto opposite track on $e\in E_d$
- $y_{i,j,e}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is sequenced before $j$ on the shared track of $e$
- $\text{canc}_i\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $\delta^{a+}_{i,s},\ \delta^{d+}_{i,s}\ge 0$ — positive-part arrival / departure delays
- $w_{i,s,t}\in\{0,1\}$ — station-platform occupancy indicator

**Speed management (TSMP):**
- $v_{i,e,k}\ge 0$ — speed at micro-step $k$ on segment $e$
- $\alpha_{i,e,k}\ge 0$ — acceleration; $\beta_{i,e,k}\ge 0$ — braking
- $\tau_{i,e,k}\ge 0$ — time spent on micro-segment $k$
- $\mathcal{E}_{i,e,k}\ge 0$ — energy consumption proxy at micro-step $k$
- $\lambda_{i,e,k,r}\in[0,1]$ — convex-combination (SOS2) weights over regimes $r$

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z = W_1\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\delta^{a+}_{i,s}
+ W_2\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\delta^{d+}_{i,s}
+ W_3\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{k\in K}\mathcal{E}_{i,e,k}
+ W_4\!\sum_{i\in I}\text{canc}_i
$$

Delay terms penalize schedule deviation (punctuality), the energy term promotes eco-driving, and the cancellation term is heavily weighted so cancellation is a last resort.

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Timetable precedence — minimum dwell and running

$$
d_{i,s}\ \ge\ a_{i,s}+\tau^{\min}_{i,s}\,(1-\text{canc}_i) \qquad \forall i,s
$$

$$
a_{i,s'(e)}\ \ge\ d_{i,s(e)}+\tau^{\min}_{i,e}\,(1-\text{canc}_i) \qquad \forall i,\ e\in E
$$

### (C2) Running-time consistency (TRP ↔ TSMP coupling)

$$
a_{i,s'(e)}-d_{i,s(e)} \;=\; \sum_{k\in K}\tau_{i,e,k}\,(1-\text{canc}_i) \qquad \forall i,e
$$

### (C3) Speed dynamics and bounds

$$
v_{i,e,k+1} = v_{i,e,k}+\alpha_{i,e,k}\,\Delta t-\beta_{i,e,k}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall i,e,\ k<|K|-1
$$

$$
0\le \alpha_{i,e,k}\le a^{\max}_i,\qquad 0\le \beta_{i,e,k}\le b^{\max}_i
$$

$$
v^{\min}_i\ \le\ v_{i,e,k}\ \le\ v^{\max}_e\,(1-x_{i,e})+v^{\max,\text{rer}}_e\,x_{i,e} \qquad \forall i,\ e\in E_d,\ k
$$

(For $e\notin E_d$: simply $v_{i,e,k}\le v^{\max}_e$.)

### (C4) Speed–position consistency & energy (piecewise-linear / SOS2)

$$
\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_{i,e,k,r}=1,\qquad \lambda \text{ is SOS2 across } r
$$

$$
v_{i,e,k}=\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_{i,e,k,r}\,v_r,\quad
\tau_{i,e,k}=\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_{i,e,k,r}\,T_r,\quad
\mathcal{E}_{i,e,k}=\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_{i,e,k,r}\,E_r
$$

Because $\tau_{i,e,k}=T_r=\delta_e/v_r$ implements the linearized $v\cdot\tau=\delta_e$, and $E_r$ tabulates the traction-energy breakpoint, position and speed remain consistent.

### (C5) Disruption constraints

For $e\in E_d$, train $i$ with $e\in\text{aff}_i$:

$$
a_{i,s'(e)}\ \ge\ t_e\,(1-x_{i,e})\,(1-\text{canc}_i) \qquad \forall i,\ e\in \text{aff}_i
$$

With auxiliary $u_{i,e}\in\{0,1\}$ indicating "$i$ traverses $e$ during the disruption window":

$$
a_{i,s(e)}\ \le\ t_e+M_1\,u_{i,e},\qquad a_{i,s(e)}\ \ge\ t_s-M_1\,(1-u_{i,e})
$$

$$
x_{i,e}\ \le\ u_{i,e}
$$

$$
x_{i,e}=0 \qquad \forall e\notin E_d,\ \forall i
$$

### (C6) Bidirectional sequencing and headway on shared track

For all $i\neq j$, $e\in E$:

$$
y_{i,j,e}+y_{j,i,e}=1
$$

$$
a_{j,s'(e)}\ \ge\ d_{i,s(e)}+h - M_2(1-y_{i,j,e}) - M_2\,\text{canc}_i - M_2\,\text{canc}_j
$$

$$
a_{i,s'(e)}\ \ge\ d_{j,s(e)}+h - M_2(1-y_{j,i,e}) - M_2\,\text{canc}_i - M_2\,\text{canc}_j
$$

### (C7) Reroute mutual exclusion (shared opposite-track capacity)

For $e\in E_d$ and $i,j$ of opposite directions:

$$
x_{i,e}+x_{j,e}\ \le\ 1 + M_3\,\bigl(1-\text{opposite}(i,j)\bigr)
$$

For conflicting directions this reduces to $x_{i,e}+x_{j,e}\le 1$; the shared physical track usage is already enforced through $y_{i,j,e}$ in (C6).

### (C8) Station dwell flexibility and platform capacity

$$
\tau^{\min}_{i,s}\,(1-\text{canc}_i)\ \le\ d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\ \le\ \tau^{\max}_{i,s}\,(1-\text{canc}_i)
$$

$$
a_{i,s}\le t+M_4(1-w_{i,s,t}),\qquad d_{i,s}\ge t-M_4(1-w_{i,s,t})
$$

$$
\sum_{i\in I} w_{i,s,t}\ \le\ \text{cap}_s \qquad \forall s,t
$$

### (C9) Linearization of positive-part delay $(x)^+$

$$
\delta^{a+}_{i,s}\ \ge\ a_{i,s}-\hat a_{i,s},\qquad \delta^{a+}_{i,s}\ \ge 0
$$

$$
\delta^{d+}_{i,s}\ \ge\ d_{i,s}-\hat d_{i,s},\qquad \delta^{d+}_{i,s}\ \ge 0
$$

### (C10) Cancellation validity

If $\text{canc}_i=1$, the $(1-\text{canc}_i)$ factors in (C1)–(C4) release the train from timetable obligations and force $\tau_{i,e,k}=0$, while $W_4$ pays the penalty.

### (C11) Domain and integrality

$$
x_{i,e},\ y_{i,j,e},\ \text{canc}_i,\ u_{i,e},\ w_{i,s,t}\in\{0,1\};\qquad \lambda_{i,e,k,r}\in[0,1]\ \text{(SOS2 across } r\text{)}
$$

All other variables non-negative as declared in §3.

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Two-tier structure.** The TRP layer decides *when* and *where* trains move; the TSMP layer decides *how*. They are tightly coupled by (C2) so the timetable is always paired with an executable speed profile.
- **Bidirectional shared track.** The disruption forces affected trains onto the opposite track, so both directions contend for one physical resource. (C6) enforces binary ordering with headway $h$; complementarity keeps exactly one ordering. (C7) prevents two conflicting-direction trains from simultaneously rerouting.
- **Reroute logic.** (C5) implements the disjunction *reroute* or *delay past the window end*, with auxiliary $u_{i,e}$ ensuring rerouting is triggered only when needed.
- **Piecewise-linear traction energy and travel time.** (C4) uses SOS2 convex combinations to avoid the bilinearity $v\cdot\tau=\delta_e$ and the nonlinear traction curve, so running time and energy stay exactly linear in $\lambda$.
- **Delay linearization.** (C9) replaces $(x)^+$ with an auxiliary variable lower-bounded by $x$ and by $0$; minimization forces equality to the positive part.
- **Objective hierarchy.** $W_1,W_2$ encode punctuality, $W_3$ encodes energy, and $W_4\gg W_1+W_2+W_3$ typically encodes "cancellation only as last resort."

## 7. Assumptions (marked)

- **A1** — Time is discretized into uniform steps $\Delta t$ for the speed profile.
- **A2** — Traction energy and running time are piecewise-linearly approximated (SOS2 over $R$ regimes).
- **A3** — Single bottleneck disruption: one contiguous blocked segment subset $E_d$ over one window $[t_s,t_e]$.
- **A4** — Delay is measured as deviation from the original schedule; weights $W_1,\dots,W_4$ are operator-tuned.
- **A5** — Headway $h$, safety margins, dwell bounds, and platform capacities are given parameters.
- **A6** — Cancellation is permitted only as a last resort with penalty $W_4\gg W_1,W_2,W_3$.
- **A7** — Double-line track: one track per direction, but during disruption affected trains may use the opposite track bidirectionally.
- **A8** — Big-M constants are chosen large enough to be non-binding at the optimum but tight enough to keep the LP relaxation useful.

## 8. Result

The formulation yields, in a single solve, a **conflict-free timetable** with arrival/departure times, rerouting decisions, sequencing on shared tracks, and per-segment piecewise-linear speed profiles, minimizing weighted delay, energy consumption, and cancellations according to operator priorities.

Text:
# Final MILP: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Overview

A high-speed railway line is disrupted by a **partial segment blockage**: one track (direction $u$) of a segment $s^*$ is unavailable during the window $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$. Affected trains may be **rerouted** onto the opposite track (bidirectional sharing), **retimed**, **reordered**, or **cancelled**. The model jointly decides retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and discrete speed profiles, minimizing weighted passenger delay, cancellation penalty, and traction energy.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Segments, indexed $s$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Stations, indexed $k$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{u, d\}$ | Directions ($u$ = up, $d$ = down) |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Position steps along a segment, indexed $p$ |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Discrete speed levels, indexed $v$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^* = \{s^*\}$ | Disrupted segment(s) |
| $\mathcal{T}_i$ | Ordered segments of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_i$ | Ordered stations of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{OD}$ | Ordered pairs $(i,j)$ with $i$ in direction $u$, $j$ in direction $d$ (opposite-direction pairs on $s^*$) |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ |
| $\Delta x$ | Distance step length |
| $t^{\text{plan,arr}}_{i,k}, t^{\text{plan,dep}}_{i,k}$ | Planned arrival/departure times |
| $r^{\min}_{i,s}, r^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Min/max running time of train $i$ on $s$ |
| $d^{\min}_{i,k}, d^{\max}_{i,k}$ | Min/max dwell time |
| $h_{\text{same}}, h_{\text{opp}}$ | Same-direction / opposite-direction headways |
| $v^{\max}_s, v^{\min}_s$ | Speed limits on segment $s$ |
| $\bar{v}_v$ | Representative speed of level $v$ |
| $E_v$ | Effective energy per unit distance at level $v$ |
| $c_{\text{delay}}, c_{\text{cancel}}, c_{\text{energy}}$ | Objective weights |
| $B, H$ | Big-M and tight planning horizon |
| $k_{\text{entry}}(s), k_{\text{exit}}(s)$ | Entry/exit stations of segment $s$ |
| $T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window |

**Assumption A6′:** Acceleration and regenerative-braking effects are folded into $E_v$ as an effective per-distance energy coefficient, keeping energy linear.

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Binary:**
- $x_i$ — 1 if train $i$ operated, 0 if cancelled
- $y_{i,s,d}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses track $d$ on segment $s$
- $z_{i,j,s,d}$ — 1 if train $i$ precedes $j$ on segment $s$, track $d$ (same direction)
- $w_{i,s,d,p,v}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $v$ at position step $p$ on $s$, track $d$
- $o_{i,j,s^*,p}$ — 1 if train $i$ occupies position $p$ on $s^*$ before $j$ (opposite direction)
- $u^{\text{ord}}_{i,j,k}$ — 1 if train $i$ departs station $k$ before $j$ arrives

**Continuous ($\ge 0$):**
- $a_{i,k}, \text{dep}_{i,k}$ — arrival/departure times
- $rt_{i,s}$ — running time on segment $s$
- $rt^{\text{aux}}_{i,s,d}$ — auxiliary for McCormick linearization
- $dw_{i,k}$ — dwell time
- $\text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,k}, \text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,k}$ — positive delays
- $e_{i,s}$ — energy on segment $s$
- $\text{pos}_{i,s,p}$ — time at which train $i$ reaches position step $p$

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \;
c_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_i} \left( \text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,k} + \text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,k} \right)
+ c_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} (1 - x_i)
+ c_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{T}_i} e_{i,s}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### (1) Cancellation / operation linking (tight horizon $H$)

$$
a_{i,k} \le H\,x_i, \quad \text{dep}_{i,k} \le H\,x_i, \quad rt_{i,s} \le H\,x_i
\qquad \forall i, k, s
$$

### (2) Dwell time

$$
\text{dep}_{i,k} \le a_{i,k} + d^{\max}_{i,k}\,x_i
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,k} \ge a_{i,k} + d^{\min}_{i,k}\,x_i
$$
$$
dw_{i,k} = \text{dep}_{i,k} - a_{i,k}
\qquad \forall i, k
$$

### (3) Segment running-time linking (entry/exit stations)

$$
a_{i,k_{\text{exit}}(s)} = \text{dep}_{i,k_{\text{entry}}(s)} + rt_{i,s}
\qquad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{T}_i
$$
$$
r^{\min}_{i,s}\,x_i \le rt_{i,s} \le r^{\max}_{i,s}\,x_i
\qquad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{T}_i
$$

### (4) Delay definition

$$
\text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,k} \ge a_{i,k} - t^{\text{plan,arr}}_{i,k}, \quad
\text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,k} \ge \text{dep}_{i,k} - t^{\text{plan,dep}}_{i,k}
\qquad \forall i, k
$$

### (5) Route / track selection

$$
\sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}} y_{i,s,d} = x_i
\qquad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{T}_i
$$
For $s \notin \mathcal{S}^*$: $y_{i,s,d_{\text{normal}}} = x_i$ (normal track enforced).

### (6) Rerouting only during disruption window

$$
\text{dep}_{i,k_{\text{entry}}(s^*)} \le T_{\text{end}} + B\big(1 - y_{i,s^*,d_{\text{opp}}}\big)
$$
$$
a_{i,k_{\text{exit}}(s^*)} \ge T_{\text{start}} - B\big(1 - y_{i,s^*,d_{\text{opp}}}\big)
\qquad \forall i
$$

### (7) Speed profile consistency

**(7a) One speed level per position step:**
$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} w_{i,s,d,p,v} = y_{i,s,d}
\qquad \forall i, s, d, p
$$

**(7b) McCormick linearization of $rt^{\text{aux}}_{i,s,d} = rt_{i,s}\,y_{i,s,d}$:**
$$
rt^{\text{aux}}_{i,s,d} \le r^{\max}_{i,s}\, y_{i,s,d}
$$
$$
rt^{\text{aux}}_{i,s,d} \ge r^{\min}_{i,s}\, y_{i,s,d}
$$
$$
rt^{\text{aux}}_{i,s,d} \le rt_{i,s} - r^{\min}_{i,s}\big(1 - y_{i,s,d}\big)
$$
$$
rt^{\text{aux}}_{i,s,d} \ge rt_{i,s} - r^{\max}_{i,s}\big(1 - y_{i,s,d}\big)
\qquad \forall i, s, d
$$

**(7c) Running time equals sum of step times:**
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \frac{\Delta x}{\bar{v}_v}\, w_{i,s,d,p,v} = rt^{\text{aux}}_{i,s,d}
\qquad \forall i, s, d
$$

**(7d) Speed limits:**
$$
w_{i,s,d,p,v} = 0 \quad \text{if } v > v^{\max}_s
$$

### (8) Position–time linking (tied to speed profile)

$$
\text{pos}_{i,s,1} = \text{dep}_{i,k_{\text{entry}}(s)}
$$
$$
\text{pos}_{i,s,p+1} = \text{pos}_{i,s,p} + \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \frac{\Delta x}{\bar{v}_v}\, w_{i,s,d,p,v}
\qquad \forall p < P
$$
$$
\text{pos}_{i,s,P} = a_{i,k_{\text{exit}}(s)}
\qquad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{T}_i
$$

### (9) Energy consumption

$$
e_{i,s} = \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} E_v \cdot \Delta x \cdot w_{i,s,d,p,v}
\qquad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{T}_i
$$

### (10) Same-direction headway (segment-level ordering)

$$
z_{i,j,s,d} + z_{j,i,s,d} \ge y_{i,s,d} + y_{j,s,d} - 1
$$
$$
z_{i,j,s,d} + z_{j,i,s,d} \le 1
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{j,k_{\text{entry}}(s)} \ge a_{i,k_{\text{exit}}(s)} + h_{\text{same}} - B\big(1 - z_{i,j,s,d}\big)
\qquad \forall i,j, s, d
$$

### (11) Opposite-direction conflict on shared track $s^*$

For $(i,j) \in \mathcal{OD}$ and all $p$:
$$
\text{pos}_{j,s^*,p} \ge \text{pos}_{i,s^*,p} + h_{\text{opp}} - B\big(1 - o_{i,j,s^*,p}\big)
$$
$$
\text{pos}_{i,s^*,p} \ge \text{pos}_{j,s^*,p} + h_{\text{opp}} - B\, o_{i,j,s^*,p}
$$

### (12) Station headway / no overtaking (station-level ordering)

$$
u^{\text{ord}}_{i,j,k} + u^{\text{ord}}_{j,i,k} \ge x_i + x_j - 1
$$
$$
u^{\text{ord}}_{i,j,k} + u^{\text{ord}}_{j,i,k} \le 1
$$
$$
a_{j,k} \ge \text{dep}_{i,k} + h_{\text{same}} - B\big(1 - u^{\text{ord}}_{i,j,k}\big)
\qquad \forall i,j, k
$$

### (13) Non-negativity and bounds

$$
a_{i,k}, \text{dep}_{i,k}, rt_{i,s}, rt^{\text{aux}}_{i,s,d}, dw_{i,k}, \text{pos}_{i,s,p}, e_{i,s}, \text{delay}^{\text{arr}}_{i,k}, \text{delay}^{\text{dep}}_{i,k} \ge 0
$$

---

## 7. Model Properties

- **Linearity:** All bilinear terms resolved via McCormick envelopes (7b) and big-M (6, 10, 11, 12). The model is a valid MILP.
- **Coupling:** Four layers — temporal ($a,\text{dep},rt,dw$), spatial ($y,z,o,u^{\text{ord}}$), kinematic ($w,\text{pos}$), economic ($e,\text{delay},x$).
- **Disruption handling:** Enters via track restriction on $s^*$ (5–6), rerouting binaries $y_{i,s^*,d}$, and opposite-direction conflicts (11).
- **Solvability:** Large-scale MILP; suitable for Gurobi/CPLEX with warm starts, or decomposition (IP on interactions + per-train plans) as described in the paper.

messages.content: You convert the text of an optimization model into a structured record. Report only what the text states as mathematics, that is, objective functions, equations and inequalities written with symbols. Do not complete, repair, improve or invent anything.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

## Sets and Indices
- $S$ : set of stations, indexed by $s$
- $L$ : set of track segments (links), indexed by $l$, where link $l$ connects station $l$ and $l+1$
- $T$ : set of trains, indexed by $i$
- $D$ : set of directions, $d \in \{0,1\}$
- $K$ : set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$
- $P$ : set of discretized positions along each link, indexed by $p$
- $L^b \subseteq L$ : set of blocked links (partial segment blockage)

## Parameters
- $\text{dir}_i$ : direction of train $i$
- $\text{orig}_i, \text{dest}_i$ : origin and destination stations of train $i$
- $t^{\text{dep}}_i$ : planned departure time of train $i$
- $t^{\text{arr}}_i$ : planned arrival time of train $i$
- $\text{run}^{\min}_l, \text{run}^{\max}_l$ : minimum/maximum running time on link $l$
- $\text{dwell}^{\min}_s, \text{dwell}^{\max}_s$ : minimum/maximum dwell time at station $s$
- $\text{headway}$ : minimum safety headway time
- $t^{\text{start}}, t^{\text{end}}$ : disruption time window
- $\text{cap}^{\text{opp}}$ : capacity of opposite track
- $M$ : large constant (big-M)
- $v^{\max}, v^{\max}_{\text{opp}}$ : maximum speed on normal/opposite track
- $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ : maximum acceleration/braking rates
- $\Delta t$ : time discretization step
- $E_{\text{coef}}$ : energy consumption coefficient
- $c_{\text{delay}}, c_{\text{energy}}, c_{\text{cancel}}, c_{\text{reroute}}$ : objective weights

## Decision Variables
- $x_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $r_{i,l} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ is rerouted onto opposite track on link $l$
- $y_{i,j,l} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on link $l$
- $u_{i,l} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ uses opposite track on link $l$
- $w_{i,l} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $i$ traverses link $l$ during disruption window
- $a_{i,s} \geq 0$ : arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\text{dep}_{i,s} \geq 0$ : departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $\text{run}_{i,l} \geq 0$ : running time of train $i$ on link $l$
- $\text{dwell}_{i,s} \geq 0$ : dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\text{delay}_i \geq 0$ : total delay of train $i$
- $v_{i,l,k} \geq 0$ : speed of train $i$ on link $l$ at speed level $k$
- $e_{i,l} \geq 0$ : energy consumption of train $i$ on link $l$
- $\text{pos}_{i,l,p} \geq 0$ : position of train $i$ on link $l$ at discretized point $p$
- $t^{\text{pos}}_{i,l,p} \geq 0$ : time at which train $i$ reaches position $p$ on link $l$

## Objective Function
$$\min \sum_{i \in T} c_{\text{delay}} \cdot \text{delay}_i + \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{l \in L} c_{\text{energy}} \cdot e_{i,l} + \sum_{i \in T} c_{\text{cancel}} \cdot z_i + \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{l \in L} c_{\text{reroute}} \cdot r_{i,l}$$

## Constraints

**(1) Service / Cancellation**
$$z_i + \sum_{s \in S} x_{i,s} \geq 1 \quad \forall i \in T$$

**(2) Arrival/Departure Time Propagation**
$$\text{dep}_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} + \text{dwell}^{\min}_s \cdot x_{i,s} - M(1 - x_{i,s}) \quad \forall i \in T, s \in S$$
$$\text{dep}_{i,s} \leq a_{i,s} + \text{dwell}^{\max}_s + M(1 - x_{i,s}) \quad \forall i \in T, s \in S$$
$$a_{i,l+1} = \text{dep}_{i,l} + \text{run}_{i,l} \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L$$

**(3) Running Time Bounds**
$$\text{run}^{\min}_l \leq \text{run}_{i,l} \leq \text{run}^{\max}_l \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L$$

**(4) Delay Definition**
$$a_{i,\text{dest}_i} - t^{\text{arr}}_i \leq \text{delay}_i \quad \forall i \in T$$

**(5) Departure from Origin**
$$\text{dep}_{i,\text{orig}_i} \geq t^{\text{dep}}_i - M \cdot z_i \quad \forall i \in T$$

**(6) Disruption Window / Blocked Links**
$$a_{i,l} \leq t^{\text{start}} + M(1 - w_{i,l}) + M \cdot r_{i,l} \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L^b$$
$$a_{i,l} \geq t^{\text{end}} - M(1 - w_{i,l}) - M \cdot r_{i,l} \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L^b$$

**(7) Rerouting Capacity**
$$r_{i,l} \leq 1 - z_i \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L^b$$
$$\sum_{i \in T} r_{i,l} \leq \text{cap}^{\text{opp}} \quad \forall l \in L^b$$

**(8) Bidirectional Conflict Avoidance (Headway)**
$$y_{i,j,l} + y_{j,i,l} = 1 \quad \forall i,j \in T, i \neq j, l \in L$$
$$a_{j,l} \geq \text{dep}_{i,l} + \text{headway} - M(1 - y_{i,j,l}) \quad \forall i,j \in T, i \neq j, l \in L$$

**(9) Speed Profile / Position-Time Consistency**
$$\text{pos}_{i,l,p+1} = \text{pos}_{i,l,p} + v_{i,l,k_0} \cdot (t^{\text{pos}}_{i,l,p+1} - t^{\text{pos}}_{i,l,p}) \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L, p \in P$$
$$t^{\text{pos}}_{i,l,p+1} \geq t^{\text{pos}}_{i,l,p} \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L, p \in P$$
$$\text{pos}_{i,l,p_0} = 0 \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L$$
$$\text{pos}_{i,l,p_{|P|}} = \text{length}_l \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L$$
$$t^{\text{pos}}_{i,l,p_0} = \text{dep}_{i,l} \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L$$
$$t^{\text{pos}}_{i,l,p_{|P|}} = a_{i,l+1} \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L$$

**(10) Speed Limits and Acceleration/Braking**
$$v_{i,l,k} \leq v^{\max} \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L, k \in K$$
$$v_{i,l,k+1} - v_{i,l,k} \leq a^{\max} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L, k \in K$$
$$v_{i,l,k} - v_{i,l,k+1} \leq b^{\max} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L, k \in K$$

**(11) Energy Consumption (Linear Surrogate)**
$$e_{i,l} \geq E_{\text{coef}} \cdot \Delta t \cdot \left(\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,l,k}\right) \cdot v^{\max} \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L$$

**(12) Rerouting / Speed Coupling**
$$v_{i,l,k} \leq v^{\max}_{\text{opp}} + M(1 - r_{i,l}) \quad \forall i \in T, l \in L, k \in K$$

## Assumptions
1. **Discretization**: Speed levels and positions are discretized to linearize nonlinear train dynamics (reasonable approximation).
2. **Energy approximation**: Energy is approximated as proportional to the sum of speeds times maximum speed (linear surrogate; can be replaced with proper piecewise-linear approximation of $v^2$).
3. **Single disruption**: Only one disruption window and one set of blocked links are considered.
4. **Opposite track capacity**: The opposite track has the same physical speed limit but reduced capacity ($\text{cap}^{\text{opp}}$).
5. **Constant headway**: Headway is constant across all links and directions.
6. **Dwell times**: Dwell times only apply at stations where the train stops ($x_{i,s}=1$).
7. **Cancellation**: Cancellation removes the train from all timing constraints via big-M.
8. **Rerouting scope**: Rerouting is allowed only on blocked links during the disruption window.
9. **Unidirectional line capacity**: The rerouting strategy maintains unidirectional line capacity on the opposite track.
10. **Bidirectional conflicts**: Rerouted trains and opposite-direction trains sharing the track must be coordinated via ordering variables and headway separation.

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code, expressed as equations. The model integrates train rescheduling (TRP) and speed management (TSMP) under a partial segment blockage disruption with bidirectional tracks and local rerouting.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S$ | Set of stations, ordered $s = 1,\dots,|S|$ |
| $\text{Seg}$ | Set of track segments $(s, s+1)$ between adjacent stations |
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $B \subseteq \text{Seg}$ | Set of blocked segments during the disruption window |

For each segment $\text{seg} = (s_{\text{from}}, s_{\text{to}})$, the endpoints are denoted $s_{\text{from}}$ and $s_{\text{to}}$.

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_{\text{seg}}$ | Length of segment seg |
| $v_k$ | Speed of level $k$ |
| $E_k$ | Energy consumption rate at speed level $k$ |
| $t^{\text{arr}}_{\text{sched}}(i,s)$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{\text{dep}}_{\text{sched}}(i,s)$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $t_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}, t_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time |
| $t_{\text{headway}}$ | Minimum safety headway between consecutive trains |
| $t_{\text{setup}}$ | Track switching / setup time for rerouting |
| $t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window start and end times |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}, w_{\text{cancel}}$ | Objective weights for delay, energy, cancellation |

---

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Rescheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Rescheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $u_{i,\text{seg}}$ | $\geq 0$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment seg |
| $e_{i,\text{seg}}$ | $\geq 0$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on segment seg |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{i,\text{seg}}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses segment seg |
| $r_{i,\text{seg}}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on seg |
| $y_{i,\text{seg}}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment seg |
| $z_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $v_{i,\text{seg},k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ travels segment seg at speed level $k$ |
| $\text{ord}_{i,j,\text{seg}}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment seg |
| $\alpha_{i,\text{seg}}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters segment seg during the disruption window |
| $\beta_{i,\text{seg}}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is affected by the blockage on seg |

---

## Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, total energy consumption, and cancellation penalty:

$$
\min Z = w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_{i,s}
\;+\; w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{\text{seg} \in \text{Seg}} e_{i,\text{seg}}
\;+\; w_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in T} z_i
$$

---

## Constraints

### (1) Delay Definition
Arrival delay is at least the deviation from the scheduled arrival time:

$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{\text{sched}}(i,s)
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (2) Dwell Time Bounds
Dwell time must lie within the allowed range (relaxed to zero if the train is cancelled):

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \;\geq\; t_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}\,(1 - z_i)
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \;\leq\; t_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}\,(1 - z_i)
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (3) Running Time Consistency
The running time on a segment equals the difference between arrival at the downstream station and departure from the upstream station:

$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s_{\text{to}}} - t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s_{\text{from}}} \;=\; u_{i,\text{seg}}
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} = (s_{\text{from}}, s_{\text{to}}) \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (4) Running Time Linked to Speed Level Selection
Running time is determined by the selected speed level; exactly one speed level is chosen if the segment is traversed:

$$
u_{i,\text{seg}} \;=\; \sum_{k \in K} \frac{L_{\text{seg}}}{v_k}\, v_{i,\text{seg},k}
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,\text{seg},k} \;=\; y_{i,\text{seg}}
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (5) Energy Consumption
Energy is a linear function of the selected speed level:

$$
e_{i,\text{seg}} \;=\; \sum_{k \in K} E_k\, v_{i,\text{seg},k}
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (6) Speed Feasibility
Maximum speed and acceleration/deceleration limits are enforced on the data side via precomputed feasible speed transitions:

$$
v_k \leq v_{\max} \qquad \forall\, k \in K
$$

$$
v_{i,\text{seg},k} + v_{i,\text{seg}',k'} \leq 1
\qquad \text{for infeasible transitions } (k,k') \text{ between consecutive segments}
$$

### (7) Route / Rerouting Logic
A cancelled train cannot traverse any segment; rerouting implies traversal; segment usage equals traversal:

$$
y_{i,\text{seg}} \;\leq\; 1 - z_i
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
r_{i,\text{seg}} \;\leq\; y_{i,\text{seg}}
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
x_{i,\text{seg}} \;=\; y_{i,\text{seg}}
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (8) Blockage Constraint
The indicator $\alpha_{i,\text{seg}}$ captures whether train $i$ enters segment seg during the disruption window:

$$
\alpha_{i,\text{seg}} \;\geq\; \frac{t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s_{\text{from}}} - t_{\text{start}}}{M}
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
\alpha_{i,\text{seg}} \;\geq\; \frac{t_{\text{end}} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s_{\text{to}}}}{M}
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
\alpha_{i,\text{seg}} \;\leq\; 1
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

If a blocked segment is used during the window, the train must reroute:

$$
r_{i,\text{seg}} \;\geq\; \alpha_{i,\text{seg}} - (1 - y_{i,\text{seg}})
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in B
$$

### (9) Headway on the Same Segment
For any two distinct trains using the same segment, safety separation is enforced via the ordering variable:

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{j,s_{\text{from}}} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s_{\text{to}}} \;\geq\; t_{\text{headway}} - M\,(1 - \text{ord}_{i,j,\text{seg}})
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s_{\text{from}}} - t^{\text{arr}}_{j,s_{\text{to}}} \;\geq\; t_{\text{headway}} - M\,\text{ord}_{i,j,\text{seg}}
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (10) Bidirectional Conflict Resolution
For rerouted trains sharing the track with opposite-direction trains, an additional setup time is required:

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{j,s_{\text{from}}} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s_{\text{to}}} \;\geq\; t_{\text{headway}} + t_{\text{setup}} - M\,(1 - \text{ord}_{i,j,\text{seg}})
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s_{\text{from}}} - t^{\text{arr}}_{j,s_{\text{to}}} \;\geq\; t_{\text{headway}} + t_{\text{setup}} - M\,\text{ord}_{i,j,\text{seg}}
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (11) Ordering Consistency
Exactly one train precedes the other on each segment:

$$
\text{ord}_{i,j,\text{seg}} + \text{ord}_{j,i,\text{seg}} \;=\; 1
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (12) Cancellation Logic
A cancelled train has zero times and uses no segments:

$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \;\leq\; M\,(1 - z_i)
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \;\leq\; M\,(1 - z_i)
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
y_{i,\text{seg}} \;\leq\; 1 - z_i
\qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; \text{seg} \in \text{Seg}
$$

### (13) Non-negativity and Binary Domains

$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s},\; t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s},\; u_{i,\text{seg}},\; e_{i,\text{seg}},\; \delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0
$$

$$
x_{i,\text{seg}},\; r_{i,\text{seg}},\; y_{i,\text{seg}},\; z_i,\; v_{i,\text{seg},k},\; \text{ord}_{i,j,\text{seg}},\; \alpha_{i,\text{seg}},\; \beta_{i,\text{seg}} \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$

---

## Assumptions (marked as such)

- **A1:** The line is discretized into stations and segments; trains travel in a fixed direction (no reversal).
- **A2:** Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set of speed levels with precomputed feasible transitions respecting acceleration/deceleration limits.
- **A3:** Energy consumption is a linear function of the selected speed level per segment.
- **A4:** The disruption is a partial segment blockage: blocked segments are unusable on the original track during $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$; rerouting to the opposite track is allowed.
- **A5:** Minimum headway and setup times ensure safety and conflict-free operation on shared tracks.
- **A6:** Dwell times are bounded; trains may extend dwell to absorb delays.
- **A7:** Cancellation is allowed as a last resort with a penalty.
- **A8:** The objective is a weighted sum of total passenger delay, total energy consumption, and cancellation penalty.

---

## Model Summary

This MILP jointly optimizes **train times** ($t^{\text{arr}}, t^{\text{dep}}$), **train orders** ($\text{ord}$), **routes** ($r, y, x$), and **speed profiles** ($v, u, e$) while ensuring a conflict-free timetable and executable speed profiles. The coupling between the rescheduling layer (constraints 1–3, 7–12) and the speed management layer (constraints 4–6) is enforced through the running-time consistency equation (3), which links timetable decisions to speed-level selections. The blockage constraint (8) and bidirectional conflict constraints (10) explicitly handle the partial segment blockage with local rerouting.

# MILP Formulation for the Real-time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

## 1. Modeling Framework

The formulation below is based on the **alternative graph** representation (Corman et al., 2010) extended with **pair-wise delay variables** as proposed in the source paper. The problem is decomposed into two sequential MILPs:

- **Model A (Sub-optimal):** Rerouting + Reordering — fast, pair-wise delay attribution without propagation.
- **Model B (Optimal):** Rescheduling — uses routes/ordering from Model A and adds delay-propagation constraints to guarantee the global optimum.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, i, j$ |
| $N$ | Set of nodes (stations, signals, junctions), indexed by $n, m$ |
| $E \subseteq N \times N$ | Set of directed block sections (edges), $e = (n, m)$ |
| $R_t$ | Set of feasible alternative routes for train $t$, indexed by $r$ |
| $N_t^r \subseteq N$ | Nodes belonging to route $r$ of train $t$ |
| $E_t^r \subseteq E$ | Edges belonging to route $r$ of train $t$ |
| $P = \{(i,j)\in T\times T : i \neq j\}$ | Set of ordered train pairs |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $a_{t,n}$ | Planned (earliest) arrival time of train $t$ at node $n$ |
| $d_{t,n}$ | Planned (earliest) departure time of train $t$ at node $n$ |
| $\tau_{t,e}$ | Minimum running time of train $t$ on edge $e$ |
| $h_{t,e}$ | Minimum headway time after train $t$ traverses edge $e$ |
| $o_{t,e}$ | Safety-relevant overlap (clearance margin behind stop signal) for train $t$ on edge $e$ |
| $\theta_{t,n}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $t$ at node $n$ |
| $L_e,\; L_t$ | Length of edge $e$, length of train $t$ |
| $v_t$ | Nominal speed of train $t$ |
| $r_t^P$ | Planned route of train $t$ |
| $\Delta(r, r_t^P)$ | Number of edges in which route $r$ deviates from the planned route |
| $\kappa_{t,e}$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on edge $e$ (linearized) |
| $M_1, M_2$ | Large positive constants (Big-M) |
| $c^\delta,\; c^e,\; c^r$ | Cost coefficients for delay, energy, and route deviation |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r$ |
| $y_{t,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses edge $e$ |
| $A_{t,n}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at node $n$ |
| $D_{t,n}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ at node $n$ |
| $w_{t,n}$ | $\geq 0$ | Waiting time of train $t$ at node $n$ |
| $\delta_{t,n}$ | $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $t$ at node $n$ |
| $z_{i,j,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is ordered after train $j$ on edge $e$ (pair-wise) |
| $e_{t,e}$ | $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on edge $e$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; c^{\delta}\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{n\in N}\delta_{t,n} \;+\; c^{e}\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{e\in E} e_{t,e} \;+\; c^{r}\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{r\in R_t}\Delta(r,r_t^{P})\,x_{t,r}
$$

The three terms represent (i) total weighted delay, (ii) total energy consumption, and (iii) penalty for deviating from the planned route.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route Selection

**(R1) Exactly one route per train**
$$
\sum_{r\in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1 \qquad \forall t\in T
$$

**(R2) Edge-route consistency**
$$
y_{t,e} = \sum_{r\in R_t\,:\,e\in E_t^r} x_{t,r} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; e\in E
$$

### 6.2 Timing Constraints

**(T1) Running time on edge** (Big-M formulation)
$$
A_{t,m} \;\geq\; D_{t,n} + \tau_{t,e} - M_1(1-y_{t,e}) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; e=(n,m)\in E
$$

**(T2) Departure not earlier than arrival**
$$
D_{t,n} \;\geq\; A_{t,n} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; n\in N
$$

**(T3) Minimum dwell time at nodes**
$$
D_{t,n} - A_{t,n} \;\geq\; \theta_{t,n} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; n\in N
$$

**(T4) Waiting time definition**
$$
w_{t,n} = D_{t,n} - A_{t,n} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; n\in N
$$

### 6.3 Delay Definition

**(D1) Arrival delay**
$$
\delta_{t,n} \;\geq\; A_{t,n} - a_{t,n} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; n\in N
$$

**(D2) Departure delay**
$$
\delta_{t,n} \;\geq\; D_{t,n} - d_{t,n} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; n\in N
$$

### 6.4 Pair-wise Ordering Variables

**(O1) Mutual exclusivity of ordering**
$$
z_{i,j,e} + z_{j,i,e} \leq 1 \qquad \forall (i,j)\in P,\; e\in E
$$

**(O2) Ordering requires edge usage by both trains**
$$
z_{i,j,e} \leq y_{i,e}, \qquad z_{i,j,e} \leq y_{j,e} \qquad \forall (i,j)\in P,\; e\in E
$$

### 6.5 Headway and Safety-Overlap Constraints

**(H1) Headway with safety overlap** (active when $i$ is after $j$ on edge $e$)
$$
A_{i,m} \;\geq\; D_{j,n} + \tau_{j,e} + h_{j,e} + o_{j,e} \;-\; M_1(1-z_{i,j,e}) \;-\; M_1(1-y_{i,e}) \;-\; M_1(1-y_{j,e})
$$
$$
\forall (i,j)\in P,\; e=(n,m)\in E
$$

### 6.6 Delay-Propagation Constraints *(only in Model B)*

**(P1) Propagation of primary delay through the headway chain**
$$
\delta_{i,m} \;\geq\; \delta_{j,n} + h_{j,e} + o_{j,e} \;-\; M_2(1-z_{i,j,e}) \;-\; M_2(1-y_{i,e}) \;-\; M_2(1-y_{j,e})
$$
$$
\forall (i,j)\in P,\; e=(n,m)\in E
$$

This constraint enforces that any delay accumulated by train $j$ at the entry of edge $e$ is transferred to train $i$ at the exit of edge $e$, plus the additional waiting time caused by the headway and overlap.

### 6.7 Energy Consumption

**(E1) Energy on traversed edges**
$$
e_{t,e} = \kappa_{t,e}\, y_{t,e} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; e\in E
$$

(If $\kappa_{t,e}$ is a non-linear function of $v_t$ and $L_e$, it is replaced by a piecewise-linear approximation.)

### 6.8 Boundary Conditions

**(B1) Fixed origin times** (no delay at origin)
$$
A_{t,\,o(t)} = a_{t,\,o(t)}, \qquad D_{t,\,o(t)} = d_{t,\,o(t)} \qquad \forall t\in T
$$

**(B2) Maximum allowed delay at destination**
$$
\delta_{t,\,dest(t)} \leq \Delta^{\max} \qquad \forall t\in T
$$

---

## 7. Model Variants

### Model A — Sub-optimal (Stage 1: Rerouting + Reordering)
Includes constraints (R1)–(R2), (T1)–(T4), (D1)–(D2), (O1)–(O2), (H1), (E1), (B1)–(B2).  
**Excludes** (P1).  
Provides a fast but possibly sub-optimal route selection and train ordering by attributing each delay to exactly one conflicting train (no propagation).

### Model B — Optimal (Stage 2: Rescheduling)
Includes **all** constraints of Model A **plus** (P1).  
Routes and the optional ordering are fixed from Model A, and the delay-propagation constraint guarantees the global optimum of the original rtRTMP.

---

## 8. Assumptions

1. **Continuous time representation** — All event times are continuous variables.
2. **Deterministic environment** — Running times, headways, and overlaps are known constants within the optimization horizon.
3. **Microscopic infrastructure** — Nodes represent signals/stations, edges represent block sections; detailed track topology is preserved.
4. **No train cancellation or turn-back** — Every train must traverse its assigned route from origin to destination.
5. **Pair-wise conflict resolution** — Higher-order (n-ary) conflicts are handled implicitly via transitivity of the pair-wise ordering variables.
6. **Homogeneous headways** — $h_{t,e}$ depends only on the preceding train and the edge, not on the following train.
7. **Linear energy model** — Energy consumption is linear in edge usage (piecewise-linear approximation if necessary).
8. **Static rolling stock** — Train length $L_t$ and nominal speed $v_t$ are constant.
9. **Big-M calibration** — $M_1$ is set to the length of the planning horizon; $M_2$ to the maximum allowable delay $\Delta^{\max}$, ensuring tight LP relaxation.
10. **Single common objective** — Delay, energy, and route deviation are aggregated through fixed weights $c^\delta, c^e, c^r$ (Pareto trade-off analysis can be performed by varying these weights).

---

## 9. Notes on Implementation

- The number of binary variables is dominated by $|T|\cdot|R_t|$ (route selection) and $|P|\cdot|E|$ (pair-wise ordering). Symmetry-breaking constraints (e.g., $z_{i,j,e} \leq z_{i,j,e'}$ for ordered edges) can substantially reduce solver time.
- Model A can be warm-started with the planned timetable; Model B can be warm-started with the solution of Model A.
- For very large networks, Benders decomposition (as in Keita et al., 2020) or the two-stage decomposition of Bettinelli et al. (2017) can be applied on top of this formulation.

# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

I selected **Model 1** as the best formulation because it is more complete in handling the disruption window explicitly (using the `z_blocked` binary with two clean disjuncts for "clears before" / "enters after"), provides a rigorous SOS2 linearization of the speed–running-time relation and the energy function, and fully linearizes the opposing-train conflict via the product binary `u`. Model 2 leaves C13 (position–time) essentially undefined and its disruption-window encoding (C6a/C6b) is not cleanly linear. Below is the refined complete model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| `T` | Set of trains, indexed `t, t'` (both directions, direction `d(t) ∈ {+1,−1}`) |
| `S = {1,…,S̄}` | Ordered stations, indexed `s` (`1`=origin, `S̄`=terminal) |
| `Seg = {1,…,S̄−1}` | Segments, indexed `i` (segment `i` joins station `i` and `i+1`) |
| `K = {0,1}` | Track options (`0` = normal directional; `1` = opposite) |
| `E ⊆ Seg` | Blocked (disrupted) segments |
| `W = {1,…,W̄}` | Discrete time points, step `Δ` |
| `R` | Speed breakpoints for SOS2, indexed `r` |
| `P` | Energy breakpoints for SOS2, indexed `p` |

## 2. Parameters (values not given are marked `[ASSUMED]`)

| Parameter | Meaning | Value |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| `L_i` | Segment length | given; `[ASSUMED]` ∈ [10,40] km |
| `vmax`, `vmin` | Speed bounds | `[ASSUMED]` 300, 80 km/h |
| `Dwell_min`, `Dwell_max` | Dwell bounds | `[ASSUMED]` 1, 10 min |
| `Headway_h` | Same-track headway | `[ASSUMED]` 3 min |
| `Headway_seg` | Opposing-train separation (shared track) | `[ASSUMED]` 4 min |
| `a_acc`, `a_dec` | Accel/decel | `[ASSUMED]` 0.5 m/s² |
| `c1, c2` | Traction per speed·distance / auxiliary | `[ASSUMED]` 0.002 kWh/(km·(km/h)²), 0.5 kWh/min |
| `η_reg` | Regenerative factor | `[ASSUMED]` 0.3 |
| `M` | Big-M | `[ASSUMED]` `T_horizon + 2·Σᵢ Run_max_i` |
| `τ_i^s, τ_i^e` | Disruption window for `i ∈ E` | given |
| `Orig_dep_t`, `Orig_arr_t(s)` | Original schedule | given |
| `C_delay, C_energy, C_cancel` | Objective weights | `[ASSUMED]` 1.0, 0.1, 1000 |
| `Δ` | Time step | `[ASSUMED]` 30 s |
| `x_{t,s}` | Fixed stop pattern (parameter) | from timetable |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary:** `cancel_t`, `k_{t,i,k}` (track use), `y^rr_{t,i}` (reroute), `z^blk_{t,i}` (normal-track passage outside window), `ord_{t,t',i}` (precedence), `u_{t,t',i,k}` (product of track-use binaries).

**Continuous (≥0):** `arr_{t,s}`, `dep_{t,s}`, `run_{t,i}`, `v_{t,i}`, `dwell_{t,s}`, `pos_{t,w}`, `Econs_t`, `delay_{t,s}`, with SOS2 weights `λ_{t,i,r}`, `μ_{t,i,p} ∈ [0,1]`.

## 4. Objective

$$
\min \; Z = C_{delay}\sum_{t}\sum_{s} delay_{t,s} \;+\; C_{energy}\sum_{t} Econs_t \;+\; C_{cancel}\sum_{t} cancel_t
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Arrival/departure consistency.** For `t`, segment `i` (direction-adjusted):
$$arr_{t,s_{down}(i)} = dep_{t,s_{up}(i)} + run_{t,i}$$

**(C2) Dwell bounds & propagation.**
$$x_{t,s}Dwell_{min} \le dwell_{t,s} \le x_{t,s}Dwell_{max}, \qquad dep_{t,s} = arr_{t,s} + dwell_{t,s}$$

**(C3) Cancellation (big-M).**
$$arr_{t,s} \le M(1-cancel_t), \quad dep_{t,s} \le M(1-cancel_t), \quad run_{t,i} \le M(1-cancel_t)$$

**(C4) Track selection.**
$$\sum_{k} k_{t,i,k} = 1 - cancel_t$$

**(C5) Rerouting only on disrupted segments.**
$$y^rr_{t,i}=0 \;\; (i \notin E), \qquad k_{t,i,1} \ge y^rr_{t,i}, \qquad k_{t,i,0}+y^rr_{t,i} \le 1$$

**(C6) Disruption blocking.** Two exit/entry disjuncts `z^out1, z^out2`, with `z^blk = z^out1 + z^out2 ≥` sufficient, and normal track only when `z^blk = 1`:
$$arr_{t,i+1} \le τ_i^s + M(1-z^{out1}_{t,i}), \quad dep_{t,i} \ge τ_i^e - M(1-z^{out2}_{t,i})$$
$$z^{out1}_{t,i}+z^{out2}_{t,i} \ge z^{blk}_{t,i}, \qquad k_{t,i,0} \le z^{blk}_{t,i} \;\; (i \in E)$$

**(C7) Running time / speed (SOS2 on `(v_r, 1/v_r)`).**
$$v_{t,i}=\sum_r v_r\lambda_{t,i,r},\quad \sum_r\lambda_{t,i,r}=1-cancel_t,\quad run_{t,i}=L_i\sum_r \tfrac{1}{v_r}\lambda_{t,i,r},\quad \lambda\;\text{SOS2}$$

**(C8) Speed bounds.** $v_{min}(1-cancel_t) \le v_{t,i} \le v_{max}(1-cancel_t)$

**(C9) Energy (SOS2 + accel/decel).**
$$Econs_t = \sum_i\sum_p \big(c_1 v_p L_i + c_2 \tfrac{L_i}{v_p}\big)\mu_{t,i,p} + \sum_s x_{t,s}\big(\eta_{acc}\tfrac{v_{max}^2}{2a_{acc}} + \eta_{dec}\tfrac{v_{max}^2}{2a_{dec}}\big)\tfrac{1}{60}$$
with `η_acc = c1`, `η_dec = −η_reg·c1`, `Σ_p μ_{t,i,p}=1−cancel_t`, `v_{t,i}=Σ_p v_p μ_{t,i,p}`.

**(C10) Same-track, same-direction headway.**
$$dep_{t',s_{down}(i)} \ge dep_{t,s_{down}(i)} + Headway_h - M(1-ord_{t,t',i})$$
$$dep_{t,s_{down}(i)} \ge dep_{t',s_{down}(i)} + Headway_h - M\,ord_{t,t',i}$$

**(C11) Product linearization.**
$$u_{t,t',i,k} \le k_{t,i,k},\quad u_{t,t',i,k} \le k_{t',i,k},\quad u_{t,t',i,k} \ge k_{t,i,k}+k_{t',i,k}-1$$

**(C12) Opposing-train separation on shared track.**
$$ord_{t,t',i}+ord_{t',t,i} \ge u_{t,t',i,k}\cdot opp(t,t')$$
$$arr_{t',i+1} \ge dep_{t,i} + Headway_{seg} - M(1-u_{t,t',i,k}\cdot opp(t,t'))$$

**(C13) Position–time consistency.** With integer `σ_{t,w}` (segment index) and fractional `f_{t,w}∈[0,1]` (big-M time-linking):
$$pos_{t,w} = P_{σ_{t,w}} + f_{t,w}(P_{σ_{t,w}+1}-P_{σ_{t,w}}), \qquad wΔ = dep_{t,σ_{t,w}} + f_{t,w}\cdot run_{t,σ_{t,w}}$$

**(C14)** Redundant with C6 (explicit disjunction form retained).

**(C15) Delay.** $delay_{t,s} \ge arr_{t,s} - Orig_arr_t(s),\quad delay_{t,s} \ge 0$

**(C16) Horizon / origin bounds.** $dep_{t,s_{origin}} \ge Orig_dep_t,\quad arr_{t,S̄} \le T_{horizon}$

**(C17) Integrality/logic.** All routing, ordering, product, and SOS2 binaries as defined; SOS2 weights satisfy adjacency.

---

## 6. Key Assumptions (marked)

1. Stop pattern `x_{t,s}` is fixed from the timetable (retained binary for later flexibility).
2. Only the **normal track** of disrupted segments is unavailable; opposite track stays usable.
3. Accel/decel occur at stations only, constant magnitudes.
4. Energy linearized over precomputed speed breakpoints; `v²` absorbed into convex combination.
5. Position–time interpolation is piecewise-linear in time.
6. Disruption windows are deterministic and known.
7. Units: times in min, distances km, speeds km/h, energy kWh.

**Model class:** MILP (SOS2 handled natively by Gurobi/CPLEX/SCIP). Binary size `O(|T|·|Seg|·|K| + |T|²·|Seg|)` — solvable directly for modest instances; large instances suit the paper's decomposition / adaptive iterative approach.
