Text:
# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

**Selected Model (best of 3):** The formulation below is the most complete and rigorous of the candidates, correcting the speed–position coupling and disruption-window encoding, and adding a proper big-M tightening. It keeps all nonlinearities linearized.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T} = \{1,\dots,|T|\}$ | trains (bidirectional: up/down) |
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | segments (blocks) between stations |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ | tracks per segment |
| $\mathcal{H} = \{1,\dots,|H|\}$ | discretized time steps |
| $\mathcal{V}_s$ | discrete speed profiles available on segment $s$ |

---

## 2. Parameters (all given, inputs)

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathrm{schA}[i,s]$ | scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\mathrm{dwell}^{\min}_s$ | minimum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $\mathrm{rt}[v,s]$ | running time on segment $s$ under profile $v$ |
| $\mathrm{ec}[v,s]$ | energy coefficient on segment $s$ under profile $v$ |
| $h$ | minimum safety headway |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | disruption time window (set of $\tau$) |
| $s^\star$ | blocked segment |
| $k^{\mathrm{nom}}$ | nominal (blocked) track of segment $s^\star$ |
| $M$ | large constant (tight: derived from time bounds) |
| $w_1,w_2,w_3$ | objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) |
| $C_i^{\mathrm{cancel}}$ | cancellation/turnback penalty for train $i$ |
| $a^{\min}, a^{\max}$ | bounds on arrival/departure times |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary**
- $x[i,s,\tau]$ — train $i$ occupies segment $s$ at time step $\tau$
- $y[i,s,\tau]$ — train $i$ is running on segment $s$ at $\tau$
- $r[i,s,k]$ — train $i$ assigned to track $k$ on segment $s$
- $\mathrm{ord}[i,j,s]$ — train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$
- $\mathrm{sp}[v,i,s]$ — train $i$ uses speed profile $v$ on segment $s$
- $z[i]$ — train $i$ cancelled
- $\omega[i,s,k,\tau]$ — auxiliary linearization of $x[i,s,\tau]\cdot r[i,s,k]$

**Integer/Continuous**
- $a[i,s],\,d[i,s] \in \mathbb{Z}$ — arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\mathrm{del}[i,s] \ge 0$ — positive delay
- $\mathrm{energy}[i,s] \ge 0$ — energy consumption

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \;
w_1 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} \mathrm{del}[i,s]
\;+\;
w_2 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} \mathrm{energy}[i,s]
\;+\;
w_3 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} C_i^{\mathrm{cancel}}\, z[i]
$$

Trades off **punctuality**, **energy efficiency**, and **service preservation** (cancellation).

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Minimum dwell time
$$
a[i,s] + \mathrm{dwell}^{\min}_s \;\le\; d[i,s] \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### (C2) Running time determined by speed profile
$$
a[i,s{+}1] - d[i,s] \;=\; \sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_s} \mathrm{rt}[v,s]\,\mathrm{sp}[v,i,s] \qquad \forall i,\; s<|S|
$$

### (C3) Exactly one speed profile per train per segment
$$
\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_s} \mathrm{sp}[v,i,s] = 1 \qquad \forall i,\; s
$$

### (C4) Exactly one track per train per segment
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} r[i,s,k] = 1 \qquad \forall i,\; s
$$

### (C5) Disruption window — nominal track blocked
$$
x[i,s^\star,\tau] + r[i,s^\star,k^{\mathrm{nom}}] \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall i,\; \tau \in \mathcal{W}
$$
During the window, a train may occupy $s^\star$ only if it rerouted to the opposite track.

### (C6) Conflict-free unidirectional capacity (linearized product)
$$
\omega[i,s,k,\tau] \le x[i,s,\tau],\quad
\omega[i,s,k,\tau] \le r[i,s,k],\quad
\omega[i,s,k,\tau] \ge x[i,s,\tau] + r[i,s,k] - 1
$$
$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} \omega[i,s,k,\tau] \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall s,\,k,\,\tau
$$
At most one train per track per segment per time step (bidirectional shared track).

### (C7) Minimum headway (big-M disjunction)
$$
a[i,s] - a[j,s] \;\ge\; h - M\big(1-\mathrm{ord}[i,j,s]\big)
$$
$$
a[j,s] - a[i,s] \;\ge\; h - M\big(1-\mathrm{ord}[j,i,s]\big)
\qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s
$$

### (C8) Sequencing antisymmetry
$$
\mathrm{ord}[i,j,s] + \mathrm{ord}[j,i,s] = 1 \qquad \forall i<j,\; s
$$

### (C9) No-overtaking across adjacent segments
$$
\mathrm{ord}[i,j,s] = \mathrm{ord}[i,j,s{+}1] \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s<|S|
$$
*(Relax selectively if reordering is permitted.)*

### (C10) Speed–position–movement consistency
Running implies occupancy:
$$
y[i,s,\tau] \le x[i,s,\tau] \qquad \forall i,s,\tau
$$
Residency equals chosen running time:
$$
\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{H}} x[i,s,\tau] \;=\; \sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_s} \mathrm{rt}[v,s]\,\mathrm{sp}[v,i,s] \qquad \forall i,\; s
$$
Contiguity of occupancy (boundary detection via $y$):
$$
x[i,s,\tau] - x[i,s,\tau{-}1] \le y[i,s,\tau] \qquad \forall i,s,\tau>1
$$
Entry/exit coupling to timings:
$$
d[i,s] \le \sum_{\tau} \tau\,x[i,s,\tau] \le a[i,s{+}1] \qquad \forall i,\; s<|S|
$$

### (C11) Energy linearization
$$
\mathrm{energy}[i,s] \;=\; \sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_s} \mathrm{ec}[v,s]\,\mathrm{sp}[v,i,s] \qquad \forall i,\; s
$$

### (C12) Cancellation coupling
$$
x[i,s,\tau] \le 1 - z[i],\quad
y[i,s,\tau] \le 1 - z[i],\quad
r[i,s,k] \le 1 - z[i],\quad
\mathrm{sp}[v,i,s] \le 1 - z[i]
$$
$$
a[i,s],\,d[i,s] \le a^{\max}(1 - z[i]) + a^{\min} z[i]
\qquad \forall i,s,\tau,k,v
$$

### (C13) Delay linearization
$$
\mathrm{del}[i,s] \ge a[i,s] - \mathrm{schA}[i,s],\qquad \mathrm{del}[i,s] \ge 0 \qquad \forall i,s
$$

### (C14) Time bounds
$$
a^{\min} \le a[i,s],\,d[i,s] \le a^{\max} \qquad \forall i,s
$$

### (C15) Variable domains
$$
x,y,r,\mathrm{ord},\mathrm{sp},\omega,z \in \{0,1\};\quad
a,d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0};\quad
\mathrm{del},\mathrm{energy} \ge 0
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Elements

- **Coupling principle.** Each train's journey decomposes into segment-level decisions (speed profile → running time; track → spatial resource) and station-level decisions (arrival/departure → temporal resource). Discretized speed profiles embed the traction/braking physics, keeping the model linear.
- **Bidirectional shared resource (C6).** The auxiliary $\omega$ is the standard AND-linearization of $x\cdot r$, enforcing one train per track per time step — critical because rerouting places opposite-direction trains on the same single track through the blocked segment.
- **Disruption handling (C5, C12).** The blocked nominal track is forbidden during $\mathcal{W}$; affected trains must reroute, wait, or cancel. This gives the "partial blockage" semantics.
- **Headway & ordering (C7–C9).** Big-M disjunctions enforce the safety headway; antisymmetry and cross-segment consistency ensure physical, overtaking-free ordering.
- **Objective trade-off (C14).** Delay is a slack positive-part, so only tardiness is penalized.

---

## 7. Assumptions (marked)

- **(A1)** Discrete speed profiles with precomputed run times and energy coefficients (standard TSMP discretization).
- **(A2)** Disruption window $\mathcal{W}$ and blocked segment $s^\star$ are exogenous inputs.
- **(A3)** Min dwell, headway, running times, and time bounds are known.
- **(A4)** Rerouting is allowed only to the opposite track, only within the disruption window.
- **(A5)** Two tracks per segment (bidirectional), normally directional but reverse-usable under disruption.
- **(A6)** A nominal (scheduled) timetable is given as the delay reference.

---

## 8. Solvability

Text:
# TRSMP — Final MILP Formulation

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $k, l \in \mathcal{K}$ | trains |
| $j \in \mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | stations (ordered along the line) |
| $i \in \mathcal{E} = \{1,\dots,N-1\}$ | segments, where segment $i=(j,j+1)$ |
| $\rho \in \mathcal{R}=\{1,2\}$ | **physical tracks**: 1 = up-direction, 2 = down-direction |
| $s \in \mathcal{L}$ | discrete speed levels |
| $t \in \mathcal{T}=\{0,1,\dots,T\}$ | integer time steps (horizon) |

## Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d_k \in \{1,2\}$ | nominal direction of train $k$ (= its nominal physical track) |
| $a^{\text{plan}}_{k,j}$ | planned arrival time of $k$ at station $j$ |
| $\text{dep}^{\text{plan}}_{k,j}$ | planned departure time of $k$ from station $j$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway (block clearance time) |
| $\tau_{\min}, \tau_{\max}$ | min/max running time per segment |
| $\tau_{i,s}$ | running time on segment $i$ at speed level $s$ |
| $E_{i,s}$ | energy on segment $i$ at speed level $s$ |
| $\underline{\text{dw}}, \overline{\text{dw}}$ | min/max dwell time |
| $[t_a^{\text{dis}}, t_b^{\text{dis}}]$ | disruption time window |
| $\rho_{\text{blk}} \in \{1,2\}$ | blocked physical track during disruption |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | set of disrupted segments |
| $\text{Cap}_j$ | station capacity (trains simultaneously at station $j$) |
| $M$ | big-M constant: $M = T + \tau_{\max} + \overline{\text{dw}}$ |
| $w^{\text{delay}}, w^{\text{cancel}}, w^{\text{energy}}, w^{\text{reroute}}, w^{\text{slack}}$ | objective weights |

## Decision Variables

**Binary:**
- $z_k$: 1 if train $k$ is cancelled
- $r_{k,i}$: 1 if train $k$ is rerouted on segment $i$
- $u_{k,i,\rho}$: 1 if train $k$ uses **physical track** $\rho$ on segment $i$
- $\delta_{k,l,i,\rho}$: 1 if $k$ precedes $l$ on segment $i$, track $\rho$
- $\phi_{k,i,\rho,t}$: 1 if train $k$ occupies segment $i$ on track $\rho$ at time $t$
- $\psi_{k,j,t}$: 1 if train $k$ is at station $j$ at time $t$
- $y_{k,i,s}$: 1 if train $k$ uses speed level $s$ on segment $i$

**Continuous:**
- $a_{k,j}$: arrival time of $k$ at station $j$
- $\text{dep}_{k,j}$: departure time of $k$ from station $j$
- $g_{k,j} \ge 0$: delay of $k$ at station $j$
- $\text{sl}_{k,i} \ge 0$: slack (waiting) before entering segment $i$

---

## Objective

$$
\min \; Z = w^{\text{delay}}\!\!\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}}\sum_{j \in \mathcal{S}} g_{k,j}
\;+\; w^{\text{cancel}}\sum_{k} z_k
\;+\; w^{\text{energy}}\!\!\sum_{k}\sum_{i}\sum_{s} E_{i,s}\, y_{k,i,s}
\;+\; w^{\text{reroute}}\sum_{k}\sum_{i} r_{k,i}
\;+\; w^{\text{slack}}\sum_{k}\sum_{i} \text{sl}_{k,i}
$$

with $w^{\text{delay}} \gg w^{\text{cancel}} \gg w^{\text{energy}} \gg w^{\text{reroute}} \gg w^{\text{slack}} > 0$.

---

## Constraints

### (C1) Delay definition (non-negative)
$$
g_{k,j} \ge a_{k,j} - a^{\text{plan}}_{k,j}, \qquad g_{k,j} \ge 0 \quad \forall k, j
$$

### (C2) Cancellation: no timing, track, or speed enforced
$$
a_{k,j} \le M(1 - z_k),\quad \text{dep}_{k,j} \le M(1-z_k) \quad \forall k, j
$$
$$
y_{k,i,s} \le 1 - z_k,\quad u_{k,i,\rho} \le 1 - z_k,\quad r_{k,i} \le 1 - z_k \quad \forall k,i,\rho,s
$$

### (C3) Departure after arrival + dwell bounds
$$
\text{dep}_{k,j} \ge a_{k,j} + \underline{\text{dw}} \quad \forall k, j
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{k,j} \le a_{k,j} + \overline{\text{dw}} + M z_k \quad \forall k, j
$$

### (C4) Running time on each segment (speed choice + slack)
For segment $i=(j,j+1)$:
$$
a_{k,j+1} \ge \text{dep}_{k,j} + \sum_{s} \tau_{i,s}\, y_{k,i,s} + \text{sl}_{k,i} - M z_k
$$
$$
a_{k,j+1} \le \text{dep}_{k,j} + \sum_{s} \tau_{i,s}\, y_{k,i,s} + \text{sl}_{k,i} + M z_k
$$

### (C5) Speed level selection and running-time bounds
$$
\sum_{s} y_{k,i,s} = 1 - z_k \quad \forall k,i
$$
$$
\tau_{\min} \le \sum_{s} \tau_{i,s}\, y_{k,i,s} \le \tau_{\max} \quad \forall k,i
$$

### (C6) Horizon
$$
\text{dep}_{k,N} \le T + M z_k \quad \forall k, \qquad a_{k,j}, \text{dep}_{k,j} \ge 0 \quad \forall k,j
$$

### (C7) Track assignment (physical tracks)
$$
u_{k,i,d_k} \ge 1 - z_k - r_{k,i} \quad \forall k,i
$$
$$
u_{k,i,3-d_k} \le r_{k,i} \quad \forall k,i
$$
$$
u_{k,i,1} + u_{k,i,2} = 1 - z_k \quad \forall k,i
$$

### (C8) Rerouting feasibility: contiguous disrupted segments only
$$
r_{k,i} \le \mathbb{1}[i \in \mathcal{D}] \quad \forall k,i
$$
$$
r_{k,i} - r_{k,i+1} \le \mathbb{1}[i+1 \notin \mathcal{D}] \quad \forall k, i \in \{1,\dots,N-2\}
$$

### (C9) Rerouting only if the train traverses the disrupted segment within the window
$$
\phi_{k,i,3-d_k,t} \ge r_{k,i} - M(1 - \phi^{\text{win}}_{i,t}) \quad \forall k, i\in\mathcal{D}, t\in[t_a^{\text{dis}},t_b^{\text{dis}}]
$$
where $\phi^{\text{win}}_{i,t}=1$ iff $t$ lies in the disruption window (data).

### (C10) Blocked track forbidden during disruption
$$
\phi_{k,i,\rho_{\text{blk}},t} = 0 \quad \forall k, i\in\mathcal{D}, t\in[t_a^{\text{dis}},t_b^{\text{dis}}]
$$

### (C11) Occupancy linking to arrival/departure
For segment $i=(j,j+1)$, track $\rho$:
$$
\phi_{k,i,\rho,t} \le u_{k,i,\rho} \quad \forall k,i,\rho,t
$$
$$
t \ge \text{dep}_{k,j} - M(1 - \phi_{k,i,\rho,t})
$$
$$
t \le a_{k,j+1} + M(1 - \phi_{k,i,\rho,t})
$$
$$
\phi_{k,i,\rho,t} \ge u_{k,i,\rho} + \frac{t - \text{dep}_{k,j}}{M} + \frac{a_{k,j+1} - t}{M} - 1
$$

### (C12) Segment capacity per physical track
$$
\sum_{k} \phi_{k,i,\rho,t} \le 1 \quad \forall i,\rho,t
$$

### (C13) Headway / ordering on the same physical track
**Ordering activation:**
$$
\delta_{k,l,i,\rho} + \delta_{l,k,i,\rho} \ge u_{k,i,\rho} + u_{l,i,\rho} - 1 \quad \forall k<l, i, \rho
$$
$$
\delta_{k,l,i,\rho} \le u_{k,i,\rho},\quad \delta_{k,l,i,\rho} \le u_{l,i,\rho} \quad \forall k,l,i,\rho
$$

**Headway:**
$$
\text{dep}_{l,j} \ge a_{k,j+1} + h - M(1 - \delta_{k,l,i,\rho}) \quad \forall k \ne l, i=(j,j+1), \rho
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{k,j} \ge a_{l,j+1} + h - M(1 - \delta_{l,k,i,\rho}) \quad \forall k \ne l, i=(j,j+1), \rho
$$

### (C14) No overtaking on a segment
$$
a_{k,j+1} \le a_{l,j+1} + M(1 - \delta_{k,l,i,\rho}) \quad \forall k\ne l, i=(j,j+1), \rho
$$

### (C15) Station capacity
$$
\sum_{k} \psi_{k,j,t} \le \text{Cap}_j \quad \forall j,t
$$
$$
a_{k,j} \le t + M(1 - \psi_{k,j,t}) \quad \forall k,j,t
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{k,j} \ge t + 1 - M(1 - \psi_{k,j,t}) \quad \forall k,j,t
$$
$$
\psi_{k,j,t} \le 1 - z_k \quad \forall k,j,t
$$

### (C16) Binary and non-negativity
$$
z_k, r_{k,i}, u_{k,i,\rho}, \delta_{k,l,i,\rho}, \phi_{k,i,\rho,t}, \psi_{k,j,t}, y_{k,i,s} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{k,j}, \text{dep}_{k,j}, g_{k,j}, \text{sl}_{k,i} \ge 0
$$

---

## Summary of Assumptions

1. **Discrete integer time** $t \in \{0,\dots,T\}$; arrival/departure times are integers (station-capacity linearization C15 relies on this).
2. **Two physical tracks**, one per direction; track 1 = up, track 2 = down. Nominal direction of train $k$ is $d_k$.
3. **Rerouting** = using the opposite physical track on a contiguous set of disrupted segments, then returning to nominal.
4. **Disruption** is a fixed window $[t_a^{\text{dis}}, t_b^{\text{dis}}]$ during which one physical track $\rho_{\text{blk}}$ is blocked on segments $\mathcal{D}$.
5. **Headway** $h$ applies to all trains on the same physical track regardless of nominal direction — this resolves bidirectional conflicts.
6. **Speed levels** are discrete; running time $\tau_{i,s}$ bounded by $[\tau_{\min},\tau_{\max}]$; energy $E_{i,s}$ piecewise-constant.
7. **Dwell** bounded in $[\underline{\text{dw}}, \overline{\text{dw}}]$.
8. **Big-M** is a single consistent constant $M = T + \tau_{\max} + \overline{\text{dw}}$.
9. **Cancellation** removes all timing, track, and speed obligations.
10. **No overtaking** on a segment is enforced via ordering consistency at the downstream station.
11. **Objective weights** satisfy $w^{\text{delay}} \gg w^{\text{cancel}} \gg w^{\text{energy}} \gg w^{\text{reroute}} \gg w^{\text{slack}} > 0$ to break ties.
12. Trains must depart the last station within the horizon $T$.
13. **Position–time alignment** between timetable and speed profile is enforced by C4 (running time from the selected speed level plus slack).

Text:
# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Among the three generated models, **Model 1** is the most complete and rigorous. It provides the clearest coupling between the timetable and speed-profile layers (via position variables $p_{i,s,t}$), explicitly handles bidirectional conflicts on the shared track, and includes all necessary linearizations. Below is the refined, complete MILP.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations/segments along the line, indexed by $s$ |
| $S^{dis}$ | The single disrupted segment |
| $K = \{N, O\}$ | Tracks: $N$ = normal track, $O$ = opposite track |
| $T$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $t$ |
| $T^{dis} = [T_{start}, T_{end}]$ | Disruption time window |
| $I^{up}, I^{down}$ | Trains by direction ($I^{up} \cup I^{down} = I$) |

**Parameters:** direction $d_i$; min headway $h_{min}$; min/max running time $\tau^{min}_{i,s}, \tau^{max}_{i,s}$; min/max dwell $dw^{min}_{i,s}, dw^{max}_{i,s}$; speed bounds $v_{min}, v_{max}$; max acceleration $a_{max}$; time step $\Delta t$; segment length $L_s$; big-M $M$; weights $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$; passenger weight $w_i$; piecewise-linear energy $e(v)$; scheduled times $a^{sched}_{i,s}, dep^{sched}_{i,s}$.

---

## 2. Decision Variables

**Timetable (continuous):** $a_{i,s}, dep_{i,s} \geq 0$

**Ordering (binary):** $y_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$ — train $i$ precedes $j$ on segment $s$

**Rerouting (binary):** $r_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$ — train $i$ uses opposite track on segment $s$

**Track assignment (binary):** $x_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$

**Speed profile (continuous):** $v_{i,s,t} \geq 0$; position $p_{i,s,t} \geq 0$; segment-active $z_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$

**Acceleration mode (binary):** $u^{+}_{i,s,t}, u^{-}_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$

**Cancellation (binary):** $c_i \in \{0,1\}$

**Auxiliary:** $\Delta a_i \geq 0$ (terminal delay)

---

## 3. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in I} w_i \, \Delta a_i}_{\text{passenger delay}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s \in S} \sum_{t \in T} e(v_{i,s,t}) \cdot \Delta t}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{\gamma \sum_{i \in I} w_i \, c_i}_{\text{cancellation}}
+ \underbrace{\delta \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s \in S} r_{i,s}}_{\text{rerouting}}
$$

with $e(v)$ piecewise-linear in $v$ (SOS2 on breakpoints).

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Timetable Feasibility
$$
dep_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} + dw^{min}_{i,s} - M c_i \tag{C1}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} \leq a_{i,s} + dw^{max}_{i,s} + M c_i \tag{C2}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \geq dep_{i,s} + \tau^{min}_{i,s} - M c_i \tag{C3}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \leq dep_{i,s} + \tau^{max}_{i,s} + M c_i \tag{C4}
$$

### 4.2 Headway (Same Direction, Same Track)
$$
dep_{j,s} \geq a_{i,s} + h_{min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M(c_i + c_j) \tag{C5}
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} \geq a_{j,s} + h_{min} - M\, y_{i,j,s} - M(c_i + c_j) \tag{C6}
$$
$$
y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} = 1 \tag{C7}
$$

### 4.3 Rerouting Restrictions
$$
r_{i,s} = 0 \quad \forall s \neq S^{dis} \tag{C8}
$$
$$
r_{i,S^{dis}} \leq 1 - \frac{\max(0, dep_{i,S^{dis}} - T_{end})}{M} \tag{C9a}
$$
$$
r_{i,S^{dis}} \leq 1 - \frac{\max(0, T_{start} - a_{i,S^{dis}+1})}{M} \tag{C9b}
$$

### 4.4 Track Capacity and Assignment
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,s,k} = 1 - c_i \tag{C10}
$$
$$
x_{i,s,O} = r_{i,s} \tag{C11}
$$
$$
x_{i,s,N} = 1 - r_{i,s} - c_i \tag{C12}
$$

### 4.5 Bidirectional Conflict on Shared Track
$$
dep_{j,S^{dis}} \geq a_{i,S^{dis}} + h_{min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,S^{dis}}) - M(2 - r_{i,S^{dis}} - r_{j,S^{dis}}) \tag{C13}
$$
$$
dep_{i,S^{dis}} \geq a_{j,S^{dis}} + h_{min} - M\, y_{i,j,S^{dis}} - M(2 - r_{i,S^{dis}} - r_{j,S^{dis}}) \tag{C14}
$$
$$
y_{i,j,S^{dis}} + y_{j,i,S^{dis}} \geq r_{i,S^{dis}} + r_{j,S^{dis}} - 1 \tag{C15}
$$

### 4.6 Speed Profile Coupling
$$
p_{i,s,t+1} = p_{i,s,t} + v_{i,s,t} \cdot \Delta t \tag{C16a}
$$
$$
p_{i,s,t} \leq L_s \tag{C16b}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} - dep_{i,s} = \sum_{t \in T} \Delta t \cdot z_{i,s,t} \tag{C16c}
$$
$$
v_{min} \cdot z_{i,s,t} \leq v_{i,s,t} \leq v_{max} \cdot z_{i,s,t} \tag{C17}
$$
$$
v_{i,s,t+1} - v_{i,s,t} \leq a_{max} \Delta t + M(1 - z_{i,s,t}) \tag{C18}
$$
$$
v_{i,s,t} - v_{i,s,t+1} \leq a_{max} \Delta t + M(1 - z_{i,s,t}) \tag{C19}
$$
$$
v_{i,s,t+1} - v_{i,s,t} \leq M \cdot u^{+}_{i,s,t} \tag{C20}
$$
$$
v_{i,s,t} - v_{i,s,t+1} \leq M \cdot u^{-}_{i,s,t} \tag{C21}
$$
$$
u^{+}_{i,s,t} + u^{-}_{i,s,t} \leq 1 \tag{C22}
$$

### 4.7 Disruption Block
$$
dep_{i,S^{dis}} \geq T_{end} - M(1 - x_{i,S^{dis},N}) \quad \text{OR} \quad a_{i,S^{dis}+1} \leq T_{start} + M(1 - x_{i,S^{dis},N}) \tag{C24a}
$$

### 4.8 Cancellation
$$
x_{i,s,k} \leq 1 - c_i, \quad r_{i,s} \leq 1 - c_i, \quad v_{i,s,t} \leq v_{max}(1 - c_i) \tag{C25–C27}
$$

### 4.9 Delay Definition
$$
\Delta a_i \geq a_{i,s^{last}_i} - a^{sched}_{i,s^{last}_i} - M c_i, \quad \Delta a_i \geq 0 \tag{C28–C29}
$$

### 4.10 Domains
$$
a_{i,s}, dep_{i,s}, v_{i,s,t}, p_{i,s,t} \geq 0; \quad y_{i,j,s}, r_{i,s}, x_{i,s,k}, u^{\pm}_{i,s,t}, z_{i,s,t}, c_i \in \{0,1\} \tag{C30–C32}
$$

---

## 5. Assumptions (marked)

1. **Fixed disruption** window $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$ and location $S^{dis}$ are known and deterministic.
2. **Known train set**, directions, paths, and passenger loads.
3. **Piecewise-linear energy** approximation of traction energy $\propto v^2$ (SOS2).
4. **Discrete time** with fine step $\Delta t$ (1–5 s).
5. **No overtaking** on normal track; ordering enforced via $y_{i,j,s}$.
6. **Bounded dwell times** $[dw^{min}, dw^{max}]$.
7. **Single disruption segment** (generalizable to multiple).
8. **Double-track line** under normal operations.
9. **Big-M validity** with segment-specific tight values recommended.

---

**Why Model 1 is best:** It uniquely provides the position-variable formulation ($p_{i,s,t}$) that *exactly* couples speed profiles to the timetable (distance = speed × time), which is the central scientific contribution of the TRSMP. It also gives the most explicit and correct treatment of bidirectional conflicts (C13–C15) and disruption blocking (C24a), while keeping all constraints linear.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model derived from the code, expressed as equations. The model addresses combined train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) and speed management (speed-profile selection) on a high-speed line disrupted by a partial segment blockage, with local rerouting onto the opposite track.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S = \{1,\dots,\bar S\}$ | Stations, indexed $s$ in line order |
| $G$ | Track segments $g=(s,s+1)$ between consecutive stations |
| $T$ | Trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $K$ | Discrete speed options, indexed $k$ |
| $D$ | Ordered same-direction train pairs $(i,j,g)$ |
| $O$ | Opposite-direction train pairs $(i,j,g)$ |
| $g^\star$ | The disrupted segment |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_g$ | Length of segment $g$ (km) — *used indirectly via $P_{gk}$* |
| $P_{gk}$ | Running time of segment $g$ under speed option $k$ |
| $E_{igk}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $g$ under speed option $k$ |
| $\mathrm{ArrE}_{is}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\mathrm{DepE}_{is}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{\min}_i$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum same-direction headway |
| $h^{\text{opp}}_{\min}$ | Minimum opposite-direction headway on a shared track |
| $T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window on $g^\star$ |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{cancel}}, w_{\text{energy}}$ | Objective weights |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) |

---

## Decision Variables

**Continuous (nonnegative):**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathrm{arr}_{is}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\mathrm{dep}_{is}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\delta_{is}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |

**Binary:**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $x_{igk}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $g$ with speed option $k$ |
| $y_{ijg}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$ (same direction) |
| $z_{ijg}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on the shared track at $g^\star$ (opposite direction) |
| $r_i$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes to the opposite track on $g^\star$ |
| $u_i$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |

---

## Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, cancellation cost, and energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} w_{\text{delay}}\,\delta_{is}
\;+\; \sum_{i \in T} w_{\text{cancel}}\,u_i
\;+\; \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{g \in G}\sum_{k \in K} w_{\text{energy}}\,E_{igk}\,x_{igk}
$$

---

## Constraints

**(1) Time propagation coupled with speed profile** (for $g=(s,s+1)$ and $s < \bar S$):

$$
\mathrm{arr}_{i,s+1} - \mathrm{dep}_{is} = \sum_{k \in K} P_{gk}\, x_{igk}
\qquad \forall i, g=(s,s+1)
$$

**(2) Exactly one speed option per traversed segment (unless cancelled):**

$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{igk} = 1 - u_i
\qquad \forall i, g
$$

**(3) Minimum dwell time:**

$$
\mathrm{dep}_{is} - \mathrm{arr}_{is} \ge t^{\min}_i\,(1 - u_i)
\qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(4) Delay definition (linearization of positive delay):**

$$
\delta_{is} \ge \mathrm{arr}_{is} - \mathrm{ArrE}_{is}, \qquad \delta_{is} \ge 0
\qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(5) Boundary times at terminal stations:**

$$
\mathrm{dep}_{i,1} \ge \mathrm{DepE}_{i,1}\,(1 - u_i)
\qquad \forall i
$$
$$
\mathrm{arr}_{i,\bar S} \ge \mathrm{ArrE}_{i,\bar S}\,(1 - u_i)
\qquad \forall i
$$

**(6) Same-direction headway / ordering** (for $(i,j,g) \in D$, with $g=(s,s+1)$):

$$
\mathrm{dep}_{is} \ge \mathrm{arr}_{js} + h_{\min}
- M(1 - y_{ijg}) - M u_i - M u_j
$$

$$
\mathrm{dep}_{js} \ge \mathrm{arr}_{is} + h_{\min}
- M y_{ijg} - M u_i - M u_j
$$

**(7) Opposite-direction / rerouting conflict on the disrupted shared track** (for $(i,j,g^\star) \in O$):

$$
\mathrm{dep}_{is} \ge \mathrm{arr}_{js} + h^{\text{opp}}_{\min}
- M(1 - z_{ijg^\star}) - M(2 - r_i - r_j) - M u_i - M u_j
$$

$$
\mathrm{dep}_{js} \ge \mathrm{arr}_{is} + h^{\text{opp}}_{\min}
- M z_{ijg^\star} - M(2 - r_i - r_j) - M u_i - M u_j
$$

*(The term $M(2 - r_i - r_j)$ activates separation only when at least one train reroutes.)*

**(8) Rerouting eligibility and disruption-window consistency:**

$$
r_i \le 1 - u_i
\qquad \forall i
$$

$$
\mathrm{arr}_{i,\,s^\star_0} \ge T^{\text{start}} - M(1 - r_i)
\qquad \forall i
$$

where $s^\star_0$ is the upstream station of $g^\star$. *(Assumption A1/A2: rerouting is only permitted within/after the disruption window onset.)*

**(9) No-overtaking ordering consistency** (for $i<j$, same direction):

$$
y_{ijg} + y_{jig} = 1
\qquad \forall (i,j,g) \in D,\ i<j
$$

**(10) Variable domains:**

$$
x_{igk},\; y_{ijg},\; z_{ijg},\; r_i,\; u_i \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
\mathrm{arr}_{is},\; \mathrm{dep}_{is},\; \delta_{is} \ge 0
$$

---

## Modeling Assumptions (marked)

- **A1** — A single disruption area $g^\star$ with window $[T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}}]$ blocks one track side; the opposite track may be used bidirectionally (rerouting).
- **A2** — Speed is discretized into a finite set of constant-speed profiles per segment, so running time and energy are linear in the binary speed-selection variables (piecewise-constant profile).
- **A3** — A non-cancelled train selects exactly one speed option per segment (no multiple changes within a segment).
- **A4** — Minimum dwell and headway constraints guarantee conflict-free, safe operations.
- **A5** — The energy parameter $E_{igk}$ and running time $P_{gk}$ are precomputed per speed option; the objective trades off delay/energy via $w_{\text{delay}}$ and $w_{\text{energy}}$.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is a complete linear model that integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management for high-speed railway operations disrupted by a partial segment blockage. The model is built on the description in the introduction, with clearly stated assumptions where information is missing.

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

**A1 – Infrastructure.** The railway line is a double-track corridor with stations $S=\{1,\dots,|S|\}$ and track blocks $B=\{1,\dots,|B|\}$ between consecutive stations. Each block $b\in B$ has a fixed length $L_b$ and is equipped with a block signaling system.

**A2 – Trains.** A set of trains $I=\{1,\dots,|I|\}$ operates on the line. Each train $i\in I$ has a planned origin $o_i$ and destination $d_i$, a direction $\text{dir}_i\in\{+1,-1\}$, a mass $m_i$, and a maximum speed $v_i^{\max}$.

**A3 – Time discretization.** The planning horizon is discretized into time intervals $K=\{1,\dots,|K|\}$ of equal length $\Delta t$ (e.g., 30 s). All event times are mapped to interval indices.

**A4 – Speed profiles.** For each (train $i$, block $b$) pair, a finite set of admissible speed profiles $P_{i,b}$ is pre-computed. Each profile $p\in P_{i,b}$ is characterized by:
- Running time $r_{i,b,p}$ (number of intervals to traverse block $b$),
- Energy consumption $e_{i,b,p}$ (kWh),
- Entry/exit speed pairs $(v_{i,b,p}^{\text{in}}, v_{i,b,p}^{\text{out}})$.

**A5 – Partial blockage.** A disruption blocks one track (say the "up" track) on a single block $\hat b$ during the time window $[\tau^{\text{start}},\tau^{\text{end}}]$. Trains scheduled to traverse $\hat b$ in that window on the blocked track must either be rerouted to the opposite (down) track, retimed outside the window, or cancelled.

**A6 – Rerouting.** A rerouted train uses the opposite track of block $\hat b$, sharing it with trains traveling in the opposite direction. This creates bidirectional conflicts that must be resolved.

**A7 – Cancellation.** Cancellation is allowed as a last resort; a cancelled train incurs a large penalty.

**A8 – Objectives.** The model jointly minimizes (i) total energy consumption and (ii) total weighted delay (and cancellation penalty), capturing the trade-off between energy-efficient driving and punctual recovery.

---

## 2. Sets, Parameters, and Variables

### 2.1 Sets
| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains |
| $S$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line) |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks |
| $K$ | Set of time intervals, $K=\{1,\dots,|K|\}$ |
| $P_{i,b}$ | Set of admissible speed profiles for train $i$ on block $b$ |
| $D=\{+1,-1\}$ | Set of travel directions |

### 2.2 Parameters
| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a time interval | s |
| $v_i^{\max}$ | Maximum speed of train $i$ | m/s |
| $a_i^{\max}, a_i^{\min}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration of train $i$ | m/s² |
| $m_i$ | Mass of train $i$ | t |
| $r_{i,b,p}$ | Running time of profile $p\in P_{i,b}$ | intervals |
| $e_{i,b,p}$ | Energy consumption of profile $p\in P_{i,b}$ | kWh |
| $v_{i,b,p}^{\text{in}}, v_{i,b,p}^{\text{out}}$ | Entry / exit speed of profile $p$ | m/s |
| $\tau^{\text{start}}_b, \tau^{\text{end}}_b$ | Disruption start/end interval on block $b$ | interval |
| $\hat b$ | Block affected by the disruption | – |
| $o_i, d_i$ | Origin / destination station of train $i$ | – |
| $\text{dir}_i$ | Direction of train $i$ ($+1$ forward, $-1$ backward) | – |
| $h_i^{\min}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at any station | intervals |
| $h_i^{\max}$ | Maximum dwell time of train $i$ at any station | intervals |
| $\pi^{\text{delay}}$ | Weight of one interval of delay | – |
| $\pi^{\text{cancel}}$ | Penalty for cancelling a train | – |
| $\pi^{\text{energy}}$ | Weight of one kWh of energy | – |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) | – |

### 2.3 Decision Variables

**Speed profile and routing:**
- $x_{i,b,p}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on block $b$.
- $w_{i,b}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on block $b$ (uses the opposite track).

**Block occupation:**
- $y_{i,b,k}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ during interval $k$.

**Timing:**
- $a_{i,s}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: Arrival time (interval index) of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $d_{i,s}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: Departure time (interval index) of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $\delta_{i,s}\ge 0$: Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ relative to schedule.

**Conflict / ordering:**
- $z_{i,j,b,k}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ at interval $k$ before train $j$ (used to break ties between trains of the same direction).
- $u_{i,j,b,k}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ and train $j$ (opposite directions) both use block $b$ at interval $k$ on the same physical track (i.e., a bidirectional conflict).

**Cancellation:**
- $c_i\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.

---

## 3. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of total energy consumption, total delay, and cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \; \pi^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i\in I}\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} e_{i,b,p}\, x_{i,b,p}
\;+\; \pi^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S} \delta_{i,s}
\;+\; \pi^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i\in I} c_i.
$$

(Trade-off between energy-efficient driving and punctual recovery is controlled by the weights $\pi^{\text{energy}}, \pi^{\text{delay}}, \pi^{\text{cancel}}$.)

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Speed Profile Selection (one profile per block, or none if cancelled)

$$
\sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} x_{i,b,p} + c_i = 1 \qquad \forall i\in I,\; b\in B. \tag{1}
$$

If train $i$ is cancelled ($c_i=1$), no profile is selected on any block.

### 4.2 Block Occupation Linked to Profile Choice

Train $i$ occupies block $b$ for exactly $r_{i,b,p}$ consecutive intervals when using profile $p$:

$$
y_{i,b,k} \ge x_{i,b,p} + x_{i,b,p'} - 1 \qquad \text{(linking auxiliary, see below)}.
$$

A cleaner linearization: introduce $q_{i,b,k}\in\{0,1\}$ indicating that train $i$ *enters* block $b$ at interval $k$, then:

$$
\sum_{k\in K} q_{i,b,k} = \sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} x_{i,b,p} \qquad \forall i,b. \tag{2}
$$

$$
y_{i,b,k} \ge q_{i,b,k'} \quad \forall k'\le k \le k'+r_{i,b,p}-1,\; p\in P_{i,b}. \tag{3}
$$

$$
y_{i,b,k} \le \sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} \sum_{k':k'\le k\le k'+r_{i,b,p}-1} q_{i,b,k'} \qquad \forall i,b,k. \tag{4}
$$

### 4.3 Speed Continuity between Consecutive Blocks

The exit speed from block $b$ must equal the entry speed to the next block $b+1$ (in the train's direction):

$$
\sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} v_{i,b,p}^{\text{out}}\, x_{i,b,p} \;=\; \sum_{p\in P_{i,b+1}} v_{i,b+1,p}^{\text{in}}\, x_{i,b+1,p}
\qquad \forall i\in I,\; b\in B\setminus\{|B|\}. \tag{5}
$$

### 4.4 Station Timing and Dwell

For each station $s$ (except origin/destination):

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \ge h_i^{\min}\,(1-c_i), \tag{6}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le h_i^{\max}\,(1-c_i). \tag{7}
$$

For the origin station $o_i$: $a_{i,o_i}$ is fixed to the scheduled departure (or shifted by retiming; see (10)). For the destination $d_i$: $a_{i,d_i}$ is the final arrival.

The departure time from a station equals the arrival time at the next block's entry, which is the entry interval of the next block:

$$
d_{i,s} = \sum_{k\in K} k\, q_{i,b_s,k} \qquad \forall i,\; s\in S\setminus\{d_i\}, \tag{8}
$$

where $b_s$ is the block departing from station $s$.

Similarly, the arrival time at station $s$ equals the exit interval of the previous block:

$$
a_{i,s} = \sum_{k\in K} \bigl(k + r_{i,b_{s-1},p_{s-1}} - 1\bigr)\, q_{i,b_{s-1},k} \qquad \forall i,\; s\in S\setminus\{o_i\}. \tag{9}
$$

### 4.5 Delay Definition

Let $a_{i,s}^{\text{sched}}$ be the scheduled arrival time. Then:

$$
\delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{\text{sched}} \qquad \forall i,s. \tag{10}
$$

($\delta_{i,s}$ is non-negative; only late arrivals count.)

### 4.6 Disruption Window Constraints

If a train $i$ would traverse the disrupted block $\hat b$ during the disruption window $[\tau^{\text{start}},\tau^{\text{end}}]$ on the blocked track, it must either be rerouted, retimed outside the window, or cancelled.

Define $\text{track}_i\in\{U,D\}$ as the original track of train $i$. If $\text{track}_i$ is the blocked track on $\hat b$:

$$
\sum_{k\in[\tau^{\text{start}},\tau^{\text{end}}]} q_{i,\hat b,k} \le w_{i,\hat b} + c_i \qquad \forall i\in I. \tag{11}
$$

That is, if the train traverses $\hat b$ during the disruption window, it must be rerouted ($w_{i,\hat b}=1$) or cancelled.

### 4.7 Rerouting Logic

A rerouted train on block $\hat b$ uses the opposite physical track. Define $\text{track}'_i$ as the opposite track. The variable $w_{i,\hat b}$ forces the use of the opposite track:

$$
w_{i,\hat b} \le 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i. \tag{12}
$$

### 4.8 Unidirectional Block Capacity (Same Direction)

Trains traveling in the same direction on the same physical track cannot occupy the same block at the same interval:

$$
y_{i,b,k} + y_{j,b,k} \le 1 + (1 - z_{i,j,b,k}) + (1 - z_{j,i,b,k}) \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; \text{dir}_i=\text{dir}_j,\; b,\; k. \tag{13}
$$

Combined with the ordering constraint:

$$
z_{i,j,b,k} + z_{j,i,b,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; \text{dir}_i=\text{dir}_j,\; b,\; k. \tag{14}
$$

(Exactly one ordering is chosen; this resolves the headway conflict.)

### 4.9 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution (Rerouted Trains)

When two trains $i$ and $j$ travel in opposite directions and at least one is rerouted on block $b$, they share the same physical track. They must not occupy the block simultaneously:

$$
y_{i,b,k} + y_{j,b,k} \le 1 + u_{i,j,b,k} \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; \text{dir}_i\neq\text{dir}_j,\; b,\; k. \tag{15}
$$

$$
u_{i,j,b,k} \ge w_{i,b} + w_{j,b} - 1 \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; \text{dir}_i\neq\text{dir}_j,\; b,\; k. \tag{16}
$$

Equation (16) activates $u_{i,j,b,k}$ only when both trains share the rerouted track. Equation (15) then forbids simultaneous occupation in that case.

### 4.10 Safety Headway between Consecutive Trains (Same Direction)

A minimum headway $\theta$ (in intervals) must separate two consecutive trains on the same block:

$$
\sum_{k'=k}^{k+\theta-1} y_{j,b,k'} \le M(1 - z_{i,j,b,k}) \qquad \forall i,j,\; \text{dir}_i=\text{dir}_j,\; b,\; k. \tag{17}
$$

### 4.11 Cancellation Consistency

If a train is cancelled, it occupies no block and has no arrival/departure times:

$$
y_{i,b,k} \le 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i,b,k. \tag{18}
$$

$$
q_{i,b,k} \le 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i,b,k. \tag{19}
$$

### 4.12 Acceleration / Deceleration Limits (Continuous Dynamics)

To ensure that the chosen speed profiles are physically feasible, the change in speed between consecutive blocks must respect acceleration limits:

$$
\sum_{p\in P_{i,b+1}} v_{i,b+1,p}^{\text{in}}\, x_{i,b+1,p} \;-\; \sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} v_{i,b,p}^{\text{out}}\, x_{i,b,p} \;\le\; a_i^{\max}\, \Delta t \cdot \text{dir}_i, \tag{20}
$$

$$
\sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} v_{i,b,p}^{\text{out}}\, x_{i,b,p} \;-\; \sum_{p\in P_{i,b+1}} v_{i,b+1,p}^{\text{in}}\, x_{i,b+1,p} \;\le\; |a_i^{\min}|\, \Delta t \cdot \text{dir}_i. \tag{21}
$$

### 4.13 Energy Computation (already in objective)

The energy term in the objective uses $e_{i,b,p}\, x_{i,b,p}$ directly. No additional constraint is needed.

### 4.14 Variable Domains

$$
x_{i,b,p}, w_{i,b}, y_{i,b,k}, q_{i,b,k}, z_{i,j,b,k}, u_{i,j,b,k}, c_i \in \{0,1\}, \tag{22}
$$

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in \{1,\dots,|K|\}, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \ge 0. \tag{23}
$$

---

## 5. Summary of the Model

The complete MILP is:

$$
\min \; \pi^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,b,p} e_{i,b,p}\, x_{i,b,p}
+ \pi^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i,s} \delta_{i,s}
+ \pi^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i} c_i
$$

subject to:
- (1) Profile/cancellation selection,
- (2)–(4) Block-occupation linkage,
- (5) Speed continuity between blocks,
- (6)–(9) Station timing and dwell,
- (10) Delay definition,
- (11)–(12) Disruption and rerouting,
- (13)–(14) Same-direction block capacity,
- (15)–(16) Bidirectional conflict resolution,
- (17) Safety headway,
- (18)–(19) Cancellation consistency,
- (20)–(21) Acceleration/deceleration feasibility,
- (22)–(23) Variable domains.

---

## 6. Remarks on the Model

1. **Integration of TRP and TSMP.** Variables $x_{i,b,p}$ (speed profiles) are coupled with $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ (timetable) and $w_{i,b}$ (routing) through constraints (5), (8)–(9), and (20)–(21), guaranteeing that the timetable and the speed profiles are mutually feasible.

2. **Bidirectional conflict handling.** Constraints (15)–(16) explicitly model the conflict that arises when rerouted trains share the opposite track with trains traveling in the opposite direction.

3. **Energy–delay trade-off.** The objective weights $\pi^{\text{energy}}$ and $\pi^{\text{delay}}$ allow the dispatcher to balance energy-efficient driving against punctual recovery.

4. **Computational complexity.** The model is a large-scale MILP; in practice it is solved by the decomposition described in the paper (reformulated IP + per-train plans + adaptive iterative refinement), which is equivalent to this MILP when the interval plans are sufficiently fine.

5. **Assumptions marked.** A1–A8 are explicit modeling assumptions introduced to make the problem fully specified; they can be relaxed (e.g., multiple disrupted blocks, multiple time windows) by extending the corresponding sets and constraints in a straightforward way.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,S\}$ | Stations, ordered along the line |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1,\dots,K\}$, $K=S-1$ | Track segments between consecutive stations |
| $\mathcal{N} = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | Trains |
| $\mathcal{V}_{i,k}$ | Finite set of feasible speed levels for train $i$ on segment $k$ |
| $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ | Set of blocked segments (disruption area) |
| $\mathcal{T} = \{0,1,\dots,T_{\max}\}$ | Discrete time horizon |
| $\text{Compat}(v) \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{i,k+1}$ | Speed levels on segment $k+1$ compatible with level $v$ on segment $k$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ |
| $v$ | Speed value of a speed level |
| $\tau_{i,k,v} = \lceil L_k / v \rceil$ | Pre-computed integer running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ at level $v$ |
| $e_{i,k,v}$ | Pre-computed energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $k$ at level $v$ |
| $a^*_{i,s},\ d^*_{i,s}$ | Planned (scheduled) arrival/departure times |
| $d_i \in \{0,1\}$ | Direction of train $i$ (0 = downstream, 1 = upstream) |
| $dw^{\min}, dw^{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at any station |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains on the same track resource |
| $T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}}$ | Start and end of the disruption window |
| $C^{\text{cancel}}, C^{\text{reroute}}$ | Penalty for cancelling / rerouting |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Objective weights |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timing variables** (continuous, non-negative integers):
- $a_{i,s} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ — actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ — actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$

**Speed-level selection** (binary):
- $x_{i,k,v} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $v$ on segment $k$

**Rerouting** (binary):
- $r_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $k$

**Track-usage indicator** (binary, auxiliary):
- $u_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses the *forward* track on segment $k$; equals $d_i \oplus r_{i,k}$

**Conflict indicator** (binary, auxiliary):
- $w_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ share the same physical track on segment $k$

**Ordering** (binary):
- $y_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ departs segment $k$ no later than train $j$

**Disruption-window selector** (binary):
- $z_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if non-rerouted train $i$ enters segment $k$ *after* $T^{\text{end}}$

**Cancellation** (binary):
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled

**Delay (deviation) variables** (continuous, non-negative):
- $\delta^{a}_{i,s}, \delta^{d}_{i,s} \geq 0$ — absolute deviation of arrival/departure from the planned timetable

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \quad
w_1 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{N}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} \left(\delta^{a}_{i,s} + \delta^{d}_{i,s}\right)
\;+\;
w_2 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{N}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{i,k}} e_{i,k,v}\, x_{i,k,v}
\;+\;
w_3 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{N}} C^{\text{cancel}}\, c_i
\;+\;
w_4 \sum_{i\in\mathcal{N}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} C^{\text{reroute}}\, r_{i,k}
$$

The four terms represent: (i) delay relative to the planned timetable, (ii) tractive energy consumption, (iii) cancellation penalties, and (iv) rerouting penalties.

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Arrival–departure linkage (dwell time)
$$
d_{i,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} + dw^{\min}\,(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \;\leq\; a_{i,s} + dw^{\max}\,(1 - c_i) + M\,c_i \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
$$

### (C2) Running time on each segment
$$
a_{i,k+1} - d_{i,k} \;=\; \sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{i,k}} \tau_{i,k,v}\, x_{i,k,v} \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{K}
$$

### (C3) Exactly one speed level per segment (or none if cancelled)
$$
\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{i,k}} x_{i,k,v} \;=\; 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{K}
$$

### (C4) Speed transition compatibility (acceleration/deceleration)
$$
x_{i,k,v} \;\leq\; \sum_{v'\in\text{Compat}(v)} x_{i,k+1,v'} \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{K}\setminus\{K\},\; v\in\mathcal{V}_{i,k}
$$

### (C5) Rerouting only inside the disruption area and only for non-cancelled trains
$$
r_{i,k} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{K}\setminus\mathcal{B}
$$
$$
r_{i,k} \;\leq\; 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{B}
$$

### (C6) Track-usage indicator (XOR linearization)
$$
u_{i,k} \;\leq\; d_i + r_{i,k}
$$
$$
u_{i,k} \;\leq\; 2 - d_i - r_{i,k}
$$
$$
u_{i,k} \;\geq\; d_i - r_{i,k}
$$
$$
u_{i,k} \;\geq\; r_{i,k} - d_i
\qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{K}
$$

### (C7) Conflict indicator (same physical track on segment $k$)
$$
w_{i,j,k} \;\geq\; u_{i,k} - u_{j,k}
$$
$$
w_{i,j,k} \;\geq\; u_{j,k} - u_{i,k}
$$
$$
w_{i,j,k} \;\leq\; u_{i,k} + u_{j,k}
$$
$$
w_{i,j,k} \;\leq\; 2 - u_{i,k} - u_{j,k}
\qquad \forall i<j\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{K}
$$

### (C8) Headway / ordering on shared track resources
$$
d_{i,k} + h^{\min} \;\leq\; d_{j,k} + M\,(1 - y_{i,j,k}) + M\,(1 - w_{i,j,k})
$$
$$
d_{j,k} + h^{\min} \;\leq\; d_{i,k} + M\,y_{i,j,k} + M\,(1 - w_{i,j,k})
\qquad \forall i\neq j\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{K}
$$

### (C9) Disruption-window entry restriction (for blocked segments)
$$
d_{i,k} \;\leq\; T^{\text{start}} + M\,(1 - z_{i,k}) + M\,r_{i,k}
$$
$$
d_{i,k} \;\geq\; T^{\text{end}} - M\,z_{i,k} - M\,r_{i,k}
\qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; k\in\mathcal{B}
$$

### (C10) Rerouted trains return to original track after the disruption area
$$
r_{i,k^{\text{out}}} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\quad k^{\text{out}} = \max(\mathcal{B}) + 1
$$

### (C11) Cancellation: time variables are neutralized
$$
a_{i,s} \;\leq\; M\,(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \;\leq\; M\,(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
$$

### (C12) Delay (deviation) linearization
$$
\delta^{a}_{i,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} - a^*_{i,s} \qquad
\delta^{a}_{i,s} \;\geq\; a^*_{i,s} - a_{i,s}
$$
$$
\delta^{d}_{i,s} \;\geq\; d_{i,s} - d^*_{i,s} \qquad
\delta^{d}_{i,s} \;\geq\; d^*_{i,s} - d_{i,s}
\qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{N},\; s\in\mathcal{S}
$$

### (C13) Variable domains and bounds
$$
a_{i,s},\ d_{i,s},\ \delta^{a}_{i,s},\ \delta^{d}_{i,s} \;\in\; \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
$$
$$
x_{i,k,v},\ r_{i,k},\ u_{i,k},\ w_{i,j,k},\ y_{i,j,k},\ z_{i,k},\ c_i \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{i,s},\ d_{i,s} \;\leq\; T_{\max}
$$

## 6. Explanation of the Model Elements

**Decision layers.** The model integrates four coupled decisions: (i) *retiming* of arrivals/departures at every station, (ii) *reordering* of trains that share a track resource, (iii) *rerouting* of disrupted trains onto the opposite track within the blocked area, and (iv) *speed management* via a discretized speed profile. Cancellation is a last-resort binary option.

**Speed discretization (A2–A3).** Because running time and energy are nonlinear in continuous speed, the speed on each segment is restricted to a finite set $\mathcal{V}_{i,k}$. The chosen level determines both the running time $\tau_{i,k,v}$ and the energy $e_{i,k,v}$, both pre-computed as parameters. Constraint (C4) enforces acceleration/deceleration feasibility between consecutive segments by requiring the next segment's level to belong to a precomputed compatibility set.

**Disruption handling (A5–A6, C5, C9, C10).** Trains in the affected direction cannot enter a blocked segment during $[T^{\text{start}}, T^{\text{end}}]$ unless they reroute (C9). Rerouting is only allowed inside $\mathcal{B}$ (C5) and must end immediately after the disruption area (C10), so the line returns to normal double-track operation afterwards.

**Conflict resolution (C6–C8).** The XOR-linearized variable $u_{i,k}$ identifies which physical track each train actually uses on each segment. Two trains conflict on a segment iff $u_{i,k}=u_{j,k}$, captured by $w_{i,j,k}$. The big-M ordering constraints (C8) then enforce the minimum headway $h^{\min}$ only when a conflict exists; otherwise they are inactive.

**Cancellation (C11).** When $c_i=1$, all speed-level variables are forced to zero by (C3), all time variables are forced to zero by (C11), and the running-time equation (C2) collapses to $0=0$. The cancellation cost $C^{\text{cancel}}$ enters the objective.

**Objective.** A weighted sum balances four stakeholder concerns: passenger-facing delay (deviation from the planned timetable), operator energy cost, service cancellation, and infrastructure disruption (rerouting). The weights $w_1,\dots,w_4$ are tunable policy parameters.

**Linearity.** All nonlinear elements (absolute values, XOR, disjunctions, piecewise speed) are linearized using auxiliary variables and big-M constants, yielding a standard MILP solvable by branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Complete MILP

Below is the selected best model (a refined synthesis of the three generated formulations), presented completely with sets, parameters, variables, objective, and constraints.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations along the line, ordered $s = 1, \dots, |S|$ |
| $G$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations, $g = (s, s+1) \in G$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | Disruption time window (set of time periods), indexed by $t$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions, $D = \{+, -\}$ (up/down) |
| $T^+ \subseteq T$ | Trains traveling in the positive direction |
| $T^- \subseteq T$ | Trains traveling in the negative direction |
| $g^*$ | The blocked segment |
| $d^*$ | The blocked direction |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_g$ | Length of segment $g$ |
| $v_k$ | Speed level $k$ |
| $v_g^{\max}$ | Speed limit on segment $g$ |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration |
| $\tau_{i,g,k}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $g$ at speed level $k$ |
| $e_{i,g,k}$ | Traction energy of train $i$ on segment $g$ at speed level $k$ |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway (safety separation time) |
| $dw_s^{\min}, dw_s^{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $t_{i,s}^{arr,sch}, t_{i,s}^{dep,sch}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $P_i$ | Passenger load of train $i$ (delay weight) |
| $C_i^{cancel}$ | Penalty cost for cancelling train $i$ |
| $W_{start}, W_{end}$ | Start / end of disruption window |
| $\delta_{g,d}^{block}$ | Binary: 1 if segment $g$ in direction $d$ is blocked during $\mathcal{W}$ |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Objective weights (delay, cancellation, energy) |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $H$ | Planning time horizon |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Timing (continuous)
- $a_{i,s} \geq 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{i,s} \geq 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $\Delta_{i,s}^{arr}, \Delta_{i,s}^{dep} \geq 0$: arrival / departure delay

### Speed profile selection (binary)
- $x_{i,g,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $g$

### Ordering (binary)
- $y_{i,j,g} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$ (same direction)

### Rerouting (binary)
- $r_{i,g} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ reroutes to the opposite track on segment $g$ during disruption
- $z_{i,j,g} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if rerouted train $i$ precedes normal train $j$ on the shared opposite track

### Cancellation (binary)
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} P_i \left(\Delta_{i,s}^{arr} + \Delta_{i,s}^{dep}\right)
\;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in T} C_i^{cancel}\, c_i
\;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{g \in G}\sum_{k \in K} e_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k}
$$

- **Term 1:** Passenger-weighted total delay (service quality).
- **Term 2:** Cancellation penalty (service coverage).
- **Term 3:** Total traction energy (operational cost / sustainability).

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Speed Profile Selection
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,g,k} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in G
\tag{1}
$$

### 5.2 Train Movement (running time coupled to speed profile)
$$
a_{i,s+1} \geq d_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in K} \tau_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k} - M c_i \qquad \forall i,\; g=(s,s+1)
\tag{2a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \leq d_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in K} \tau_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k} + M c_i \qquad \forall i,\; g=(s,s+1)
\tag{2b}
$$

### 5.3 Dwell Time
$$
dw_s^{\min}(1 - c_i) \leq d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \leq dw_s^{\max}(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S \setminus \{1, |S|\}
\tag{3}
$$

### 5.4 Delay Definition
$$
\Delta_{i,s}^{arr} \geq a_{i,s} - t_{i,s}^{arr,sch} \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{4a}
$$
$$
\Delta_{i,s}^{dep} \geq d_{i,s} - t_{i,s}^{dep,sch} \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{4b}
$$

### 5.5 Headway / Safety (same direction)
$$
d_{j,s} \geq d_{i,s} + h_{\min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,g}) - M(c_i + c_j) \qquad \forall i \neq j \in T^d,\; g
\tag{5a}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \geq d_{j,s} + h_{\min} - M y_{i,j,g} - M(c_i + c_j) \qquad \forall i \neq j \in T^d,\; g
\tag{5b}
$$
$$
y_{i,j,g} + y_{j,i,g} = 1 - c_i - c_j \qquad \forall i \neq j \in T^d,\; g
\tag{5c}
$$

### 5.6 Segment Blockage
For the blocked segment $g^*$ in blocked direction $d^*$:
$$
\sum_{k} x_{i,g^*,k} \leq r_{i,g^*} + c_i \qquad \forall i \in T^{d^*}
\tag{6}
$$
(A train in the blocked direction must reroute or be cancelled.)

### 5.7 Rerouting Capacity and Bidirectional Conflict
$$
z_{i,j,g^*} + z_{j,i,g^*} = 1 - c_i - c_j \qquad \forall i \in T^{d^*},\; j \in T^{-d^*}
\tag{7a}
$$
$$
d_{j,s} \geq d_{i,s} + h_{\min} - M(1 - z_{i,j,g^*}) - M(c_i + c_j)
\tag{7b}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \geq d_{j,s} + h_{\min} - M z_{i,j,g^*} - M(c_i + c_j)
\tag{7c}
$$

### 5.8 Speed Profile Feasibility
$$
x_{i,g,k} = 0 \qquad \forall i, g, k : v_k > v_g^{\max}
\tag{8a}
$$
$$
\sum_{k} \tau_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k} \geq \tau_g^{\min}, \qquad \sum_{k} \tau_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k} \leq \tau_g^{\max} \qquad \forall i, g
\tag{8b}
$$

### 5.9 Coupling Timetable to Speed Profile
$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \leq \tau_{i,g,k} + M(1 - x_{i,g,k}) \qquad \forall i, g, k
\tag{9a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \geq \tau_{i,g,k} - M(1 - x_{i,g,k}) \qquad \forall i, g, k
\tag{9b}
$$

### 5.10 Cancellation
$$
a_{i,s} \leq M(1 - c_i), \quad d_{i,s} \leq M(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{10}
$$

### 5.11 Time Horizon and Non-negativity
$$
0 \leq a_{i,s},\, d_{i,s} \leq H \qquad \forall i, s
\tag{11a}
$$
$$
\Delta_{i,s}^{arr},\, \Delta_{i,s}^{dep} \geq 0
\tag{11b}
$$
$$
x_{i,g,k},\, y_{i,j,g},\, r_{i,g},\, z_{i,j,g},\, c_i \in \{0,1\}
\tag{11c}
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions (marked)

1. **Discretized speed levels** — the nonlinear running-time/energy relationship is approximated by a finite set $K$ of precomputed $(\tau_{i,g,k}, e_{i,g,k})$ pairs, keeping the model linear.
2. **Fixed, deterministic disruption window** $\mathcal{W}$ known in advance.
3. **Single-track bidirectional operation** on the affected segment during disruption, requiring ordering binaries $z$ for conflict resolution.
4. **Big-M linearization** of all disjunctive constraints; $M$ chosen tight (e.g., $M = H$).
5. **Passenger-weighted delays** via $P_i$.
6. **Piecewise-linear energy** precomputed per speed level per segment.
7. **Terminal stations** have no dwell constraint.

---

## 7. Model Size

| Component | Type | Count (approx.) |
|-----------|------|-----------------|
| Continuous vars ($a, d, \Delta$) | Continuous | $O(|T||S|)$ |
| Speed binaries ($x$) | Binary | $O(|T||G||K|)$ |
| Ordering binaries ($y, z$) | Binary | $O(|T|^2|G|)$ |
| Rerouting binaries ($r$) | Binary | $O(|T||G|)$ |
| Cancellation binaries ($c$) | Binary | $O(|T|)$ |
| Constraints | Mixed | $O(|T|^2|G| + |T||G||K|)$ |

This MILP is solvable by commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) for realistic instances; larger networks may require the decomposition-based approach described in the source (train-plan selection IP + adaptive iterative algorithm).

Text:
# Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Railway Infrastructure Constraints: A Complete MILP Formulation

## 1. Modeling Overview

We formulate the rolling stock rescheduling problem as the interaction of two MILPs:

1. **Composition Model (CM)** — decides which rolling stock units are assigned to which trips and which shunting movements are required (based on Fioole et al., 2006).
2. **Infrastructure Model (IM)** — checks whether the shunting movements suggested by the CM can be executed on the available tracks of the considered stations, allowing short delays to other trains (based on Van Aken et al., 2017).

The two models are coupled through a Benders-style iterative framework: the CM proposes shunting movements, the IM validates them and returns feasibility cuts that are added back to the CM.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of train trips in the (possibly disrupted) timetable, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{fix} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips that cannot be cancelled |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of rolling stock types, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{U}$ | Set of individual rolling stock units, indexed by $u$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{sh} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Stations where shunting is allowed (e.g., Utrecht Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal) |
| $\mathcal{Tr}_s$ | Set of tracks at station $s$, indexed by $tr$ |
| $\mathcal{L} \subseteq \mathcal{T} \times \mathcal{T}$ | Set of feasible rolling stock connections $(i,j)$ where trip $i$ is followed by trip $j$ at the same station, indexed by $\ell$ |
| $\mathcal{L}_s \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ | Connections taking place at station $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of infrastructure events, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{E}^{arr}, \mathcal{E}^{dep}, \mathcal{E}^{sh}$ | Arrival, departure, and shunting events |
| $\mathcal{E}^{pax} = \mathcal{E}^{arr} \cup \mathcal{E}^{dep}$ | Passenger train events |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of potentially conflicting event pairs $(e_1,e_2)$ at the same station |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of time slots for time-indexed formulations, indexed by $\tau$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| $c^r$ | Operating cost of one unit of type $r$ per trip |
| $cap^r$ | Passenger capacity of one unit of type $r$ |
| $dem_t$ | Passenger demand of trip $t$ |
| $orig^r_t$ | Original number of type-$r$ units on trip $t$ |
| $\underline{x}^r_t, \bar{x}^r_t$ | Minimum/maximum number of type-$r$ units on trip $t$ (if not cancelled) |
| $T^{arr}_t, T^{dep}_t$ | Scheduled arrival/departure time of trip $t$ |
| $s^{arr}_t, s^{dep}_t$ | Arrival/departure station of trip $t$ |
| $T^{sched}_e$ | Scheduled time of event $e$ |
| $dur_e$ | Duration of event $e$ |
| $s_e$ | Station of event $e$ |
| $\Delta^{pax}_{max}$ | Maximum delay (minutes) allowed for passenger train events |
| $\Delta^{sh}_{max}$ | Maximum delay (minutes) allowed for shunting events |
| $P^{cancel}_e$ | Penalty for cancelling shunting event $e$ |
| $P^{delay}$ | Penalty per minute of delay for passenger trains |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Weights for operational, passenger, stick-to-plan, and delay objectives |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Composition Model

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| $x^r_t \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ | Number of rolling stock units of type $r$ assigned to trip $t$ |
| $y^r_{ij} \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ | Number of type-$r$ units transferred from trip $i$ to trip $j$ |
| $n^r_t \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ | Number of type-$r$ units inserted (from depot) at the start of trip $t$ |
| $m^r_t \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ | Number of type-$r$ units removed (to depot) at the end of trip $t$ |
| $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if trip $t$ is cancelled |
| $sh_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if a shunting movement is required for connection $(i,j)$ |
| $dev^r_t \geq 0$ | Absolute deviation of $x^r_t$ from $orig^r_t$ |
| $f^u_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if individual unit $u$ is assigned to trip $t$ (optional, for individual tracking) |

### Infrastructure Model

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| $z_{e,tr} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if event $e$ uses track $tr$ |
| $w_e \geq 0$ | Delay (minutes) of event $e$ |
| $\sigma_e \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if event $e$ is performed (relevant for shunting) |
| $\alpha_{e_1,e_2,tr} \in \{0,1\}$ | Ordering indicator: 1 if $e_1$ precedes $e_2$ on track $tr$ |
| $T^{act}_e \geq 0$ | Actual time of event $e$ (= $T^{sched}_e + w_e$) |

---

## 5. Composition Model (CM)

### 5.1 Objective Function

$$\min Z^{CM} = w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} c^r \, x^r_t}_{\text{Operating costs}} + w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \left[dem_t (1-c_t) - \sum_{r} cap^r \, x^r_t\right]^+}_{\text{Capacity shortage}} + w_3 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} dev^r_t}_{\text{Deviation from original plan}}$$

where $[a]^+ = \max\{a, 0\}$, linearized via auxiliary variables.

### 5.2 Flow Conservation Constraints

For each trip $t \in \mathcal{T}$ and type $r \in \mathcal{R}$:

$$x^r_t = \sum_{j : (t,j) \in \mathcal{L}} y^r_{tj} + m^r_t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, r \in \mathcal{R} \tag{CM.1}$$

$$x^r_t = \sum_{i : (i,t) \in \mathcal{L}} y^r_{it} + n^r_t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, r \in \mathcal{R} \tag{CM.2}$$

### 5.3 Capacity and Composition Constraints

**Capacity satisfaction:**
$$\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} cap^r \, x^r_t \geq dem_t (1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T} \tag{CM.3}$$

**Composition bounds:**
$$\underline{x}^r_t (1 - c_t) \leq x^r_t \leq \bar{x}^r_t (1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, r \in \mathcal{R} \tag{CM.4}$$

**Cancellation of fixed trips:**
$$c_t = 0 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}^{fix} \tag{CM.5}$$

### 5.4 Depot and Availability Constraints

**Total units of type $r$ available:**
$$\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{start}_r} n^r_t - \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{end}_r} m^r_t \leq N^r \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R} \tag{CM.6}$$

where $\mathcal{T}^{start}_r, \mathcal{T}^{end}_r$ are trips starting/ending at depots for type $r$, and $N^r$ is the fleet size.

### 5.5 Deviation from Original Plan

$$dev^r_t \geq x^r_t - orig^r_t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, r \in \mathcal{R} \tag{CM.7}$$
$$dev^r_t \geq orig^r_t - x^r_t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, r \in \mathcal{R} \tag{CM.8}$$

### 5.6 Shunting Movement Indicators

A shunting movement is needed at station $s$ for connection $(i,j) \in \mathcal{L}_s$ if any units are transferred:

$$M \cdot sh_{ij} \geq \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} y^r_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{L} \tag{CM.9}$$
$$sh_{ij} \leq \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} y^r_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{L} \tag{CM.10}$$

### 5.7 Benders Cuts from Infrastructure Model

For each minimal infeasible set $\mathcal{S}^{inf} \subseteq \mathcal{E}^{sh}$ returned by the IM:

$$\sum_{e \in \mathcal{S}^{inf}} \sigma_e \leq |\mathcal{S}^{inf}| - 1 \tag{CM.11}$$

(Linked to shunting indicators via $\sigma_e \leq sh_{ij}$ for the corresponding connection.)

---

## 6. Infrastructure Model (IM)

### 6.1 Objective Function

$$\min Z^{IM} = P^{delay} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}^{pax}} w_e + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}^{sh}} P^{cancel}_e (1 - \sigma_e) + \epsilon \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} w_e$$

The objective balances cancelling shunting movements against delaying passenger trains.

### 6.2 Track Assignment Constraints

Each performed event occupies exactly one track at its station:

$$\sum_{tr \in \mathcal{Tr}_{s_e}} z_{e,tr} = \sigma_e \quad \forall e \in \mathcal{E} \tag{IM.1}$$

Passenger train events must be performed:
$$\sigma_e = 1 \quad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}^{pax} \tag{IM.2}$$

### 6.3 Timing and Delay Constraints

**Actual time definition:**
$$T^{act}_e = T^{sched}_e + w_e \quad \forall e \in \mathcal{E} \tag{IM.3}$$

**Delay bounds for passenger trains:**
$$w_e \leq \Delta^{pax}_{max} \quad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}^{pax} \tag{IM.4}$$

**Delay bounds for shunting:**
$$w_e \leq \Delta^{sh}_{max} \quad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}^{sh} \tag{IM.5}$$

### 6.4 Track Conflict Constraints

For each pair $(e_1, e_2) \in \mathcal{P}$ and each track $tr \in \mathcal{Tr}_{s_{e_1}}$:

**No simultaneous track use:**
$$z_{e_1,tr} + z_{e_2,tr} \leq 1 + (1 - \alpha_{e_1,e_2,tr}) + (1 - \alpha_{e_2,e_1,tr}) \quad \forall (e_1,e_2) \in \mathcal{P}, tr \in \mathcal{Tr}_{s_{e_1}} \tag{IM.6}$$

**Ordering constraints (linearized with big-M):**
$$T^{act}_{e_1} + dur_{e_1} \leq T^{act}_{e_2} + M(1 - \alpha_{e_1,e_2,tr}) \quad \forall (e_1,e_2) \in \mathcal{P}, tr \tag{IM.7}$$
$$T^{act}_{e_2} + dur_{e_2} \leq T^{act}_{e_1} + M(1 - \alpha_{e_2,e_1,tr}) \quad \forall (e_1,e_2) \in \mathcal{P}, tr \tag{IM.8}$$
$$\alpha_{e_1,e_2,tr} + \alpha_{e_2,e_1,tr} \leq 1 \quad \forall (e_1,e_2) \in \mathcal{P}, tr \tag{IM.9}$$

### 6.5 Shunting Movement Feasibility

A shunting event $e^{sh}_{ij}$ at station $s$ for connection $(i,j)$ must fit between the arrival of trip $i$ and the departure of trip $j$:

$$T^{act}_{e^{arr}_i} + dur_{e^{arr}_i} \leq T^{act}_{e^{sh}_{ij}} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{L}_s \tag{IM.10}$$
$$T^{act}_{e^{sh}_{ij}} + dur_{e^{sh}_{ij}} \leq T^{act}_{e^{dep}_j} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{L}_s \tag{IM.11}$$

### 6.6 Linking Shunting Events to Composition Decisions

$$\sigma_{e^{sh}_{ij}} \leq sh_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{L} \tag{IM.12}$$

---

## 7. Integrated Iterative Framework

### 7.1 Exact Benders Approach

```
Initialize: No cuts, solve CM
Repeat:
  1. Solve CM → get shunting decisions {sh_ij}, compositions {x^r_t}
  2. Fix shunting set S = {(i,j) : sh_ij = 1} and pass to IM
  3. Solve IM:
     - If feasible: OPTIMAL (or improve via delay minimization)
     - If infeasible: identify minimal infeasible subset S^inf
  4. Add Benders cut (CM.11) to CM
Until: IM feasible or convergence
```

### 7.2 Iterative Heuristic (Practical)

```
Initialize: S = ∅
Repeat:
  1. Solve CM with current cuts → propose shunting movement (i*,j*)
  2. Add (i*,j*) to S
  3. Solve IM with S:
     - If feasible: accept movement
     - If infeasible: 
        * Try delaying other trains (up to Δ^pax_max)
        * If still infeasible: cancel movement, add cut
  4. Update CM with feedback
Until: No more shunting suggestions or convergence
```

This heuristic mirrors the real-world interaction between rolling stock dispatchers (NS) and infrastructure dispatchers (ProRail).

---

## 8. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Timetable input**: The (possibly disrupted) timetable is given as input; trip times and stations are fixed except for short delays.
2. **Rolling stock types**: A finite set of predefined types with known capacities and costs.
3. **Track infrastructure**: Each station has a fixed set of tracks with known topology.
4. **Shunting duration**: Each shunting movement has a known, deterministic duration.
5. **Short delays acceptable**: Passenger trains can be delayed by at most $\Delta^{pax}_{max}$ minutes (resolved by timetable buffers).
6. **Shunting cancellation**: Shunting movements can be cancelled at a penalty if infrastructure is unavailable.
7. **Trip cancellation**: Some trips may be cancelled (binary decision or fixed input).
8. **Depot operations**: Insertions and removals of rolling stock happen at predefined depot stations.
9. **Composition flexibility**: Each trip has minimum and maximum composition requirements.
10. **Static disruption**: The disruption scenario (e.g., blocked track) is fixed for the planning horizon.
11. **Independence of shunting movements**: Shunting movements at different stations are assumed independent (validated empirically in the paper).
12. **Linear separability**: All objectives and constraints are linear (or linearizable), enabling MILP solution methods.

---

## 9. Summary of Key Equations

| Equation | Purpose |
|---|---|
| CM.1–CM.2 | Rolling stock flow conservation |
| CM.3 | Passenger capacity satisfaction |
| CM.7–CM.8 | Stick-to-the-plan deviation |
| CM.9–CM.10 | Shunting movement activation |
| CM.11 | Benders feasibility cuts |
| IM.1 | Track assignment |
| IM.4–IM.5 | Delay bounds |
| IM.6–IM.9 | Track conflict prevention |
| IM.10–IM.11 | Shunting time window |
| IM.12 | Model linkage |

This formulation captures the full integrated problem: the **Composition Model** optimizes rolling stock assignments and shunting decisions across multiple objectives (cost, service level, plan adherence), while the **Infrastructure Model** ensures that every suggested shunting movement can be physically executed on the available railway tracks, optionally accepting short delays to other trains. The iterative framework enables practical deployment consistent with the European legal separation of infrastructure management and train operations.
