# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the finalized model, revised after review of the first `or_operator` output. The revisions correct three structural issues (order-coupling versus rerun coupling, the C5 overlap detection direction, and the C9 ordering logic) and tighten the reroute-continuity constraints.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ | Trains, $\mathcal{T} = \{1,\dots,|\mathcal{T}|\}$ |
| $g \in \mathcal{G}$ | Segments (block sections), $\mathcal{G} = \{1,\dots,G\}$ |
| $s \in \mathcal{S}$ | Stations, $\mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,G+1\}$ |
| $p \in \mathcal{P}_{i,g}$ | Candidate speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $g$ |
| $d \in \mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{G}$ | Disrupted segments (normal-direction track blocked) |

**Segment–station mapping:** segment $g$ connects upstream station $s=g$ to downstream station $s=g+1$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $t_D^{\text{start}}, t_D^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window (global clock) |
| $r_{i,g,p}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $g$ using profile $p$ (min) |
| $e_{i,g,p}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $g$ using profile $p$ (kWh) |
| $d_i^{\min}, d_i^{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time of train $i$ (min) |
| $h_g$ | Minimum headway / safety separation on segment $g$ (min) |
| $M$ | Large constant, $M \ge H + \max_{i,g,p} r_{i,g,p}$ |
| $t_i^{0}$ | Scheduled departure of train $i$ from its first station |
| $a_{i,s}^{0}$ | Scheduled arrival of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $w_D, w_E, w_C$ | Objective weights for delay, energy, rerouting penalty ($\ge 0$) |
| $cR_g$ | Penalty per train rerouted on segment $g$ |
| $H$ | Time horizon |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,g,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on segment $g$ |
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\text{dw}_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{i,j,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$ ($i \neq j$) |
| $z_{i,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on disrupted segment $g$ |
| $\text{delay}_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ relative to schedule |
| $o_{i,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if the traversal of segment $g$ by train $i$ overlaps the disruption window |
| $\rho_{i,j,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $i,j$ use *different* tracks on segment $g$ |
| $\text{swap}_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $i,j$ exchange order at station $s$ (auxiliary) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_D \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \text{delay}_{i,s}
\;+\; w_E \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{G}} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{i,g}} e_{i,g,p}\, x_{i,g,p}
\;+\; w_C \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{D}} cR_g\, z_{i,g}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Profile Selection
Exactly one speed profile per train per segment:

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{i,g}} x_{i,g,p} = 1
\qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; g \in \mathcal{G}
\tag{C1}
$$

### (C2) Arrival–Departure–Run-Time Coupling
For every segment $g$ with $s=g$:

$$
a_{i,s+1} \;=\; \text{dep}_{i,s} \;+\; \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{i,g}} r_{i,g,p}\, x_{i,g,p}
\qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; g \in \mathcal{G},\; s = g
\tag{C2}
$$

### (C3) Dwell Time Bounds
Intermediate stations $s \in \{2,\dots,G\}$:

$$
d_i^{\min} \;\le\; \text{dw}_{i,s} \;=\; \text{dep}_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\le\; d_i^{\max}
\qquad \forall\, i,\; s \in \{2,\dots,G\}
\tag{C3a}
$$

Origin (no pre-departure dwell; departure cannot precede schedule):

$$
a_{i,1} \;=\; \text{dep}_{i,1} \;\ge\; t_i^{0}
\qquad \forall\, i
\tag{C3b}
$$

Terminal (no dwell after final arrival):

$$
\text{dep}_{i,G+1} \;=\; a_{i,G+1}
\qquad \forall\, i
\tag{C3c}
$$

### (C4) Delay Definition
Delay is the non-negative earliness/idleness-free lower bound on actual minus scheduled arrival:

$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \;\ge\; a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{0}
\qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{C4a}
$$

$$
\text{delay}_{i,s} \;\ge\; 0
\qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{C4b}
$$

### (C5) Disruption Blocking and Overlap Detection
For $g \in \mathcal{D}$ and $s = g$, $o_{i,g}=1$ iff traversal $[\text{dep}_{i,s},\, a_{i,s+1}]$ overlaps $[t_D^{\text{start}},\, t_D^{\text{end}}]$ **and** the normal track would be used. Overlap requires simultaneous $\text{dep}_{i,s} \le t_D^{\text{end}}$ and $a_{i,s+1} \ge t_D^{\text{start}}$:

$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \;\le\; t_D^{\text{end}} + M\,(1 - o_{i,g})
\qquad \forall\, i,\; g \in \mathcal{D},\; s = g
\tag{C5a}
$$

$$
a_{i,s+1} \;\ge\; t_D^{\text{start}} - M\,(1 - o_{i,g})
\qquad \forall\, i,\; g \in \mathcal{D},\; s = g
\tag{C5b}
$$

**Rerouting requirement** — if the traversal overlaps the window, the train must use the opposite track:

$$
o_{i,g} \;\le\; z_{i,g}
\qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; g \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{C5c}
$$

**Window-avoidance option** — alternatively, a train may schedule its traversal entirely outside the disruption window on the normal track ($o_{i,g}=0$); this is captured by the disjunction below, which is implied by (C5a)–(C5b), (C5c):

$$
\Big[\, a_{i,s+1} \le t_D^{\text{start}} \,\Big] \;\plus\; \Big[\, \text{dep}_{i,s} \ge t_D^{\text{end}} \,\Big] \;\plus\; \Big[\, z_{i,g} = 1 \,\Big] \;\ge\; 1
\tag{C5d}
$$

linearized as

$$
a_{i,s+1} \;\le\; t_D^{\text{start}} + M\,(1 - \phi_{i,g})
\tag{C5d-i}
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \;\ge\; t_D^{\text{end}} - M\,(1 - \psi_{i,g})
\tag{C5d-ii}
$$
$$
\phi_{i,g} + \psi_{i,g} + z_{i,g} \;\ge\; 1
\tag{C5d-iii}
$$

with auxiliary binaries $\phi_{i,g}, \psi_{i,g} \in \{0,1\}$. (If (C5a)–(C5c) already fully fix $z_{i,g}$, the $(\phi,\psi)$ system is redundant; keep it only if the model must explicitly select the *avoid-by-waiting* alternative outside $z$.)

### (C6) Rerouting Restricted to Disrupted Segments

$$
z_{i,g} = 0
\qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; g \in \mathcal{G} \setminus \mathcal{D}
\tag{C6}
$$

### (C7) Track-Sharing Indicator (Exact XOR Linearization)
$\rho_{i,j,g}=1$ iff $i$ and $j$ use different tracks on $g$ (i.e., $z_{i,g} \neq z_{j,g}$):

$$
\rho_{i,j,g} \;\ge\; z_{i,g} - z_{j,g}
\qquad \forall\, i < j,\; g
\tag{C7a}
$$
$$
\rho_{i,j,g} \;\ge\; z_{j,g} - z_{i,g}
\qquad \forall\, i < j,\; g
\tag{C7b}
$$
$$
\rho_{i,j,g} \;\le\; z_{i,g} + z_{j,g}
\qquad \forall\, i < j,\; g
\tag{C7c}
$$
$$
\rho_{i,j,g} \;\le\; 2 - z_{i,g} - z_{j,g}
\qquad \forall\, i < j,\; g
\tag{C7d}
$$

### (C8) Conflict-Free Operation (Headway on Shared Track)

$$
y_{i,j,g} + y_{j,i,g} = 1
\qquad \forall\, i < j,\; g
\tag{C8a}
$$

$$
a_{j,s+1} \;\ge\; \text{dep}_{i,s} + h_g - M\,(1 - y_{i,j,g}) - M\,\rho_{i,j,g}
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j,\; g,\; s = g
\tag{C8b}
$$

$$
a_{i,s+1} \;\ge\; \text{dep}_{j,s} + h_g - M\,(1 - y_{j,i,g}) - M\,\rho_{i,j,g}
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j,\; g,\; s = g
\tag{C8c}
$$

If $\rho_{i,j,g}=0$ (same track), the active inequality enforces separation $a_{j,s+1} \ge \text{dep}_{i,s}+h_g$ or the reverse. If $\rho_{i,j,g}=1$ (opposite tracks), both constraints relax by $M$.

### (C9) Ordering Consistency Across Consecutive Segments
Order can change only at a station, and only if the swap indicator is on. **Corrected direction of the implication** — a swap at station $s=g+1$ permits $\,y_{i,j,g} > y_{i,j,g+1}$ only via $swap_{i,j,s}$:

$$
y_{i,j,g} - y_{i,j,g+1} \;\le\; \text{swap}_{i,j,s}
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j,\; g \in \{1,\dots,G-1\},\; s = g+1
\tag{C9a}
$$
$$
y_{j,i,g} - y_{j,i,g+1} \;\le\; \text{swap}_{i,j,s}
\qquad \forall\, i \neq j,\; g \in \{1,\dots,G-1\},\; s = g+1
\tag{C9b}
$$

with $\text{swap}_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$. Setting $\text{swap}_{i,j,s}=0$ forces $y_{i,j,g} = y_{i,j,g+1}$ (no overtaking). To charge a cost or forbid swaps, fix $\text{swap}=0$ or add a penalty term to the objective.

### (C10) Reroute Continuity at Disruption Boundaries
Rerouting is local: a train may leave the normal track only on disrupted segments and must rejoin it immediately after. Transitions are permitted only at the boundary stations:

$$
z_{i,g} \;\le\; z_{i,g+1} \quad \text{for } g,\,g+1 \in \mathcal{D}
\qquad \forall\, i
\tag{C10a}
$$

$$
z_{i,g} \;\le\; z_{i,g-1} \quad \text{for } g-1,\,g \in \mathcal{D}
\qquad \forall\, i
\tag{C10b}
$$

(no fragmented rerouting inside the disrupted area). For entry into the disrupted area ($g-1 \notin \mathcal{D},\ g \in \mathcal{D}$) and exit ($g \in \mathcal{D},\ g+1 \notin \mathcal{D}$), (C6) already forces $z_{i,g-1}=z_{i,g+1}=0$, so physical continuity is handled implicitly. Optionally enforce that a rerouted traversal spans the window:

$$
a_{i,s} \;\le\; t_D^{\text{start}} + M\,z_{i,g}
\qquad \text{or} \qquad
a_{i,s} \;\ge\; t_D^{\text{end}} - M\,(1 - z_{i,g})
\tag{C10c}
$$

for the entry station $s$ of a disrupted $g$ (use one of the two forms depending on whether rerouting implies early or late transit).

### (C11) Time Horizon Bounds

$$
0 \;\le\; a_{i,s} \;\le\; H, \qquad 0 \;\le\; \text{dep}_{i,s} \;\le\; H
\qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{C11}
$$

---

## 6. Variable Domain Summary

| Variable | Domain |
|----------|--------|
| $x_{i,g,p},\; y_{i,j,g},\; z_{i,g},\; o_{i,g},\; \rho_{i,j,g},\; \text{swap}_{i,j,s},\; \phi_{i,g},\; \psi_{i,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $a_{i,s},\; \text{dep}_{i,s},\; \text{dw}_{i,s},\; \text{delay}_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ |

---

## 7. Linearization Notes

1. **Speed-profile discretization (A2):** nonlinear train dynamics are precomputed into a finite set of Pareto-efficient $(r_{i,g,p}, e_{i,g,p})$ pairs; selecting exactly one via (C1) is an SOS-1 linearization, so energy and running time enter linearly.
2. **Overlap indicator $o_{i,g}$ (C5a–b):** two-sided big-M encoding of the conjunction "traversal end $\ge t_D^{\text{start}}$ **and** traversal start $\le t_D^{\text{end}}$". The implication *overlap $\Rightarrow$ reroute* is the single inequality $o_{i,g} \le z_{i,g}$.
3. **Track-sharing XOR $\rho_{i,j,g}$ (C7a–d):** exact linear XOR of two binaries, avoiding the product $z_i z_j$ inside (C8).
4. **Disjunctive headway (C8b–c):** classic big-M disjunction for two trains on one resource, with $y_{i,j,g}+y_{j,i,g}=1$; $\rho_{i,j,g}=1$ relaxes both directions because opposite tracks are independent.
5. **Delay (C4a–b):** one-sided bounds are exact because the objective is monotone non-decreasing in $\text{delay}_{i,s}$.
6. **Ordering (C9a–b):** implication encoding that allows swaps only at stations via $\text{swap}_{i,j,s}$; the direction has been corrected relative to a naïve formulation so that $y_{i,j,g}$ and $y_{i,j,g+1}$ differ only when the swap flag is active.

---

## 8. Modelling Assumptions

- **A1 (Fixed stops):** every train serves its scheduled station set; no cancellations or skip-stops (could be added as skip binaries at the cost of extra linearization).
- **A2 (Precomputed profiles):** speed profiles are discrete and computed offline.
- **A3 (Single-track occupancy):** on any track resource, at most one train occupies a segment at any instant; enforced by (C8).
- **A4 (Local, unidirectional rerouting):** only within the disruption window and only on disrupted segments; rejoin normal track immediately after (C6, C10).
- **A5 (Bounded dwell):** dwell times lie in $[d_i^{\min}, d_i^{\max}]$ at intermediate stops.
- **A6 (Deterministic disruption):** $[t_D^{\text{start}}, t_D^{\text{end}}]$ and $\mathcal{D}$ are known.
- **A7 (Bounded horizon and big-M):** $M \ge H + \max_{i,g,p} r_{i,g,p}$.
- **A8 (Objective weights):** $w_D, w_E, w_C \ge 0$ are policy weights that trade off delay, energy, and rerouting.

# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

The following assumptions are made (marked where they represent reasonable extrapolations, since the input does not specify them):

- **(A1)** The railway line is discretized into a set of *segments* indexed by \(j \in \mathcal{J}\), each bounded by two stations. (Assumption: segments are the smallest track-resource unit for blockage.)
- **(A2)** Each segment has two directional tracks, \(d \in \mathcal{D} = \{+,-\}\) (up/down). During a partial blockage, one direction on a subset of segments is unavailable in a given time window.
- **(A3)** During the disruption window, an affected train may **reroute** onto the opposite track (bidirectional operation), so the opposite track becomes a shared resource with potential conflicts.
- **(A4)** Speed management is captured by a piecewise-constant **speed-level** discretization \(s \in \mathcal{S}\), each with a known running time and energy consumption per segment.
- **(A5)** Trains cannot overtake within a segment (no in-segment overtaking); ordering is decided at segment-entry.
- **(A6)** Minimum headway (safety separation) applies between consecutive trains on the same track segment.
- **(A7)** Dwell times are bounded below/above by \(d^{\min}, d^{\max}\); departure/arrival times of unaffected trains remain fixed (or within a small tolerance).
- **(A8)** The disruption window \([T^{\text{start}}_j, T^{\text{end}}_j]\) on segment \(j\) blocks one direction only.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| \(\mathcal{T}\) | set of trains, \(i,k \in \mathcal{T}\) |
| \(\mathcal{J}\) | set of segments, \(j \in \mathcal{J}\) |
| \(\mathcal{J}^{+}_i\) | segments traversed by train \(i\) (in its nominal route) |
| \(\mathcal{S}\) | set of discretized speed levels, \(s \in \mathcal{S}\) |
| \(\mathcal{D} = \{+,-\}\) | travel directions |
| \(\mathcal{R}_i\) | set of alternative routes available to train \(i\) (nominal + rerouted variants) |
| \(\mathcal{J}^{\text{dis}}\subseteq\mathcal{J}\) | segments affected by the partial blockage |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling (TRP) Variables

\[
a_{i,j} \ge 0 \quad \text{arrival time of train } i \text{ at (end of) segment } j
\]
\[
d_{i,j} \ge 0 \quad \text{departure time of train } i \text{ from (start of) segment } j
\]
\[
w_{i,j} \ge 0 \quad \text{dwell time of train } i \text{ at station between } j \text{ and } j+1
\]
\[
y_{i,k,j} \in \{0,1\} \quad =1 \text{ if train } i \text{ precedes train } k \text{ on segment } j
\]
\[
z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\} \quad =1 \text{ if train } i \text{ is rerouted on segment } j
\]
\[
u_{i} \in \{0,1\} \quad =1 \text{ if train } i \text{ is cancelled}
\]

### 3.2 Speed Management (TSMP) Variables

\[
x_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad =1 \text{ if train } i \text{ uses speed level } s \text{ on segment } j
\]
\[
\tau_{i,j} \ge 0 \quad \text{running time of train } i \text{ on segment } j
\]
\[
e_{i,j} \ge 0 \quad \text{energy consumed by train } i \text{ on segment } j
\]

### 3.3 Auxiliary Linkage

\[
\Delta_{i,k,j} \ge 0 \quad \text{separation time between trains } i \text{ and } k \text{ on segment } j
\]

---

## 4. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| \(L_j\) | length of segment \(j\) |
| \(v_s\) | speed of level \(s\) |
| \(\tau_{j,s} = L_j / v_s\) | running time on \(j\) at speed \(s\) |
| \(e_{j,s}\) | energy per unit distance at speed \(s\) (traction model) |
| \(h_{\min}\) | minimum headway (safety) |
| \(d^{\min}, d^{\max}\) | min/max dwell time |
| \(T^{\text{start}}_j, T^{\text{end}}_j\) | blockage window on segment \(j\) |
| \(T^{\text{arr}}_i, T^{\text{dep}}_i\) | scheduled arrival/departure of train \(i\) |
| \(M\) | sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| \(c^{\text{delay}}, c^{\text{energy}}, c^{\text{cancel}}, c^{\text{reroute}}\) | cost coefficients |
| \(\alpha, \beta\) | weighting of delay vs. energy |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted combination of total delay, energy consumption, cancellation, and rerouting penalties:

\[
\boxed{
\min \; Z =
\alpha \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} \left( a_{i,J_i} - T^{\text{arr}}_i \right)^+}_{\text{arrival delay}}
+ \beta \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}^+_i} e_{i,j}}_{\text{energy}}
+ c^{\text{cancel}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} u_i
+ c^{\text{reroute}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}^{\text{dis}}} z_{i,j}
}
\]

The delay term is linearized via auxiliary variable \(\delta_i \ge a_{i,J_i}-T^{\text{arr}}_i\), \(\delta_i \ge 0\).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Running-Time / Speed-Level Coupling (TSMP)

Each train picks exactly one speed level per segment:

\[
\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} x_{i,j,s} = 1 \quad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; j\in\mathcal{J}^+_i
\tag{C1}
\]

Running time is the chosen level's time:

\[
\tau_{i,j} = \sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} \tau_{j,s}\, x_{i,j,s}, \quad \forall i,j
\tag{C2}
\]

Energy is the chosen level's energy:

\[
e_{i,j} = \sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} e_{j,s}\, x_{i,j,s}, \quad \forall i,j
\tag{C3}
\]

Speed limits (e.g., through curves/turnouts):

\[
x_{i,j,s} = 0 \quad \text{if } v_s > v^{\max}_j
\tag{C4}
\]

### 6.2 Timetable Consistency

Arrival = departure (of segment) + running time:

\[
a_{i,j} = d_{i,j} + \tau_{i,j} \quad \forall i,j
\tag{C5}
\]

Departure from next segment = arrival + dwell:

\[
d_{i,j+1} = a_{i,j} + w_{i,j} \quad \forall i,j
\tag{C6}
\]

Dwell bounds:

\[
d^{\min}\le w_{i,j} \le d^{\max}
\tag{C7}
\]

Fixing unaffected trains (or bounded deviation):

\[
|d_{i,0}-T^{\text{dep}}_i| \le \varepsilon \quad \forall i \notin \mathcal{T}^{\text{aff}}
\tag{C8}
\]

### 6.3 Disruption / Blockage Constraint

Train \(i\) may not traverse segment \(j\) in the blocked direction during the window unless rerouted:

\[
z_{i,j} = 0 \Rightarrow \big[ a_{i,j} \le T^{\text{start}}_j \;\text{or}\; d_{i,j} \ge T^{\text{end}}_j \big]
\]

Linearized (big-M):

\[
a_{i,j} \le T^{\text{start}}_j + M z_{i,j}, \quad
d_{i,j} \ge T^{\text{end}}_j - M(1-z_{i,j}), \quad \forall i, j\in\mathcal{J}^{\text{dis}}
\tag{C9}
\]

Rerouting only permitted if an opposite track exists:

\[
z_{i,j} \le r_{i,j} \quad \forall i,j
\tag{C10}
\]

### 6.4 Headway / Conflict-Free Constraints (Bidirectional)

On any segment \(j\) — whether nominal or shared after rerouting — the entry order must be consistent:

\[
y_{i,k,j}+y_{k,i,j}=1, \quad \forall i\ne k,\; j\in\mathcal{J}^+_i\cap\mathcal{J}^+_k
\tag{C11}
\]

If \(i\) precedes \(k\):

\[
d_{k,j} \ge a_{i,j} + h_{\min} - M(1-y_{i,k,j})
\tag{C12}
\]

Segment occupancy for trains sharing the same physical track (nominal + rerouted opposite-direction):

\[
a_{k,j} \ge a_{i,j} + h_{\min} - M(1-y_{i,k,j}) - M\,b_{i,k,j}
\tag{C13}
\]

where \(b_{i,k,j}\) is a conflict-auxiliary (1 if two trains never share the same physical track). Simpler form (common in literature) — for every pair sharing a physical track:

\[
y_{i,k,j}+y_{k,i,j} = 1 \quad \forall (i,k)\text{ sharing physical track of } j
\tag{C14}
\]

and (C12) enforces separation.

### 6.5 Rerouted Services Direction Consistency

If \(i\) rerouted on \(j\), its direction reverses relative to nominal design:

\[
z_{i,j}=1 \Rightarrow \text{direction}(i,j) = \text{opposite of nominal}
\tag{C15}
\]

(encoded via route selection variables on a directed-arc graph; in compact form constraint C15 is realized by route-alternative index sets.)

### 6.6 Cancellation Logic

If train \(i\) is cancelled, all its temporal variables are relaxed:

\[
a_{i,j} \le M(1-u_i), \quad d_{i,j}\le M(1-u_i), \quad \forall j
\tag{C16}
\]

### 6.7 Precedence Transitivity (per segment)

\[
y_{i,k,j} + y_{k,l,j} - 1 \le y_{i,l,j}, \quad \forall i,k,l \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{C17}
\]

### 6.8 Variable Domains

\[
a_{i,j}, d_{i,j}, w_{i,j}, \tau_{i,j}, e_{i,j}, \delta_i \ge 0
\]
\[
x_{i,j,s},\; y_{i,k,j},\; z_{i,j},\; u_{i}\in\{0,1\}
\]

---

## 7. Summary of Model

| Component | Content |
|---|---|
| **Objective** | Weighted sum of arrival delay, energy, cancellations, rerouting penalties |
| **TSMP constraints** | (C1)–(C4): speed-level selection ↔ running time ↔ energy |
| **TRP timing** | (C5)–(C8): arrival/departure/dwell linkage and fixing unaffected trains |
| **Disruption** | (C9)–(C10): blockage window and reroute eligibility |
| **Bidirectional conflict** | (C11)–(C14): order + headway on shared track |
| **Rerouting** | (C15): direction reversal encoding |
| **Cancellation** | (C16) |
| **Transitivity** | (C17) |
| **Domain** | continuous + binary |

---

## 8. Key Modeling Contributions (relative to the input)

1. **Integration:** Speed level choice \(x_{i,j,s}\) and running time \(\tau_{i,j}\) are coupled exactly (C2) — bridging TRP and TSMP in a single MILP.
2. **Partial blockage:** Explicit big-M encoding (C9) of the time window, avoiding time-indexing that would explode the model.
3. **Rerouting as binary route choice:** \(z_{i,j}\) captures opposite-track diversion, and (C14) turns the opposite track into a shared bidirectional resource, correctly generating conflict constraints between opposite-direction trains.
4. **Energy–delay trade-off:** The objective explicitly balances delay, energy, cancellation and rerouting, matching the paper's motivating claim that acceleration-early-vs-decelerate-late strategies have different energy profiles.
5. **Decomposability:** The model separates naturally into (i) an **IP over interaction variables** \(\{y_{i,k,j}, z_{i,j}\}\) and (ii) independent **single-train plans** \(\{x_{i,j,s}, a, d, w, \tau, e\}\), matching the claimed decomposition into an IP master and train plan subproblems.

# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a partial segment blockage (e.g., one track of a double-track line unavailable) occurs during a known disruption time window. Trains may be rerouted onto the opposite track within the disruption area, requiring bidirectional coordination. We integrate train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profile selection) into a single MILP.

**Assumptions (marked as such where information is missing):**

- **(A1)** The line is discretized into a set of segments $e \in \mathcal{E}$ between consecutive stations; each segment has a nominal free-run travel time and a length.
- **(A2)** Each segment is divided into a finite set of *speed profile options* $p \in \mathcal{P}_e$, each characterized by a running time $r_{e,p}$ and energy consumption $E_{e,p}$. *(Assumption: discrete speed profiles are precomputed; this is standard in TSMP literature.)*
- **(A3)** The disruption affects a subset of segments $\mathcal{E}^{D} \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ during a time window $[T^{D,start}, T^{D,end}]$. Within this window, only one train may occupy the disrupted segment at a time (single-track operation), regardless of direction.
- **(A4)** Rerouting is permitted only within the disruption area; trains may use the opposite track but must respect bidirectional conflict constraints.
- **(A5)** Dwell times at stations are bounded: $d^{min} \le d_{i,k} \le d^{max}$.
- **(A6)** Train cancellation is allowed with a penalty cost.
- **(A7)** Headway times $h$ between consecutive trains on the same track must be respected.
- **(A8)** All times are discretized to integer minutes (or seconds) for MILP tractability.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{E}^{D}$ | Set of disrupted segments, $\mathcal{E}^{D} \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_e$ | Set of speed profiles on segment $e$, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_i$ | Set of stations visited by train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of routes (tracks), indexed by $r$ (e.g., up/down) |
| $\mathcal{T}^{ord}$ | Set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ that may conflict |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $r_{e,p}$ | Running time of train on segment $e$ using profile $p$ |
| $E_{e,p}$ | Energy consumption on segment $e$ using profile $p$ |
| $d^{min}, d^{max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between trains |
| $T^{D,start}, T^{D,end}$ | Disruption time window |
| $a_{i,s}^{0}$ | Original scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $dep_{i,s}^{0}$ | Original scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $c^{delay}$ | Unit cost of delay |
| $c^{energy}$ | Unit cost of energy |
| $c^{cancel}$ | Penalty cost for cancelling a train |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $\delta$ | Minimum separation time on disrupted segment |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $dep_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x_{i,e,p}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $e$ |
| $y_{i,e,r}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ on segment $e$ |
| $z_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\alpha_{i,j,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$ |
| $\beta_{i,e}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses disrupted segment $e$ during disruption window |
| $u_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Entry time of train $i$ into segment $e$ |
| $v_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Exit time of train $i$ from segment $e$ |

### 4.2 Auxiliary Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\Delta_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $w_{i,e}$ | Continuous | Waiting/holding time before segment $e$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total cost comprising delay cost, energy cost, and cancellation penalty:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{c^{delay} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{K}_i} \Delta_{i,s}}_{\text{delay cost}} 
+ \underbrace{c^{energy} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_e} E_{e,p} \, x_{i,e,p}}_{\text{energy cost}} 
+ \underbrace{c^{cancel} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Delay Definition

$$
\Delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{0}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{1}
$$

$$
\Delta_{i,s} \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{2}
$$

### 6.2 Speed Profile Selection

Each train selects exactly one speed profile per segment (if not cancelled):

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_e} x_{i,e,p} = 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E} \tag{3}
$$

### 6.3 Route Selection

Each train selects exactly one route per segment (if not cancelled):

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} y_{i,e,r} = 1 - z_i, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E} \tag{4}
$$

### 6.4 Running Time Consistency

The running time on segment $e$ depends on the selected speed profile:

$$
v_{i,e} - u_{i,e} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_e} r_{e,p} \, x_{i,e,p}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E} \tag{5}
$$

### 6.5 Timetable Coupling (Arrival–Departure–Segment)

For each train $i$ and consecutive stations $s_k, s_{k+1}$ connected by segment $e$:

$$
u_{i,e} = dep_{i,s_k}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e = (s_k, s_{k+1}) \tag{6}
$$

$$
a_{i,s_{k+1}} = v_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e = (s_k, s_{k+1}) \tag{7}
$$

### 6.6 Dwell Time Constraints

$$
d^{min} \le dep_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le d^{max}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{8}
$$

### 6.7 Headway Constraints (Same Direction, Same Track)

For trains $i, j$ on the same segment $e$ and same route $r$:

$$
u_{j,e} \ge v_{i,e} + h - M(1 - \alpha_{i,j,e}) - M(2 - y_{i,e,r} - y_{j,e,r}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; e, \; r \tag{9}
$$

$$
u_{i,e} \ge v_{j,e} + h - M \alpha_{i,j,e} - M(2 - y_{i,e,r} - y_{j,e,r}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; e, \; r \tag{10}
$$

### 6.8 Bidirectional Conflict Constraints (Disrupted Segments)

On disrupted segments $\mathcal{E}^D$, only one train may occupy the segment at a time (regardless of direction):

$$
u_{j,e} \ge v_{i,e} + \delta - M(1 - \alpha_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i \neq j, \; e \in \mathcal{E}^D \tag{11}
$$

$$
u_{i,e} \ge v_{j,e} + \delta - M \alpha_{i,j,e}, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; e \in \mathcal{E}^D \tag{12}
$$

### 6.9 Disruption Window Occupancy Indicator

Train $i$ traverses disrupted segment $e$ during the disruption window:

$$
u_{i,e} \le T^{D,end} + M(1 - \beta_{i,e}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}^D \tag{13}
$$

$$
v_{i,e} \ge T^{D,start} - M(1 - \beta_{i,e}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}^D \tag{14}
$$

### 6.10 Rerouting Constraints

If train $i$ traverses disrupted segment $e$ during the disruption window, it must use the opposite track (rerouting):

$$
y_{i,e,r^{opp}} \ge \beta_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; e \in \mathcal{E}^D \tag{15}
$$

### 6.11 Cancellation Constraints

If train $i$ is cancelled, all timing variables are fixed to zero:

$$
a_{i,s} \le M(1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{16}
$$

$$
dep_{i,s} \le M(1 - z_i), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{17}
$$

### 6.12 Ordering Variable Consistency

$$
\alpha_{i,j,e} + \alpha_{j,i,e} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j, \; e \in \mathcal{E} \tag{18}
$$

### 6.13 Non-negativity and Binary Constraints

$$
a_{i,s}, \; dep_{i,s}, \; u_{i,e}, \; v_{i,e}, \; \Delta_{i,s}, \; w_{i,e} \ge 0 \tag{19}
$$

$$
x_{i,e,p}, \; y_{i,e,r}, \; z_i, \; \alpha_{i,j,e}, \; \beta_{i,e} \in \{0,1\} \tag{20}
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = c^{delay} \sum_{i,s} \Delta_{i,s} + c^{energy} \sum_{i,e,p} E_{e,p} x_{i,e,p} + c^{cancel} \sum_{i} z_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & (1)–(20)
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 8. Key Modeling Features

| Feature | Constraint(s) |
|---------|---------------|
| Delay minimization | (1)–(2) |
| Speed profile selection | (3), (5) |
| Route selection (rerouting) | (4), (15) |
| Timetable–speed coupling | (6)–(7) |
| Dwell time bounds | (8) |
| Same-direction headway | (9)–(10) |
| Bidirectional conflict on disrupted segments | (11)–(12) |
| Disruption window detection | (13)–(14) |
| Cancellation handling | (16)–(17) |
| Train ordering | (18) |

---

## 9. Assumptions and Remarks

- **(R1)** The model assumes discrete speed profiles are precomputed via a separate TSMP subproblem; continuous speed control is approximated by profile selection.
- **(R2)** The big-M formulation for disjunctive constraints is standard but may be tightened using time bounds.
- **(R3)** The model is a MILP and can be solved directly for small instances; for large-scale instances, decomposition (as described in the paper) is recommended.
- **(R4)** The bidirectional conflict constraints (11)–(12) ensure that on disrupted segments, only one train occupies the segment at a time, effectively modeling single-track operation.
- **(R5)** The rerouting constraint (15) forces trains traversing during the disruption window to use the opposite track, consistent with the partial blockage scenario.

This formulation provides a complete, self-contained MILP for the integrated TRSMP under partial segment blockages, capturing retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed profile selection in a unified framework.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage with Local Rerouting

*Note: The model was drafted by the `or_operator`. After review, the original formulation contained a critical flaw — the "speed-profile template" approach used in Section 5.3 replaces the actual speed-management decision by an offline pre-computation, which defeats the integration of TRP and TSMP that is the core scientific contribution of the paper. Feedback was provided to reintroduce an endogenous, linearly-representable speed profile. The final model below reflects the corrected version.*

---

## 0. Assumptions (explicitly stated)

1. **Time discretization**: Planning horizon $\mathcal{T}=\{0,\dots,T_{max}\}$, unit step $\Delta t$.
2. **Space discretization**: Each segment $s$ is divided into $K$ position samples of length $\Delta x_s = L_s/K$.
3. **Piecewise-constant acceleration** on each sample; speed linear within a sample.
4. **Linearized Davis resistance** $R(v)=a_0 + a_1 v$ (quadratic term dropped; standard MILP-safe simplification).
5. **Fixed train mass** $m_i$; fixed direction $d_i\in\{+1,-1\}$.
6. **No overtaking within a segment**: ordering is a binary per segment.
7. **Rerouting** allowed only onto the opposite track, only on blocked segments, only during the disruption window.
8. **Cancellation** removes a train via $z_i$ and big-$M$.
9. **Energy**: tractive/regenerative split linearized via binary sign selectors (no $\max$ terms remain nonlinear).
10. **Speed profile is endogenous** (variable $v_{i,s,k}$), coupled to the timetable through a *linear average-speed* identity — this is the corrected replacement for the template approach.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Trains, index $i$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Ordered segments (block sections), index $s$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Stations between segments, index $p$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Position samples in a segment, $k=0,\dots,K$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{block}$ | Segments blocked on the normal track |
| $d_i\in\{+1,-1\}$ | Train direction |

---

## 2. Parameters

**Timetable**: $A^{sched}_{i,p}$, $D^{sched}_{i,p}$, weights $w^{arr},w^{dep},w^{E},w^{C}$.

**Running/Dwell**: $run^{min}_{i,s}, run^{max}_{i,s}, dw^{min}_{i,p}, dw^{max}_{i,p}$.

**Headway**: $h^{dep}, h^{arr}, h^{block}$.

**Disruption**: $T_{start}, T_{end}$, $B_s\in\{0,1\}$ (blocked on normal track).

**Physical**: $L_s,\ \Delta x_s=L_s/K$, $v^{max}_{i,s}$, $v^{min}$, $a^{max}$, $a^{min}<0$, $m_i$, $F^{max}_i$, $F^{brake}_i$, $a_0,a_1,\eta^{trac},\eta^{regen}$.

**Big-M**: $M^{time}=T_{max}$, $M^{E}$ large.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,p}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | arrival time |
| $d_{i,p}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | departure time |
| $t^{in}_{i,s}, t^{out}_{i,s}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | segment entry / exit times |
| $\delta^{A}_{i,p},\delta^{D}_{i,p}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | positive delays |
| $r_{i,s}$ | bin. | 1 if rerouted to opposite track on $s$ |
| $y_{i,j,s}$ | bin. | 1 if $i$ traverses $s$ before $j$ |
| $\sigma_{i,s}$ | bin. | 1 if $i$ occupies blocked normal track in window |
| $z_i$ | bin. | 1 if train cancelled |
| $v_{i,s,k}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | speed at position sample $k$ |
| $\bar v_{i,s}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | average speed on segment $s$ |
| $E_{i,s}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | energy on segment $s$ |
| $o^{diff}_{i,j,s}$ | bin. | 1 if $i,j$ use different tracks on $s$ |
| $P^{+}_{i,s},P^{-}_{i,s}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | traction/braking force magnitude |
| $\zeta_{i,s}$ | bin. | 1 if net tractive force is positive |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i}\sum_{p}\big(w^{arr}\delta^{A}_{i,p}+w^{dep}\delta^{D}_{i,p}\big)}_{\text{delay}} + \underbrace{w^{E}\sum_{i,s}E_{i,s}}_{\text{energy}} + \underbrace{w^{C}\sum_i z_i}_{\text{cancellation}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Cancellation (deactivation linking)

$$
a_{i,p}\le M^{time}(1-z_i),\quad d_{i,p}\le M^{time}(1-z_i),\quad \delta^{A}_{i,p}\le M^{time}(1-z_i),\quad \delta^{D}_{i,p}\le M^{time}(1-z_i)
$$
$$
r_{i,s}\le 1-z_i,\quad v_{i,s,k}\le v^{max}_{i,s}(1-z_i),\quad E_{i,s}\le M^{E}(1-z_i)
$$

### 5.2 Timetable Consistency

$$
\delta^{A}_{i,p}\ge a_{i,p}-A^{sched}_{i,p},\qquad \delta^{D}_{i,p}\ge d_{i,p}-D^{sched}_{i,p}
$$
$$
dw^{min}_{i,p}-M^{time}z_i \;\le\; d_{i,p}-a_{i,p}\;\le\; dw^{max}_{i,p}+M^{time}z_i
$$
$$
run^{min}_{i,s}-M^{time}z_i \;\le\; t^{out}_{i,s}-t^{in}_{i,s}\;\le\; run^{max}_{i,s}+M^{time}z_i
$$
with $t^{in}_{i,s}=d_{i,p},\ t^{out}_{i,s}=a_{i,p+1}$ (indexing per direction).

### 5.3 Endogenous Speed–Timing Coupling (corrected, fully linear via average speed)

Define average speed $\bar v_{i,s}$ and require it satisfies the segment length–time relation exactly:

$$
L_s = \tfrac{1}{2}\big(v_{i,s,0}+v_{i,s,K}\big)\,(t^{out}_{i,s}-t^{in}_{i,s}) \quad \text{is bilinear} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{linearize as:}
$$

$$
\bar v_{i,s}\;\ge\;\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\frac{v_{i,s,k}+v_{i,s,k+1}}{2}-\epsilon_s, \qquad
\bar v_{i,s}\;\le\;\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\frac{v_{i,s,k}+v_{i,s,k+1}}{2}+\epsilon_s
$$
$$
\bar v_{i,s}\,(t^{out}_{i,s}-t^{in}_{i,s}) = L_s \;\Longrightarrow\; \text{replaced by the linear outer-approximation:}
$$
$$
L_s \;\ge\; \bar v_{i,s}\,\tau^{lo}_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}\,\bar v^{lo}_{i,s} - \bar v^{lo}_{i,s}\tau^{lo}_{i,s}, \quad L_s \;\le\; \bar v_{i,s}\,\tau^{hi}_{i,s} + \tau_{i,s}\,\bar v^{hi}_{i,s} - \bar v^{hi}_{i,s}\tau^{hi}_{i,s}
$$
where $\tau_{i,s}=t^{out}_{i,s}-t^{in}_{i,s}$, and the bounds $(\bar v^{lo},\bar v^{hi}),(\tau^{lo},\tau^{hi})$ are derived from $v^{min},v^{max}$ and $run^{min},run^{max}$. These are the **McCormick envelopes** of the bilinear term $\bar v_{i,s}\cdot\tau_{i,s}$, keeping the model exactly linear.

**Speed and acceleration limits** (piecewise-constant acceleration):
$$
0 \le v_{i,s,k} \le v^{max}_{i,s}\quad\forall k
$$
$$
a^{min}\,\Delta \bar\tau_{i,s}\;\le\; v_{i,s,k+1}-v_{i,s,k}\;\le\; a^{max}\,\Delta \bar\tau_{i,s}\quad\forall k
$$
where $\Delta \bar\tau_{i,s}=\tau_{i,s}/K$ is a continuous variable; the products $a^{max}\Delta\bar\tau$ are handled by the same McCormick envelope logic.

### 5.4 Rerouting Restrictions

$$
r_{i,s}\le B_s \quad\forall i,\ s\in\mathcal{S}^{block}
$$
$$
t^{out}_{i,s}\le T_{start}+M^{time}(1-\sigma_{i,s})+M^{time}z_i
$$
$$
t^{in}_{i,s}\ge T_{end}-M^{time}\sigma_{i,s}-M^{time}z_i
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,s}\le 1-r_{i,s}
$$
Interpretation: a train on the normal track ($r=0$) must clear a blocked segment before $T_{start}$ or enter after $T_{end}$; otherwise it must reroute.

### 5.5 Bidirectional Conflict-Free Ordering and Headway

**Track-difference linearization** (two tracks per train only):
$$
r_{i,s}-r_{j,s}\le o^{diff}_{i,j,s},\quad r_{j,s}-r_{i,s}\le o^{diff}_{i,j,s},\quad r_{i,s}+r_{j,s}\le 2-o^{diff}_{i,j,s}
$$
same-track indicator $=1-o^{diff}_{i,j,s}$.

**Ordering anti-symmetry**:
$$
y_{i,j,s}+y_{j,i,s}\ge 1-z_i-z_j,\qquad y_{i,j,s}+y_{j,i,s}\le 1
$$

**Headway (big-M)**:
$$
t^{in}_{j,s}\ge t^{out}_{i,s}+h^{block}-M^{time}(1-y_{i,j,s})-M^{time}o^{diff}_{i,j,s}-M^{time}z_i-M^{time}z_j
$$
$$
t^{in}_{i,s}\ge t^{out}_{j,s}+h^{block}-M^{time}y_{i,j,s}-M^{time}o^{diff}_{i,j,s}-M^{time}z_i-M^{time}z_j
$$

**Station departure headway**:
$$
d_{j,p}\ge d_{i,p}+h^{dep}-M^{time}\xi_{i,j,p}-M^{time}z_i-M^{time}z_j,\quad \xi_{i,j,p}+\xi_{j,i,p}=1
$$

### 5.6 Disruption Window Exclusion

Covered by the $\sigma$ constraints of 5.4: no normal-track occupancy of a blocked segment inside $[T_{start},T_{end}]$.

### 5.7 Endogenous Energy Computation (fully linear)

Tractive/braking force over segment (linearized Davis, average acceleration):
$$
F_{i,s}=m_i\frac{v_{i,s,K}-v_{i,s,0}}{\tau_{i,s}}+m_i a_0 + a_1\,\bar v_{i,s}
$$
(sign of the first term handled below). Split with binary $\zeta_{i,s}$:
$$
F_{i,s}=P^{+}_{i,s}-P^{-}_{i,s},\quad 0\le P^{+}_{i,s}\le F^{max}_i\,\zeta_{i,s},\quad 0\le P^{-}_{i,s}\le F^{brake}_i\,(1-\zeta_{i,s})
$$
Energy (traction minus regeneration):
$$
E_{i,s}=\eta^{trac}P^{+}_{i,s}L_s-\eta^{regen}P^{-}_{i,s}L_s
$$
All terms affine in continuous variables and binaries — **linear**.

---

## 6. Complete Model

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& Z=\sum_{i,p}\big(w^{arr}\delta^{A}_{i,p}+w^{dep}\delta^{D}_{i,p}\big)+w^{E}\sum_{i,s}E_{i,s}+w^{C}\sum_i z_i\\
\text{s.t.}\;& (5.1)\text{ cancellation},\ (5.2)\text{ timetable},\ (5.3)\text{ speed-timing (McCormick)},\\
& (5.4)\text{ rerouting},\ (5.5)\text{ conflict-free ordering},\ (5.6)\text{ exclusion},\ (5.7)\text{ energy}\\
& a,d,t^{in},t^{out},\delta^{A},\delta^{D},v,\bar v,E,P^{+},P^{-}\ge 0;\quad r,y,\sigma,z,o^{diff},\zeta,\xi\in\{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 7. Notes on the Review / Corrections Applied

- **Flaw found in first draft**: the "speed-profile template" selection in §5.3 collapses the endogenous speed-management problem into offline selection, destroying the TRSMP integration that is the paper's core contribution.
- **Correction**: reintroduced endogenous speed variables $v_{i,s,k}$ and coupled them to timings via a **McCormick linearization** of the average-speed–traversal-time product $\bar v_{i,s}\cdot\tau_{i,s}=L_s$ and of the acceleration–time product. This keeps the model **strictly MILP** while preserving full co-optimization.
- **Energy** is now computed endogenously (§5.7) with binary sign selectors, again fully linear.
- The bidirectional conflict logic ($y$, $o^{diff}$, big-$M$ headway) is retained unchanged and is correct.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

## Model Overview

Based on the paper's description, I present a complete MILP formulation for the rtRTMP with a multi-stage decomposition approach. The model addresses rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling of trains in real-time while minimizing overall delays.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $B$ | Set of block sections (track segments), indexed by $b$ |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$ |
| $R_i^b$ | Set of routes for train $i$ that include block section $b$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations/platforms, indexed by $s$ |
| $B_s$ | Set of block sections adjacent to station $s$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ that may conflict |
| $\mathcal{C}_b$ | Set of conflicting train pairs on block section $b$ |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Units |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| $t_i^{dep}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from origin | seconds |
| $t_i^{arr}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at destination | seconds |
| $\tau_{i,b}$ | Running time of train $i$ on block section $b$ | seconds |
| $\tau_{i,s}^{dwell}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ | seconds |
| $h_b$ | Minimum headway (safety separation time) on block $b$ | seconds |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) | seconds |
| $w_i^{delay}$ | Weight/priority factor for delay of train $i$ | dimensionless |
| $\alpha$ | Weight for total delay objective | dimensionless |
| $\beta$ | Weight for maximum delay objective | dimensionless |
| $e_i$ | Entry time of train $i$ into the network | seconds |
| $l_i$ | Exit time of train $i$ from the network | seconds |

---

## Decision Variables

### Routing Variables
$$x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in T, r \in R_i$$

$= 1$ if train $i$ is assigned to route $r$, $0$ otherwise.

### Scheduling Variables (Continuous)
$$d_{i,b}^{arr} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T, b \in B$$

Arrival time of train $i$ at the end of block section $b$.

$$d_{i,b}^{dep} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T, b \in B$$

Departure time of train $i$ from block section $b$.

$$d_{i,s}^{dwell} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T, s \in S$$

Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$.

### Delay Variables
$$\delta_i \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in T$$

Total delay of train $i$ (difference from scheduled arrival).

$$\delta^{max} \geq 0$$

Maximum delay among all trains.

### Ordering Variables (Binary)
$$y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b, b \in B$$

$= 1$ if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block section $b$, $0$ otherwise.

### Pair-wise Waiting Variables (for sub-optimal model)
$$z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{P}$$

$= 1$ if train $i$ waits for train $j$ (indicating the source of delay).

---

## Objective Function

### Primary Objective: Minimize Total Weighted Delay

$$\min \quad Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in T} w_i^{delay} \cdot \delta_i + \beta \cdot \delta^{max}$$

**Assumption:** The paper focuses on minimizing train delays. We include both total delay and maximum delay components with weights $\alpha$ and $\beta$ to allow trade-off between efficiency and fairness.

---

## Constraints

### 1. Route Selection Constraints

Each train must be assigned exactly one route:

$$\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T \quad (1)$$

### 2. Route-Block Consistency

Train $i$ uses block $b$ if and only if its selected route includes $b$:

$$\sum_{r \in R_i^b} x_{i,r} = u_{i,b} \quad \forall i \in T, b \in B \quad (2)$$

where $u_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ is an auxiliary variable indicating whether train $i$ traverses block $b$.

**Assumption:** $u_{i,b}$ is implicitly defined; in implementation, it can be substituted directly.

### 3. Travel Time Constraints

For consecutive blocks $b_1, b_2$ in route $r$ of train $i$:

$$d_{i,b_2}^{arr} \geq d_{i,b_1}^{dep} + \tau_{i,b_2} - M(1 - x_{i,r}) \quad \forall i \in T, r \in R_i, (b_1, b_2) \in \text{seq}(r) \quad (3)$$

**Explanation:** If train $i$ uses route $r$, arrival at next block is at least departure from previous block plus running time.

### 4. Dwell Time Constraints

At each station $s$ on the route:

$$d_{i,b}^{dep} \geq d_{i,b'}^{arr} + \tau_{i,s}^{dwell} - M(1 - x_{i,r}) \quad \forall i \in T, r \in R_i, s \in r, b, b' \in B_s \quad (4)$$

**Explanation:** Departure from station must respect minimum dwell time after arrival.

### 5. Headway/Safety Constraints (Ordering)

For conflicting train pairs $(i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b$ on block $b$:

$$d_{j,b}^{arr} \geq d_{i,b}^{dep} + h_b - M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) \quad (5)$$

$$d_{i,b}^{arr} \geq d_{j,b}^{dep} + h_b - M \cdot y_{i,j,b} \quad (6)$$

**Explanation:** Either train $i$ precedes $j$ (constraint 5 active) or $j$ precedes $i$ (constraint 6 active), ensuring minimum headway.

### 6. Ordering Variable Consistency

$$y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1 \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b, b \in B \quad (7)$$

**Explanation:** Exactly one train precedes the other on each block.

### 7. Delay Computation

$$\delta_i \geq d_{i,b_{dest}}^{arr} - t_i^{arr} \quad \forall i \in T \quad (8)$$

**Explanation:** Delay is the difference between actual and scheduled arrival at destination.

### 8. Maximum Delay Definition

$$\delta^{max} \geq \delta_i \quad \forall i \in T \quad (9)$$

### 9. Entry Time Constraints

$$d_{i,b_{orig}}^{dep} \geq e_i \quad \forall i \in T \quad (10)$$

**Explanation:** Trains cannot depart before their entry time into the network.

### 10. Pair-wise Waiting Constraints (Sub-optimal Model Extension)

For the sub-optimal model that disregards delay propagation:

$$z_{i,j} \leq \sum_{b \in B} y_{j,i,b} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{P} \quad (11)$$

$$\sum_{j: (i,j) \in \mathcal{P}} z_{i,j} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in T \quad (12)$$

**Explanation:** $z_{i,j} = 1$ indicates train $i$ waits for train $j$. Constraint (12) limits each train to wait for at most one other train (simplified model assumption).

### 11. Delay Propagation Constraints (Global Optimum Model Extension)

For the extended model considering delay propagation:

$$d_{i,b}^{dep} \geq d_{j,b}^{arr} + h_b - M(1 - y_{j,i,b}) - M(1 - u_{i,b}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b, b \in B \quad (13)$$

**Explanation:** If train $j$ precedes train $i$ on block $b$, then train $i$'s departure is constrained by train $j$'s arrival plus headway, propagating delays.

### 12. Route Compatibility Constraints

If routes $r_i$ and $r_j$ are incompatible (e.g., conflicting movements at junctions):

$$x_{i,r_i} + x_{j,r_j} \leq 1 \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{P}_{incompat}, (r_i, r_j) \in \mathcal{R}_{incompat} \quad (14)$$

### 13. Variable Domains

$$x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in T, r \in R_i \quad (15)$$

$$y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b, b \in B \quad (16)$$

$$z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{P} \quad (17)$$

$$d_{i,b}^{arr}, d_{i,b}^{dep}, d_{i,s}^{dwell}, \delta_i, \delta^{max} \geq 0 \quad (18)$$

---

## Model Assumptions

1. **Linear running times:** Running times $\tau_{i,b}$ are constant and do not depend on speed profiles or traffic conditions.

2. **Fixed minimum dwell times:** Dwell times are bounded below by $\tau_{i,s}^{dwell}$; no upper bound is imposed (trains can wait).

3. **Deterministic disturbances:** Primary delays are known at optimization time; no stochastic effects are modeled.

4. **Block section exclusivity:** At most one train can occupy a block section at a time (enforced via headway constraints).

5. **Route pre-enumeration:** All feasible routes $R_i$ for each train are pre-computed and finite.

6. **No overtaking within blocks:** Trains maintain their order throughout a block section.

7. **Instantaneous speed changes:** Acceleration/deceleration times are included in running times $\tau_{i,b}$.

8. **Single objective aggregation:** The multi-objective nature (total delay vs. max delay) is handled via weighted sum with parameters $\alpha, \beta$.

9. **Sub-optimal model assumption:** The pair-wise waiting formulation (constraints 11-12) disregards delay propagation, meaning delays do not cascade through subsequent conflicts.

10. **Global optimum model:** Constraints (13) capture delay propagation, ensuring the model finds the true global optimum for the original rtRTMP.

---

## Model Decomposition Strategy

The paper proposes a multi-stage framework:

### Stage 1: Rerouting and Reordering (Sub-optimal MILP)
- **Variables:** $x_{i,r}$, $y_{i,j,b}$, $z_{i,j}$
- **Objective:** Minimize pair-wise delays (simplified)
- **Output:** Fixed route selection $\bar{x}_{i,r}$ and optional ordering $\bar{y}_{i,j,b}$

### Stage 2: Rescheduling (Optimal MILP)
- **Fixed:** Routes from Stage 1 ($x_{i,r} = \bar{x}_{i,r}$)
- **Variables:** $d_{i,b}^{arr}$, $d_{i,b}^{dep}$, $\delta_i$
- **Objective:** Minimize total delays with delay propagation
- **Output:** Final schedule

### Global Optimum Model
- Combines both stages with delay propagation constraints (13)
- Guarantees global optimum for the original rtRTMP

---

## Computational Complexity

The model is NP-hard due to:
- Binary routing variables $x_{i,r}$ (combinatorial route selection)
- Binary ordering variables $y_{i,j,b}$ (train sequencing)
- Coupling constraints between routing and scheduling

**Complexity Reduction Strategies (from paper):**
1. Pre-filter routes via TRSP heuristic
2. Decompose into sub-problems
3. Add valid inequalities to reduce equivalent solutions
4. Use runtime-efficient implementation techniques

---

## Summary

This MILP formulation captures the essential elements of the rtRTMP as described in the paper:
- **Rerouting:** Route selection variables $x_{i,r}$
- **Reordering:** Ordering variables $y_{i,j,b}$
- **Rescheduling:** Continuous timing variables $d_{i,b}^{arr}$, $d_{i,b}^{dep}$
- **Objective:** Minimize weighted total and maximum delays
- **Constraints:** Safety headways, dwell times, travel times, route consistency

The model supports both the sub-optimal (fast) and global optimum (accurate) solution approaches described in the paper, with the key difference being the treatment of delay propagation through constraints (11-12) vs. (13).

Text:
# A MILP Model for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

*Model inspired by the RECIFE-MILP framework (Pellegrini et al., 2015), enhanced for ETCS L2 with Trackside Train Detection (TTD). All assumptions made to fill information gaps are explicitly marked **[A#]**.*

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of block sections (TDSs) along the line, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{sw} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of sections containing switches **[A1: distinction switch / non-switch track, per paper]** |
| $\mathcal{S}^{st} = \mathcal{S} \setminus \mathcal{S}^{sw}$ | Plain-line sections |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of routes (paths) through the network, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_i \subseteq \mathcal{R}$ | Routes available to train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{S}_r \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Ordered sequence of sections in route $r$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of speed-profile options, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discretised time instants (time horizon), indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{K}^{dep}_i$ | Set of departure time instants of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{K}^{arr}_i$ | Set of arrival time instants of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of pairs of trains $(i,j)$ sharing at least one section (potential conflicts) |

---

## 2. Parameters

**Timetable and rolling stock**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $d_i^{req}$ | Requested (scheduled) departure time of train $i$ from its origin |
| $a_i^{req}$ | Requested (scheduled) arrival time of train $i$ at its destination |
| $L_i$ | Length of train $i$ |
| $v_i^{max}$ | Maximum speed of train $i$ |
| $w_i$ | Priority weight of train $i$ (delay cost coefficient) |

**Infrastructure**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\ell_s$ | Length of section $s$ |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |

**Signalling / braking (DTG-specific)**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\tau_i^{setup}$ | Route setting / interlocking time for train $i$ |
| $\tau_i^{react}$ | Driver + train reaction time of train $i$ |
| $b_i(v)$ | Absolute braking distance of train $i$ at speed $v$ **[A2: computed from braking curves; here linearised via profile options $p$]** |
| $b_{i,p}$ | Braking distance of train $i$ under speed-profile option $p$ |
| $\sigma$ | Safety margin behind the rear of the preceding train **[A3]** |
| $h_i^{min}$ | Minimum technical headway of train $i$ |

**Speed-profile options (enhancement 1)**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $v_{i,p,s}$ | Average speed of train $i$ on section $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $T_{i,p,s}$ | Running time of train $i$ on section $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $F_{i,p}$ | Extra delay (penalty) of train $i$ associated with profile $p$ (e.g., energy / comfort) **[A4]** |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Routing and sequencing**

$$x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\ r \in \mathcal{R}_i \quad\text{(train $i$ uses route $r$)}$$

$$y_{i,p} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\ p \in \mathcal{P} \quad\text{(train $i$ uses speed-profile option $p$)}$$

$$\delta_{ij} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{E} \quad\text{(ordering: } \delta_{ij}=1 \Rightarrow i \text{ precedes } j)$$

**Timing**

$$t_{i,s}^{in} \ge 0 \quad\text{entry time of train } i \text{ into section } s$$
$$t_{i,s}^{out} \ge 0 \quad\text{exit time of train } i \text{ from section } s$$
$$d_i \ge 0 \quad\text{actual departure time of train } i$$
$$a_i \ge 0 \quad\text{actual arrival time of train } i$$

**Delay**

$$\Delta_i^{dep} \ge 0,\qquad \Delta_i^{arr} \ge 0 \quad\text{(departure / arrival delay of train } i)$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total weighted delay plus profile penalty:

$$
\min Z = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} w_i \left( \Delta_i^{dep} + \Delta_i^{arr} \right) \;+\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} F_{i,p}\, y_{i,p}
$$

*(RECIFE-MILP uses total delay; the profile term is the DTG enhancement so that slower, less energy-consuming profiles are only chosen when they do not increase delay.)*

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Route and profile selection

Each train selects exactly one route and one speed profile:

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} x_{i,r} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{1}
$$

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} y_{i,p} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{2}
$$

### 5.2 Departure / arrival and delay definition

$$
d_i \ge d_i^{req}, \qquad a_i \ge a_i^{req} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{3}
$$

$$
\Delta_i^{dep} \ge d_i - d_i^{req}, \qquad \Delta_i^{arr} \ge a_i - a_i^{req} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{4}
$$

### 5.3 Running times along the route (speed-profile enhancement)

For each train, section, and profile, the running time is fixed by the profile:

$$
t_{i,s}^{out} - t_{i,s}^{in} \;\ge\; \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} T_{i,p,s}\, y_{i,p} \;-\; M\bigl(1 - x_{i,r}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,\ s \in \mathcal{S}_r,\ r \in \mathcal{R}_i \tag{5a}
$$

$$
t_{i,s}^{out} - t_{i,s}^{in} \;\le\; \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} T_{i,p,s}\, y_{i,p} \;+\; M\bigl(1 - x_{i,r}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,\ s \in \mathcal{S}_r,\ r \in \mathcal{R}_i \tag{5b}
$$

Continuity of movement between consecutive sections of the chosen route:

$$
t_{i,s'}^{in} \;\ge\; t_{i,s}^{out} \qquad \forall i,\ (s,s') \text{ consecutive in } \mathcal{S}_r \tag{6}
$$

### 5.4 Timetable coupling

$$
d_i = t_{i,s_0}^{in}, \qquad a_i = t_{i,s_N}^{out} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{7}
$$

where $s_0, s_N$ are the first and last sections of the chosen route.

### 5.5 Route-setting / interlocking time at switches

At switch sections, a route setup time is required before the train may enter **[A1, A5]**:

$$
t_{i,s}^{in} \;\ge\; t_{i,s^-}^{out} + \tau_i^{setup} - M\bigl(1 - x_{i,r}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,\ s \in \mathcal{S}^{sw} \cap \mathcal{S}_r \tag{8}
$$

### 5.6 DTG train separation (core enhancement 2)

Two consecutive trains $i$ (leading) and $j$ (following) on the same section must respect the **speed-dependent absolute braking distance** rather than a fixed number of blocks. The rear of train $i$ must clear the section by at least the braking distance of train $j$ at its current speed plus reaction distance and safety margin:

$$
t_{j,s}^{in} \;\ge\; t_{i,s}^{out} + \tau_j^{react} + \frac{b_{j,p} + \sigma + L_i}{v_{j,p,s}} - M\bigl(1 - \delta_{ij}\bigr) - M\bigl(1 - y_{j,p}\bigr) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{E},\ s \in \mathcal{S},\ p \in \mathcal{P} \tag{9}
$$

and symmetrically for the reverse order:

$$
t_{i,s}^{in} \;\ge\; t_{j,s}^{out} + \tau_i^{react} + \frac{b_{i,p} + \sigma + L_j}{v_{i,p,s}} - M\,\delta_{ij} - M\bigl(1 - y_{i,p}\bigr) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{E},\ s \in \mathcal{S},\ p \in \mathcal{P} \tag{10}
$$

**Interpretation.** The headway term $(b_{j,p}+\sigma+L_i)/v_{j,p,s}$ is exactly the *speed-dependent* separation distance of DTG signalling: the faster train $j$ runs, the longer its braking distance, hence the larger the required headway. This replaces the fixed-block constraint of RECIFE-MILP, where separation is a fixed number of blocks.

### 5.7 Minimum technical headway

$$
t_{j,s}^{in} \;\ge\; t_{i,s}^{in} + h_j^{min} - M\bigl(1 - \delta_{ij}\bigr) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{E},\ s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{11}
$$

### 5.8 End-of-authority at section boundary (DTG principle)

The MA is always released at a TDS boundary, i.e., a train may only enter section $s$ when the preceding train has fully left it:

$$
t_{j,s}^{in} \;\ge\; t_{i,s}^{out} - M\bigl(1 - \delta_{ij}\bigr) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{E},\ s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{12}
$$

*(Constraint (12) is implied by (9) but retained for clarity; it enforces the "end of authority at TDS boundary" property of ETCS L2 with TTD.)*

### 5.9 Speed-dependent brake indication point

For each train, the brake indication point must lie inside the section preceding the occupied one. This is guaranteed structurally by (9)–(10): the term $b_{j,p}/v_{j,p,s}$ shifts the entry time of $j$ so that its braking curve ends before the rear of $i$. No additional constraint is needed; the enhancement is embedded in the headway term. **[A6]**

### 5.10 Variable domains

$$
x_{i,r},\ y_{i,p},\ \delta_{ij} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
t_{i,s}^{in},\ t_{i,s}^{out},\ d_i,\ a_i,\ \Delta_i^{dep},\ \Delta_i^{arr} \ge 0
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions Made

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| **A1** | The paper distinguishes switches from plain track; we model this via $\mathcal{S}^{sw}$ and a route-setup time $\tau_i^{setup}$ at switch sections. |
| **A2** | Braking distance $b_i(v)$ is nonlinear; we linearise it by discretising the speed profile into a finite set $\mathcal{P}$ of options, each with a constant $b_{i,p}$ and $v_{i,p,s}$. This is the "speed profile options" enhancement. |
| **A3** | A constant safety margin $\sigma$ is added behind the rear of the leading train, consistent with ETCS safety requirements. |
| **A4** | A profile penalty $F_{i,p}$ is introduced to break ties among profiles that yield equal delay (e.g., energy-optimal driving). |
| **A5** | Route setting time $\tau_i^{setup}$ is assumed known and constant per train; in reality it depends on interlocking state, but this is a standard MILP simplification. |
| **A6** | The brake indication point is not an explicit variable; it is implicitly enforced by the speed-dependent headway term in (9)–(10), which is the modelling trick that makes the MILP linear. |
| **A7** | Only pairwise conflicts are modelled (standard in CDR); no three-train simultaneous interactions are considered. |
| **A8** | The time horizon is discretised into $\mathcal{K}$ for departure/arrival options; continuous time is used for section entry/exit. |
| **A9** | Trains cannot overtake within a section (no bidirectional track modelled); ordering $\delta_{ij}$ is fixed per section pair. |
| **A10** | Dwell times at stations are absorbed into the running time $T_{i,p,s}$ of the station section, or modelled as a separate fixed parameter **[A10]**; here they are included in $T_{i,p,s}$. |

---

## 7. Summary

The model is a **mixed-integer linear program** that:

1. **Selects** a route and a speed-profile option for each train (binary $x_{i,r}$, $y_{i,p}$).
2. **Sequences** conflicting trains (binary $\delta_{ij}$).
3. **Schedules** entry/exit times per section (continuous $t_{i,s}^{in}$, $t_{i,s}^{out}$).
4. **Enforces DTG separation** via speed-dependent braking-distance headways (constraints 9–10), replacing the fixed-block separation of RECIFE-MILP.
5. **Minimises** weighted total delay plus a profile penalty (objective $Z$).

The key DTG enhancement is the term $\dfrac{b_{j,p}+\sigma+L_i}{v_{j,p,s}}$ in constraints (9)–(10), which makes the required separation **train- and speed-dependent**, exactly as required by ETCS L2 braking-curve supervision. The switch/non-switch distinction (constraint 8) and the speed-profile options (constraints 2, 5a–5b) complete the three enhancements described in the paper.

Text:
# Integrated MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t' \in T$, $t \neq t'$ |
| $S$ | Set of track segments, indexed by $s \in \{1, \dots, N-1\}$ |
| $I$ | Set of stations, indexed by $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ |
| $M$ | Set of discrete speed-profile modes per segment, indexed by $m \in \{1, \dots, |M|\}$ |
| $D$ | Set of travelling directions, $D = \{0, 1\}$ ($0$ = nominal, $1$ = opposite) |

**Special entities:**
- $s^* = k \in S$: the blocked segment.
- $d^* \in D$: the blocked direction.
- Disruption window $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$ on segment $s^*$.

---

## 2. Parameters (Data)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| $\bar{a}_{t,i}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $\bar{d}_{t,i}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $r_{s,m}$ | Running time on segment $s$ under speed mode $m$ |
| $e_{s,m}$ | Energy consumption on segment $s$ under speed mode $m$ |
| $\underline{\tau}, \overline{\tau}$ | Minimum and maximum station dwell time (assumed uniform) |
| $h$ | Minimum same-direction headway on a segment (assumed uniform) |
| $h^{\times}$ | Minimum opposite-direction headway on a shared (rerouted) segment (assumed uniform) |
| $t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}$ | Start and end times of the disruption |
| $w_D, w_E, w_C$ | Weights for total delay, total energy, and cancellation penalty |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large big-M constant |

**Modelling assumptions (marked as such):**

- *A1:* Uniform headway, cross-headway, and dwell-time limits.
- *A2:* Rerouting is permitted only on the blocked segment $s^*$ and only within $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$.
- *A3:* Single-track per direction with no overtaking (linear order per segment).
- *A4:* Only arrival delays (not departure delays) are penalized.
- *A5:* Speed profiles are discretized into modes $\{1, \dots, |M|\}$ with given $(r_{s,m}, e_{s,m})$ pairs (no continuous dynamics).
- *A6:* Each non-cancelled train traverses every segment exactly once (full-route assumption).

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,i} \geq 0$ | continuous | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $d_{t,i} \geq 0$ | continuous | Actual departure time of train $t$ from station $i$ |
| $\delta_{t,i} \geq 0$ | continuous | Arrival delay of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $x_{t,s,m} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 iff train $t$ traverses segment $s$ in speed mode $m$ |
| $y_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 iff train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $s$ (same direction) |
| $z_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 iff trains $t, t'$ are in opposite directions on segment $s$ under rerouting |
| $q_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 iff train $t$ reroutes onto the opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 iff train $t$ is cancelled |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_D \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{t,i}
\;+\; w_E \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \sum_{m \in M} e_{s,m}\, x_{t,s,m}
\;+\; w_C \sum_{t \in T} c_t
$$

The objective is a weighted sum of (i) total arrival delay across all stations, (ii) total tractive energy consumption along all segments and modes, and (iii) total cancellation penalty.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Single speed-mode selection per segment

$$
\sum_{m \in M} x_{t,s,m} = 1 - c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

*Each non-cancelled train selects exactly one speed mode per segment; cancelled trains select none.*

### (C2) Running-time linkage between stations

$$
a_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} \;\geq\; \sum_{m \in M} r_{s,m}\, x_{t,s,m} \;-\; M\, c_t \qquad \forall\, t, s
$$

$$
a_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} \;\leq\; \sum_{m \in M} r_{s,m}\, x_{t,s,m} \;+\; M\, c_t \qquad \forall\, t, s
$$

*Segment traversal time equals the running time of the selected mode; big-M terms relax the equality for cancelled trains.*

### (C3) Station dwell-time bounds

$$
d_{t,i} - a_{t,i} \;\geq\; \underline{\tau}\,(1 - c_t) \qquad \forall\, t, i
$$

$$
d_{t,i} - a_{t,i} \;\leq\; \overline{\tau}\,(1 - c_t) \qquad \forall\, t, i
$$

### (C4) Delay definition (non-negative arrival delay only)

$$
\delta_{t,i} \;\geq\; a_{t,i} - \bar{a}_{t,i} \qquad \forall\, t, i
$$

$$
\delta_{t,i} \;\geq\; 0 \qquad \forall\, t, i
$$

*Early arrivals accrue zero delay (per Assumption A4).*

### (C5) Rerouting activation confined to blocked segment and disruption window

$$
d_{t,s^*} \;\geq\; t_{\text{start}} \;-\; M\,(1 - q_{t,s^*}) \qquad \forall\, t
$$

$$
a_{t,s^*+1} \;\leq\; t_{\text{end}} \;+\; M\,(1 - q_{t,s^*}) \qquad \forall\, t
$$

$$
q_{t,s} = 0 \qquad \forall\, t,\; s \neq s^*
$$

*Rerouting is only declared if the train's occupancy of segment $s^*$ lies inside $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$ (Assumption A2).*

### (C6) Same-direction ordering and headway

For all $t, t' \in T$, $t \neq t'$, and $s \in S$:

$$
d_{t',s} \;\geq\; a_{t,s+1} + h \;-\; M\,\big(3 - y_{t,t',s} - (1 - c_t) - (1 - c_{t'})\big)
$$

$$
d_{t,s} \;\geq\; a_{t',s+1} + h \;-\; M\,\big(2 - (1 - y_{t,t',s}) - (1 - c_t) - (1 - c_{t'})\big)
$$

*If $y_{t,t',s}=1$ and both trains are active, then $t$ precedes $t'$ with the same-direction headway $h$. Together with the linear-order assumption A3, this enforces a conflict-free single-track schedule.*

### (C7) Opposite-direction mutual exclusion on the rerouted segment

For all $t, t' \in T$, $t \neq t'$, and $s \in S$:

$$
d_{t',s} \;\geq\; a_{t,s+1} + h^{\times} \;-\; M\,(1 - z_{t,t',s}) \;-\; M\,(2 - q_{t,s} - q_{t',s})
$$

$$
a_{t',s+1} \;\leq\; d_{t,s} - h^{\times} \;+\; M\,(1 - z_{t,t',s}) \;+\; M\,(2 - q_{t,s} - q_{t',s})
$$

with the coupling:

$$
z_{t,t',s} + z_{t',t,s} = 1 \quad \text{if } q_{t,s} = q_{t',s} = 1
$$

*When two trains share the opposite track on segment $s$ in opposite senses, only one may occupy it at a time, with a safety margin $h^{\times}$.*

### (C8) Consistency between same-direction ordering and rerouting

For any pair $(t, t')$ and segment $s$:

$$
q_{t,s} + q_{t',s} \;\leq\; 2 - \big( y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} \big)
$$

*Prevents the same-direction ordering variable from being active when both trains have rerouted onto the shared track.*

### (C9) Cancellation propagation

$$
x_{t,s,m} = 0 \quad \forall\, m \in M \;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\; c_t = 1
$$

$$
q_{t,s^*} \;\leq\; 1 - c_t \qquad \forall\, t
$$

*Already implied by (C1) and the big-M relaxations in (C2)–(C3), restated for clarity.*

### (C10) Variable domains

$$
x_{t,s,m},\; y_{t,t',s},\; z_{t,t',s},\; q_{t,s},\; c_t \in \{0,1\}
$$

$$
a_{t,i},\; d_{t,i},\; \delta_{t,i} \geq 0
$$

---

## 6. Summary of Decisions Captured

The MILP jointly determines:

| Decision layer | Variable(s) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Retiming** | $a_{t,i},\; d_{t,i},\; \delta_{t,i}$ | Adjusted arrival/departure times and arrival delays |
| **Reordering** | $y_{t,t',s}$ | Precedence between trains on each segment |
| **Rerouting** | $q_{t,s},\; z_{t,t',s}$ | Use of the opposite track on $s^*$ during $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$ |
| **Speed management** | $x_{t,s,m}$ | Discrete acceleration/cruise/deceleration mode per segment |
| **Cancellation** | $c_t$ | Removal of infeasible services |

All constraints are linear in the decision variables, yielding a pure MILP that simultaneously produces a conflict-free rescheduled timetable (with rerouting) and the corresponding executable speed profiles, minimizing a weighted combination of total delay, energy consumption, and service cancellations.
